documents.title: You Don't Know Jack
documents.tagline: Angel of mercy… or murderous “Doctor Death”?
documents.overview: Controversy and legal problems follow Dr. Jack Kevorkian as he advocates assisted suicide.
documents.plot:
You Don't Know Jack is a 2010 American television biographical film written by Adam Mazer and directed by Barry Levinson for HBO. Al Pacino stars as Jack Kevorkian, the Michigan pathologist and right-to-die activist dubbed "Dr. Death" by the press, with Brenda Vaccaro as his sister Margo Janus, John Goodman as his friend and medical technician Neal Nicol, Susan Sarandon as Janet Good, founder of a regional chapter of the Hemlock Society, and Danny Huston as his lawyer Geoffrey Fieger. It premiered on HBO in April 2010.

Moved by the case of David Rivlin, a quadriplegic man who went to court to be removed from his respirator, by the sight of a dying woman in a hospital and by the memory of his mother's painful death decades earlier, Kevorkian builds his first suicide machine, the "Mercitron," from parts bought at flea markets. The device allows a patient to self-administer, through an intravenous line, a harmless saline solution followed by drugs that induce a coma and then stop the heart. Because the drugs are expensive and difficult to obtain, he also develops a method using carbon monoxide. Rivlin, however, becomes agitated during their meeting, and he later dies after his respirator is removed and food and water are withheld. In an interview with the journalist Jack Lessenberry, Kevorkian condemns the cruelty of such a drawn-out death and begins offering his services as a "death counselor."

His first patient is Janet Adkins, a woman from Portland, Oregon, in the early stages of Alzheimer's disease, whose death in the back of his van in 1990 makes national headlines. Over the following years Kevorkian helps more than a hundred people end their lives, provoking outrage and admiration in equal measure. Fieger defends him in a series of trials, winning acquittals, while prosecutors, religious groups and medical authorities try to stop him. Increasingly determined to force a legal confrontation, Kevorkian videotapes himself directly administering a lethal injection to a man with ALS and allows it to be broadcast on 60 Minutes in 1998, leading to his conviction for second-degree murder.

The film received positive reviews, with an 83 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes praising Levinson's direction and Pacino's outstanding performance. Pacino won the Primetime Emmy Award and the Golden Globe Award for his portrayal, and the real Kevorkian attended the premiere.

documents.title: Life-Size
documents.tagline: She was a perfect doll. Now she's the real thing.
documents.overview: After her mom's death, Casey pulls away from everyone in her life, including her emotionally distant dad. With help from a magic spell, she tries to bring her mother back from the dead; instead, Casey's words accidentally awaken one of her least favorite toys: a statuesque Barbie clone named Eve. Things get worse when Casey's dad develops a crush on his daughter's living doll.
documents.plot:
Casey Stuart is a tomboyish girl who is the quarterback of her school's 7th-grade football team. After the passing of her mother, Casey has become withdrawn from old friends, and her widowed father, Ben, has been focused on his work at his law firm and missing her football games. Casey, determined to resurrect her mother, finds a book called "The Book of Awakenings" at a local bookstore. The book contains instructions on how to resurrect the dead and states that a successful resurrection will become permanent unless it is undone before sunset on the fourth day after it begins.
Following the book's instructions, Casey collects artifacts from her mother's life, including locks of her hair in her hairbrush. However, the resurrection is unwittingly sabotaged when Drew McDonald, Ben's co-worker who has a crush on Ben, gives Casey an Eve doll, a plastic fashion doll in the form of a young pretty woman, manufactured by Marathon Toys. Eve is stated to have many add-on accessories, including outfits appropriate to taxing careers such as law enforcement, medicine and outer space, and lives in Sunnyvale, "in the middle of America". Drew discovers the Eve doll soon discarded by Casey and uses the hairbrush to brush the doll's hair. With strands from Casey's Eve doll remaining on the brush as Casey utters the incantation, the magic acts on her doll rather than her mother, and Casey wakes up the next morning to find Eve in bed with her in full-size human form. Casey is upset by this, but Eve is excited about being a real woman.
Casey begins to look for the second volume of the book with instructions on how to undo the resurrection downtown but sees that she has to wait for it to arrive to the store. Leaving the store, she accidentally falls onto the street. Eve steps in front of the truck, using her police training to stop it, as Ben discovers Casey's whereabouts. Thankful that Eve saved his daughter, he asks how he can repay Eve. After Eve tells him she is from out-of-town and does not have any possessions nor a place to stay, Ben helps her buy her new clothes and lets her stay at their house. When Eve mentions that she has had numerous jobs including working as a doctor, police officer, and secretary, Ben hires her as a temp at the firm. She tries to do secretarial work and fails, but helps boost the morale of Ben's coworker, Ellen. She is then invited to a corporate event where she sings her theme song on stage, much to everyone's enjoyment.
During this time, tension builds between Casey and her father, which is further increased by Ben's attraction to Eve, which Casey resents as a betrayal to her mother. However, as Eve helps Casey with her self-confidence and coping with the loss of her mother, they gradually become friends. By the time the second volume of the magic book arrives at the bookstore, Casey has decided she likes Eve, so she does not buy it.

documents.title: True Legend
documents.tagline: "King Of Beggars"
documents.overview: Su Qi-Er, a wealthy man living during the Qing Dynasty who loses his fortune and reputation as a result of a conspiracy against him. After being forced out onto the streets, Su dedicates his life to martial arts and reemerges as a patriotic hero known as the "King of Beggars."
documents.plot:
True Legend (Chinese: 苏乞儿) is a 2010 Chinese-Hong Kong martial arts film directed by Yuen Woo-ping, his first film as director since Tai Chi Boxer in 1996. Vincent Zhao stars as the Chinese folk hero Su Can, also known as Beggar So, the legendary master of drunken boxing, with Zhou Xun, Andy On and Jay Chou. Gordon Liu, Leung Kar-yan, Michelle Yeoh and David Carradine, in one of his final roles, make cameo appearances. Set in late Qing dynasty China, the film was released in both 2D and 3D.

Su Can is a celebrated general who resigns from military service to devote himself to martial arts and family life. His adoptive brother Yuan Lie has long been jealous of him. Years earlier, Su's father killed Yuan's father, who had turned to evil, and then raised Yuan as his own son. Five years after Su's retirement, he has married Yuan's sister Ying and they have a young son, Feng. Yuan returns as a powerful governor, having mastered a deadly technique known as the Five Venom Fists and fused armor into his body, and he kills Su's father in revenge.

When Su confronts him, Yuan defeats him easily and throws him into a river, and Ying leaps in after him. Rescued by a healer, the couple survive, but Su is badly crippled and turns to drink. With Ying's support he slowly rebuilds his strength in seclusion, training against imagined opponents, the God of Wushu and an old sage, and develops a new fighting style. He returns to rescue his son, but the cost is devastating, and grief drives him into a period of madness during which he wanders the streets with Feng as a beggar. During this time he perfects the drunken fist style that will make him a legend, and in the final act he is drawn into a brutal series of fights against foreign wrestlers.

The film received moderately positive reviews, with a 63 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 62. It won the Lotus Action Asia award at the 13th Deauville Asian Film Festival and was praised for Yuen's choreography; Charlie Jane Anders of Gizmodo's io9 called it pure old-school awesomeness, comparing it to Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, although some critics found its two halves uneven.

documents.title: Letters to Juliet
documents.tagline: What if you had a second chance to find true love?
documents.overview: An American girl on vacation in Italy finds an unanswered "letter to Juliet" -- one of thousands of missives left at the fictional lover's Verona courtyard, which are typically answered by the "secretaries of Juliet" -- and she goes on a quest to find the lovers referenced in the letter.
documents.plot: An American girl on vacation in Italy finds an unanswered "letter to Juliet" -- one of thousands of missives left at the fictional lover's Verona courtyard, which are typically answered by the "secretaries of Juliet" -- and she goes on a quest to find the lovers referenced in the letter.

documents.title: Falling Down
documents.tagline: A Tale Of Urban Reality.
documents.overview: An ordinary man frustrated with the various flaws he sees in society begins to psychotically and violently lash out against them.
documents.plot:
Falling Down is a 1993 American crime thriller film directed by Joel Schumacher and written by Ebbe Roe Smith, starring Michael Douglas as William Foster, an unemployed defense worker whose frustrations boil over into violence on a single day in Los Angeles, and Robert Duvall as Martin Prendergast, a police sergeant on his last day before retirement who tries to track him down. Barbara Hershey, Rachel Ticotin and Tuesday Weld co-star.

On a sweltering morning, Foster is trapped in a Los Angeles traffic jam when his air conditioning fails. He abandons his car and sets off on foot, briefcase in hand, intent on reaching his ex-wife Beth's home in Venice for his daughter's birthday party. His journey across the city becomes a series of escalating confrontations. He smashes up a convenience store after its owner refuses to give him change for a phone call, beats off two gang members who try to rob him and, after their friends open fire in a drive-by that kills bystanders but misses him, walks away with their bag of weapons. At a fast-food restaurant, refused breakfast because the menu has just switched to lunch, he accidentally fires a gun into the ceiling, then complains that his burger looks nothing like the picture. Alarmed by his calls, Beth, who has a restraining order against him, alerts the police. Meanwhile Prendergast, who has been coaxed into retirement by his wife, insists on investigating the string of incidents and, remembering Foster's "D-FENS" vanity license plate from the morning traffic jam, realizes that one man is behind them all. With his partner, Detective Sandra Torres, he visits Foster's mother, who is surprised to learn that her son has lost his job. At a military surplus store, Foster's growing sense of grievance meets real bigotry when the owner, a neo-Nazi who admires his violence, tries to recruit him and then turns on him, with deadly results. As Foster makes his way toward Venice, Prendergast races to reach Beth and their daughter before he does.

Falling Down was nominated for the Palme d'Or at the 1993 Cannes Film Festival, and Smith's screenplay won the Edgar Award. Reviews were mixed, with praise for Douglas and Duvall but criticism of its violence and tone; it holds a 77% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. The film grossed $96 million against a $25 million budget and topped the US box office in its first two weeks.

documents.title: The Human Centipede (First Sequence)
documents.tagline: Their flesh is his fantasy
documents.overview: During a stopover in Germany in the middle of a carefree road trip through Europe, two American girls find themselves alone at night when their car breaks down in the woods. Searching for help at a nearby villa, they are wooed into the clutches of a deranged retired surgeon who explains his mad scientific vision to his captives' utter horror. They are to be the subjects of his sick lifetime fantasy: to be the first to connect people, one to the next, and in doing so bring to life "the human centipede."
documents.plot:
Lindsay and Jenny, tourists from New York City visiting Germany, get a flat tire on their way to a nightclub and seek help at the house of Dr. Josef Heiter. He drugs the women with Rohypnol in their water and locks them up in a makeshift medical ward.
The misanthropic, psychopathic surgeon Heiter is a retired world-renowned expert at separating conjoined twins, but dreams of "making new creatures." He plans to surgically connect his three victims' mouths to their anus, so that they share a single digestive system. His prior experiment, the 3Dog, conjoined three Rottweilers into a "conjoined triplet"; all three dogs died following the operation.
Lindsay and Jenny find themselves trapped on their gurneys next to a Dutch truck driver, whom Heiter kidnapped at the beginning of the film. Heiter declared the trucker incompatible with the ladies and ends his life. He later kidnaps Japanese tourist Katsuro. After Lindsay tries to escape and fails, Heiter decides to make her the middle segment of the centipede. Heiter performs the surgery, placing Katsuro at the lead, Lindsay in the middle, and Jenny at the rear; mutilating Lindsay and Jenny's mouths and stitching each to the anus of the person in front. He severs the ligaments of his victims' knees, forcing them to crawl.
Once the operation is complete, Heiter takes the centipede to his living room, takes photos of each segment to humiliate them, and passes a mirror around so the segments can view their new form. Heiter treats his human centipede as a pet by caging the centipede in a dog kennel, training them into obeying his orders, forcing Katsuro to eat dog food at dinner, and belittling Katsuro with racist insults and beating him with a crop when he becomes rebellious.
Eventually, Katsuro needs to defecate. He does so after apologizing to the girls, after which Lindsay is forced to swallow his excrement. Heiter becomes irritated after being kept awake at night by the caged centipede and threatens Katsuro (who, as the front part of the centipede, has his mouth free and is still able to speak) with the removal of his vocal cords. When the centipede attempts to escape while Heiter is swimming, all three segments are punished by being beaten with the crop. During a checkup, Heiter is displeased to learn that Lindsay is constipated. He proposes to use laxatives on Lindsay, but discovers that Jenny is dying from sepsis.
Two detectives, Kranz and Voller, visit the house to investigate the disappearance of the three tourists as well as the trucker. Heiter is inspired to add them as replacements for Jenny in a new four-segment centipede. He offers the detectives more spiked water, causing them to become suspicious and obtain a search warrant for his home. After the detectives leave, the victims attempt to escape, and Katsuro attacks Heiter. He injures him, but their attempt to escape fails.

documents.title: Conan the Barbarian
documents.tagline: Enter an age undreamed of
documents.overview: A quest that begins as a personal vendetta for the fierce Cimmerian warrior soon turns into an epic battle against hulking rivals, horrific monsters, and impossible odds, as Conan realizes he is the only hope of saving the great nations of Hyboria from an encroaching reign of supernatural evil.
documents.plot:
Conan the Barbarian is a 2011 American sword-and-sorcery film based on Robert E. Howard's character, directed by Marcus Nispel and written by Thomas Dean Donnelly, Joshua Oppenheimer and Sean Hood. Jason Momoa stars as Conan, with Leo Howard as the young Conan, Rachel Nichols as Tamara, Stephen Lang as the warlord Khalar Zym, Rose McGowan as his daughter Marique, Ron Perlman as Conan's father Corin, Saïd Taghmaoui as the thief Ela-Shan and Nonso Anozie as Artus, while Morgan Freeman narrates.

Conan, born on a battlefield, is the son of Corin, a Cimmerian chieftain and blacksmith. His village is destroyed by Khalar Zym, who is gathering the pieces of the Mask of Acheron, an artifact made by sorcerers to enslave the world and later broken up among the barbarian tribes, so that he can resurrect his dead wife, the evil sorceress Maliva, and conquer Hyboria. Zym takes the Cimmerians' fragment, kills Corin and leaves Conan the only survivor. Years later, Conan has become a pirate still hunting Zym. In Messantia, he gets himself captured with Ela-Shan to reach Lucius, one of Zym's men, and learns that Zym needs a pure-blooded female descendant of the Acheronians to unleash the mask's power before Conan frees Lucius's prisoners, who kill him. When Zym and Marique attack a monastery, the monk Fassir sends his pupil Tamara, the descendant they seek, to flee. Conan rescues her, captures Zym's lieutenant Remo and catapults him back into Zym's camp as a message. In a confrontation, Zym recognizes the boy he spared, and Marique poisons Conan, who is saved by Tamara and recovers on his ship. Conan heads for Zym's kingdom, and Tamara, sent after him by Artus, spends the night with him, but is captured on her way back to the ship. With Ela-Shan's help, Conan breaks into Zym's castle, where Zym uses Tamara's blood to restore the mask and plans to make her body a vessel for Maliva's soul. Conan fights a tentacled creature guarding the dungeons, frees Tamara, reclaims his father's sword and cuts off Marique's hand before she is killed. As Maliva's spirit begins to possess Tamara on a bridge, Conan destroys it, sending Zym into the lava below. He returns Tamara to her birthplace and visits his old village, content that he has avenged his father.

Released in August 2011, it was a critical and commercial failure that grossed about $48.8 million against a $90 million budget and holds a 25% Rotten Tomatoes rating, though it earned a Saturn Award nomination for its makeup.

documents.title: Four Lions
documents.tagline: We are four Lions.
documents.overview: A group of Muslim men living in Sheffield hatch an inept plan to become suicide bombers.
documents.plot:
Four radicalised British Muslims living in Sheffield (three of whom are British Pakistanis) aspire to become suicide bombers: Omar, who is deeply critical of Western society and interventionism; his dim-witted and anxious cousin Waj; Barry, a bad-tempered and rash English convert; and the naive Faisal. When Omar and Waj travel to an al-Qaeda-affiliated training camp in Pakistan, Barry recruits a fifth member, Hassan, after witnessing him pretending to commit a suicide bombing at a conference. The training in Pakistan ends in disaster when Omar accidentally destroys part of the camp while attempting to shoot down a drone, and the pair are forced to flee. Omar uses the experience to assert authority over the group on his return to Britain.
The group disagrees about what their target should be. Barry wants to bomb a local mosque as a false flag operation to "radicalise the moderates" and Faisal suggests blowing up a Boots because it sells contraceptives. Ahmed, Omar's conservative, pacifist brother, tries to talk him out of doing anything violent; however, Omar and his wife, Sofia, mock Ahmed for his unwillingness to be in the same room as a woman, and accuse him of keeping his wife in a cupboard. Sofia instigates a water gun fight with him, prompting Ahmed to leave in a huff. After the group begins production of the explosives, Hassan is left to watch the safehouse as Barry, Waj and Faisal test detonate a small amount of TATP contained in a microwave, using a nearby fireworks show to cover the sound.
When they return, they find Hassan dancing with an oblivious neighbour. The group suspects they have been compromised and transport the explosives to a new location in grocery bags. Faisal trips up while crossing a field and is killed in the explosion. This angers Omar, who berates the others and leaves. Faisal's head is found, tipping off the authorities, and Omar tells the others and they reconcile. Omar decides to target the upcoming London Marathon due to having access to mascot costumes, which they use to conceal the bombs. Meanwhile, armed police raid Omar's brother's house.
At the Marathon, Waj expresses doubts about the morality of their plot, but Omar convinces him to go through with it. A police officer approaches the group, which leads Hassan to attempt to alert the officer about their plot, but he is killed when Barry remotely detonates his bomb. The remaining three panic and run away as the police search for them. Omar has a change of heart, feeling guilt about manipulating Waj into dying for a cause he does not understand and attempts to prevent the attack. Two police snipers receive Omar's description, a man dressed as the Honey Monster, but one of them mistakenly kills a bystander in a Wookiee costume.
Waj is cornered by police in a kebab shop and takes the staff hostage. Omar calls Waj and convinces him to let all but one of the hostages go. Barry finds Omar, snatches his phone, and swallows the SIM card.

documents.title: St Trinian's 2: The Legend of Fritton's Gold
documents.original_title: St Trinian's 2: The Legend of Fritton's Gold
documents.overview: The girls of St. Trinians are on the hunt for buried treasure after discovering headmistress Miss Fritton is related to a famous pirate.
documents.plot:
St Trinian's 2: The Legend of Fritton's Gold is a comedy film that explores several themes, primarily revolving around the mischievous and anarchic nature of its titular school. At its core, the movie delves into the idea of rebellion against authority and societal norms.

The story follows the students as they embark on a treasure hunt to uncover the hidden riches of Fritton's Gold, which serves as a metaphor for their own desires for freedom and independence. As they navigate through various obstacles and challenges, they must confront the constraints imposed upon them by the adult world and the expectations placed upon them by society.

Throughout the film, the characters' actions are driven by a desire to break free from the shackles of conformity and forge their own paths in life. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, often resulting in humorous and chaotic situations as the students' antics lead to unexpected consequences.

The movie also touches on the idea of class and social status, highlighting the disparities between the wealthy elite and those from more humble backgrounds. The students' quest for Fritton's Gold serves as a symbol of their desire to level the playing field and challenge the existing power structures.

Ultimately, St Trinian's 2: The Legend of Fritton's Gold is a lighthearted and entertaining film that uses humor and satire to comment on the human desire for freedom and self-expression.

documents.title: Bruce Lee: A Warrior's Journey
documents.tagline: You know the legend. Now meet the man.
documents.overview: Legendary martial artist Bruce Lee is the subject of this thoughtful documentary by Lee aficionado John Little. Using interviews, behind-the-scenes footage and action sequences from Lee's last (unfinished) film, Game of Death, Little paints a textured, complex portrait of the world's most famous action hero
documents.plot:
Bruce Lee: A Warrior's Journey is a 2000 documentary written and directed by John Little, an author and long-time researcher of Bruce Lee's life and writings, about the martial artist, his philosophy of Jeet Kune Do and his unfinished final film, Game of Death. Produced by Concord Productions with Warner Bros. and Media Asia, it premiered in San Francisco on 22 October 2000 and was released on VHS and DVD by Warner Home Video.

The film is divided into five parts. The first three trace Lee's life and the development of his ideas about combat and self-expression through archive material, rare behind-the-scenes footage and interviews with people who knew him, among them his widow Linda Lee Cadwell, his early student Taky Kimura, his friend and student Dan Inosanto, the hapkido grandmaster Ji Han-jae and the basketball star Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Lee's student and co-star in Game of Death. Jackie Chan, Sammo Hung and Chuck Norris are also among those credited.

The last two parts turn to Game of Death itself. Lee had shot the climactic fight sequences in 1972, in which his character battles his way up the levels of a pagoda against a different martial arts master on each floor, but interrupted filming to star in Enter the Dragon and died in 1973 before he could complete it. In 1978 Golden Harvest released a Game of Death built around roughly eleven minutes of his footage, filling out the rest with look-alikes and a new story. Some twenty-three further minutes of Lee's original material, long thought lost, were rediscovered in 1999 by Bey Logan, and Little edited them according to Lee's own script notes and outlines to present the pagoda finale much as Lee had intended, with his original English and Cantonese dialogue.

The music is by Wayne Hawkins, and Raymond Chow is among the producers. The DVD also included The Story, a short film shot in South Korea under Little's direction that dramatises the storyline Lee had planned for the full film. The documentary was later included as a bonus feature on the 2004 special edition DVD of Enter the Dragon, and it has been dubbed and broadcast in several countries, including Italy, where it aired on Discovery Channel and Rai 4.

documents.title: The Order
documents.tagline: Unleash The Power.
documents.overview: When Rudy, an artifacts smuggler, goes to Jerusalem to rescue his kidnapped archeologist father, he faces deportation by a scheming police chief. Now, to find his dad and recover a sacred scroll, he'll have to outwit officials and a ruthless sect. With the help of a beautiful Israeli cop, Rudy battles a faction of religious zealots determined to see a holy war at all costs.
documents.plot:
The Order is a 2001 American action adventure film directed by Sheldon Lettich and written by Jean-Claude Van Damme, who also stars in a dual role. Charlton Heston appears as Professor Walter Finley, with Sofia Milos as police lieutenant Dalia Barr, Brian Thompson as the cult leader Cyrus Jacob, Ben Cross as police chief Ben Ner, and Vernon Dobtcheff as the hero's father. Set largely in Israel, the film was released direct to DVD in the United States on 12 March 2002.

The film opens in 1099 at the end of the First Crusade, as Crusaders sack Jerusalem and slaughter its inhabitants. Horrified by the violence, a Flemish knight named Charles Le Vaillant, played by Van Damme, founds a new religious order intended to unite Christians, Jews and Muslims. Proclaiming himself its leader and messiah, he writes the order's sacred texts, but during a journey to Syria his camp is attacked by Christian knights and he is killed. The final chapter of the order's scripture, which Le Vaillant had buried in a secret location, is lost in the desert.

In the present day, Rudy Cafmeyer, also played by Van Damme, is a thief and smuggler of valuable antiquities. After a botched robbery of a Fabergé egg that ends with the treasure being destroyed, he learns that his father Oscar, an archaeologist and museum curator, has travelled to Israel in pursuit of a secret he has discovered and has been kidnapped. Rudy flies to Israel to find him. His father's associate, Professor Walt Finley, gives him the key to a safe-deposit box in East Jerusalem before being shot dead by unknown attackers. Rudy's search brings him into contact with the Order, which has survived for centuries as a peaceful community, until the fanatical disciple Cyrus seizes control by having its leader killed and begins preaching an imminent holy war. Hounded by the hostile police chief Ben Ner and secretly helped by Lieutenant Dalia Barr, a former member of the Order, Rudy follows a map toward hidden tunnels beneath Jerusalem to rescue his father and stop Cyrus.

The film combines martial arts action with an Indiana Jones-style treasure hunt and touches on themes of religious fanaticism and coexistence in the Holy Land, featuring chases through the streets and markets of Jerusalem.

Released without a theatrical run in the United States, The Order belongs to the series of international action films Van Damme made in the early 2000s, reuniting him with Lettich, who had directed him in Lionheart and Double Impact.

documents.title: 22 Bullets
documents.tagline: The revenge of the Professional.
documents.overview: Charly Matteï has turned his back on his life as an outlaw. For the last three years, he's led a peaceful life devoting himself to his wife and two children. Then, one winter morning, he's left for dead in the parking garage in Marseille's Old Port, with 22 bullets in his body. Against all the odds, he doesn't die...
documents.plot:
22 Bullets, released in France as L'Immortel, is a 2010 French gangster action film directed by Richard Berry. Loosely inspired by events in the life of the Marseille gangster Jacky Imbert, it is based on Franz-Olivier Giesbert's 2007 novel L'Immortel. Jean Reno stars as Charly Matteï, with Kad Merad, Marina Foïs, Jean-Pierre Darroussin and JoeyStarr in key supporting roles. Shooting began in Marseille in February 2009 and continued in Avignon and, for eight weeks, in Paris.

Three years before the story opens, Marseille crime boss Charly Matteï walked away from the underworld, handing his business to his old friend Tony Zacchia, and he now now lives quietly for his wife and two children. Then his old life returns with a vengeance when an eight-man hit squad ambushes him in an underground car park, killing his dog and leaving him for dead with twenty-two bullets in his body. Against all odds he survives.

Matteï at first tries to identify those responsible without resorting to bloodshed, but his restraint is read as weakness, and his loyal friend Karim is murdered by the same men. Swearing vengeance, Matteï sets out to hunt down the gunmen and the people who sent them. He confronts the hit squad at a birthday celebration and announces that he will kill each of them at a moment of his own choosing. The investigation is led by police officer Marie Goldman, whose husband, also a policeman, was murdered years earlier by a killer who was never caught; ignored by her superiors, she is still determined to find out who was responsible.

When Matteï's son is kidnapped, he strikes a deal with Goldman, who is torn between her duty and her desire to punish the men she suspects of killing her husband, Zacchia's associates. The police obtain a USB drive incriminating Zacchia in fraud and money laundering. Matteï rescues his son and confronts Zacchia at his home, and Zacchia is on the point of killing him when the police burst in and arrest them both. Matteï is released for lack of evidence. Goldman had told him that one of the eight shooters deliberately missed, and Matteï realises it was his friend and lawyer, coerced by Zacchia; he forgives him. The film ends with Matteï walking on a beach with his family, at peace with his past.

documents.title: Super 8
documents.tagline: It Arrives.
documents.overview: In 1979 Ohio, several youngsters are making a zombie movie with a Super-8 camera. In the midst of filming, the friends witness a horrifying train derailment and are lucky to escape with their lives. They soon discover that the catastrophe was no accident, as a series of unexplained events and disappearances soon follows. Deputy Jackson Lamb, the father of one of the kids, searches for the terrifying truth behind the crash.
documents.plot:
Super 8 is a science fiction adventure film directed by J.J. Abrams and written by Abrams and Damon Lindelof. The movie takes place in the summer of 1979, in the fictional town of Lillian, Ohio.

The story begins with a young boy named Joe Lamb (Joel Courtney), who lives with his single mother, Alice (Elle Fanning), and his older brother, Charles (Zachary Quinto). The family is struggling to make ends meet after their father's death. Joe is an avid fan of science fiction movies and spends most of his time making his own short films using a Super 8 camera.

One day, while exploring the woods near his home, Joe stumbles upon a mysterious train carrying a secret government experiment. The train is carrying a strange creature that has been infected with a deadly virus. As the creature escapes from the train, it begins to wreak havoc on the town of Lillian.

Joe soon discovers that the creature is not just any ordinary monster, but a shape-shifting alien being that can take on various forms. The government is trying to cover up the incident and silence anyone who witnesses the creature's existence. Joe teams up with his friends, Charles, Cary (Ryan Lee), and Martin (Kyle Chandler), to uncover the truth behind the creature and the government's involvement.

As the story unfolds, Joe and his friends embark on a thrilling adventure to stop the alien creature and save their town from destruction. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including military personnel and other creatures that are also infected with the virus.

Throughout the movie, Abrams pays homage to classic science fiction films of the 1970s and 1980s, such as E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial and Close Encounters of the Third Kind. The film's nostalgic value is enhanced by its use of Super 8 footage, which adds a unique visual style to the movie.

As the final confrontation approaches, Joe and his friends face off against the alien creature in an epic battle. In the end, they manage to defeat the creature and save their town from destruction. However, not before realizing that the government's involvement was more sinister than they initially thought.

The movie concludes with a sense of closure for the characters, as Joe and his mother are finally able to find some peace after the traumatic events of the summer. The film ends on a hopeful note, with Joe reflecting on the lessons he learned from his adventure and the importance of friendship and perseverance in the face of adversity.

Overall, Super 8 is a heartwarming and thrilling adventure that pays homage to classic science fiction films while also offering something new and unique.

documents.title: Splice
documents.tagline: Science's newest miracle...is a mistake.
documents.overview: Elsa and Clive, two young rebellious scientists, defy legal and ethical boundaries and forge ahead with a dangerous experiment: splicing together human and animal DNA to create a new organism. Named "Dren", the creature rapidly develops from a deformed female infant into a beautiful but dangerous winged human-chimera, who forges a bond with both of her creators - only to have that bond turn deadly.
documents.plot:
Splice is a 2009 science fiction horror film directed by Vincenzo Natali and written by Tyler Labine and Vincenzo Natali. The movie stars Adrien Brody, Sarah Polley, and David Hewlett.

The story begins with two scientists, Dreyfuss (David Hewlett) and Werner (Adrien Brody), who work at a biotech company called Medtech Industries. They are part of a team led by Dr. Emma Cullen (Sarah Polley), who is working on a top-secret project to create life from DNA samples.

The team has been experimenting with the genetic material of various animals, including monkeys and pigs, in an attempt to create a new species that can be used for medical research. However, their experiments have been unsuccessful, and they are about to give up when Emma discovers a unique DNA sample that she believes holds the key to creating life.

Emma decides to use this DNA sample to create a new organism, which she names "Dren." As Dren begins to grow and develop, the team is amazed by its rapid progress and potential. However, as Dren grows in size and strength, it becomes clear that something is not quite right.

Dren's behavior becomes increasingly erratic and violent, and the team realizes that they have created a being with a twisted sense of self-preservation. As tensions rise, Emma begins to question whether she has made a terrible mistake by creating life.

As Dren continues to evolve, it becomes clear that it is not just a simple organism, but a being with its own desires and motivations. The team is forced to confront the consequences of their actions and the ethics of playing God.

The movie builds towards a tense and suspenseful climax as Emma and her colleagues try to understand and control Dren's behavior. In the end, they are faced with a horrific choice: to destroy Dren or risk everything to save it.

Throughout the movie, Natali explores themes of scientific hubris, the ethics of genetic engineering, and the dangers of playing God. The film is also notable for its graphic and disturbing content, which includes scenes of violence, gore, and body horror.

Overall, Splice is a thought-provoking and unsettling sci-fi horror film that challenges viewers to consider the consequences of scientific progress without moral responsibility.

documents.title: The Tourist
documents.tagline: It all started when he met a woman.
documents.overview: American tourist Frank meets mysterious British woman Elsie on the train to Venice. Romance seems to bud, but there's more to her than meets the eye. Remake of the 2005 French film "Anthony Zimmer", written and directed by Jérôme Salle.
documents.plot:
The Tourist is a 2010 romantic thriller film directed by Florian Henckel von Donnersmarck and starring Angelina Jolie, Johnny Depp, and Paul Bettany.

The movie begins with Frank Taylor (Johnny Depp), a widowed father who travels to Venice, Italy for his daughter's wedding. He meets Elise Sellas (Angelina Jolie), a beautiful and charming woman who is also attending the wedding. The two strike up a conversation, and despite their initial awkwardness, they find themselves drawn to each other.

As Frank and Elise spend more time together, they begin to develop feelings for each other. However, their budding romance is complicated by the presence of Elise's husband, Alexander (Paul Bettany), who is revealed to be a ruthless and cunning man with a dark past.

Unbeknownst to Frank, Elise is being pursued by her ex-husband, who has been trying to kill her. As Frank gets closer to Elise, he becomes entangled in her life and begins to uncover the truth about her past. Meanwhile, Alexander's true intentions are revealed, and Frank finds himself in a desperate bid to protect Elise from harm.

As the story unfolds, Frank and Elise's relationship deepens, but they are also forced to confront their own personal demons. Frank is haunted by his wife's death, while Elise struggles with her complicated past and her feelings for Alexander.

The plot takes a dramatic turn when Frank discovers that Elise is in grave danger, and he must use all his wits and resourcefulness to protect her. In the process, he uncovers a web of deceit and betrayal that threatens to destroy everything he holds dear.

In the end, Frank and Elise's love for each other prevails, but not without great cost. The movie ends on a bittersweet note, with Frank and Elise parting ways, but forever changed by their experience together.

Throughout the film, the cinematography is stunning, capturing the beauty of Venice and its canals. The performances from Depp and Jolie are also noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to their characters. While some critics have panned the movie's plot as predictable, many have praised its atmospheric setting and the chemistry between the leads.

Overall, The Tourist is a romantic thriller that explores themes of love, loss, and redemption. With its stunning visuals and strong performances, it is a must-see for fans of the genre.

documents.title: Skyfall
documents.tagline: Think on your sins.
documents.overview: When Bond's latest assignment goes gravely wrong, agents around the world are exposed and MI6 headquarters is attacked. While M faces challenges to her authority and position from Gareth Mallory, the new Chairman of the Intelligence and Security Committee, it's up to Bond, aided only by field agent Eve, to locate the mastermind behind the attack.
documents.plot:
Skyfall is a 2012 British spy action film directed by Sam Mendes and produced by Michael Wilson and Barbara Broccoli. The film stars Daniel Craig, Javier Bardem, Judi Dench, and Raoul Trujillo.

The story begins with James Bond (Daniel Craig), a seasoned secret agent working for MI6, the British intelligence agency. He is haunted by his troubled past, particularly the death of his parents at the hands of Raoul Silva (Javier Bardem), a former MI6 agent turned rogue. The film's opening scene shows an elderly M (Judi Dench) being attacked by Silva, who has escaped from a maximum-security prison.

Bond is tasked with tracking down and capturing Silva, but he soon realizes that his nemesis has a personal vendetta against him. As Bond delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that Silva was once a brilliant MI6 agent who was betrayed by M, who had been keeping secrets about his past. Silva's plan is to destroy MI6 and everyone in it, starting with M.

As Bond navigates the complex web of espionage, he encounters a new ally, Sévérine (Bérénice Marlohe), a French woman who works for a private security company called Skyfall. However, she is revealed to be working for Silva, who has been manipulating her all along.

Bond's investigation takes him to Turkey, where he encounters a group of mercenaries who are being led by Raoul Silva. He also meets Patrice (Ola Rapace), a Swedish mercenary who becomes an ally in his quest to stop Silva.

As the story unfolds, Bond discovers that Silva has been using a complex system of hacking and surveillance to gather intelligence on MI6 and its agents. He also learns that M's past is shrouded in secrecy, and that she had been keeping secrets about her own life and relationships with other agents.

The film's climax features an intense showdown between Bond and Silva at Skyfall Lodge, the Scottish estate of James Bond's family. In a thrilling sequence, Bond faces off against Silva, who has rigged the lodge with explosives and is determined to destroy it.

In the end, Bond manages to defeat Silva, but not before he reveals that M had been keeping secrets about her own past and relationships with other agents. The film ends with M being forced to retire from MI6 due to the damage caused by Silva's actions, and Bond reflecting on his own past and the weight of his responsibilities as a secret agent.

Overall, Skyfall is a gripping and intense spy thriller that explores themes of loyalty, betrayal, and redemption. The film features stunning action sequences, memorable characters, and a complex plot that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

documents.title: It's a Boy Girl Thing
documents.tagline: They've turned into the things they hated most... each other.
documents.overview: A visit to a natural history museum proves catastrophic for two high school rivals, an overachiever and a jock, when an ancient Aztec statue casts a spell that causes them to switch bodies and see exactly what it's like to walk in the other's shoes.
documents.plot: A visit to a natural history museum proves catastrophic for two high school rivals, an overachiever and a jock, when an ancient Aztec statue casts a spell that causes them to switch bodies and see exactly what it's like to walk in the other's shoes.

documents.title: Easy A
documents.tagline: A comedy about a good girl a small favor and a big rumor
documents.overview: Olive, an average high school student, sees her below-the-radar existence turn around overnight once she decides to use the school's gossip grapevine to advance her social standing. Now her classmates are turning against her and the school board is becoming concerned, including her favorite teacher and the distracted guidance counselor. With the support of her hilariously idiosyncratic parents and a little help from a long-time crush, Olive attempts to take on her notorious new identity and crush the rumor mill once and for all.
documents.plot:
The story is narrated by Olive Penderghast, a 17-year-old high school student living in Ojai, California, speaking into her webcam. Desperate to avoid going on a camping trip with her best friend Rhiannon Abernathy and Rhiannon's hippie parents, Olive dishonestly claims she is going on a date with a college boy that weekend; truthfully, she stays home all weekend listening to "Pocketful of Sunshine" from a musical greeting card her grandmother sent her. Pressed by Rhiannon the following Monday, Olive eventually lies about having lost her virginity to her fictional date. Prudish, devout Christian student Marianne Bryant overhears their conversation, and Olive's story soon spreads throughout the school. The school's church group, run by Marianne, decides to "save" Olive from her supposed promiscuity. Olive confides the truth to her classmate Brandon, a gay student who is bullied for his sexual orientation. She agrees to serve as his "beard" and pretend to have sex with him at a teen party so people will believe he is straight.
After a fight with Rhiannon, Olive decides to embrace her new reputation as a "tramp" and begins to dress more provocatively. She stitches a red "A" onto her clothes, inspired by Hester Prynne from Nathaniel Hawthorne's 1850 novel The Scarlet Letter, which she has been reading in English class. Boys who have had no previous luck with girls beg Olive to increase their popularity by letting them claim they have had sex with her, which she does in exchange for gift cards to various stores. Marianne's ex-boyfriend Micah contracts chlamydia from having sex with the school guidance counselor, Mrs. Griffith, but claims Olive was the one who gave it to him. Because Mrs. Griffith's husband, Mr. Griffith, is Olive's favorite teacher, she accepts the blame to spare their marriage.
The church youth group, now including Rhiannon, begins harassing Olive in an attempt to get her to drop out of school. She goes on a date with Rhiannon's crush, Anson, which ends with her storming off angrily after he tries bribing her to actually have sex with him and not just claim that she did. Olive reconnects with Todd, her childhood crush and the school mascot, who says he does not believe the rumors because she lied for him when he was not ready for his first kiss years ago. She asks everyone who paid her to admit the truth, but nobody is willing to relinquish their newfound reputations. When Mrs. Griffith refuses to admit to her affair with Micah, Olive threatens to expose her; Mrs. Griffith says no one would believe her. Olive immediately informs Mr. Griffith, who subsequently separates from his wife.
After talking with her mother, Olive comes up with a plan – she performs a song-and-dance number at a pep rally to draw people's attention and tells them to watch her webcast that night, promising an online sex show with Todd. In actuality, Olive uses the webcast to explain the truth of what happened, which has served as the frame story for the film.

documents.title: Kites
documents.overview: A wounded man searches for his sweetheart in the Mexican desert while on the run from the police, bounty hunters, and others.
documents.plot:
Jay Ray is a dance teacher in Las Vegas, Nevada. As a side hustle, he marries immigrant women to get them green cards in exchange for money. When Gina, the rich daughter of a powerful Anglo-Indian casino owner, Bob Grover, falls for him, Jay goes along to marry into money. He discovers that his future brother-in-law, the vicious, homicidal Tony, is about to marry a Mexican woman named Natasha, whom Jay knows as Linda, the last of the immigrant women he married. On the night before "Natasha" and Tony's wedding, Linda and Jay humorously agree to a "divorce". A jealous, gun-wielding Tony arrives at her apartment while Jay is there. After he hits her, Linda impulsively knocks him out with a heavy object while he tussles with J. Linda and Jay go on the run toward Mexico, with Tony and the police in pursuit. They are helped by a friend of J, Robin. Robin gives them fake passports and IDs so that they can escape and build the life they want.
In the following week, Jay and Linda get married in Mexico. On the day of their wedding, they come back to their house. There, Robin comes to give them the passports and is unexpectedly shot by Tony and his men. Linda and Jay escape, but Jay is shot in the process. During a car chase, Linda stops the car by a train, puts Jay aboard it, and drives off. Back in the present, J meets with Jamaal, one of Bob's employees, and is ambushed. Jamaal is killed, but not before telling Jay of Linda's whereabouts. Jay kills off all of Tony's men and then kills Tony by smashing his face into the car door and he is then shot by Gina. He drives off to the location where Jamaal said Linda was last seen. It is shown that after Jay was put aboard the train, Linda was ambushed on a cliff and sent Jay a text message saying, "I am going...Sorry, forget me." She drives off of the cliff, killing herself by drowning. Jay cries and then smiles, jumping off the cliff as well. Finally, he is reunited with Linda under the ocean, and they embrace in death.

documents.title: Sex and the City 2
documents.tagline: Carrie on.
documents.overview: Carrie, Charlotte, and Miranda are all married now, but they're still up for a little fun in the sun. When Samantha gets the chance to visit one of the most extravagant vacation destinations on the planet and offers to bring them all along, they surmise that a women-only retreat may be the perfect excuse to eschew their responsibilities and remember what life was like before they decided to settle down.
documents.plot:
Sex and the City 2 is a 2010 American romantic comedy film written and directed by Michael Patrick King, the second and final film based on the HBO television series and the sequel to Sex and the City (2008). It stars Sarah Jessica Parker, Kim Cattrall, Kristin Davis and Cynthia Nixon, with John Corbett and Chris Noth. The film was released in the United States on May 27, 2010.

Carrie, Samantha, Charlotte and Miranda reunite for the wedding of their friends Stanford and Anthony. Three of the women are now married, while Samantha, single at 52, is fighting the effects of menopause. Back in New York, Miranda quits her law firm after constant disrespect from its new managing partner, and Charlotte, a stay-at-home mother of two, feels overwhelmed and worries that her husband Harry may be attracted to their young nanny, Erin. Carrie and Mr. Big have settled into married life but disagree about how to spend their free time: she wants to go out, while he prefers to stay home and watch television. When he gives her a television for their bedroom as an anniversary present, she feels unappreciated, and he proposes that she spend two days a week at her old apartment, an arrangement she accepts with some unease. Samantha, meanwhile, is hired to develop a PR campaign for a wealthy sheikh, who invites her and her friends on an all-expenses-paid luxury trip to Abu Dhabi. There Samantha's hormone supplements are confiscated, Charlotte struggles to be away from her children, Miranda embraces the new culture, and Carrie befriends her butler, an underpaid worker from India. In a souq, Carrie unexpectedly runs into her former fiancé Aidan, and a dinner with him ends in a kiss that she feels obliged to confess to Big. As the women's Western habits clash with local customs, Samantha's public flirtation with a Danish architect leads to trouble with the authorities, and the friends' getaway comes to an abrupt end, sending them back to New York to sort out their lives.

The film received highly unfavorable reviews, with criticism aimed at its plot, its running time and its portrayal of the Middle East, which many called culturally insensitive. It holds a 16% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 27 out of 100, yet it grossed $294.7 million worldwide against a $95 million budget.

documents.title: The Social Network
documents.tagline: You don't get to 500 million friends without making a few enemies.
documents.overview: The tale of a new breed of cultural insurgent: a punk genius who sparked a revolution and changed the face of human interaction for a generation, and perhaps forever.
documents.plot:
The Social Network is a biographical drama film directed by David Fincher, released in 2010 by Columbia Pictures. The movie tells the story of the founding of Facebook and its early success.

The film begins with Mark Zuckerberg (played by Jesse Eisenberg), a brilliant but awkward college student at Harvard University. Mark is portrayed as an outsider who struggles to connect with his peers due to his social anxiety and lack of charisma. However, he finds solace in coding and computer science, which becomes his passion.

Mark's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss (played by Armie Hammer), two identical twin brothers who are also Harvard students. The twins approach Mark with an idea for a social networking site called "Facemash," which allows users to compare the photos of two students and vote on which one is more attractive. Mark agrees to help the twins, but later decides to use their idea as a starting point for his own project.

Mark creates a new website called "Thefacebook" and launches it from his dorm room. The site quickly gains popularity among Harvard students, and Mark becomes an overnight sensation. However, he faces opposition from the Winklevoss twins, who claim that they came up with the idea first and demand a share of the profits.

As Facebook's popularity grows, Mark attracts the attention of Eduardo Saverin (played by Andrew Garfield), his friend and business partner. Eduardo helps Mark to refine the site's design and expand its user base. However, their partnership is put to the test when Mark decides to drop Eduardo as a co-founder and replace him with Cameron Winklevoss.

The film takes a dramatic turn when Mark meets Natalie Portman (playing herself), who becomes his love interest. Their relationship is portrayed as intense but short-lived, and Mark's focus on Facebook begins to suffer.

As Facebook's user base grows exponentially, Mark faces increasing pressure from investors and the media. He also has to deal with the Winklevoss twins' lawsuit against him, which claims that they came up with the idea for Facebook first.

The film's climax features a dramatic confrontation between Mark and Eduardo at a coffee shop in Palo Alto, California. The two men engage in a heated argument over their partnership and the future of Facebook.

In the end, Mark emerges victorious but scarred by his experiences. He has created a global phenomenon, but at what cost? The film ends with Mark sitting alone in his office, staring at his computer screen as he reflects on the consequences of his actions.

The Social Network received widespread critical acclaim for its portrayal of the Facebook saga. The film won several awards, including three Academy Awards (Best Original Score, Best Film Editing, and Best Adapted Screenplay). Jesse Eisenberg's performance as Mark Zuckerberg was particularly praised, earning him an Oscar nomination for Best Actor.

documents.title: Knight and Day
documents.tagline: Every Hit Man Deserves a Second Shot!
documents.overview: A fugitive couple goes on a glamorous and sometimes deadly adventure where nothing and no one – even themselves – are what they seem. Amid shifting alliances and unexpected betrayals, they race across the globe, with their survival ultimately hinging on the battle of truth vs. trust.
documents.plot:
Knight and Day is a 2010 action comedy film directed by James Mangold and starring Tom Cruise and Cameron Diaz.

The movie begins with June Havens (Cameron Diaz), a seemingly ordinary housewife living in Los Angeles. However, her mundane life takes an unexpected turn when she's approached by a mysterious man named Roy Miller (Peter Sarsgaard) who claims to be a former CIA operative. He warns her that her husband, Ben (Jordi Mollà), is actually a deadly assassin working for the organization.

June initially dismisses Roy's warnings but soon finds herself in the middle of a high-stakes adventure when she's kidnapped by Ben and his team. She's forced to participate in a series of high-speed chases and action-packed sequences as they try to evade their pursuers.

As June navigates this treacherous world, she meets Roy again, who reveals that he's actually a former CIA operative turned rogue agent. He claims to be working to take down Ben and his organization, which is secretly manipulating world events for its own gain.

Throughout the movie, June finds herself torn between her loyalty to her husband and her growing feelings for Roy. As they work together to uncover the truth about Ben's organization, they develop a romantic connection that adds an extra layer of tension to their mission.

The plot thickens as June discovers that Ben is actually working for a shadowy organization known as "The Syndicate," which has infiltrated every level of society. The Syndicate is using its operatives to manipulate world events and control the global economy.

As June and Roy get closer to uncovering the truth, they find themselves in increasing danger. They must use all their skills and resources to stay one step ahead of Ben's team and The Syndicate's agents.

In the climactic final act, June and Roy finally expose The Syndicate's plans and bring down its leaders. However, not before a thrilling car chase sequence where June uses her wits and resourcefulness to outsmart Ben's team and escape.

The movie ends with June and Roy sharing a romantic moment, as they realize that their feelings for each other are genuine. They decide to leave their past lives behind and start anew, free from the dangers of The Syndicate.

Overall, Knight and Day is an action-packed adventure with plenty of twists and turns. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of Tom Cruise and Cameron Diaz will enjoy this fun and entertaining ride.

documents.title: The White Ribbon
documents.original_title: Das weiße Band - Eine deutsche Kindergeschichte
documents.overview: Strange events happen in a small village in the north of Germany during the years just before World War I, which seem to be ritual punishment. The abused and suppressed children of the villagers seem to be at the heart of this mystery.
documents.plot: An aged tailor recalls his life as the schoolteacher of a small village in Northern Germany that was struck by a series of strange events in the year leading up to WWI.

documents.title: The Horde
documents.overview: A bunch of crooked cops raid a ruined building located in an impoverished suburb of Paris, determined to furiously avenge the death of one of them, murdered by the ruthless criminal gang hidden on top of the dark labyrinth that will become a deathly trap when the living, unexpectedly turned into the undead by a mysterious plague, begin to devour the world.
documents.plot:
The Horde (French: La Horde) is a 2009 French zombie action horror film directed by Yannick Dahan and Benjamin Rocher, who wrote it with Stéphane Moïssakis and Arnaud Bordas, expanding on their earlier short film Rivoallan. Claude Perron stars as the police officer Aurore, with Jean-Pierre Martins as Ouessem, Aurélien Recoing as Jimenez and Antoine Oppenheim as Tony, while Eriq Ebouaney and Doudou Masta play the gangster brothers Adewale and Bola Markudi, Yves Pignot plays René and Jo Prestia also appears. Christopher Lennertz composed the score.

After one of their colleagues is murdered by a gang, a small group of police officers decides to take revenge outside the law. The killers are holed up in a condemned high-rise tower in a run-down housing project on the outskirts of Paris, and the officers storm the building at night intending to take down the notorious drug dealer behind the killing. The raid goes disastrously wrong: half the team is shot dead and the survivors are captured by the gangsters.

Just as the prisoners are about to be executed, strange screams echo through the building. The dead are rising, and the city outside is being overrun by a mysterious plague that turns the living into flesh-eating zombies. Trapped together in the decaying tower and besieged by the undead horde, cops and criminals are forced into an uneasy alliance, fighting their way through the labyrinth of stairwells and flats even as the old hostility between the two sides threatens to tear their fragile truce apart.

Made for about €2 million, partly financed by some 468 film fans through an online crowdfunding scheme, the film was shot in 2008, with exteriors filmed in the Forestière estate in Clichy-sous-Bois and interiors built in a former warehouse on the Île-Saint-Denis; around 300 volunteer extras recruited online played the zombies. It screened at festivals including London FrightFest and Sitges in 2009 before opening in France on 10 February 2010, and IFC Films released it in the United States that August. French critics were mostly hostile, faulting crude dialogue, stereotyped characters, video-game staging and borrowed ideas, though some admired its brute energy and Pignot's performance; international reviews were mixed, with roughly 45% positive on Rotten Tomatoes. It won awards for screenplay and special effects at Fantasporto.

documents.title: Voices of a Distant Star
documents.tagline: A love story that transcends time and space...
documents.overview: It is 2046 when a mysterious alien force begins their annihilation of the human race. Leaving behind the one person she loves, Mikako joins the interstellar battle as a pilot. And so - while Mikako risks her life to save mankind - Noboru waits. The two lovers, worlds apart, desperately strive to remain connected as the gap between them widens at a frightening pace.
documents.plot:
A schoolgirl named Mikako Nagamine (Mika Shinohara (original Japanese), Sumi Muto (Japanese), Cynthia Martinez (English)) is recruited into the UN Space Army to fight in a war against a group of aliens called the Tarsians—named after the Tharsis region of Mars where they were first encountered. As a Special Agent, Mikako pilots a giant robotic mecha called a Tracer as part of a fighting squadron attached to the spacecraft carrier Lysithea. When the Lysithea leaves Earth to search for the Tarsians, Mikako's friend Noboru Terao (Makoto Shinkai (original Japanese), Chihiro Suzuki (Japanese), Adam Conlon (English)) remains on Earth. The two continue to communicate across space using the e-mail facilities on their mobile telephones. As the Lysithea travels deeper into space, messages take increasingly longer to reach Noboru on Earth, and the time-lag of their correspondence eventually spans years.
The narrative begins in 2047. Mikako is apparently alone in a hauntingly empty city, trying to contact people through her mobile telephone. She wakes up in her Tracer orbiting an extrasolar planet. She then goes to Agartha, the fictional fourth planet of the Sirius Solar System. Mikako sends an e-mail to Noboru (which shows the date 2047-09-16), with the subject "I am here", which would reach him eight years later. Some flashes of imagery, perhaps indicative of memory, a hallucination, or even a mystical encounter, are then shown. The room shown at the beginning of the animation is presented again; Mikako is squatting in the corner, sobbing and pleading with her doppelganger to let her see Noboru again so she can tell him she loves him.
The ship's alarm warns Mikako that the Tarsians are surrounding her, but she does not understand. A climactic battle ensues. On Earth, Noboru receives the message almost nine years later. At Agartha, three of the four carriers equipped with the warp engines which brought the expeditionary force to Sirius have been destroyed. The Lysithea is still intact after Mikako joins the fight and stops its destruction. After winning the battle, Mikako lets her damaged Tracer drift in space.
In the manga, 16-year-old Mikako sends a message to 25-year-old Noboru, telling him that she loves him. By this time, Noboru himself has joined the UN, which has launched a rescue mission for the Lysithea. When Mikako hears that the UN is sending help for their rescue, she consults a list of people on the mission, and finds that Noboru is among them. The manga ends with Mikako saying that they will definitely meet again.

documents.title: Tales from Earthsea
documents.tagline: Once Man and Dragon were one. Man chose Land and Sea, Dragon chose Wind and Fire.
documents.overview: Something bizarre has come over the land. The kingdom is deteriorating. People are beginning to act strange... What's even more strange is that people are beginning to see dragons, which shouldn't enter the world of humans. Due to all these bizarre events, Ged, a wandering wizard, is investigating the cause. During his journey, he meets Prince Arren, a young distraught teenage boy. While Arren may look like a shy young teen, he has a severe dark side, which grants him strength, hatred, ruthlessness and has no mercy, especially when it comes to protecting Teru. For the witch Kumo this is a perfect opportunity. She can use the boy's "fears" against the very one who would help him, Ged.
documents.plot:
Tales from Earthsea (Gedo Senki) is a 2006 Japanese animated epic fantasy produced by Studio Ghibli and distributed by Toho, marking the directorial debut of Gorō Miyazaki, who also co-wrote it. It draws on elements of the first four books of Ursula K. Le Guin's Earthsea series and on Hayao Miyazaki's illustrated story Shuna's Journey. The Japanese voice cast includes Junichi Okada as Prince Arren, Aoi Teshima as Therru, Bunta Sugawara as the archmage Sparrowhawk, Yūko Tanaka as the warlock Cob and Teruyuki Kagawa as the slaver Hare; the English dub features Timothy Dalton, Willem Dafoe and Cheech Marin.

Dragons fighting in the skies above a storm are taken as an omen that the world's balance is failing. In the kingdom of Enlad, where plague is spreading, young Prince Arren inexplicably kills his father the king, takes his sword and runs away. Rescued from wolves in the desert by the archmage Sparrowhawk, he travels with him to Hort Town, where he saves a girl, Therru, from the slaver Hare, only to be captured himself. Sparrowhawk frees him and brings him to the farm of his old friend Tenar, who has taken in Therru, a scarred girl abandoned by her parents. Sparrowhawk's meddling angers Cob, the sorcerer who rules Hort Town.

Arren admits to Therru what he has done and confesses that he feels something pursuing him, which turns out to be his own double. Fleeing it, he collapses in a swamp and is taken to Cob's castle, where the warlock learns his true name, Lebannen, and uses it to control him. Hare kidnaps Tenar to lure Sparrowhawk, who discovers that Cob is upsetting the balance by opening the door between life and death in pursuit of immortality. Sparrowhawk breaks Cob's hold over Arren but is captured. Therru meets Arren's double, the light within him, and learns his true name; she finds the despairing prince and restores his hope, sharing her own true name, Tehanu. Arren finally draws his sword, sealed by magic until then, and cuts off Cob's hand. The ageing warlock seizes Therru and strangles her atop a tower, but she is revealed to be an immortal dragon and destroys him. Arren returns home with Sparrowhawk to atone, promising to come back.

Released in July 2006, the film topped the Japanese box office for five weeks and was the year's highest-grossing domestic film, but reviews were mixed; it won the Bunshun Raspberry Award for worst film while earning a Japan Academy Prize nomination.

documents.title: Charlie St. Cloud
documents.tagline: Life is for living.
documents.overview: Accomplished sailor Charlie St. Cloud has the adoration of his mother Claire and his little brother Sam, as well as a college scholarship that will lead him far from his sleepy Pacific Northwest hometown. But his bright future is cut short when a tragedy strikes and takes his dreams with it. After his high-school classmate Tess returns home unexpectedly, Charlie grows torn between honoring a promise he made four years earlier and moving forward with newfound love. And as he finds the courage to let go of the past for good, Charlie discovers the soul most worth saving is his own.
documents.plot: Accomplished sailor Charlie St. Cloud has the adoration of his mother Claire and his little brother Sam, as well as a college scholarship that will lead him far from his sleepy Pacific Northwest hometown. documents.title: Immortals
documents.tagline: The Gods need a hero.
documents.overview: Theseus is a mortal man chosen by Zeus to lead the fight against the ruthless King Hyperion, who is on a rampage across Greece to obtain a weapon that can destroy humanity.
documents.plot:
Immortals is a 2011 American fantasy action film directed by Tarsem Singh and written by Krikor Oskanyan, Michael Robert Johnson, and Charles Randolf. The movie stars Henry Cavill, Mickey Rourke, Kellan Lutz, Stephen Dorff, and Isabel Lucas.

The story begins in ancient Greece, where the gods of Mount Olympus are at war with the Titans. The mortal king Hyperion (Mickey Rourke) is a powerful warrior who has been chosen by Zeus to lead the Olympian forces against the Titans. However, Hyperion's son Theseus (Henry Cavill), a young and inexperienced warrior, is destined for greatness.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Theseus is not just any ordinary mortal. He is the son of Zeus and a mortal woman, Aethera (Isabel Lucas). The gods have chosen Theseus to be their champion in the war against the Titans, and he is trained by the god Apollo (Stephen Dorff) to wield the powerful sword Excalibur.

Meanwhile, the Titan king Atlas (Danny Huston) has stolen Zeus's lightning bolt, which gives him immense power over the world. The gods are powerless without the lightning bolt, and they turn to Theseus for help. Theseus sets out on a perilous journey to reclaim the lightning bolt and defeat the Titans.

Along the way, Theseus meets the warrior Kael (Kellan Lutz), who becomes his ally in the battle against the Titans. Together, they face numerous challenges and obstacles as they journey through treacherous landscapes and fight off hordes of monstrous creatures.

As the story reaches its climax, Theseus and Kael finally reach Atlas's lair, where they engage in an epic battle with the Titan king. In the end, Theseus emerges victorious, but not without great cost. He kills Atlas and retrieves the lightning bolt, which he uses to defeat the remaining Titans and save the world.

However, the movie takes a dark turn as Theseus is forced to confront his own destiny. He realizes that he is destined for greatness, but at what cost? The movie ends with Theseus standing alone, having fulfilled his purpose but also losing himself in the process.

Throughout the movie, there are many themes and motifs that are woven throughout the story. One of the most prominent is the struggle between fate and free will. Theseus is forced to follow a predetermined path, but he also has the power to choose his own destiny. This theme is reflected in the character of Kael, who is initially hesitant to join Theseus on his quest.

The movie also explores the idea of identity and self-discovery. Theseus is a complex character who struggles to come to terms with his own identity. He is both mortal and god, human and divine. As he navigates the world of the gods, he must confront his own limitations and weaknesses.

Overall, Immortals is a visually stunning movie that features impressive action sequences and breathtaking cinematography. The story is engaging and suspenseful, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats. While it may not be perfect, the movie has its moments, and fans of fantasy and adventure will likely find it entertaining.

documents.title: Brown Sugar
documents.tagline: When did you first fall in love with hip-hop?
documents.overview: Friends since childhood, a magazine editor and a hip-hop record executive stumble into romantic territory.
documents.plot: Sidney and Dre can attribute their lifelong friendship and the launch of their careers to one single childhood instant... witnessing the birth of hip-hop on a New York street corner. Now some 15 years later, she is a revered music critic at a national magazine and he is a successful, though unfulfilled, hip-hop record company executive. Both come to realize that their true life passions will only be fulfilled by remembering what they learned that day on the corner.

documents.title: The Adjustment Bureau
documents.tagline: Fight for your fate.
documents.overview: A man glimpses the future Fate has planned for him – and chooses to fight for his own destiny. Battling the powerful Adjustment Bureau across, under and through the streets of New York, he risks his destined greatness to be with the only woman he's ever loved.
