documents.title: Normal
documents.overview: A deadly car accident brings together a group of previously unrelated people, each of whom is forced to deal with the emotional fallout.
documents.plot:
Normal is a 2007 Canadian drama directed by Carl Bessai about several unrelated people whose lives remain bound together by a deadly car crash. Carrie-Anne Moss, Kevin Zegers, Callum Keith Rennie and Andrew Airlie lead the ensemble cast, with Tygh Runyan in a supporting role. The film follows three families as they struggle, two years after the accident, to return to anything resembling a normal life.

The crash killed sixteen-year-old Nickie Reichert, who had been a passenger in one of the cars. His mother, Catherine, played by Moss, remains consumed by grief. She refuses to let anyone touch Nickie's belongings, which remain exactly where he left them, and her mourning leads her to neglect both her husband Dale and their younger son Brady, who has always lived in his brother's shadow and now feels invisible within his own family.

Walter Braugher, a college professor, was the driver of the other car. Although he had been drinking, he was found not criminally negligent, but he has been unable to escape his guilt or his self-doubt, which shows itself in his continued drinking. He has grown distant from his wife Abby and seeks comfort in a relationship with Sherri Banks, one of his students. Also in Walter's car that night was his brother Dennis, who is autistic and has been too frightened to leave his apartment ever since.

The third family is that of Jordie, Nickie's friend, who was driving the stolen car the two boys were riding in. Recently released from a youth detention center, where he served time for the theft, Jordie has become sullen and withdrawn. His father Carl, a psychotherapist, has never forgiven him, and the resentment has also damaged Carl's marriage to Jordie's stepmother Elise. Neglected by the people around them, Jordie and Elise both long to feel loved again. As the stories intersect, each character must confront what happened that night and search for a way to forgive others and themselves and move forward.

Normal earned significant recognition in Canada. Rennie won the Genie Award for Best Supporting Actor at the 29th Genie Awards for his performance, and the film was nominated for Best Motion Picture, losing to Passchendaele. It also won the award for Best Western Canadian Film at the 2007 Vancouver International Film Festival. The few reviews collected by Rotten Tomatoes were negative.

documents.title: Megamind
documents.tagline: His brain is off the chain.
documents.overview: Bumbling supervillain Megamind finally defeats his nemesis, the superhero Metro Man. But without a hero, he loses all purpose and must find new meaning to his life.
documents.plot:
Megamind is a 2010 American animated superhero comedy film produced by DreamWorks Animation. The movie follows the story of Megamind, a supervillain who was created by the scientist Dr. Minion.

The film begins with the introduction of Metro Man, a powerful superhero who saves the city of Metro City from various villains and disasters. However, when Metro Man is killed by his arch-nemesis, Titan, Megamind sees an opportunity to become the greatest hero the world has ever known. He decides to take on the mantle of Metro Man and becomes a supervillain.

Megamind's plan is to kill Metro City's mayor, Roxanne Ritchi, who he believes will be the perfect target for his evil plans. However, things don't go as planned when Megamind discovers that Roxanne is not only alive but also intelligent and resourceful. Despite this, Megamind continues with his plan, using his advanced technology to create a massive robot to destroy the city.

As the story unfolds, we see glimpses of Megamind's troubled past, where he was created by Dr. Minion as part of an experiment to create the perfect supervillain. However, things didn't go as planned, and Megamind ended up being rejected by his creator. This rejection led to a deep-seated insecurity in Megamind, which drives him to seek validation through his evil deeds.

Meanwhile, Roxanne Ritchi is introduced as a brilliant and feisty journalist who is determined to uncover the truth behind Metro Man's death. She teams up with Hal Stewart, a bumbling but lovable cop who becomes her partner in solving the mystery of Metro Man's demise.

As Megamind continues his plan to destroy the city, Roxanne and Hal begin to close in on him. However, just as they think they have finally caught him, Megamind reveals that he has been playing a cat-and-mouse game with them all along. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Titan, Metro Man's arch-nemesis, was actually the one who killed Metro Man.

In the end, Megamind and Roxanne team up to take down Titan, who has become increasingly unstable due to his own ego and desire for power. The movie culminates in an epic battle between Megamind, Roxanne, Hal, and Titan, with Megamind ultimately emerging victorious.

Throughout the film, we see a transformation in Megamind from a self-centered villain to a hero who has finally found redemption. With Roxanne by his side, Megamind learns to let go of his insecurities and find purpose beyond being a supervillain. The movie ends on a heartwarming note, with Megamind and Roxanne sharing a romantic moment as the city celebrates their victory over Titan.

Overall, Megamind is a hilarious and action-packed animated film that explores themes of identity, redemption, and the power of friendship. With its witty humor, lovable characters, and engaging storyline, it's no wonder why this movie has become a beloved classic among animation fans.

documents.title: Going the Distance
documents.tagline: A comedy about meeting each other halfway.
documents.overview: Erin and Garrett are very much in love. When Erin moves to San Francisco to finish her journalism degree and Garrett stays behind in New York to work in the music industry, they gamely keep the romance alive with webcams and frequent-flyer miles. But just when it seems the lovers will soon be reunited, they each score a big break that could separate them for good.
documents.plot:
Erin Langford is a graduate journalism student recently hired as a summer intern at a New York City newspaper. Out with a friend at a bar, she meets Garrett, who interrupts her game of Centipede. They drink together and end up at his place, where they smoke marijuana and have sex while Garrett's roommate Dan "DJs their hook up". The next morning, before she can leave, Erin agrees to have breakfast with him. Telling him she is only in the city for six weeks, they agree to keep it casual.
Erin and Garrett soon develop feelings for each other, and she tries to get a permanent position at the paper. Before the end of her internship, she writes a well-received article and is told to contact them in January regarding possible job openings. Working for a record label, Garrett is assigned to manage a band he dislikes, and he begins to hate his job.
When Erin's six weeks are over, she and Garrett find it difficult to let go. After driving her to the airport and saying goodbye, Garrett runs after her, admitting that he is crazy about her and wants to have a long-distance relationship, to which she agrees.
Over the following months, Erin and Garrett spend their free time trying to figure out when they can see each other. He gives her a surprise visit on Thanksgiving. After an emotional reunion, they go to Erin's sister Corinne's house, where she is staying, and start to have passionate sex on the dining room table. Unbeknownst to them, Erin's brother-in-law Phil is having dinner at the table in the dark, and Corinne walks in on the awkward scene. The next day, they see The Boxer Rebellion perform, but Garrett is jealous Erin is friends with Damon, a handsome bartender, and eventually has to return to NYC.
In January, Erin calls her former boss, but they are not hiring. Unable to find comfort in a phone conversation with Garrett, she gets drunk with Damon and almost kisses him, but goes home. Her professor recommends her for a position at the San Francisco Chronicle and she goes for an interview. Garrett tries to have phone sex with Erin, but it ends up being awkward, leaving both feeling ridiculous.
A month later, while Erin is packing for a weekend in NYC, she gets a call from the Chronicle and is offered the job. Upon arriving in New York, she tells Garrett about the job offer, blindsiding him with the news. Their happy reunion quickly devolves into a fight, causing Erin to spend the first night of her trip at a friend's.
They make up the next day, and he calls her a week later saying he wants her to move to NYC, live together and start afresh. She agrees, but while visiting San Francisco to sort things out, a conversation with Corinne makes Garrett realize he should not be the reason Erin turns down the job, and they part ways after an emotional conversation and a long hug at the airport.
Six months later, Erin's career is going well, having written her first front-page story.

documents.title: Just Wright
documents.tagline: In this game every shot counts.
documents.overview: A physical therapist falls for the basketball player she is helping recover from a career-threatening injury.
documents.plot: Physical therapist Leslie Wright lands the dream job of working with basketball superstar Scott McKnight, helping him recover from a career-threatening injury. All goes well and soon Leslie finds herself falling in love with him. Just as their friendship deepens, however, Scott focuses his attention back on his tenuous relationship with his ex-fiancé Morgan, Leslie's gorgeous godsister, who would love to be the basketball player's trophy wife.

documents.title: Beastly
documents.tagline: Love is never ugly.
documents.overview: A modern-day take on the "Beauty and the Beast" tale where a New York teen is transformed into a hideous monster in order to find true love.
documents.plot:
Kyle Kingson is the arrogant and vain son of news anchor Rob Kingson. After he bullies Kendra Hilferty, not knowing she is a witch, for defacing his pictures, she transforms him into a bald, scarred, heavily tattooed shell of his former self. She warns Kyle that he will remain altered for the rest of his life, unless he finds someone who loves him by the next spring. Kyle is taken to live in a private house with their maid Zola Davies and his blind tutor Will. Both are comforts to Kyle when his father, unable to deal with his transformation, has abandoned him.
As spring nears, Kyle finds himself infatuated with Lindy Taylor, a former classmate he had avoided. He rescues her drug-addicted father from two dealers, fatally shooting one; the other vows to kill Lindy. Kyle persuades Lindy's father to allow her to move in with him. At first, Kyle uses a false identity and introduces himself as Hunter. He also refuses to see Lindy and hides from her, which angers her to the point that she stops speaking to him. Kyle eventually reveals his face and the two begin to warm up to each other. Kyle writes a letter professing his love for Lindy but does not give it to her for fear of rejection. He visits Kendra to plead for more time; she states the spell cannot be undone, but agrees to restore Will's vision and grant green cards to Zola's three children in Jamaica if he gets Lindy to fall in love with him. Seeing his apparent change of heart, she bids him good luck.
The surviving drug dealer lands in jail. Kyle and Lindy visit Lindy's hospitalized father, who overdosed. Kyle gives her the letter but regrets it when she tells him she considers him a good friend. Lindy calls him after reading the letter, but a heartbroken Kyle does not answer the phone. Persuaded by Will and Zola, Kyle goes to meet Lindy one last time before she leaves on a school trip to Machu Picchu. Kyle tells her to go, but as she leaves, Lindy tells him that she loves him, breaking the curse. Kyle's former self is restored but Lindy does not recognize him and tries to call Hunter but Kyle's phone rings instead. When Lindy realizes what happened, the two share a passionate kiss on the side of the street.
After the curse is lifted, Will wakes up with the ability to see and Zola receives the green cards. An intern (implied to be Kendra) approaches Rob Kingson's office.
An alternate ending was filmed, in which Lindy gets kidnapped by the drug dealer and Kyle is shot while saving her. As he lies injured in her arms, she confesses her love to him, breaking the curse in a fashion more closely based on the book and the original Beauty and the Beast story. This ending was not used in the official release.

documents.title: 5 Centimeters per Second
documents.tagline: At what speed must I live to see you again?
documents.overview: Three moments in Takaki's life: his relationship with Akari and their forced separation; his friendship with Kanae, who is secretly in love with him; the demands and disappointments of adulthood, an unhappy life in a cold city.
documents.plot:
The story is set in Japan, beginning in the early 1990s up until the present day (2008), with each act centered on a boy named Takaki Tōno.

In 1991, Takaki Tōno quickly befriends Akari Shinohara after she transfers to his elementary school in Tokyo. They grow close due to shared interests, such as preferring to stay inside during recess due to their seasonal allergies. Takaki and Akari refer to each other using their given names without honorifics, which is an indicator of close friendship and intimacy in Japanese culture.

Shortly after graduating from elementary school in 1994, Akari moves to the nearby prefecture of Tochigi due to her parents' jobs. The two keep in touch by writing letters but eventually drift apart. When Takaki learns that his family will move to Kagoshima in 1995, he decides to meet with Akari one last time since they will be too far apart to see each other once he moves. He also writes a letter for Akari confessing his feelings for her. However, Takaki loses the letter during the journey and a severe snowstorm delays his train for several hours.
Late that night, Takaki finally arrives at Iwafune Station, and the two lovers share their first kiss under a cherry tree. At that moment, Takaki realizes they will never be together. They spend the night in a nearby shed due to the snowstorm. The next morning, Akari sees Takaki off at the train station, and the two promise to continue writing to each other. As the train departs, Takaki concludes that the loss of his letter is not important anymore after their kiss, while Akari looks at her own letter addressed to Takaki, which she decided not to give him.

In 1999, Takaki is in the third year of senior high in Tanegashima, home to the Tanegashima Space Center. Kanae Sumida, a classmate of Takaki, has loved him ever since first meeting him in middle school but has never had the courage to confess her feelings to him. She tries to spend as much time with him as she can. However, Takaki seems oblivious to Kanae's feelings and treats her as a good friend. Kanae notices that Takaki is always writing emails to someone and staring off into the distance. It is revealed that Takaki's emails are never sent to anyone, and he deletes them afterwards. He also has recurring dreams of Akari.
One evening, as Kanae prepares to confess her love to Takaki, a rocket is launched into the sky, and they both gaze up at it. Kanae realizes that Takaki is looking for something far beyond what she can offer and decides not to confess her feelings, though she believes she will always love him. With such thoughts, she cries herself to sleep.

In 2008, Takaki is a programmer in Tokyo, and Akari is preparing to marry another man. Takaki still longs for Akari to the detriment of his lifestyle. He receives a call from his current girlfriend but does not answer, signifying the end of the relationship. Depressed, Takaki quits his job as he is unable to cope with his feelings for Akari.

documents.title: Eat Pray Love
documents.tagline: Let Yourself GO
documents.overview: Liz Gilbert had everything a modern woman is supposed to dream of having – a husband, a house and a successful career – yet like so many others, she found herself lost, confused and searching for what she really wanted in life. Newly divorced and at a crossroads, Gilbert steps out of her comfort zone, risking everything to change her life, embarking on a journey around the world that becomes a quest for self-discovery. In her travels, she discovers the true pleasure of nourishment by eating in Italy, the power of prayer in India and, finally and unexpectedly, the inner peace and balance of true love in Bali.
documents.plot: A married woman realizes how unhappy her marriage really is, and that her life needs to go in a different direction. After a painful divorce, she takes off on a round-the-world journey to "find herself".

documents.title: Unthinkable
documents.tagline: Right and Wrong no longer exist
documents.overview: The government gets wind of a plot to destroy America involving a trio of nuclear weapons for which the whereabouts are unknown. It's up to a seasoned interrogator and an FBI agent to find out exactly where the nukes are.
documents.plot: The government gets wind of a plot to destroy America involving a trio of nuclear weapons for which the whereabouts are unknown. It's up to a seasoned interrogator and an FBI agent to find out exactly where the nukes are.

documents.title: Undisputed III: Redemption
documents.tagline: One deadly tournament. Last fight for freedom.
documents.overview: Russian inmate Boyka, now severely hobbled by the knee injury suffered at the end of Undisputed 2. No longer the feared prison fighter he was, he has declined so far that he is now good only for cleaning toilets. But when a new prison fight tournament begins - an international affair, matching the best fighters from prisons around the globe, enticing them with the promise of freedom for the winner - Boyka must reclaim his dignity and fight for his position in the tournament.
documents.plot:
Undisputed III: Redemption is a 2010 American martial arts action film directed by Isaac Florentine, the sequel to Undisputed II: Last Man Standing and the third installment in the Undisputed franchise. Scott Adkins reprises his role as the Russian prison fighter Yuri Boyka, with Mykel Shannon Jenkins as Turbo, Mark Ivanir as Gaga, Hristo Shopov as Warden Kuss and Marko Zaror as the Colombian fighter Dolor. It was released direct-to-video in 2010.

Years after his defeat by George "Iceman" Chambers, Boyka has been reduced to working as a janitor in a Russian prison, his knee badly damaged. When he hears about the Prison Spetz Competition, an international tournament between prison fighters that offers the winner a chance at freedom, he trains in secret to rehabilitate his knee, shaves off his long hair and beard, and challenges the reigning Russian champion, defeating him to win the right to represent his country.

At the brutal Gorgon prison in Georgia, Boyka joins fighters from around the world under the cruel Warden Kuss. The prisoners are forced to labor in a quarry, while the Colombian favorite, Raul "Dolor" Quiñones, receives special treatment and performance-enhancing drugs. Boyka initially clashes with the brash American fighter Turbo, but the two gradually develop mutual respect and begin training together. Boyka discovers that the tournament is rigged for profit in Dolor's favor, organized by a syndicate that includes the mobster Gaga and his associate Farnatti. As the competition proceeds and Boyka and Turbo advance alongside Dolor and the Brazilian Rodrigo Silva, they learn that defeated fighters are taken away and executed. When the organizers decide to eliminate the remaining fighters, Boyka and Turbo must not only fight for their lives in the ring but also find a way to escape, leading to Boyka's climactic final bout against Dolor despite his injuries.

Undisputed III received positive reviews from martial-arts fans and critics, who praised its elaborate fight choreography, Adkins's acrobatic performance and Florentine's direction, and it is often regarded as one of the best direct-to-video action films of its era. Its success led to a further sequel, Boyka: Undisputed, in 2016.

documents.title: You Again
documents.tagline: What doesn't kill you... is going to marry your brother.
documents.overview: History -- make that high school -- may repeat itself when Marni learns that Joanna, the mean girl from her past, is set to be her sister-in-law. Before the wedding bells toll, Marni must show her brother that a tiger doesn't change its stripes. On Marni's side is her mother, while Joanna's backed by her wealthy aunt.
documents.plot:
You Again is a 2010 American comedy directed by Andy Fickman and written by Moe Jelline. Kristen Bell stars as a young woman who discovers that her brother is marrying her high school tormentor, with Jamie Lee Curtis, Sigourney Weaver, Odette Yustman, James Wolk, Victor Garber, Kristin Chenoweth and Betty White in supporting roles. It was released by Touchstone Pictures on September 24, 2010.

In 2002, in the fictional town of Ridgefield, California, the awkward teenager Marni Olsen is relentlessly bullied by the popular girl JJ, while her brother Will, the school's basketball star, remains oblivious, even when JJ humiliates Marni during an important game. Eight years later, Marni has become a successful public relations executive in Los Angeles and has just been promoted to her firm's New York office. She returns home for Will's wedding to a woman named Joanna, whom she has never met, and is horrified to discover that Joanna is JJ. Her family adores the bride-to-be, who appears not to remember Marni at all, and Marni sets out to expose what she believes is an act.

The rivalry soon spreads to the older generation. Joanna's aunt Ramona, played by Weaver, wealthy and glamorous, turns out to have been the high school best friend turned nemesis of Marni and Will's mother Gail, played by Curtis. As the wedding approaches, the two mothers revive their decades-old feud, competing for attention with escalating one-upmanship, while Marni's wisecracking grandmother Bunny, played by White, offers commentary from the sidelines. Marni's attempts to reveal Joanna's past lead to a series of disasters and alienate her from her brother. Eventually both pairs of women confront the old wounds behind their rivalries, Joanna faces up to her past behavior, and apologies lead to reconciliation in time for the wedding.

The film was panned by critics, many of whom found its premise thin despite its talented cast, though some enjoyed its slapstick, musical numbers and surprise cameos. It opened at number five and grossed about $32 million worldwide against a $20 million budget. It was Betty White's last live-action feature film role before her death in 2021.

documents.title: Zookeeper
documents.tagline: Welcome to his jungle.
documents.overview: Kindhearted Griffin Keyes is one of the best-loved caretakers at the Franklin Park Zoo, but since he is more comfortable with the animals than with females of his own species, his love life is lacking. When Griffin decides that the only way to get a girlfriend is to find a more-glamorous career, the animals panic. To keep him from leaving, they reveal their secret ability to talk and offer to teach him the rules of courtship, animal-style.
documents.plot: Kindhearted Griffin Keyes is one of the best-loved caretakers at the Franklin Park Zoo, but he's more comfortable with the animals than with females of his own species as proven by his failed marriage proposal to the self-absorbed Stephanie several years ago. The animals have listened to Griffin pine over her for years and, after she reappears in his life, they decide to help Griffin rekindle the relationship and become the alpha male she wants him to be. They inadvertently reveal their secret ability to talk and, after Griffin's initial shock, teach him the rules of courtship, animal-style. Surprisingly, the animals' advice really works and Griffin is about to get everything he's ever dreamed of--or is he?

documents.title: Your Highness
documents.tagline: Get your quest on.
documents.overview: A fantasy movie about an arrogant, lazy prince and his more heroic brother who must complete a quest in order to save their father's kingdom.
documents.plot:
Your Highness is a 2011 American stoner comedy fantasy film directed by David Gordon Green and written by Danny McBride and Ben Best. McBride stars alongside James Franco, Natalie Portman, Zooey Deschanel and Justin Theroux in a sword-and-sorcery parody about an idle prince forced to join his heroic brother on a quest. Universal Pictures released it on April 8, 2011.

In the Kingdom of Mourne, King Tallious has two sons: the dashing and accomplished Fabious and the lazy, cowardly Thadeous. Returning from a victorious campaign against the evil sorcerer Leezar, Fabious brings home Princess Belladonna, whom he has rescued from a tower and intends to marry. Thadeous, named best man, skips the wedding after overhearing Fabious's Knights Elite mocking him. Leezar crashes the ceremony, revealing that he was the one who imprisoned Belladonna, and abducts her again. The king gives Thadeous an ultimatum: help his brother rescue the princess or be banished.

Accompanied by Thadeous's servant and friend Courtney, the brothers consult the Great Wize Wizard, who explains that Leezar intends to fulfill a prophecy by mating with a virgin when two moons converge, siring a dragon that will let him conquer the kingdom. Leezar can be stopped only with the Blade of Unicorn, hidden in a labyrinth, to which a magic compass will lead them. On the road they discover that Fabious's servant Julie is spying for Leezar and that the Knights Elite have defected to him. Captured by a tribe of wild women and forced to fight in an arena by the warlord Marteetee, they are rescued by Isabel, a warrior seeking vengeance for the murder of her family. When Isabel steals the compass and Fabious sets off alone in disgust, only to be captured by Leezar's men, Thadeous at last rises to the occasion. Teaming up with Isabel, he enters the labyrinth, slays a minotaur and claims the Blade. The companions storm Leezar's castle and free Fabious, who kills the sorcerer before he can carry out the ritual. Fabious marries Belladonna, and Isabel returns to declare her love for Thadeous, inviting him on a new quest.

Your Highness was a commercial failure, grossing about $28 million worldwide against a reported $50 million budget, and was poorly reviewed; Rotten Tomatoes reports 27% approval, its consensus judging its scatological humor monotonous despite its lavish production. Franco later mocked the film himself.

documents.title: Priest
documents.tagline: The War is Eternal. His Mission is Just the Beginning.
documents.overview: In an alternate world, humanity and vampires have warred for centuries. After the last Vampire War, the veteran Warrior Priest lives in obscurity with other humans inside one of the Church's walled cities. When the Priest's niece is kidnapped by vampires, the Priest breaks his vows to hunt them down. He is accompanied by the niece's boyfriend, who is a wasteland sheriff, and a former Warrior Priestess.
documents.plot:
Priest is a 2011 American action horror film directed by Scott Stewart and written by Cory Goodman, loosely adapted from the Korean comic by Hyung Min-woo. Paul Bettany stars as a nameless warrior priest, with Karl Urban as the villain Black Hat, Cam Gigandet as the sheriff Hicks, Maggie Q as Priestess, Lily Collins as Lucy Pace, Stephen Moyer and Mädchen Amick as Owen and Shannon Pace, and Christopher Plummer as Monsignor Orelas.

In an alternate world, centuries of war between humans and vampires have left the surface ravaged and humanity ruled by an authoritarian Church from walled cities. The war was won by the Priests, an order of elite warriors, after which the surviving vampires were confined to reservations and the Priests were cast aside. Hicks, the sheriff of a frontier town, brings Priest word that vampires have killed Shannon, mortally wounded Owen and kidnapped Lucy, whom Hicks loves. When Orelas refuses to reinstate him, Priest defies him and leaves the city, and the Church sends other Priests and a Priestess after him.

At a vampire reservation Priest and Hicks learn that the creatures have gathered in the hive of Sola Mira, supposedly abandoned since the war. There Priestess joins them rather than bring Priest back, and together they destroy a monstrous guardian and find that the vampires have bred a new army. Arriving at the town of Jericho, they find it emptied and the pursuing Priests crucified by a band led by Black Hat, a human who rides an armored train by day to strike towns at night, with the cities as his ultimate goal. Priestess reveals that Lucy is actually Priest's daughter. On the train Priest learns that Black Hat is his former comrade, captured at Sola Mira and given the vampire queen's blood to become a hybrid immune to sunlight. When the detonator is destroyed, Priestess rides a motorcycle loaded with explosives into the engine, and the derailment kills Black Hat and the vampires. Priest returns to warn the disbelieving Church that the war is not over, then sets out with Priestess to rally the other Priests.

Released in May 2011, the film was largely panned, with a 16% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it sleek but dull and derivative, and a Metacritic score of 41.

documents.title: Transformers: Dark of the Moon
documents.tagline: The invasion we always feared. An enemy we never expected.
documents.overview: The Autobots continue to work for NEST, now no longer in secret. But after discovering a strange artifact during a mission in Chernobyl, it becomes apparent to Optimus Prime that the United States government has been less than forthright with them.
documents.plot:
Transformers: Dark of the Moon is a 2011 science fiction action film directed by Michael Bay and produced by Steven Spielberg, Don Murphy, Tom DeSanto, and Lorenzo di Bonaventura. The movie is the third installment in the live-action Transformers film series.

The story begins with Sam Witwicky (Shia LaBeouf), now a college student, who is struggling to find his place in the world after the events of the previous films. He is haunted by nightmares and feels disconnected from his friends and family. Meanwhile, Optimus Prime (Peter Cullen) has been searching for the AllSpark, a powerful energy source that could bring about peace between humans and Autobots.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when the Decepticons, led by Megatron (Hugo Weaving), launch a surprise attack on Chicago, targeting the White House. The Autobots, including Optimus Prime, Bumblebee (Kevin Dunn), and Jazz (Dax Shepard), arrive to defend the city, but they are vastly outnumbered.

As the battle rages on, Sam discovers that the Decepticons' plan is to use the AllSpark to awaken Megatron from his slumber. The Autobots are unable to stop the Decepticons, and Optimus Prime is mortally wounded in the process.

With the help of Carly Spencer (Rosie Huntington-Whiteley), a new love interest for Sam, he discovers that the AllSpark has been hidden within the White House. However, it's too late, as Megatron awakens and begins to wreak havoc on the city.

In a desperate attempt to stop Megatron, Optimus Prime sacrifices himself by using his own energy to destroy the AllSpark, which in turn destroys the Decepticon leader. The Autobots are able to defeat the remaining Decepticons, but not before they suffer heavy losses.

The movie concludes with Sam and Carly sharing a moment of connection, as Sam finally finds his place in the world. The film ends on a hopeful note, with Optimus Prime's spirit watching over Sam and the city, symbolizing the beginning of a new era of peace between humans and Autobots.

Throughout the movie, Michael Bay's signature style is evident, with fast-paced action sequences, stunning visual effects, and a pulsating soundtrack. The film received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $1 billion worldwide.

documents.title: Morning Glory
documents.tagline: Breakfast TV just got interesting.
documents.overview: A young and devoted morning television producer is hired as an executive producer on a  long-running morning show at a once-prominent but currently failing station in New York City. Eager to keep the show on air, she recruits a former news journalist and anchor who disapproves of co-hosting a show that does not deal with real news stories.
documents.plot:
Aspiring news producer Becky Fuller is laid off from her job at Good Morning, New Jersey. Her mother advises she pursue another career, but Becky perseveres; IBS News, seeking a producer for its struggling national morning show, DayBreak, calls Becky for an interview.
During a job interview at IBS News, executive Jerry Barnes bluntly dismisses Becky's credentials and characterizes DayBreak as a lost cause. After this discouraging interview, she shares an elevator with veteran television journalist Mike Pomeroy, who coldly brushes off her expressions of admiration for his career achievements. Despite his initial doubts, Jerry reluctantly hires Becky as DayBreak's executive producer, prompting her move to New York City.
On her first day, Becky finds the show in turmoil, lacking both clear direction and funding. After meeting the sharp-witted, long-suffering co-host Colleen Peck, Becky fires Colleen's lecherous on-air partner, Paul McVee, to the delight of the crew. Seeking a prominent replacement, she discovers a clause in Mike Pomeroy's contract that requires him to accept a formal job offer or forfeit his salary. By invoking this clause, Becky forces the unwilling, underutilized veteran journalist to become Colleen's new co-host.
Becky meets Adam Bennett, a fellow IBS producer who had previously worked with the difficult Pomeroy on other programs. They begin dating, and he initially supports her dedication to her job. Contemptuous of morning television, Mike tries to sabotage his DayBreak debut by getting drunk. He refuses to banter, rejects segments he feels are beneath him, and antagonizes Colleen.
Jerry informs Becky that IBS wants to cancel DayBreak, blaming her for the show's dwindling viewership. After a heated confrontation with Mike, she takes a radical approach. Persuading Jerry to give her the show's remaining six weeks to revitalize ratings, Becky sends Ernie, DayBreak's weatherman, on stunts such as riding roller coasters and skydiving.
Colleen joins Becky's campaign to rejuvenate the show, appearing in colorful segments that increase the show's ratings, but Jerry remains unconvinced. Adam, not realizing what is on the line, claims she is too caught up in improving the ratings. Seeing this as the type of criticism she has heard from other men, Becky walks out.
With the six-week deadline approaching, Mike surprisingly insists on covering an obscure sauerkraut festival. Becky accompanies him but soon realizes that their true destination is the Governor's summer estate. Despite her warnings that the show will be canceled, Mike confronts the Governor on charges of racketeering, breaking the story of his arrest on live television. Afterward, Mike confides in Becky, explaining that his own historical overcommitment to his career came at the expense of his family and personal life.
The on-air arrest spikes DayBreak's ratings enough to secure another year for the show and Becky receives a job offer from the Today show.

documents.title: The Last Exorcism
documents.tagline: Believe In Him.
documents.overview: After years of performing “exorcisms” and taking believers’ money, Reverend Marcus travels to rural Louisiana with a film crew so he can dispel what he believes is the myth of demonic possession. The dynamic reverend is certain that this will be another routine “exorcism” on a disturbed religious fanatic but instead comes upon the blood-soaked farm of the Sweetzer family and a true evil he would have never thought imaginable.

documents.title: Grown Ups
documents.tagline: Boys will be boys. . . some longer than others.
documents.overview: After their high school basketball coach passes away, five good friends and former teammates reunite for a Fourth of July holiday weekend.
documents.plot:
Grown Ups is a 2010 American comedy film directed by Dennis Dugan and written by Adam Sandler, Fred Wolf, and Tim Herlihy. The movie stars Adam Sandler, Kevin James, Chris Rock, David Spade, Rob Schneider, and Salma Hayek.

The story begins with Lenny Feder (Adam Sandler), a wealthy and successful businessman who is married to Roxanne Chase-Feder (Salma Hayek). They have two children, but their marriage has become stale due to the lack of intimacy. Lenny's friends from high school, including Eric Lamonsoff (Kevin James), Kurt McKenzie (Chris Rock), Marcus Higgins (David Spade), and Rob Hilliard (Rob Schneider), are all going through similar midlife crises.

The group decides to take a trip together to Central America for their friend's 40th birthday party. However, things quickly go awry when they discover that the party is actually a funeral for their old high school friend, who died in a tragic accident. The group is forced to confront their past and re-evaluate their lives.

Upon arrival at the funeral, Lenny realizes that he has lost touch with his friends and that they have all become more like family than friends. He decides to take matters into his own hands and organize a backyard barbecue for the group's 40th birthday party, which becomes an opportunity for them to reconnect and reminisce about old times.

As the party progresses, Lenny's marriage is put to the test when Roxanne discovers that he has been having an affair with a younger woman. The group rallies around Lenny, offering their support and advice, but ultimately, it's up to Lenny to make things right with his wife.

Throughout the movie, the characters' relationships are put to the test as they navigate love, friendship, and growing older. In the end, Lenny learns a valuable lesson about the importance of family and friendship, and he makes amends with Roxanne. The movie ends on a heartwarming note, with the group celebrating their 40th birthdays together and looking forward to many more years of friendship.

Overall, Grown Ups is a lighthearted and entertaining comedy that explores themes of friendship, love, and growing older. With its talented ensemble cast and witty dialogue, it's no wonder why this movie became a box office hit.

documents.title: Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives
documents.original_title: ลุงบุญมีระลึกชาติ
documents.overview: Suffering from acute kidney failure, Boonmee has chosen to spend his final days surrounded by his loved ones in the countryside. Surprisingly, the ghost of his deceased wife appears to care for him, and his long lost son returns home in a non-human form. Contemplating the reasons for his illness, Boonmee treks through the jungle with his family to a mysterious hilltop cave—the birthplace of his first life.
documents.plot:
Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives (Thai: Lung Bunmi Raluek Chat) is a 2010 Thai fantasy drama written, produced and directed by Apichatpong Weerasethakul. It stars Thanapat Saisaymar as Boonmee, a farmer in his final days, with Jenjira Pongpas as his sister-in-law Jen, Sakda Kaewbuadee as his nephew Tong, Natthakarn Aphaiwong as the ghost of his wife Huay and Jeerasak Kulhong as his lost son Boonsong. The film was the final part of Primitive, a multi-platform art project by the director, and is steeped in ideas of reincarnation and memory.

Boonmee, who is dying of kidney failure, lives on his farm in northeastern Thailand with Jen and Tong, cared for by his Laotian assistant Jaai, who gives him dialysis. One evening at dinner, Huay, who died more than a decade earlier, quietly materializes at the table, having heard the prayers said for her. Soon a hairy figure with glowing red eyes joins them: Boonsong, who vanished years earlier after becoming obsessed with a creature he had photographed, a monkey ghost, and who has since mated with one and taken on its form.

The family accepts these visitors with calm and curiosity. Boonmee wonders whether his illness is the result of karma, a consequence of killing communists while serving in the army and of killing insects on his farm. Interwoven with these scenes is a mysterious episode about a princess who, seeing a more beautiful version of herself reflected in a forest pool, gives herself to a talking catfish. As death approaches, Huay leads Boonmee, Jen and Tong through the jungle at night to a cave, where Boonmee senses he was born in a past life he cannot remember, and he recounts a dream of a future in which people from the past are made to disappear.

Unfolding at a slow, meditative pace, the film blends folklore, Buddhist belief, political memory and the history of cinema itself, and was partly inspired by a 1983 book by the Buddhist abbot Phra Sripariyattiweti about a man who could recall his past lives.

Uncle Boonmee premiered at the 2010 Cannes Film Festival, where it won the Palme d'Or, the first Thai film to do so. It was released in the United States by Strand Releasing in March 2011. It received near-universal acclaim, with 90 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 87, and is regarded by many critics as one of the greatest films ever made.
production_companies: Foundation for Art and Creative Technology (FACT)

documents.title: Life As We Know It
documents.tagline: A comedy about taking it one step at a time.
documents.overview: After a distastrous first date for caterer Holly and network sports director Messer, all they have is common is a dislike for each other and their love for their goddaughter Sophie. But when they suddenly become all Sophie has in this world, Holly and Messer must set their differences aside. Juggling careers and social calendars, they'll have to find common ground while living under the same roof.
documents.plot:
Holly Berenson is the owner of a small Atlanta bakery, and Eric Messer is a promising television technical sports director for the Atlanta Hawks. Their best friends, Peter and Alison, set them up on a blind date that goes horribly wrong and results in both hating each other with a passion.
As the years go by, Peter and Alison get married and have a baby girl named Sophie. They also select Holly and Eric – who teasingly tolerate each other – as the godparents.
Shortly after Sophie's first birthday, Peter and Alison are killed in a car crash. Holly and Eric learn that their friends named them Sophie's joint guardians. After discovering that none of Peter and Alison's relatives are fit to take care of Sophie, the two put their differences aside and move into Sophie's home.
Living together proves to be a struggle. One evening, Holly is away at an important catering job when Eric is given the opportunity to direct a big basketball game. He takes Sophie with him, but her crying distracts him, leading to him making a big mistake on the broadcast. When they get home, Eric and Holly argue, but later they make up.
Holly goes on a date with Sam, Sophie's pediatrician. The date is cut short when Eric calls to tell Sam that Sophie has a high fever. When they join him at the hospital, Eric sees Holly kiss Sam.
Over time, the guardians discover that raising a child is more expensive than they had expected, so Holly can no longer afford to expand her business. Eric helps by investing in her company. They cement the new relationship by going on a date, which ends with them having sex and developing strong feelings.
Their Child Protective Services caseworker Janine tells them they must make a firm commitment, either to stay together, or break up, as waffling in between would be bad for Sophie. Eric is offered his dream job with the Phoenix Suns, and does not discuss it with Holly. When she finds out, she tells him to take the job, accusing him of looking for a way out of raising Sophie.
At Thanksgiving break, Eric returns from Phoenix for a visit, hoping to patch things up with Holly. She invites him to a dinner that she and Sam are hosting for neighbors and friends. Eric and Holly argue loudly when he learns she is planning to sell the house soon, as the upkeep is too costly. She accuses him of deserting her and Sophie, while he points out how quickly she replaced him.
Eric tells Holly he loves her, but leaves the dinner, planning to return to Phoenix. Once alone with Holly, Sam says that if he and his former wife had fought the way that Eric and she did, they would still be together. He tells Holly to work out her feelings for Eric, and leaves. That night, Sophie calls Holly "Mama" for the first time.
Janine visits to make her final determination whether Holly and Eric are fit parents. Holly realizes that she cannot take care of Sophie without Eric, and that she loves him.

documents.title: Ondine
documents.tagline: The truth is not what you know. It's what you believe.
documents.overview: An Irish fisherman discovers a woman in his fishing net believing her to be a mermaid.
documents.plot:
Syracuse, uncomfortably called "Circus" by some, is trawling on his boat and finds a scantily clad young woman caught in his net. He sees she is alive and resuscitates her. She calls herself Ondine and refuses to be taken to the hospital, not wanting to be seen by anyone else. He shelters her in a caravan house that belonged to his late mother in a quiet harbor, which makes him late for picking up his daughter Annie who uses a wheelchair and lives with his ex-wife Maura. During Annie's dialysis, he tells her a story about a fisherman that catches a woman out of the sea. Annie explains the woman could be a magical selkie.
Annie receives a new powerchair from the CRC, and upon returning home is greeted by Maura's boyfriend Alex. Maura flips off Syracuse for missing the doctor who had news on a kidney match for Annie.
Next morning, Syracuse finds Ondine washing clothes in a stream, singing in an unknown language. She follows him on his boat to work that day. He pulls up only empty lobster pots until Ondine starts singing, after which every pot contains a catch. Still not wanting to be seen, Ondine refuses to follow Syracuse to the fish market where the lobsters are sold. He buys a dress and lies to the store clerk that it's for Annie when she grows up.
When Syracuse picks up Annie from her school, he continues the fisherman story by explaining how the woman sings to the fish for him to catch, a song in a language he has never heard before. Annie states that Selk is the language of the selkie. Syracuse stammers that his lobsters hear her sing, which makes Annie curious as to whose story this is, and she secretly follows him to the caravan. When Syracuse asks how long she will stay, Ondine says it is up to him. He happily replies forever and happily ever after, like the fairytale he has been building with Annie, who watches them without being noticed.
Annie is seen back home studying all her new library books on seals and selkies. Alex says selkies are Scottish creatures, but the one Annie saw is not.
Syracuse regularly torments the local priest in confession because there aren't any AA meetings in town. He recalls a recurring nightmare where he is at Alex's funeral and reunited with Maura, still with her drinking problem. As the priest pushes the subject away, Syracuse reveals he pulled a woman out of the water with his net and kept her, reminding the priest he can't tell anyone.
Ondine is shown alone, tidying up the caravan, then tries her new clothing as if the experience was a first, especially when she stretches leggings over one splayed hand so it looks webbed.
The next day, Annie sees Ondine swimming and approaches her on the dock. They bond as Annie tells her about selkies and ostensibly Ondine herself, which Ondine goes along with, kissing Annie goodbye before the child goes back to her mother. Syracuse goes in the library asking for books about selkies, but discovers that Annie took them all.

documents.title: The Divide
documents.tagline: The lucky ones died in the blast
documents.overview: Survivors of a nuclear attack are grouped together for days in the basement of their apartment building, where fear and dwindling supplies wear away at their dynamic.

documents.title: The Disappearance of Alice Creed
documents.tagline: Where is Alice Creed?
documents.overview: A rich man's daughter is held captive in an abandoned apartment by two former convicts who abducted her and hold her ransom in exchange for her father's money.
documents.plot:
Criminals Vic and Danny kidnap a woman named Alice Creed, the only child of a wealthy family. In a secured room, they forcibly strip her of all her clothes, handcuff her to a bed, and gag her – all while wearing jumpsuits and ski masks themselves. After taking pictures of her they put a tracksuit on her and a hood over her head. The men leave to dispose of all three's clothes and send the pictures to Alice's father for ransom. The men refuse to let her out of her shackles, even to go to the toilet, seemingly just to embarrass her. Neither shows emotion while humiliating Alice, but Vic mocks Danny for being less calm.
Vic leaves to make preparations, whilst Danny guards Alice. Alice persuades Danny to uncuff her, then grabs his pistol and fires a warning shot. To keep from being shot, Danny removes his ski mask and reveals he is her former lover. He says he met Vic while in prison and chose her as their victim. Danny plans to double-cross Vic and offers to start a new life with Alice and the money. As Vic returns, Alice agrees to go along with Danny's plan and be tied back up. Danny tries and fails to dispose of the spent bullet casing in the toilet, ultimately forcing himself to swallow it when Vic beats down the door. The two then discuss their plans to run away together after collecting the ransom and share a passionate kiss, revealing they were lovers in prison.
Later, when Vic is away again, Alice seduces Danny and handcuffs him to the bed, but finds the door bolted shut when she tries to escape. She finds a mobile phone and dials 999 but is unable to tell the operator where she is. She threatens Danny with his gun for the front door keys. Danny tells her they are in his pocket and knocks her out when she tries to retrieve them. Vic returns and says the exchange is on. Danny leaves the two and goes to the van.
Vic finds the mobile phone and sees the 999 call as well as the bullet hole in the wall. He ungags and threatens her. She screams for Danny, then tells Vic that Danny intends to double-cross him. Vic is shocked by the betrayal. When Danny returns, Vic says he feels something is 'not right', but Danny does not reveal anything. They inject Alice with a sedative and take her to a deserted, rural warehouse where they chain her in a back room. Vic asks Danny for his keys to the locks and drives him to the woods to pick up the ransom. There, Vic confronts Danny and threatens to kill both him and Alice. He says the hole they dug for the ransom is now for Danny. Danny flees, and Vic shoots him. Although wounded, Danny manages to hide. Vic retrieves the ransom elsewhere and returns for Alice. As he tries to inject her again, Danny appears and grabs his gun. During the standoff, Alice learns of Vic and Danny's true relationship.
Danny shoots Vic point blank and, to Alice's horror, leaves her in the dark and handcuffed to the railing next to the dying man. However, Vic revives long enough to throw the keys to her.

documents.title: Ironclad
documents.tagline: Heavy metal goes medieval.
documents.overview: In the year 1215, the rebel barons of England have forced their despised King John to put his royal seal on the Magna Carta, a seminal document that upheld the rights of free men. Yet within months of pledging himself to the great charter, the King reneged on his word and assembled a mercenary army on the south coast of England with the intention of bringing the barons and the country back under his tyrannical rule. Barring his way stood the mighty Rochester castle, a place that would become the symbol of the rebel's momentous struggle for justice and freedom.
documents.plot: In the year 1215, the rebel barons of England have forced their despised King John to put his royal seal on the Magna Carta, a seminal document that upheld the rights of free men. Yet within months of pledging himself to the great charter, the King reneged on his word and assembled a mercenary army on the south coast of England with the intention of bringing the barons and the country back under his tyrannical rule. Barring his way stood the mighty Rochester castle, a place that would become the symbol of the rebel's momentous struggle for justice and freedom.
production_companies: Film & Entertainment VIP Medienfonds 4 GmbH & Co. KG (I)

documents.title: The Karate Kid
documents.tagline: A Challenge He Never Imagined. A Teacher He Never Expected.
documents.overview: Twelve-year-old Dre Parker could have been the most popular kid in Detroit, but his mother's latest career move has landed him in China. Dre immediately falls for his classmate Mei Ying but the cultural differences make such a friendship impossible. Even worse, Dre's feelings make him an enemy of the class bully, Cheng. With no friends in a strange land, Dre has nowhere to turn but maintenance man Mr. Han, who is a kung fu master. As Han teaches Dre that kung fu is not about punches and parries, but maturity and calm, Dre realizes that facing down the bullies will be the fight of his life.
documents.plot:
The Karate Kid is a 2010 martial arts drama directed by Harald Zwart from a screenplay by Christopher Murphey, based on a story by Robert Mark Kamen. A remake of the 1984 film, it moves the story to China and replaces karate with kung fu. Jaden Smith stars as a young American boy, with Jackie Chan as his teacher, Taraji P. Henson as his mother, and Wenwen Han, Zhenwei Wang and Yu Rongguang in supporting roles. It was filmed in Beijing.

Twelve-year-old Dre Parker moves from Detroit to Beijing with his widowed mother, Sherry, who has been transferred by her employer. He quickly develops a crush on Meiying, a young violinist, but this draws the hostility of Cheng, a kung fu student who repeatedly bullies and beats him. After Dre takes revenge with a bucket of dirty water, Cheng and his gang chase him down and attack him, until the apartment building's quiet maintenance man, Mr. Han, intervenes and effortlessly fends them off, revealing himself as a kung fu master.

Han explains that the boys have been taught to be merciless by their teacher, Master Li. When Han and Dre visit Li's studio to make peace, Li demands a fight, and Han instead agrees that Dre will compete against Li's students in an upcoming open tournament, on condition that they leave him alone until then. Han's training begins unconventionally, with Dre spending days repeatedly taking off, hanging up and putting on his jacket, which turns out to build the muscle memory for kung fu techniques. Han teaches him that kung fu is about serenity and maturity rather than violence, and takes him to a mountain temple where he witnesses a woman mirroring a cobra. Dre learns that Han lost his wife and young son in a car accident he blames himself for, and helps his teacher face his grief, while also winning back the approval of Meiying's father after their friendship briefly gets her into trouble.

At the tournament, Dre advances through the rounds, until a student of Li's is ordered to injure his leg in the semifinal and is disqualified. Insisting on competing, Dre has Han treat his leg with traditional cupping, and in the final against Cheng, he uses the cobra stance he saw at the temple to win with a kick to the head. Cheng presents him with the trophy, and Li's students bow to Han in respect.

Released by Columbia Pictures on June 11, 2010, the film received generally positive reviews and grossed about $359 million worldwide.

documents.title: Marmaduke
documents.tagline: Live Large
documents.overview: When Phil and Debbie Winslow relocate from their native Kansas to the sunny climes of Orange County, their big-hearted, havoc-wreaking Great Dane gets a taste of the dog's life, California-style.
documents.plot: When Phil and Debbie Winslow relocate from their native Kansas to the sunny climes of Orange County, their big-hearted, havoc-wreaking Great Dane gets a taste of the dog's life, California-style.

documents.title: Jane Eyre
documents.tagline: She sought refuge… and found a place haunted by secrets.
documents.overview: After a bleak childhood, Jane Eyre goes out into the world to become a governess. As she lives happily in her new position at Thornfield Hall, she meet the dark, cold, and abrupt master of the house, Mr. Rochester. Jane and her employer grow close in friendship and she soon finds herself falling in love with him. Happiness seems to have found Jane at last, but could Mr. Rochester's terrible secret be about to destroy it forever?
documents.plot:
Jane Eyre is a 2011 romantic gothic drama directed by Cary Joji Fukunaga and written by Moira Buffini, based on Charlotte Brontë's 1847 novel. It stars Mia Wasikowska as Jane Eyre and Michael Fassbender as Edward Rochester, with Jamie Bell as St. John Rivers, Judi Dench as the housekeeper Mrs. Fairfax, Sally Hawkins as Jane's cruel aunt Mrs. Reed, Simon McBurney, Imogen Poots, Holliday Grainger and Tamzin Merchant.

The film opens with Jane fleeing Thornfield Hall in tears and collapsing on the moors, where she is taken in by the clergyman St. John Rivers and his sisters. Through flashbacks, it recounts her harsh childhood as an orphan mistreated by her aunt and cousin, and her years at the austere Lowood School, where she loses her friend Helen Burns to consumption. At eighteen, Jane becomes governess to Adèle, the young French ward of Edward Rochester, the brooding master of Thornfield Hall.

Jane and Rochester are drawn to each other through their frank, spirited conversations, while mysterious events disturb the house, including a fire in Rochester's bedroom and a violent attack on a visitor from Jamaica, Richard Mason. Although Rochester appears to be courting the elegant Blanche Ingram, he eventually declares his love for Jane and proposes. Their wedding is interrupted by the revelation that Rochester is already married to Bertha, Mason's sister, whose madness has led him to lock her away in the house. Heartbroken, Jane leaves Thornfield, and while living with the Rivers family she must choose between a loveless offer of marriage and missionary work and her enduring feelings for Rochester.

Fukunaga's version emphasizes the gothic atmosphere and psychological intensity of the novel, using a non-linear structure built around Jane's flight from Thornfield.

Jane Eyre opened in a limited release in the United States on 11 March 2011, achieving the best specialty debut of the year, and was released in Britain in September. It received positive reviews, with 85 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised Wasikowska's portrayal, and a Metacritic score of 76. Michael O'Connor's costume design was nominated for an Academy Award.

documents.title: Bad Boys for Life
documents.tagline: Ride together. Die together.
documents.overview: Marcus and Mike are forced to confront new threats, career changes, and midlife crises as they join the newly created elite team AMMO of the Miami police department to take down the ruthless Armando Armas, the vicious leader of a Miami drug cartel.
documents.plot:
Bad Boys for Life is a 2020 American action comedy film directed by Adil El Arbi and Bilall Fallah, and written by Peter Craig. The movie stars Will Smith, Martin Lawrence, Vanessa Hudgens, Alexander Ludwig, and Nick Nolte.

The film takes place nine years after the events of Bad Boys II (2003). Mike Lowrey (Will Smith) is now a retired Miami cop who has moved to Los Angeles with his wife, Syd (Vanessa Hudgens), and their son. Meanwhile, Marcus Burnett (Martin Lawrence) is still working as a Miami cop.

The story begins with the return of the villainous Armando Diaz's (Joel Rodriguez) nephew, Javier (Alexander Ludwig), who seeks revenge against Mike and Marcus for killing his uncle in the previous film. Javier kidnaps Syd, forcing Mike to come out of retirement and team up with Marcus once again to rescue her.

As they delve deeper into the case, they discover that Javier is working for a powerful cartel leader named Elena (Vanessa's character has been replaced by a new one, played by Vanessa Hudgens), who seeks revenge against the United States for killing her family. The two former partners must put aside their differences and work together to take down Elena and her team.

Throughout the film, Mike and Marcus face various challenges as they navigate their way through the cartel's operations. They also have to deal with the fact that they are no longer as young or as skilled as they used to be, which makes it harder for them to keep up with the younger and more agile cartel members.

As the story unfolds, Mike and Marcus discover that Elena is using a new technology to control people's minds, making her an almost unstoppable force. The two former partners come up with a plan to infiltrate Elena's operation and take her down from the inside.

The film features plenty of action-packed sequences, including car chases, shootouts, and hand-to-hand combat. Will Smith and Martin Lawrence reprise their roles as Mike and Marcus, delivering their signature humor and chemistry that fans have come to expect from the franchise.

In the end, Mike and Marcus successfully take down Elena and her team, saving Syd and restoring order to Miami. The film concludes with a heartwarming moment between Mike and his son, as well as a nod to the original Bad Boys duo's partnership.

Overall, Bad Boys for Life is an entertaining action-comedy that delivers on its promise of high-octane action and witty banter. While it may not be as groundbreaking as some of the other films in the franchise, it provides a fun and satisfying conclusion to the series.

documents.title: Gulliver's Travels
documents.tagline: Something big is going down.
documents.overview: Travel writer Lemuel Gulliver takes an assignment in Bermuda, but ends up on the island of Liliput, where he towers over its tiny citizens.
documents.plot:
Gulliver's Travels is a 2010 American fantasy adventure comedy directed by Rob Letterman, in his live-action debut, and written by Joe Stillman and Nicholas Stoller. Loosely based on the first part of Jonathan Swift's 1726 novel but set in the present day, it stars Jack Black as Lemuel Gulliver, with Jason Segel, Emily Blunt, Amanda Peet, Billy Connolly, Chris O'Dowd, T.J. Miller, James Corden and Catherine Tate. 20th Century Fox released it in the United States on December 25, 2010.

Gulliver works in the mail room of a New York newspaper and secretly adores the travel editor, Darcy Silverman. Trying to impress her, he submits a travel piece cobbled together from plagiarised material, and Darcy rewards him with an assignment to investigate the Bermuda Triangle. Sailing into the Triangle, he falls asleep at the helm, is caught by a storm and a waterspout, and washes up on Lilliput, an island of tiny people whose society resembles old Europe.

Treated as a monster, he is imprisoned in a cave, where he meets Horatio, a commoner jailed by General Edward for loving Princess Mary, whom Edward wants for himself. Gulliver rescues Mary from raiders of the rival island Blefuscia and puts out a fire threatening King Theodore, and is hailed as a hero. Claiming to be the President of Manhattan, he lives in luxury and stages Lilliputian versions of films and his own boasts, while advising Horatio on wooing Mary. The humiliated Edward sabotages the island's defences, and when Gulliver single-handedly defeats the Blefuscian fleet, Edward defects.

Using plans from a video game manual Gulliver lost, Edward pilots a giant robot that leads a Blefuscian invasion, forces Gulliver to confess he is just a mail-room worker, and banishes him to Brobdingnag, where a giant girl keeps him as a doll. Horatio finds him and reveals that Darcy, who followed him into the Triangle, is being held by the Blefuscians. Gulliver escapes, defeats Edward in a duel with Horatio's help, and ends the war by persuading both sides to make peace, before returning home with Darcy as a genuine travel writer.

Critics were dismissive, with a 19% Rotten Tomatoes approval. Made for about $112 million, the film flopped in North America but grossed $237 million worldwide.

documents.title: Passion Play
documents.tagline: Love Is Stronger Than Death.
documents.overview: An angel under the thumb of a ruthless gangster is saved by a trumpet player down on his luck.
documents.plot:
Passion Play is a 2011 American fantasy drama film written and directed by Mitch Glazer, in his feature directorial debut, and executive produced by Rebecca Wang. Mickey Rourke stars as a down-and-out jazz trumpeter, with Megan Fox as a carnival performer born with wings, Bill Murray as a gangster, and Rhys Ifans, Kelly Lynch and Robert Wisdom in supporting roles. Filmed from December 2009, it premiered at the 2010 Toronto International Film Festival, where its poor reception led to talk of a direct-to-video release.

Nate Poole is a washed-up jazz musician and recovering heroin addict whose luck has run out. After a gig one night he is attacked, tied up and driven into the desert by a hitman. Just as he is about to be executed, his would-be killer is shot dead by a group of Native Americans, who leave Nate unharmed. Wandering through the desert, he reaches a travelling carnival and freak show, full of fire eaters and sword swallowers, and asks to use a telephone.

There he becomes fascinated by Lily Luster, a beautiful young woman with real wings who is exhibited as one of the sideshow's attractions. Lily is aloof at first, but begins to see the kindly Nate as a possible escape from her life. When the carnival owner, Sam Adamo, tries to kill Nate, Lily saves him by stealing a truck, and the two run away to the city, where they begin a tentative romance.

Fearing for his life, Nate goes to see Happy Shannon, the wealthy gangster who ordered his death after Nate slept with Happy's wife, whom Happy also had killed. Nate offers him most of the profits from putting Lily on display, but Happy only believes in her wings after seeing her from a distance. He then takes Lily for himself, promising to leave Nate alive as long as she stays with him. Nate realises that he loves her and tries in vain to free her. Adamo, discovering where Lily is, breaks in to take her back and is shot dead by Happy.

When Nate learns that Happy is showing Lily in a glass case at a theatre, he smashes the case and the two flee to the roof, pursued by Happy's men. Lily doubts she can fly, so Nate leaps from the building and she jumps after him, catching him in mid-air. As they fly over the desert, Nate glimpses his own body lying where the hitman had taken him, suggesting that everything since had been his dying dream.

The film was savaged by critics, holding a 3% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Tangled
documents.tagline: They're taking adventure to new lengths.
documents.overview: When the kingdom's most wanted-and most charming-bandit Flynn Rider hides out in a mysterious tower, he's taken hostage by Rapunzel, a beautiful and feisty tower-bound teen with 70 feet of magical, golden hair. Flynn's curious captor, who's looking for her ticket out of the tower where she's been locked away for years, strikes a deal with the handsome thief and the unlikely duo sets off on an action-packed escapade, complete with a super-cop horse, an over-protective chameleon and a gruff gang of pub thugs.
documents.plot:
Tangled is a 2010 animated musical fantasy film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. The movie is a modern retelling of the classic fairy tale Rapunzel, with a few twists and creative liberties.

The story follows Princess Rapunzel (voiced by Mandy Moore), a young woman with long, magical hair that has healing properties. She lives in a tower in the kingdom of Corona, guarded by Mother Gothel (voiced by Donna Murphy), who claims to be Rapunzel's mother. However, it is revealed that Gothel has been using Rapunzel's hair to stay young and beautiful.

One day, thief Flynn Rider (voiced by Zachary Levi) stumbles upon the tower while on the run from the law. He convinces Rapunzel to join him on a journey to see the floating lights in the sky, which she believes are her only connection to the outside world. As they travel together, they develop feelings for each other and become embroiled in a plot by Gothel to use Rapunzel's hair to gain control over the kingdom.

Throughout their adventure, Rapunzel discovers her true identity and the secrets of her past. She also learns about her royal heritage and the prophecy that foretells her destiny as the queen of Corona. Meanwhile, Flynn must confront his own troubled past and learn to trust himself and others.

The movie features a range of memorable characters, including Maximus (voiced by Donal Logue), a loyal and lovable horse who becomes Rapunzel's companion, and Pascal (voiced by Jeffrey Tambor), a chatty and endearing pet chameleon. The film's soundtrack, featuring songs like "When Will My Life Begin" and "I've Got a Dream," is also noteworthy for its catchy melodies and heartfelt lyrics.

Overall, Tangled offers a fresh take on the classic Rapunzel story, with engaging characters, witty humor, and stunning animation. The movie's themes of self-discovery, friendship, and embracing one's true identity make it a delightful and entertaining watch for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Dinner for Schmucks
documents.tagline: Takes One To Know One.
documents.overview: Rising executive Tim Conrad works for a boss who hosts a monthly dinner in which the guest who brings the biggest buffoon gets a career-boost. Tim plans on not attending until he meets Barry, a man who builds dioramas using stuffed mice. Barry's blundering but good intentions send Tim's life into a downward spiral, threatening a major business deal and possibly scuttling Tim's engagement to his fiancee.

documents.title: Rampage
documents.tagline: Vengeance is ruthless.
documents.overview: The boredom of small town life is eating Bill Williamson alive. Feeling constrained and claustrophobic in the meaningless drudgery of everyday life and helpless against overwhelming global dissolution, Bill begins a descent into madness. His shockingly violent plan will shake the very foundations of society by painting the streets red with blood.
documents.plot:
Rampage is a 2009 action thriller written and directed by Uwe Boll, starring Brendan Fletcher as Bill Williamson, Shaun Sipos as his friend Evan Drince, Michael Paré as Sheriff Melvoy, and Lynda Boyd and Matt Frewer as Bill's parents. It received a theatrical release in Germany and went direct to video elsewhere. Notably, it was the first of Boll's films to earn mainly positive reviews, and it spawned two sequels, Rampage: Capital Punishment (2014) and Rampage: President Down (2016).

Bill Williamson is a 23-year-old mechanic living with his parents in the fictional small town of Tenderville, Oregon. He feels overwhelmed by the world's problems, by constant television and radio news and by the political rants of Evan, apparently his only friend. His parents tell him it is time to move out, a coffee shop owner annoys him, and his boss condescendingly refuses him a raise.

At home, Bill quietly prints counterfeit money and builds a suit of steel body armor with a ballistic helmet and a mask. Heavily armed, he drives into town, first disabling the police by blowing up their headquarters with a remote-controlled van bomb. He then walks through the streets shooting people at random, his armor deflecting the bullets of the officers who try to stop him. Moving from a salon to a bingo hall to a bank, he kills almost indiscriminately, robbing the bank and then burning what appears to be the stolen money while declaring that money is worthless. His rampage leads to a forest where Evan is waiting for a paintball match and where the sheriff pursues him, and as the death toll mounts it becomes clear that Bill's killing spree is part of a calculated plan rather than a sudden outburst.

The film presents a bleak, provocative critique of a society saturated by media and money, with a protagonist who believes the world's population must be reduced, and it is shot in a raw visual style.

Rampage surprised many reviewers. /Film said Boll had finally made a good, if not great, film, and Bloody Disgusting praised his evolution as a director, while Variety's Peter Debruge called it uncompromising and nearly unwatchable, criticizing both its subject and its visual style.
production_companies: Boll Kino Beteiligungs GmbH & Co. KG

documents.title: Dogtooth
documents.tagline: The cat is the most feared animal there is!
documents.overview: Three teenagers are confined to an isolated country estate that could very well be on another planet. The trio spend their days listening to endless homemade tapes that teach them a whole new vocabulary. Any word that comes from beyond their family abode is instantly assigned a new meaning. Hence 'the sea' refers to a large armchair and 'zombies' are little yellow flowers. Having invented a brother whom they claim to have ostracized for his disobedience, the uber-controlling parents terrorize their offspring into submission.
documents.plot:
A couple and their adult son and two adult daughters live in a fenced compound. The children have no knowledge of the outside world; their parents say they will be ready to leave once they lose a dogtooth, and that one can safely leave only by car. The children entertain themselves with endurance games, such as holding their hands under hot water. They believe they have a brother on the other side of the fence to whom they throw supplies. The parents reward good behavior with stickers and bad with violence.
The father pays an employee of his factory, Christina, to come to the house and have sex with the son. Frustrated by the son's refusal to give her cunnilingus, Christina trades her headband with the elder daughter in exchange for cunnilingus from her. The elder daughter convinces the younger daughter to lick her shoulder by bartering the headband. Later, the younger daughter volunteers to lick the elder again. The elder has nothing to offer in exchange, but the younger does not mind and experiments by licking other body parts.
The father visits a dog training facility and demands to have his dog returned. The trainer refuses because the dog has not finished its training, and asks: "Do we want an animal or a friend?" When the children are terrified by a stray cat in the garden, the son kills it with a pair of pruning shears. Deciding to take advantage of the incident, the father shreds his clothes, covers himself in fake blood, and tells his children that their unseen brother was killed by a cat, the most dangerous creature. After he teaches them to bark on all fours to fend off cats, the family holds a memorial service for the brother.
Christina again barters for oral sex from the elder daughter. The daughter rejects her offer of hair gel and demands the Hollywood VHS tapes in her bag. She watches the films (Rocky IV and Jaws) in secret and afterwards recreates scenes and quotes their dialogue. When the father discovers the tapes, he beats her with one of them, then goes to Christina's flat and hits her with her VCR, cursing her future children to be corrupted by "bad influences".
The parents decide that, with Christina no longer available, they will have the son choose one of his sisters as a new sexual partner. After fondling both sisters with his eyes closed, he chooses the elder. She is uncomfortable during their sex and afterwards threatens her brother in the style of Hollywood film dialogues.
During a performance for the parents' wedding anniversary, the younger daughter stops to rest, but the elder continues and dances the choreography from Flashdance, disturbing her parents. That night, she knocks out one of her dogteeth with a dumbbell and hides in the boot of her father's car. The father discovers her tooth fragments and searches for her fruitlessly. He drives to work the next day; the car sits outside the factory, unattended.

documents.title: Middle Men
documents.tagline: Business is a lot like sex ... getting in is easy, pulling out is hard.
documents.overview: Chronicles Jack Harris, one of the pioneers of internet commerce, as he wrestles with his morals and struggles not to drown in a sea of conmen, mobsters, drug addicts, and pornstars.
documents.plot:
Middle Men is a 2009 American black comedy-drama film directed by George Gallo and written by Gallo and Andy Weiss, inspired by the experiences of Christopher Mallick, founder of ePassporte, who was accused of taking millions from its customers to finance the film. Luke Wilson stars as Jack Harris, with Giovanni Ribisi as Wayne Beering, Gabriel Macht as Buck Dolby, James Caan as the lawyer Jerry Haggerty, Jacinda Barrett as Jack's wife Diana, Laura Ramsey as Audrey Dawns and Rade Šerbedžija as Nikita Sokoloff.

In 2004 Jack leaves his Houston home with millions of dollars to pay off Russian gangsters. In 1997 Los Angeles, Jack is running a nightclub for an ailing friend, while nearby two drug-addled friends, Wayne and Buck, a former NASA scientist, wonder why the internet has no pornography. Buck quickly writes a program that lets visitors pay by credit card to view explicit pictures, and the money pours in. They give Sokoloff, a Russian mobster with a strip club, a quarter of the business for access to his dancers, then fail to pay him. Haggerty, the crooked lawyer they hire, brings in Jack, who becomes a partner and buys Haggerty out for $200,000. When Sokoloff's nephew comes to collect $400,000 and threatens Jack's family, one of Jack's bodyguards kills him with a single punch; the partners dump the body at sea, and Sokoloff, doubting their cover story, demands a half share. Jack abandons the website to concentrate on billing, and their company, 24/7 Billing, becomes a hugely profitable middleman for other adult sites. Seduced by money, he neglects his family and begins an affair with Audrey, a porn star whose live stream, it emerges, is used by the government to track terrorists. The resentful Haggerty manipulates Wayne and Buck into processing payments for child pornography sites run by Denny Z, and when the pair confide in him about the nephew's death, he turns Sokoloff against Jack. Sokoloff's men kidnap the son of Jack's maid, believing him to be Jack's own son. Jack signs his share over in exchange for the boy but backdates the contract to before the child pornography business began; Sokoloff kills Haggerty and lets Jack go. Wayne and Buck later testify against Denny Z, Sokoloff flees, reportedly to Moscow, and Jack's wife takes him back.
