Released in the United States on 6 August 2010, Middle Men grossed only $754,301 against a $20 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with a 39% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a Metacritic score of 60.

documents.title: Ramona and Beezus
documents.tagline: A Little Sister Goes A Long Way.
documents.overview: Ramona is a little girl with a very big imagination and a nose for mischief. Her playful antics keep everyone in her loving family on their toes, including her older sister Beezus, who's just trying to survive her first year of high school. Through all the ups and downs of childhood, Ramona and Beezus learn that anything's possible when you believe in yourself and rely on each other.
documents.plot:
Adventurous and creative third-grader Ramona Quimby often finds herself in trouble at school and at home, and usually spends time with her neighbor and best friend, Howard Kemp. When her father Robert loses his job and the family falls into severe debt, Ramona's efforts to earn money end up backfiring in humorous ways. She repeatedly embarrasses her older sister, Beatrice, in front of Henry Huggins the paperboy (who is also Beatrice's crush) by calling her the family nickname, "Beezus".
Although he had worked as an executive in a company since Beezus's birth, Robert quarrels with Dorothy (his wife and the girls' mother) when he considers pursuing a new, more creative career. Meanwhile, Ramona's visiting aunt Beatrice, her sister's namesake, is one of the few who accepts her despite all her eccentricities. After a car-painting accident involving Bea's old flame Hobart, who happens to be Howard's uncle, Ramona gives up her money-making schemes.
The next day, Ramona ruins her school portrait by cracking a raw egg in her hair and making a face when the photographer asks her to say "Peas" instead of "Cheese". Ramona's worries increase the following day, when her classmate Susan reveals that after her own father lost his job, her parents divorced and her father moved to Tacoma. The news makes Ramona physically sick, and Robert has to pick her up early from school, interfering with a sudden job interview. Instead of being angry, Robert decides to spend the rest of his day drawing a mural with Ramona. While Ramona and Beezus attempt to make dinner for their parents, the pan catches fire while Beezus is on the phone with Henry. During the ensuing argument, Henry overhears that Beezus loves him. Still upset, Ramona goes to feed her cat Picky-Picky but is devastated to find him dead. The girls' private funeral for their cat helps them reconcile. A job offer for Robert in Oregon leads Ramona's parents to decide to sell their house.
As the family touches up the garden during an open house, Ramona inadvertently initiates a water fight with the neighbors, which floods the neighbors' backyard and exposes a box that Hobart buried there years ago. The box contains mementos of Bea and Hobart's teenage romance, and in light of their rekindling relationship, he proposes to her. Hesitantly, Bea accepts, and the family begins planning the impromptu wedding.
Furious that her aunt broke her promise not to get "reeled in" with Hobart again, Ramona rushes home, seeking solace in the attic. The fragile floorboards break, leaving her legs dangling from the ceiling during the open house. After they clear out, Robert scolds her for her lack of maturity. Feeling unwanted, Ramona decides to run away. Unable to convince her not to leave, Dorothy helps her pack. Opening the heavy suitcase at a bus stop, Ramona discovers that Dorothy intentionally made it heavy to keep her from getting far. Inside, Dorothy packed a book of Robert's sketches of Ramona.

documents.title: Winter's Bone
documents.tagline: Talking Just Causes Witnesses
documents.overview: 17 year-old Ree Dolly sets out to track down her father, who put their house up for his bail bond and then disappeared. If she fails, Ree and her family will be turned out into the Ozark woods. Challenging her outlaw kin's code of silence and risking her life, Ree hacks through the lies, evasions and threats offered up by her relatives and begins to piece together the truth.
documents.plot: After discovering her father put their house up for his bail bond and then disappeared, 17-year-old Ree Dolly must confront the local criminal underworld and the harsh Ozark wilderness in order to to track down her father and save her family.

documents.title: Cyrus
documents.tagline: John met the woman of his dreams. Then he met her son...
documents.overview: With John's social life at a standstill and his ex-wife about to get remarried, a down on his luck divorcée finally meets the woman of his dreams, only to discover she has another man in her life - her son. Before long, the two are locked in a battle of wits for the woman they both love-and it appears only one man can be left standing when it's over.
documents.plot:
Jamie informs her ex-husband John that she is getting married. Even though they have been apart for seven years, the news devastates John, who was already depressed. At a party the next night, John gets more and more drunk until he ends up urinating in the bushes, where Molly strikes up a conversation. Molly goes back to John's house but leaves during the night, after they have had sex. Molly returns for dinner the next night, and again leaves after they have had sex. John follows her to her house and falls asleep in his car. The next morning, he approaches the house and meets Molly's 21-year-old son Cyrus. Cyrus invites John inside and makes friendly conversation with him. Molly is startled to see John in her house when she returns, but the trio have dinner together. John is unnerved by the unnatural intimacy between Molly and Cyrus.
The next morning, John cannot find his shoes, which he had left in the living room. Through the day, he gets increasingly disturbed by their disappearance and starts to worry that Cyrus is messing with him. He ropes Jamie into meeting Molly and Cyrus, in order to appraise his paranoia. Jamie finds Cyrus sweet, if a little overly intimate with his mother. Relieved, John returns for another night at Molly's home. As they begin to have sex for the first time in her house, Cyrus screams in his room, and Molly runs to comfort him. She does not return to John, who goes out looking for her in the middle of the night. He encounters Cyrus holding a large kitchen knife, allegedly making a snack. Cyrus says he had a night terror, and that Molly has gone to sleep. He then advises John to back off on the relationship because he is scaring off Molly. John leaves a note for her and goes home. In the morning, Cyrus sits Molly down and tells her that John had confessed to him that she was coming on too strong. When she presses Cyrus for details, he explodes in a tantrum and storms off, checking through the window to make sure that she is upset. When Cyrus finally comes home, he explains that he has rented a room and will be moving out. After a few happy days alone together, John decides to move in with Molly.
One night, as they begin to have sex, Cyrus surprises them and says that he has been having panic attacks and wants to return home. John confronts Cyrus privately, and Cyrus admits that he has been deliberately sabotaging their relationship. He moves back home, and John remains wary of him. The night before Jamie's wedding, he warns Cyrus not to cause trouble. At the wedding, however, Cyrus is hurt when he sees how the event stirs romantic feelings between John and his mother. Drunk, he confronts John in the bathroom and attacks him, yelling that John will not take his mother away from him. As John defends himself, they spill out of the bathroom, into open view. Cyrus makes it look like John attacked him. John advises Molly to open her eyes, and storms off, furious.

documents.title: Pokémon: Arceus and the Jewel of Life
documents.original_title: 劇場版ポケットモンスター ダイヤモンド&パール アルセウス 超克の時空へ
documents.tagline: A tale untold. A legend unleashed.
documents.overview: When the creator of the world, Arceus, comes to pass judgement on humanity for the theft of the legendary Jewel of Life, Ash and his friends are sent back in time to possibly reverse the events that led to Arceus' vendetta.
documents.plot: When the creator of the world, Arceus, comes to pass judgement on humanity for the theft of the legendary Jewel of Life, Ash and his friends are sent back in time to possibly reverse the events that led to Arceus' vendetta.

documents.title: Dragon Ball Z: The Tree of Might
documents.original_title: ドラゴンボールZ 地球まるごと超決戦
documents.tagline: From the seeds of destruction, a new threat has arisen.
documents.overview: Goku and friends must stop a band of space pirates from consuming fruit from the Tree of Might before it's destructive powers drain Earth's energy.
documents.plot:
Dragon Ball Z: The Tree of Might is a 1990 Japanese animated science fantasy martial arts film produced by Toei Animation, based on the popular manga and anime series Dragon Ball Z. The movie takes place during the Saiyan Saga of the original Dragon Ball Z series.

The story begins with Goku and his friends celebrating the defeat of Frieza on Planet Namek. However, their celebration is short-lived as a powerful being known as Turles arrives on Earth. Unbeknownst to Goku and his friends, Turles is actually the long-lost brother of Raditz, the Saiyan who killed Goku's father.

Turles reveals that he has come to Earth to destroy it and its inhabitants, and to claim the Tree of Might, a powerful being with the ability to grant wishes. The Tree of Might is located on Earth and is guarded by a group of powerful warriors known as the Guardians of the Tree.

Goku and his friends soon discover Turles' true intentions and band together to stop him. Along the way, they meet a new ally in the form of Tien Shinhan, a powerful warrior from the planet Capricorn who has come to Earth to help defend it against Turles.

As the battle between Goku and Turles intensifies, the two engage in an epic fight that pushes both warriors to their limits. Meanwhile, Vegeta, who had been watching the battle from afar, becomes increasingly frustrated with his own lack of power compared to Turles' abilities.

In the end, it is revealed that Turles was actually sent to Earth by Frieza as a test to see if Goku and his friends could defeat him. With this knowledge, Goku and his friends are able to gain the upper hand in their battle against Turles, and he is ultimately defeated.

The movie ends with Goku and his friends celebrating their victory over Turles, while Vegeta finally finds the strength and confidence to join them as a powerful warrior. The Tree of Might is also shown to be destroyed, but its legacy lives on through the power of the warriors who defended it.

Overall, Dragon Ball Z: The Tree of Might is an action-packed and entertaining film that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and the power of determination. With its epic battles and memorable characters, it remains a beloved entry in the Dragon Ball Z franchise.

documents.title: Dragon Ball Z: The Return of Cooler
documents.original_title: ドラゴンボールZ 激突!!100億パワーの戦士たち
documents.tagline: The odds are 10 billion to 2.
documents.overview: Cooler has resurrected himself as a robot and is enslaving the people of New Namek. Goku and the gang must help.
documents.plot:
Dragon Ball Z: The Return of Cooler is a 1992 anime film directed by Daisuke Nishio, produced by Toei Animation. It is the third Dragon Ball Z feature film and serves as a sequel to the previous two films, Dragon Ball Z: The World's Strongest and Dragon Ball Z: The Tree of Might.

The story begins with Goku and his friends enjoying their victory over Majin Buu in the previous film. However, their celebration is short-lived as they soon discover that Cooler, the brother of Frieza, has returned to Earth seeking revenge against Goku and his friends for defeating him in the past.

Cooler, who possesses a powerful new technique called "Gravity Ball," begins to wreak havoc on the planet, using his abilities to create massive earthquakes and destroy entire cities. The Z Warriors, led by Goku, must band together once again to stop Cooler's destructive rampage.

As the battle between the Z Warriors and Cooler intensifies, it becomes clear that Cooler is not just a mindless villain, but rather a complex character with a deep-seated hatred for Goku and his friends. Throughout the film, Cooler's backstory is slowly revealed, showing how he was once a powerful warrior who was defeated by Goku in their previous encounter.

Despite being outmatched by Cooler's Gravity Ball technique, Goku and his friends refuse to give up, using their unique abilities and teamwork to try and find a way to counter Cooler's attacks. Meanwhile, Vegeta, who had previously allied himself with the Z Warriors against Frieza, begins to question his loyalty to the group, feeling that he is being held back by his own pride.

As the final battle between the Z Warriors and Cooler reaches its climax, Goku and his friends discover that Cooler's true weakness lies in his emotional vulnerability. Using this knowledge, they are able to develop a strategy to defeat Cooler once and for all.

In the end, the Z Warriors emerge victorious, having successfully defeated Cooler and saved the Earth from destruction. The film concludes with Goku and his friends reflecting on their victory, while Vegeta finally finds redemption by acknowledging his loyalty to the group.

Overall, Dragon Ball Z: The Return of Cooler is a thrilling and action-packed film that showcases the bravery and determination of the Z Warriors as they face off against one of their most formidable foes yet.

documents.title: Dragon Ball Z: Bio-Broly
documents.original_title: ドラゴンボールＺ 超戦士撃破!!勝のはオレだ
documents.tagline: Broly is back! And this time a case of mistaken identity might be the end of the planet!
documents.overview: Jaga Bada, Mr. Satan's old sparring partner, has invited Satan to his personal island to hold a grudge match. Trunks and Goten decide to come for the adventure and Android #18 is following Satan for the money he owes her. Little do they know that Jaga Bada's scientist have found a way to resurrect Broly, the legendary Super Saiyan.
documents.plot:
Dragon Ball Z: Bio-Broly is a 1994 Japanese animated science fiction martial arts film directed by Daisuke Nishio and produced by Toei Animation. The movie takes place during the Androids Arc of the Dragon Ball Z series.

The story begins with Goku, Trunks, and Pan traveling to the planet Vagar, where they meet a young boy named Broly, who is being raised by his mother, Paragus. However, their peaceful encounter is disrupted by the arrival of Dr. Gero's androids, led by Android 17 and Android 18.

The androids are searching for Broly, as he possesses a unique genetic makeup that makes him incredibly powerful. The androids plan to capture Broly and use his DNA to create an even more powerful being. Meanwhile, Goku and his friends soon discover that the androids' true intention is to destroy Vagar and harvest its energy.

As the story unfolds, Broly's powers grow stronger, and he becomes a formidable opponent for Goku and his friends. However, despite his incredible abilities, Broly struggles with his own identity and purpose in life. He is torn between his desire to protect those he cares about and his need to assert himself as a powerful warrior.

Throughout the movie, Goku and Broly engage in an epic battle that showcases their incredible strength and martial arts skills. Meanwhile, Trunks and Pan work together to help Paragus defeat Android 17 and Android 18.

As the conflict escalates, Broly's true nature is revealed: he is not just a powerful warrior but also a being with a deep sense of compassion and empathy. He begins to question his own existence and the purpose of his powers.

In the climactic final battle, Goku and Broly face off against each other. Despite their incredible strength, they are evenly matched, and it seems that neither can gain the upper hand. However, in a surprising twist, Broly's compassion and empathy ultimately lead him to spare Goku's life, realizing that his powers could be used for good or evil.

The movie concludes with Broly deciding to leave Vagar and find a new purpose in life, one that does not involve causing destruction and chaos. Goku and his friends bid farewell to Paragus and Broly, who sets off on a new journey, determined to use his powers for the greater good.

Overall, Dragon Ball Z: Bio-Broly is an action-packed and emotionally resonant film that explores themes of identity, compassion, and the responsible use of power. The movie features stunning animation, memorable characters, and epic battles that will keep fans of the Dragon Ball Z series on the edge of their seats.

documents.title: Dragon Ball Z: Fusion Reborn
documents.original_title: ドラゴンボールZ 復活のフュージョン!! 悟空とベジータ
documents.tagline: Hell’s gates have opened.
documents.overview: Not paying attention to his job, a young demon allows the evil cleansing machine to overflow and explode, turning the young demon into the infamous monster Janemba. Goku and Vegeta make solo attempts to defeat the monster, but realize their only option is fusion.
documents.plot:
In the other world, a teenage oni is manning a cleansing machine and the loud volume of his walkman distracts him, causing the machine to explode. The oni is engulfed by the freed evil spirit essence and transforms into Janemba, a massive childlike monster with dimensional manipulation abilities. As a result, the deceased are resurrected.
Goku and Pikkon are fighting in a tournament when they are interrupted by the appearance of a strange crystal-like substance and are sent to investigate the disturbance by the Grand Kai. They find the afterlife's "check-in station" to be encased in the crystal-like barrier which is also immune to their energy blasts. From inside of the station, its trapped attendant King Yemma directs them to the monster, Janemba, who refuses to drop the barrier. Goku lures Janemba to hell while Pikkon works to free Yemma.
Meanwhile, Earth comes under siege by an array of zombies, soldiers and past villains led by Frieza, who attack a city until Gohan and Videl intervene, with the former destroying him causing the villains to flee in terror. The two along with Bulma, Goten and Trunks gather the magical Dragon Balls and summon the dragon Shenron to ask him to rebuild the barrier between the living and dead, but he is unable to do so since only Yemma can control the boundaries of the afterlife. Forcing them to continue the fight against those who escaped hell. Goten and Trunks faced a Dictator with alongside his army, he appeared to be a parody of Adolf Hitler truly showing the horrors being released. In hell, Janemba uses his unorthodox powers to best Goku until he powers up to Super Saiyan 3, shaking Other World while he does it, and seemingly kills Janemba. He merely transforms into a much smaller, albeit far more powerful and sinister form - Super Janemba. Goku is overwhelmed by Super Janemba but Vegeta has regained his physical body and arrives in time to help. However, the two Saiyans are still no match for Super Janemba and are forced to hide. Goku proposes using the Fusion Dance technique, but Vegeta pridefully refuses to join bodies with Goku.
Pikkon continues to try and free Yemma to no avail, and in his anger, insults the crystal substance which causes it to slightly crack. However, Pikkon's worst insults do not cause enough damage to rescue Yemma so he decides to aid Goku and Vegeta in their fight. After much persuasion, Vegeta agrees to fuse with Goku but Vegeta fails to extend his forefinger when required and the fusion fails, resulting in a weak, obese form named Veku. Super Janemba beats Veku severely and almost kills him, but the fusion wears off and Goku and Vegeta escape in time. Pikkon arrives to stall Super Janemba while Goku and Vegeta attempt the fusion again, this time successfully transforming into the immensely powerful Super Gogeta, who swiftly gains the advantage over Janemba and he uses his power to defeat the demon, causing him to revert into his oni form, who flees.

documents.title: Dragon Ball Z: Wrath of the Dragon
documents.original_title: ドラゴンボールZ 龍拳爆発!!悟空がやらねば誰がやる
documents.tagline: If he doesn't do it, who will?
documents.overview: The Z Warriors discover an unopenable music box and are told to open it with the Dragon Balls. The contents turn out to be a warrior named Tapion who had sealed himself inside along with a monster called Hildegarn. Goku must now perfect a new technique to defeat the evil monster.
documents.plot:
Dragon Ball Z: Wrath of the Dragon is a 1995 Japanese animated science fantasy martial arts film produced by Toei Animation, based on the Dragon Ball Z manga series created by Akira Toriyama. The movie takes place after the events of the Androids Arc in the Dragon Ball Z anime series.

The story begins with a mysterious and powerful being known as Janemba, who is said to be the reincarnation of the demon king Piccolo Jr.'s evil spirit. Janemba is awakened from his slumber by the evil wizard Babidi, who seeks to use him to destroy Goku and take over the Earth.

Babidi's plan involves using a magical ritual to merge with Janemba's body, creating an even more powerful being known as Majin Buu. However, the ritual goes awry, and instead of merging with Janemba, Babidi is consumed by his own evil energy.

Meanwhile, Goku and his friends are unaware of the impending threat and continue their daily lives. However, when a series of mysterious events occur, they begin to suspect that something is amiss. They soon discover that Janemba has been awakened and is wreaking havoc on the Earth.

As the story unfolds, Goku and his allies, including Trunks, Goten, and Piccolo, band together to stop Janemba and Babidi. Along the way, they encounter a number of powerful foes, including the evil wizard's minions and a group of powerful warriors known as the "Warriors of Destruction."

The final battle takes place in the city of Capsule Corp., where Goku and his friends face off against Janemba and Babidi. In the end, Goku is able to defeat Janemba using the Spirit Bomb technique, while Trunks and Goten work together to defeat Babidi.

Throughout the movie, there are several themes that are explored, including the nature of evil and the power of friendship and teamwork. The film also features a number of action-packed sequences, showcasing the martial arts skills of the Dragon Ball Z characters.

Overall, Dragon Ball Z: Wrath of the Dragon is an exciting and entertaining addition to the Dragon Ball Z franchise, offering fans a thrilling adventure filled with intense battles and memorable moments.

documents.title: Detective Conan: Crossroad in the Ancient Capital
documents.original_title: 名探偵コナン 迷宮の十字路
documents.overview: Mouri Kogoro is called to a special case in the ancient capital of Kyoto. There, Conan meets Heiji and they team up once again to solve the case, recover the stolen Healing Buddha statue, and even discover the identity of Heiji's first love.
documents.plot:
A series of murders occurs across Tokyo, Osaka, and Kyoto, in which five men are killed using traditional Japanese weapons such as sword and bow and arrow. The perpetrator is described as wearing a Noh mask depicting an elderly man. Investigations conducted jointly by the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department, Osaka Prefectural Police, and Kyoto Prefectural Police reveal that the victims were all members of Genji Hotaru, a criminal group specializing in the theft of antique art. The remaining known members of the group are its leader, known as Yoshitsune, his subordinate Benkei, and Ise Saburo, though their true identities remain unknown.
Around the same time, Kogoro Mouri travels to Kyoto with Conan Edogawa and the others at the request of Ryuen, a monk from Sannoji Temple. Eight years earlier, a secret Buddhist statue—the Medicine Buddha, which is revealed only once every twelve years—was stolen from the temple. Recently, the temple received a mysterious drawing believed to indicate the statue's location, and Kogoro is asked to decipher it. At Sannoji Temple, the group meets several individuals connected to the case, including the monk Enkai, antique art dealer and temple patron Sakura Shozo, Noh actor Mizuo Harutaro, and used bookstore owner Taiga Saijo.
While searching for clues related to the drawing, Conan visits Gojo Bridge, a location historically associated with Minamoto no Yoshitsune and Musashibo Benkei, where he encounters Heiji Hattori. Heiji is independently investigating the Genji Hotaru murders, and the two decide to cooperate. During the investigation, Heiji recounts his first love: a girl he met in Kyoto eight years earlier, who was wearing a kimono and singing a temari uta (traditional Japanese ballad) at a temple. He also mentions a crystal ball he picked up at that time, which he continues to carry as a keepsake.
Conan and Heiji later travel to Mount Kurama, where they are attacked by an unknown assailant wielding a bow and arrow and wearing a motorcycle suit. That night, Sakura Shozo is murdered at a teahouse in Ponto-chō. Shortly afterward, Heiji is attacked again while escorting Kazuha Toyama home. The assailant challenges him to a duel using wooden swords, and Heiji is severely injured and hospitalized. Conan eventually deciphers the code in the drawing and determines that the Medicine Buddha statue is hidden at Bukkoji Temple. When Heiji arrives there, he receives a phone call from the culprit, who reveals that Kazuha has been kidnapped and orders Heiji to come to Gyokuryu Temple on Mount Kurama.
At Gyokuryu Temple, "Heiji" confronts the criminal and identifies him as Saijo, who is revealed to be Benkei. Saijo orders his disciples to attack, but "Heiji" intervenes, later revealed to be Conan, who temporarily regresses back into Shinichi Kudo by the cold will and alcohol with the help of Ai Haibara, in disguise. The real Heiji soon joins the confrontation, allowing Kazuha to escape with him into a room within the temple.

documents.title: Detective Conan: Magician of the Silver Sky
documents.original_title: 名探偵コナン 銀翼の奇術師
documents.overview: Once again, Kaitou Kid crosses swords with Conan Edogawa in this annual installment of the Detective Conan movie franchise. After receiving a letter from the thief, famous actress Juri Maki seeks the help of private detective Kogorou Mouri to protect the Star Sapphire—the "Jewel of Destiny," said to represent faith, fate, and hope.
documents.plot: Once again, Kaitou Kid crosses swords with Conan Edogawa in this annual installment of the Detective Conan movie franchise. After receiving a letter from the thief, famous actress Juri Maki seeks the help of private detective Kogorou Mouri to protect the Star Sapphire—the "Jewel of Destiny," said to represent faith, fate, and hope.

documents.title: Detective Conan: Strategy Above the Depths
documents.original_title: 名探偵コナン 水平線上の陰謀
documents.overview: Fifteen years ago in a barren stretch of the Pacific, a cruise ship collided with an iceberg and was lost at sea. More than a decade later, Hideto Yashiro—a ship engineer—died in a fatal car accident. The unlikely connection between these events only comes to light on the luxury liner St. Aphrodite during her maiden voyage. Aboard it on a much needed vacation, Kogorou Mouri, his daughter Ran, Conan Edogawa, and the Detective Boys enjoy a trip provided by Sonoko Suzuki's family. But their fun is soon cut short when a game of hide-and-seek leads to Sonoko's disappearance.
documents.plot:
Fifteen years ago, a cargo ship named Yashiromaru, built by the Yashiro group, sank while colliding with iceberg. Fifteen years later on a new on a 100 million yen luxurious cruise ship named the MS Aphrodite, also built by the Yashiro group, Conan Edogawa and the rest were invited to the cruise through Sonoko Suzuki. Earlier, the husband of the CEO of the Yashiro family group, an established ship architect, apparently had a heart-attack and drove his car down a cliff.
On Aphrodite, the CEO herself was found murdered in her room. Later, her father, the president of the Yashiro group was also found missing. He had been thrown off the cruise into the ocean, seemingly by the same person. At the welcoming party, Kogoro Mouri shows off his deduction skills, and concluded that the sub-designer of the cruise, Minako Akiyoshi, was the murderer.
However, Conan has different ideas. Hironari Kusaka, a scriptwriter who worked in co-operation with Akiyoshi on a script, was the culprit. Kusaka reveals to Aphrodite captain Wataru Kaido that the accident from 15 years ago was a scheme to sink Yashiromaru deliberately to get insurance. His father was murdered when he discovered the captain of the ship was drugged by Kaido when he was a vice captain and left to die. Kusaka immediately set off bombs and escaped by sea and the Detective Boys gave chase.
After they, Juzo Megure, Ninzaburou Shiratori and Wataru Takagi of Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department successfully took down Kusaka, more bombs were ignited. All passengers were evacuated, but Ran returned to her hiding place during the hide-and-seek game to find a "gold medal" made by sea-shells the Detective Boys made for her. However, as Aphrodite swayed, she fainted in the enclosed area. Just before Kaido evacuates, Akiyoshi takes him hostage, turning out she was the real murderer after all, and was the one who did all three killings and made Kusaka think that he did them himself.
Akiyoshi also revealed that her father was the captain who died while Yashiromaru sank. Kogoro, however, deduced correctly this time and managed to subdue Akiyoshi. He was originally trying to find evidence to prove her innocence because of her strong resemblance to his wife Eri Kisaki, but the more investigation he does, the more guilty she became. As Kogoro and Conan began to evacuate, they found out that Ran was missing. They find her under the deck of the boat with the help of a fire axe. Afterwards, a helicopter of Japan Coast Guard comes and picks them up, just before Aphrodite sinks stern-first to the bottom of the ocean.
In the post-credits scene, Conan explained he knew where Ran was because when he kicked the volleyball, Ran said she heard a soccer ball, meaning she was in a place with a tough wall. The Detective Boys come, and told Ran they made a better "gold medal" for her, and put it on her.

documents.title: Detective Conan: The Private Eyes' Requiem
documents.original_title: 名探偵コナン 探偵たちの鎮魂歌（レクイエム）
documents.overview: Synopsis Kogoro and Conan came to Yokohama according to a request from a mysterious man. But that was a trap of this man. Ran and the Detective Boys will be taken as hostages. If they don't solve the request of the man within 12 hours, the bombs attached to the hostages will explode. Furthermore, the man know that Conan`s true identity is Kudo Shinichi. Also Hattori Heiji, the High School Detective of the West, and Kaito Kid enter the stage. Will they be able to solve the mystery within the time limit and save Ran and the others? And who in the world is the client?
documents.plot:
In Yokohama, Conan Edogawa, Kogoro, Ran Mouri, Ayumi Yoshida, Genta Kojima, Mitsuhiko Tsuburaya and Ai Haibara are invited to visit a mysterious client in a hotel named Red Castle beside a theme park called Miracle Land. Ran and the kids leave after being given free theme park wristbands, while Conan and Kogoro are forced by the client to solve a mystery to remove the wristbands, which are set to detonate. The client also reveals that the wristbands given to Ran and company are set to detonate should they leave the premises. The client reveals that two other detectives gave up, one named Ryu killed, while one is still working.
Conan and Kogoro investigate an abandoned hotel where they find ski masks and a gun, which were used for a robbery. On the same date of the robbery, the Kaito Kid stole some jewels from a nearby company. Kogoro retrieves the bag, but ends up getting arrested as Kid's accomplice. During the questioning, the client calls Conan, correctly identifies him as Shinichi Kudo and gives him a second clue. Conan meets Heiji Hattori who reveals that he is also part of the search, with his friend Kazuha Toyama also held captive.
Heiji and Conan work together and end up in Yokohama Oceanic University where they join together with Saguru Hakuba, a famous British-Japanese detective. They find out that one of the former presidents of the club, Nishio Masaharu, was charged with the murder of a classmate. Heiji then confirms with the client through the phone that the mystery he wants them to solve was the murder case. They are attacked by two motorcyclists working for Souichiro Miyama, the art museum owner who is trying to kill Kid. To escape, the three detectives split up, while Conan ends up falling from a bridge and breaks his leg. Meanwhile at Miracle Land, the mugger attempts to take Ayumi hostage when they reaches the entrance, but was backfired by Sonoko Suzuki and Miwako Sato, who was go on a date with Wataru Takagi at the park.
Kogoro is already giving his report to the client in Red Castle when Heiji knocks him out so he does not get killed for giving a wrong conclusion. They then discover the client, later confirmed as Suehiko Ito, who is a blind wheelchair user and reveal the truth to him. Ito, Nishio and Reiko Shimizu, a woman who Ito was in love with, were staging the robbery of an armored truck. The robbery went wrong when a guard was killed and the robbers' escape was then witnessed by Kid. Thus, Nishio was murdered in order to keep the involvement of the other two silent. Conan and Heiji reveal that Nishio was already dead before Ito shot him and that Reiko was the true killer. When Ito panicked and tried to leave the city, his car was sabotaged in an attempt to kill him. Reiko appears at that moment and confirms the truth behind the incident. She attempts to kill the detectives but is knocked out.

documents.title: Detective Conan: Jolly Roger in the Deep Azure
documents.original_title: 名探偵コナン 紺碧の棺 （ジョリー・ロジャー）
documents.overview: The Isle of Koumi, a beautiful island in the Pacific Ocean. On the island, people pass an old legend down from generation to generation that there was the Seabed Palace, an ancient ruin at the bottom of the sea, where the treasure of 2 female pirates, Anne Bonnie & Mary Reed (who really existed 300 years ago), was left. When Conan and his friends visit Koumi Island while on vacation, they meet some treasure hunters. There was something suspicious about them.
documents.plot: The Isle of Koumi, a beautiful island in the Pacific Ocean. On the island, people pass an old legend down from generation to generation that there was the Seabed Palace, an ancient ruin at the bottom of the sea, where the treasure of female pirates Anne Bonny and Mary Reed was left. When Conan and his friends visit Koumi while on vacation, they meet some suspicious treasure hunters.

documents.title: Detective Conan: Full Score of Fear
documents.original_title: 名探偵コナン 戦慄の楽譜（フルスコア）
documents.overview: Serial murders involving all kinds have happened. All the victims are from a Music School led by a famous pianist. Conan and company have been invited to a opening concert of the Music Hall built by the pianist. The biggest attraction of this concert is the world famous violin called "Stradivarius" and a special appearance of a singer who has perfect pitch.
documents.plot:
At Domoto Music Academy, a violinist named Soko Wakabe is observing two students during a practice while she sends a message on her cellphone and the explosion occurs, injuring Wakabe and killing students. Elsewhere, an unknown person reads the news on the computer and comments on how he is getting closer to his plan of a "Silent Night."
Later, on the grounds outside the academy, Conan Edogawa talks to Ran Mouri on the phone as Shinichi Kudo. He investigates and sees an old man who is the former piano tuner turned director of the Domoto Concert Hall named Takumi Fuwa carefully picking up a piano key from the piano destroyed in the explosion and putting it in his pocket before leaves in a car. Ran invites him to go to a rehearsal with her at the concert hall that is opening soon. He declines and tells her she's meddling too much which causes her to angrily reply that he will never be like Sherlock Holmes because he's tone deaf and Ran angrily hangs up.
At the rehearsal; Kogoro, Ran, Sonoko Suzuki, and the Detective Boys are introduced to the person who will be performing for the Domoto Concert Hall opening; the organist and former pianist Kazuki Domoto, Fuwa, German professional organ tuner Hans Müller, son of Kazuki and pianist Genya, soprano Rara Chigusa, violinist Shion Yuhane, and the main soprano Reiko Akiba. The Detective Boys help Akiba to help their class choir to sing their school anthem. She agreed but asked them to leave immediately, possibly to allow Shion, who is shy, to perform without fear.
The next day, Ran plays the piano while the kids sing the Teitan Elementary School anthem. Akiba comments on their performance; Genta Kojima is too loud, Mitsuhiko Tsuburaya is not putting enough feelings into it as he was staring at Ai Haibara, Ai is singing like an adult, Ayumi Yoshida is perfect, and Conan is off-key the whole time. He is revealed later to have a perfect pitch. Genta steals a drink of Akiba's tea and suffers in agonizing pain. At the hospital, the doctor says that Genta's throat is severely inflamed by chemicals, and he will not be able to speak for about four days. The Detective Boys, Sonoko, and Akiba accompany Genta home. On the way home, they are chased by a truck, so at one of the turns, Akiba takes a different route to get the truck away from them. She trips and is about to be run over until a taxi comes and the car turns, only for the culprit to escape.
Later, two more murders occur. One explosion kills Osamu Shida, with the foot joint of a flute left on the scene. The other murder occurs when the paraglider of the victim is cut with fine cuts to cause it to plunge from mid-air. In the victim's car is the headjoint of the flute. These 2 victims, together with the 2 dead victims from the earlier explosion, formerly belonged to a group called the Quarter Quintet. Conan, indebted to Akiba for a reason he has forgotten, follows her to the forest as she is known to relax there on the day before the concert.

documents.title: When in Rome
documents.overview: Teenage sisters Charli and Lola are on the verge of an experience beyond their wildest dreams! Pack your bags and jet off to Rome as the girls start their summer internship working for the legendary Derek Hanson - the totally cool international tycoon whose empire reaches from airlines to cutting-edge fashion. Amid the fabulous sights of this exciting city, the girls do their best to impress their boss, while still finding time to design their own line of very hip clothing, meet some very cute guys and turn their summer abroad into one awesome adventure they - and you - will never forget!
documents.plot:
When in Rome is a 2002 American adventure comedy directed by Steve Purcell and starring Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen. Produced by the twins' company Dualstar Entertainment Group together with Tapestry Films, it skipped theaters and was released directly to home video by Warner Home Video on November 26, 2002. The supporting cast includes Leslie Danon, Julian Stone and Michelangelo Tommaso.

The Olsens play Leila and Charli Hunter, sisters who travel to Rome to take part in a summer internship program at a fashion company. They are joined by four other young interns from around the world, Paolo, Nobu, Dari and Heidi. Shortly after the program begins, a series of careless accidents gets the sisters dismissed, but their luck turns when they cross paths with the wealthy businessman Derek Hammond, who gives them their positions back. While spending a day at Hammond's home, Leila meets his rebellious nephew Ryan, and the two are quickly drawn to one another, while Charli begins to fall for her fellow intern Paolo.

Back at the office the girls start to take their responsibilities more seriously and form close friendships with the rest of the intern group. Their newfound commitment is tested when the scheming Mr. Tortoni, the head of the company, sabotages an important delivery by making off with the dresses intended for a photo shoot. With Ryan's assistance, Leila manages to photograph the theft and brings the evidence to Derek. The interns then rally together to produce a replacement collection from Charli's own designs, finishing just in time for the big day. The shoot is a success and Tortoni is forced to take the interns back. When Derek arrives, it emerges that Tortoni's actions were driven by long-standing jealousy over Derek's fortune and his romance with a woman named Jamie.

Like many of the Olsen twins' projects of the period, When in Rome combines a picturesque European setting with light romance and a message about friendship, teamwork and taking responsibility, and it was aimed squarely at the pair's large preteen audience. It was one of a string of international-setting adventures the sisters made for the direct-to-video market in the early 2000s, alongside titles set in other foreign cities, before they moved on to the theatrical comedy New York Minute in 2004.

documents.title: Mobile Suit Gundam I
documents.tagline: Thrust into the thick of battle, a young boy and a secret weapon are earth's last hope!
documents.overview: In the year Universal Century 0079, humans have colonized the area of space lying in between the Earth and the moon. However the ambitious Zabi family, rulers of the Duchy of Zeon (the grouping of colonies furthest from the earth) has sparked a war.
documents.plot: In the year Universal Century 0079, humans have colonized the area of space lying in between the Earth and the moon. However the ambitious Zabi family, rulers of the Duchy of Zeon (the grouping of colonies furthest from the earth) has sparked a war.

documents.title: Real Steel
documents.tagline: If you get one shot, make it real.
documents.overview: Charlie Kenton is a washed-up fighter who retired from the ring when robots took over the sport. After his robot is trashed, he reluctantly teams up with his estranged son to rebuild and train an unlikely contender.
documents.plot:
Real Steel is a 2011 American science fiction sports film produced and directed by Shawn Levy, based on Richard Matheson's 1956 short story "Steel," which had earlier been adapted as an episode of The Twilight Zone. Hugh Jackman stars as Charlie Kenton, a washed-up former boxer, with Dakota Goyo as his son, Max, Evangeline Lilly as Bailey Tallet, Anthony Mackie and Kevin Durand. The film was released by Touchstone Pictures in October 2011, with Steven Spielberg among its executive producers.

In the 2020s, human boxing has been replaced by fights between giant robots. Charlie, a former contender who scrapes a living fighting robots in small venues, loses his machine, Ambush, in a bout against a bull at a Texas carnival run by Ricky, and flees without paying the bet he lost. He then learns that his former girlfriend has died and that he must attend a custody hearing for their eleven-year-old son, Max, whom he has never known. Max's wealthy aunt, Debra, and her husband, Marvin, want custody, and Charlie agrees to give it up in exchange for money, on the condition that he takes care of Max for the summer while the couple travels.

Using the money, Charlie buys Noisy Boy, a once-famous robot from the World Robot Boxing league, but it is destroyed in an underground arena. While scavenging for parts in a junkyard, Max finds Atom, an old sparring robot that saves him from a fall. Atom is built to withstand punishment and has a rare "shadow" function that allows it to mimic human movements. Max insists on fighting with Atom, and Charlie, drawing on his boxing experience, teaches the robot to fight. The underdog robot wins a series of bouts and becomes a crowd favorite, earning a chance to face Zeus, the undefeated champion of the World Robot Boxing league. Along the way, Charlie grows closer to Max and Bailey and begins to rediscover the man he once was, and he must decide whether to give up his son.

Real Steel received generally positive reviews, with critics praising its visual effects, Jackman's and Goyo's performances and its crowd-pleasing spirit, though some found it formulaic. It grossed about $300 million worldwide and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Visual Effects.

documents.title: Dragon Ball Z: The History of Trunks
documents.original_title: ドラゴンボールZ・絶望への反抗!!残された超戦士・悟飯とトランクス
documents.tagline: This is the story of the future that never was.
documents.overview: It has been thirteen years since the Androids began their killing rampage and Son Gohan is the only person fighting back. He takes Bulma's son Trunks as a student and even gives his own life to save Trunks's. Now Trunks must figure out a way to change this apocalyptic future
documents.plot:
Dragon Ball Z: The History of Trunks is a Japanese anime television special based on Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball manga, adapted from a bonus chapter of the series. It originally aired in Japan on February 24, 1993, between episodes 175 and 176 of the Dragon Ball Z television series. The special depicts the bleak alternate future from which the time traveler Trunks came, showing how he and Gohan fought to survive against the Androids 17 and 18, two artificial beings created by Dr. Gero to destroy Goku.

In this timeline, Goku dies of a viral heart disease, and because his death is from natural causes, he cannot be revived with the Dragon Balls. Six months later, two androids appear and kill Earth's greatest fighters, including Piccolo, Vegeta, Krillin, Tien and Yamcha. With Piccolo's death, Kami also dies and the Dragon Balls cease to exist, leaving no way to bring anyone back to life.

Thirteen years later, the androids have killed most of humanity and continue to terrorize the remaining survivors for sport. Gohan, Goku's son and the only surviving warrior, has become a Super Saiyan but still cannot defeat them. He trains Trunks, the teenage son of Vegeta and Bulma, who longs to reach the Super Saiyan level himself. After a battle in which Gohan loses an arm, he knocks Trunks unconscious and goes to face the androids alone, fearing that Earth would be left without a defender if both of them died. When Trunks finds Gohan's body, his grief and rage finally transform him into a Super Saiyan. Years later, after failing to defeat the androids alone, Trunks travels back in time in a machine built by his mother to bring Goku a cure for his heart disease, setting up the events of the main series.

The special is known for its dark, tragic tone, which contrasts with much of the series, and for its focus on the bond between Gohan and Trunks.

In North America, the special was released on VHS and DVD in October 2000 by Funimation and later as a remastered double feature with Bardock – The Father of Goku. Anime News Network praised its sympathetic characters and exceptional action sequences, while noting that familiarity with the television series is recommended.

documents.title: Little Fockers
documents.tagline: Kids bring everyone closer, right?
documents.overview: It has taken 10 years, two little Fockers with wife Pam and countless hurdles for Greg to finally get in with his tightly wound father-in-law, Jack. After the cash-strapped dad takes a job moonlighting for a drug company, Jack's suspicions about his favorite male nurse come roaring back. When Greg and Pam's entire clan descends for the twins' birthday party, Greg must prove to the skeptical Jack that he's fully capable as the man of the house.
documents.plot:
Five years after their wedding, Greg Focker and his wife Pam are preparing to celebrate the fifth birthday of their twin children Samantha and Henry, while planning to move to a new house. However, things go awry for Greg when his in-laws Jack and Dina Byrnes visit them, and Jack announces that he is looking for his successor as the head of the Byrnes family.
Recently, Jack has been diagnosed with a heart condition and has become embittered by his daughter Debbie's divorce from her husband Bob. As Jack's original plan to declare Bob as his successor has failed, and his son Denny is a disappointment to him, he decides to pass the role to Greg, naming him "The Godfocker".
Despite Greg reluctantly accepting the role, Jack remains skeptical and begins to suspect Greg of infidelity when he sees him with drug representative Andi Garcia, who openly flirts with him. The presence of Sustengo, an erectile dysfunction drug that Greg promotes as a side job, also prompts Jack to think that he is no longer sexually attracted to Pam. Furthermore, he starts to doubt his ability to provide for his family when he is initially reluctant to enroll his children in a private school.
During a medical conference promoting Sustengo, Greg meets Bob at a bar and he tells him of Jack's original intention to name him "The Bobfather" as his successor. His relief and happiness with leaving Jack's family makes Greg slightly uncomfortable. Meanwhile, Jack tries to convince Pam to consider divorcing Greg and renewing her relationship with her ex-fiancé Kevin Rawley, whom Jack thinks is more financially and personally suitable for her.
Eventually, following a confrontation with Jack at a clinic, Greg escapes to his and Pam's unfinished new house, where Andi shows up. She tries to cheer him up, but drinks too much wine and makes sexual advances towards him. Watching from a window and misunderstanding the situation, a disappointed Jack leaves and lies to Pam and Dina about not finding Greg.
Greg's parents Bernie and Roz rejoin the family the next day at the twins' birthday party. Enraged at Greg's apparent infidelity, Jack engages him in a physical fight despite Greg insisting that he was rejecting Andi. The fight ends with Jack having a heart attack and collapsing. Greg quickly takes charge of the situation, looking after Jack. As paramedics take him away, Jack quietly admits that he believes Greg after observing his carotid artery, which remained stable while he proclaimed his innocence. Impressed with his integrity and quick thinking, Jack approves of him to be "The Gregfocker".
Four months later, on Christmas Day, Greg and Pam's parents celebrate the holidays with them in their new house. Bernie informs Greg and Pam that he and Roz have sold their Miami home and are moving to Chicago, only two houses away from theirs.

documents.title: Godzilla: Tokyo S.O.S.
documents.original_title: ゴジラ×モスラ×メカゴジラ／東京SOS
documents.tagline: Three giant monsters, one violent final battle!!
documents.overview: Mothra and her fairies return to Japan to warn mankind that they must return Kiryu to the sea, for the dead must not be disturbed. However Godzilla has survived to menace Japan leaving Kiryu as the nation's only defense.
documents.plot:
The Shobijin visit the elderly Shinichi Chujo, his scientist nephew Yoshito, and his grandson Shun to warn them that Godzilla continues returning to Japan because the Japanese government used the first Godzilla's skeleton in the cyborg MFS-3 Kiryu's construction. If the government returns the skeleton to the ocean, Mothra, the descendant of the first Mothra who attacked Japan forty-three years ago, will take Kiryu's place in defending Japan.
As Kiryu undergoes repair and modifications, the Kiryu squadron is sent to the United States for further training, with Kyosuke Akiba taking Akane Yashiro's place should Godzilla return while she is away. Due to the first Mothra's attack, Japanese prime minister Hayato Igarashi denies Chujo's request, but agrees to discontinue the Kiryu project once the cyborg exterminates Godzilla. Sometime later, Godzilla resurfaces to attack Tokyo despite his injuries sustained since the last battle with Kiryu. Chujo and Shun summon Mothra to battle Godzilla. With the repairs finished, the government deploys Kiryu, but Godzilla knocks both it and Mothra out, injuring Chujo and Shun during the fray.
Meanwhile, on Himago Island, the uncharted volcanic island in Ogasawara island chain, twin Mothra larvae hatch from their egg and rush to help their mother. As Yoshito, with help from the Shobijin, uses a maintenance hatch to enter and repair Kiryu from its internal backup cockpit, the Japan Xenomorph Self-Defense Forces (JXSDF) and larvae try to hold Godzilla off, but the injured Mothra sacrifices herself to protect the latter from Godzilla's atomic breath while a separate attack warps Kiryu's maintenance hatch, trapping Yoshito inside. Nonetheless, he completes the repairs, allowing Kiryu to wound Godzilla before its spirit is reawakened by Godzilla's roar.
After the larvae bind Godzilla in a silk cocoon, Akiba is ordered to kill Godzilla per Yoshito and the Shobijin's request. However, Kiryu lifts Godzilla and uses its boosters to carry them both out to sea. Akiba's fellow pilot, Azusa Kisaragi, blasts the hatch open. Kiryu turns over to let Yoshito escape before it plunges into the ocean and drifts into an underwater trench with Godzilla. As Japan celebrates their victory, Yoshito salutes Kiryu while the larvae return to Infant Island with the Shobijin.
In a post-credits scene, an undisclosed laboratory is shown with canisters containing the DNA of numerous monsters.

documents.title: Secretariat
documents.tagline: The Impossible True Story
documents.overview: Housewife and mother Penny Chenery agrees to take over her ailing father's Virginia-based Meadow Stables, despite her lack of horse-racing knowledge. Against all odds, Chenery - with the help of veteran trainer Lucien Laurin - manages to navigate the male-dominated business, ultimately fostering the first Triple Crown winner in 25 years.
documents.plot:
In 1969, Denver housewife and mother Penny Chenery learns of her own mother's death and returns to her childhood home, where she reunites with Mrs. Ham, her father's secretary, and comforts her confused and elderly father. At her mother's funeral, Penny meets Arthur "Bull" Hancock and his son, Seth Hancock, of Claiborne Farm in Kentucky. The Hancocks offer any help she may need during her efforts to bring Meadow Stables back to profitability. Penny's brother Hollis informs her of a dishonest sale that was about to be made by the trainer until their mother stopped him. Penny fires the trainer and asks Bull Hancock to help her find a new trainer. He recommends Lucien Laurin, an aging French Canadian, who initially turns down Penny's offer.
Penny's father make a deal with leading owner Ogden Phipps that if Phipps bred his best stallion (Bold Ruler) to Chenery's two best mares (Somethingroyal and Hasty Matelda), the two owners would each receive one foal, flipping a coin to decide who would choose. Bold Ruler, the stallion, was fast but couldn't last over distances. Hasty Matelda is the obvious choice for her young age, but Somethingroyal's bloodline is made up of many horses with good stamina. Penny hopes to choose Somethingroyal's foal for the interesting mix of speed and stamina. Phipps wins the toss and chooses Hasty Matelda's foal, leaving Penny with Somethingroyal's foal, Secretariat.
When Secretariat enters his first race at Aqueduct race track in Queens, New York City, everyone has high expectations. The jockey, Paul Feliciano, is young with little experience, which worries Penny, but Lucien reassures her. During the race, Secretariat is repeatedly hit by other horses and comes in fourth. Penny and Lucien argue, and Lucien blames Paul for the loss, but Penny realizes the only way that Secretariat will ever win is if he has an experienced jockey. Penny's flight back home is canceled on the day of the race, and she misses her daughter Kate's solo in a play, but her son holds up the pay phone so Penny can hear Kate sing.
Penny gets experienced Canadian jockey Ron Turcotte to ride Secretariat to many victories. Secretariat is named horse of the year after a successful two-year-old season. Penny's father suffers a stroke and dies, leaving Penny and her brother Hollis to inherit the estate. Although she needs six million dollars to pay estate taxes, Penny refuses to sell Secretariat and instead syndicates him, selling 32 shares worth more than six million dollars, as long as he can win a three-year-old distance race. She tries to sell a share to Ogden Phipps, who instead offers to buy the horse for seven million dollars. Penny refuses to sell him. When Phipps demands to know why, she tells him Secretariat's value will triple when he wins the Triple Crown – a feat no horse has accomplished in twenty-five years. During this time, Frank "Pancho" Martin, trainer of rival horse Sham, tries to provoke a match race with Secretariat.

documents.title: RED
documents.tagline: Still armed. Still dangerous. Still got it.
documents.overview: After surviving an assault from a squad of hit men, retired CIA black ops agent Frank Moses reassembles his old team for an all-out war. Frank reunites with old Joe, crazy Marvin and wily Victoria to uncover a massive conspiracy that threatens their lives. Only their expert training will allow them to survive a near-impossible mission -- breaking into CIA headquarters.
documents.plot:
RED is a 2010 action comedy film directed by Robert Schwentke, based on the comic book series of the same name by Warren Ellis and Cully Hamner. The movie stars Bruce Willis, Helen Mirren, John Malkovich, Morgan Freeman, and Mary-Louise Parker.

The story begins with Frank Moses (Bruce Willis), a retired CIA operative who lives a quiet life in Asheville, North Carolina, under an assumed identity. However, his peaceful existence is disrupted when he receives a mysterious phone call from his old colleague, Marvin Boggs (John Malkovich). Boggs reveals that he has been murdered and leaves behind a cryptic message for Moses.

Moses soon discovers that he is being hunted by the CIA and other government agencies, who want to silence him due to his knowledge of classified information. He teams up with Sarah Ross (Mary-Louise Parker), his ex-wife, and Marvin's widow, Victoria (Helen Mirren). Together, they embark on a mission to uncover the truth behind Boggs' murder and clear Moses' name.

As they delve deeper into the conspiracy, they are joined by Harry Bellafonte (Morgan Freeman), another retired CIA operative who has been hiding in plain sight as a florist. The group soon realizes that they are being pursued by a ruthless agent named Beck (Brian Cox) and his team.

Throughout their journey, Moses and his team encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, deadly assassins, and unexpected allies. Along the way, they also uncover a web of deceit and corruption within the CIA, which threatens to destroy their lives.

As the stakes grow higher, Moses and his team must use their skills and experience to stay one step ahead of their pursuers. In a thrilling climax, they engage in an intense battle with Beck's team, resulting in a dramatic showdown that will determine their fate.

Ultimately, Moses and his team succeed in exposing the truth behind Boggs' murder and bringing down the corrupt agents who have been hunting them. The movie concludes with Moses and Sarah reuniting, while Harry finds redemption by finally revealing himself to the world as a retired CIA operative.

Overall, RED is an action-packed comedy that pays homage to the classic spy films of the 1960s and 1970s. With its witty dialogue, memorable characters, and high-octane action sequences, it has become a beloved favorite among fans of the genre.

documents.title: Mega Piranha
documents.tagline: They were created to save mankind. Something went wrong.
documents.overview: When a science experiment goes horribly wrong, gigantic fish gain appetites for human flesh.
documents.plot:
The film focuses on the Orinoco River in Venezuela, where a strain of genetically modified piranha have escaped into an isolated tributary of the river. Through human interference of the local environment, the megapiranha manage to escape from their isolated spot and swim downstream, killing all that cross their path. The megapiranha gradually make their way towards Florida at the height of the tourist season.
After the outbreak, a team including Special Agent Fitch and Sarah Monroe, work to contain the megapiranhas within Venezuela. They begin to get into trouble with the authorities when they attempt to cross over the Venezuelan border. Not having proper clearance and documentation, Special Agent Fitch resorts to using the diplomacy of his fist and drives off. He is pursued by Colonel Antonio Diaz in a high-speed chase through the jungle. Throughout the chase, Fitch alternates driving a Toyota Camry and Hyundai Elantra while Diaz is seen at different points in a GMC Jimmy, Chevrolet Suburban, Suzuki XL-7, and Ford Explorer. Fitch escapes by stealing a helicopter and heads to the International Super Bunker (ISB). During the journey, the helicopter runs out of fuel and Sarah Monroe rigs the emergency oxygen tank to the fuel line to make it to the ISB safely.
The megapiranhas continue to move north, consuming two battleships and a nuclear submarine. They eventually reach south Florida, where they kill at least five Puerto Ricans on a beach and manage to blow up two hotels. Meanwhile, the only force that can stop them is located at the ISB. After the megapiranhas prove impervious to both torpedoes and depth charges—and even a nuclear torpedo fails to stop them—Special Agent Fitch and Professor Sarah Monroe conclude that the only way to stop the megapiranhas is to face them in their own terrain: underwater. An army of SCUBA divers armed with guns would make the huge fish bleed, causing them to enter a feeding frenzy and kill each other. If this were to fail, then a massive nuclear strike would be used to destroy the megapiranha, as well as most of Florida.
In the middle of the operation, Colonel Diaz arrives in a helicopter, presumably using multiple fuel tanks to do this journey. The Colonel aims to get revenge on Agent Fitch and throws a rope into the water to trick him into climbing up into the enemy helicopter. Fitch, upon his arrival, shoots the pilot in the mouth with a flare gun, which causes the pilot's head to explode. Fitch then uses a homing beacon (which is actually a canister of CO2) to attract a megapiranha, jumping out of the helicopter shortly before it is consumed by the fishy behemoth.
Fitch is pursued by the megapiranha that ate the helicopter, eventually hiding in a reef where the megapiranha is unable to follow. When the piranha opens its mouth, Fitch shoots his gun at the helicopter still in the beast's jaws. The helicopter explodes, killing the fish.

documents.title: Contagion
documents.tagline: Nothing spreads like fear
documents.overview: As an epidemic of a lethal airborne virus - that kills within days - rapidly grows, the worldwide medical community races to find a cure and control the panic that spreads faster than the virus itself.
documents.plot:
Contagion is a 2011 medical thriller film directed by Steven Soderbergh, produced by Warner Bros. Pictures, and distributed by Warner Bros. The movie stars Matt Damon, Kate Winslet, Jude Law, Laurence Fishburne, Gwyneth Paltrow, Marion Cotillard, and Bryan Cranston.

The story begins with a mysterious outbreak of pneumonia-like symptoms in Shanghai, China. Dr. Ian Sussman (Laurence Fishburne), an epidemiologist at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), is called to investigate the source of the illness. He soon discovers that the disease is highly contagious and spreading rapidly around the world.

As the outbreak spreads, a young woman named Beth Emhoff (Gwyneth Paltrow) returns home from a business trip in Shanghai, only to fall ill with the mysterious pneumonia-like symptoms. Her husband, Mitch (Matt Damon), is frantic with worry as he tries to find out what's happening to his wife.

Meanwhile, Dr. Ally Hextall (Kate Winslet), an infectious disease specialist at the University of Wisconsin, is working on a vaccine for the disease. She teams up with Dr. Jeremy Renner (Jude Law) and Dr. Ellis Cheever (Laurence Fishburne) to develop a treatment.

As the outbreak spreads globally, the world descends into chaos. Governments struggle to contain the spread of the disease, while citizens are left to fend for themselves. The CDC works tirelessly to identify the source of the outbreak and find a cure.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when it is revealed that the disease was not created in a lab, but rather originated from a bat in China. The virus mutates rapidly, making it even more contagious and deadly.

As the world teeters on the brink of disaster, Dr. Sussman and his team work around the clock to develop a vaccine. Meanwhile, Mitch is desperate to find out what happened to his wife and how he can save her.

The movie's climax features a dramatic showdown between Dr. Hextall and the virus, as she works tirelessly to develop a cure. In the end, she succeeds in creating a vaccine that can be mass-produced and distributed globally.

The final scene shows the world slowly returning to normal, with people going about their daily lives once again. The movie ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that humanity has learned from its mistakes and is better equipped to handle future pandemics.

Overall, Contagion is a gripping thriller that explores the rapid spread of a deadly disease and the global response to it. With its talented cast, intricate plot, and timely themes, the movie is both entertaining and thought-provoking.

documents.title: Cats & Dogs: The Revenge of Kitty Galore
documents.original_title: Cats & Dogs: The Revenge of Kitty Galore
documents.tagline: Just like real spies... only furrier.
documents.overview: The ongoing war between the canine and feline species is put on hold when they join forces to thwart a rogue cat spy with her own sinister plans for conquest.
documents.plot:
Cats & Dogs: The Revenge of Kitty Galore is a 2010 American live-action/animated comedy film directed by Chris Columbus and produced by Warner Bros. Entertainment.

The movie begins with the introduction of Kitty Galore (played by Michelle Monaghan), a wealthy socialite and inventor who has lost her cat, Snowball III, to a group of dogs led by Fifi LaFume (voiced by Shirley MacLaine). The dogs, who are secretly working for their owner, Warren Lightman (played by Chris Kattan), have been stealing valuable items from around the world.

Kitty Galore teams up with her former flame, Buddy Cooper (played by Chris Pine), a dog who is also an agent of the FELIS (Federation for the Enforcement of Laws and Inter Species) organization. Together, they hatch a plan to take down Warren Lightman and his canine accomplices.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Kitty Galore's true intentions are not entirely pure. She has a personal vendetta against Warren Lightman, who she believes wronged her in the past. Meanwhile, Buddy Cooper is struggling with his own identity as a dog who was raised by cats and feels like an outsider among both species.

The plot thickens when Snowball III, Kitty Galore's cat, returns to her side, revealing that he has been working undercover for FELIS all along. Together, they concoct a plan to infiltrate Warren Lightman's headquarters and steal the valuable item he is hiding: a powerful device that can control the minds of animals.

The movie culminates in an action-packed showdown between Kitty Galore and her canine enemies. In the end, Kitty Galore emerges victorious, but not without realizing that her true feelings for Buddy Cooper are still strong. The film concludes with Kitty Galore and Buddy Cooper sharing a romantic moment, as Snowball III looks on.

Throughout the movie, there are plenty of humorous moments, including cameos from other celebrities like Jack McBrayer and Bobby Cannavale. The film's blend of live-action and animation adds to its visual appeal, making it an entertaining watch for both kids and adults.

Overall, Cats & Dogs: The Revenge of Kitty Galore is a lighthearted, family-friendly comedy that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and love. While it may not be the most complex or sophisticated film, it delivers plenty of laughs and action to keep audiences entertained.

documents.title: Burning Bright
documents.tagline: His Feeding. Your Frenzy.
documents.overview: After her lousy stepfather steals her savings to buy a vicious tiger, Kelly loses all hope of going to college. But Kelly's situation worsens when a hurricane leaves her and her autistic brother boarded up in their house with the man-eating beast. This edge-of-your-seat thriller follows the gutsy heroine and her younger sibling as they struggle to outwit the ravenous predator and find a way to survive.
documents.plot:
Burning Bright is an American horror thriller of 2010 directed by Carlos Brooks. Briana Evigan stars as Kelly Taylor, a young woman trapped with her autistic younger brother Tom, played by Charlie Tahan, and a starving tiger inside their boarded-up house during a hurricane, with Garret Dillahunt as their stepfather John Gaveneau, Mary Rachel Dudley as their mother Catherine and Meat Loaf in an uncredited role.

Planning to open a safari attraction, John buys a Bengal tiger named Lucifer from a travelling circus. When Kelly tries to place Tom in a care facility before she leaves for college, her payment bounces, and she learns that John has spent the money, which their late mother intended for Tom's care, on the tiger. John refuses to give it back, arguing that there was no will, and has the house boarded up against an approaching hurricane. Kelly is warned that she will lose her scholarship if she defers college yet again. That night someone frees Lucifer inside the house and nails the front door shut.

In the morning Kelly finds a note saying John has gone to the store, spots the tiger prowling the foyer and discovers that Tom is missing from his bed. With the house sealed and emergency lines jammed by the storm, she escapes the tiger by climbing a laundry chute, finds Tom and struggles to keep him safe through his sensory meltdowns. They hide under a bed doused in perfume, in a cupboard from which Kelly smashes an escape route through the wall, and Lucifer wounds her leg. In John's study she discovers life insurance policies on both siblings and a gun, but the first chamber is empty. Kelly breaks out through a window and reaches her car, then returns for Tom, promising never to leave him. Fending Lucifer off with a makeshift torch, she hides Tom in an empty chest freezer and lulls him to sleep. At dawn John returns to unseal the door, and Kelly realises he trapped them; he confesses that he murdered their mother when she planned to leave him. Lucifer then mauls him to death, and Kelly and Tom slip out into the storm-wrecked landscape, hand in hand.

Shot in Florida from July 2008, the film was released straight to DVD by Lionsgate on 17 August 2010. Retrospective reviews were warmer: Bloody Disgusting praised its solid direction and performances, and CHUD called it entertaining and at times surprisingly good.

documents.title: The Cutting Edge: Fire & Ice
documents.overview: Alexandra "Alex" Delgado, a pairs figure skater, found her career come to an abrupt halt after her partner (on and off the ice) became injured. As their love affair cooled, a heartbroken Alex stopped competing and turned to teaching. Enter James Van Behr the smoldering bad boy of speed skating, who has had fiery Alex in his sights as a skating partner ever since he was banned from speed skating. There aren't many girls who say no to him but she may well be the first. However, he pushes her buttons, challenging her like no one else - and her fighting spirit returns. She agrees to be his partner and they begin a grueling practice regimen fueled (and occasionally derailed) by their own tempestuous relationship, which heats up as they get closer to competition. But will their passion destroy Alex's chance to bring home the gold again?
documents.plot:
The Cutting Edge: Fire & Ice is a 2010 American sports romance television film directed by Stephen Herek and written by Holly Brix. Made for the ABC Family cable channel, which first aired it on March 14, 2010, it is the sequel to The Cutting Edge: Chasing the Dream (2008) and the fourth instalment of The Cutting Edge series. Francia Raisa reprises her role as figure skater Alexandra "Alex" Delgado from the third film, opposite Brendan Fehr as a hot-headed speed skater who wants to become her pairs partner.

Alex's competitive career came to an abrupt end when her skating partner, who was also her boyfriend, was injured, and as their romance cooled she stopped competing altogether. Heartbroken, she now earns her living teaching children to skate, avoids dating, and worries her mother, who fears she is throwing away her dreams and will end up alone. James McKinsey, meanwhile, is the cocky bad boy of speed skating, banned from his sport after punching a teammate. With his agent he hatches a plan to switch to pairs figure skating, recruiting Zhen Zheng, a coach who loves a challenge but speaks no English and works through a translator, Mr. Wan. Finding a partner is harder, since most assume the move is merely a publicity stunt until his suspension is lifted. James has long had the fiery Alex in his sights, and she becomes perhaps the first woman to turn him down, but his provocations rekindle her fighting spirit and she agrees to partner him. Their gruelling training regime is repeatedly derailed by their tempestuous relationship. James parties the night before practice and shows up hungover, while the disciplined but cautious Alex hesitates over a daring new move he devises. Gradually, though, they find common ground: they bond during a bar fight, Alex learns that James is good with children, and he discovers she can shoot pool. A game of strip poker is interrupted when Alex's mother drops by. As their mutual attraction grows and the national championships in Montreal draw near, Alex must stay focused and learn to trust both her partner and her own feelings, while James works to overcome his selfish reputation.

Raisa plays Alex and Fehr plays James, with Zhenhu Han as Zhen Zheng, Russell Yuen as Mr. Wan and Dan Jeannotte as Angus Dwell. Reviewers considered it sweet but predictable, praising the chemistry between Raisa and Fehr and the energetic skating sequences, while noting the film's heavy reliance on montages.

documents.title: Mortal Kombat: Rebirth
documents.overview: MORTAL KOMBAT: REBIRTH is a short film released by Kevin Tancharoen (Director) in 2010. It was originally made as a proof of concept for Tancharoen's pitch to Warner Brothers for a reboot movie franchise. This 8-minute short features an intricate fight scene choreographed by Larnell Stovall. It also reintroduces classic Mortal Kombat characters, including: Jax (Michael Jai White), Sonya Blade (Jeri Ryan), Johnny Cage (Matt Mullins), Scorpion (Ian Anthony Dale), Baraka (Lateef Crowder) and Shang Tsung (James Lew).
documents.plot: Deacon City Police Captain Jackson Briggs informs the assassin Hanzo Hasashi about the criminals Reptile and Baraka; the latter has recently killed actor-turned-undercover-officer Johnny Cage in a fight. Briggs believes they were both working for a man named Shang Tsung. He asks Hasashi to kill them in a mysterious tournament hosted by Tsung. When offered his freedom in exchange for accomplishing such tasks, Hasashi reveals that he willingly had himself incarcerated—and could free himself at any time. Then Sonya Blade arrives with a folder and informs Hasashi that his enemy Sub-Zero is alive and the one he killed was his brother. It becomes clear to Hasashi that the terms of his participation in the tournament involve killing Reptile, Baraka and Shang Tsung in return for access to Sub-Zero. Since the real Sub-Zero will be at the tournament, Hasashi, now calling himself Scorpion, agrees to participate.

documents.title: Woochi: The Demon Slayer
documents.tagline: World beware. The wizard is coming.
documents.overview: Spanning four centuries in Korea, this epic action-adventure concerns a powerful pipe and a trio of wizards who will do anything to protect it.
documents.plot:
Five hundred years ago in the Joseon period, the Flute of the prophecy fell into the hands of evil goblins, propelling the world into a whirlwind of disorder. The ancient Taoist wizards turn to the greatest ascetics of their time, the Master (Baek Yoon-sik) and Hwadam (Kim Yoon-seok) for help in vanquishing the goblins and trust each wizard with one-half of the Flute. Meanwhile, the Master's rascal student Jeon Woochi (Gang Dong-won) tricks the king with the art of transformation and creates a fiasco, which makes the three Taoist wizards and Hwadam visit the Master. But they find the Master murdered and his half of the Flute missing. Woochi is framed for the murder, and as punishment, he and his trusty dog Chorangyi (Yoo Hae-jin) are imprisoned inside a scroll by the wizards.
Seoul, 2009. For some strange reason, goblins that had been sealed up in the past begin to appear one by one, wreaking havoc on the city. The three Taoist wizards had been enjoying their years of retirement as a priest, a monk, and a shaman, while Hwadam has long disappeared in order to polish his Taoist art. After much discussion, the three wizards unseal the scroll and call forth Jeon Woochi and Chorangyi. Being offered freedom in return for catching the goblins, Woochi sets out on his task. But what began as a hunt for goblins slowly turns into Woochi's personal sightseeing expedition of the modern-day world. And to top it off, he meets a woman with the same face as the one that had captivated him so many centuries ago (Im Soo-jung). Together with Seo In-kyung (his new, yet old love), Woochi begins his adventure.
Unbeknownst to anyone, Hwadam has been secretly releasing the goblins to distract the Taoist wizards away for his own personal motive. Having taken the Flute for himself, Hwadam intends to release the Arch God who has been imprisoned in a human body. He discovers In-kyung whom he suspects is the Arch God. After failing to make it in the acting business partially due to her innocent and cute looks, Hwadam uses his powers and changes her into a self-assured and savvy actress. The director having been frustrated with his chosen actress' behavior, takes notice of In-kyung and has her cast as his new leading lady. Both Woochi and Chorangyi discover Hwadam's true motive in murdering the Master in order to steal the flute for himself.
Soon the truth comes out when Chorangyi reveals to the three Taoist wizards that Hwadam played them for fools and had murdered the Master in order to take the Flute for himself. Confronting him, the wizards realize that they had wrongfully imprisoned Woochi and trick Hwadam into believing they're giving up the flute. Woochi takes the flute and it leads to a battle between him and Hwadan. The Flute is destroyed, but Hwadam makes his final stand. He is stopped by In-kyung using the Arch-God's power and making the Taoist wizards realize that she was the Arch-God herself.

documents.title: Man, Woman & the Wall
