documents.tagline: Some fantasies should never be fulfilled.
documents.overview: When Ryo, a young magazine reporter, moves into a new apartment he is greeted by the passionate sounds of his astonishingly beautiful neighbor Satsuki. Realizing the wall dividing their apartments is paper thin, the captivated journalist begins to eavesdrop on every detail of the girl next door's life: her conversations, her bubble baths... her breathless cries. While Ryo's fantasies escalate into something bordering on love and obsession, Satsuki becomes increasingly hysterical over the bizarre and dirty phone calls terrorizing her every night. When their lives finally converge delusions and reality blur forcing the unthinkable to happen.
documents.plot:
Man, Woman & the Wall (Japanese: Kikareta Onna) is a 2006 Japanese erotic drama written and directed by Masashi Yamamoto, the filmmaker behind Junk Food. It stars the pinup and adult-video star Sora Aoi, also credited as Sola Aoi, who had moved into mainstream acting a few years earlier, alongside Keita Ōno, Hiroto Katō, Takashi Oda and Shō Nishino. Produced by Transformer, Inc. and running 84 minutes, the film plays with the conventions of the Japanese pink film, the low-budget softcore genre, while gently parodying them.

Ryo Kawase (Ōno) is a reporter for a small magazine who writes about organized crime. His modest income is enough to rent a small apartment with a tiny bathtub and, unfortunately, an extremely thin wall, through which he can hear almost everything that happens next door. His neighbor is the beautiful Satsuki (Aoi), and Ryo soon becomes captivated by the sounds coming from her home: her bubble baths, her lovemaking with her boyfriend Yuta (Katō), and the obscene, frightening phone calls she receives at night. Methodical rather than desperate, he installs a movable microphone along the wall to hear more clearly, and even tells a co-worker casually about what he is doing, while imagining the scenes that go with the sounds. When he and Satsuki eventually meet, their series of platonic dates develops into a sweet friendship. A blind spot in his listening setup, however, leads him to discover that someone else has already bugged her apartment, and Ryo sets out to identify the intruder without revealing what he knows. When Satsuki at last wants to give herself to him, his desire fades: the real woman cannot match the one he has built in his imagination.

The film was released on DVD in the United States by TLA Releasing. Jeffrey M. Anderson of Combustible Celluloid gave it three stars out of four, likening it to an old-fashioned "nudie cutie" but finding it cheerful and spirited, praising Aoi's appeal and the fact that she is given a real role, and noting the director's use of sound, color and the Japanese cityscape, though he found the DVD transfer poor. The Swiss site Molodezhnaja considered it mediocre overall, finding the story thin and the voyeurism theme quickly exhausted, but singled out the ending as its most intelligent part.

documents.title: 16 Wishes
documents.tagline: Everyone's sweet 16 is special, Abby's is magical.
documents.overview: The story about Abby Jensen, a girl who's been eager to reach her 16th birthday and has kept a secret wish list since she was a little girl. When the Big Day actually arrives, utter disaster strikes, leaving Abby to think her birthday is ruined. But when a mysterious box of magical birthday candles arrives to turn things around, Abby's 16 Wishes start to come true. Her day gets better and better...until she makes one wish that threatens to change everything.
documents.plot:
Abby Jensen has been planning her sweet sixteen since she was a little girl and keeps a list of wishes that she wants to come true. When her sixteenth birthday finally arrives, she adds her crush, Logan, as her sixteenth and final wish to the list. Throughout the day, Abby is visited by a peculiar woman named Celeste. Celeste first appears as an exterminator when the Jensens' house is swarmed by wasps from a nest that had been building up for 16 years. Celeste saves Abby's list, but the family is unable to return inside until the wasps are exterminated.
Abby meets her best friend, Jay Kepler, at the bus stop, where he gives her a necklace as a birthday gift. Celeste returns, dressed as a mailwoman, and gives Abby 16 candles and a matchbox. Abby lights the first candle, and her first wish—meeting celebrity Joey Lockhart—is fulfilled. Realizing that the numbers on the candles correspond to the numbers of the wishes on her list, Abby lights the eighth candle, granting her wish for a car. When Celeste emerges from the car, Abby deduces that Celeste is a magical being, as she appears every time a wish is granted.
Abby unsuccessfully attempts her third wish. Celeste warns her that there is a limit to how many wishes can be granted within an hour and that at midnight, the wishes she made will become permanent. Throughout the school day, Abby uses the candles to beat her rival, Krista Cook (who has the same birthday), in a volleyball match and to become student body president.
Jay agrees to take Abby shopping for a dress for her party but drops his wallet. They are followed by Krista, who convinces the clerk to eject them. Abby uses the ninth candle to make a wish to be treated like an adult, creating consequences of adulthood that she did not previously consider: Abby is suddenly 22 years old and no longer in high school. None of her classmates remember her, and she cannot live with her parents due to the ongoing wasp infestation in their home. She has an apartment, but the landlord is ready to evict her for nonpayment of rent. Desperate for an explanation, Abby makes a wish to beckon Celeste. Celeste arrives and reveals that the candles grant her wishes literally, as shown when her wish to be treated like an adult physically turned her into one.
Abby unsuccessfully tries to alter and add to her wish list. When she makes a wish for her parents to understand her, it is granted, but her parents only understand her under the impression that she is an adult. Finding Jay at Krista’s sweet sixteen, she manages to restore his memories of their friendship by showing him the necklace he gave her, but he remains unable to help her. After talking to Krista, Abby learns that the two are on good terms in adulthood and that Jay wanted to be student body president.
Abby returns to her apartment, where she meets Celeste and laments her selfishness.

documents.title: Vampires Suck
documents.tagline: Some sagas just won't die.
documents.overview: Becca, an anxious, non-vampire teen is torn between two boys. Before she can choose, Becca must get around her controlling father, who embarrasses Becca by treating her like a child. Meanwhile, Becca's friends contend with their own romantic issues - all of which collide at the prom.
documents.plot: Becca, an anxious, non-vampire teen is torn between two boys. Before she can choose, Becca must get around her controlling father, who treats her like a child. Meanwhile, Becca's friends contend with their own romantic issues – all of which collide at the prom.

documents.title: Crocodile
documents.tagline: Ever feel like something is watching you?
documents.overview: A group of friends including Brady Turner, Claire and Duncan McKay go out on a boat trip on a lake in Southern California, but their joyful weekend turns into horror, when a giant killer crocodile searching for its stolen eggs, picks off anyone who gets in its way. Can they all escape in one piece or will they slowly and painfully fall to the mammoth reptile.
documents.plot:
Crocodile is a 2000 direct-to-video horror film directed by Tobe Hooper, an international co-production between the United States and Mexico. Mark McLachlan, Caitlin Martin, Chris Solari, D. W. Reiser and Julie Mintz star in a story about college students on a spring-break houseboat trip who unknowingly enrage a giant crocodile that hunts them one by one. It was followed by Crocodile 2: Death Swamp, which has no connection to the original beyond featuring the same giant crocodile and its sole surviving offspring.

Eight young friends, among them Brady, Claire, Duncan, Kit, Annabelle, Sunny, Foster and Hubs, set off on a weekend boat trip on a remote lake in Southern California for spring break. Before they leave, the local sheriff warns them to stay out of trouble. At a bonfire that night, Kit tells the others a local legend about Harlan, an eccentric hotel owner who decades earlier kept an enormous crocodile named Flat Dog as an attraction. Believing the animal to be an avatar of the ancient Egyptian crocodile god Sobek, Harlan built a shrine to it and led a cult of worshippers, until the townspeople drove him out and burned his hotel.

Nearby, two local fishermen destroy a nest of crocodile eggs and are attacked and eaten by a huge crocodile. The next day, while the friends continue to party, Annabelle's dog runs off and the group stumbles upon the same nest, with one of them pocketing an egg. Soon the furious mother crocodile begins stalking them, picking them off as they try to escape through the swamps and back roads around the lake. The survivors seek help from the sheriff, and they must figure out how to stop the animal before it kills them all, while tensions within the group over romance and old grudges complicate their efforts to stay alive.

Crocodile received poor reviews and holds a 25 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on a small number of reviews. Joseph O'Brien of Rue Morgue noted occasional flashes of Hooper's characteristic weirdness, including a scene in which a crocodile hunter attacks the creature that killed his father, and likened the film to an episode of Dawson's Creek in which most of the cast is eaten by a giant reptile, an experience he did not consider entirely unrewarding.

documents.title: Batman: Under the Red Hood
documents.tagline: Dare to Look Beneath the Hood.
documents.overview: One part vigilante, one part criminal kingpin, Red Hood begins cleaning up Gotham with the efficiency of Batman, but without following the same ethical code.
documents.plot:
Ra's al Ghul hires the Joker as a distraction so that Ra's could destroy Europe's financial districts. He realizes his mistake when he is unable to control
Joker, who captures Jason Todd, the second Robin and Batman's partner. In Sarajevo, Bosnia, Joker brutally assaults and tortures Jason in an abandoned warehouse with a crowbar. Joker eventually leaves and locks Jason inside the warehouse with a bomb, which explodes and kills Jason before Batman arrives.
Five years later in Gotham City, a mysterious vigilante called Red Hood assembles a meeting of the city's most prominent drug dealers. He announces a takeover of their drug trade, taking 40 percent of their profit while offering them protection from Black Mask and Batman, but threatens to kill them if anyone is caught dealing drugs to children. Batman stops an attempted theft of a shipment that belonged to Black Mask, which contains the advanced android Amazo. Batman destroys Amazo with the help of Jason's predecessor Dick Grayson, using the name Nightwing, and discovers the thieves are working for Red Hood. The thieves are killed by a sniper shot before they can reveal any more. Batman identifies the shooter as the Red Hood, and chases him to Ace Chemicals. The Red Hood references the creation of the Joker in this same building before blowing up the facility. Batman and Nightwing interrogate Joker at Arkham Asylum about Red Hood, but he denies any involvement.
An infuriated Black Mask puts a hit on Red Hood for Amazo's destruction. Batman and Nightwing prevent Red Hood from hijacking Black Mask's next weapon shipment. They chase Red Hood to a train station, where he escapes after detonating a bomb, which injures Nightwing. As Alfred Pennyworth tends to Nightwing, Batman realizes that the Red Hood is trained and has knowledge of Batman's tactics, gear and his secret identity. Batman recalls Jason performing the same maneuvers as Robin and that Jason grew more violent as he aged.
Black Mask sends the Fearsome Hand of Four to lure Red Hood. They nearly overpower him until Batman helps incapacitate three of them and Red Hood kills the fourth, horrifying Batman. Red Hood explains that he is doing what Batman will not: killing criminals who are not afraid. Batman analyzes a blood sample of Red Hood drawn from the battle and it matches to Jason. After discovering that Jason's corpse is fake, Batman confronts Ra's al Ghul and demands to know the truth. Ra's explains that he felt responsible for Jason's death and, as a peace offering, swapped Jason's body for a fake and revived him in the Lazarus Pit, but following his resurrection, Jason was driven insane and escaped.
After surviving an assassination attempt by Red Hood, Black Mask sets the Joker free, tasking him with killing Red Hood. However, Joker instead abducts Black Mask and the drug dealers and plans to set them on fire. Red Hood appears and reveals his real target is Joker. Batman saves the hostages and Red Hood takes Joker.

documents.title: Trouble Every Day
documents.tagline: The hunger to love.
documents.overview: Shane and June Brown are an American couple honeymooning in Paris in an effort to nurture their new life together, a life complicated by Shane’s mysterious and frequent visits to a medical clinic where cutting edge studies of the human libido are undertaken.
documents.plot: Newlyweds Shane and June arrive in Paris for their honeymoon. In the process of trying to find a cure for his strange, bloodthirsty disease, Shane stumbles upon the story of a doctor and his flesh eating wife.

documents.tagline: It takes a pair to beat the odds.
documents.overview: Inspired by a true story, a comedy centered on a 27-year-old guy who learns of his cancer diagnosis and his subsequent struggle to beat the disease.
documents.plot: Inspired by a true story, a comedy centered on a 27-year-old guy who learns of his cancer diagnosis and his subsequent struggle to beat the disease.

documents.title: I Am Love
documents.overview: Emma left Russia to live with her husband in Italy. Now a member of a powerful industrial family, she is the respected mother of three, but feels unfulfilled. One day, Antonio, a talented chef and her son's friend, makes her senses kindle.
documents.plot: Emma has left Russia to live with her husband in Italy. Now a member of a powerful industrial family, she is the respected mother of three, but feels unfulfilled. One day, Antonio, a talented chef and her son's friend, makes her senses kindle.

documents.title: Men in Black 3
documents.tagline: Back in time.
documents.overview: Agents J and K are back...in time. J has seen some inexplicable things in his 15 years with the Men in Black, but nothing, not even aliens, perplexes him as much as his wry, reticent partner. But when K's life and the fate of the planet are put at stake, Agent J will have to travel back in time to put things right. J discovers that there are secrets to the universe that K never told him - secrets that will reveal themselves as he teams up with the young Agent K to save his partner, the agency, and the future of humankind.
documents.plot:
Men in Black 3 is a science fiction comedy film directed by Barry Sonnenfeld and released in 2012 by Columbia Pictures.

The movie takes place in 2012, with Agent J (Will Smith) and Agent K (Tommy Lee Jones) on a mission to stop an alien threat. However, during the mission, Agent K is killed by an alien, leaving Agent J alone to carry on his work.

In order to prevent the destruction of the world, Agent J travels back in time to 1969, where he meets a younger version of Agent K (played by Josh Brolin). The two agents must work together to stop an evil alien named Boris the Animal (Jemaine Clement) from killing Agent K and taking over the world.

As they travel through time, Agent J learns about the origins of the Men in Black organization and the history of Agent K. He also discovers that Boris was once a member of the organization but became corrupted by his own power and desire for revenge against Agent K.

Throughout their journey, Agent J and Agent K encounter various characters from the 1960s, including a young version of Agent Z (Michael Stuhlbarg) and a young version of Agent O (Emma Thompson). They also visit iconic locations such as Woodstock and the Apollo 11 launch site.

As they get closer to stopping Boris, Agent J and Agent K must navigate through time and confront their own personal demons. Along the way, Agent J learns more about his own past and the origins of the Men in Black organization.

In the end, Agent J and Agent K successfully stop Boris and prevent him from killing Agent K. However, Agent J is left to return to his own time, where he finds that 2012 has been destroyed by an alien invasion. The movie ends with Agent J and Agent Z (played by Michael Stuhlbarg) working together to rebuild the world.

Men in Black 3 received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $624 million worldwide. The movie's blend of action, comedy, and science fiction elements made it a fun and entertaining ride for audiences.

documents.title: Noel
documents.tagline: Miracles are closer than you think
documents.overview: Christmas Eve in New York, and the lonely divorced publisher, Rose Collins, needs a miracle to improve the health of her mother, interned in a hospital with Alzheimers. She feels sorry for another patient and meets his visitor. Meanwhile, Nina Vasquez breaks her engagement with her beloved fiancé Mike due to his suffocating jealousy, but misses him. Mike is stalked by a stranger, bartender Artie Venzuela. The poor Jules arranges to spend Christmas Eve in the hospital, where he spent the best Christmas of his life when he was a teenager. The lives of some of these characters cross with others along the night.
documents.plot:
Noel is a 2004 American Christmas drama directed by Chazz Palminteri and written by David Hubbard. Its ensemble cast includes Penélope Cruz, Susan Sarandon, Paul Walker, Alan Arkin and Daniel Sunjata, with Robin Williams in an uncredited role. The film follows several intersecting stories that unfold on Christmas Eve in New York City,.

Rose Collins, a divorced publisher, struggles to care for her mother, who has Alzheimer's disease. As she considers suicide on a riverbank, a former priest named Charlie Boyd saves her, and they spend the night together at her apartment. Charlie admits he has lost his faith, but the next morning he tells Rose that it has been restored by a telepathic conversation with her mother, who wants Rose to move on with her life. Furious, Rose throws him out.

A young couple, Nina Vasquez and Mike Riley, are close to breaking up because of Mike's growing jealousy, and when he attacks one of Nina's platonic friends, she leaves him. At her family's Christmas celebration she meets Rose, who has ended up at the house through a series of coincidences, and the two women go to a bar. Meanwhile, an elderly waiter, Artie Venizelos, searches for his late wife every Christmas and becomes convinced that Mike is her reincarnation, making advances toward him. When Artie collapses and is taken to the hospital, Mike learns from a colleague that Artie once committed manslaughter in a jealous rage and that his wife then died in a car crash that was a suicide. Mike takes this as a sign that he must conquer his own jealousy. A depressed young man, Jules Calvert, whose only happy memory is a Christmas party in a hospital when he was a teenager, lets a criminal break his hand in hope of reliving it, only to learn that the past cannot be recovered. Rose, ashamed of how she treated Charlie, returns to the hospital and finds that he has been in a coma for some time and has no visitors. Across the hall, her mother has finally started eating thanks to Dr. Baron, and Rose agrees to have dinner with him.

Noel premiered at the 2004 Toronto International Film Festival and was acquired by Convex Group, owner of the Flexplay disposable DVD technology, which gave it a "trimultaneous" release in cinemas, on self-expiring Flexplay discs and on TNT within the same month. Critics largely dismissed it as sentimental; it holds a 28% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, and Dave Kehr of The New York Times called it a heap of platitudes.

documents.title: The Illusionist
documents.tagline: When life loses its wonder, all it takes is one person who still believes in magic
documents.overview: A French illusionist travels to Scotland to work. He meets a young woman in a small village. Their ensuing adventure in Edinburgh changes both their lives forever.
documents.plot:
In 1959 Paris, an out-of-work illusionist packs his belongings, including an ill-tempered rabbit, and moves to London. Unable to compete with modern entertainment such as rock and roll, he plies his trade at smaller gatherings in bars, cafés, and parties. He accepts the invitation of a drunken party patron to visit a remote Scottish island, where he entertains the locals. Staying in a room above the pub, he meets a girl, Alice, who is captivated by his illusions and kindness, including a gift of red shoes.
Alice believes the downtrodden performer possesses genuine magical powers, and follows him to Edinburgh, where he performs at a modest theatre. They share a room in a run-down guest house favoured by other fading performers. The illusionist sleeps on a couch, and the girl keeps busy by cleaning and cooking food that she shares with the neighbours. The girl's affections even tame the rabbit, but the illusionist's increasingly meagre wages, spent on gifts for Alice, lead him to pawn his magic kit and secretly take on demeaning jobs.
Alice attracts the affection of a handsome young man. After the illusionist sees them walking together, he leaves her with money and a note stating "Magicians do not exist". He also releases the rabbit on Arthur's Seat, where it soon meets other rabbits. As Alice moves in with her boyfriend, the illusionist departs on a train hauled by a locomotive bearing the number 4472. On the train, he performs one last simple magic trick for a child.

documents.title: Black Death
documents.tagline: In an age of darkness one man will face the ultimate battle against evil.
documents.overview: As the plague decimates medieval Europe, rumours circulate of a village immune from the plague. There is talk of a necromancer who leads the village and is able to raise the dead. A fearsome knight joined by a cohort of soldiers and a young monk are charged by the church to investigate. Their journey is filled with danger, but it's upon entering the village that their true horror begins.

A fearsome knight joined by a cohort of soldiers and a young monk are charged by the church to investigate. documents.title: Legend of the Guardians: The Owls of Ga'Hoole
documents.original_title: Legend of the Guardians: The Owls of Ga'Hoole
documents.tagline: On his way to finding a legend...he will become one.
documents.overview: Soren, a young barn owl, is kidnapped by owls of St. Aggie's, ostensibly an orphanage, where owlets are brainwashed into becoming soldiers. He and his new friends escape to the island of Ga'Hoole, to assist its noble, wise owls who fight the army being created by the wicked rulers of St. Aggie's. The film is based on the first three books in the series.
documents.plot:
In a world where owls are the dominant species, the story begins with a young owl named Soren, who lives on the island of Ga'Hoole. Soren is an outcast among his peers due to his unusual appearance and behavior. He is fascinated by the stories of the Great Tree, a sacred place where the ancient wisdom of the owls is stored.

Soren's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets a wise old owl named Ewan, who tells him about the prophecy of the Owls of Ga'Hoole. According to legend, five owls will gather at the Great Tree and choose a new leader to save their world from the evil Pure Ones. Soren is chosen by Ewan to embark on this perilous journey.

Soren sets out with his friends, Kludd, a skilled but arrogant owl, and Gylfie, a young and curious owl. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous landscapes, ferocious predators, and rival owls who seek to claim the leadership of Ga'Hoole for themselves.

As Soren and his companions journey deeper into the unknown, they discover that the Pure Ones are led by a ruthless leader named Blind Eye, who seeks to destroy all non-Pure owls. The group soon realizes that their quest is not just about choosing a new leader but also about saving their world from destruction.

Throughout their journey, Soren and his friends face numerous challenges, including treacherous mountain passes, dark forests, and treacherous rivers. Along the way, they meet other owls who join their cause, including Gylfie's brother, Alaric, and a mysterious owl named Rook.

As the group nears the Great Tree, they are ambushed by Blind Eye's minions, leading to a fierce battle that tests Soren's leadership skills. In the heat of the battle, Soren discovers his true potential as a leader and proves himself worthy of the prophecy.

In the end, Soren and his companions reach the Great Tree, where they face off against Blind Eye in an epic showdown. With the help of his friends and allies, Soren defeats Blind Eye and claims the leadership of Ga'Hoole. The movie concludes with Soren standing atop a mountain, looking out over the land he has saved, surrounded by his fellow owls.

The Legend of the Guardians: The Owls of Ga'Hoole is an action-packed adventure that explores themes of leadership, friendship, and self-discovery. With stunning animation and a richly detailed world, this movie is sure to captivate audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Step Up 3D
documents.tagline: Two Worlds. One Dream.
documents.overview: A tight-knit group of New York City street dancers, including Luke and Natalie, team up with NYU freshman Moose, and find themselves pitted against the world's best hip hop dancers in a high-stakes showdown that will change their lives forever.
documents.plot:
Step Up 3D is a 2010 American dance drama film directed by Jon M. Chu and written by Michael Genet, John Stockwell, and Stephen Peters. The movie stars Kenny Wormald, Amanda Seyfried, Adam G. Sevani, and Sharni Vinson.

The story begins with Tyler Gage (Kenny Wormald), a rebellious teenager who has just been released from juvenile detention after getting into a fight in his hometown of Baltimore. Tyler is determined to turn his life around and prove himself as a dancer. He meets Emily (Amanda Seyfried), the daughter of a wealthy businessman, at an art gallery opening where she is showcasing her mother's artwork.

Tyler and Emily meet again at a high school dance competition, where they bond over their shared passion for dance. Tyler is impressed by Emily's talent and decides to ask her out on a date. As they spend more time together, Tyler learns that Emily is struggling to find her place in the world after being diagnosed with a rare eye condition.

Meanwhile, Tyler's friend Chase (Adam G. Sevani) is trying to make it big as a dancer by performing at various events and competitions. However, his rival, Moose (Sharni Vinson), is also vying for attention and tries to sabotage Chase's performances.

As the story unfolds, Tyler and Emily grow closer, but their relationship is put to the test when Tyler's past comes back to haunt him. His ex-girlfriend, Nora (Mary Elizabeth Winstead), returns to town and tries to win him back. Tyler must choose between his old life and his new one with Emily.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Moose's behavior becomes increasingly erratic and threatening. In a tense confrontation, Moose attacks Chase, leaving him severely injured. Tyler and his friends band together to protect their friend and take down Moose.

In the end, Tyler and Emily confess their love for each other and decide to pursue their dreams together. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Tyler and Emily performing a romantic dance routine in 3D, surrounded by their friends and family.

Throughout the film, the dance sequences are showcased in stunning 3D, adding an extra layer of excitement and energy to the performances. The movie features a range of dance styles, from hip-hop to contemporary, and showcases the talents of its cast.

Overall, Step Up 3D is a heartwarming and action-packed film that explores themes of love, friendship, and redemption. With its impressive dance sequences and strong performances, it's no wonder why this movie became a fan favorite among dance enthusiasts and music lovers alike.

documents.title: Python
documents.tagline: Created by nature... redesigned by man.
documents.overview: Sleepy New Haven California is a small town with a big problem. A sixty foot slithering horror has arrived and shattered the town's tranquillity on it's path of death and destruction... Growing violent and more savage with each attack the gigantic creature soon becomes an unstoppable feeding machine raging beyond control of it's creator, leaving only the stripped bones of it's victims in it's wake.
documents.plot:
Python, released theatrically in the Philippines as Anaconda 2000, is a 2000 American made-for-television horror film directed by Richard Clabaugh about a genetically engineered snake loose near a small town. Its cast of cult favorites includes Frayne Rosanoff as John Cooper, Robert Englund as scientist Anton Rudolph, Casper Van Dien as NSA agent Bart Parker, William Zabka as Deputy Greg Larston, Dana Barron as Kristin, Wil Wheaton as Tommy, Jenny McCarthy as Francesca Garibaldi.

An NSA plane crashes near the town of Ruby after its cargo, an enormous reticulated python, breaks free. The snake survives and kills two women camping in the woods. When one victim's body is found corroded by acid, suspicion falls on John, who works at a plating plant that uses acid. Parker prepares to recapture the creature with Anton, one of its creators, who explains that it is a hybrid of several snake species able to spray corrosive stomach acid and warns that Parker's men are outmatched. The python kills a real estate agent and his client, Francesca, and after more bodies turn up, Sheriff Griffin Wade closes the plant and arrests John, though he must free him when the NSA arrives with a cover story blaming a rogue operative.

Tracking the snake by radar, the NSA team open fire on what proves to be its shed skin, and the python wipes them out, leaving Anton as the only survivor. The next morning it kills Tommy and attacks his girlfriend, Theresa, who hides after it wrecks her truck. John and Kristin find the wreck, are chased to the water treatment center, and meet Theresa and the shaken Anton there. With Greg's help over the radio, they lure the python inside with John as bait, but the bomb fails to go off, and Anton sacrifices himself to detonate it manually. The python emerges unharmed, so the survivors trick it into the plating plant and push its vulnerable underbelly into a vat of acid, killing it. Six months later the plant has become a bar and bike shop that trades on the story, Greg has been accepted to Quantico to train with the FBI, and John announces that Kristin is pregnant.

Shot in Los Angeles and Malibu, Python premiered on U.S. television on August 9, 2000, and opened in Philippine theaters on October 25, 2000, under a title linking it to the unrelated 1997 film Anaconda. Reviews were mixed, praising the ensemble while faulting the effects and story. It was followed by three made-for-TV sequels: Pythons 2, New Alcatraz and Boa vs. Python.

documents.title: Faster
documents.tagline: Slow justice is no justice
documents.overview: After 10 years in prison, Driver is now a free man with a single focus - hunting down the people responsible for brutally murdering his brother.
documents.plot:
Faster is a 2010 American action thriller directed by George Tillman Jr. from a script by Tony and Joe Gayton. Dwayne Johnson stars as a recently released convict on a mission of revenge, with Billy Bob Thornton, Oliver Jackson-Cohen, Carla Gugino, Maggie Grace, Mike Epps, Moon Bloodgood, Adewale Akinnuoye-Agbaje and Tom Berenger in the supporting cast. CBS Films released it in the United States on November 24, 2010, with Sony handling international distribution.

Upon walking out of prison, Jimmy Cullen, credited only as "Driver," picks up a 1970 Chevrolet Chevelle, a handgun and a list of names. He drives straight to a telemarketing office in Bakersfield, California, and shoots a man named Prescott Ashton. He then confronts Roy Grone, who supplied the car and weapon, and pressures him for more information. Driver is soon pursued on two fronts: by a pair of detectives, the veteran Slade Humphries and his partner Cicero, and by a wealthy, highly skilled hitman known only as "Killer," who has been hired to stop him.

The next name on the list leads Driver to Kenneth Tyson, a man who records snuff films, whom he kills before escaping a hallway shootout with Killer. The encounter troubles the assassin, who proposes to his girlfriend Lily and becomes personally fixated on finishing the job. Meanwhile, the detectives dig into Driver's past and learn that he was double-crossed after a bank robbery years earlier. Cicero recalls a video, filmed by Tyson, showing the murder of Driver's older half-brother Gary and a man shooting Driver in the head; he survived only because of a metal plate surgically placed in his skull. As Driver works his way through the gang responsible, the hunters and the hunted converge, and the true identity of the man who orchestrated the betrayal is revealed.

Faster received mixed reviews from critics. On Rotten Tomatoes about 41% of 128 reviews were positive, and the site's consensus welcomed Johnson's return to hard-hitting action roles while judging that the film did not deliver enough of the thrills it promised. Commentators often compared its lean, brooding tone to the revenge thrillers of the 1970s, and it marked a deliberate shift by Johnson away from the family comedies he had made in the preceding years.

documents.title: Lottery Ticket
documents.tagline: Winning is Just the Beginning Surviving is Another Story
documents.overview: Kevin Carson is a young man living in the projects who has to survive a three-day weekend after his opportunistic neighbors find out he's holding a winning lottery ticket worth $370 million
documents.plot: Kevin Carson is a young man living in the projects who has to survive a three-day weekend after his opportunistic neighbors find out he's holding a winning lottery ticket worth $370 million.

documents.title: Let Me In
documents.tagline: Innocence dies. Abby doesn't.
documents.overview: A bullied young boy befriends a young female vampire who lives in secrecy with her guardian.  A remake of the movie “Let The Right One In” which was an adaptation of a book.
documents.plot: A bullied young boy befriends a young female vampire who lives in secrecy with her guardian.  A remake of the movie “Let The Right One In” which was an adaptation of a book.

documents.title: Paranormal Activity 2
documents.tagline: In 2009 you demanded it. Nothing can prepare you for what's next.
documents.overview: Days after welcoming a newborn baby, Dan and Kristi Rey return home one day to find their house ransacked with seemingly no explanation. Their fear forces them to put in security cameras, which begin to capture strange activity around the house.
documents.plot:
Paranormal Activity 2 is a 2010 American supernatural horror film directed by Todd Lincoln and written by Marcus Nispel, Christopher Landon, and Oren Peli. The movie serves as a prequel to the first film and explores the events that led up to the original story.

The film begins with Katie Featherston's character, Katie, now 19 years old, living in a new apartment with her boyfriend, Micah (Mark Fredrichs). They are trying to start their life together after the traumatic events of the previous year. However, strange occurrences begin to happen, and they soon discover that their apartment is haunted by an evil spirit.

As the haunting intensifies, Katie starts experiencing terrifying visions and nightmares, which she believes are connected to her sister, Kristi (Sprague Grayden), who died in a car accident two years ago. The entity seems to be targeting Katie, and Micah tries to help her cope with the situation.

Meanwhile, a documentary crew, led by Dr. Fredric Foster (John Gulager), is filming Katie's experiences as part of an experiment to capture evidence of paranormal activity. As the haunting escalates, the crew becomes increasingly entangled in the events unfolding before their cameras.

Throughout the film, it becomes clear that the entity is not just a random spirit but is actually connected to Kristi's death and the family's dark past. The entity seems to be manipulating Katie's perceptions of reality, making her question what is real and what is not.

As the story unfolds, Micah starts to experience strange occurrences as well, which suggests that he may also be vulnerable to the entity's influence. The tension builds up as Katie becomes more and more desperate to uncover the truth behind the haunting.

In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Kristi's death was not an accident but a deliberate act of murder committed by her boyfriend, who was possessed by the evil spirit at the time. The entity has been manipulating events from beyond the grave, using Katie as its vessel to exact revenge on Micah and his family.

The film culminates in a terrifying climax as Katie confronts the entity head-on, determined to put an end to the haunting once and for all. In the end, Katie manages to defeat the entity, but not before it unleashes a devastating attack that leaves her severely traumatized.

Paranormal Activity 2 received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $193 million worldwide. The film's prequel status allowed it to explore new themes and characters while still maintaining the core essence of the original story.

documents.title: Saw 3D
documents.tagline: Do you want to play a final game?
documents.overview: (AKA- Saw: The Final Chapter)  As a deadly battle rages over Jigsaw's brutal legacy, a group of Jigsaw survivors gathers to seek the support of self-help guru and fellow survivor Bobby Dagen, a man whose own dark secrets unleash a new wave of terror.
documents.plot:
Saw 3D is a 2010 American supernatural thriller film directed by Kevin Greutert and written by Patrick Melton and Marcus Nispel. The film stars Tobin Bell, Costas Mandylor, Betsy Russell, and Sean Patrick Flanery.

The story begins with Jigsaw (Tobin Bell), also known as John Kramer, who is revealed to be alive in a hospital bed after being mortally wounded by his own trap. He explains that he has been watching the events of the previous films from his hospital room and decides it's time for one final test.

The main plot follows Dr. Lawrence Gordon (Cary Elwes), who is still recovering from his ordeal in Saw II, and Adam Faulkner (Sean Patrick Flanery), a young man who has been diagnosed with a terminal illness. Jigsaw tasks them with finding the next victim, Amanda Young (Shawnee Smith), who has escaped from one of his traps.

As they search for Amanda, they are joined by Detective Eric Matthews (Costas Mandylor) and his son Daniel (Chris Pascoe). The group soon discovers that Amanda is being held captive in a warehouse, where she is forced to participate in a series of gruesome tests designed by Jigsaw.

Throughout the film, the characters must work together to survive the traps and uncover the secrets behind Jigsaw's motivations. Along the way, they are forced to confront their own personal demons and make difficult choices that will ultimately determine who will live and who will die.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Amanda is not what she seems, and her true intentions are revealed. The film builds towards a shocking twist, which reveals that Jigsaw's plan was not just about testing his victims, but also about finding a way to transfer his consciousness into a new body.

The film culminates in a tense showdown between the characters and Amanda, who has become increasingly unhinged as the tests progress. In the end, only one person is left alive, and it is revealed that Jigsaw's plan was successful, but at a great cost.

Overall, Saw 3D is a thrilling and suspenseful film that explores the themes of mortality, morality, and the consequences of playing with fire. The film's twist ending adds a new layer of complexity to the series, leaving audiences questioning what is real and what is just a product of Jigsaw's twisted imagination.

documents.title: Scream 4
documents.tagline: New decade. New rules.
documents.overview: Sidney Prescott, now the author of a self-help book, returns home to Woodsboro on the last stop of her book tour. There she reconnects with Sheriff Dewey and Gale, who are now married, as well as her cousin Jill and her Aunt Kate. Unfortunately, Sidney's appearance also brings about the return of Ghostface, putting Sidney, Gale, and Dewey, along with Jill, her friends, and the whole town of Woodsboro in danger.
documents.plot:
Scream 4 is a 2011 American slasher film directed by Wes Craven and written by Kevin Williamson. The movie takes place 10 years after the events of the original Scream, with the Ghostface killer still at large.

The story begins with Sidney Prescott (Neve Campbell), now a successful author, returning to Woodsboro for the release of her new book, "Truth or Dare." She is accompanied by her husband, Phil (David Arquette), and their teenage daughter, Jill (Emma Roberts). The town has changed little since the original murders, and Sidney is still haunted by the traumatic events of her past.

As the story unfolds, a series of murders takes place in Woodsboro, with the killer using the same tactics as the original Ghostface. The main suspect is Charlie Walker (Rory Culkin), a high school student who has been obsessed with Sidney since childhood. However, it becomes clear that there are multiple killers involved, each with their own motivations and backstories.

One of the new characters introduced in Scream 4 is Jill Roberts, Sidney's daughter, who becomes the target of the Ghostface killer. As the body count rises, Jill finds herself at the center of a new wave of terror, forcing her to confront the dark legacy of her mother's past.

Throughout the movie, the characters are forced to navigate their own personal demons and relationships, all while trying to uncover the identity of the killer. The film pays homage to the original Scream, with many nods to the first two movies, including a memorable scene in which Jill is stalked by the Ghostface killer in a similar fashion to Sidney's experiences.

As the plot thickens, it becomes clear that the killers are not just random psychopaths, but rather individuals who have been influenced by the original murders. The film's climax features a shocking twist, as the true identity of the killer is revealed, and the motivations behind their actions are exposed.

Ultimately, Scream 4 delivers on its promise of a thrilling and suspenseful ride, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats. While some may find the film's self-awareness and meta-humor to be a bit too much, it is undeniable that Wes Craven and Kevin Williamson have crafted a movie that is both a loving tribute to the original Scream and a fresh take on the horror genre.

In conclusion, Scream 4 is a masterclass in suspenseful storytelling, with a complex web of characters and plot twists that will keep viewers guessing until the very end. With its blend of humor, horror, and social commentary, it is a must-see for fans of the franchise and horror enthusiasts alike.

documents.title: One Piece: Strong World
documents.original_title: ワンピース フィルム ストロングワールド
documents.tagline: There's gonna be a rumble in the jungle!
documents.overview: 20 years after his escape from Impel Down, the legendary pirate Shiki, the Golden Lion, reappears causing massive upheaval to the Marines. During his long seclusion, he was able to come up with a scheme to bring the World Government to his knees. On his way to execute the plan, Shiki crosses paths with the Straw Hat Pirates and becomes so impressed with Nami's knowledge of meteorology that he abducts her to forcedly enlist her into his crew. Luffy and the gang end up on a strange land populated with monstrous beasts as they desperately search for Shiki and Nami.
documents.plot:
One Piece Film: Strong World is a 2009 Japanese animated fantasy adventure film directed by Munehisa Sakai from a screenplay by Hirohiko Kamisaka, and the tenth feature film based on Eiichiro Oda's manga One Piece. Oda served as executive producer and created the original story and character designs, a first for the franchise. Mayumi Tanaka voices Monkey D. Luffy, with Kazuya Nakai, Akemi Okamura, Kappei Yamaguchi and Hiroaki Hirata, and actor Naoto Takenaka voices the villain Shiki. It was released in Japan on 12 December 2009.

Shiki, the legendary pirate known as the Golden Lion, who escaped from the prison Impel Down twenty years earlier, uses his Devil Fruit power to make objects float and destroys a fleet of Navy ships, sending a warning to Vice Admiral Garp and Fleet Admiral Sengoku. Days earlier, the Straw Hat Pirates read news of attacks in the East Blue, their home sea, and Luffy vows to protect it, just as Shiki's flying ship appears above them. During a storm, Nami's skill as a navigator impresses Shiki, who learns that she warned of the danger. He offers to take the crew to the East Blue, but instead abducts Nami and scatters the rest of the Straw Hats across his floating islands.

The islands are inhabited by monstrous animals created through genetic experiments by Shiki's eccentric scientist, Doctor Indigo. Luffy fights his way through the beasts, while the crew, split into groups, struggles to survive. Shiki tries to persuade Nami to become his navigator, revealing his plan to use the evolved creatures to conquer the East Blue as a demonstration of his power against the World Government. To protect her friends and the villagers of the islands, Nami pretends to accept, while secretly trying to sabotage his plan. With the help of a small electric bird named Billy, whom Shiki rejected, Luffy and the reunited crew storm Shiki's fortress to rescue Nami, leading to a climactic battle between Luffy and the Golden Lion.

Strong World received praise for its story, animation and action, and was a major box-office success in Japan, grossing over 4.8 billion yen and becoming the highest-grossing One Piece film at the time.

documents.title: The Smurfs
documents.tagline: Smurf Happens.
documents.overview: When the evil wizard Gargamel chases the tiny blue Smurfs out of their village, they tumble from their magical world and into ours -- in fact, smack dab in the middle of Central Park. Just three apples high and stuck in the Big Apple, the Smurfs must find a way to get back to their village before Gargamel tracks them down.
documents.plot:
The Smurfs is a 2011 American fantasy comedy film directed by Raja Gosnell and produced by Jerry Mendelsohn, Jordan Kerner, and Peter Venkata. The movie is based on the Belgian comic book series created by Peyo.

Beginning:
The film opens with Papa Smurf (voiced by Hank Azaria) warning his fellow Smurfs about a powerful sorcerer named Gargamel (played by Johnny Knoxville), who seeks to capture them and use their essence to gain immortality. The Smurfs are living in harmony in the forest, but they know that Gargamel's return is imminent.

Plot Development:
The story follows Brainy Smurf (voiced by Jayma Mays) as he discovers a magical book that allows him to travel through time and space. He decides to take his friends on a trip to New York City, where they can experience the human world. However, Gargamel and his cat, Azrael, also discover the book's location and follow the Smurfs to the city.

As the Smurfs navigate the urban jungle, they encounter various obstacles, including traffic, skyscrapers, and humans who are unaware of their existence. Meanwhile, Brainy Smurf becomes smitten with a human woman named Sophie (played by Emma Stone), who is initially oblivious to the Smurfs' presence.

Plot Twist:
As Gargamel's plan unfolds, he uses Azrael to capture the Smurfs and extract their essence. However, Brainy Smurf's book allows him to travel back in time and warn his friends about the impending danger. The Smurfs work together to outsmart Gargamel and Azrael, using their unique skills to evade capture.

Climax:
The final confrontation takes place at the Empire State Building, where the Smurfs face off against Gargamel and Azrael. Brainy Smurf uses his book to create a portal that allows him to travel back in time and prevent Gargamel from capturing the Smurfs' essence.

Ending:
In the end, the Smurfs successfully defeat Gargamel and return to their forest home. Sophie, who has grown attached to the Smurfs, decides to leave New York City with Brainy Smurf, starting a new life together. The film concludes with the Smurfs returning to their village, where they are welcomed back as heroes.

Overall, The Smurfs is a lighthearted and entertaining film that brings the beloved comic book characters to life on the big screen. While it may not be a critically acclaimed movie, it provides plenty of humor and action for fans of all ages.

documents.title: Yogi Bear
documents.tagline: Please do not feed the bears.
documents.overview: A documentary filmmaker travels to Jellystone Park to shoot a project and soon crosses paths with Yogi Bear, his sidekick Boo-Boo, and Ranger Smith.
documents.plot: A documentary filmmaker travels to Jellystone Park to shoot a project and soon crosses paths with Yogi Bear, his sidekick Boo-Boo, and Ranger Smith.

documents.title: StreetDance 3D
documents.tagline: Teo Worlds. One Dream.
documents.overview: In order to win the Street Dance Championships, a dance crew is forced to work with ballet dancers from the Royal Dance School in exchange for rehearsal space.
documents.plot:
In inner city London, a street dance crew "Jay-20" is on the verge of breaking up after its leader, Jay (Ukweli Roach), leaves the group unexpectedly, leaving his girlfriend Carly (Nichola Burley) in charge of the crew. The group loses the use of their usual rehearsal space. With a big street dance competition approaching the crew is forced to try and raise money or practice in other locations. Eventually they secure a space in a ballet school, on the condition that they include five ballet dancers in their routine for the competition. At first, they struggle to get along, but they all become friends in the end.
One of the teachers at the ballet school, Helena (Charlotte Rampling), takes Carly to a ballet where she starts getting ideas for their routine. When she arrives home, Carly finds Jay waiting for her and the two spend the night having sex. During a dance battle in a club the next night, the team learn that Jay has betrayed the team by joining The Surge, a rival crew. All for the sake of winning the competition. Jay brags about his sex with Carly and Tomas (Richard Winsor), a ballet dancer, punches Jay out of anger. Carly, upset over her boyfriend's betrayal, flees the club and is nearly hit by a car before Tomas pulls her out of the way. Tomas then takes Carly back to his apartment where they dance on the roof, eventually kissing. Carly then leaves him alone on the roof, while they both look at the sunrise and smile.
The next day at the school, Carly announces that they won't try to be better, they will be themselves by performing a routine that is both street and ballet. And that the new name of their dance crew is "Breaking Point". Another teacher at the school, outraged that her students are being corrupted, deliberately plans a Royal Ballet audition for the same day as the street dance finals. The ballet dancers promise Carly they will make it, but the auditions were running overtime.
In an attempt to give Breaking Point more time to wait for the ballet dancers to arrive, Carly's friend Eddie (George Sampson) goes out onto the dance floor and starts dancing, surprising the crew and wowing the audience. Jay tries to convince Carly to just give up but she states that she is sorry for him. The ballet team turn up in time, and their teacher Helena drives the Royal Ballet judges to the street dancing final so they can see the dancers perform. The routine is a success, Carly and Tomas kiss during the performance, and the crowd is enthralled. Jay is shocked that The Surge have been beaten and he's lost Carly.
The film ends with Breaking Point and The Surge dancing to N-Dubz' "We Dance On".

documents.title: Due Date
documents.tagline: Leave your comfort zone.
documents.overview: Peter Highman must scramble across the US in five days to be present for the birth of his first child. He gets off to a bad start when his wallet and luggage are stolen, and put on the 'no-fly' list. Peter embarks on a terrifying journey when he accepts a ride from an actor.
documents.plot:
Due Date is a comedy film released in 2010, directed by Todd Phillips and starring Robert Downey Jr. and Zach Galifianakis.

The movie begins with Peter Highman (played by Robert Downey Jr.), a successful architect who is on his way to Los Angeles for a medical procedure that will save the life of his pregnant wife, Audrey (played by Michelle Monaghan). However, due to a series of unfortunate events, including a flight cancellation and a missed connection, Peter's plans are derailed.

As he tries to find an alternative route to Los Angeles, Peter meets two men who claim to be traveling to the same destination: Dwayne (played by Zach Galifianakis), a slacker on his way to meet his son for the first time, and Ethan (played by Juliette Lewis's brother Owen Wilson was initially cast but dropped out due to scheduling conflicts), a pregnant woman's husband.

Initially, Peter is frustrated with the duo's antics and lack of motivation, but as they embark on their journey together, he begins to see them in a different light. Dwayne, who has never met his son before, is struggling to come to terms with his new role as a father, while Ethan is trying to prepare himself for the arrival of his child.

As they travel across the country, the trio faces various challenges, including run-ins with eccentric characters, traffic jams, and unexpected detours. Along the way, Peter learns valuable lessons about life, love, and the importance of family. He also begins to see Dwayne as a surrogate son figure, who reminds him of his own father.

As they near their destination, the group encounters a series of comedic misadventures, including a wild night in Albuquerque and a disastrous encounter with a group of bikers. However, despite the setbacks, Peter's bond with Dwayne grows stronger, and he begins to see the world through his friend's eyes.

In the end, Peter finally reaches Los Angeles and reunites with Audrey, who has been waiting anxiously for her husband's return. As they prepare to welcome their new baby, Peter reflects on the journey he shared with Dwayne and realizes that it was a transformative experience that taught him the value of friendship and family.

Throughout the movie, Downey Jr.'s wit and charm shine through as he brings Peter to life, while Galifianakis's deadpan humor provides plenty of comedic moments. The chemistry between the two leads is undeniable, making their unlikely friendship one of the film's most memorable aspects.

Overall, Due Date is a heartwarming comedy that explores themes of family, friendship, and redemption. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and hilarious antics, it's no wonder this movie became a box office hit.

documents.title: Never Let Me Go
documents.tagline: These students have everything they need. Except time.
documents.overview: As children, Kathy, Ruth, and Tommy spend their childhood at an idyllic and secluded English boarding school. As they grow into adults, they must come to terms with the complexity and strength of their love for one another while also preparing for the haunting reality awaiting them.
documents.plot: As children, Kathy, Ruth, and Tommy spend their childhood at an idyllic and secluded English boarding school. As they grow into adults, they must come to terms with the complexity and strength of their love for one another while also preparing for the haunting reality awaiting them.

documents.title: Tekken
documents.tagline: Survival is no game
documents.overview: In the year of 2039, after World Wars destroy much of the civilization as we know it, territories are no longer run by governments, but by corporations; the mightiest of which is the Mishima Zaibatsu. In order to placate the seething masses of this dystopia, Mishima sponsors Tekken, a tournament in which fighters battle until only one is left standing.
documents.plot:
Tekken is a 2009 American science fiction martial arts film loosely based on the video game series developed and published by Namco Bandai Games. Directed by Dwight Little from a screenplay by Alan B. McElroy, it stars Jon Foo as Jin Kazama and Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa as Heihachi Mishima, with Kelly Overton, Ian Anthony Dale, Cung Le, Darrin Dewitt Henson, Candice Hillebrand and Luke Goss. Announced by Namco Bandai in 2002, the film did not begin development until 2007; Little, experienced with sports films, aimed for realism, removing the games' supernatural elements and comic relief characters and casting trained martial artists for its fights.

After a devastating conflict known as the Terror Wars, governments have collapsed and eight megacorporations divide the world, with North America ruled by the Tekken Corporation. To maintain their power, the corporations stage an annual fighting tournament, the Iron Fist, whose champion wins fame and fortune. In 2039, Jin Kazama lives with his mother Jun in the Anvil, a slum surrounding Tekken City, and earns money smuggling contraband for resistance groups. Jun, who raised and trained him alone and told him his father was dead, forbids him from entering the tournament. When Tekken's enforcers hunt Jin down after a run, Jun is killed, and Jin swears revenge against the corporation's chairman, Heihachi Mishima. Finding an old fighter ID revealing that his mother was once an Iron Fist competitor, he wins a wild card place by defeating Marshall Law and enters Tekken City with the backing of former boxer Steve Fox, who reveals that he knew Jun. There Jin befriends the fighter Christie Monteiro and wins brutally against Miguel Caballero Rojo, impressing Heihachi's son Kazuya, whose job offer Jin refuses. After surviving an assassination attempt by Nina and Anna Williams on Kazuya's orders, Jin fights his way through the tournament as Kazuya imprisons his father and seizes control of the corporation, setting the stage for a confrontation that reveals the truth about Jin's family.

Tekken premiered at the American Film Market in November 2009 and was released in Japan by Warner Bros. on March 20, 2010. It was a box-office bomb, grossing $1.6 million worldwide, and critics praised its fight scenes but criticized its unfaithful story and acting, as did the game series' director Katsuhiro Harada. A prequel, Tekken 2: Kazuya's Revenge, followed in 2014.

documents.title: Tom and Jerry: The Fast and the Furry
documents.original_title: Tom and Jerry: The Fast and the Furry
documents.overview: After being evicted from their old house by Tom's owner for causing major damage, cat and mouse Tom and Jerry enter a race entitled the "Fabulous Super Race" to win a mansion.
documents.plot:
Tom and Jerry: The Fast and the Furry is a 2005 American animated action comedy featuring the cat-and-mouse duo Tom and Jerry. Produced by Warner Bros. Animation and Turner Entertainment, it is the third made-for-video Tom and Jerry feature and was written and directed by Bill Kopp, who also voices Tom. The voice cast includes Charlie Adler, Jeff Bennett, John DiMaggio, Jess Harnell and Tom Kenny. Released alongside Tom and Jerry: Blast Off to Mars, it marked the 65th anniversary of the characters' 1940 debut. Kidtoon Films gave it a limited theatrical release in selected US cities in September 2005 before it appeared on DVD and VHS, making it the final Tom and Jerry film released on videotape.

After one of their usual chases destroys their house, Tom and Jerry are thrown out by Tom's owner. When they see an advertisement for the "Fabulous Super Race," a televised reality competition offering a mansion to the winner, each builds a car from junkyard parts and heads to Globwobbler Studios in Hollywood to enter. Their rivals include Grammy, a speed-loving old woman with her dog Squirty; Gorthan, a dark lord who is also a florist; the vain movie star Steed Dirkly; a determined single mother of four called Soccer Mom; and Dr. Professor, an eccentric scientist who eliminates himself before the race begins.

The first leg runs from Hollywood to Mexico, but because the show's ratings are so high, the studio's ruthless head, J.W., keeps extending the race to new and more dangerous locations, beginning with the Amazon jungle and moving on to other far-flung locations around the globe. Throughout the competition Tom and Jerry are more interested in sabotaging each other than in winning, using every trick they can think of. Their schemes frequently backfire on themselves or knock out other racers instead, while the smug Steed repeatedly takes the lead. As the field of competitors shrinks, the two rivals find themselves among the last racers standing, and they must decide whether their feud matters more than the prize.

Reviews were modest. Renee Schonfeld of Common Sense Media gave the film two stars out of five, noting that unlike some of the duo's wittier parodies it was less clever and more simply devoted to thrills and spills. The film's title and premise spoof racing films and reality competition shows of the period.

documents.title: Inuyasha the Movie: Affections Touching Across Time
documents.original_title: 犬夜叉 時代を越える想い
documents.overview: InuYasha is a half-demon who was trapped in the Legendary Tree and was set free by Kagome, a girl who traveled 500 years through time. This time, both of them will have to face Menomaru, a Chinese demon whose father, known as Hyoga, came 300 years ago to invade Japan, but was stopped by InuYasha's Father. InuYasha and Kagome, along with Sango, Miroku, Shippou, Kaede and Myoga, will try to stop Menomaru in his becoming the most powerful demon ever.
documents.plot:
Inuyasha the Movie: Affections Touching Across Time is a 2001 Japanese animated film directed by Norihiro Takemoto and produced by Sunrise. The movie takes place after the events of the first season of the Inuyasha anime series.

The story begins with Inuyasha, Kagome, Miroku, Sango, and Shippo on a journey to find the Sacred Waterfall, which is said to have healing properties that can cure any wound. However, they are not the only ones searching for it, as Naraku, the main antagonist of the series, also seeks to obtain its power.

As they near the waterfall, they encounter a young girl named Kikyo, who is revealed to be Inuyasha's half-sister and the reincarnation of the demon princess. Kikyo has been cursed by Naraku, causing her to lose her memories and become trapped in a time loop, reliving the same day over and over.

Inuyasha and his friends soon discover that Kikyo is stuck in this time loop because she is unable to move on from her past life due to her feelings for Inuyasha. The group decides to help Kikyo break free from the curse by finding a way to make her remember her true identity and love for Inuyasha.

Throughout their journey, the group faces various challenges and obstacles as they try to reach the Sacred Waterfall before Naraku does. Along the way, they also encounter other characters who aid or hinder their progress.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Kikyo's memories are tied to her feelings for Inuyasha, and that she is unable to let go of him even in death. The group must find a way to help Kikyo overcome her emotions and move on from her past life.

In the end, Inuyasha and his friends successfully break the curse, allowing Kikyo to remember her true identity and love for Inuyasha. However, this comes at a great cost, as Kikyo is forced to leave the world of the living behind and return to the afterlife.

The movie ends with Inuyasha reflecting on the events that transpired, realizing that his feelings for Kikyo were genuine but also acknowledging that he must move forward with his life. The film concludes with a sense of closure and new beginnings for the characters, as they look towards their future adventures together.

Overall, Inuyasha the Movie: Affections Touching Across Time is a heartwarming and emotional tale that explores themes of love, loss, and redemption. The movie's focus on character development and relationships adds depth to the story, making it a standout entry in the Inuyasha franchise.

documents.title: Skyline
documents.tagline: Don't look up
documents.overview: When strange lights descend on the city of Los Angeles, people are drawn outside like moths to a flame where an extraterrestrial force threatens to swallow the entire human population off the face of the Earth. Now the band of survivors must fight for their lives as the world unravels around them.
documents.plot:
Skyline is a 2010 American science fiction disaster film directed by the brothers Greg and Colin Strause and co-produced and written by Liam O'Donnell. It stars Eric Balfour as Jarrod, Scottie Thompson as his girlfriend Elaine, Donald Faison as his friend Terry, Brittany Daniel, Crystal Reed and David Zayas as a group of people trapped in a Los Angeles apartment building during an alien invasion.

Jarrod and Elaine travel to Los Angeles to celebrate the birthday of Jarrod's best friend Terry, joining Terry's girlfriend Candice and his assistant Denise. During an argument, Elaine reveals that she is pregnant. Early the next morning, mysterious blue lights descend from the sky, hypnotizing anyone who looks at them and drawing them upward into enormous alien ships hovering over the city. Jarrod is nearly taken but is saved by Terry, and the survivors realize that the aliens are harvesting humans on a massive scale.

Trapped in the building, the group tries to escape by car, but monstrous aliens of various sizes block every route, and one by one the survivors are killed or abducted. The building's concierge, Oliver, joins the remaining survivors, who hide in an apartment and watch as the United States military launches a counterattack, including a nuclear strike against one of the ships, which manages to repair itself. Jarrod, who was briefly exposed to the light, begins to undergo strange physical changes. As the situation becomes hopeless, Jarrod and Elaine are finally pulled into the mothership, where they discover the horrifying purpose of the invasion: the aliens are harvesting human brains to power their own creatures.

The film was produced on a modest budget, with its visual effects created by the Strause brothers' own effects company, Hydraulx, which was responsible for most of the film's spectacle.

Skyline was released in the United States on November 12, 2010. It was panned by critics, receiving 15 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, but grossed 68.3 million dollars worldwide against a budget estimated between 10 and 20 million dollars. It launched a film series that continued with Beyond Skyline (2017), Skylines (2020) and Skyline: Warpath (2025).

documents.title: How Do You Know
documents.tagline: How do you know it's love?
documents.overview: After being cut from the USA softball team and feeling a bit past her prime, Lisa finds herself evaluating her life and in the middle of a love triangle, as a corporate guy in crisis competes with her current, baseball-playing beau.
documents.plot: After being cut from the USA softball team and feeling a bit past her prime, Lisa finds herself evaluating her life and in the middle of a love triangle, as a corporate guy in crisis competes with her current, baseball-playing beau.

documents.title: 30 Days of Night: Dark Days
documents.tagline: Don't walk into the dark.
documents.overview: After surviving the incidents in Barrow, Alaska, Stella Olemaun relocates to Los Angeles, where she intentionally attracts the attention of the local vampire population in order to avenge the death of her husband, Eben.
documents.plot:
30 Days of Night: Dark Days is an American horror film of 2010 directed by Ben Ketai, who wrote it with Steve Niles, creator of the comic book miniseries on which it is based. The sequel to 30 Days of Night (2007), it stars Kiele Sanchez as Stella Oleson, a role originated by Melissa George, with Rhys Coiro as Paul, Diora Baird as Amber, Harold Perrineau as Todd, Ben Cotton as Dane and Mia Kirshner as the vampire queen Lilith.

A year after vampires slaughtered much of Barrow, Alaska, during its month-long polar night, the widowed Stella travels the world trying to convince people that vampires are real, indifferent to the danger after the loss of her husband Eben. Guided by a mysterious contact named Dane, she gives a lecture in Los Angeles, where she switches on ultraviolet lamps that incinerate several vampires in the audience. She is detained by Agent Norris, one of the humans who serve the vampires and hide their crimes. Released, she is approached by Paul, Amber and Todd, a band of hunters sent by Dane, who believe that killing Lilith, the queen who directs the vampires and ordered the Barrow massacre, will send the rest into dormancy. Dane turns out to be a vampire who has kept his humanity by drinking only hospital blood.

A raid on a vampire nest goes wrong and Todd is bitten; when he turns, Stella kills him while Paul hesitates. The survivors capture and interrogate another vampire, free a captive named Jennifer and learn that Lilith is on a ship in the bay about to sail for Alaska. Lilith turns the cancer-stricken Norris into a vampire, and he kills Dane. Aboard the ship Amber is devoured, and Stella kills Norris, but Paul dies fighting Lilith. Stella hides in a tub of blood, ambushes the queen and beheads her, and the remaining vampires let her go. Back in Barrow, she digs up Eben and feeds him her blood; he revives, embraces her and sinks his fangs into her neck.

The film premiered at San Diego Comic-Con in July 2010 and went straight to DVD and Blu-ray in October. Reviews were poor, with Fangoria calling it generic, though Dread Central praised its dark, nihilistic ride.

documents.title: Arthur 3: The War of the Two Worlds
documents.original_title: Arthur 3: la guerre des deux mondes
documents.tagline: The Final...
documents.overview: Maltazard, the Evil M, is now 7 feet tall and evolving among the humans, causing terror wherever he goes. His goal is simple: forming an army of giant henchmen and ruling over the universe. Meanwhile, Arthur is still a Minimoy, and thus in a state where he's unable to fend him off. With the help of Selenia and Betameche, he hatches a plan to regain his usual size: all they must do is infiltrate Arthur's house through the pipeworks, catch an electric train from his bedroom to his grandfather's study and find an elixir that will make him grow back to his human size. Sounds simple enough, if it weren't for Darkos, Maltazard's own son, hot on their tails.
documents.plot:
Arthur 3: The War of the Two Worlds (French: Arthur 3: La Guerre des deux mondes) is a 2010 English-language French fantasy film combining live action and computer animation, directed and co-written by Luc Besson from the last book of his Arthur children's series. The third film in the series and a direct continuation of Arthur and the Revenge of Maltazard (2009), it was shot back to back with its predecessor in Normandy. Freddie Highmore returns as Arthur, alongside Mia Farrow, Ron Crawford, Robert Stanton and Penny Balfour, with Selena Gomez, Lou Reed and Iggy Pop among the English voice cast.

The story resumes where the previous film ended. The evil Maltazard has grown to human size and escaped into the human world, while Arthur is still trapped at the tiny scale of the Minimoys. With Princess Selenia and her brother Prince Betameche, Arthur sets out to recover a potion from his family house that can restore normal size. Maltazard gets hold of it first and uses it to enlarge his army of followers, threatening Arthur's family and the surrounding town.

Arthur manages to regain his human form with an elixir of life provided by a queen bee. Meanwhile his grandfather Archibald persuades Prince Darkos, Maltazard's son, to turn against his father, and enlarges him with a second dose of the potion. Arthur and Darkos together confront the villain. In the final showdown Selenia and Betameche shrink Maltazard back to his Minimoy size, allowing Arthur to capture him, while the United States Army defeats his giant forces. Maltazard is afterwards kept as a prisoner by Arthur's family.

Released in France by EuropaCorp on 13 October 2010, the film was a box-office success at home and received mixed to fairly positive French reviews. With a budget of about 69 million euros, it was among the most expensive French productions of its time, and after the international failure of the earlier instalments it caused heavy losses for the studio. It went directly to video in the United States, and in Britain and Ireland it was combined with the second film as Arthur and the Great Adventure. It was Lou Reed's last acting role before his death in 2013, and a spin-off, Arthur, malédiction, followed in 2022.

documents.title: Memories
documents.tagline: Three unforgettable tales from the masters of anime.
documents.overview: In this anime anthology, a salvage ship crew happens upon a haunted vessel in "Magnetic Rose"; a cold tablet turns a lab worker into a biological weapon in "Stink Bomb"; and an urban populace carries on an endless war with an unseen foe in "Cannon Fodder."
documents.plot:
The Corona, a deep space salvage freighter, is out on a mission when it encounters a distress signal and responds to it. They come upon a spaceship graveyard orbiting a giant space station. The crew's two engineers, Heintz and Miguel, enter it to get a closer look. Once inside, they discover an opulent European interior and several furnished rooms in varying states of decay, but find no signs of life.
The men learn that the station belongs to a once-famous opera diva named Eva Friedel who disappeared after the murder of her fiancé, Carlo Rambaldi, a fellow singer. Continuing to search for the distress signal's source, the engineers split up, with each experiencing paranormal encounters, including strange noises and visions of Eva. Miguel enters the dilapidated underbelly of the station, and in a cavernous chamber, he finds a broken piano playing the distress signal. He begins to hallucinate and Eva suddenly runs up to kiss him. Heintz finds a theater stage and sees Eva, who stabs him when he approaches. Suddenly paralyzed, Heintz relives a memory of his wife and his daughter Emily. The illusion disappears when Eva takes his wife's form and tells him that he "will never leave".
Heintz rushes to save Miguel, but Miguel disappears deeper into the cavern, having been seduced by Eva into thinking he is Carlo. Eva reveals to Heintz that she murdered the real Carlo for refusing to marry her and has since forced others to relive his likeness. She makes Heintz relive Emily's death, and entices Heintz to stay with his daughter's doppelganger. Heintz resists and shoots the massive computer embedded in the ceiling of the cavern, causing the AI hologram of Eva to malfunction.
Meanwhile, the Corona has been struggling against a powerful magnetic field coming from the station, pulling the ship towards it. In desperation, the crewmen Aoshima and Ivanov fire a powerful energy cannon; gouging deep enough into the structure to reach the cavern and Heintz, moments before the ship is torn apart. Heintz is ejected into space along with the space-suit-clad skeletons of Eva's past victims, as Eva hauntingly sings to a conjured audience. The Corona is destroyed and becomes part of the rose-shaped structure around the station. The whereabouts of the real (and long-deceased) Eva are shown, and a representation of Eva is seen talking romantically with Miguel (now fully embracing his new identity as Carlo). Heintz is last seen drifting in space, still alive.

Lab technician Nobuo Tanaka, battling the flu, mistakes some experimental pills for medicine and swallows one. The pills were intended to help soldiers counter biological weapons, but it reacts to a flu shot that he had received before the medicine, causing his body to produce vast amounts of a highly toxic gas. While taking a nap, the odor he emits kills everyone in the laboratory. Horrified, he reports the incident to headquarters, who instruct him to deliver the experimental drug to Tokyo.

documents.title: Ghostbusters
documents.tagline: Who You Gonna Call?
documents.overview: Following a ghost invasion of Manhattan, paranormal enthusiasts Erin Gilbert and Abby Yates, nuclear engineer Jillian Holtzmann, and subway worker Patty Tolan band together to stop the otherworldly threat.
documents.plot:
Ghostbusters (2016) is a supernatural comedy film directed by Paul Feig, starring Melissa McCarthy, Kristen Wiig, Kate McKinnon, Leslie Jones, Chris Hemsworth, and Bill Murray.

The movie begins with Erin Gilbert (Kristen Wiig), a paranormal researcher who has written a book about ghosts. She meets Abby Yates (Melissa McCarthy), another ghost hunter, at a bar where they share a drink and discuss their shared interest in the supernatural. The two women meet again at a coffee shop, where they discover that they are long-lost friends from college.

As they reconnect, Erin reveals to Abby that she has been researching ghosts for years, but her research was initially met with skepticism by her academic peers. However, after discovering a mysterious entity known as "Rowan," which is connected to an ancient Sumerian deity, Erin and Abby decide to team up and start their own ghost-hunting business.

The two women recruit two other experts: Jillian Holtzmann (Kate McKinnon), a quirky engineer who creates gadgets for the Ghostbusters, and Patty Tolan (Leslie Jones), a street-smart New Yorker with a talent for tracking down supernatural entities. Together, they form a team known as the "Ghostbusters."

The Ghostbusters soon discover that Rowan is connected to an ancient Sumerian deity named Gozer, who was worshipped by a cult in New York City. The cult, led by a charismatic leader named Vinz Clortho (Neil Casey), plans to bring about the apocalypse and resurrect Gozer.

As the Ghostbusters delve deeper into the mystery, they realize that Rowan is not just a simple ghost but a powerful entity with supernatural abilities. They also discover that Erin's past is connected to the cult, which makes her a target for Vinz Clortho.
