The team faces numerous challenges as they try to stop the cult and prevent Gozer from being resurrected. Along the way, they encounter various supernatural entities, including ghosts, demons, and otherworldly creatures.

As the stakes grow higher, the Ghostbusters realize that they need to work together to defeat Vinz Clortho and his minions. In a thrilling climax, the team faces off against Vinz Clortho in an epic battle of wits and supernatural powers.

In the end, the Ghostbusters succeed in defeating Gozer and banishing him back to the underworld. The movie concludes with Erin and Abby reflecting on their newfound friendship and the challenges they faced as women in a male-dominated field.

Ghostbusters (2016) is a fun and action-packed film that pays homage to the original 1984 classic while introducing new characters and plot twists. The movie features impressive visual effects, witty humor, and a talented cast of comedic actresses who bring their characters to life with charm and wit.

documents.title: Ong Bak 3
documents.tagline: The biggest fight of all is with himself.
documents.overview: Ong Bak 3 picks up where Ong Bak 2 had left off. Tien is captured and almost beaten to death before he is saved and brought back to the Kana Khone villagers. There he is taught meditation and how to deal with his Karma, but very soon his arch rival returns challenging Tien for a final duel.
documents.plot: Tien is captured and almost beaten to death before he is saved and brought back to the Kana Khone villagers. There he is taught meditation and how to deal with his Karma, but very soon his arch rival returns challenging Tien for a final duel.

documents.title: Love & Other Drugs
documents.tagline: Addicted to one-night stands or dependent on one another?
documents.overview: Maggie is an alluring free spirit who won't let anyone – or anything – tie her down. But she meets her match in Jamie, whose relentless and nearly infallible charm serves him well with the ladies and the cutthroat world of pharmaceutical sales. Maggie and Jamie's evolving relationship takes them both by surprise, as they find themselves under the influence of the ultimate drug: love.
documents.plot:
In 1996, womanizer Jamie Randall is fired from a Pittsburgh electronics store for having sex with his manager's girlfriend. His wealthy brother Josh refers him for a job as a pharmaceutical sales representative.
After attending a Pfizer training program, Jamie goes to work for them, attempting to get doctors to prescribe Zoloft. He is rebuffed, much to the surprise of his regional manager Bruce, who sees him as his ticket to the Chicago market.
Bruce suggests Jamie get Dr. Stan Knight to prescribe Zoloft instead of Prozac, so other doctors will follow. He tries to gain access to Dr. Knight by flirting with his female employees while secretly discarding the Prozac samples.
Knight eventually allows Jamie to observe him examine one of his patients, Maggie Murdock, who has early onset Parkinson's disease. Taking an interest in Maggie, Jamie obtains her number from one of Knight's assistants, whom he previously seduced.
Jamie and Maggie go on a date and agree that neither is interested in a serious relationship, so they start having casual sex. He is beaten up by top-selling Prozac rep, Trey Hannigan, who discovers that Jamie has been discarding his samples. Maggie reveals Trey is an ex-boyfriend, and she tells Jamie a rumor about Jamie's company developing a new drug to treat erectile dysfunction. Bruce confirms that Viagra is about to be marketed.
Jamie starts selling Viagra, which is an instant success. He reveals that he wants a serious relationship, but Maggie breaks up with him. He confronts her while she helps senior citizens onto a bus bound for Canada to obtain cheap prescription drugs. They argue, but Jamie refuses to leave and waits for Maggie all night at a bus stop. Touched, she reciprocates feelings and they resume their relationship.
Maggie accompanies Jamie to a medical conference, where she ends up at a Parkinson's support group across the street. She invites Jamie, and he meets a man whose wife is in the final stages of the disease. Asked for his advice, the man tells him to leave Maggie before her symptoms inevitably worsen.
After the convention, Maggie finally tells Jamie that she loves him. He begins researching Parkinson's and takes her to different specialists around the country for tests. Jamie becomes angry when they arrive at an appointment only to discover it has been rescheduled. Feeling he only wants to be with her if there is a hope for a cure, Maggie breaks up with him.
Sometime later, Jamie and Josh are invited to a party by Knight, where Jamie takes Viagra and has a threesome with two women. He awakens with a rare side effect and goes to the hospital. Sometime later, he goes to a restaurant and encounters Maggie on a date. Bruce arrives and reveals Jamie has been promoted to the Chicago office.
While packing, Jamie finds the videotape recorder with a video of himself and Maggie in happier times. He realizes he wants to be with her, but her boss tells him she has left for Canada for a prescription drug run.

documents.title: The Next Three Days
documents.tagline: What if you had 72 hours to save everything you live for?
documents.overview: A married couple's life is turned upside down when the wife is accused of murdering her boss. Her husband John would spend the next few years trying to get her released, but there's no evidence that negates the evidence against her. When the strain of being separated from her husband and son gets to her, John decides to find a way to break her out.
documents.plot:
In Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, Lara Brennan is sentenced to life in prison for murder. Three years later, her young son Luke ceases to acknowledge her during prison visits, despite the efforts of her husband John. Following the failure of Lara's appeal, her lawyer urges John to accept the evidence: after a public fight with her boss, Lara was seen leaving the parking lot where her boss was bludgeoned with a fire extinguisher; though Lara claims to have bumped into the real suspect, her fingerprints were on the murder weapon and the victim's blood was found on her coat. Out of legal options, Lara attempts suicide, and John becomes determined to break her out of prison.
John consults former inmate Damon Pennington, who wrote a book about his seven prison escapes, and makes the necessary preparations over the next three months, studying the routines inside Allegheny County Jail. Attempting to buy fake passports from a drug dealer, he is directed to a bar where he is instead beaten and robbed by the dealer and his friend. A deaf motorcyclist from the bar later sells him the forged documents for $3,700, and John buys a handgun. Nearly caught testing a bump key inside the jail, a panicked John is seen vomiting outside by the detectives who arrested Lara; they follow him home, suspicious that he has sold the house and other assets. John learns how to break into the van for the medical lab that conducts Lara's diabetes tests.
Learning that Lara will be transferred to a high-security prison in three days, John is unable to close the house sale in time and prepares to rob a bank, but cannot go through with it, and nearly runs over a mother and her child in his stress. A visit with Lara leads to an argument and, in a fit of quiet rage, she declares she is guilty, but John refuses to believe her. He tails a local drug dealer to a meth lab, setting fire to the building and taking the cash at gunpoint, but a shoot-out leaves one of the criminals dead and a second wounded. John breaks his tail light as he drives the wounded dealer to a hospital, but the man bleeds out and dies, so John leaves his body at a bus stop. John's father finds his plane tickets and realizes his plan, and they share a final goodbye.
Setting his plan in motion, John cuts the medical lab's phone lines and plants falsified blood tests in the van indicating that Lara is in a state of hyperkalemia, before leaving Luke at a birthday party. With her doctor unable to contact the lab, Lara is transferred to a hospital. Detectives trace John's broken tail light while investigating the meth lab incident and break into his empty house, realizing he is planning to free his wife. At the hospital, John incapacitates Lara's guards and convinces her to escape with him. Confronted by the detectives, they manage to slip away into a crowd of Pittsburgh Penguins fans and board the subway. Detectives order the railway stations locked down.

documents.title: The Experiment
documents.tagline: They never imagined it would go this far
documents.overview: 20 men are chosen to participate in the roles of guards and prisoners in a psychological study that ultimately spirals out of control.
documents.plot:
Volunteers arrive for a psychological study led by Dr. Archaleta (Stevens), among them Travis (Brody), a proud anti-war protester, and Michael Barris (Whitaker), a 42-year-old man who still lives with his domineering mother.
After interviews measuring responses to scenes of violence, a chosen 26 are driven to an isolated prison setting with 24 hour camera coverage. The group is split into six guards and 20 prisoners, thereafter referred to only by number. Travis is assigned as a prisoner (#77), and Barris as a guard. Prisoners are required to fully consume three meals a day, participate in 30 minutes of daily recreation, remain within designated areas, and avoid speaking to guards unless spoken to first. Guards must ensure prisoners obey the rules and deal commensurately with transgressions within 30 minutes. Archaleta stresses that the experiment will end immediately at the first sign of violence or quitting. If all rules are followed for two weeks, each man will be compensated $14,000.
Travis' cellmates are Benjy, a graphic novelist, and Nix, a member of the Aryan Brotherhood who served prison time before. Barris, concerned that some guards may be capable of violence, tries to dissuade them from aggressive behavior. Instead, the guards grow more forceful to make prisoners 'obey at all costs'. Barris gradually becomes more sadistic. Realizing that the defiant Travis is influencing prisoner dissent, Barris instructs other guards to abduct him, shave his head, and urinate upon him. When Archaleta fails to intervene, Barris reasons that his actions were "commensurate". When fellow guard Bosch dissents, Barris pressures him to continue.
Travis discovers that Benjy, now severely ill, concealed his need for insulin, believing he could cure his diabetes merely through dieting. Bosche tries to help find Benjy's insulin, but is caught by other guards. Barris provides Benjy's insulin, but later has all the guards beat Bosche severely and orders Travis to clean the prison toilets. When Travis taunts Barris, the guards respond by shoving his head into the toilet, nearly drowning him.
One morning during roll call, Travis removes his shirt as a sign of protest, followed by the other prisoners. He climbs up to one of the cameras and demands they be released, but the guards choke him. When Benjy tries to defend Travis, Barris bludgeons him. Guards lock Travis into an old boiler pipe overnight, attack the remaining prisoners, and handcuff each man across the cell doors.
While locked in the boiler, Travis discovers a hidden infrared camera. As his despondency turns to anger, he manages to escape and interrupts a guard’s attempt to rape a prisoner. The intended victim and Travis beat the guard and knock him out before freeing the other prisoners. Finding Benjy dead from his head injury, Travis leads an assault against the guards, chasing them through the building.

documents.title: Vanishing on 7th Street
documents.tagline: Stay in the light.
documents.overview: A mysterious global blackout yields countless populations to simply vanish, leaving only their clothes and possessions behind. A small handful of survivors band together in a dimly-lit tavern on 7th Street, struggling to combat the apocalyptic horror. Realizing they may in fact be the last people on earth, a dark shadow hones in on them alone.
documents.plot:
Paul, a projectionist in a Detroit theater, is reading about the 16th-century disappearance of the Roanoke Colony when the lights suddenly go out. He finds that all the staff and patrons have vanished, leaving only their clothes behind. He comes across a security guard holding a flashlight; as Paul had a headlamp on for his reading, they deduce that people holding sources of light are protected against whatever dwells in the darkness. Upon hearing a sound in a department store, the guard investigates when his flashlight goes out, and he vanishes. As Paul hears the guard cry out, his headlamp also goes out. The scene changes to a hospital where a woman in scrubs, Rosemary, frantically looks for anyone left alive and continuously calls for a child named Manny.
The following morning, TV reporter Luke Ryder wakes to find the power out. Leaving his apartment, the downtown streets are empty except for abandoned cars and piles of clothing. He reaches his television station, also abandoned, and finds a recording that shows his girlfriend vanishing on air when the lights go out. A live feed from Chicago shows a newscaster telling people to always keep a light on themselves.
Three days pass, and Luke is alone in the darkness, trying to scavenge flashlight batteries and checking cars. He finds a bar powered by a portable generator, where the bartender's young son, James Leary, waits alone. James believes his mother is at a church down the street and will soon return. Luke explains that it is 11 a.m. but dark out, implying that the sun no longer provides light.
Luke and James are later joined by Rosemary, who made her way to the bar, thinking her son Manny might have been brought there by his father. On the third day of darkness, Paul appears in the street, suffering from a severe concussion. He reveals that the darkness had taken him, but his headlamp had reactivated, and he reappeared. Paul tells them about the mystery of the Roanoke Colony, where over 100 settlers disappeared overnight, and they seem to be experiencing the same thing. He tells them that the word "CROATOAN" was found carved into a fence post at the site of the empty colony.
With the generator failing and Paul needing medical help, Luke suggests going to Chicago, having seen the live video feed. He and Rosemary go into the street to retrieve one of the abandoned trucks. After their flashlights begin losing power, they return to the hospital for matches and batteries. In the street, Rosemary ignores Luke's warnings that the sound of a baby crying is just the darkness trying to trick her. She is lured under a solitary street light and disappears when the light goes out. Back at the bar, the generator suffers from short circuits, causing the lights to flicker. Having lost sight of James, Paul searches for him in the bunker tunnels below the bar. When the lights fail, James, wearing a glow-stick necklace, is safe, but Paul vanishes.

documents.title: Piranha 3D
documents.tagline: There's something in the water.
documents.overview: Each year the population of sleepy Lake Victoria, Arizona explodes from 5,000 to 50,000 residents for the annual Spring Break celebration. But then, an earthquake opens an underwater chasm, releasing an enormous swarm of ancient Piranha that have been dormant for thousands of years, now with a taste for human flesh. This year, there's something more to worry about than the usual hangovers and complaints from locals, a new type of terror is about to be cut loose on Lake Victoria.
documents.plot:
Piranha 3D is a 2010 American horror film directed by David R. Ellis and written by Christopher Hoadley, Josh Stolberg, and Doug Taylor. The movie is a remake of the 1978 film Piranha, which was itself an adaptation of Joe Dante's 1978 film of the same name.

The story takes place in the fictional town of Long Beach, California, where a group of college students are preparing for the annual Spring Break festivities. Among them is Jake (Dustin Hoffman), a fisherman who has been hired to transport a shipment of piranhas from South America to a local aquarium. Unbeknownst to Jake, the piranhas have escaped during the journey and are now swimming in the waters off Long Beach.

As the students arrive at the beach, they begin to notice that something is amiss. At first, it's just small fish biting people, but soon the attacks escalate into full-blown piranha attacks. The main character, Fisherman (Jerry O'Connell), teams up with a local fisherman, Jake (Dustin Hoffman), and a group of college students to try and stop the piranhas before they kill everyone.

As the body count rises, the group discovers that the piranhas are not just mindless killers but are actually attracted to human blood. They also learn that the piranhas have been genetically engineered to be more aggressive and deadly than their natural counterparts.

The movie's plot development is driven by a series of gruesome and intense attacks on the students and locals, which escalate in frequency and ferocity as the story progresses. Along the way, the group discovers that the source of the piranha infestation is a local water treatment plant that has been releasing untreated sewage into the ocean.

As the body count rises, the survivors are forced to confront their own mortality and the true horror of the situation. In the end, only a few characters remain, including Fisherman (Jerry O'Connell) and his girlfriend, Liz ( Elisabeth Shue), who manage to escape the carnage by fleeing in a boat.

The ending is a classic horror movie finale, with the survivors barely escaping the clutches of the piranhas. The final shot is of the empty beach, littered with the bodies of the victims, as the camera pans out to reveal the true extent of the carnage.

Overall, Piranha 3D is a fun and gory horror movie that pays homage to the classic films of the genre while also offering something new and different. With its over-the-top violence and gore, it's sure to appeal to fans of the horror genre.

documents.title: My Rainy Days
documents.overview: Because of her past, 17-year-old Rio lives her days filling the emptiness in her heart with money--until one day, she meets a university professor named Kouki and falls in love.
documents.plot:
My Rainy Days (Japanese: Tenshi no Koi, literally "Angel's Love") is a 2009 Japanese romantic drama written and directed by Yuri Kanchiku in her directorial debut, adapted from the cell phone novel of the same name. Model Nozomi Sasaki plays a seventeen-year-old schoolgirl in her first leading film role, with Shosuke Tanihara and Hikaru Yamamoto in the cast.

Rio Ozawa, a beautiful and calculating high school student, earns money with her friends Maki and Miho through compensated dating and extortion. After defending her naive classmate Tomoko from a bully, Naoko, Rio draws Tomoko into the clique and into the scheme, though Naoko is secretly Rio's lover. When a photo shop mixes up Rio's prints with those of another Ozawa, she meets Kouki, a withdrawn 35-year-old history professor, to swap them, and he suddenly faints. Visiting him in the hospital, Rio grows close to him, quits her schemes, ends things with Naoko and asks him to tutor her. When she scores 99 on a history test, Kouki agrees to a date, and he later kisses her. Rio does not know that he had surgery for a brain tumor three years earlier that did not remove it completely, and to spare her, he abruptly withdraws from her life.

Naoko returns to school and tries to stab Tomoko, but Rio shields her. On the roof, Naoko reveals that she was repeatedly raped by her mother's boyfriend and killed him, then jumps to her death after declaring her love for Rio. Rio confesses that she had ordered Naoko to bully Tomoko, and the two drift apart until Rio collapses from stress and they reconcile. Kouki's cousin Kaori gives Rio his new address, and Rio tells him that she was raped and had an abortion three years earlier, turning to prostitution to avoid being hurt again. Kouki faints once more, and Rio learns of the tumor. He admits that meeting her made him wish for more time, and he agrees to surgery despite the risk to his memory, telling her he loves her. After Rio graduates, she finds him on a rainy day; he does not seem to remember her but walks her to the station under his umbrella, then returns to shelter her again, and she embraces him.

The film premiered as a special screening at the 22nd Tokyo International Film Festival and opened in Japan on 7 November 2009. It grossed about $1.09 million across four countries. Reviews were generally positive; The Hollywood Reporter said it avoided conventional tearjerking pitfalls.

documents.title: Superman/Shazam!: The Return of Black Adam
documents.original_title: Superman/Shazam!: The Return of Black Adam
documents.tagline: We fight for those you can't fight for themselves!
documents.overview: Chosen the world’s protector against the Seven Deadly Enemies of Man – pride, envy, greed, hatred, selfishness, laziness and injustice – young Billy Batson accepts his destiny as Captain Marvel. Battling alongside Superman against nefarious Black Adam, Billy soon discovers the challenge super heroes ultimately face: is it revenge or justice?
documents.plot:
Superman/Shazam!: The Return of Black Adam is a 2010 American animated superhero short film directed by Joaquim Dos Santos and written by Michael Jelenic, part of the DC Showcase series. George Newbern voices Superman and Jerry O'Connell Captain Marvel, reprising their roles from Justice League Unlimited, with Arnold Vosloo as Black Adam, Zach Callison as Billy Batson and James Garner as the wizard Shazam. It was released on November 9, 2010, as the main feature of the DC Showcase Original Shorts Collection, and is the longest of the series.

In Fawcett City, Billy Batson is an orphan who has been thrown out by his foster parents and lives alone in a rundown apartment, scraping by while still showing kindness to others. He meets the reporter Clark Kent at a diner for an article about his life, but the meeting is interrupted when Black Adam bursts in, declaring that he intends to kill the boy before the wizard can reach him. Clark buys Billy time to escape and changes into Superman to fight the villain. Billy flees into the subway with the help of a homeless man he had earlier tried to defend from bullies, but Adam corners him on the tracks, and he seems to be struck by a train.

Billy instead finds himself aboard an empty subway car that carries him to a vast cavern, where the ancient wizard Shazam reveals that he is the next chosen champion. Five thousand years earlier Adam had been Shazam's champion, but he decided to rule humanity rather than protect it and was banished to the far reaches of the universe. Seeking to correct his mistake, the wizard grants Billy his powers and tells him to speak his name when he needs help.

Emerging to face Adam, Billy says "Shazam" and a bolt of lightning transforms him into Captain Marvel. Together with Superman he battles Adam across the city. Adam smashes a dam, and while Superman stops the flood, Adam takes a woman hostage and forces Billy to give up his powers before throwing her into the air. Superman saves her and frees Billy, who transforms again and defeats Adam, but is stopped by Superman before he can kill him in anger. The homeless man then reveals himself as Tawky Tawny, a tiger who serves as Billy's guardian, and threatens Adam with banishment. Rather than be exiled again, Adam speaks the magic word and reverts to mortal form, crumbling into dust from his great age. Days later, when the same bullies confront Billy, he smiles as lightning strikes.

documents.title: Hatchet II
documents.tagline: Victor Crowley Lives.
documents.overview: Picking up right where the original ended, Marybeth escapes the clutches of the swamp-dwelling killer Victor Crowley. After learning the truth about her family’s connection to the hatchet-wielding madman, Marybeth returns to the Louisiana swamps along with an army of hunters to recover the bodies of her family and exact the bloodiest revenge against the bayou butcher.
documents.plot:
Immediately after Hatchet, Marybeth Dunston is attacked by Victor Crowley but manages to escape. Jack Cracker finds her and takes her back to his cabin but forces her to leave after discovering her last name, telling her to visit Reverend Zombie. Not long after she leaves, Jack is killed by Victor.
Marybeth returns to Reverend Zombie's shop, and he lets her in. After learning her last name, he tells her that her father, Sampson, was one of the boys responsible for causing the fire that led to Victor's death as a child. He also gives her more details on Victor's backstory; Thomas, Victor's father, had cheated on his wife Shyann with her nurse Lena after Shyann was diagnosed with stomach cancer. Moments before dying, Shyann placed a curse on the child conceived by Lena from the affair. Months later, Lena gave birth to Victor Crowley but died of fright after seeing Victor's deformed face.
Marybeth tells Reverend Zombie she wants to go back and retrieve the remains of her father and brother. He agrees but tells her she must bring a family member. After she leaves, Zombie calls Justin (the brother of Shawn from the first film) and tells him to summon a group of hunters (specifically including a man named Trent Graves) to go with them. Marybeth returns home, where her uncle Bob promptly shows up. He reluctantly agrees to accompany her to a recruitment meeting in Zombie's shop, where Zombie tells the hunters he will pay them $5,000 for the head of Victor Crowley. Marybeth, Bob, and the hunters proceed to venture into the swamp.
As night descends, they find the boat, and as the rest leave, two hunters, Cletus and Chad, stay by the boat while the others fan out. Marybeth, Zombie, Justin, Bob, and Trent look for Crowley's shed, as well as the bodies of his victims. Along the way, Zombie explains to Justin that Trent, Sampson, and Sampson's brother were the kids who started the fire that led to Victor's death. Since Victor has already killed Sampson, Zombie believes that if Crowley kills Bob and Trent, his soul will be at peace, and he will finally leave the swamp. Meanwhile, Victor begins murdering each of the hunters one by one.
While searching the cabin, the remaining party members hear Victor outside. As they hide, Justin tells Marybeth about Zombie's plot to get her uncle and Trent killed. As she runs to warn Bob, Victor appears behind Justin and kills him with a belt sander. Trent is murdered quickly thereafter, and Zombie drags Marybeth out of the house, trapping Bob inside with Victor, who murders him. Zombie declares Victor Crowley is dead, but Marybeth then reveals Bob was not her real uncle and was her father's best friend; her real uncle had died of leukemia when Marybeth was twelve. Now realizing his plan has failed, Zombie turns to see Victor breaking through the cabin wall. Zombie attempts to fight Victor but is brutally killed in doing so.

documents.title: Dog Pound
documents.tagline: Fighting Back Is The Only Way Out
documents.overview: Three juvenile delinquents arrive at a correctional center and are put under the care of an experienced guard.
documents.plot:
Dog Pound is a 2010 Canadian prison drama and psychological thriller directed and co-written by Kim Chapiron. A reworking of the 1979 British borstal film Scum, it moves the story to a juvenile detention center in the United States, and it is the only one of Chapiron's films to go direct to video in some markets. Since its release it has developed a cult following for its raw portrayal of life behind bars.

Three teenagers, Butch, Davis and Angel, arrive at the Enola Vale juvenile detention center in Montana. Butch has been transferred after attacking and blinding a guard at another facility, and the intake officer singles him out from the start. Goodyear, a tough but fair correctional officer, urges the new arrivals to keep their heads down and follow the rules so they can earn a second chance on the outside.

Butch tries at first to conform, but he and his friends are soon targeted by the facility's chief bully, Banks, and his henchmen. Refusing to name his attackers, Butch is thrown into solitary confinement, and when he gets out he takes brutal revenge, establishing his place in the inmate hierarchy and providing temporary protection for Davis and Angel. That fragile balance collapses when a confrontation during a work detail leaves Angel fatally injured, and Butch, a witness, is sent back to solitary during the investigation. Without his protection, Davis falls victim to further abuse and despair. As grief and anger spread through the dormitory, the inmates stage a protest, and Butch's rage finally explodes into a violent uprising that the staff struggle to contain.

The film is a bleak study of institutional violence, showing how a system meant to rehabilitate young offenders instead breeds cruelty, hierarchy and hopelessness.

Dog Pound premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on 24 April 2010 and was released in Canada on 7 September 2010, followed by releases in France, the United States, Spain and the United Kingdom. Reviews were mixed to positive, with 63 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 57; CinemaBlend called it intense and not suited to every viewer.

documents.title: Legendary
documents.tagline: Some Legends are born out of Struggle.
documents.overview: A book-smart teenager joins his school's wrestling team as a way to reunite his surviving family members, who split apart after the death of his father, a college wrestling legend, 10 years ago.
documents.plot:
Legendary is a 2010 American sports drama directed by Mel Damski and produced by WWE Studios. Devon Graye stars as Cal Chetley, a teenage high school wrestler, with professional wrestler John Cena as his older brother Mike, Patricia Clarkson as their mother Sharon, Danny Glover, Madeleine Martin and Tyler Posey. The film was released in the United States in September 2010.

Cal is an intelligent but physically slight and socially awkward teenager in a small Oklahoma town who is regularly bullied at school. His father, a celebrated wrestling coach, died years earlier in an accident, and his older brother Mike, once a star wrestler with a promising future, has drifted into a troubled and aimless life. Mike has been estranged from the family for about a decade, and Sharon, who has raised Cal alone, has had no contact with her elder son.

Cal decides to join his high school's wrestling team, hoping that following in the family tradition will help him reconnect with Mike and bring his broken family back together. Sharon is opposed to the idea, worried that Cal will be hurt and that wrestling will revive old wounds, and she is even more upset when she learns that Cal has secretly sought out Mike for coaching. Mike, who carries guilt over the circumstances of their father's death, is initially unwilling to help, but gradually agrees to train his younger brother. As Cal endures defeats and hard training under his coach and Mike's guidance, and as he befriends a girl named Luli, he grows in confidence and resolve, and his determination slowly forces the family to confront the past. Danny Glover's character, a local fisherman who narrates parts of the story, offers Cal advice along the way, as Cal prepares for a crucial match that will test both his skill and his family's ability to heal.

Critics received the film poorly. It holds a 19 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus described it as maudlin, predictable and clichéd, pinning its talented cast under a heavy layer of formulaic schmaltz, and a Metacritic score of 39. The film was a commercial failure in its limited theatrical release, and it was later marketed on home video largely on the strength of Cena's wrestling fame.

documents.title: It's Kind of a Funny Story
documents.original_title: It's Kind of a Funny Story
documents.tagline: Sometimes what's in your head isn't as crazy as you think.
documents.overview: A clinically depressed teenager gets a new start after he checks himself into an adult psychiatric ward.
documents.plot:
Contemplating suicide, depressed teenager Craig Gilner seeks help at a local hospital. After telling a doctor named Dr. Mahmoud that he needs immediate help, Craig is admitted for five days at the hospital's adult psychiatric floor, due to the temporary closure of the psychiatric floor for adolescents.
Craig's hospitalization was spurred on by the stress of his academically competitive high school and upcoming summer program applications. He was also facing feelings of inferiority in the shadow of his best friend Aaron, and pressure from his father to succeed academically. At first, Craig is uncertain if he made the right choice to stay on the psychiatric floor, fearing his friends may find out where he is, particularly Nia, his crush and Aaron's girlfriend.
Throughout his stay, Craig bonds with various patients in the psychiatric unit. Craig is introduced to Bobby (Zach Galifianakis), a patient who takes Craig under his wing. During a group discussion, Craig learns that Bobby is stressed about an upcoming interview, hoping to move to a group home. Bobby worries that the sweater he is wearing is all he has to wear for the interview, so Craig offers him one of his dad's dress shirts to wear.
Noelle (Emma Roberts), a patient admitted for self-harm, is impressed by Craig's kindness, and leaves him a note to meet with her later on. They attend a painting session for patients together, where Craig paints a picture of an imaginary city map which he describes as "like my own brain". Bobby tells Craig he is a father of a little girl, and has attempted to kill himself six times. As Craig tries to help Bobby with his problems, Bobby, in turn, helps Craig gain the courage to ask out Noelle.
One night, Nia stops by the hospital to visit Craig, revealing that she and Aaron have broken up. Craig invites Nia to his room, where she tries to seduce him. However, they are interrupted by Craig's roommate, Muqtada, who has not left their shared room during his stay. As Nia runs out, Craig chases her, declaring he loves her, unaware that Noelle is standing behind him. Upset, Noelle storms off, leaving behind a self-portrait she had planned to give him.
Craig eventually wins Noelle's forgiveness, and the pair briefly sneak out of the ward, onto the hospital roof. There, Noelle asks him out, and they kiss. Craig has an interview with the head physician, Dr. Minerva; he explains that he has realized that he wants to become an artist, and is thankful his problems aren't as bad as others.
That night, Craig asks the staff for a pizza party, so the patients can say goodbye to him and Bobby—both are being discharged the following day. Craig calls Aaron, asking him to bring a particular record. When Aaron arrives, he tells him that he and Nia are working out their problems and they hug. At the party, Craig plays the record of Egyptian music, bringing Muqtada out of his room.

documents.title: Tomorrow, When the War Began
documents.tagline: Where were you when everything changed?
documents.overview: Ellie Linton, a teen from an Australian coastal town, leads her friends on an excursion to a camp deep in the woods, dubbed "Hell." Upon their return, the youths find that their town has been overrun by an enemy army, and their friends and family have been imprisoned. When the hostile invaders become alerted to their presence, Ellie and her friends band together to escape -- and strike back against -- this mysterious enemy.
documents.plot:
The film begins with a video log by Ellie Linton. She asks the camera how she can tell their story. She suggests to herself "from the beginning."
Ellie, a high school student in the fictional rural New South Wales town of Wirrawee sets off on a camping trip to a remote valley known as "Hell's Gate", or simply "Hell". She is joined by her close childhood friend Corrie McKenzie, Corrie's boyfriend Kevin Holmes, Ellie's next-door neighbour Homer Yannos, her high school crush Lee Takkam, and her friends Robyn Mathers and Fiona "Fi" Maxwell. During their second night camping, Ellie wakes to a sky full of military aircraft.
Returning to Wirrawee, the group finds their homes abandoned, without power, internet or telephone service. From a hilltop, the group sees that the only lights are at the hospital and the showground. Upon reaching the showground, they find that the townspeople are being detained by a foreign military force. Ellie witnesses a man being shot in the head, and in her horror retreats too quickly, being spotted by a searchlight. They flee but are pursued by soldiers into the backyard of a house. Ellie explodes the fuel tank of a ride-on lawn mower, eliminating the soldiers. In the confusion, Lee and Robyn go missing.
Hiding at Corrie's house, the group witness an RAAF jet fighter being shot down by enemy aircraft. When an enemy helicopter performs a close examination of the house, Homer shoots out its searchlight. The group barely escape as a jet destroys the home.
Ellie and Homer sneak back into town, and find Robyn in her house. Lee has been wounded, and is being treated by Dr. Clements, the local dentist, who informs them that the invading forces are bringing in their equipment from ships moored in Cobbler's Bay, over the Heron Bridge. After a brief skirmish with a pair of armed buggies, Robyn, Homer, Lee and Ellie meet back at Corrie's home. They decide to return to Hell. On the way, they stop at a house and are greeted by school mate Chris, who is incredibly stoned and has no idea that a war is going on.
Ellie and Lee have a deep conversation about their lives, briefly kissing. When Ellie checks on Chris, who is meant to be standing watch, she finds him asleep while a military car narrowly passes by the house. She angrily wakes Chris up, rebuking him for almost getting them killed, and prepares to shoot him, but when her friends witness this, she relents.
They return to Hell, with plans to use it as a secluded hideout. While there, Lee tries to talk to Ellie about their feelings towards each other, but she angrily replies that she is confused and storms off. The group hears a radio transmission revealing that Australia has been invaded by Asian "Coalition Nations", who want Australia's vast natural resources to sustain their own growing populations. The transmission also reveals that Cobbler's Bay is one of only three main ports being used by the invaders.

documents.title: Monsters
documents.tagline: After Six Years, They're No Longer Aliens. They're Residents
documents.overview: Six years ago NASA discovered the possibility of alien life within our solar system. A probe was launched to collect samples, but crashed upon re-entry over Central America. Soon after, new life forms began to appear and half of Mexico was quarantined as an infected zone. Today, the American and Mexican military still struggle to contain "the creatures," while a journalist agrees to escort a shaken tourist through the infected zone in Mexico to the safety of the U.S. border.

documents.title: I Spit on Your Grave
documents.tagline: It's date night.
documents.overview: Jennifer is a writer working on a new novel and, needing to get out of the city to finish it, hires a riverside apartment in upstate New York to finish her book—attracting the attention of a number of rowdy male locals.
documents.plot:
I Spit on Your Grave is a 2010 American rape and revenge film, a remake of the controversial 1978 cult film of the same name, which was originally titled Day of the Woman. Directed by Steven R. Monroe and written by Stuart Morse from the original screenplay by Meir Zarchi, it stars Sarah Butler, Jeff Branson, Daniel Franzese, Rodney Eastman, Chad Lindberg, Tracey Walter and Andrew Howard. CineTel's president, Paul Hertzberg, produced it.

Novelist Jennifer Hills leaves New York City for a rented cabin in rural Louisiana to write in seclusion. On the way, gas station attendant Johnny Miller gives her directions and humiliates himself by flirting with her. When her plumbing clogs, it is repaired by Matthew, a stuttering plumber with an intellectual disability, whom she thanks with a quick kiss. Matthew mentions the kiss to Johnny and his friends Andy and Stanley, and Johnny, still stung by her rebuff, decides she must be taught a lesson. The men break into the cabin to torment and assault her. She escapes into the woods and finds Sheriff Storch, but after he brings her back and discovers drugs and alcohol there, he dismisses her account. When the others return, all five men rape her while Stanley films the attack. As Storch prepares to shoot her, Jennifer throws herself into the river and disappears.

Jennifer secretly begins stalking her attackers. Stanley finds his camera and tape stolen, Storch intercepts a copy sent to his wife, and the men turn on one another. Fearing loose ends, Storch kills Earl, the cabin's owner, during a hunting trip. Jennifer then takes her revenge one by one. She overpowers Matthew despite his apology, traps Stanley and leaves him to be blinded by crows while his camera records, kills Andy in a bathtub of lye, and tortures and mutilates Johnny, repeating the men's taunts to each of them. Posing as a teacher, she lures Storch to a park through his daughter, knocks him out and binds him with his own shotgun aimed at him, its trigger tied to the wrist of the unconscious Matthew. When Matthew wakes and moves, the gun fires and kills both men, and Jennifer, waiting outside, smiles at the sound.

Filming began in Louisiana in November 2009. It was released in the United States by Anchor Bay on October 8, 2010, grossing $572,809 on a $2 million budget. Reviews were generally negative, with 31% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 27, and Roger Ebert gave it zero stars. Two sequels followed.

documents.title: Flipped
documents.tagline: You never forget your first love.
documents.overview: When Juli meets Bryce in the second grade, she knows it's true love. After spending six years trying to convince Bryce the same, she's ready to give up - until he starts to reconsider.
documents.plot:
Flipped is a 2010 American romantic comedy-drama co-written and directed by Rob Reiner, based on Wendelin Van Draanen's 2001 novel. Callan McAuliffe and Madeline Carroll star as Bryce and Juli, with Rebecca De Mornay, Anthony Edwards, John Mahoney, Penelope Ann Miller and Aidan Quinn. Set from the late 1950s, it alternates between its two leads' perspectives. Warner Bros. released it in American cinemas on August 6, 2010.

In 1957, seven-year-old Bryce Loski moves in across the street from Julianna "Juli" Baker. Juli falls for him at first sight, but Bryce is unnerved and spends the next years trying to avoid her; at one point he pretends to date a popular girl to discourage her, a ruse that backfires. When Bryce's grandfather Chet moves in with the family, he takes an interest in Juli, who climbs an old sycamore tree she loves in an attempt to stop it being cut down. Her father Richard eventually talks her down, then consoles her with a painting of the tree, and Chet shows Bryce a newspaper article about her stand, hoping to open his eyes.

Juli raises hens from a school science project and gives the Loskis free eggs, but she is hurt to discover that Bryce has been throwing them away, supposedly because the Bakers' unkempt yard makes his father doubt their safety. Embarrassed, Juli sets about fixing the yard, and Chet helps her, becoming her friend. When Bryce's father sneers at the Bakers, Chet points out that they rent the house and spend much of their money caring for Juli's mentally disabled uncle Daniel. Encouraged by Chet to look beyond appearances, Juli begins to question her feelings, and after overhearing Bryce appear to go along with his friend Garrett's mockery of her and Daniel, she loses interest in him. A strained family dinner leaves Bryce stung by her new indifference and seeing her as a person for the first time.

At the school's charity auction of "basket boys", Juli spends her egg money on another boy, Eddie, while Bryce is won by the popular Sherry. Realising that he is in love with Juli, Bryce tries to kiss her in front of everyone, and she flees in humiliation. He ends his friendship with Garrett and tries in vain to talk to her. Finally, with her father's permission, he plants a sycamore sapling in her front yard. Juli joins him, and as they plant it together they realise they have never truly talked.

The film drew lukewarm reviews and grossed about $4.3 million, but has since found a wider following.

documents.title: Tom and Jerry Meet Sherlock Holmes
documents.original_title: Tom and Jerry Meet Sherlock Holmes
documents.overview: Tom and Jerry need to learn to work together in order to help Sherlock Holmes with an investigation of a jewel theft. But still, they are cat and mouse!
documents.plot: Tom and Jerry need to learn to work together in order to help Sherlock Holmes with an investigation of a jewel theft. But still, they are cat and mouse!

documents.title: Soul Surfer
documents.tagline: When you come back from a loss, beat the odds, and never say never, you find a champion.
documents.overview: The true story of teen surfer Bethany Hamilton, who lost her arm in a shark attack and courageously overcame all odds to become a champion again, through her sheer determination and unwavering faith.
documents.plot:
Soul Surfer is a biographical sports drama film released in 2011, directed by Sean McNamara and produced by Brookwell-McNamara Entertainment. The movie tells the inspiring true story of professional surfer Bethany Hamilton.

The film begins with Bethany (played by AnnaSophia Robb) growing up on the island of Kauai, Hawaii, where she develops a passion for surfing at a young age. She is encouraged by her father, John (played by Dennis Quaid), who teaches her how to ride the waves and supports her dreams.

As Bethany's skills improve, she begins competing in local surf competitions, eventually earning recognition as one of the top junior surfers in Hawaii. Her talent and dedication catch the attention of professional surfer and mentor, Duke Kahanamoku (played by Chris Pine), who becomes a source of inspiration for Bethany.

Tragedy strikes when Bethany is attacked by a shark while surfing on December 31, 2003, during New Year's Eve celebrations. The incident leaves her with a severed arm and a deep emotional scar. Despite the odds against her, Bethany refuses to give up on her dreams and undergoes extensive surgery and rehabilitation.

With the support of her family, including her mother, Cheri (played by Lorraine Nicholson), and her father, John, Bethany begins an incredible journey of recovery and perseverance. She learns to adapt to her new prosthetic arm and continues to pursue her passion for surfing.

As Bethany's physical healing progresses, she faces a series of mental and emotional challenges. She struggles with feelings of anger, sadness, and self-doubt, but ultimately finds solace in her faith and the support of those around her.

The film culminates with Bethany's triumphant return to competitive surfing, where she faces off against some of the world's top surfers. Despite facing setbacks and injuries, Bethany perseveres and eventually wins several major competitions, including the ASP World Surfing Championship.

Throughout the movie, Soul Surfer showcases Bethany's remarkable resilience, determination, and faith in the face of adversity. The film is a testament to the power of the human spirit and serves as an inspiration to audiences worldwide.

Overall, Soul Surfer is a heartwarming and uplifting film that celebrates the triumphs and challenges faced by Bethany Hamilton. With its inspiring true story, stunning surfing sequences, and outstanding performances from the cast, this movie is sure to leave viewers feeling uplifted and motivated.

documents.title: Lake Placid 3
documents.tagline: Don't forget you're lunch.
documents.overview: A game warden moves his family to Lake Placid, once the site of deadly crocodile attacks. Locals assure him the crocs are gone, but his mischievous young son finds a few baby crocs and begins feeding them. They quickly grow into very big adults and start attacking the game warden's family and nearby town.
documents.plot:
At Black Lake, in Aroostook County, Maine, young couple April and Jason go skinny dipping and are attacked and killed by juvenile crocodiles. Meanwhile, at the house of the deceased Sadie Bickerman, her nephew Nathan, his wife Susan, and their son Connor, are cleaning out the house so they can sell it. However, sheriff Tony Willinger soon arrives, and convinces Nathan and Susan not to sell. Connor chases an escaped pet lizard down to the lake and encounters the juvenile crocodiles that eat the lizard and begins to secretly feed them.
Two years later, Connor has continued to feed the now adult crocodiles stolen meat from the supermarket, but is soon caught for shoplifting by Dimitri and sent home by Susan to his babysitter Vica. However, Connor goes to the lake to feed the crocodiles, followed by Vica; who is attacked while her dog Teddy is eaten. Vica, whose arm is badly injured, finds Susan at Sadie's house, where they tend to Vica's arm and Connor confesses to feeding the crocodiles out of spite for a pet and due to the fact that his parents haven't been spending time with him. Meanwhile, Nathan is searching the lake; due to a number of elk disappearances. He meets four teenagers - Ellie, Tara, Aaron and Charlie - who are camping on the lake. The teenagers show Nathan an elk head they previously found, leading Nathan to believe that it was the act of hunter Reba, but the head disappears before he can show it to Tony. Nevertheless, he persuades Tony to search the lake to ensure that it is clear of crocodiles. While the teenagers camp, they decide to go swimming and the girls go into the woods to strip off their clothes and get into their bikinis. Charlie spies on them and watches them stripping their clothes and taking pictures, but he is then eaten by a crocodile.
Reba is approached by teenager Brett, to help him find his girlfriend Ellie; who he fears will be taken advantage of by Aaron. Reba agrees and takes Brett out onto the lake in her boat with Jonas and Walt. As they stop to hunt elk, a crocodile attacks the boat and knocks the group into the water. Walt is devoured, but the others escape to shore and are stranded in the woods. After hours, Ellie and Aaron search for the missing Charlie, leaving Tara by the lake where she is killed by a crocodile. Ellie and Aaron return to find her missing, so they decide to try and get help. They discover Charlie's corpse, then find Brett's jacket. Ellie decides to search for Brett, upsetting Aaron; who walks the other way, only to be attacked by a crocodile.
After searching the lake, Nathan and Tony arrive at Sadie's house and join Susan, Connor and Vica. They decide to try and escape from the house to go to a hospital, but as they do so, Vica and Tony are devoured, and the car is submerged in the lake. Nathan, Susan and Connor take shelter in the house.

documents.title: Devil
documents.tagline: Bad Things Happen For A Reason
documents.overview: A group of people are trapped in an elevator high above Philadelphia, and one of them is the devil.
documents.plot:
Devil is a 2010 American supernatural horror film directed by John Erick Dowdle, with a screenplay by Brian Nelson based on a story by M. Night Shyamalan. Released by Universal Pictures on September 17, 2010, it was the first and only entry in The Night Chronicles, a planned trilogy of standalone horror films produced by Shyamalan. Its premise draws on the idea of a "Devil's Meeting", in which the Devil comes to Earth to torment wrongdoers, and Shyamalan described its structure as a nod to Agatha Christie's And Then There Were None.

After a man leaps to his death from a Philadelphia skyscraper leaving a note about the Devil, an elevator in the same building stalls with five strangers inside: a temporary security guard, a mechanic who is a Marine veteran, a mattress salesman, a young woman and an elderly woman. Watching on a camera that lets them speak to the passengers but not hear them, guards Ramirez and Lustig see what Ramirez believes is the Devil's face. Each time the lights fail, someone is hurt or killed, starting with the salesman. Detective Bowden, still grieving the wife and son he lost in a hit-and-run five years earlier, takes charge as the repairman and then Lustig die in accidents.

Bowden's team finds that every passenger has a guilty past, from assault and a Ponzi scheme to theft, while the unidentified mechanic becomes the chief suspect. The old woman is found hanged, and the guard Ben and then Sarah are killed in later blackouts. The mechanic's fiancée identifies him as Tony Janekowski, revealing that "Jane Kowski" was a false identity: the Devil had taken the old woman's form. Tony confesses that he caused the hit-and-run, and because he repents, the Devil cannot take his soul. Bowden, who reveals that the victims were his own family, forgives him.

Chris Messina plays Bowden, with Logan Marshall-Green as Tony, Geoffrey Arend, Bojana Novakovic, Jenny O'Hara, Bokeem Woodbine, Matt Craven, and Jacob Vargas as Ramirez, who also narrates. Filming began in Toronto in October 2009. Not screened for critics, the film drew mixed reviews, with 49% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, a Metacritic score of 44 and a CinemaScore of C+, but it earned $63.4 million on a $10 million budget.

documents.title: Unstoppable
documents.tagline: 1,000,000 Tons. 100,000 Lives. 100 Minutes.
documents.overview: A runaway train, transporting deadly, toxic chemicals, is barreling down on Stanton, Pennsylvania,  and proves to be unstoppable until a veteran engineer and young conductor risk their lives to try and stop it with a switch engine.
documents.plot:
Unstoppable is a 2010 American action thriller film directed by Tony Scott and starring Denzel Washington and Chris Pine.

The movie begins with two railroad workers, Frank Barnes (Denzel Washington) and Will Colson (Chris Pine), who are part of a crew tasked with inspecting the rail tracks for any potential hazards. During their inspection, they discover that a train carrying toxic chemicals has been left unattended on a bridge over the river, and it's headed straight towards a populated area.

As Frank and Will try to alert their superiors about the impending disaster, they realize that no one seems to be taking them seriously. The railroad company is more concerned with meeting its deadlines than with ensuring public safety. Frustrated and feeling ignored, Frank decides to take matters into his own hands and sets out to stop the train himself.

Frank's plan involves using a locomotive to derail the toxic train by ramming it from behind. However, he knows that this is a high-risk move, as it could result in catastrophic consequences if anything goes wrong. Despite the risks, Frank is determined to save lives and decides to put his plan into action.

As Frank sets out to stop the train, Will becomes increasingly concerned about his friend's actions and tries to persuade him to reconsider. However, Frank is resolute in his decision, and he begins to make his way towards the train.

The tension builds as Frank gets closer to the train, and the audience is left wondering if he will be able to stop it in time. The film's climax features a heart-pumping sequence where Frank uses his knowledge of the train's systems to outsmart the engineer and bring the train to a safe halt.

In the end, Frank's bravery and quick thinking save countless lives, but not without some personal costs. The movie ends on a somber note, with Frank reflecting on the consequences of his actions and the sacrifices he made to prevent a disaster.

Throughout the film, Denzel Washington delivers a powerful performance as Frank Barnes, bringing depth and nuance to the character. Chris Pine provides solid support as Will Colson, playing off Washington's intensity to create a compelling dynamic between the two leads.

Overall, Unstoppable is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of bravery, sacrifice, and the importance of putting public safety above all else. With its gripping plot and strong performances, it's no wonder this film has become a modern classic in the action-thriller genre.

documents.title: Nang Nak
documents.tagline: Death Never Do Us Part.
documents.overview: In a rural village in Thailand, Mak is sent to fight in a war and leaves his pregnant wife, Nak. Mak is injured and barely survives. He returns home to his doting wife and child, or so he thinks.

documents.title: 127 Hours
documents.tagline: There is no force more powerful than the will to live.
documents.overview: The true story of mountain climber Aron Ralston's remarkable adventure to save himself after a fallen boulder crashes on his arm and traps him in an isolated canyon in Utah.
documents.plot:
"127 Hours" is a biographical drama film directed by Danny Boyle, released in 2010 by Fox Searchlight Pictures. The film is based on the true story of Aron Ralston, an American outdoorsman and mountain climber.

The movie begins with Aron Ralston (played by James Franco) as a successful outdoor enthusiast who has spent years exploring the wilderness. He is shown to be in his element, free-spirited and adventurous. However, this carefree life takes a drastic turn when he becomes trapped in a canyon in Utah.

On April 26, 2003, Aron is on a solo hike in the Blue John Canyon, trying to find a way out of the narrow passageway. As he navigates through the tight space, his arm gets caught under a boulder, which falls and pins him against the wall. Panicked and desperate for help, Aron tries to free himself but is unable to do so.

The next 127 hours (the title refers to the duration of Aron's entrapment) are filled with intense physical and mental struggles as he tries to survive without food or water. He uses his knowledge of wilderness survival to ration his remaining energy, creating a makeshift shelter and signaling for help using his phone and other objects.

As time passes, Aron becomes increasingly desperate, and the psychological strain begins to take its toll on him. He starts to hallucinate and experience vivid dreams, which serve as a coping mechanism to deal with the unbearable situation.

Meanwhile, back in civilization, Aron's friends and family are frantically searching for him. His girlfriend, Cindy (played by Kate Mara), is particularly worried and tries to reach out to him through phone calls and messages.

In a dramatic turn of events, Aron finally manages to free himself from the boulder using his knowledge of anatomy and leverage. However, in doing so, he suffers severe injuries, including a mangled arm and deep lacerations on his hand.

The film's climax shows Aron making his way out of the canyon, where he is met by rescuers who had been searching for him for days. The movie ends with Aron being airlifted to safety, where he undergoes extensive surgery to repair his injuries.

Throughout the film, James Franco delivers a powerful and nuanced performance as Aron Ralston, capturing the complexity of his character's emotions and struggles. The film's tense atmosphere and stunning cinematography add to the overall sense of urgency and desperation that defines Aron's ordeal.

Overall, "127 Hours" is a gripping and emotionally charged drama that explores themes of survival, resilience, and redemption in the face of unimaginable adversity.

documents.title: Wild Target
documents.tagline: They said 'Take her out'. He got the wrong idea.
documents.overview: Victor Maynard is a middle-aged, solitary assassin who lives to please his formidable mother, despite his own peerless reputation for lethal efficiency. His professional routine is interrupted when he finds himself drawn to one of his intended victims. After sparing her life, he unexpectedly acquires a young apprentice. Believing Victor to be a private detective, his two new companions tag along, while he attempts to thwart the murderous attentions of his unhappy client.
documents.plot:
Victor Maynard is a reclusive hit-man perpetuating a family line of professional assassins. His father, a well-known assassin, is deceased, but he operates under the constant watchful gaze of his domineering mother, Louisa, who wants him to preserve the family reputation.
Rose is an ingenious con artist, who manages to sell a fake Rembrandt, painted by her friend in the Restoration Department of the National Gallery, to Ferguson, a billionaire, for £900,000. Ferguson responds by hiring Victor to assassinate her. Victor takes the contract, but misses several opportunities to kill her, finally giving up the attempt entirely as he falls in love with his intended victim.
Thwarting another assassin's attempt to kill Rose, Victor encounters Tony, an apparently homeless young man, who is thrown into the already complex lives of Victor and Rose. For a while Victor mistakenly wonders if he is sexually attracted to Tony, but later adopts the young man as a protégé and apprentice in the assassination business.
Ferguson, still determined to have his revenge, hires Dixon, reputed to be second only to Victor in proficiency, to kill both Rose and Victor. While staying at a luxurious hotel to hide from Ferguson's men, the trio are discovered and Ferguson chases them in the street, resulting in a car crash where Ferguson becomes grievously injured, and the trio successfully escapes.
Dixon, with a henchman, tracks the trio to the Maynard family home, deep in the English countryside. Louisa kills the henchman, but Dixon grabs Victor's father's Mauser gun to kill Victor. The gun turns out to be a booby trap, which fires backward due to a clogged barrel, killing Dixon. Victor and Rose bury the two assassins.
Three years later, Victor and Rose are married and have a son named Angel. While eating lunch outside their house, Tony comes out and asks where the family cat is; and Victor sees that his son has killed and buried the cat discreetly. Victor proudly smiles at his son, realizing that his son has what it takes to be his successor.

documents.title: Black Swan
documents.tagline: Perfection is not what it seems.
documents.overview: A journey through the psyche of a young ballerina whose starring role as the duplicitous swan queen turns out to be a part for which she becomes frighteningly perfect.
documents.plot:
Nina Sayers, an introverted young dancer employed by the New York City Ballet, lives with her overprotective mother, Erica, a former ballerina. After forcing the current principal dancer, Beth MacIntyre, into retirement due to her age, artistic director Thomas Leroy announces that the company is opening the season with Tchaikovsky's Swan Lake and he is looking for a new dancer for the dual roles of the innocent and fragile White Swan, Odette, and the dark and sensual Black Swan, Odile. When Nina visits the dressing room previously occupied by Beth, she steals Beth's lipstick.
At the auditions, Nina gives a flawless performance as Odette, but struggles to embody Odile. The arrival of newcomer Lily in the middle of Nina's audition causes her to lose her balance during her fouettés. As a result, Thomas passes on Nina for the lead role and she returns home to her mother devastated. Later that night, Nina practices her fouettés in front of a mirror, but she pushes too hard and breaks her toenail. While tending to her injury, Erica reassures Nina that everything will be okay by tomorrow morning. Determined to win the lead role, Nina meets with Thomas in his office the next morning and asks him to reconsider.
Thomas seemingly dismisses Nina and claims he has chosen Veronica, but he challenges her to change his mind. When Thomas critiques Nina's strengths and weaknesses as a dancer, he forcibly kisses her. She responds by biting his lips and apologizes before running out of his office. Nina congratulates Veronica, but Veronica accuses Nina of cruelly pranking her before storming off. Confused, Nina sees the cast list and learns she has been cast in the lead role. At a gala celebrating the new season, Thomas announces Nina as the company's new principal dancer as well as Beth's retirement and final performance, causing Beth to walk out.
An intoxicated Beth confronts Nina and accuses her of providing sexual favors to Thomas in exchange for the role. At Thomas's loft, he asks Nina questions about her sex life before suggesting that she masturbate to loosen her inhibitions. Nina does so the next morning, but stops upon seeing her mother asleep in a chair next to her. During rehearsals, Nina and the rest of the company learn that Beth has been hospitalized. Thomas reveals to Nina that Beth was hit by a car, convinced that she had attempted suicide. Nina visits Beth in hospital and is distraught to see her injured legs, having been permanently paralyzed.
Thomas and Nina observe Lily, who has a physical resemblance to Nina but also an uninhibited quality that Nina lacks. As opening night nears, Nina begins having hallucinations and finds scratch marks on her back. Following a sensual one-on-one rehearsal between Nina and Thomas, he admonishes her for her lack of progress. Nina learns from Thomas that he was told by Lily to go easy on her, leading to a falling out between the two dancers.

documents.title: Camp Rock 2: The Final Jam
documents.tagline: It's all about the music.
documents.overview: Mitchie can't wait to go back to Camp Rock and spend the summer making new music with her friends and superstar Shane Gray. But the slick new camp across the lake, Camp Star, has drummed up some serious competition – featuring newcomers Luke and Dana. In a sensational battle of the bands, with Camp Rock's future at stake, will Camp Star's flashy production and over-the-top antics win out, or will Camp Rockers prove that music, teamwork, and spirit are what truly matter?

documents.title: Dragon Ball Z: Broly – Second Coming
documents.original_title: ドラゴンボールＺ 危険なふたり！超戦士はねむれない
documents.tagline: Broly Is Back!
documents.overview: A Saiyan Space pod crash-lands on Earth out of which a wounded Saiyan crawls: Broly, the Legendary Super Saiyan. The wounded Broly shouts out in frustration and turns into normal form. The place soon freezes, trapping him in it and he falls into a coma.
documents.plot:
Dragon Ball Z: Broly - Second Coming is a 1994 Japanese animated science fantasy martial arts film directed by Daisuke Nishio and produced by Toei Animation. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1993 film Dragon Ball Z: Broly - The Legendary Super Saiyan.

The story begins with Goku, Trunks, and Pan training on Earth when they are suddenly attacked by a group of powerful warriors from the planet Vagar. These warriors are revealed to be members of the Ginyu Force, a group of elite fighters who serve under Frieza, the main antagonist of the Dragon Ball Z series.

The Ginyu Force is led by Captain Ginyu, a skilled fighter with the ability to transform into different forms. The team's mission is to capture Goku and use his power to awaken Broly, a powerful warrior from the planet Vegeta who was thought to be dead.

Meanwhile, on Planet Vegeta, Broly is awakened by the energy of the Ginyu Force's attack on Earth. He quickly becomes enraged and begins to wreak havoc on the planet, destroying everything in his path.

Goku, Trunks, and Pan soon discover that Broly has been awakened and are forced to flee from him. They eventually team up with Vegeta, who is initially reluctant to help them but ultimately joins forces to stop Broly.

As the battle between Goku's allies and Broly intensifies, it becomes clear that Broly's power is far greater than anyone had anticipated. Despite his incredible strength, however, Broly struggles with his own emotions and identity, which makes him a complex and sympathetic character.

In the end, Goku and Vegeta are able to defeat Broly using a combination of their skills and teamwork. However, not before Broly's true nature is revealed: he is actually the long-lost son of Vegeta and the one who was responsible for his father's downfall on Planet Vegeta.

The movie concludes with Broly's spirit being sent back to Planet Vegeta, where he will be able to find peace and redemption. Goku and his friends are left to reflect on the events that transpired and the true nature of their enemy, Frieza, who is still at large.

Overall, Dragon Ball Z: Broly - Second Coming is a thrilling and action-packed film that explores themes of identity, power, and redemption. The movie's complex characters and intricate plot make it a must-see for fans of the Dragon Ball Z series.

documents.title: Our Lady of the Assassins
documents.overview: World-weary arthur Fernando has returned to his native Colombia to live out his days in peace.  But Fernando's once-quiet hometown has become a hotbed of violence, drugs and corruption.  On the brink of despair, Fernando meets Alexis, a beautiful but hardened street kid who lives by the rule of the gun.  Together, they forge an unlikely relationship.
documents.plot:
Our Lady of the Assassins (Spanish: La virgen de los sicarios) is a 2000 Spanish-language romantic crime drama directed by Barbet Schroeder from a screenplay by Fernando Vallejo, adapted from his own 1994 novel. Germán Jaramillo stars as Fernando, a Colombian writer in his fifties who returns to his native Medellín after some thirty years away, with Anderson Ballesteros as Alexis, Juan David Restrepo as Wilmar and Manuel Busquets as Alfonso.

Fernando has come home to die and finds the city he remembers transformed by the violence of the drug cartel wars. At a party given by an old friend he meets Alexis, a handsome young man, and falls for him at once. Their relationship, beyond sex, consists largely of Fernando reminiscing about the peaceful city of his youth while Alexis explains the everyday reality of robberies, shootings and killings. Alexis's company softens Fernando's sardonic, bitter outlook a little.

Fernando soon discovers that Alexis is himself a member of a gang and a hired killer, or sicario, and that rival gangs want him dead. Alexis fends off several attempts on his life with his skill with a pistol, but he is eventually shot dead by two boys on a motorcycle, at a moment when he no longer has his gun, which had been lost partly because of Fernando's own suicidal impulses.

After giving money to Alexis's mother, Fernando wanders the streets and meets Wilmar, a boy who resembles Alexis strikingly in both appearance and manner. He takes him to lunch and the two begin an affair that recreates his earlier relationship. Fernando is shocked to learn that Wilmar, also a killer, was the one who shot Alexis, and he vows to kill him, until he finds out that Alexis had begun the feud by murdering Wilmar's brother. The two plan to leave Colombia together, but Wilmar is killed when he goes to bid his mother farewell. Recognising that the endless cycle of violence in Medellín leaves no room for happiness, Fernando appears, in the final scene, to be contemplating taking his own life.

Shot on early high-definition video cameras, which gave it a documentary-like look, the film was among the first features made in HD. It won the President of the Italian Senate's Gold Medal at the 2000 Venice Film Festival, where it competed for the Golden Lion, and holds 77% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 73.

documents.title: Frozen
documents.tagline: No one knows you're up there.
documents.overview: When three skiers find themselves stranded on a chair lift at a New England ski resort that has closed for the next week, they are forced to make life or death choices that prove to be more perilous than staying put and freezing to death.
documents.plot:
Frozen is a 2010 American psychological horror survival film written and directed by Adam Green, starring Shawn Ashmore and Kevin Zegers and introducing Emma Bell. It follows three friends stranded on a chairlift after a day of skiing, forced to make life-or-death choices. It was filmed at Snowbasin near Ogden, Utah, in February 2009.

Dan Walker, his girlfriend Parker O'Neal and his best friend Joe Lynch spend a day at a ski resort. On the last evening, with the resort about to close for the week because of incoming bad weather, they persuade the lift operator to let them take one final run. A replacement operator takes over and, mistaking three other skiers for them, shuts down the lift, leaving the friends stranded high above the ground. As a snowstorm sets in, a snow groomer passes below without its driver noticing them.

Realizing that no one knows where they are and that they will not survive until the resort reopens, Dan jumps from the chair, breaking both legs. Unable to reach him, Parker and Joe can only listen as a pack of wolves tears him apart. Grieving, the two blame each other before finding comfort, and Parker admits that she had hoped to marry Dan. The next morning, Joe shimmies along the razor-sharp cable to a support tower, badly cutting his hands and loosening the bolt that secures their chair. Climbing down, he fends off the wolves with a ski pole and sets off down the mountain on Parker's snowboard, promising to bring help, with the pack in pursuit. Parker spends another night alone on the lift. When Joe does not return, she tries to reach the tower herself, but the chair's bolt gives way and it drops to a few meters above the ground. She jumps, and the falling chair crushes her ankle. Sliding and crawling down the slope, she passes the wolves feeding on Joe's body, but they ignore her. Reaching a road, she is picked up by a passing driver who takes her to hospital, and she closes her eyes remembering Dan's words.

Frozen premiered at the 2010 Sundance Film Festival, where audience members reportedly fainted, and was released by Anchor Bay Films in North American theaters on February 5, 2010, grossing slightly less than $2.7 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed to positive, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 64% approval and Metacritic a score of 43. Bell later reprised her role in an epilogue scene in Hatchet II.

documents.title: The Dilemma
documents.tagline: Two best friends. Nothing could come between them... or could it?
documents.overview: Longtime friends Ronny and Nick are partners in an auto-design firm. They are hard at work on a presentation for a dream project that would really launch their company. Then Ronny spots Nick's wife out with another man, and in the process of investigating the possible affair, he learns that Nick has a few secrets of his own. As the presentation nears, Ronny agonizes over what might happen if the truth gets out.
