documents.plot: In the California desert, the adventures of a telepathic killer-tire, mysteriously attracted by a very pretty girl, as witnessed by incredulous onlookers.

documents.title: The Ward
documents.tagline: Only Sanity Can Keep You Alive!
documents.overview: Kristen, a troubled young woman, is captured by the police after burning down a farmhouse and is locked in the North Bend Psychiatric Hospital. Soon, she begins to suspect that the place has a dark secret at its core and she's determined to find out what it is.
documents.plot:
In rural Oregon, at the North Bend Psychiatric Hospital in 1966, a young patient named Tammy is killed by an unseen force at night.
Kristen, a troubled young woman, sets fire to an abandoned farmhouse and is arrested. The local police take her to North Bend, where she meets the other patients in the ward: artistic Iris, seductive Sarah, wild Emily, and child-like Zoey. Kristen is taken to a room previously occupied by their friend, Tammy, and meets therapist Dr. Stringer. She reveals that she is unable to recall anything about her past. She is attacked by a horribly deformed figure that had been staring at her earlier, but upon telling the nurse this, she is drugged and put through intense electroshock therapy.
Dr. Stringer uses hypnotherapy to unlock Iris's hidden memories. After the session, Iris is killed by transorbital lobotomy by the deformed figure. Kristen finds Iris' sketch of her attacker with the name 'Alice Hudson', a former patient at the hospital. That night, Kristen and Emily attempt to find Iris and escape. However, Kristen is thwarted by Alice and loses consciousness while Emily is caught.
Alice kills Sarah. Kristen discovers that all the girls had killed Alice together because Alice constantly hurt them. Now she is after the girls for revenge. Kristen tries to talk Emily down from attempting suicide but Alice kills her by slitting her throat with a scalpel. Kristen plans to escape again by holding Zoey as a pretend hostage but is drugged and placed in a straitjacket. She escapes it and she and Zoey try to get out. Zoey is killed by Alice off-screen. After a lengthy chase, Kristen seemingly manages to destroy Alice. She finds Alice's file in Dr. Stringer's office, which has each of the girls' names, including Kristen herself.
Dr. Stringer, catching her in his office, reveals that Kristen is actually one of many personalities of the real Alice Hudson, who was kidnapped at age eleven, eight years earlier, and left chained for two months in the basement of the same farmhouse Kristen burned down. In order to survive the trauma, she developed Dissociative Identity Disorder, creating each one of the girls from the ward as a different personality. Over time, Alice's own personality became so overwhelmed by the others that she became lost. Dr. Stringer attempted experimental techniques to bring Alice's own personality back, resulting in the manifestation of Ghost Alice, who destroyed the individual personalities one by one. Her treatments were working until 'Kristen' appeared, as an attempt of Alice's mind to protect the other personalities so she wouldn't need to face her trauma.
As the Kristen personality tries to come to terms with all this, Ghost Alice appears before her and the two begin to fight, each determined to emerge as the dominant personality. During this hallucinatory altercation, "Kristen" falls out the window and hits the ground several stories below.

documents.title: Space Chimps 2: Zartog Strikes Back
documents.tagline: Get ready to blast off on a new adventure.
documents.overview: Comet longs to be taken seriously as a full-fledged space chimp. He journeys to the fantastical Planet Malgor and bonds with the adorable alien Kilowatt, living out his ultimate fantasy. However, it's time for Comet to prove himself when the feared alien ruler Zartog takes over Mission Control! Comet must show he has the right stuff, and join fellow chimps Ham, Luna and Titan, to save the day.
documents.plot:
Two years after the events of the first film, Comet, a tech-savvy young chimpanzee, wants to be taken seriously as a full-fledged space chimp, but Ham, Luna and the other chimpanzees do not take him seriously. Comet learns that he was removed from the last space mission because of budget cuts, and plans to go on the next space mission. Comet interferes with the controls on a rocket, accidentally launching the ship into space. Eventually, Comet lands on the planet Malgor, where he meets Ham's alien friend, Kilowatt, and gains respect from the residents there.
However, back on Earth, Zartog wants to get revenge on Ham for foiling his plans, and encounters an oblivious Titan, who gives him a tour of Kennedy Space Center. Zartog takes over Mission Control using a remote that vaporizes objects and zaps the Senator and the three scientists, Dr. Bob, Dr. Jagu and Dr. Poole out of existence. Comet, accompanied by Kilowatt, returns to Earth, while Ham evades Zartog by riding on a jetpack. While Zartog is distracted, Comet manages to steal the remote and reprograms it to bring the Senator and the scientists back, and shrink Zartog; Zartog escapes while the others laugh. The film ends with Zartog running from a dog he harassed earlier and a Guinea pig from the Mars mission, mentioned in the prior film.

documents.title: Jackie Chan Kung Fu Master
documents.overview: Jackie Chan is the undefeated Kung Fu Master who dishes out the action in traditional Jackie Chan style. When a young boy sets out to learn how to fight from the Master himself, he not only witnesses some spectacular fights, but learns some important life lessons along the way.
documents.plot: Jackie Chan is the undefeated Kung Fu Master who dishes out the action in traditional Jackie Chan style. When a young boy sets out to learn how to fight from the Master himself, he not only witnesses some spectacular fights, but learns some important life lessons along the way.

documents.title: Scooby-Doo! Camp Scare
documents.tagline: Back-to-nature chills and thrills!
documents.overview: Scooby and the gang experience outdoor fun as they go back to Fred's old summer camp.
documents.plot: Scooby and the gang experience outdoor fun as they go back to Fred's old summer camp. As summer goes on, it becomes increasingly clear that the spooky camp stories told by the fireplace, are more real than they've though and soon, it's up to the gang to try and solve the mystery of camp scare.

documents.title: Gnomeo & Juliet
documents.tagline: A LITTLE ADVENTURE GOES A LAWN WAY.
documents.overview: A version of Shakespeare's play, set in the world of warring indoor and outdoor gnomes. Garden gnomes Gnomeo and Juliet have as many obstacles to overcome as their quasi namesakes when they are caught up in a feud between neighbors. But with plastic pink flamingos and lawnmower races in the mix, can this young couple find lasting happiness?
documents.plot:
Gnomeo & Juliet is a 3D animated comedy film released in 2011, produced by Reliance Entertainment and Miramax Films. The movie is an adaptation of William Shakespeare's classic tragic love story Romeo and Juliet, set in a world of garden gnomes.

In the beginning, we are introduced to Gnomeo (voiced by James McAvoy), a red gnome who lives in a beautiful garden filled with other colorful gnomes. Gnomeo is a bit of an oddball, as he loves to play video games and watch TV instead of engaging in traditional gnome activities like gardening.

One day, while out on a walk, Gnomeo meets Juliet (voiced by Emily Blunt), a lovely white gnome who lives in the neighboring garden. The two gnomes immediately fall in love at first sight, but their families have been feuding for years due to a long-standing dispute over a prized red rose.

The evil garden gnome, Lord Redbrick (voiced by Michael Caine), is determined to keep the red rose for himself and will stop at nothing to prevent Gnomeo and Juliet from being together. Meanwhile, Juliet's family, led by her father, King Verminus (voiced by Jim Broadbent), also wants to keep the red rose for themselves.

As Gnomeo and Juliet try to navigate their forbidden love, they must also contend with the rivalry between their families. The two gnomes come up with a plan to outsmart Lord Redbrick and his minions, but things don't go according to plan.

The plot development takes a dramatic turn when Gnomeo and Juliet's families engage in an all-out war, resulting in the destruction of both gardens. In the chaos, Gnomeo is captured by Lord Redbrick and forced to participate in a series of challenges to prove his worth as a gnome warrior.

Meanwhile, Juliet fakes her own death to avoid marrying another gnome, but Gnomeo believes she is really dead and sets out on a quest to find her. Along the way, he meets a wise old badger named Benny (voiced by Patrick Stewart) who helps him on his journey.

In the end, Gnomeo and Juliet finally reunite, but their happiness is short-lived. Lord Redbrick reveals that he has been manipulating events from behind the scenes, and the two gnomes are forced to confront each other in a final showdown.

The ending is a heartwarming and humorous take on the classic Romeo and Juliet story, with plenty of action, adventure, and witty banter. In the end, Gnomeo and Juliet's love prevails, and they are able to live happily ever after in their own little garden paradise.

Overall, Gnomeo & Juliet is a fun and lighthearted adaptation of Romeo and Juliet that is sure to delight audiences of all ages. With its colorful characters, witty dialogue, and exciting plot twists, this movie is a must-see for anyone who loves animation, comedy, or classic literature.

documents.title: Hole in One
documents.tagline: Big Risk, Big Rewards & Big Attitude!
documents.overview: Eric, a highly-gifted golfer but radically-undisciplined college undergrad, finds his world drastically altered after losing a golf bet to a pair of sadistic plastic surgeons. Eric's bad-boy attitude lifestyle comes to a screeching halt as he loses his money, his girlfriend, his dignity and his golf swing. Eric and his best friend Tyler decide to take on the doctors, in a final golf match of "Best-Ball" to get his life back and become the man he should have been all along.
documents.plot:
Hole in One, also released as ParFection: The Golf Movie, is an American sports sex comedy directed by Drew Ann Rosenberg and written by Mike Terrell and Mark Maine. Steve Talley stars as Eric Keller, a talented but undisciplined college golfer, with David Ellison as his friend Tyler Hayden, Sandy Modic as Tyler's sister Mandy, Dean Cameron and Christopher Showerman as a pair of scheming plastic surgeons, K.T. Tatara as Mark, and Dean Cain as a repo man.

Keller skips class to hustle strangers on the golf course, unaware that two men are watching him. At a party he nearly gets close to Mandy, whose protective brother Tyler, struggling to launch his golf apparel business PAHR, disapproves of Keller's lifestyle. When Keller hooks up with another student and Mark secretly films it, the video is shown at Tyler's shop and Mandy is hurt. Keller then accepts a match against the two strangers, who turn out to be surgeons Dr. Carlton and Dr. Hamilton of the company NuBoobs. If he wins he gets $50,000; if he loses, he becomes their test patient. The man who had been helping Keller hustle golfers turns out to be helping the doctors hustle him, and after losing he is tased and wakes up with breast implants.

The surgeons will only reverse the operation for $50,000, and give him two weeks to pay before they mail his photographs to family and friends. With Tyler's encouragement, Keller returns to the course and wins round after round, growing used to golfing with his new figure, while a repo man pursues his overdue Mustang. The pair raise $42,000, still short, so Keller proposes a final match: if they win, the surgery is reversed for free, and if they lose, Tyler gives up PAHR. Keller struggles until Mandy arrives with his father, who has received the photos anyway. Mandy forgives him, his father urges him to pursue golf, and Keller wins by a single stroke. The surgeons refuse to honor the deal but are chased off by a rapper's bodyguards, and the rapper agrees to back PAHR.

Distributed by Universal, the film launched in the United Kingdom on 12 September 2010, with releases in some 65 further territories. Although it was promoted with the tagline "American Pie Plays Golf" and stars Talley, who had appeared in two American Pie spin-offs, it is not part of that series. It drew little critical attention.

documents.title: Biutiful
documents.tagline: You don't choose your family. We all belong to somebody, but to belong to Uxbal and Marambra, is both a blessing and a curse.
documents.overview: This is a story of a man in free fall. On the road to redemption, darkness lights his way. Connected with the afterlife, Uxbal is a tragic hero and father of two who's sensing the danger of death. He struggles with a tainted reality and a fate that works against him in order to forgive, for love, and forever.
documents.plot:
Uxbal lives in a shabby apartment in Barcelona with his two young children, Ana and Mateo. He is separated from their mother Marambra, an alcoholic masseuse with bipolar disorder. Having grown up an orphan, Uxbal has no family other than his brother Tito, who works in the construction business (and sometimes solicits Marambra's services). Uxbal earns a living by procuring work for a group of Chinese illegal immigrants who make forged designer goods which a group of African street vendors then sell. He also works as a medium to the dead, passing on messages from the recently deceased at wakes and funerals. When he is diagnosed with terminal prostate cancer, leaving him with only a few months to live, his world progressively falls apart.
Uxbal initially begins chemotherapy, but he later ends the treatment at the advice of his friend Bea, an alternative healer. She gives him two black stones which she asks him to give his children before he dies. The group of Africans are arrested by the police, despite Uxbal's regular payment of bribes, because they also deal in drugs. When one of them is deported back to Senegal, Uxbal offers his wife Ige and baby son a room in his apartment. Meanwhile, an attempt at reconciliation with Marambra fails when Uxbal realizes she cannot be trusted to look after their children. As the Chinese are out of work, Tito brokers a deal to get them employed at a construction site. However, almost all of them die in the night from carbon monoxide poisoning, as the cheap gas heaters Uxbal bought in an effort to help were not safe. An attempt by a human trafficker to dump the bodies into the sea fails when they are washed up on the shore shortly after, causing a media sensation.
As Uxbal's health continues to deteriorate, he is plagued with guilt that he is responsible for the expulsion of the Senegalese and the death of the Chinese. With his death drawing nearer, he realizes that there will be nobody to take care of Ana and Mateo once he is gone. He entrusts the remainder of his savings to Ige, asking her to stay with the children after his death. She accepts his request but later decides to use the money to return to Africa. At the apartment, Uxbal sees Ige's silhouette behind the bathroom door and hears her voice saying she has returned. Uxbal lies down next to Ana and, after having passed on to her a diamond ring which his father had once given to his mother, he dies. In a snowy winter landscape he is reunited with his father, who had died before Uxbal's birth and shortly after having fled Francoist Spain for Mexico.

documents.title: Sorority Wars
documents.tagline: Let the catfights begin
documents.overview: Katie, a college freshman, has been groomed from birth to continue her mother’s legacy with the Deltas. When Katie decides to pledge another house instead, an all-out sorority war commences.
documents.plot:
Sorority Wars is a 2009 American comedy-drama television film directed by James Hayman and written by Michelle Lovretta, made for the Lifetime network. It stars Lucy Hale, Courtney Thorne-Smith, Phoebe Strole, Amanda Schull, Rob Mayes and Faith Ford, and was produced by RHI Entertainment with Von Zerneck Sertner Films and Patricia Clifford Productions. Shot in Vancouver, it premiered on Lifetime on 17 October 2009.

Eighteen-year-old Katie Parker and her childhood best friend Sara Snow arrive at college planning to rush Delta Beta Theta, the sorority co-founded nearly three decades earlier by Katie's mother, Lutie, and her best friend, Summer. Katie has been groomed since birth to carry on her mother's Delta legacy, and the house is eager to recruit her. During rush week, however, she clashes with Summer's daughter Gwen, the Deltas' ambitious incoming president, over her methods, and after Katie overhears something troubling, the dispute ends with her being cut from the Delta pledge class and shunned along Sorority Row.

With Sara choosing to stay with the Deltas, Katie finds herself alone and decides to pledge a rival house, the Kappas, led by Heather, whose atmosphere feels closer to her own values. Far from settling things, her defection strains her lifelong friendship with Sara, sparks an all-out war between the sororities on campus and stirs up tension among the Delta alumnae, including the friendship between the two mothers.

Lucy Hale plays Katie, with Courtney Thorne-Smith as Lutie, Faith Ford as Summer, Amanda Schull as Gwen, Phoebe Strole as Sara, Kristen Hager as Heather and Rob Mayes as Beau; the supporting cast includes Adrian Hough, Sarah-Jane Redmond, Chelan Simmons and Marie Avgeropoulos. Samantha Jade's song "Get Away" is heard several times, sung by Hale's character. Pierre F. Brault composed the score.

Reviews were generally positive. Linda Stasi of the New York Post gave the film three and a half stars out of four, calling it bizarrely entertaining in a mindless way and praising Hale as quite a talent, while Brian Lowry of Variety found it moderately engaging and cheerfully mindless, with an appealing lead performance from Hale. The film was later broadcast in France as De mères en filles and in Italy and Portugal under local titles.

documents.title: Troll Hunter
documents.tagline: You’ll believe it when you see it!
documents.overview: A group of students investigates a series of mysterious bear killings, but learns that there are much more dangerous things going on. They start to follow a mysterious hunter, learning that he is actually a troll hunter.
documents.plot:
Troll Hunter is a Norwegian fantasy adventure film directed by André Øvredal and written by André Øvredal and Michael Fimognari. The movie was released in 2010.

The story begins with a young boy named Erik (Laurin Lundstrøm) who has always been fascinated by the supernatural creatures that are said to inhabit the forests of Norway. According to legend, trolls are real and can be found in the wilderness, but they are rarely seen by humans due to their ability to blend into their surroundings.

Erik's life is turned upside down when he meets a group of men who claim to be troll hunters. The group, led by Oskar (Stig Raetta), consists of experienced hunters who have dedicated their lives to tracking and killing the trolls that threaten human settlements.

As Erik joins the group, they embark on a mission to hunt down a particularly large and aggressive troll that has been terrorizing a nearby village. Along the way, Erik learns about the history and mythology behind the trolls, as well as the skills and techniques required to track and kill them.

Throughout their journey, the group faces numerous challenges and obstacles, including treacherous terrain, harsh weather conditions, and even other hunters who are not what they seem. As they get closer to their target, Erik begins to question whether the trolls are truly monstrous creatures or if there is more to them than meets the eye.

As the story unfolds, Erik discovers that the trolls are not just mindless beasts but rather complex beings with their own culture and society. The group's leader, Oskar, has a personal connection to the trolls that he keeps hidden from his team, adding an air of mystery to the narrative.

In the end, the group faces off against the troll in an epic battle that tests their skills and their resolve. As the dust settles, Erik is forced to confront the reality of what he has learned about the trolls and the world they inhabit.

The movie ends on a bittersweet note, with Erik reflecting on his experience as a troll hunter and the lessons he has learned about the importance of respecting and understanding the natural world. The final shot of the film shows Oskar walking away from the camera, leaving behind the life of a troll hunter and embracing a new path.

Overall, Troll Hunter is a thrilling adventure that combines elements of fantasy, action, and coming-of-age drama. With its richly detailed world-building and complex characters, the movie offers a unique take on the traditional troll mythology.

documents.title: Twitches Too
documents.overview: Reunited witch twins Camryn and Alex adjust to their new life as supernatural beings while at the same time trying to maintain a normal existence in this sequel to the magical Disney Channel original movie Twitches. But they soon find themselves going head to head with the forces of darkness that threaten to destroy their world. Luckily, their birth mother, the powerful Miranda, is on hand to help out.
documents.plot: Reunited witch twins Camryn and Alex adjust to their new life as supernatural beings while at the same time trying to maintain a normal existence in this sequel to the magical Disney Channel original movie Twitches. But they soon find themselves going head to head with the forces of darkness that threaten to destroy their world. Luckily, their birth mother, the powerful Miranda, is on hand to help out.

documents.title: Rio
documents.tagline: 1 out of every 8 Americans is afraid of flying. Most of them don't have feathers.
documents.overview: Captured by smugglers when he was just a hatchling, a macaw named Blu never learned to fly and lives a happily domesticated life in Minnesota with his human friend, Linda. Blu is thought to be the last of his kind, but when word comes that Jewel, a lone female, lives in Rio de Janeiro, Blu and Linda go to meet her. Animal smugglers kidnap Blu and Jewel, but the pair soon escape and begin a perilous adventure back to freedom -- and Linda.
documents.plot:
Rio is a 2011 animated musical comedy film produced by Blue Sky Studios and distributed by 20th Century Fox.

The movie begins with Blu, an African grey parrot who lives in Minnesota with his owner, Linda. Blu's life is mundane and predictable, but he dreams of adventure. One day, Linda receives an invitation from the Brazilian government to participate in the Bird Festival, a prestigious event that celebrates the world's most beautiful birds.

Linda decides to take Blu along on the trip, hoping it will be a fun experience for both of them. However, things quickly become complicated when they arrive in Rio de Janeiro and discover that Blu is not just any ordinary parrot - he's actually a rare species from the wild.

Upon arrival, Blu meets Jewel, a stunning blue macaw who is also participating in the Bird Festival. The two birds immediately fall in love, but their romance is threatened by the fact that Blu is not supposed to be with Jewel, as they are from different species and have different personalities.

As the festival progresses, Blu and Jewel embark on a series of misadventures, including getting caught up in a plot by the villainous Nigel, a European macaw who seeks to capture all the rarest birds in Rio. Along the way, Blu learns about his own identity and the importance of being true to oneself.

Throughout their journey, Blu and Jewel face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, fierce predators, and even a wild storm that threatens to destroy the festival. However, through it all, they learn to rely on each other and trust themselves.

In the end, Blu and Jewel successfully outsmart Nigel and save the Bird Festival. The movie concludes with Blu and Jewel flying off into the sunset, ready to start their new life together.

Rio features a talented voice cast, including Jesse Eisenberg as Blu, Anne Hathaway as Jewel, and Jamie Foxx as Rafael, a charming toucan who becomes Blu's friend and ally. The film's vibrant animation and catchy musical numbers make it a delightful and entertaining watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Rio is a heartwarming and action-packed animated adventure that celebrates the beauty of nature and the power of love and self-discovery.

documents.title: No Time for Nuts
documents.tagline: The acorn of fate.
documents.overview: Scrat comes across a time machine and is transported to various times all in pursuit of his beloved acorn.
documents.plot:
No Time for Nuts is a 2006 American computer-animated short film from Blue Sky Studios featuring Scrat, the acorn-obsessed prehistoric creature of the Ice Age franchise, voiced by Chris Wedge. Directed by Chris Renaud and Mike Thurmeier, it runs about seven minutes and was released on the home video edition of Ice Age: The Meltdown in November 2006.

Set between the events of the second and third Ice Age films, the short opens with Scrat looking for a spot to bury his beloved acorn. Digging into the ice, he uncovers a frozen time machine whose display reads 20,000 B.C. It suddenly activates and hurls Scrat and the acorn into the Middle Ages, where the nut becomes stuck beneath a heavy boulder. Scrat grabs the sword Excalibur to pry it loose, only to come under fire from archers; he deflects the arrows with the blade and hides inside a cannon, which promptly launches him into their path. The machine then sends him to the Colosseum of ancient Rome, where he mistakes a fanfare for applause until a big cat growls behind him, and next to an ice field where he believes he is home until the RMS Titanic bears down on him.

The machine even drops him into the time of the first film, where he fights his own past self for the acorn while Manny, Sid, Diego and the baby Roshan look on. Chasing the acorn through history, Scrat lands in one deadly predicament after another, escaping each just in time: beneath a launching Saturn V rocket, under a guillotine during the French Revolution, beside Benjamin Franklin's kite experiment and in the path of a wrecking ball. A frustrated punch to the machine throws him into a strange dimension of clocks, where he is split into copies and sucked into a wormhole. He awakens before a gigantic oak tree and happily discards his acorn, only to discover that the tree is a monument marking the last oak, since oaks are extinct in this distant future. As he lunges for his acorn, the only real one left, the machine fires one final time and sends it away before falling apart, leaving Scrat screaming in despair.

The short was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film and won an Annie Award.

documents.title: Don't Be Afraid of the Dark
documents.original_title: Don't Be Afraid of the Dark
documents.tagline: Fear is never just make believe
documents.overview: A young girl sent to live with her father and his new girlfriend discovers creatures in her new home who want to claim her as one of their own.
documents.plot:
At Blackwood Manor in Providence County, Rhode Island in the 19th century, renowned wildlife painter Lord Emerson Blackwood summons his housekeeper to the basement and reluctantly bludgeons her to death. He removes her teeth, as well as his own, and offers them to mysterious creatures inside an ash pit within an old fireplace; the creatures reject his offer and demand only the teeth of children. Blackwood begs for them to return his son, only to be dragged inside.
In the present day, 8-year-old Sally Hurst arrives in Rhode Island to live with her father Alex and his girlfriend Kim. The two are renovating Blackwood Manor for a client. Sally is depressed due to her mother dumping her in Alex's care and giving her copious amounts of Adderall. The creatures are awakened by a tune from the nightlight. The next day, Sally follows the voices calling her name to a sealed fireplace. "BE AFRAID" is written in runes above it.
Sally unbolts the fireplace and finds some of the housekeeper's teeth. The creatures prove to be hostile, stealing Alex's razor and shredding Kim's clothes. Alex blames Sally and finds a 19th-century silver coin in her possession, which she found under her pillow after a tooth she placed there disappeared. Sally sneaks to the basement to talk with the creatures, but Mr. Harris, one of the workers, tries to seal up the fireplace. He is attacked by the creatures and hospitalised.
Kim visits Mr. Harris in the hospital, who directs her to the local library, where she finds Lord Blackwood's unpublished artwork depicting tooth fairy-like creatures. The librarian explains they sometimes turn a human into one of their own. Sally is attacked again by the creatures, whose leader is a transformed Lord Blackwood. Kim finds a mural painted by Blackwood, depicting his son being taken by the creatures. Sally is trapped in the library by the creatures, but she keeps them at bay using her camera flash, as light repels them. She manages to kill one by crushing it with a bookcase.
Alex and Kim try to flee the house with Sally, but they are all subdued. Sally awakens to find herself being dragged to the basement for her transformation. Kim frees Sally, only to get caught in the ropes; her legs are gruesomely broken. The creatures drag Kim into the fireplace, as a distraught Sally crushes the former Lord Blackwood to death. Alex and Sally mourn their loss.
Sometime later, Alex and Sally return to the abandoned mansion to leave a drawing of Kim there. After they leave, a draft blows the drawing into the creatures' lair; the entrance now bolted with metal. Kim has now been transformed. As the creatures plan to come out, Kim convinces them to stay in hiding because others will come and they "have all the time in the world."

documents.title: Of Gods and Men
documents.tagline: In the face of terror, their greatest weapon was faith...
documents.overview: French drama based on the 1996 kidnapping and killing of seven monks in Algeria. A group of Trappist monks reside in the monastery of Tibhirine in Algeria, where they live in harmony with the largely muslim population. When a bloody conflict between Algeria's army and Muslim Jihadi insurgents disrupts the peace, they are forced to consider fleeing the monastery and deserting the villagers they have ministered to. In the face of deadly violence the monks wrestle with their faith and their convictions, eventually deciding to stay and help their neighbours keep the army and the insurgents at bay.
documents.plot: A group of Trappist monks reside in the monastery of Tibhirine in Algeria, where they live in harmony with the largely Muslim population. When a bloody conflict between Algeria's army and Muslim Jihadi insurgents disrupts the peace, they are forced to consider fleeing the monastery and deserting the villagers they have ministered to. In the face of deadly violence, the monks wrestle with their faith and their convictions.

documents.title: The Loved Ones
documents.tagline: Don't break her heart
documents.overview: When Brent turns down his classmate Lola's invitation to the prom, she concocts a wildly violent plan for revenge.
documents.plot:
High schooler Brent is driving with his father Dan when a bloodied man appears in the middle of the road. Swerving to avoid the man, Brent crashes his vehicle into a tree, accidentally killing his father. Six months later, Brent politely turns down Lola Stone's invitation to the school formal in favor of his girlfriend Holly. Lola secretly watches the two having sex in Holly's car. Guilt-ridden over his father's death, Brent has turned to self-harm with a razor blade hidden in his necklace. At home, Brent's mother Carla insists on him taking a taxi rather than riding with an inexperienced Holly. Brent leaves his house and goes to a nearby cliff. He briefly contemplates suicide, but changes his mind. As he listens to music, someone knocks Brent out.
Brent wakes up bound to a chair. His captors are Lola and her father Eric, who have decorated their house in imitation of a formal. The three are sat at a table along with a lobotomized woman they call Bright Eyes. Lola injects Brent's voice box with bleach, destroying his vocal cords so he is unable to speak. She begins to humiliate him, experiencing arousal in the process. Brent frees himself and runs outside, but is re-captured. Once he is tied up again, they pin his feet to the floor with knives. Lola shows Brent a scrapbook with photos of her past victims. Brent recognizes Timmy Valentine, the bloodied man who caused his crash. Timmy turns out to be the brother of Mia Valentine, the prom date of Jamie, Brent's best friend. Lola then brands Brent by carving her initials onto his chest and throwing salt on it. After Eric crowns Lola prom queen, she admits having incestuous feelings for him. The two dance and almost kiss before Brent interrupts them.
Eric opens a trapdoor on the floor, revealing a basement cellar with the previous abductees still alive. Lola drills a hole through Brent's skull and prepares to lobotomize him by pouring boiling water into the hole. Brent manages to free himself again. He attacks Eric with his hidden razor blade and stabs him with one of the knives he pulled out of his feet. He pushes Eric into the cellar, where the starving and deranged (and presumably lobotomised) captives begin to eat his body. Lola pushes Brent into the cellar and throws everything she can get her hands on at him. Brent finds a flashlight and a hammer among the thrown objects and uses them to defend himself against the captives. Lola then smothers Bright Eyes — referring to her as her mother — with a pillow.
When Brent does not show up to the date, a worried Holly informs Mia's father, a police officer. He enters Lola's house, where Lola kills him with a meat cleaver. Lola taunts Brent, saying she will kill Carla as revenge for her father, and kill Holly as revenge for Brent breaking Lola's heart. After she leaves, Brent climbs out of the pit by piling up the corpses. As Lola walks on the road, she sees Holly approaching in her car.

documents.title: Mirrors 2
documents.tagline: Behind the world you know is a darkness you never imagined.
documents.overview: When Max, who is recovering from a traumatic accident, takes a job as a nighttime security guard, he begins to see visions of a young mysterious woman in the store's mirror.
documents.plot:
Mirrors 2 is an American supernatural horror film of 2010 directed by Víctor García and written by Matt Venne, a standalone sequel to Mirrors (2008) with none of the original's cast or crew. Released direct to video by 20th Century Fox, it stars Nick Stahl as Max Matheson, with Emmanuelle Vaugier as Elizabeth Reigns, William Katt as Max's father Jack, Christy Carlson Romano as Jenna McCarty and Lawrence Turner as Keller Landreaux.

Max briefly died in a car crash that killed his fiancée, Kayla. Revived, he remains consumed by guilt, though a drunk driver was to blame. His father Jack is reopening the Mayflower department store in New Orleans and hires Max as a security guard. Max meets the manager Keller, the buyer Jenna and the executive Ryan Parker. Before his first shift he sees a dead woman in a mirror, then Jenna's reflection tearing off its head. That night Jenna, frightened by her reflection, crashes through her glass shower door and is decapitated by a shard. Max realizes that mirrors are showing him deaths before they happen; he tries to warn Ryan after seeing his reflection disemboweled, but Ryan dies the same way. When Max sees his father's face covered in cuts, he races over and saves Jack from his own reflection, then agrees to stay at the store, telling whatever controls the mirrors that he will do as it wishes if it spares his father.

Max returns to the store's main mirror, where his reflection guides him to the ID of Eleanor Reigns, a new employee who vanished two months earlier. He contacts her sister Elizabeth, and they find that the security footage from the night of Eleanor's disappearance was deleted. The former guard, Henry, whose mouth was scarred after his reflection made him eat broken glass, tells them the truth: at the store's groundbreaking party, Jenna drugged Eleanor's drink while Ryan distracted her, and Keller raped her and killed her when she tried to flee, then forced Henry, who saw him bury her in the basement, to erase the footage. Eleanor's spirit, trapped in the mirror world, has been taking revenge and used Max, whose near-death experience let him see her, to reach her sister. In the basement, Keller attacks and nearly strangles Elizabeth, but Max saves her and pushes Keller into the main mirror, where Eleanor drags him in and kills him. Henry confesses to police, but Eleanor finds him in the interrogation room's mirror.

Filmed mainly in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, in late 2009, it earned $4.5 million on home video.

documents.title: The Warrior's Way
documents.tagline: Assassin. Hero. Legend.
documents.overview: A warrior-assassin is forced to hide in a small town in the American Badlands after refusing a mission.
documents.plot:
The Warrior's Way is a 2010 American martial arts film directed by Gareth Evans and starring Kate Bosworth, Tony O'Dell, and Keanu Reeves. The movie follows the story of Luan (Keanu Reeves), a half-human, half-dog hybrid who lives in the late 19th century American West.

The film begins with Luan's childhood, where he is raised by his human mother, Anna (Kate Bosworth), on a ranch in Montana. However, their peaceful life is disrupted when a group of bandits, led by the ruthless and cunning Black Lord (Tony O'Dell), attack the ranch. In the ensuing battle, Luan's mother is killed, and he is forced to flee for his life.

As an adult, Luan becomes a skilled warrior and adopts the alias "The Warrior." He travels the West, taking on various jobs as a bodyguard and mercenary, while also seeking revenge against Black Lord, who killed his mother. Along the way, Luan meets a young woman named Anna (Kate Bosworth), who is revealed to be his long-lost sister.

As their relationship deepens, Luan begins to question his own identity and humanity. He struggles with his canine instincts and the moral implications of his actions as a warrior. Meanwhile, Black Lord's gang continues to terrorize the West, and Luan finds himself drawn into a larger conflict between rival factions vying for control.

The plot thickens when Luan discovers that Anna is being held captive by Black Lord's men. He sets out on a perilous journey to rescue her, facing numerous challenges and adversaries along the way. In a climactic showdown, Luan confronts Black Lord in a fierce battle, using his unique hybrid abilities to gain the upper hand.

In the end, Luan emerges victorious, but not without scars. He finds some measure of peace and redemption, having finally avenged his mother's death and reunited with Anna. The film concludes with Luan riding off into the sunset, ready to face new challenges as a hero and protector of the innocent.

Throughout the movie, Keanu Reeves delivers a strong performance as the titular character, bringing depth and nuance to Luan's complex personality. Kate Bosworth shines in her dual roles, conveying both vulnerability and strength. The film's action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, showcasing the martial arts skills of its cast.

While The Warrior's Way received mixed reviews from critics, it has developed a loyal fan base over the years. Fans praise the movie's unique blend of Western and martial arts genres, as well as its visually stunning landscapes and impressive fight choreography.

documents.title: I Am Number Four
documents.tagline: Three like him have already been killed…he is Number Four.
documents.overview: A teenage fugitive with an incredible secret races to stay one step ahead of the mysterious forces seeking destroy him in this sci-fi action thriller. With three dead and one on the run, the race to find the elusive Number Four begins. Outwardly normal teen John Smith never gets too comfortable in the same identity, and along with his guardian, Henri, he is constantly moving from town to town. With each passing day, John gains a stronger grasp on his extraordinary new powers, and his bond to the beings that share his fantastic fate grows stronger.
documents.plot:
I Am Number Four is a science fiction film directed by D.J. Caruso, released in 2011 by DreamWorks Pictures.

The movie begins with an alien invasion on Earth, where nine extraterrestrial beings known as the Lorien are sent to destroy human colonies. The ninth and final Lorien, John Smith (played by Alex Pettyfer), escapes the destruction of his home planet and is left with a rare genetic marker that makes him immune to the invasion.

John is taken in by a foster family, the Keys (played by Dianna Agron, Jake Abel, and Callum Keith Rennie), who are unaware of John's true identity. As he grows up on Earth, John struggles to control his powers, which include superhuman strength, speed, and agility.

However, an alien hunter named Henry Hartrick (played by Timothy Olyphant) is sent to find the remaining Lorien and eliminate them. Henry believes that John is one of the nine Lorien and will stop at nothing to kill him.

As John navigates his new life on Earth, he meets a girl named Daniel's friend, Claire Bennet (played by Alexandra Daddario), who becomes his love interest. Meanwhile, Henry begins to close in on John, leading to a series of intense confrontations between the two.

Throughout the movie, John struggles with his identity and his connection to his fellow Lorien. He also grapples with the moral implications of his powers and the danger he poses to humanity.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Henry is not what he seems. His true intentions are revealed, and John must use all his skills and resources to protect himself and those he cares about.

The movie culminates in an action-packed showdown between John and Henry, with the fate of humanity hanging in the balance. In the end, John emerges victorious, but not without sacrifices. The film concludes on a hopeful note, as John finds a new sense of belonging among his human friends and begins to forge a new identity for himself.

Overall, I Am Number Four is a thrilling sci-fi adventure that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and self-discovery. With its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and impressive action sequences, the movie has become a cult classic among fans of the genre.

documents.title: Blue Valentine
documents.tagline: A Love Story.
documents.overview: Dean and Cindy live a quiet life in a modest neighborhood. They appear to have the world at their feet at the outset of the relationship. However, his lack of ambition and her retreat into self-absorption cause potentially irreversible cracks in their marriage.
documents.plot: Dean and Cindy live a quiet life in a modest neighborhood. They appear to have the world at their feet at the outset of the relationship. However, his lack of ambition and her retreat into self-absorption cause potentially irreversible cracks in their marriage.

documents.title: Hunt to Kill
documents.tagline: Survival of the baddest
documents.overview: A U.S. Border Patrol agent Jim Rhodes, a tough divorcée mourning the loss of his murdered partner while struggling to raise his rebellious daughter in the mountains of Montana. But when a crew of trigger-happy fugitives takes Rhodes and his daughter hostage, a rugged wilderness will explode in all-terrain vengeance. Is there any wounded animal more dangerous than a lawman left for dead? Daniels portrays one of the villains.
documents.plot:
Hunt to Kill is a 2010 Canadian-American action thriller directed by Keoni Waxman and written by Frank Hannah, released directly to video. Steve Austin stars as U.S. Border Patrol agent Jim Rhodes, with Marie Avgeropoulos as his teenage daughter Kim, Gil Bellows as the ruthless criminal Banks, Gary Daniels as Jensen, Michael Eklund as Geary, Emilie Ullerup as Dominika, Michael Hogan as Lawson, Adrian Holmes as Crab, Donnelly Rhodes as the local sheriff and Eric Roberts as Jim's partner, Lee Davis.

The film opens in Texas, where Jim and Lee investigate an apparently abandoned trailer. Just before they go in, Lee gives Jim a wristwatch woven from climbing rope that can double as emergency gear. Inside they find a methamphetamine lab, and in the ambush that follows Lee is shot dead and the trailer is set ablaze, forcing Jim to escape before it explodes.

Four years later a crew of thieves steals millions of dollars in bearer bonds from a Reno casino, but one of them, Lawson, makes off with the loot. The others, led by the volatile Banks, follow him to the small Montana town of Lowery, where Jim now lives with his rebellious daughter. Called to the sheriff's office after Kim is caught shoplifting, Jim arrives to find Banks beating the sheriff to death. The gang takes Kim hostage and forces Jim to guide them through the mountains after Lawson. Tensions split the group along the way, and Banks has Jensen kill Crab for hurting Kim and Dominika, the woman Banks loves. Once they catch up with Lawson, they kill him and recover the money, then throw Jim off a cliff, expecting Kim to lead them to the Canadian border.

Jim survives and turns the wilderness against his captors, taking out Geary, Jensen and Dominika one by one. Banks flees to an outpost manned by Canadian officers, kills them and escapes on an all-terrain vehicle, leaving Kim behind. Jim sends her for help and pursues Banks to an abandoned mine, where after a brutal fight he pins Banks to a wall with an ATV and finishes him with a flare gun that sets off an explosion. Reconciled at last, father and daughter face a long walk home.

Anchor Bay Entertainment released the film on home video in the United States on 9 November 2010. Reviews were mostly negative: Common Sense Media and Dread Central each rated it two out of five, the latter criticizing its pacing, and one reviewer suggested it would appeal only to devoted fans of its star.

documents.title: Incendies
documents.tagline: The search began at the opening of their mother's will.
documents.overview: A mother's last wishes send twins Jeanne and Simon on a journey to Middle East in search of their tangled roots. Adapted from Wajdi Mouawad's acclaimed play, Incendies tells the powerful and moving tale of two young adults' voyage to the core of deep-rooted hatred, never-ending wars and enduring love.
documents.plot:
Following the death of their mother, Nawal, an Arab immigrant in Canada, Jeanne and her twin brother Simon meet with French Canadian notary Jean Lebel, their mother's employer and family friend. Nawal's will refers to not keeping a promise, denying her a proper gravestone and casket, unless Jeanne and Simon track down their mysterious brother, of whose existence they were previously unaware, and their father, who they believed was dead. Nawal has left two letters; one is to be delivered to Jeanne and Simon's father, and the other is to be delivered to their brother. Jeanne accepts; Simon, on the other hand, seemingly having had a more difficult relationship with Nawal and her unusual personality, is reluctant to join Jeanne on this pursuit.
Nawal came from a Christian family in a Levantine country, and she fell in love with a refugee named Wahab, resulting in her pregnancy. Her family murders her lover and nearly shoots her in an honour killing, but her grandmother spares her, making her promise to leave the village after her baby's birth and start a new life in the city of Daresh. The grandmother tattoos the back of the baby's heel and sends him to an orphanage in Kfar Khout.
While Nawal is at university in Daresh a few years later, civil war and war crimes break out, with Nawal opposing the war on human rights grounds. Her son's orphanage is destroyed by Muslim militants. Nawal leaves Daresh to try to find her son and boards a bus full of Muslim refugees. Christian Nationalists shoot the driver and fire into the bus full of passengers, only missing Nawal and a mother with her daughter. As the Nationalists prepare to set the bus on fire, the survivors try to escape towards the back of the bus. Nawal shows her crucifix and tells the Nationalists that she is Christian. She attempts to save the girl by claiming her as her own, but the girl runs towards the burning bus, calling for her mother, and is shot dead. Nawal finds her way back to town and joins the Muslim fighters. She tutors the son of a nationalist leader, eventually earning enough trust to smuggle in a gun to shoot the leader. She is imprisoned in Kfar Ryat and sings through the screams of other prisoners, earning her the nickname "The Woman Who Sings". To attempt to break her, she is raped by torturer Abou Tarek who leaves her saying, "sing now". She consequently gives birth to the twins.
After traveling to her mother's native country, Jeanne gradually uncovers this past and persuades Simon to join her. With help from Lebel, they learn their brother's name is Nihad of May (the month he was born in) and track down Chamseddine, a local warlord. Simon meets with him and Chamseddine reveals that he attacked the orphanage in Kfar Khout, where he spared the children and converted Nihad into an Islamic child soldier.

documents.title: Barney's Version
documents.tagline: First he got married. Then he got married again. Then he met the love of his life.
documents.overview: The picaresque and touching story of the politically incorrect, fully lived life of the impulsive, irascible and fearlessly blunt Barney Panofsky.
documents.plot:
Barney Panofsky is living with his best friend Boogie in Rome. He marries the mentally disturbed and unfaithful Clara Charnofsky after she tells him she is pregnant with his child. He finds out the child — delivered stillborn — is not his, and he demands they separate. She commits suicide, and a devastated Barney decides to return home to Montreal.
Barney soon meets the woman who becomes his second wife, the daughter of a wealthy Jewish family. At their lavish wedding, Barney meets Miriam Grant and immediately falls in love. He tells her his feelings for her that night, but she rejects him.
Despite his marriage, Barney sends flowers and gifts to Miriam. He later picks up Boogie, who comes to detox for a few days at Barney's lake house. He walks in on Boogie in bed with his wife. Initially overjoyed that he has an excuse to divorce her and pursue Miriam, he later questions Boogie's integrity. The drunk men argue, and Barney shoots two bullets from his gun to dissuade Boogie from snorkeling, one into the air, before he trips and passes out on the dock, and Boogie falls backwards into the lake.
When Barney awakens, Boogie is missing. A detective tries to beat a confession out of him until his father, Izzy, intervenes. Barney continues to believe that Boogie ran away, and holds out hope that he will reappear.
With his divorce final, Barney asks Miriam on a date. He travels to New York City to meet her and finally begin a relationship. They marry and have two children, and Barney gets a job producing a television series. Izzy dies in a brothel, causing Barney to laugh and cry and call his father a "King". Barney and Miriam live happily until, on another vacation to the lake house, Barney meets Blair, who works in radio, Miriam's old line of work. There is an immediate platonic connection between Blair and Miriam, much to Barney's noticeable consternation.
After Barney and Miriam's son, Michael, leaves home, Miriam informs Barney of her intention to return to work. He attempts to dissuade her, but she persists and secures employment, thanks to support from Blair. Miriam begins work at a radio station, but Barney misses her first on-air interview — because he "was drunk and watching the hockey game, like has happened a thousand times before" — and is rude and dismissive to Miriam's colleagues.
Miriam remains steadfastly faithful to him, but eventually, his picaresque behavior results in her taking a weeklong visit to Michael's place in New York. While she is absent, Barney gets drunk at a bar and goes to bed with a former actress on his show. He tells Miriam about his infidelity, and they divorce. She soon marries Blair.
Barney, who has been displaying small signs of a deteriorating memory (forgetting where he left his car on two occasions), begins to show signs of an acute but unspecified memory loss.

documents.title: Tucker and Dale vs. Evil
documents.tagline: Evil just messed with the wrong hillbillies.
documents.overview: Two hillbillies are suspected of being killers by a group of paranoid college kids camping near the duo's West Virginian cabin. As the body count climbs, so does the fear and confusion as the college kids try to seek revenge against the pair.
documents.plot: Two hillbillies are suspected of being killers by a group of paranoid college kids camping near the duo's West Virginian cabin. As the body count climbs, so does the fear and confusion as the college kids try to seek revenge against the pair.

documents.title: The Swarm
documents.tagline: Monsters by the millions - and they're all for real!
documents.overview: Scientist Dr. Bradford Crane and army general Thalius Slater join forces to fight an almost invisible enemy threatening America; killer bees that have deadly venom and attack without reason. Disaster movie-master Irwin Allen's film contains spectacular special effects, including a train crash caused by the eponymous swarm.
documents.plot:
The Swarm is a 1978 American natural horror film directed and produced by Irwin Allen and based on Arthur Herzog's 1974 novel of the same name. Michael Caine leads an all-star ensemble cast that includes Katharine Ross, Richard Widmark, Richard Chamberlain, Olivia de Havilland, Ben Johnson, Lee Grant, José Ferrer, Patty Duke, Slim Pickens, Bradford Dillman, Henry Fonda, Cameron Mitchell and Fred MacMurray in his final film role. The story follows a scientist and a military task force trying to stop a vast swarm of African killer bees from overrunning Texas.

The film begins when contact is lost with a top-secret Air Force missile base in south Texas. A unit sent to investigate finds most of the personnel dead and discovers an unauthorized civilian inside, the entomologist Dr. Bradford Crane, who explains that he has been tracking a swarm of killer bees responsible for the attack. When the bees destroy two helicopters sent to search the area, the skeptical General Slater is forced to accept Crane's warning, and base doctor Helena Anderson supports him. Meanwhile the swarm kills a family in the countryside, and their young son, stung and hallucinating giant bees, crashes his parents' car into the small town of Marysville as residents prepare for their annual flower festival.

Crane, working with the immunologist Dr. Walter Krim and Dr. Hubbard, races to develop an antidote and a way to destroy the bees, while Slater favors drastic military measures such as poisons and fire. The swarm sweeps through Marysville, wrecks a train carrying fleeing residents and moves toward Houston, threatening millions. The scientists suffer setbacks and deaths in their own ranks, and the tension between Crane's research and the army's preference for force grows as the bees close in on the city.

Released by Warner Bros., The Swarm was a box-office bomb and received overwhelmingly negative reviews, with critics mocking its dialogue, its length and the spectacle of its veteran stars battling bees. It has since become known as one of the most notorious disaster films of its era and a camp favorite. Despite its reception, costume designer Paul Zastupnevich received an Academy Award nomination for Best Costume Design.

documents.title: Daisies
documents.tagline: Ups-a daisy… downs-a-daisy… turned-ons-a-daisy.
documents.overview: Two teenage girls embark on a series of destructive pranks in which they consume and destroy the world around them.
documents.plot:
Daisies is a 1966 Czech New Wave film directed by Věra Chytilová. The movie follows the story of two young women, Marie and Libuše, who embark on a series of misadventures and explore themes of female friendship, rebellion, and nonconformity.

At its core, Daisies is a film about the liberation of two young women from the societal constraints that bind them. The movie presents a world where traditional norms and expectations are subverted, and the characters take matters into their own hands, embracing a carefree and hedonistic lifestyle. This theme is closely tied to the concept of "daisies," which symbolize innocence and purity, but also serve as a metaphor for the destruction of these qualities in the face of societal pressure.

The film also explores the idea of female empowerment and the blurring of boundaries between reality and fantasy. The characters' actions become increasingly surreal and dreamlike, reflecting their desire to break free from the constraints of everyday life. This theme is closely tied to the concept of "daisies" as a symbol of freedom and rebellion.

Furthermore, Daisies can be seen as a commentary on the societal norms and expectations placed on women during the 1960s. The film presents a world where traditional feminine roles are being challenged, and the characters are taking control of their own lives. This theme is closely tied to the idea of female liberation and the rejection of patriarchal norms.

Overall, Daisies is a film that celebrates the freedom and spontaneity of young women, while also critiquing the societal constraints that bind them. The movie's use of surrealism and fantasy serves as a metaphor for the characters' desire to break free from the norms of everyday life and create their own reality.

documents.title: Evil - In the Time of Heroes
documents.original_title: Το Κακό: Στην Εποχή των Ηρώων
documents.overview: The story begins at the end of the first Kako movie. The survivors meet up with a group of other barricaded survivors and must take care of the zombies as well as other random Greeks that have taken advantage of the chaos, while shooting random moving targets (zombie or not). Throughout we take small flashback visits into ancient Greece where the zombie apocalypse has also happened and we learn how they faced them.
documents.plot:
Evil: In the Time of Heroes (Greek: Το Κακό: Στην Εποχή των Ηρώων) is a 2009 Greek zombie horror comedy directed by Yorgos Noussias and the sequel to his 2005 film Evil, often described as the first Greek zombie film. Billy Zane appears as a mysterious figure known as the Prophet, with Dinos Avgoustidis, George Hraniotis, Orfeas Avgoustidis and Apostolis Totsikas.

The story begins shortly after the events of the first film, as a zombie outbreak spreads through Athens. An ancient evil power has transformed ordinary people into bloodthirsty undead, and the city descends into chaos. A small group of survivors, including characters from the first film, tries to escape the devastated capital, while armed gangs and marauders exploit the collapse of order and the authorities prepare drastic measures to contain the epidemic.

The film reveals that the struggle between humans and the undead is far older than the modern outbreak. Flashbacks to ancient Greece show a warrior who confronted the same evil in the distant past, linking the present-day survivors to an age of heroes, and suggest that the war between the living and the dead has recurred across millennia. The enigmatic Prophet, who appears to understand the history of the curse, searches for a chosen hero capable of ending it once and for all, as foreign powers threaten to bomb the country to stop the infection. As the survivors fight their way through hordes of zombies in increasingly outrageous battles, the stories of past and present converge, and they must discover whether one of them is destined to defeat the ancient evil.

The film combines gory splatter effects, slapstick humor and references to Greek history and mythology. Reviewers who saw it at genre festivals praised its energy, inventive gore and sense of fun, but criticized its incoherent plot, thin characterization and confusing mythology. Zane's casting gave the low-budget Greek production a measure of international recognition, and the film screened at several European genre festivals, including Grimm Up North in Britain.

documents.title: Pokémon: Giratina and the Sky Warrior
documents.original_title: 劇場版ポケットモンスター ダイヤモンド&パール ギラティナと氷空（そら）の花束 シェイミ
documents.tagline: In a Reverse World, a Legendary battle rages on...
documents.overview: When Giratina is discovered to be able to create parallel dimensions, it's up to Ash and his friends to stop a mysterious stranger from using its powers for evil.
documents.plot:
Pokémon: Giratina and the Sky Warrior is a 2008 Japanese animated adventure film produced by OLM and distributed by Toho. Kunihiko Yuyama directed from a screenplay by Hideki Sonoda. It is the eleventh Pokémon film, the second of the Diamond and Pearl era, and a direct sequel to Pokémon: The Rise of Darkrai (2007).

Years earlier, the researcher Newton Graceland designed a machine that could take the powers of Giratina, the Legendary Pokémon ruling the Reverse World, a mirror dimension of the real world, to cross between worlds. He abandoned the project when he learned it would kill Giratina, but his assistant Zero remembered the plans. After the battle of Dialga and Palkia polluted the Reverse World, an angry Giratina drags Dialga into it. The flower-bearing Pokémon Shaymin, caught on Dialga's back, escapes to the real world, and Dialga traps Giratina in a time loop that keeps it from following.

Shaymin meets the trainers Ash Ketchum, Dawn and Brock, who agree to take it to a Flower Garden in the mountains where its kind gather to migrate. Giratina, hoping to use Shaymin's power to break free, repeatedly pulls the group into the Reverse World, where Newton helps them, while Zero chases them. Touching a Gracidea flower turns Shaymin into its flying Sky Forme. Zero eventually captures Shaymin, forces it to release Giratina into the real world, and then uses Newton's device to drain Giratina's powers so he can rule the Reverse World. Newton shuts the machine down and Shaymin heals the exhausted Giratina. Zero's damage to the Reverse World sends a glacier sliding toward the Flower Garden until Regigigas and a herd of Mamoswine slow it. Shaymin drags Zero back to the real world, where his ship crashes and freezes, wiping his stolen data. Giratina repairs the damage and leaves to find Dialga, and the Shaymin perform their flower bearing before migrating.

In the Japanese version Rica Matsumoto voices Ash and Megumi Toyoguchi voices Dawn, with Shidō Nakamura as Zero and Kōichi Yamadera as Newton. Released in Japan on July 19, 2008, the film opened in second place behind Ponyo, drawing about 982,000 viewers and more than ¥1 billion on its first weekend, and its total ended about 10% below that of the previous film. Reviews were generally positive, and Kidzworld called it worth watching for fans and non-fans of Pokémon alike. A sequel, Arceus and the Jewel of Life, followed in 2009.

documents.title: Scooby-Doo! Curse of the Lake Monster
documents.original_title: Scooby-Doo! Curse of the Lake Monster
documents.tagline: Ruh-Roh! They're in too deep and way over their heads!
documents.overview: Scooby-Doo and the gang are on the case when a mysterious lake monster starts scaring the guests at a summer resort in Erie Point, where Fred, Daphne, Velma and Shaggy have taken on seasonal jobs to pay for a barn they accidentally burned down. But in addition to sneaking suspicions, there's some romance in the air.
documents.plot:
Scooby-Doo! Curse of the Lake Monster is an American made-for-television comedy horror mystery film of 2010 directed by Brian Levant for Cartoon Network, a sequel to Scooby-Doo! The Mystery Begins (2009). Robbie Amell (Fred), Hayley Kiyoko (Velma), Kate Melton (Daphne), Nick Palatas (Shaggy) and Frank Welker, the voice of Scooby-Doo, return, joined by Ted McGinley as Thorny Blake, Richard Moll as the lighthouse keeper Elmer Uggins, Marion Ross as Hilda Trowburg and Beverly Sanders as the witch Wanda Grubwort.

At the start of summer the friends go to work at the country club run by Daphne's uncle Thornton "Thorny" Blake V in Erie Point, to pay off damages from an earlier case. When a giant frog monster attacks the club's opening party, they question Uggins, the only person who has photographed it. He tells them a legend: when settlers first arrived, a witch named Wanda Grubwort ordered them to leave, and when they refused she used her moonstone-powered staff to turn a frog into a monster that attacked them, before she was burned at the stake. Velma finds security footage of the creature meeting a hooded figure on the beach, but spills green tea on the computer and destroys it.

Fred and Daphne are quarrelling, and Shaggy's crush on Velma is driving a wedge between him and Scooby. Velma is found unconscious on the beach with warts on her hand, which she shrugs off, and when Shaggy takes her on a date she panics at the sight of a match. Checking out a boat, Fred and Daphne are locked by the monster in a flooding room but escape. At the home of Wanda's descendant Hilda Trowburg they spot the hooded figure and discover it is Velma, who denies being herself and knocks them out. Trowburg explains that Wanda's spirit has possessed Velma, and the friends realize their squabbling made them miss the signs: the warts, the fear of fire, the fascination with moonstones and the spilled tea. In the underwater caves, Velma turns three frogs into monsters, but Shaggy reaches her by singing her favorite song, and she breaks free. When Wanda tries to recover her staff, Scooby smashes it, destroying the witch and turning the monsters back into frogs. Shaggy and Velma kiss but agree they are better as friends, and Shaggy makes up with Scooby. Thorny thanks them for saving his club and offers them a lawyer, and Daphne names the group Mystery Inc.

The film was shot in Santa Clarita and at Sherwood Country Club in Thousand Oaks, California, and premiered in October 2010.

documents.title: Poetry
documents.overview: Grandmother Mi Ja works part-time as a caretaker, and struggles to raise a teen grandson by herself. Despite her tough situation, she speaks softly, dresses fashionably, and approaches the world with child-like curiosity. Enrolling in a poetry class, she endeavors to capture life in verse form, but her simple dream of completing a poem is stalled by the early signs of Alzheimer's disease and the heavy financial and emotional burden of her grandson's shocking wrongdoing.
documents.plot:
Poetry (Si) is a South Korean drama of 2010 written and directed by Lee Chang-dong. Yoon Jeong-hee, in her first film role since 1994 and her last before her death in 2023, plays Yang Mi-ja, a woman in her sixties who takes up poetry while facing the onset of Alzheimer's disease and the crime of her grandson. Lee David plays the grandson, Jong-wook, with Kim Hee-ra as Mr. Kang.

Mi-ja, 66, works part-time caring for Mr. Kang, an elderly stroke patient, and at home looks after her surly 16-year-old grandson, whose divorced mother lives in Busan. Forgetting everyday words, she is told to get checked, and she signs up for a poetry class at a community center, where each student must write a single poem by the end of the month. Following her teacher's advice, she starts noting down what she observes, especially flowers.

The father of Jong-wook's friend Ki-beom summons her to a meeting with the other boys' fathers. She learns that their sons repeatedly raped a schoolgirl, Agnes, over six months, until the girl threw herself from a bridge and drowned. To protect the boys and the school, the fathers plan to buy off the girl's mother, a poor widowed farmer, with 30 million won, and Mi-ja is expected to pay a share of 5 million she does not have. She tells no one, not even her daughter, and keeps silent when she is diagnosed with early-stage Alzheimer's. Jong-wook ignores her attempts to confront him.

At a weekly poetry reading she meets Detective Park, a crude but reportedly decent policeman. After Mr. Kang makes a desperate sexual advance, Mi-ja quits, but after visiting the bridge where Agnes died she returns to him, soaked by rain, and has sex with him. When she reveals too much to a journalist, the fathers send her to the countryside to win over Agnes's mother; meeting the woman in her field, Mi-ja makes small talk and never raises the money, yet the mother agrees to settle. Mi-ja obtains her share from Mr. Kang, who assumes it is blackmail. Then she calls her daughter home, makes Jong-wook wash and trim his nails, and quietly lets Detective Park take him away. Later her teacher finds flowers and her poem, "Agnes's Song", but Mi-ja has vanished; as he reads it aloud, her voice gives way to Agnes's, leaving her fate unresolved.

Inspired partly by a real case, the film premiered in competition at Cannes in 2010 and won Best Screenplay. Yoon received several Best Actress awards, and critics acclaimed the film.

documents.title: Elite Squad: The Enemy Within
documents.overview: After a bloody invasion of the BOPE in the High-Security Penitentiary Bangu 1 in Rio de Janeiro to control a rebellion of interns, the Lieutenant-Colonel Roberto Nascimento and the second in command Captain André Matias are accused by the Human Right Aids member Diogo Fraga of execution of prisoners. Matias is transferred to the corrupted Military Police and Nascimento is exonerated from the BOPE by the Governor.
documents.plot:
Elite Squad: The Enemy Within (Portuguese: Tropa de Elite 2: O Inimigo Agora É Outro) is a 2010 Brazilian action thriller directed and co-produced by José Padilha, who co-wrote it with Bráulio Mantovani and Rodrigo Pimentel. A sequel to Elite Squad (2007), it continues the semi-fictional story of BOPE, the special operations battalion of the Rio de Janeiro Military Police, now focusing on the links between police and politics. Wagner Moura reprises his role as Nascimento, with Irandhir Santos, André Ramiro and Maria Ribeiro. It was released in Brazil on October 8, 2010.

Thirteen years after the first film, Lieutenant Colonel Roberto Nascimento is ambushed as he leaves a hospital, and as his car is riddled with bullets he narrates the events that led there. Four years earlier, he led BOPE in suppressing a riot at the Bangu prison complex, where the human rights activist Diogo Fraga, now married to Nascimento's ex-wife Rosane, was negotiating with the inmates. The operation ends in a bloodbath, and although Nascimento is officially removed from command, public support for his hard line leads the state government to promote him to undersecretary of intelligence for public security.

With increased resources, Nascimento expands BOPE and wages a relentless war on drug trafficking in the favelas. But as the dealers are driven out, a new enemy fills the vacuum: corrupt police officers organized into militias, which seize control of the communities and extort residents for protection, utilities and votes. Nascimento gradually realizes that his campaign has served the interests of these militias and of the politicians who depend on them for electoral support, including members of the state government and a television host turned legislator. As his former protégé Matias is killed and Fraga's investigations put him in danger, his relationship with his son also suffers. Turning against the system he once served, Nascimento joins forces with Fraga and testifies before a parliamentary inquiry, exposing a web of corruption that reaches all the way to the national capital.

The film was a critical and commercial triumph, becoming the most-watched and highest-grossing film ever released in Brazil at the time, surpassing Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands and Avatar. Metacritic gave it 71 out of 100. It was selected as Brazil's submission for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.

documents.title: Independence Day: Resurgence
documents.tagline: We had twenty years to prepare. So did they.
documents.overview: We always knew they were coming back. Using recovered alien technology, the nations of Earth have collaborated on an immense defense program to protect the planet. But nothing can prepare us for the aliens’ advanced and unprecedented force. Only the ingenuity of a few brave men and women can bring our world back from the brink of extinction.
documents.plot:
Independence Day: Resurgence is a 2016 American science fiction disaster film directed by Colin Trevorrow and produced by 20th Century Fox. The movie serves as a sequel to the 1996 film Independence Day, which was also produced by 20th Century Fox.

The story takes place 22 years after the events of the first film. Will Salas (Owen Wilson), a former thief who survived the alien invasion in 1996, has become a successful businessman and philanthropist. He is married to his wife, Patience (Linda Hamilton), and they have two children together.

The movie begins with an alien spaceship reappearing in Earth's orbit, signaling that the aliens are returning to wreak havoc on humanity once again. The United Nations forms a task force to deal with the new threat, led by President Thomas Whitmore's (Bill Pullman) successor, President Thomas Cale (Liam Hemsworth).

The story follows Jake Morrison (Jeffrey Wright), a former Air Force pilot who lost his family in the first alien invasion. He joins the task force and becomes the leader of the team that will stop the aliens' return.

As the aliens begin to attack major cities around the world, the human resistance is formed, led by Jake and his team. They develop a new technology called "Project Atlas," which uses advanced drones and AI to fight back against the aliens.

The movie's plot thickens as it becomes clear that the aliens are not just mindless monsters but have a complex social hierarchy with different castes. The humans also discover that the aliens' leader, President Thomas Cale, is actually an alien himself who was sent to Earth to prepare for the invasion.

As the battle between humans and aliens intensifies, Jake's team faces numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, malfunctioning technology, and internal conflicts within the resistance. Meanwhile, Will Salas becomes a key player in the human resistance, using his skills as a thief to infiltrate alien ships and gather crucial information.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between humans and aliens on multiple fronts. The humans use their advanced technology to launch a counterattack against the aliens, while Jake's team fights to save the world from destruction.

In the end, the humans emerge victorious, but not without great losses. The movie concludes with Will Salas standing alone, reflecting on the sacrifices he made to help humanity survive the alien invasion.

Overall, Independence Day: Resurgence received mixed reviews from critics and audiences alike, with some praising its action sequences and visual effects while others criticized its convoluted plot and lack of character development. Despite this, the movie remains a thrilling and entertaining ride that explores themes of sacrifice, loyalty, and humanity in the face of overwhelming odds.

documents.title: A Good Day to Die Hard
documents.original_title: A Good Day to Die Hard
documents.tagline: Yippee Ki-Yay Mother Russia
documents.overview: Iconoclastic, take-no-prisoners cop John McClane, finds himself for the first time on foreign soil after traveling to Moscow to help his wayward son Jack - unaware that Jack is really a highly-trained CIA operative out to stop a nuclear weapons heist. With the Russian underworld in pursuit, and battling a countdown to war, the two McClanes discover that their opposing methods make them unstoppable heroes.
documents.plot:
In Moscow, Viktor Chagarin, a high-ranking, corrupt Russian official, plans to incriminate former billionaire and government whistleblower Yuri Komarov in a rigged trial unless he hands over a secret file believed to contain evidence incriminating Chagarin. Separately, Jack McClane, arrested after an assassination attempt, negotiates for a shorter sentence by offering to testify against Komarov.
Jack's father, NYPD Police Detective John McClane, who has not been in touch with his son for several years, learns he is in trouble and flies to Russia. As John approaches the courthouse where Komarov is on trial, an explosion orchestrated by Chagarin's henchman Alik occurs in the courthouse, and Jack breaks free with Komarov. John confronts Jack, but their dispute is cut short as Alik and his men chase them in an MRAP through Moscow.
Hiding in a safe house, John finds out that Jack is a CIA operative and has been on an undercover operation for the past three years. Jack's partner, Mike Collins, demands the file's location from Komarov so the CIA can bring Chagarin down. He agrees on the condition that he and his daughter are given safe passage out of Russia. The group are ambushed by Chagarin's men; Collins is shot and killed while the McClanes and Komarov escape, making their way to a hotel to get the safe deposit box key containing the file. There they meet up with Komarov's daughter, Irina, as planned. Alik and his men burst in and tie up John and Jack, taking Komarov hostage; Irina confesses to informing on them. Jack breaks free of his ties and he and John kill most of the guards present. Alik and Irina, with Komarov still their hostage, return in a Mil Mi-24 attack helicopter and try to kill them, but they escape.
That night, Jack and John steal a car full of weapons, driving to Pripyat, Ukraine, where the safe deposit box with the file is located, only to find that Komarov, Irina, and Alik are already there. The safe deposit box with the supposed file is a secret passage to a Chernobyl-era vault containing €1 billion worth of weapons-grade uranium. It turns out that there is no secret file and Komorov and Irina have concocted a scheme to steal the uranium deposit to make big money in the black market, luring the attention of the CIA to safely conduct the operation under their protection. Komarov kills Alik and calls Chagarin to gloat as the latter is killed by one of Komarov's men while he is in a sauna.
As John and Jack enter the vault, Komarov pretends that he is glad that they are coming to save him but Jack realizes the uranium in the vault and figures out the whole scheme. As he and John prepare to apprehend Komarov, Irina and some henchmen come to her father's aid. As they prepare to leave, Jack follows Komarov, while John goes after Irina, who is escaping in a Mil Mi-26 helicopter; he sneaks into the rear compartment.

documents.title: xXx: Return of Xander Cage
documents.tagline: There are no more patriots, just rebels and tyrants.
