documents.title: In Time
documents.tagline: Time Is Power
documents.overview: In the not-too-distant future the aging gene has been switched off. To avoid overpopulation, time has become the currency and the way people pay for luxuries and necessities. The rich can live forever, while the rest try to negotiate for their immortality. A poor young man who comes into a fortune of time, though too late to help his mother from dying. He ends up on the run from a corrupt police force known as 'time keepers'.
documents.plot:
In Time is a 2011 science fiction action film directed by Andrew Niccol and written by Niccol. The movie takes place in a dystopian future where time has become the ultimate currency.

The story follows Will Salas (played by Justin Timberlake), a poor man living on the outskirts of society, who lives in a world where people trade years of their lives for material possessions. The rich live forever, while the poor are left with mere minutes to live. Will's life changes when he meets Sylvia Weis (played by Amanda Seyfried), a wealthy woman who gives him 100 hours of her time.

With this newfound wealth, Will sets out on a journey to change his fate and that of those around him. He teams up with Henry Hamilton (played by Matt Bomer), a wealthy man who is struggling with the consequences of his own immortality. Together, they embark on a mission to redistribute time among the poor, challenging the existing social hierarchy.

As Will and Henry navigate this new world, they attract the attention of the authorities, led by Raymond Leon (played by Cillian Murphy). Leon is determined to capture Will and maintain the status quo, which has kept him in power for years. The two men engage in a cat-and-mouse game, with Will using his newfound wealth to evade capture.

Throughout the movie, Will's character undergoes significant development as he grapples with the consequences of his actions. He begins to question the morality of the system and the true cost of immortality. As he gets closer to his goal, he must confront the harsh realities of a world where time is currency, and the rich will stop at nothing to maintain their power.

The movie's climax features an intense showdown between Will and Leon, with the fate of humanity hanging in the balance. In the end, Will emerges victorious, but not without scars. He has changed the course of history, but at what cost? The movie ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that a new era of equality and justice may be possible.

Overall, In Time is a thought-provoking commentary on class inequality and the consequences of unchecked power. With its unique premise and engaging characters, it offers a thrilling ride that will keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

documents.title: Smile
documents.tagline: Point. Shoot. Die.
documents.overview: A carefree summer vacation turns into an inescapable terror trap for a group of young students who buy a vintage instant camera from a mysterious local shop owner...
documents.plot:
Smile is a 2009 English-language Italian supernatural horror film written and directed by Francesco Gasperoni in his feature debut. Set and shot in Morocco, it follows a group of young friends on holiday who are picked off one by one after being photographed with a cursed instant camera. The cast includes Harriet MacMasters-Green, Antonio Cupo, Giorgia Massetti, Manuela Zanier, Mourad Zaoui, Robert Capelli Jr. and Tara Haggiag, with Armand Assante as the mysterious Tollinger. It was produced by Luce Cinecittà, Morocco Movie Group and Moviemaker with support from the Italian Ministry of Cultural Heritage and Activities.

The film opens with Tollinger at work as a forensic photographer, moving from one violent crime scene to the next. A group of university students then sets off by battered van for a relaxing, adventurous holiday in the mountains of Morocco, where they want to camp and have heard legends of black demons with flaming hands. Their leader, Clarissa, is an aspiring photojournalist determined to record every moment, but after her own camera is stolen and the van suffers a flat tyre following a near accident, she visits an antique shop in a nearby village. There the sinister owner, Tollinger, sells her a vintage Polaroid camera for a fraction of its value, throws in a roll of film and urges her to take lots of pictures of her friends. As the trip continues, a local hunter warns them not to use the camera bought in the bazaar, and gruesome deaths begin among the group. They realize that the camera has the power to kill anyone it photographs and that the deaths match the images, and the survivors, among them Tommy, who panics as the killings mount, race to decipher the supernatural clues in the photographs before they become the next victims.

Smile opened in about 150 Italian cinemas on August 28, 2009, with releases in France and elsewhere in Europe that autumn and a direct-to-DVD release planned for the United States. Filming took place over five weeks with a half-Italian, half-Moroccan crew assisted by the Casablanca film school. Italian critics were largely negative: Valerio Ceddia of Quinlan.it found it predictable and unintentionally ridiculous, though he praised the unusual misty mountain locations. HorrorNews.net was kinder, calling it a straightforward possessed-object horror film in the vein of Final Destination, with brisk pacing and decent effects. A sequel was later planned.

documents.title: I Saw the Devil
documents.tagline: Abandon all compassion.
documents.overview: Kyung-Chul is a dangerous psychopath who kills for pleasure. Soo-Hyun, a top-secret agent, decides to track down the murderer himself. He promises himself that he will do everything in his power to take vengeance against the killer, even if it means that he must become a monster himself.
documents.plot:
Jang Kyung-chul, a school bus driver, encounters a woman named Jang Joo-yun and offers to fix her flat tire. After beating her unconscious and bringing her to his house, Kyung-chul methodically dismembers her, unaware of her ring falling into a floor drain. Kyung-chul scatters the body parts into a local river, where it is discovered, prompting the police to conduct a search led by Squad Chief Jang, Joo-yun's father, and Squad Chief Oh. Joo-yun's fiancé, Kim Soo-hyun, an NIS agent, vows to exact revenge on the perpetrator.
After learning of the four suspects from Jang, Soo-hyun privately interrogates two of them. The violent encounter (part torture) of the first two suspects absolves them as his wife's killer. But they are not without fault, one suspect turns himself in for killing multiple schoolgirls in fear of Soo-hyun's return and seeks help from the police in the hospital. Upon searching the home of Kyung-chul (the third suspect), Soo-hyun finds Joo-yun's ring which confirms Jang Kyung-chul to be his fiancée's killer.
A short time later, Kyung-chul brings a schoolgirl home and begins to rape her. Soo-hyun interrupts and knocks him unconscious. Instead of killing Kyung-chul, Soo-hyun forces him to swallow a GPS tracking transmitter, allowing him to track Kyung-chul's movements and listen to his conversations while also fracturing his left arm.
Waking up, Kyung-chul is offered a ride by a taxi, which already carries a passenger. The taxi has a license with a profile picture of the taxi's owner, which Kyung-chul notices is not the one driving this taxi. He has stepped into a hijacked vehicle, and the occupants are acting strangely. Kyung-chul attacks them seconds before they attack and murders them. Kyung-chul checks the trunk of the taxi and finds a murder victim (presumably the taxi driver) and a bag of fresh clothes. He leaves their bodies on the side of the road, and cleans up in a nearby river.
Kyung-chul drives to a clinic to have his wounds looked at. After being treated, Kyung-chul proceeds to rape a nurse. Soo-hyun arrives, subdues him, and slashes his achilles tendon before leaving. At this point, Soo-hyun's intention becomes clear: he wants to torture Kyung-chul as long as possible. Kyung-chul visits the home of his friend Tae-joo, a cannibalistic murderer and meets his girlfriend Se-jung who seems nonchalant about the meeting.
After learning of the situation, Tae-joo remarks that his tormentor must be related to one of his victims. Kyung-chul deduces Soo-hyun's identity after recalling that his wedding ring matched that of Joo-yun. Soo-hyun arrives and incapacitates Kyung-chul, Tae-joo, and his girlfriend Se-jung. The next day, Tae-joo and Se-jung, still unconscious, are arrested by the police and sent to the hospital. Soo-hyun and Kyung-chul receive treatment for their wounds, aided by Soo-hyun's trusted subordinate, who helps them evade the cops.

documents.title: The Nutcracker: The Untold Story
documents.tagline: Experience the Holiday Classic as You've Never Seen it Before
documents.overview: Set in 1920s Vienna, this is the tale of a little girl, whose godfather gives her a special doll one Christmas Eve.
documents.plot:
The Nutcracker in 3D, also released as The Nutcracker: The Untold Story, is a 2010 Christmas musical fantasy film adapted from Tchaikovsky's 1892 ballet The Nutcracker. Andrei Konchalovsky directed, co-wrote and produced the film, a co-production of the United Kingdom, Russia and Hungary that sets the story in 1920s Vienna and sets lyrics to Tchaikovsky's music. First screened at the European Film Market in February 2009, it opened in the United States and Canada on November 24, 2010.

Young Mary lives with her parents, Joseph and Louise, and little brother, Max. On Christmas Eve, while her parents are at a party, her Uncle Albert gives the children a dollhouse and a nutcracker named NC, who comes to life that night and grows to human size. In the sitting room, now enormous, Mary meets NC's toy friends: Gielgud, a courtly chimpanzee; Tinker, a fussy opera-singing clown; and Sticks, a drummer boy. Atop the Christmas tree the Snow Fairy, who resembles Mary's mother, reveals that NC is a prince whose kingdom was seized by the Rat King and his mother, the Rat Queen, who cursed him. Because Mary believes in him, NC briefly becomes a boy again, and she sees his city, where the light-fearing Rat King forces people to burn children's toys in factories so that the smoke blots out the sun.

The rats' robotic dogs topple the tree, and Mary wakes in bed to parents who dismiss her story. The next night NC is captured along with Tinker and Sticks, and Max is lured to the rat city and imprisoned. With Gielgud, Mary slips through a portal in the attic and, disguised as a rat, finds the factory where NC lies lifeless. Her declaration of love breaks the curse for good, the workers rise up, and after a fight aboard the rats' helicopter, the King and Queen revert to rats and flee into the sewers. NC is crowned and promises Mary they will meet again. Back home, her parents apologize and vow to spend more time with her, and Uncle Albert introduces his new neighbor, a boy who looks like the prince and asks to be called NC.

Elle Fanning plays Mary, with Nathan Lane as Uncle Albert, John Turturro as the Rat King, Frances de la Tour as the Rat Queen, Richard E. Grant as Joseph and Yulia Vysotskaya as Louise and the Snow Fairy; Charlie Rowe and Shirley Henderson share the role of the Nutcracker. It was roundly panned, with 0% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, criticism of its Nazi-like rats and toy-burning imagery, and earnings of about $20 million against a $90 million budget.

documents.overview: Blending lively music and brilliant animation, this sequel to the original 'Fantasia' restores 'The Sorcerer's Apprentice' and adds seven new shorts.

documents.title: The Roommate
documents.tagline: 2,000 colleges. 8 million roommates. Which one will you get?
documents.overview: When Sara, a young design student from Iowa, arrives for college in Los Angeles, she is eager to fit in and get to know the big city. Her wealthy roommate, Rebecca, is more than eager to take Sara under her wing and show her the ropes. The two become close, but when Sara begins to branch out and make more friends on campus, Rebecca becomes resentful. Alarmed, Sara moves in with her new boyfriend, causing Rebecca's behavior to take a violent turn.
documents.plot:
Sara Matthews is starting her freshman year of college in Los Angeles. She meets party girl Tracy, frat boy Stephen—her love interest—and Rebecca, her wealthy but shy college roommate who bears an uncanny resemblance to her. The girls begin to bond and Rebecca learns that Sara had an older sister, Emily, who died when Sara was nine, and an ex-boyfriend, Jason, who keeps calling her in attempts to reconcile.
Over time, Rebecca's obsession with Sara grows, which causes her to drive away anyone who could come between them. Claiming that she is a bad influence, Rebecca attacks Tracy in the shower, pins her down, rips out her belly button ring, and threatens to kill her unless she stays away from Sara. Tracy moves to another dorm, fearful of Rebecca. An old friend of Sara's named Irene invites Sara to move in with her when Sara's cat Cuddles is discovered by an RA. Rebecca kills Cuddles, lying to Sara that the cat ran away, inflicts injuries upon herself, and says she was assaulted by a thug.
Feeling sympathetic, Sara decides to spend Thanksgiving with Rebecca. When Sara's fashion design professor, Roberts, kisses her, Rebecca plans to get the professor out of the picture by seducing him while recording their dialogue on a tape recorder to make it sound like he was trying to rape her. During her Thanksgiving stay, Sara overhears a conversation between Rebecca and her father, hinting Rebecca has had trouble making friends in the past. After Rebecca's mother mentions that Rebecca is supposed to be taking medication, Sara and Stephen find a bottle of unused Zyprexa pills, used to treat schizophrenia or bipolar disorder.
Sara decides to move in with Irene; however, that evening at a club, Rebecca seduces Irene and they go back to Irene's place. The following morning, Sara goes to Irene's apartment, but she is not there. Meanwhile, Rebecca gets Sara's sister's name tattooed in the same place on her breast as Sara. Alarmed, Sara finally realizes Rebecca is obsessed with her and removes her belongings from the dorm. Jason arrives at Sara's dorm and slips a note under her door, saying that he wants to see her. Rebecca intercepts it, and disguises herself as Sara. She then goes to Jason's hotel room and stabs him to death.
Sara receives a text message from Irene saying she needs to meet with her right away, and she calls Stephen so he can meet her there. She arrives and finds a gagged Irene handcuffed to the bed. Rebecca reveals herself and points a gun at Sara, proclaiming her love and loyalty, before tearfully revealing she was responsible for what happened to Tracy, Cuddles, Professor Roberts, Irene, and Jason, and that she did it all to win Sara's friendship.
Rebecca moves to smother Irene, and Sara attempts to stop her. Sara tries to call for help, but the phone is dead. Bound and helpless, Irene pleads for Sara to save herself. Sara tries to get out the window to get help.

documents.title: A Turtle's Tale: Sammy's Adventures
documents.tagline: Hatch Me If You Can
documents.overview: A sea turtle who was hatched in 1959 spends the next 50 years traveling the world while it is being changed by global warming. Born on a Baja, California beach in 1959, new hatchling Sammy must do what his fellow newborn sea turtles are doing: race across the beach to the ocean before they are captured by a seagull or crab. Thus begins Sammy's incredible fifty-year ocean journey. Along the way he meets his best friend, a fellow turtle named Ray, and overcomes obstacles both natural and man-made while trying to fulfill his dream of travelling around the world. Throughout his voyage, Sammy never forgets about Shelly - the turtle he saved on his first day and loves passionately from afar.
documents.plot: Born on a Baja, California beach in 1959, new hatchling Sammy races across the beach to the ocean while avoiding being caught by seagulls and crabs. Thus begins Sammy's incredible fifty-year ocean journey where he overcomes obstacles, both natural and man-made, while trying to fulfill his dream of travelling around the world. Along the way he meets his best friend, a fellow turtle named Ray, and never forgets about Shelly, a turtle he saved that first day on the beach and the one he's always loved.

documents.title: The Help
documents.tagline: Change begins with a whisper.
documents.overview: Aibileen Clark is a middle-aged African-American maid who has spent her life raising white children and has recently lost her only son; Minny Jackson is an African-American maid who has often offended her employers despite her family's struggles with money and her desperate need for jobs; and Eugenia "Skeeter" Phelan is a young white woman who has recently moved back home after graduating college to find out her childhood maid has mysteriously disappeared. These three stories intertwine to explain how life in Jackson, Mississippi revolves around "the help"; yet they are always kept at a certain distance because of racial lines.
documents.plot:
The Help is a drama film released in 2011, directed by Tate Taylor and produced by 1492 Pictures, DreamWorks Pictures, and Playtone. The movie is based on the novel of the same name by Kathryn Stockett.

The story takes place in Jackson, Mississippi, during the early 1960s, a time of great social change and racial tension. The film follows three main characters: Skeeter Phelan (played by Emma Stone), Aibileen Clark (played by Viola Davis), and Minny Jackson (played by Octavia Spencer).

Skeeter, a young white woman, returns to her hometown after graduating from college with a degree in journalism. She decides to write a book about the experiences of African American maids in the South during that era, which was largely unseen and unheard by the general public.

Aibileen, a wise and kind black maid who has been working for various white families in Jackson, becomes Skeeter's confidant and guide. Aibileen shares her own story of raising white children while struggling with racism and sexism in her daily life. She also introduces Skeeter to Minny, another black maid who is known for her sharp wit and outspoken nature.

As the story unfolds, Skeeter begins to gather stories from other African American maids, including Hilly Holbrook (played by Jessica Chastain), a well-meaning but clueless socialite who inadvertently perpetuates racist stereotypes. The maids share their experiences of being treated poorly, being forced to do menial tasks, and facing humiliation at the hands of their white employers.

Through Aibileen's guidance, Skeeter learns about the complexities of racial relationships in Jackson during that time period. She also begins to question her own privilege as a white woman growing up in a predominantly black community.

As the book nears completion, Hilly discovers that one of the maids has been secretly writing about their experiences and decides to take action against them. The maids are forced to confront the consequences of speaking out against racism and sexism.

The film culminates with Aibileen's story being published in a local newspaper, which sparks a wave of outrage and change in Jackson. The publication of the book also brings attention to the struggles faced by African American women during that era, highlighting their resilience and strength in the face of adversity.

Throughout the movie, the characters' relationships are complex and multifaceted, reflecting the nuances of racial dynamics in the South during the 1960s. The film ultimately celebrates the power of storytelling and the importance of giving voice to those who have been silenced for too long.

The Help received widespread critical acclaim, earning several Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, Best Actress for Viola Davis, and Best Supporting Actress for Octavia Spencer, who won the award.

documents.title: Super Troopers 2
documents.tagline: The mustache rides. Again.
documents.overview: When an international border dispute arises between the U.S. and Canada, the Super Troopers- Mac, Thorny, Foster, Rabbit and Farva, are called in to set up a new Highway Patrol station in the disputed area.
documents.plot:
Super Troopers 2 is a comedy film that explores several themes, primarily revolving around the camaraderie and brotherhood among its characters. The movie delves into the idea of loyalty and friendship as the five Vermont state troopers - Mac, Thorny, Foster, Rabbit, and Farva - embark on a mission to protect the state's maple syrup industry from an invasive Canadian company.

The film also touches upon the theme of identity and growth, as the characters navigate their personal lives and confront their own limitations. The movie pokes fun at the idea of masculinity and traditional male roles, often using humor to comment on societal expectations and stereotypes.

Furthermore, Super Troopers 2 features a strong sense of community and regional pride, celebrating the unique culture and traditions of Vermont. The film's lighthearted tone and comedic approach allow it to tackle these themes in an entertaining and engaging way, making it a fun and entertaining ride for audiences.

documents.title: Fallen
documents.tagline: A prophecy. A destiny. A fallen angel.
documents.overview: For high schooler Aaron Corbett, turning 18 means becoming not just a man but a nephilim, too -- half human, half angel, with supernatural abilities.
documents.plot:
Fallen is a 2006 American supernatural fantasy television film, the first part of a three-part miniseries made for ABC Family and based on the young-adult novels by Thomas E. Sniegoski. Directed by Mikael Salomon, known for his work on Band of Brothers and Rome, from a script by Sara Cooper, it stars Paul Wesley as Aaron Corbett, Tom Skerritt as Zeke, Lisa Lackey as Verchiel, Fernanda Andrade as Vilma and Rick Worthy as the archangel Camael, with Chelah Horsdal, Alex Ferris and Byron Mann. It premiered on 23 July 2006, and this first part is subtitled The Beginning.

Each part opens with narration over biblical images telling the legend of the fallen angels and of the Nephilim, half-angel, half-human beings considered abominations, whom soldier angels known as the Powers are determined to purge from the world. Aaron is a troubled orphan who has spent three years with a loving foster family in a small American town. He has become a popular wrestling star at school and has learned to control the violent urges that plagued his past. On his eighteenth birthday, however, he begins to suffer intense headaches, discovers he can understand and speak languages he has never studied, displays sudden bursts of strength and is alarmed to hear the thoughts of his dog Gabriel, all of which disrupts his studies and his budding romance with his classmate Vilma. A homeless man named Zeke, actually a fallen angel in disguise, reveals that Aaron is a Nephilim and that few like him survive the transformation. Aaron also learns that he may be the Redeemer of prophecy, able to absolve fallen angels and send them back to Heaven, which puts him in the sights of the Powers, led by the ruthless Verchiel, who hunt him down.

The two later parts, The Journey and The Destiny, aired in 2007, bringing the full miniseries to over four hours. In Variety, Laura Fries noted that the film follows the books closely in plot, though Verchiel, male in the novels, is played by a woman. She found Cooper's script talky and its symbolism simplistic, and Salomon's camera gimmicks distracting, but credited the film with deeper character development than expected and decent effects. Reviewing the miniseries on DVD Talk, Thomas Spurlin praised Wesley's performance and the supporting cast but found the exposition-heavy story far too long.

documents.title: Animals United
documents.overview: A group of animals waiting for the annual flood they rely on for food and water discover that the humans, who have been destroying their habitats have built a dam for a leisure resort. The animals endeavour to save the delta and send a message to the humans not to interfere with nature.
documents.plot:
Animals United (German: Konferenz der Tiere) is a 2010 German animated adventure comedy directed and produced by Reinhard Klooss and Holger Tappe, loosely based on Erich Kästner and Walter Trier's 1949 book The Animals' Conference. In the German version, Ralf Schmitz voices Billy the meerkat and Thomas Fritsch voices Socrates the lion, alongside Christoph Maria Herbst, Bastian Pastewka and Oliver Kalkofe, while the English dub features James Corden, Stephen Fry and Andy Serkis. It was released in Germany on October 7, 2010.

In Africa's Okavango Delta, the yearly flood has failed to arrive, and as water grows scarce the animals, including a herd of rhinos and a herd of buffaloes, quarrel fiercely over what little remains. Billy, a young meerkat, and his friend Socrates, a lion, set out to find water. Their journey takes them into a feared place known as the Valley of Death, and along the way they meet a ragtag band of animals from around the world, including Sushi the polar bear, Toby the kangaroo, Smiley the Tasmanian devil, an elderly pair of Galápagos tortoises and Charles the rooster, all of whom have been driven from their homes by human activity and have made their way to Africa.

The animals discover the cause of the drought: a dam has been built to supply a luxury resort, the Eden Paradise Hotel, which is hosting an international climate conference. With the help of Toto, a chimpanzee kept as the hotel's mascot, they try to restore the river, but the poacher Hunter captures Socrates. The animals then hold their own conference, where the old tortoises warn of the bleak future facing wildlife before passing away.

Determined to act, Billy and his friends cross the Valley of Death to the dam. Toto foils Hunter's attempt to stop them from a biplane, and the animals send a swarm of locusts into the conference hall, where they devour everything, including the delegates' documents and clothes. Billy rescues Socrates, the animals turn the tables on Hunter, and the dam is breached, sending water flowing back into the delta. The animals celebrate, invite Toto to live with them, and set off to hold humanity to account.

Produced by Ambient Entertainment, the film drew more than 1.5 million viewers in German cinemas and grossed over $50 million worldwide. International reviews were largely unfavorable; The Hollywood Reporter called it bombastic, preaching too much while entertaining too little. A sequel, Pets United, followed on Netflix in 2019.

documents.overview: Two 19th-century opportunists become serial killers so that they can maintain their profitable business supplying cadavers to an anatomist.

documents.title: Ed, Edd n Eddy's Big Picture Show
documents.original_title: Ed, Edd n Eddy's Big Picture Show
documents.tagline: One Failed Scam Gone Bad!
documents.overview: When a scam goes horribly wrong and leaves the neighborhood kids furious, the Eds embark on a journey to find Eddy's brother in the "Ed, Edd, n Eddy" series finale.
documents.plot:
"The Eds"—Ed, Edd and Eddy—anxiously flee their devastated cul-de-sac after their most recent money-making scheme backfires heavily and severely injures their neighbors Jonny, Kevin, Nazz and Rolf, who plot to retaliate violently. After narrowly escaping, Eddy recommends seeking protection from his older brother. Since Eddy does not actually know where he lives, Edd tries to piece together Eddy's inconsistent facts about him to determine a location. To find the Eds, Jonny takes his wooden board Plank with him on a city bus, Rolf rides on his pig Wilfred, and Nazz joins Kevin to travel via Kevin's prized bicycle. While Jimmy and Sarah, Ed's younger sister, were not involved or affected by the scheme, they decide to have a picnic while watching their retaliation. On the way over, they run into the Kanker Sisters; Lee, Marie and May. Upon learning about the other children's intent from them, the Kankers set out to save the Eds while taking the duo hostage.
Meanwhile, the Eds are left to wander aimlessly under Eddy's direction. In a cow pasture, Edd profiles Eddy's brother and reasons that given his con artistry, he would likely be found at a place involving pranks. Ed uses one of his decade-old comic books to suggest visiting the Lemon Brook Gag Factory. Upon arriving, they discover that it has been out of business ever since and Edd finds no clues in the office. Meanwhile, Wilfred, fed up with Rolf's abrasive attitude towards him, attacks his owner in a frenzy and abandons him.
After leaving the factory, Eddy claims his brother was once a whaler, so Edd deduces he must live by the sea. They build a boat and ride on it over a river to find him. The river ends in a swamp, where the boat is destroyed. Ed and Eddy then prank Edd into believing that they sank to their demises in quicksand. Enraged, Edd berates Eddy for the prank and his scamming before deciding to return home. As Ed laments over their damaged friendship, Eddy is initially enraged by this, but soon breaks down crying and accepts responsibility for their predicament, prompting Edd to forgive him as the Eds continue their adventure.
Elsewhere, Nazz loses her patience with Kevin prioritizing his bicycle over her well-being and feelings while Jimmy and Sarah escape from the Kankers and are accompanied by Wilfred. The Kankers abduct Kevin, Nazz and Rolf before the Eds come across a coastal amusement park the next morning called "Mondo A-Go Go", which matches a postcard Eddy received from his brother. They conclude that Eddy's brother works there and find his whale-based trailer as the Kankers catch up to them. Eddy's brother reveals himself and, although he originally seems willing to help Eddy, is eventually shown to be physically abusive towards him without reason, leaving everyone appalled. When Edd tries to interfere, Eddy's brother assaults him, prompting everyone to defend Eddy.

documents.title: Mars Needs Moms
documents.tagline: Mom needs a little space.
documents.overview: When Martians suddenly abduct his mom, mischievous Milo rushes to the rescue and discovers why all moms are so special.
documents.plot:
Mars Needs Moms is a 3D science fiction comedy film directed by Simon Wells and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie was released on March 18, 2011.

In the beginning of the story, we are introduced to Milo (played by Seth Green), an 11-year-old boy who lives with his mother, Marta (played by Mindy Sterling), in a suburban town. Milo's life is ordinary and uneventful, but he longs for adventure and excitement. One day, while out on a walk, Milo discovers that Marta has been abducted by aliens from Mars.

The aliens, known as the Martian Moms, arrive on Earth to collect human mothers to take back to their planet. They use a device called the "Moms' Transporter" to abduct the mothers, leaving behind only one child per family. The Martian Moms believe that human children are inferior and will eventually grow up to be loyal servants.

Milo soon discovers that his mother has been taken by the aliens and sets out on a journey to rescue her. He meets a robot named Gadget (voiced by Dan Fogler), who was also left behind by his own mother, and together they embark on a quest to Mars to find Marta.

Upon arrival on Mars, Milo and Gadget encounter various obstacles and challenges as they navigate the planet's harsh environment. They meet a group of Martian kids who are being raised by the alien mothers, but have grown up to be rebellious and independent. The kids, led by a character named Lopax (voiced by Elisabeth Harnois), join forces with Milo and Gadget to help them on their mission.

As they journey deeper into Mars, Milo and his new friends face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, hostile aliens, and the harsh conditions of the Martian environment. Along the way, Milo learns valuable lessons about responsibility, loyalty, and the importance of family.

In the end, Milo and Gadget successfully rescue Marta from the clutches of the Martian Moms. However, in a surprising twist, it is revealed that the Martian Moms' plan was not to enslave humans, but to protect them from an even greater threat: a massive asteroid that is on a collision course with Earth.

With the help of the Martian kids and their mothers, Milo and Gadget are able to deflect the asteroid and save humanity. The movie ends with Milo returning home to his mother, who has been reunited with him, but not before learning about the incredible adventure he had on Mars.

Overall, Mars Needs Moms is a fun and action-packed sci-fi comedy that explores themes of family, loyalty, and responsibility. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has its fans and offers a unique blend of humor, adventure, and heart.

documents.title: Firebreather
documents.tagline: Forged in Darkness, Born in Flames
documents.overview: It's not easy being a teen like Duncan. His mom wants him to pay more attention to his homework, while his dad - a 120-foot-tall monster known as a Kaiju - wants him to become the next King of All Monsters. When these worlds collide, Duncan must use his human wits and his Kaiju powers - including super strength, agility and the ability to breathe fire - to protect his family and friends from a giant monster rampage.
documents.plot:
Firebreather is an American computer-animated superhero television film of 2010 based on the Image Comics series created by Phil Hester and Andy Kuhn. Directed by Peter Chung from a screenplay by James Krieg, it premiered on Cartoon Network on 24 November 2010. Jesse Head voices the teenage hero Duncan Rosenblatt, with Dana Delany as his mother Margaret, Kevin Michael Richardson as his monstrous father Belloc, Amy Davidson as Jenna, Tia Texada as Isabel, Dante Basco as Kenny and Reed Diamond as Agent "Blitz" Barnes.

On the last day of the war between humans and the giant monsters called Kaiju, their dragon-like king Belloc attacks a city, but when a woman named Margaret confronts him, the two fall in love and he withdraws. Their son, Duncan, is born with Kaiju features and powers. Sixteen years later, Margaret and Duncan move to a new town, where he fears his appearance will make him a target. He falls for the popular Jenna, makes an enemy of her former boyfriend Troy, and befriends the outcasts Kenny and Isabel, a Kaiju-obsessed girl who develops a crush on him. Blitz Barnes, an agent of a monster-defence agency posing as a gym teacher, discovers that Duncan can breathe fire.

At a party, Duncan grows closer to Jenna, but Belloc arrives and carries him off to his desert lair, presenting him to the other Kaiju as his heir and hurling him into a lava pit, from which Duncan emerges transformed. Back at school, Isabel has made him a celebrity by claiming he saved everyone from Belloc. Duncan secretly leaves a precious red crystal in Jenna's locker to replace the Homecoming money stolen by Troy's friends, and asks her to the dance. On a mission with Blitz, he spares a Kaiju he could have killed. At Homecoming, a jealous Kenny tells Duncan that Isabel likes him only because of his father, and Jenna, overhearing, storms out. Two Kaiju, Abaddon and Astaroth, then attack. Duncan holds them off, sprouts wings to save Blitz from a fall, and with the help of Belloc, summoned by Margaret and Jenna, buries the monsters in an avalanche instead of killing them. Belloc lets himself be captured so as to stay close to his son, Jenna, who has realised Duncan left the crystal, apologises, and Duncan soars away on his new wings.

Reviewing it at New York Comic Con, Mania.com gave the film a B+, praising its blend of teenage angst and monster battles while noting that the characters sometimes looked puppet-like.

documents.title: The Lincoln Lawyer
documents.tagline: This Case is a Dangerous Game of Life and Death.
documents.overview: A lawyer conducts business from the back of his Lincoln town car while representing a high-profile client in Beverly Hills.
documents.plot: Mick Haller is a charismatic defense attorney who does business out of his Lincoln Continental sedan. Mick spends most of his time defending petty crooks and other bottom-feeders, so it comes as quite a surprise when he lands the case of a lifetime: defending a Beverly Hills playboy who is accused of attempted murder. However, what Mick initially thinks is an open-and-shut case with a big monetary reward develops into something more sinister.

documents.title: Apollo 18
documents.tagline: There's a reason we've never gone back to the moon.
documents.overview: Officially, Apollo 17 was the last manned mission to the moon. But a year later in 1973, three American astronauts were sent on a secret mission to the moon funded by the US Department of Defense. What you are about to see is the actual footage which the astronauts captured on that mission. While NASA denies its authenticity, others say it's the real reason we've never gone back to the moon.

Sent into the world by her father on a mission, Hanna journeys across Europe, eluding agents dispatched after her by a ruthless intelligence operative. As she nears her ultimate target, Hanna faces startling revelations about her existence.

documents.title: Avalon High
documents.overview: Disney Channel's production of Julie Sherman Wolfe's screenplay adaptation of the popular novel Avalon High by Meg Cabot. Elaine "Ellie" Harrison has just moved from Minnesota to Annapolis, Maryland while her parents take a year long sabbatical to continue their medieval studies in nearby DC. Her new high school, Avalon High, seems like a typical high school with the stereotypical students: Lance the jock, Jennifer the cheerleader, Marco, the bad boy/desperado, and Will, the senior class president, quarterback, and all around good guy. But not everyone at Avalon High is who they appear to be, not even Ellie herself. Eventually, it becomes apparent that Avalon High is a situation where the ancient Arthurian legend is repeating itself. Will, Jennifer, Lance, Marco, and Mr. Morton all correspond to King Arthur, Queen Guinevere, Knight Lancelot, Mordred, and Merlin, respectively.
documents.plot: Elaine "Ellie" Harrison has just moved from Minnesota to Annapolis, Maryland while her parents take a year-long sabbatical to continue their medieval studies in nearby Washington D.C. Her new high school, Avalon High, seems like a typical high school with the stereotypical students: Lance the jock, Jennifer the cheerleader, Marco, the bad boy/desperado, and Will, the senior class president, quarterback, and all around good guy. But not everyone at Avalon High is who they appear to be, not even Ellie herself. Eventually, it becomes apparent that Avalon High is a situation where the ancient Arthurian legend is repeating itself.

documents.title: Just Go with It
documents.tagline: Sometimes a guy's best wingman... is a wingwoman
documents.overview: A plastic surgeon, romancing a much younger schoolteacher, enlists his loyal assistant to pretend to be his soon to be ex-wife, in order to cover up a careless lie. When more lies backfire, the assistant's kids become involved, and everyone heads off for a weekend in Hawaii that will change all their lives.  A remake of Cactus Flower (1969).
documents.plot:
Just Go with It is a 2011 American romantic comedy film directed by Dennis Dugan and starring Adam Sandler, Jennifer Aniston, and Brooklyn Decker.

The movie begins with Danny Maccabee (Adam Sandler), a successful plastic surgeon who has been married to his high school sweetheart, Palmer Dodge (Brooklyn Decker), for three years. However, their marriage is on the rocks due to Palmer's lack of interest in sex and her desire to have children. Feeling suffocated by the situation, Danny decides to end the relationship.

One day, while working on a new face, Danny meets Katherine Murphy (Jennifer Aniston), his receptionist who has been secretly admiring him from afar. Katherine is a single mother with a young son, who is struggling to make ends meet after her husband's death. Despite their instant attraction, Danny tries to keep his distance, fearing that he will get hurt again.

However, when Palmer reveals that she is pregnant, Danny sees an opportunity to win her back and proposes a fake engagement to Katherine, claiming that they are having an affair. The plan works initially, but things start to get complicated as Katherine begins to develop real feelings for Danny.

As the story unfolds, Katherine's son, Gabe (Nathan Parsons), becomes a catalyst for change in Danny's life. Through his interactions with Gabe, Danny starts to see Katherine in a different light and realizes that he has fallen in love with her. Meanwhile, Palmer's pregnancy progresses, and she begins to realize that she is not ready to be a mother.

The plot thickens when Katherine discovers the truth about Danny's fake engagement and feels betrayed. However, instead of being angry, she decides to give it another chance and proposes a real relationship to Danny. The movie culminates with Danny and Katherine confessing their love for each other and starting a new life together.

Throughout the film, Adam Sandler delivers his signature comedic charm, while Jennifer Aniston brings warmth and depth to her character. Brooklyn Decker shines as Palmer, providing a perfect foil to the on-screen chemistry between Sandler and Aniston. The movie's lighthearted tone, witty dialogue, and engaging storyline make it an enjoyable watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Just Go with It is a heartwarming romantic comedy that explores themes of love, relationships, and self-discovery. With its talented cast, engaging plot, and uplifting message, this movie is sure to leave viewers feeling entertained and inspired.

documents.title: The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 1
documents.original_title: The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 1
documents.tagline: Forever is just the beginning
documents.overview: The new found married bliss of Bella Swan and vampire Edward Cullen is cut short when a series of betrayals and misfortunes threatens to destroy their world.
documents.plot:
Several months after the events of the previous film, human Bella Swan and vampire Edward Cullen are getting married. During the reception, werewolf Jacob Black, who had left town upon receiving his invitation to the wedding, returns, much to Bella's delight. They share a dance in the woods, where Bella says that she and Edward plan to consummate their marriage on their honeymoon while she is still human. Jacob becomes furious, fearing that such an act could kill her.
After the wedding, Bella and Edward travel to an island off the coast of Rio de Janeiro for their honeymoon, and they have sex for the first time. Two weeks later, Bella vomits after waking and realizes her period is late. She informs Carlisle Cullen, a medical doctor and Edward's adoptive father, that she believes she is pregnant.
Edward is distraught, as it is highly unlikely a human could survive giving birth to a vampire's baby. He encourages Bella to receive an abortion from Carlisle. She refuses and convinces Edward's sister Rosalie to be her bodyguard. The couple flies back home to Forks, Washington, where Jacob rushes to the Cullens' house to find a pale, underweight, and visibly pregnant Bella. He implores her to terminate the pregnancy immediately, but she refuses.
Jacob storms out of the Cullens' residence and meets in the woods with his packmates, including their leader Sam, who soon feels they should kill Bella to ensure her half-vampire child does not harm anyone. Jacob refuses, and he and several other werewolves separate from the pack.
As Bella's pregnancy progresses, her health declines rapidly. She soon realizes the fetus is craving blood, so she begins drinking human blood obtained by Carlisle from the hospital, improving her health. As a half-vampire, the fetus's development is far more accelerated than that of a human fetus, and thus Bella's pregnancy progresses at an alarming rate.
Edward's resentment for the baby dissolves when he discovers he can read its thoughts. When Bella suddenly goes into labor, Edward, Jacob, and Rosalie begin performing an emergency C-section while Carlisle is out obtaining blood. The procedure is excruciatingly painful, and Bella falls unconscious, though she wakes to find she has delivered a healthy daughter, whom she names Renesmee—a combination of her mother's name and Edward's mother's name.
Bella's heart suddenly stops, and Jacob desperately attempts CPR. Edward injects Bella's heart with his venom in an attempt to transform her into a vampire, but his action seems futile as Bella remains lifeless. A distraught Jacob decides to kill Renesmee for apparently causing Bella's death; however, when he looks into the baby's eyes, he "imprints" on her: a werewolf phenomenon in which one realizes one's soulmate. This prevents his pack from killing her as their most absolute law is not to harm anyone who has been imprinted on.
Over the course of two days, though still unconscious, Bella's injuries heal and her figure returns to normal.

documents.title: The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 2
documents.original_title: The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 2
documents.tagline: The epic finale that will live forever
documents.overview: After the birth of Renesmee, the Cullens gather other vampire clans in order to protect the child from a false allegation that puts the family in front of the Volturi.
documents.plot:
The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 2 is a 2012 American fantasy romance film directed by Bill Condon, based on the fourth and final novel of Stephenie Meyer's Twilight Saga. The movie concludes the story of Bella Swan (Kristen Stewart) and her husband Edward Cullen (Robert Pattinson), who are now a family with their newborn daughter Renesmee.

The story begins with the Volturi, an ancient vampire coven, believing that the Cullens have created an "immortal child," which is against the law of the vampire world. The Volturi, led by Aro (Michael Sheen), believe that the Cullens are hiding a secret and plan to destroy them.

The Cullens gather witnesses from around the world to testify on their behalf, including Jacob Black (Taylor Lautner), who has fallen in love with Renesmee. The Cullens also prepare for a potential battle against the Volturi, while Bella and Edward try to protect their daughter from the danger that surrounds her.

As the story unfolds, the Cullens face off against the Volturi in a dramatic showdown. The movie features stunning action sequences, impressive visual effects, and emotional moments between the characters.

Throughout the film, Bella struggles with her newfound motherhood and her relationship with Edward, who is still struggling to accept their daughter as one of his own. Meanwhile, Jacob's love for Renesmee deepens, and he must come to terms with his role in the Cullens' lives.

Ultimately, the Cullens are able to prove that Renesmee is not an immortal child, but a half-human, half-vampire hybrid, which changes the rules of the vampire world. The Volturi are defeated, and the Cullens are finally able to live in peace with their daughter by their side.

The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 2 concludes the series on a hopeful note, with Bella and Edward's love stronger than ever, and Renesmee growing up as a powerful and unique individual. The movie features stunning visuals, impressive action sequences, and emotional moments that will leave audiences satisfied and fulfilled.

Overall, The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn - Part 2 is a satisfying conclusion to the series, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers engaged until the very end.

documents.title: Prison-A-Go-Go!
documents.overview: A women-in-prison action comedy featuring girls running amok! Multiple Shower Scenes! Kung Fu Food Fights! Mutant Zombies! Evil Scientists, Prominent Product Placement, and Mud Wrastlin!
documents.plot:
Prison-A-Go-Go! is a 2003 American low-budget action comedy directed by Barak Epstein, who wrote it with Mike Wiebe, and produced by WorldWide International Picture Studios, known for campy B-movies. A deliberate parody of and homage to the women-in-prison exploitation genre, it also borrows from zombie horror, mad-scientist pictures and ninja films. Laurie Walton plays the heroine Janie, with Lauren Graham as her sister Callista, Travis Willingham as the villainous Dr. Hurtrider, Rhonda Shear as the inmate Jackpot and Ilram Choi as a ninja, while Mary Woronov and the Troma Entertainment chief Lloyd Kaufman make cameo appearances and Wiebe plays the prison's new warden.

Janie, a small-town veterinarian, sees her sister kidnapped by the henchmen of Dr. Hurtrider, a self-described scientist and torturer who intends to experiment on Callista in his absurd quest to cure the common cold, using torture, lobotomies and genetic mutation even on people who are not sick. The abductors conveniently leave behind a business card giving the doctor's address as the biggest prison in the Philippines, and the dim-witted Janie concludes that the only way to reach her sister is to get herself locked up there. She kills a local vagrant, receives her sentence and is shipped off to the institution.

Inside, she finds a surreal place where the guards are gay, the women are more victims of fashion than of violence and the newly hired warden, appointed by an executive played by Woronov, is spectacularly lazy. An on-screen shower clock counts down to the next of the film's many shower scenes. Teaming up with the queen bee Jackpot, a gang of fellow inmates and a reluctant, acrobatic ninja, Janie must find Callista before Hurtrider turns her into a human-porcupine hybrid, while his laboratory experiments also produce flesh-eating zombies. The film also promised kung fu food fights and mud wrestling.

Shot on 35 mm film with rented equipment, Prison-A-Go-Go! premiered at the 2003 Deep Ellum Film Festival, where it was named best feature, and it won four prizes at that year's B-Movie Film Festival, including best B-movie, best director and best actress for Shear, followed by festival awards in 2004. It was released on DVD in 2005. Critics were largely unimpressed. DVD Talk found it a tiresome spoof with occasional laughs, praising Woronov, Wiebe and Choi, and Film Blitz felt it pointed out the genre's clichés without exaggerating them enough to be truly funny.

documents.title: Crazy, Stupid, Love.
documents.tagline: This is crazy. This is stupid. This is love.
documents.overview: Cal Weaver is living the American dream. He has a good job, a beautiful house, great children and a beautiful wife, named Emily. Cal's seemingly perfect life unravels, however, when he learns that Emily has been unfaithful and wants a divorce. Over 40 and suddenly single, Cal is adrift in the fickle world of dating. Enter, Jacob Palmer, a self-styled player who takes Cal under his wing and teaches him how to be a hit with the ladies.
documents.plot:
Cal Weaver is a middle-aged family man whose wife Emily asks for a divorce after she reveals an affair she had with co-worker David Lindhagen. The news stuns Cal, who jumps out of their moving car when Emily tries to talk about the affair. The divorce also ends his friendship with best friend Bernie Riley, whose wife sides with Emily over Cal.
After moving into his own apartment, Cal begins frequenting an upscale bar, where he talks loudly about his wife cheating and divorce. He meets Jacob Palmer, a young man and womanizer who frequently beds different women but was recently rejected by a law school graduate, Hannah. Jacob takes pity on Cal and offers to teach him how to pick up women. After a few awkward attempts to talk to women, Cal seduces a woman named Kate at the bar. This experience gives him the confidence to seduce other women, and he begins to emulate Jacob's example successfully.
Eventually, Cal and Emily reunite at their 13-year-old son Robbie's parent–teacher conference, where she is impressed by his newfound confidence and fitted clothes. Their reunion goes well until they meet Robbie's teacher, who turns out to be Kate, and who spitefully reveals her and Cal's tryst because he never called her afterwards. In the ensuing argument, Cal inadvertently confesses to having sex with nine women since their separation, so Emily leaves in disgust that Cal did this as payback for her cheating while also openly dating David.
Robbie makes numerous grand gestures to win the heart of his babysitter Jessica, who is Bernie's daughter. She eventually dissuades him after revealing she likes someone older, without revealing it is Cal. On the advice of a promiscuous classmate, she takes nude photos of herself, intending to give them to him. Emily calls Cal under the guise of needing help with the pilot light on her water heater, but he sees through the ruse. Realizing that she called just because she missed him, Cal decides to win her back.
Meanwhile, Hannah is offended by her boyfriend when he offers her a position at his firm instead of proposing as expected. She returns to the bar, finds Jacob, and throws herself at him. As Jacob ends up walking her through his process of seducing women, they end up developing genuine chemistry and start dating.
Jacob returns Cal's calls, asking for advice about being in a real relationship and meeting his girlfriend's parents. Jessica's mother finds the naked photos, which make her and Bernie believe that Cal and Jessica are in an illicit relationship. He furiously drives to Cal's, with Jessica following to stop him.
Cal and his kids create a makeshift mini golf set in their backyard to remind Emily of their first date. During the gathering, Jacob and Hannah show up, and Hannah is revealed to be Cal and Emily's daughter. Cal is appalled that Jacob is dating his daughter, and forbids her from seeing him. Emily supports their relationship.

documents.title: Wanderlust
documents.tagline: Leave your baggage behind
documents.overview: Rattled by sudden unemployment, a Manhattan couple surveys alternative living options, ultimately deciding to experiment with living on a rural commune where free love rules.
documents.plot: Rattled by sudden unemployment, a Manhattan couple surveys alternative living options, ultimately deciding to experiment with living on a rural commune where free love rules.

documents.title: The Resident
documents.tagline: She Thought She Was Living Alone
documents.overview: Juliet, a beautiful doctor, has found the perfect New York apartment to start a new life after separating from her husband. It's got spacious rooms, a spectacular view, and a handy, handsome landlord. But there are secrets behind every wall and terror in every room as Juliet gets the unnerving feeling that she is not alone.
documents.plot:
The Resident is a 2011 American psychological thriller directed by Antti Jokinen and starring Hilary Swank and Jeffrey Dean Morgan, with Lee Pace, Aunjanue Ellis and Christopher Lee in supporting roles. Produced by the revived Hammer Films, it marked Lee's return to the studio for the first time since To the Devil a Daughter in 1976. Swank plays a newly separated woman who moves into a New York apartment and comes to suspect that someone is watching her.

Juliet Devereau, an emergency room physician, rents a spacious Brooklyn apartment from its charming landlord, Max. She has recently left her husband Jack after discovering his affair, though she still has feelings for him. Unknown to Juliet, someone is stalking her, watching from across the street and apparently entering the apartment when she is away. At a party she runs into Max and flirts with him, and the two begin a tentative romance, but when they are about to sleep together she stops, admitting that she cannot stop thinking about Jack, and she ends things with Max.

A flashback reveals that Max is the one stalking her. He has rebuilt the apartment with hidden passageways and a two-way mirror that allow him to spy on her, and he lives with his elderly grandfather August, played by Lee. After Juliet's rejection, Max's obsession grows darker. He enters her apartment while she is at work and violates her private space, watches her reconcile with Jack and begins drugging her wine so he can be near her while she is unconscious. After oversleeping repeatedly, Juliet suspects something is wrong and installs security cameras. Max attacks and injures Jack and, one night, attempts to assault the drugged Juliet before she stirs and he flees. Tests at the hospital reveal high levels of Demerol in her system, and the camera footage finally shows her the truth. When Max returns and attacks her again, Juliet must fight for her life inside the hidden spaces of the building he controls.

Critical response was mostly negative: Rotten Tomatoes reports that 35% of 31 critics gave it a positive review. The Guardian called it generic and intermittently silly, while the Financial Times praised Swank's performance and Total Film described it as a sturdy, moody thriller undone by its over-the-top climax. A novelization by Francis Cottam was published in 2011.

documents.title: Grave Encounters
documents.tagline: They Were Searching For Proof.  They Found it.
documents.overview: A crew from a paranormal reality television show lock themselves in a haunted psychiatric hospital. They search for evidence of paranormal activity as they shoot what ends up becoming their final episode.
documents.plot: A crew from a paranormal reality television show lock themselves in a haunted psychiatric hospital. They search for evidence of paranormal activity as they shoot what ends up becoming their final episode.

documents.title: Naruto Shippuden the Movie: The Lost Tower
documents.original_title: 劇場版 NARUTO -ナルト- 疾風伝 ザ・ロストタワー
documents.overview: Assigned on a mission to capture Mukade, a missing-nin, Naruto Uzumaki sets out for the once glorious historic ruins of "Ouran", where he pursues and corners the rouge ninja. Mukade's goal is revealed to be a dormant leyline within the ruins; he unleashes the power of the leyline, causing a light to envelop Naruto, sending him into the past, 20 years before the series began. When Naruto awakens, he comes into contact with the Fourth Hokage, Minato Namikaze.
documents.plot:
Naruto Shippuden the Movie: The Lost Tower is a 2010 Japanese animated action-adventure fantasy film based on Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto manga and its anime adaptation. It is the fourth film in the Naruto Shippuden series, directed by Masahiko Murata and produced by Studio Pierrot, and it was released in Japan on July 31, 2010. The Japanese voice cast includes Junko Takeuchi as Naruto, Chie Nakamura as Sakura, Toshiyuki Morikawa as Minato, Kazuhiko Inoue as Kakashi and Satoshi Hino as Sai. A comic short, Naruto, the Genie, and the Three Wishes!!, was screened alongside it, and the theme song "if" was performed by Kana Nishino.

Naruto Uzumaki, Sakura Haruno, Sai and their captain Yamato are sent to capture Mukade, a rogue ninja. They track him to the thousand-year-old ruins of Loran, a desert city, where he plans to dominate the ninja world by seizing the power of the Ryūmyaku, an ancient stream of chakra flowing deep underground. Mukade breaks a seal placed long ago by Minato Namikaze, Naruto's father and the Fourth Hokage, unleashing a blast of light that engulfs Naruto and Yamato while Sakura and Sai escape on one of Sai's ink birds.

Naruto awakens twenty years in the past, in the time of Loran's prosperity, and meets the city's young queen, Sāra. Mukade, it turns out, was thrown back six years earlier and has taken the identity of Anrokuzan, a minister who murdered Sāra's mother and now uses the kingdom's kidnapped citizens to build an army of puppet ninjas. Naruto vows to protect Sāra, and he is soon joined by a younger Minato, along with Kakashi Hatake, Shibi Aburame and Chōza Akimichi, who are on their own mission to stop Anrokuzan. Fighting side by side with the father he never knew, though neither recognizes the other, Naruto helps rescue Loran's people. When Anrokuzan transforms the tower into a gigantic puppet, Naruto and Minato combine their chakra in a powerful attack, and Minato finally seals the Ryūmyaku and erases everyone's memories so that history remains unchanged.

Back in the present, the team reunites in the ruins and meets Sāra's daughter, who carries a chakra blade that her mother received from a "hero in a dream." Naruto recognizes it as his own, while Sakura insists he must have been dreaming.

The film is set after episode 143 of the Naruto: Shippuden anime. It was released on DVD in Japan in April 2011, and Viz Media released it in North America on September 17, 2013.

documents.title: Take Me Home Tonight
documents.tagline: Best. Night. Ever.
documents.overview: Recent MIT grad Matt Franklin should be well on his way to a successful career at a Fortune 500 company, but instead he rebels against maturity by taking a job at a video store. Matt rethinks his position when his unrequited high-school crush, Tori, walks in and invites him to an end-of-summer party. With the help of his twin sister and his best friend, Matt hatches a plan to change the course of his life.

documents.title: Ticking Clock
documents.overview: A reporter stumbles upon the journal of a murderer with plans to butcher specific girls, and he begins to investigates on his own, and finding that every trail leads to a 9-year-old orphan living in a group home.
documents.plot:
Ticking Clock is a 2011 American mystery thriller directed by Ernie Barbarash and released direct to DVD in the United States on January 4, 2011. Cuba Gooding Jr. stars as the investigative reporter Louis Hicks, with Neal McDonough as the serial killer Keech, Nicki Aycox as Polly, Austin Abrams as the boy James, Danielle Nicolet as Louis's wife Gina and Yancey Arias as a detective.

The film opens as Keech kills a woman and then comforts her crying baby son. Louis is struggling with a faltering career and a troubled marriage, and is having an affair with a district attorney, Felicia, who ends their relationship. That same day Keech murders her at her home. Louis fights the intruder, who escapes but leaves behind his journal, which lists two more murders planned over the next three days. Louis copies down the names, but Keech steals back both the journal and the note, and when Louis goes to the police he becomes a suspect in Felicia's death.

Louis tracks down one of the intended victims, a schoolteacher named Vicki, but Keech reaches her first and kills her in a bar after talking with her about a boy she reported for hurting a cat. With the police still unconvinced, Louis sends a scrap of Keech's coat and a bloody fingerprint to a friend at a crime lab. The blood matches an eleven-year-old orphan, James, who lives in a boys' home run by Polly, and the coat's fabric behaves unlike any known material. James, a disturbed boy who wishes he could go back in time and fix his life, shows Louis a box of dead animals and then angrily sends him away.

Realising that Polly is the next name on the list, Louis concludes that Keech is James grown up and returned from the future. Jailed by sceptical police, he is visited by Keech posing as his lawyer, who confirms that he has travelled back from 2032 with a pocket-watch time machine. Keech explains that he killed his abusive mother hoping to change his childhood, but every change has led someone else to condemn him to the same fate, and he now plans to kill Polly and frame Louis. On the roof of the boys' home, young James confronts his older self and slashes him with a dropped knife, Keech accidentally knocks the boy off the roof and shoots Louis, and with James's death Keech vanishes and all of his victims are restored to life.

Ticking Clock received negative reviews, with Dread Central calling it an iffy thriller with an intriguing but underdeveloped premise.

documents.title: The Beaver
documents.tagline: He's here to save Walter's life.
documents.overview: Suffering from a severe case of depression, toy company CEO Walter Black begins using a beaver hand puppet to help him open up to his family. With his father seemingly going insane, adolescent son Porter pushes for his parents to get a divorce.
documents.plot:
The Beaver is a 2011 American psychological drama directed by Jodie Foster and written by Kyle Killen. It stars Mel Gibson as Walter Black, Foster as his wife Meredith, Anton Yelchin as their teenage son Porter and Jennifer Lawrence as Norah, with Cherry Jones and Riley Thomas Stewart. The film marked the second collaboration between Gibson and Foster, after the 1994 western comedy Maverick.

Walter Black is the chief executive of a family toy company that is sliding toward bankruptcy, and he has sunk into a deep, paralyzing depression. Unable to reach him, Meredith asks him to leave the family home, much to the relief of Porter, who resents his father and fears becoming like him. Living alone in a hotel and at his lowest point, Walter finds a beaver hand puppet in a dumpster. He begins to wear the puppet constantly and to speak only through it in a gruff voice, as if the beaver were a separate personality guiding him.

At first the strange arrangement seems to work miracles. Walter reconnects with his younger son Henry and wins back Meredith, and the company enjoys an unexpected revival thanks to a new line of building kits for children inspired by the beaver. Meanwhile, Porter, who earns money writing papers for classmates, is hired by Norah, a classmate, to write her graduation speech, and the two grow close as he senses that she is hiding grief over the death of her brother. Yet as Walter's dependence on the puppet deepens, Meredith realizes that the beaver is not a therapy but a sign of how ill her husband is, and the family must face the darkness behind the puppet before it consumes Walter entirely.

The film treats mental illness with a mix of dark humor and sincerity, exploring depression, identity and the burdens that parents pass on to their children.

The Beaver premiered at the SXSW Film Festival on March 16, 2011, and was released in the United States by Summit Entertainment on May 6, 2011. It received mixed reviews, with about 62 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 60; Gibson's performance and Foster's direction were praised, but the film was a box-office flop against its 21 million dollar budget.

documents.title: Martha Marcy May Marlene
documents.tagline: You can get away. But you can never escape.
documents.overview: After several years of living with a cult, Martha finally escapes and calls her estranged sister, Lucy, for help. Martha finds herself at the quiet Connecticut home Lucy shares with her new husband, Ted, but the memories of what she experienced in the cult make peace hard to find. As flashbacks continue to torment her, Martha fails to shake a terrible sense of dread, especially in regard to the cult's manipulative leader.
documents.plot:
A 22-year-old woman named Martha has been abused by a cult in the Catskill Mountains for two years. The patriarch, Patrick, named her Marcy May. She escapes into the woods, arriving at a nearby town. In a diner, she is confronted by Watts, a cult member, who attempts to persuade her to return, but when she refuses, he lets her leave. Martha calls her sister, Lucy, who picks her up and takes her to the vacation lake house in Connecticut that she shares with her husband, a successful architect named Ted.
Martha exhibits strange behavior by skinny dipping in public, sleeping all the time, not eating, and arguing with Lucy and Ted about how to live, specifically arguing over the need for career and possessions. Lucy reveals she abandoned Martha and is now attempting to get her back into her life, while she and Ted are also trying to have their own child. One night, Martha climbs into bed with Ted and Lucy while they are having sex, angering Ted and Lucy. Martha attempts to phone the cult because she misses them, accidentally finds out her friend Zoe is not on the farm with the cult, and hangs up when cult matriarch Katie answers using the code name "Marlene Miller."
In flashbacks, Martha recalls a series of disturbing events that led to her escape from the cult. She was originally recruited into the cult by Zoe. Martha was initially receptive but somewhat wary of Patrick, Katie, and Zoe. She was later convinced by Zoe and Patrick to let her guard down and "share herself", only to end up being drugged by Katie and brutally raped by Patrick; Katie and Zoe later explained to her that the rape was a cleansing ritual and told her she should be happy. Martha later "prepared" new initiate Sarah to be abused in the same way Katie had. Patrick urged Martha to kill a cat, which Martha refused. Her refusal prompted him to berate her for failing to follow the cult's ideals. Patrick constantly attempted to impregnate Martha to spread his genes, despite her resistance. Martha subsequently began participating in burglaries with the other cultists, including one where they murdered a homeowner who walked in on them. After witnessing the murder, Martha had a mental breakdown, to which Patrick responded by forcefully subduing her and berating her again; he then shifted to telling her that she was his favorite person and that he would never let her go.
Lucy and Ted host a party at their home, inviting numerous friends from the city. Martha is visibly nervous during the gathering. She has a psychotic episode when she misidentifies the bartender as a cult member; Lucy and Ted sedate her. Ted attempts to convince Lucy to send Martha to a psychiatric hospital, an idea Lucy rejects.
Later that night, Martha has a nightmare of being sexually abused by Patrick. Ted tries to calm her down, but Martha, thinking he is Patrick, kicks him down the staircase in a frightened panic.

documents.title: Margin Call
documents.tagline: Be first. Be smarter. Or cheat.
documents.overview: A thriller that revolves around the key people at an investment bank over a 24-hour period during the early stages of the financial crisis.
documents.plot: Set in the high-stakes world of the financial industry, involving the key players at an investment firm during one perilous 24-hour period in the early stages of the 2008 financial crisis. An entry-level analyst unlocks information that could prove to be the downfall of the firm.

documents.title: Arthur Christmas
documents.tagline: Ever wonder how 2 Billion presents get delivered all in 1 night?
documents.overview: Each Christmas, Santa and his vast army of highly trained elves produce gifts and distribute them around the world in one night. However, when one of 600 million children to receive a gift from Santa on Christmas Eve is missed, it is deemed ‘acceptable’ to all but one—Arthur. Arthur Claus is Santa’s misfit son who executes an unauthorised rookie mission to get the last present half way around the globe before dawn on Christmas morning.
documents.plot:
Arthur Christmas is a heartwarming animated comedy film released in 2011 by Columbia Pictures. The movie follows the story of Arthur, the eldest son of Santa Claus, who is struggling to live up to his father's expectations.

The film begins on Christmas Eve at the North Pole, where Santa and his wife, Mrs. Claus, are preparing for the big night. However, with the help of their elves, they manage to deliver all the presents in record time, thanks to a high-tech system that allows them to track every child's gift. The system is so efficient that it becomes redundant, and Arthur finds himself feeling unappreciated and overlooked.

As Christmas Eve comes to an end, Santa announces his retirement and names Arthur as his successor. However, Arthur is not interested in taking over the reins of the North Pole, and he spends most of his time trying to avoid his responsibilities. Meanwhile, a young girl named Sophie receives a gift that was left behind by Santa's high-tech system, which fails to deliver it on time.

Sophie teams up with Arthur's younger brother, Steve, who is more interested in playing video games than helping out at the North Pole. Together, they embark on a mission to find the missing gift and return it to its rightful owner. Along the way, they encounter a series of hilarious misadventures, including a run-in with a group of bumbling burglars.

As Arthur and Steve journey through the city, they begin to realize that Christmas is not just about presents, but about the joy and love that comes with giving and receiving. They also learn more about their father's legacy and the importance of following in his footsteps.

In the end, Arthur and Steve successfully deliver the gift, and Sophie returns home with a newfound appreciation for the magic of Christmas. Meanwhile, Santa is forced to come out of retirement and help his sons on their mission, proving that he still has what it takes to be a great Santa Claus.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and colorful, with a mix of traditional and computer-generated imagery. The voice cast, including James McAvoy as Arthur, Hugh Laurie as Steve, and Bill Nighy as Santa, brings the characters to life in a way that is both humorous and heartwarming.

Overall, Arthur Christmas is a delightful holiday film that celebrates the spirit of giving and the importance of family. With its witty humor, lovable characters, and stunning animation, it's a must-see for families around the world.

documents.title: Winnie the Pooh
documents.tagline: Oh Pooh.
documents.overview: During an ordinary day in Hundred Acre Wood, Winnie the Pooh sets out to find some honey. Misinterpreting a note from Christopher Robin, Owl convinces Pooh, Tigger, Rabbit, Piglet, Kanga, Roo, and Eeyore that their young friend has been captured by a creature named "Backson" and they set out to rescue him.
documents.plot: During an ordinary day in Hundred Acre Wood, Winnie the Pooh sets out to find some honey. Misinterpreting a note from Christopher Robin, Owl convinces Pooh, Tigger, Rabbit, Piglet, Kanga, Roo, and Eeyore that their young friend has been captured by a creature named "Backson" and they set out to rescue him.

documents.title: Open Season 3
documents.tagline: Boog and Elliot are Back and the Fur is Going to Fly!
documents.overview: Boog, Elliot, and their forest friends return with an all-new adventure, this time in a Big Top Circus! The comedy begins when Boog's pals choose their family obligations over the annual guy's trip, and a disappointed Boog decides to take a trip of his own, which leads him right into the middle of a circus ring...literally. When he switches places with a devious look-a-like circus grizzly and falls for an alluring Russian troupe member, he'll come to realize that maybe you don't have to choose between family and friendship after all.
