The comedy begins when Boog's pals choose their family obligations over the annual guy's trip, and a disappointed Boog decides to take a trip of his own, which leads him right into the middle of a circus ring...literally. When he switches places with a devious look-a-like circus grizzly and falls for an alluring Russian troupe member, he'll come to realize that maybe you don't have to choose between family and friendship after all.

documents.title: Donkey's Christmas Shrektacular
documents.overview: Deck the halls with Donkey’s laughter in this all-new holiday collection. Donkey presents his very own carolling stage show featuring his Far Far Away pals in this merry, musical treat with all the trimmings! Join in the fun as they bring their own Shrektacular spirit to festive holiday songs, a fun Donkey Decoration scramble, and a hilarious virtual Yule Log that’s so funny… it’s on fire.
documents.plot:
Donkey's Christmas Shrektacular, whose short is also titled Donkey's Caroling Christmas-tacular, is a 2010 American computer-animated musical holiday short from DreamWorks Animation, set in the world of the Shrek films. Directed by Walt Dohrn, with Raman Hui also credited as co-director in some sources, and written by Dohrn and Ryan Crego, it was produced by Gina Shay, Teresa Cheng and Chad Hammes with music by Matt Mahaffey. It was released on 7 December 2010 as a bonus holiday DVD packaged with the home release of Shrek Forever After, and as a special feature on that film's Blu-ray.

The short takes place in the Candy Apple, the friendly new incarnation of the Poison Apple tavern, where Donkey hosts a Christmas party and persuades everyone to join him in a caroling stage show. He opens with "It's the Most Wonderful Time of the Year" alongside his fairy-tale friends. Shrek, who surprises everyone by agreeing to sing, joins Fiona, their three ogre children and the ogre army in a gleefully gross ogre version of "Jingle Bells", with lyrics about bug cocoons and cricket slurps. Puss in Boots follows with "Fleas Navidad", a take on "Feliz Navidad" that he claims is a classic from his village, and the whole company closes with "Fairy Tale Rock", a rendition of "Jingle Bell Rock". Running gags in the background include Gingy trying to rescue lifeless gingerbread cookies, the Three Little Pigs preparing for swimsuit weather and Rumpelstiltskin trapped in a cage.

Eddie Murphy returns as Donkey, after being replaced by Dean Edwards in Scared Shrekless, alongside Mike Myers as Shrek, Cameron Diaz as Fiona and Antonio Banderas as Puss. Walt Dohrn voices Rumpelstiltskin, Jon Hamm the ogre Brogan, Cody Cameron Pinocchio and the pigs, Conrad Vernon Gingy and Aron Warner the Big Bad Wolf, with Craig Robinson and Jane Lynch also among the ogres. It was the last Shrek production to reunite the core original cast until Shrek 5.

The holiday disc rounds out the main short with a Donkey decoration game and Shrek's Yule Log, a half-hour virtual fireplace in Shrek's house in which characters such as Rumpelstiltskin, Puss, Fiona and Gingy wander through with festive gags.

documents.title: Mean Girls 2
documents.tagline: The Plastics are back!
documents.overview: After a clique of girls makes life difficult, a new student forms a rival group to take control of the school's corridors.
documents.plot:
Mean Girls 2 is a 2011 American teen comedy TV film directed by Melanie Mayron from a script by Cliff Ruby, Elana Lesser and Allison Schroeder. A sequel to the 2004 film Mean Girls, it stars Meaghan Martin as Jo Mitchell, Maiara Walsh as Mandi Weatherly, Jennifer Stone as Abby Hanover, Nicole Gale Anderson, Claire Holt, Diego Boneta as Tyler and Linden Ashby, with Tim Meadows returning as Principal Ron Duvall.

Jo, a tomboy who has changed schools many times because of her father's work rebuilding NASCAR engines, arrives at North Shore High School in Ohio hoping to get into Carnegie Mellon, which her late mother attended. There she meets the Plastics, a clique led by Mandi, with the airheaded Chastity and the germ-phobic Hope. Jo befriends Mandi's outcast rival Abby, and the two are drawn into a prank war. Abby's wealthy father offers to pay Jo's college tuition if she stays friends with his daughter, and Jo reluctantly agrees. She falls for Tyler, a classmate from shop class, and the group gains Quinn, a student journalist. Mandi bugs the car Tyler borrows for a date in order to humiliate Jo, who then learns that Tyler is Mandi's stepbrother.

The feud escalates: Mandi tries to wreck Jo's Carnegie Mellon prospects and sabotages one of her father's engines. When Mandi plans her invitation-only birthday party, Jo throws an open party for Abby on the same night. The Plastics lace Abby's pizza with ipecac, but Jo hides it and later hands a slice to Mandi's boyfriend Nick, who vomits on Mandi. Jo, Abby and Quinn form the "Anti-Plastics", and Jo challenges Mandi for homecoming queen, but Jo realises she is becoming just like Mandi and tries to return the money. Mandi learns of the arrangement and persuades Quinn to expose it in the school paper, straining Jo's friendship with Abby. Mandi and Nick then steal the homecoming charity money meant for an animal shelter and plant it in Jo's shed, getting her expelled. Jo challenges Mandi to flag football. Learning that Jo was probably framed, Tyler and Abby recruit the tech-savvy Elliott, who finds video of the theft and sends it to the whole school. The Anti-Plastics win the game, Mandi and Nick are arrested, Jo is allowed to graduate, and she and Abby go on to Carnegie Mellon together.

Shot in Atlanta over twenty days in July 2010 the film premiered on ABC Family on January 23, 2011, and came out on DVD a month later. Reviews were negative; Entertainment Weekly saw it as a cheap remake of the original.

documents.title: Horrible Bosses
documents.tagline: Ever wish your boss was dead?
documents.overview: For Nick, Kurt and Dale, the only thing that would make the daily grind more tolerable would be to grind their intolerable bosses into dust. Quitting is not an option, so, with the benefit of a few-too-many drinks and some dubious advice from a hustling ex-con, the three friends devise a convoluted and seemingly foolproof plan to rid themselves of their respective employers... permanently.
documents.plot:
Nick Hendricks, Dale Arbus, and Kurt Buckman are friends working in Riverside, California, who despise their bosses: Nick works at a financial firm for the sadistic Dave Harken, who hints at a possible promotion for Nick for months, only to award it to himself; Dale is a dental assistant being sexually harassed by his boss, Dr. Julia Harris, who threatens to tell his fiancée Stacy that he had sex with her unless he actually has sex with her; Kurt enjoys working for the kind-hearted Jack Pellit at his chemical company, but after Jack unexpectedly dies of a heart attack, the company is taken over by Jack's arrogant, cocaine-addicted son Bobby, whose apathy and incompetence threaten the future of the company.
One night, over drinks, Kurt jokingly suggests that their lives would be happier if their bosses were no longer alive. Initially hesitant, they eventually agree to kill their bosses. In search of a hitman, the trio meet Dean "Motherfucker" Jones, an ex-con who offers to be their "murder consultant." Jones suggests that they kill each other's bosses to hide their motives, while making the deaths look like accidents.
The trio sneak into Bobby's house, and Kurt steals his phone. They next go to Harken's house, where Kurt and Nick go inside while Dale waits in the car as a lookout. Harken returns home and confronts Dale for littering, and then has an allergic reaction from the peanut butter on the litter. Dale saves him by stabbing him with an EpiPen, but Nick and Kurt think he is stabbing Harken to death and flee, with Kurt accidentally dropping Bobby's phone in Harken's bedroom.
The next night, Kurt watches Julia's home, but she seduces and has sex with him. Nick and Dale wait outside Bobby's and Harken's houses, respectively, to commit the murders, but are hesitant to follow through. Harken discovers Bobby's phone in his bedroom and uses it to find his address, suspecting his wife, Rhonda, is having an affair with Bobby. Harken drives over and shoots Bobby dead, while Nick secretly witnesses the murder.
Nick flees at high speed, setting off a traffic camera. The trio meet at a bar and plan to leave the police an anonymous tip to get Harken arrested. However, the police bring them in for questioning, as the camera footage makes Nick the prime suspect in Bobby's murder.
Dale points out that they lack sufficient evidence to hold them there, forcing the police to release them. However, the trio are warned that forensics is sweeping the house for DNA, so they realize the prank Kurt pulled during their first break-in has left enough evidence to convict them. The trio consult with Jones again, but learn that he never actually killed anyone or committed any felonies, having been imprisoned for only bootlegging a film. Jones suggests that they get Harken to confess and secretly tape it.

documents.title: Prom
documents.tagline: There are hundreds of nights in high school, but there’s only one prom.
documents.overview: At “Prom,” every couple has a story and no two are exactly alike. As the big dance approaches for Nova Prescott, it’s a battle of wills as she finds herself drawn to the guy who gets in the way of her perfect prom. Fellow seniors Mei and Tyler harbor secrets, while others face all the insecurity and anticipation that surrounds one of high school’s most seminal events.
documents.plot:
Prom is a 2011 American teen romantic comedy directed by Joe Nussbaum, written by Katie Wech and produced by Ted Griffin and Justin Springer for Walt Disney Pictures. Aimee Teegarden stars as Nova Prescott and Thomas McDonell as Jesse Richter, with Danielle Campbell as Simone, Nolan Sotillo as Lucas, DeVaughn Nixon as Tyler, Kylie Bunbury as Jordan and Nicholas Braun as Lloyd. It follows students at a Michigan high school before their prom.

Nova, on the prom committee, hopes her crush Brandon will ask her to the dance. Mei fears telling her boyfriend Justin she got into a different university. Shy Lucas wants to ask his lab partner Simone, and Lloyd cannot find a date at all. When the popular Tyler takes his girlfriend Jordan on a candlelit date in the shed where the prom decorations are stored, a candle left burning sets it on fire. Nova must rebuild everything, and the principal tells Jesse, a disrespectful student indifferent to prom, to help her or not graduate. The two reluctantly begin working together, and as Brandon fails to ask her out, Nova grows closer to Jesse. A spying mission at a rival school ends with police catching them.

As Lucas courts Simone, Tyler, who has been cheating on Jordan, begins pursuing her too. Simone surprises Lucas with concert tickets, and he drops his friend Corey to take her, but after Jordan dumps Tyler, Tyler asks Simone to prom that night, and she accepts. Mei finally tells Justin the truth, and he is proud of her. Nova admits to her friends that she has feelings for Jesse, but her father, who overhears, tells Jesse he is dragging her down and must not ask her to prom. On prom night, Lucas begs Simone not to go, then makes amends by taking Corey to the concert. Nova learns what her father did and storms out, while Jesse's mother persuades him to go after her. At the dance, Tyler abandons Simone, who leaves to dance with Lucas outside. As a heartbroken Nova is about to leave, the broken fountain springs back to life; Jesse has fixed it, and he asks her to prom.

Disney developed the film after the success of High School Musical 3, in the vein of John Hughes, with a modest budget and newcomers. Shot in Los Angeles, it was the first major release filmed on Arri Alexa cameras. Released on April 29, 2011, it opened fifth and grossed $10.1 million domestically. Reviews were mixed to negative. Rotten Tomatoes reported 36% approval, calling it more nuanced and less cynical than expected but just as corny and clichéd.

documents.title: The Man from Nowhere
documents.tagline: Nothing to lose, nothing to compromise.
documents.overview: His only friend called him 'the man from nowhere'... Taesik, a former special agent becomes a loner after losing his wife in a miserable accident and lives a bitter life running a pawnshop. He only has a few customers and a friend named Somi, a little girl next door. As Taesik spends more and more time with Somi, he gets attached to her. Then Somi is kidnapped by a gang, and as Taesik tries to save Somi by becoming deeply associated with the gang his mysterious past is revealed.
documents.plot:
Cha Tae-sik is a quiet man running a pawnshop. His only friend is So-mi, a little girl living next door. So-mi's mother Hyo-jeong is a go-go dancer and opium addict. Instructed by her lover, Hyo-jeong steals a large pack of opium being sold at the bar where she works and hides it in a camera bag, which she pawns to Tae-sik for safekeeping. Drug lord Oh Myung-gyu tasks his subordinate brothers, Man-seok and Jong-seok, with retrieving the opium. Jong-seok locates Hyo-jeong and tortures her in front of So-mi until she reveals the location of the drugs.
Jong-seok's lackeys Du-chi and Bear go to the pawnshop, but Tae-sik easily overpowers them. Holding So-mi hostage, Jong-seok forces Tae-sik to deliver the opium to Myung-gyu. Man-seok, tired of working for his brother, informs the police, but Myung-gyu evades arrest. Tae-sik is arrested after discovering Hyo-jeong's body, with her organs harvested, in the trunk of his car. Tae-sik escapes from the police station, alarming them with his display of combat skills. Upon further investigation, the officers discover that Tae-sik was a former covert operative for South Korean Army Intelligence, but retired after an assassin killed his pregnant wife.
The brothers track down Hyo-jeong's lover and kill him, while the brothers' bodyguard Ramrowan kills Myung-gyu, thus allowing the brothers to take over his operations. Following a lead from the burner phone Jong-seok gave him, Tae-sik tracks Du-chi to a nightclub. As Tae-sik asks about the brothers, Ramrowan walks in and shoots at them, killing Du-chi and wounding Tae-sik. Tae-sik escapes and finds his former partner, who gives Tae-sik medical care and helps him acquire a gun. Tae-sik goes back to the city and discovers a drug manufacturing plant; in the process of destroying it, he kills Jong-seok and frees the enslaved child workers.
Tae-sik confronts Man-seok's gang at his condominium. Claiming that he had So-mi's eyes harvested, Man-seok shows Tae-sik a container with two preserved eyeballs. Enraged, Tae-sik brutally kills the gang members, including Ramrowan and Man-seok. As Tae-sik prepares to commit suicide out of grief, a dirty but unharmed So-mi finds him. Ramrowan, who took pity on her because she had been kind to him, had spared her life—the eyes in the container belonged to the gangsters' surgeon. The police allow Tae-sik and So-mi to ride together after Tae-sik's arrest. When So-mi falls asleep, Tae-sik asks them to stop at a small convenience store where he buys a backpack along with other school supplies. Tae-sik tells So-mi that she is going to be on her own as the police have to take him away. Before leaving, Tae-sik asks her for a hug and breaks down in tears as they embrace.

documents.title: Death Race 2
documents.tagline: 10 killer drivers, 20,000 rounds of ammo. 1 survivor.
documents.overview: In the world's most dangerous prison, a new game is born: Death Race. The rules of this adrenaline-fueled blood sport are simple, drive or die. When repentant convict Carl Lucas discovers there's a price on his head, his only hope is to survive a twisted race against an army of hardened criminals and tricked-out cars.
documents.plot:
A gang robs a bank on behalf of crime boss Markus Kane. When two police officers unexpectedly enter the building, getaway driver Carl "Luke" Lucas urges his accomplices to abort the robbery, but they refuse. Luke intervenes, resulting in the death of one of the robbers. He then kills a police officer and abandons the remaining accomplices to complete Markus's plan. After a high-speed chase, Luke is captured, sentenced to life in prison, and eventually transferred to Terminal Island. Markus, convinced Luke will trade information for immunity despite Luke's vow of silence, orders his assassination.
Terminal Island is a for-profit, maximum-security prison operated by business magnate R. H. Weyland of Weyland Corporation. One of Weyland's primary revenue streams is "Death Match", a televised, pay-per-view gladiatorial combat event in which inmates fight using weapons or improvised defensive gear. September Jones, a disgraced former Miss Universe now employed by Weyland, hosts the spectacle.
Upon arrival, Luke befriends fellow inmates "Lists", Goldberg, and Rocco. He draws September's attention after defending Lists from an attempted assault. September makes sexual advances toward Luke and pressures him to participate in a Death Match in exchange for privileges, but he refuses. In retaliation, she selects Lists to fight "Big Bill", the massive prisoner who attacked Luke earlier. Luke jumps into the arena to protect Lists, briefly aided by convict ring girl Katrina Banks. Racial tensions escalate, sparking a riot as prisoners flood the arena and attempt to rape the female inmates. Katrina fights back, and the women are evacuated. Guards regain control, Luke surrenders, and afterward, he speaks privately with Katrina. Learning Luke is still alive, Markus places a $1 million bounty on his head.
Seeking greater profits, September launches a new event called "Death Race". Inmates can earn their freedom by winning five races over three days, driving heavily armed, reinforced cars. Female prisoners serve as navigators. Luke enters the race with Katrina as his navigator and Lists, Goldberg, and Rocco as his pit crew. Luke wins the first race and is congratulated by Weyland, who offers Katrina as his prize. Alone together, Luke and Katrina tease each other and have sex. Later, September places Luke in solitary confinement under the guise of protecting him from bounty hunters. Katrina is taken to Markus, who offers her freedom in exchange for killing Luke.
During the second race, nearly all competitors target Luke, except for triad member "14K", whom Luke previously saved. Katrina tells Luke about Markus's offer. Near the end of the race, Luke's car malfunctions due to sabotage. He ejects Katrina before the vehicle is struck by Big Bill's heat-seeking missile. Luke's pit crew and Katrina are unable to rescue him from the burning wreck. Meanwhile, Big Bill's navigator kills her partner after he murders his pit crew and attacks her.

documents.title: Bloomington
documents.overview: A former child actress attends college in search of independence and ends up becoming romantically involved with a female professor. Their relationship thrives until an opportunity to return to acting forces her to make life-altering decisions.
documents.plot:
Bloomington is a 2010 independent coming-of-age drama written and directed by Fernanda Cardoso, filmed in Indianapolis, Indiana, and Los Angeles. It follows a former child actress who goes to college seeking independence and becomes romantically involved with a female professor, a relationship tested when the younger woman is offered a chance to return to acting.

Jackie Kirk, once the star of a television series, enrolls at a college in Bloomington, Indiana, where her classmates are in awe of her acting past and she tries to fit in as an ordinary student. At an on-campus mixer she meets Catherine Stark, a lesbian professor who has noticed her, and the two begin a secret affair that would cause a scandal if discovered. The relationship draws Jackie away from campus social life as the two women grow closer and help each other discover more about themselves.

When Jackie is suddenly offered the chance to return to acting, Catherine becomes uneasy, believing they would always have to hide what they are to each other. She pulls away, insisting they were never in a real relationship and that Jackie is not worth the risk, while Jackie argues that Catherine is. Jackie also clashes with her classmate Sandy, who resents her for competing for a scholarship she does not need and believes the affair has earned her special treatment. After Jackie slaps her, Sandy punches her in the face. The next day Jackie turns up at Catherine's door with a black eye, and Catherine hurries her inside as photographers take pictures. Learning that Catherine is going to a party with an unnamed date, Jackie insults her by suggesting she cannot support herself. When Catherine comes home with a man and takes him to her bedroom, Jackie leaves for a party with her own friends and flirts with a friend named Zach. After Jackie departs for Los Angeles to film a new movie based on her old series, the affair is partly exposed and Catherine loses her job. Months later the two spend one last night together and say a formal goodbye, and Jackie returns to California and her new role.

Allison McAtee plays Catherine and Sarah Stouffer plays Jackie, with Erika Heidewald as Sandy, Ray Zupp as Zach and Katherine Ann McGregor as Lillian. Reviews were mixed. AfterEllen called it a sexy, offbeat and fantastic little drama, while Autostraddle complained that its issues were left unresolved and that it lacked subtlety.

documents.title: The Secret World of Arrietty
documents.original_title: 借りぐらしのアリエッティ
documents.tagline: Do not be seen by humans. That's been the law of children of the underfloor.
documents.overview: 14-year-old Arrietty and the rest of the Clock family live in peaceful anonymity as they make their own home from items "borrowed" from the house's human inhabitants. However, life changes for the Clocks when a human boy discovers Arrietty.
documents.plot:
The Secret World of Arrietty is a 2010 Japanese animated fantasy film directed by Hiromasa Yonebayashi, based on the novel "The Borrowers" by Mary Norton. The movie follows the story of an 11-year-old boy named Sho and his relationship with a young girl named Arrietty.

In post-war Japan, Sho lives in a small house with his father, who is a widower. One day, while exploring the attic, Sho discovers a tiny door that leads to a secret world inhabited by the Borrowers, a family of tiny people who live in the walls and floors of houses. The Borrowers are skilled at "borrowing" small items from humans, which they use to survive.

Arrietty, the protagonist, is the daughter of the Borrower family. She is curious and adventurous, but also kind and gentle. Sho befriends Arrietty, who borrows a spoon from him, and they begin to communicate through notes and drawings. As their friendship grows, Sho learns about the world of the Borrowers and their struggles to survive in a human-dominated society.

However, their friendship is threatened by the Borrower family's need to borrow more and more items from humans, which puts them at risk of being discovered. The Borrowers' leader, Pod Clock, is determined to find a way to live safely among humans, but his methods are often reckless and put the entire family in danger.

As Sho and Arrietty spend more time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their social differences make it difficult for them to express their emotions. Meanwhile, Sho's father is struggling to come to terms with his own grief and loneliness after the loss of his wife.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when the Borrower family is discovered by a human, who threatens to expose their secret world to the outside world. Arrietty must make a difficult decision to save her family and protect Sho's friendship, while also considering the consequences of revealing the existence of the Borrowers to humans.

In the end, Sho and Arrietty find a way to resolve their differences and come up with a plan to coexist peacefully. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Sho and Arrietty looking forward to a future where they can live together in harmony.

The Secret World of Arrietty is a beautifully animated film that explores themes of friendship, love, and acceptance. The movie's attention to detail and its imaginative world-building make it a delight to watch, while its thoughtful portrayal of complex emotions and relationships makes it a relatable and engaging story for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: One Day
documents.tagline: Twenty years. Two people.
documents.overview: A romantic comedy centered on Dexter and Emma, who first meet during their graduation in 1988 and proceed to keep in touch regularly. The film follows what they do on July 15 annually, usually doing something together.
documents.plot:
One Day is a 2011 romantic drama directed by Lone Scherfig, with a screenplay by David Nicholls adapted from his 2009 novel. It stars Anne Hathaway and Jim Sturgess as two friends whose relationship is traced through a single date, St. Swithin's Day, 15 July, over twenty years, with Patricia Clarkson, Ken Stott and Romola Garai in supporting roles.

Emma Morley, from a working-class northern family, and Dexter Mayhew, a privileged Winchester-educated southerner, spend a chaste night together after graduating from Edinburgh University in 1988 and agree to stay friends. Emma moves to London hoping to write but ends up waitressing in a Mexican restaurant, where she meets the would-be comedian Ian, while Dexter drifts abroad, teaching English in Paris. On a 1992 holiday in Dinard, Emma rebuffs him because he will not commit. Dexter becomes a brash late-night television host, arrives drunk to see his terminally ill mother, who tells him he is not yet a nice person, and grows increasingly obnoxious; Emma, now a teacher living unhappily with Ian, breaks with him in 1996 after a coke-fuelled dinner at which he mocks her profession, saying she loves but no longer likes him. By the late 1990s Dexter's career has collapsed and he is with Sylvie, while Emma leaves Ian, who nonetheless urges her to publish her stories. Reconciled at a friend's wedding in 2000, Emma has a book deal and Dexter is engaged to a pregnant Sylvie, who later cheats on him with his old friend Callum. In 2003 Dexter visits Emma, now a successful author in Paris; she chases after him, and they finally become a couple, marry and try for a child while he runs a café. In 2006 Emma is killed by a lorry while cycling. Dexter spirals, but is eventually steadied by his daughter Jasmine, his father, Sylvie and even Ian. In 2011 he climbs Arthur's Seat with Jasmine, and a flashback returns to the day after they first met in 1988.

Hathaway plays Emma and Sturgess plays Dexter, with Clarkson and Stott as his parents, Garai as Sylvie and Rafe Spall as Ian. A Random House Films and Focus Features production co-financed by Film4, it was shot from July 2010 in Edinburgh, London and Brittany. Focus released it in the US on 19 August 2011. Reviews were largely negative, at 36% on Rotten Tomatoes, though Roger Ebert praised its wit; Hathaway's Yorkshire accent drew particular criticism.

documents.title: Trigun: Badlands Rumble
documents.original_title: トライガン バッドランド ランブル
documents.overview: In a quicksand surrounded town called Makka, rumors spread of a legendary robber named Gasback is after the town. To protect it, Mayor Kepler has hired bounty hunters. These hunters have been following Gasback from town to town in hopes of getting the bounty. Vash the Stampede is in town, along with Meryl and Milly, along with the female bounty hunter Amelia and Nicholas D. Wolfwood.
documents.plot:
Trigun: Badlands Rumble is a 2010 Japanese animated science fiction action film directed by Satoshi Nishimura and produced by Madhouse, based on Yasuhiro Nightow's manga Trigun. It follows the gunman Vash the Stampede as he arrives in a city where bounty hunters have gathered to claim a huge reward on the robber Gasback. The film was Hiromi Tsuru's final performance as the insurance agent Meryl Stryfe before her death in 2017.

Twenty years before the story, Gasback's gang robs a bank and then betrays him; their leader, Cain, shoots him and leaves him for the police. Vash stops Gasback from killing his former partners, and Gasback escapes to continue his career of crime. In the present, Cain is mayor of Macca City, having used his loot to upgrade its power plant and erect a bronze statue of himself. He insures the statue with the Bernardelli Insurance Society, which sends Meryl and Milly Thompson to protect it, and the city fills with bounty hunters expecting Gasback to strike. Vash helps a young woman, Amelia, fend off thugs, but she scorns his flirting. Gasback, meanwhile, is guarded by Nicholas D. Wolfwood, who owes him his life but refuses to take part in his robberies, and he destroys the businesses of his other former accomplices.

When the bounty hunters give up and leave, Gasback fights his way into Cain's mansion. In the standoff, Cain shoots his old associates, and Amelia learns that Vash let Gasback escape two decades earlier. Vash lets Gasback go again, and the robber detaches the city's power plant and hauls it away, crushing Cain's statue. Pursuing Gasback to kill him, Amelia is followed by Vash, who is shot and vanishes into quicksand, but he survives thanks to a piece of tough smoked meat in his coat and is rescued by Meryl and Milly. In a final duel, Gasback unleashes an electrical weapon against Vash, and Amelia blocks it with a glove that he recognizes as one he made for his wife. Amelia is his daughter, born after he abandoned her mother, who died in poverty and shunned for her connection to him. Embracing Vash's ideals, Amelia spares her father. Gasback, his gang and his former accomplices are arrested, and the plant is restored to the city. Vash and Wolfwood set off across the desert after a new group of outlaws.

The film had its North American premiere at Sakura-Con in Seattle on April 2, 2010, and debuted at number fourteen on ten screens. Funimation later licensed it for English-language release.

documents.title: Limitless
documents.tagline: What if a pill could make you rich and powerful?
documents.overview: A paranoia-fueled action thriller about an unsuccessful writer whose life is transformed by a top-secret "smart drug" that allows him to use 100% of his brain and become a perfect version of himself. His enhanced abilities soon attract shadowy forces that threaten his new life in this darkly comic and provocative film.
documents.plot:
Limitless is a 2011 science fiction thriller film directed by Neil Burger and written by Luke Evans and Eric Warren Singer. The movie stars Bradley Cooper, Robert De Niro, and Abbie Cornish.

The story follows Eddie Morra (played by Bradley Cooper), a struggling writer who works as a janitor at a publishing company in New York City. One day, while cleaning up after a party, Eddie stumbles upon a mysterious pill that he finds on the floor. The pill is labeled "NZT-48" and is produced by the pharmaceutical company PerkinReidy.

Eddie takes the pill, which gives him an extraordinary boost of intelligence, memory, and cognitive abilities. He becomes incredibly intelligent, able to learn new information at an incredible rate, and his memory expands exponentially. Eddie's newfound abilities allow him to excel in his job as a writer, and he quickly becomes a successful author.

However, Eddie soon realizes that the pill has a dark side effect: it slowly kills him over time. As the days pass, Eddie's body begins to deteriorate, and he must find a way to reverse the effects of the NZT-48 before it's too late.

Eddie's newfound abilities also attract the attention of the pharmaceutical company PerkinReidy, which wants to exploit his brain for their own gain. The company's CEO, Carl Van Loon (played by Robert De Niro), will stop at nothing to get Eddie to work for them and help develop a new line of NZT-based products.

As Eddie navigates this treacherous world, he meets Sarah (played by Abbie Cornish), a beautiful and intelligent woman who becomes his love interest. Together, they try to uncover the truth about the NZT-48 pill and its effects on Eddie's body.

Throughout the movie, Eddie's character undergoes significant development as he struggles with the consequences of his newfound abilities. He must confront the darker aspects of his own personality and the moral implications of using a powerful substance like NZT-48 to enhance his cognitive abilities.

The movie builds towards a thrilling climax as Eddie and Sarah try to outsmart Van Loon and his henchmen, who will stop at nothing to get their hands on Eddie's brain. In the end, Eddie must make a choice between saving himself or using his abilities to help others.

Overall, Limitless is a gripping sci-fi thriller that explores themes of identity, morality, and the consequences of playing with fire when it comes to human cognition. The movie features impressive performances from its cast, particularly Bradley Cooper, who brings depth and nuance to Eddie's character.

documents.title: Oscar and the Lady in Pink
documents.overview: Listening in to a conversation between his doctor and parents, 10-year-old Oscar learns what nobody has the courage to tell him. He only has a few weeks to live. Furious, he refuses to speak to anyone except straight-talking Rose, the lady in pink he meets on the hospital stairs. As Christmas approaches, Rose uses her fantastical experiences as a professional wrestler, her imagination, wit and charm to allow Oscar to live life and love to the full, in the company of his friends Pop Corn, Einstein, Bacon and childhood sweetheart Peggy Blue. Written by American Film Market

documents.title: Robot Chicken: Star Wars Episode III
documents.original_title: Robot Chicken: Star Wars Episode III
documents.overview: Robot Chicken: Star Wars Episode III, directed by Chris McKay, combines the satirical sensibilities of Green and Matthew Senreich's Robot Chicken with characters of the Star Wars universe.
documents.plot: Millions of years from now, after Socrates, Shakespeare and the bible are long forgotten, only two great works will remain: the sci-fi cinema epic Star Wars and Adult Swim's stop-motion animated, cheap gag extravanganza Robot Chicken. And now, for the first time, they come together for the third time, in this all new special. That's right, all your mot beloved Star Wars characters are going back through the comedy meat grinder.

documents.title: Romantics Anonymous
documents.overview: What happens when a man and a woman share a common passion? They fall in love. And this is what happens to Jean-René, the boss of a small chocolate factory, and Angélique, a gifted chocolate maker he has just hired. What occurs when a highly emotional man meets a highly emotional woman? They fall in love, and this is what occurs to Jean-René and Angélique who share the same handicap. But being pathologically timid does not make things easy for them. So whether they will manage to get together, join their solitudes and live happily ever after is a guessing matter.
documents.plot: With his beloved chocolate business turning sour, socially awkward boss Jean-René decides to enlist an extra pair of hands. Enter Angélique, a chronically shy young woman who shares Jean- René's passion for all things sugar and sweet. She is the answer to his prayers, in ways he didn t realise. Because while he is looking for a sales rep to keep his sinking ship afloat, she is in fact a gifted, albeit covert, chocolatière extraordinaire whose treats are legendary around town. As the pair become more and more acquainted it is not long before chocolate is not the only sensual element in the air.

documents.title: Perfect Sense
documents.tagline: Without love there is nothing
documents.overview: In Glasgow, Scotland, while a mysterious pandemic begins to spread around the world, Susan, a brilliant epidemiologist, falls in love with Michael, a skillful cook.

documents.title: Ultramarines: A Warhammer 40,000 Movie
documents.tagline: In the grim darkness of the far future there is only war.
documents.overview: A squad of Ultramarines answer a distress call from an Imperial Shrine World. A full Company of Imperial Fists was stationed there, but there is no answer from them. The squad investigates to find out what has happened there.
documents.plot:
The film opens with footage from the planet Mithron with a group of Space Marines of the Imperial Fists Chapter under attack from an unknown enemy. A Space Marine by the name of Nidon is told to protect "the Codex" and races to obey his orders, just before a fireball engulfs them all. Elsewhere, aboard a Space Marine Strike Cruiser, Brother Proteus and Captain Severus of the Ultramarines Chapter's 2nd Company spar in a training duel. Proteus manages to disarm Severus; however, he quickly escapes Proteus's grasp and in turn defeats him, proclaiming that a Space Marine never yields. Following this, Proteus and the other newly initiated members of the 2nd Company's Ultima Squad are then shown a sacred weapon in their ship's reclusium, a Relic Thunder Hammer. The Captain and his right-hand man, Apothecary Pythol, lead the initiates in a swearing-in ceremony on the Hammer. With the ceremony finished, Ultima Squad prepare themselves for their first mission as a squad—a sortie to the planet of Mithron.
In orbit above the planet, Captain Severus departs the cruiser with only Pythol and the ten-strong Ultima Squad as support, all of whom are highly eager to prove themselves in battle finally. En route to the planet's surface, Severus addresses the squad, informing them of the distress call received shortly before all contact with the planet was lost, and how it is still unclear whether it is automated or not. Soon enough, they arrive on the tough and unforgiving desert surface of Mithron, and head in the direction of the only location of importance on the planet: a shrine guarded by a full company of one hundred Marines from the Imperial Fists. En route to the shrine, Proteus senses something shadowing them and opens fire on it, but when the others fail to find any evidence of their supposed pursuer, they quickly dismiss his concerns as just nerves, something which Proteus denies. Soon afterward though, Ultima Squad discovers that a terrible battle has indeed taken place, with the garrison force annihilated and the planet's Imperial shrine desecrated. It is also evident that the forces of Chaos are responsible, and against Pythol's advice to retreat, Severus decides they must continue the mission to search for any remaining survivors.
While approaching the ruins, the Ultramarines are ambushed by the Black Legion. Three of the Ultramarines (squad leader Veteran Sergeant Crastor, Brother Lycos, and Brother Boreas) are killed, but the ambush is thwarted. The squad then continues on, and eventually makes it inside the shrine. While traveling through a dark passage, though, they are attacked by a Daemon Prince, which kills Brother Maxillius and grapples with Severus, causing them both to fall through a wall and down a ravine. With Severus gone and Crastor dead, command of the squad then falls to Proteus, who decides to continue with the mission.

documents.title: Julia's Eyes
documents.tagline: You can't hide in the dark
documents.overview: The story of a woman who is slowly losing her sight whilst trying to investigate the mysterious death of her twin sister.
documents.plot:
Julia's Eyes (Spanish: Los ojos de Julia) is a 2010 Spanish psychological horror thriller film directed by Guillem Morales and written by Morales and Oriol Paulo. Belén Rueda stars in the dual role of Julia and her twin sister, Sara, with Lluís Homar as Julia's husband, Isaac, Pablo Derqui, Joan Dalmau and Clara Segura. The film was produced by Guillermo del Toro, Joaquín Padró and Mar Targarona.

In the opening scene, Sara, a blind woman tormented by an unseen presence, prepares to hang herself in her basement but changes her mind; as she tries to remove the noose, the stool is kicked away from beneath her. Far away, Julia, who suffers from the same degenerative eye disease as her sister but can still see, collapses, sensing that something is wrong. Refusing to believe that Sara killed herself, particularly since she had been awaiting surgery that might restore her sight, Julia begins to investigate, despite the objections of Isaac, who has learned from a doctor that Sara's operation had failed.

Julia meets Sara's blind elderly neighbor, Soledad, who predicts that Isaac will leave her, just as Soledad's own son abandoned her after she lost her sight. Learning that Sara had a mysterious boyfriend, Julia follows the trail to a nearby hotel, where an elderly janitor warns her of people who live in the shadows and are so ignored that they become invisible. Soon after, Isaac vanishes, and Julia becomes convinced that the same unseen figure who stalked Sara has taken him, though the police are skeptical. As witnesses connected to the case begin to die, Julia's eyesight deteriorates rapidly under the stress, forcing her to undergo an operation of her own. Recovering with her eyes bandaged and dependent on a caregiver, she becomes increasingly vulnerable to the presence she has been hunting, and must uncover the identity of the invisible man before she loses her sight completely.

Julia's Eyes received mostly positive reviews, with 90 percent of 39 critics on Rotten Tomatoes giving it a favorable review; the consensus called it a smart, suspenseful and visually distinctive Spanish thriller. Philip French of The Guardian commented on its use of blindness as both a plot device and a metaphor, and critics praised Rueda's performance and Morales's stylish direction.

documents.title: The Three Musketeers
documents.tagline: Every legend has a new beginning.
documents.overview: The hot-headed young D'Artagnan along with three former legendary but now down on their luck Musketeers must unite and defeat a beautiful double agent and her villainous employer from seizing the French throne and engulfing Europe in war.
documents.plot:
The Three Musketeers is a 2011 period action-adventure film directed by Paul W. S. Anderson, a loose adaptation of Alexandre Dumas's 1844 novel adding fantastical airships. Logan Lerman stars as D'Artagnan, with Matthew Macfadyen, Ray Stevenson and Luke Evans as the musketeers Athos, Porthos and Aramis, Milla Jovovich as Milady de Winter, Mads Mikkelsen as Rochefort, Orlando Bloom as the Duke of Buckingham and Christoph Waltz as Cardinal Richelieu.

In Venice, the musketeers Athos, Porthos and Aramis, aided by Milady de Winter, steal Leonardo da Vinci's designs for a flying warship, only for Milady to betray them and sell the plans to the Duke of Buckingham. A year later, the young D'Artagnan leaves Gascony for Paris, hoping to become a musketeer like his father, only to find that the regiment has been disbanded. After a humiliating encounter with Rochefort, the captain of Cardinal Richelieu's guard, he unwittingly offends Athos, Porthos and Aramis and arranges to duel each of them, but when Richelieu's guards interrupt, the four fight side by side. Summoned before the young King Louis XIII, they are honored rather than punished.

Richelieu, scheming to seize power, has Milady plant forged love letters among the queen's possessions and steal her diamond necklace, taking it to London to suggest an affair with Buckingham. If the queen cannot wear the necklace at an upcoming ball, the king will be forced to execute her and go to war with England. Learning of the plot from the queen's lady-in-waiting, Constance the musketeers travel to London. There they outwit Milady and Buckingham, steal Buckingham's airship and recover the necklace, while Milady leaps from the ship rather than face execution.

On their return to France, they are attacked by Rochefort aboard a larger airship built from Milady's copies of the plans, and the battle ends with both vessels crashing onto Notre-Dame Cathedral, where D'Artagnan kills Rochefort in a duel. The necklace is returned to the queen in time for the ball, and the musketeers cover up the affair using Milady's written authorization from Richelieu, who vows revenge after they refuse to serve him. Meanwhile, Buckingham rescues Milady and advances on France with an armada of ships and airships.

The film received negative reviews, with critics faulting its writing and characters; Rotten Tomatoes reported 27% approval. It grossed $132 million worldwide against a production budget of $75 million.

documents.title: The Other Woman
documents.tagline: Love makes everything possible.
documents.overview: Emilia, a law-school graduate, falls in love with her married boss, Jack. After Emilia marries Jack, her happiness turns unexpectedly to grief following the death of her infant daughter. Devastated, Emilia nonetheless carries on, attempting to forge a connection with her stepson William and to resist the interference of Jack's jealous ex-wife.
documents.plot:
The Other Woman is an American drama written and directed by Don Roos, completed in 2009 and adapted from Ayelet Waldman's novel Love and Other Impossible Pursuits, the title under which it was released in the United Kingdom. Natalie Portman stars alongside Scott Cohen, Lisa Kudrow, Charlie Tahan and Lauren Ambrose, and the film was distributed in the United States by IFC Films.

Emilia is a young New York lawyer whose relationship with the married Jack ended his first marriage and led to their own. Her life has since been shattered by the death of their newborn daughter Isabel from what was recorded as sudden infant death syndrome. Emilia treats the loss as a punishment, believes she cannot have more children, and finds her marriage straining under her grief. She is regarded as a homewrecker by Jack's furious ex-wife Carolyn, who is now expecting another child herself.

Emilia also struggles with her precocious young stepson William, whose blunt remarks about Isabel wound her, including his observation that under Jewish law the baby had not lived long enough to count as a full person. Her clumsy attempts to bond with the boy backfire and lower her standing with both Carolyn and Jack. Eventually Emilia confesses the secret she has never told anyone: on the morning Isabel died, the baby had not been in her crib but asleep on Emilia's breast, and Emilia has been tormented by the belief that she smothered her daughter after falling asleep. She moves out, reconciles with her father, whose infidelity once hurt her mother, and returns to work with old friends at a Legal Aid office.

Carolyn unexpectedly asks to see her and admits she had told William that Emilia might have caused Isabel's death, adding that her son had rebuked her for it. She then tells Emilia that she has reviewed the autopsy report, which shows Emilia did not kill her child. Freed of her guilt, Emilia tells Jack the whole story, and a later crisis involving William brings them together again, with Jack asking her on a date. On the day Carolyn's baby is born, Emilia gives William a toy boat from her own childhood and tells him she loves him; after a moment he replies that he does too.

The film received mostly negative reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 37% approval; critics praised Portman and Kudrow but faulted Roos's direction.

documents.title: Underworld: Awakening
documents.tagline: Vengeance Returns
documents.overview: Having escaped years of imprisonment, vampire warrioress Selene finds herself in a changed world where humans have discovered the existence of both Vampire and Lycan clans and are conducting an all-out war to eradicate both immortal species. Now Selene must battle the humans and a frightening new breed of super Lycans to ensure the death dealers' survival.
documents.plot:
Underworld: Awakening is a 2012 American action horror film directed by Måns Mårlind and Björn Stein, from a screenplay by Len Wiseman, John Hlavin, J. Michael Straczynski and Allison Burnett based on a story by Wiseman and Hlavin. The fourth Underworld film, it stars Kate Beckinsale as the vampire warrior Selene, with Stephen Rea, Michael Ealy, Theo James, India Eisley and Charles Dance.

After humanity discovers vampires and Lycans, a program to study them becomes an extermination campaign, the Purge, and Selene and her lover Michael are captured. Selene is kept in cryogenic suspension for twelve years, during which both species are hunted almost to extinction. Breaking free, she learns another subject has escaped and begins seeing through someone else's eyes. Following them, she meets David, a young vampire, and fights off Lycans hunting the other escapee, a frightened girl. When a Lycan bites the girl, she partly transforms and tears it apart, and Selene realizes the girl is her daughter with Michael. The girl had freed Selene from her tank.

David takes them to his coven, where the girl's wound finally heals after she drinks blood. The coven distrusts her. When Lycans attack, Selene is overpowered by a giant "Super-Lycan" that heals instantly and is immune to silver, and David's father Thomas surrenders the girl to the Lycans. Selene revives the dying David with her blood. With Sebastian, a sympathetic human detective, she traces the Lycans to Antigen, the corporation behind the facility. Antigen is secretly run by Lycans, and its director, Dr. Jacob Lane, needs the girl's DNA to perfect his race. The Super-Lycan is Lane's son Quint. Selene and Sebastian storm the building to rescue the girl, whom they call Eve. Selene begins thawing Michael, Subject 0, but must leave him to save Eve. David, now immune to sunlight thanks to Selene's blood, joins the fight. Selene kills Quint with a silver grenade, and Eve kills Lane. When they return for Michael, his tank is empty, and they vow to find him first.

Shooting began in Vancouver in March 2011 without a finished script. Scott Speedman did not return as Michael and appears only in archive footage. Sony released it in January 2012. It opened at number one and grossed about $160 million worldwide on a $70 million budget, the highest total in the series. Rotten Tomatoes reported 25% approval and judged it heavy on action and light on story. Underworld: Blood Wars followed in 2016.

documents.title: Henry's Crime
documents.tagline: The real crime is not committing to your dreams.
documents.overview: An aimless man is sent to prison for a crime he did not commit, an ex-con targets the same bank he was sent away for robbing.

documents.title: Sarah's Key
documents.tagline: Uncover the mystery.
documents.overview: On the night of 16 July 1942, ten year old Sarah and her parents are being arrested and transported to the Velodrome d'Hiver in Paris where thousands of other jews are being sent to get deported. Sarah however managed to lock her little brother in a closet just before the police entered their apartment. Sixty years later, Julia Jarmond, an American journalist in Paris, gets the assignment to write an article about this raid, a black page in the history of France. She starts digging archives and through Sarah's file discovers a well kept secret about her own in-laws.
documents.plot:
In 1942, 10-year-old Sarah Starzynski hides her younger brother from French police by locking him in a secret closet and telling him to stay there until she returns. She takes the key with her when she and her parents are transported to the Vélodrome d'Hiver, where they are held in inhuman conditions by the Paris Police and French Secret Service.
The deportees are transferred to the French-run Beaune-la-Rolande internment camp. The adults are deported to the Auschwitz concentration camp, leaving the children in the camp. When Sarah tries to escape with her friend Rachel, a sympathetic Paris police guard spots them. When Sarah begs him to let them go so she can save her brother, he hesitates then lifts the barbed wire to let them out.
Sarah and Rachel fall asleep in a dog house at a farm where they are discovered by the farmers, Jules and Genevieve Dufaure. Despite knowing what they are and the associated danger, the Dufaures decide to help the girls. Rachel is dying, and when they call attention to themselves by calling in a doctor, a skeptical German officer asks them if they know anything about a second Jewish child. The officer begins a search for the second child, only to be interrupted when the French physician carries out the dead body of Rachel. Days later, the Dufaures take Sarah back to her family's apartment building in Paris. Sarah runs up to her apartment, knocking on the door furiously. A boy, 12 years old, answers. She rushes into her old room and unlocks the cupboard. Horrified by what she finds, she starts screaming hysterically.
After the war, Sarah continues to live as a family member with the Dufaures and their two grandsons. When she turns 18, she moves to the United States, hoping to put everything that happened behind her. She stops corresponding with the Dufaures when she gets married and has a son, William. When her son is nine, Sarah – still despondent and blaming herself for her brother's death - drives her car into the path of an oncoming truck. It is explained to her son that her death was merely an accident.
In the present, the French husband of journalist Julia inherits the apartment of his grandparents (his elderly father was the boy who opened the door to Sarah in August 1942). Having previously done an article on the Vel' d'Hiv Roundup, Julia finds her interest piqued when she learns that the apartment came into her husband's family at about the time of the Roundup and she begins to investigate what happened 60 years earlier. Her father-in-law tells Julia what he knows so she will quit prying.
Julia begins an obsessive quest to find any trace of Sarah, eventually learning of her life in Brooklyn and finally locating William in Italy. She meets with him and asks him for information about his mother, but learns to her surprise that William does not know his mother's history or even that she was Jewish, believing only that she had been a French farm girl.

documents.title: Mutant Pumpkins from Outer Space
documents.overview: Susan Murphy (a.k.a. Ginormica) and the Monsters are now working with the US government as special ops. So when an alien presence is detected in Susan's hometown of Modesto, California -- right before Halloween -- the team is dispatched to investigate. Everything appears normal, right down to the jack-o-lanterns peering out from every doorstep and windowsill. But when Halloween arrives, those innocent-looking carved pumpkins reveal themselves for what they really are mutant aliens. The altered pumpkins then start to implement their fiendish plan to take over Earth. The Monsters are there to combat the mutant gourds and try to smash their wicked scheme!
documents.plot:
Monsters vs. Aliens: Mutant Pumpkins from Outer Space is an animated Halloween television special of 2010 from DreamWorks Animation, based on the Monsters vs. Aliens franchise and directed by Peter Ramsey in his directing debut. The voice cast returns, with Reese Witherspoon as Susan Murphy, also known as Ginormica, Seth Rogen as B.O.B., Hugh Laurie as Dr. Cockroach, Will Arnett as the Missing Link and Kiefer Sutherland as General Monger, joined by Rainn Wilson as the villainous pumpkin Wicked Jack and Jeffrey Tambor and Julie White as Susan's parents. It premiered on RTÉ One in Ireland on 26 October 2010 and on NBC in the United States two days later.

One night a UFO drops a strange green goo onto a pumpkin field, and Farmer Jeb, going out to investigate, is seized by something among the pumpkins. On Halloween, Susan and her friends prepare to celebrate, except Dr. Cockroach, who hates the holiday because bullies once stole his favorite candy, a swirly pop. General Monger then reports aliens in Modesto, California, and sends the team to investigate. Meanwhile Jeb's pumpkins are being given away for free, and one family takes home the biggest, which their son names Wicked Jack.

While Susan checks the pumpkin patch, the others search the suburbs: Cockroach scans passersby, Link fails to frighten anyone and B.O.B. forgets what to say at each door, until an old lady's gift of a swirly pop rekindles Cockroach's love of the holiday. Susan finds the captive Jeb and learns that the goo has brought the pumpkins to life. As they attack trick-or-treaters, the monsters defend the children and discover that the creatures grow by eating candy. Led by a now giant Wicked Jack, the pumpkin army marches on the Murphy house, where Jack fuses with the others into an even larger monster.

Noticing B.O.B.'s indigestion after gorging on sweets, Cockroach plans to overfeed the pumpkins. While Susan distracts Jack, the children, backed by Link and a candy-firing Gatling platform, carry it out, and Cockroach sacrifices his swirly pop as the last ammunition. Susan knocks Jack's head off and Insectosaurus finishes him; Cockroach gives his swirly pop to a little girl, and Susan's parents accept sharing her with the world. In a final twist, goo from a stray pumpkin creates a mutant carrot.

The special came out on DVD in the United Kingdom in September 2010 and in the United States in 2011, and was followed by the short sequel Night of the Living Carrots.

documents.title: Star Trek Into Darkness
documents.tagline: Earth Will Fall
documents.overview: When the crew of the Enterprise is called back home, they find an unstoppable force of terror from within their own organization has detonated the fleet and everything it stands for, leaving our world in a state of crisis.  With a personal score to settle, Captain Kirk leads a manhunt to a war-zone world to capture a one man weapon of mass destruction. As our heroes are propelled into an epic chess game of life and death, love will be challenged, friendships will be torn apart, and sacrifices must be made for the only family Kirk has left: his crew.
documents.plot:
Star Trek Into Darkness is a 2013 science fiction action film directed by J.J. Abrams and written by Roberto Orci and Alex Kurtzman. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2009 film Star Trek, ignoring the events of the original Star Trek series.

The film begins with Captain James T. Kirk (Chris Pine) being court-martialed for his actions in the previous film, which resulted in the destruction of the Klingon ship Khitomer. The Federation is divided over whether to allow Kirk to continue as captain of the USS Enterprise, and he faces a vote of no confidence.

Meanwhile, a terrorist known as Khan (Benedict Cumberbatch) escapes from prison on the planet Sarpeidon, where he was being held for his role in the destruction of the planet. Khan is revealed to be a genetically engineered superhuman who seeks revenge against Kirk, whom he blames for his imprisonment and subsequent death.

As Khan begins to wreak havoc on the galaxy, the Enterprise is sent to investigate. However, they soon discover that Khan has a personal vendetta against Kirk, and that he plans to destroy the Federation unless Kirk agrees to meet with him.

Kirk's first officer, Mr. Spock (Zachary Quinto), is killed by Khan during a confrontation on the planet Sarpeidon. This event sets off a chain reaction of events as Kirk becomes increasingly obsessed with stopping Khan and finding out what happened to his friend.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Khan's true intention is not just to destroy the Federation, but also to prove himself as a superior being. He believes that he can do better than humanity and that he has the right to rule over the galaxy.

Kirk teams up with his old nemesis, Admiral Marcus (Peter Weller), who reveals that Khan was once a human scientist named Dr. Leonard McCoy's friend. However, when Khan discovered that he had the potential to be a superhuman, he became obsessed with the idea of becoming one himself and began experimenting on himself.

Kirk eventually discovers that Khan has created an army of genetically engineered superhumans known as the "Nobunaga" who are loyal only to him. He also learns that Khan's ultimate goal is to destroy the Federation and take its resources for himself.

In a final confrontation, Kirk faces off against Khan on the planet Sarpeidon. However, just as it seems like Kirk has the upper hand, Spock returns from the dead, having sacrificed himself to save his friend. With Spock's help, Kirk is able to defeat Khan and destroy his ship.

The film ends with Kirk reflecting on the events that have transpired and realizing that being a leader means making difficult choices and putting the needs of others before one's own desires. The movie concludes with a sense of closure for the characters, as they move forward into a new era of exploration and discovery.

Overall, Star Trek Into Darkness is an action-packed adventure that explores themes of leadership, loyalty, and the consequences of playing god. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the franchise generally enjoyed the film's thrilling plot and memorable performances from the cast.

documents.title: The Water Horse
documents.tagline: How Do You Keep A Secret This Big?
documents.overview: A lonely boy discovers a mysterious egg that hatches a sea creature of Scottish legend.
documents.plot:
The Water Horse: Legend of the Deep is a 2007 fantasy drama film directed by Jay Russell and written by Robert Nelson Jacobs, based on Dick King-Smith's children's novel The Water Horse. Alex Etel stars as Angus MacMorrow, a young boy who raises a mysterious creature that grows into the legendary Loch Ness Monster, with Emily Watson as his mother, Anne, Ben Chaplin as the handyman Lewis Mowbray and David Morrissey as Captain Hamilton. Produced by Revolution Studios and Walden Media with Beacon Pictures, it was distributed by Columbia Pictures, with visual effects by Weta Digital.

In present-day Scotland, two American tourists in a pub ask an old man about the famous "surgeon's photograph" of the Loch Ness Monster, and he begins to tell them the true story. In 1942, during the Second World War, Angus lives on an estate on the shores of Loch Ness with his mother, the housekeeper, and his sister, Kirstie. His father, a sailor in the Royal Navy, has been missing since his ship was sunk a year earlier, but Angus refuses to believe that he will not return. While collecting shells on the shore, Angus finds a strange egg, which hatches into a small creature that he names Crusoe. He keeps it secret, eventually confiding in Kirstie and in Lewis, the new handyman, who tells him the legend of the water horse, a creature of which only one exists at a time, laying a single egg before dying.

As Crusoe grows rapidly, keeping him hidden becomes impossible. Meanwhile, soldiers of the Royal Artillery commanded by Captain Hamilton arrive at the estate to set up guns to defend the loch against German submarines. Angus and Lewis release Crusoe into the loch, where Angus forms a deep bond with the creature, riding on its back through the water. But the creature's existence begins to attract attention, and when the soldiers learn of it and their guns are turned on the loch, Crusoe becomes frightened and dangerous. Angus must overcome his own fear of the water and his grief for his father in order to protect Crusoe and help him escape the anti-submarine nets that trap him in the loch.

The Water Horse received generally positive reviews, with 74 percent of critics on Rotten Tomatoes giving it a favorable review; the consensus described it as a fine family film that infuses a classic tale with imagination, humor, heart and inventive special effects. It grossed more than $100 million worldwide.

documents.title: S.W.A.T.: Firefight
documents.overview: Los Angeles S.W.A.T. officer, Lt. Paul Cutler, is sent to train the Detroit S.W.A.T. team on new anti-terrorism and homeland security techniques. Cutler has a hard time settling into his assignment as he locks horns with his new captain and encounters resistance from the team he must lead. Cutler begins to adjust to his new assignment, starting a budding romance with police psychologist Kim Byers along the way. Unexpectedly, a routine hostage call turns deadly, and a relentless ex-government agent named Walter Hatch vows revenge on Cutler and the entire S.W.A.T. team for killing the woman he loves. Cutler must use his considerable S.W.A.T. training and knowledge to save his teammates and defeat a trained killer.

documents.title: Beverly Hills Chihuahua 2
documents.tagline: The family just got bigger
documents.overview: Puppy mayhem turns the lives of newlywed Chihuahua parents Papi and Chloe upside down when their rambunctious, mischievous puppies present one challenge after another. But when their human owners end up in trouble, the tiny pups will stop at nothing to save them - because in good times and hard times, the family always sticks together. So Papi, Chloe and the puppies embark on a heroic adventure, proving once again that big heroes come in small packages.
documents.plot:
Beverly Hills Chihuahua 2 is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores several key themes. At its core, the movie is about the power of friendship and loyalty. The story follows Chloe, a pampered Chihuahua who finds herself separated from her owner and must navigate an unfamiliar world to find her way back home.

Throughout the film, Chloe forms strong bonds with a group of street-smart dogs, including a wise-cracking mutt named Duke, who becomes her unlikely ally. As they face various challenges together, Chloe learns valuable lessons about perseverance, adaptability, and the importance of staying true to oneself.

The movie also touches on themes of identity and self-discovery. Chloe's journey is not just about finding her way back home but also about discovering her own strengths and weaknesses. Along the way, she encounters a range of characters who teach her valuable lessons about courage, kindness, and the value of following one's heart.

Furthermore, Beverly Hills Chihuahua 2 explores themes of belonging and acceptance. Chloe's experiences on the streets are marked by both loneliness and connection, highlighting the complexities of finding one's place in the world. The film suggests that true belonging can be found through shared experiences and relationships with others, rather than solely through material possessions or social status.

Overall, Beverly Hills Chihuahua 2 is a lighthearted yet meaningful film that celebrates the importance of friendship, self-discovery, and embracing one's unique qualities.

documents.title: Minions: Home Makeover
documents.overview: A social worker is coming to Gru's house to check if it's suitable for children. Margo, Edith, Agnes and the Minions must take care of the situation.
documents.plot:
Minions: Home Makeover, released simply as Home Makeover, is a 2010 American computer-animated comedy short produced by Illumination Entertainment and Universal Pictures as a follow-up to the feature Despicable Me. Directed by Kyle Balda and Samuel Tourneux and written by Brett Hoffman, it runs between four and five minutes. It was released in December 2010 as one of three new shorts, together with Orientation Day and Banana, included with the home-video release of Despicable Me, appearing among the bonus features of the Blu-ray and in the Minion Madness collection.

Set after the events of the film, the short opens in Gru's house while the supervillain is out on an errand. Margo answers an unexpected telephone call from Miss Hattie's Home for Girls, the orphanage the three sisters came from, and, pretending to be Gru, learns that a social worker is on the way to inspect whether the house is safe and suitable for children. If it is not, the girls will be sent back to the orphanage. With little time to spare, Margo, Edith and Agnes enlist the Minions to give the lair a rapid child-friendly makeover.

The comedy comes from the gap between a villain's home and a family home, and from the inventive, chaotic solutions the girls and the Minions devise. Tennis balls are stuck over the spikes inside a coffin, the pins are pulled from a voodoo doll, a clown nose is placed on a skull in the dining room, Gru's own shrink ray is used to make the weapons smaller, and a paint-filled bazooka turns the walls pink. To complete the illusion, the Minions stand in for the master of the house with a makeshift "Mr. Gru". The inspector seems satisfied with the result until the real Gru comes home: the disguise falls apart, the startled social worker faints, and Gru, taking in his newly "girly" lair, passes out as well.

The voice cast reunites the girls of the feature, with Miranda Cosgrove as Margo, Dana Gaier as Edith and Elsie Fisher as Agnes, while Pierre Coffin voices both the Minions and the social worker. The short was later collected among Illumination's short films on streaming and television platforms, where it carries a TV-Y7 rating.

documents.title: She's on Duty
documents.tagline: She's a natural born fighter… back to school!
documents.overview: A boisterous detective goes undercover in a high school in order to befriend the teenage daughter of a notorious gangster.
documents.plot: A boisterous detective goes undercover in a high school in order to befriend the teenage daughter of a notorious gangster.

documents.title: Shaolin
documents.tagline: In a land torn by strife, the righteous monks of Shaolin stand as a beacon of hope for the oppressed masses.
documents.overview: China is plunged into strife as feuding warlords try to expand their power by warring over neighboring lands. Fuelled by his success on the battlefield, young and arrogant Hao Jie sneers at Shaolin's masters when he beats one of them in a duel. But the pride comes before a fall. When his own family is wiped out by a rival warlord, Hao is forced to take refuge with the monks. As the civil unrest spreads and the people suffer, Hao and the Shaolin masters are forced to take a fiery stand against the evil warlords. They launch a daring plan or rescue and escape.
documents.plot:
Shaolin is a 2011 Hong Kong–Chinese martial arts film directed by Benny Chan. Andy Lau stars as the warlord Hou Jie, with Nicholas Tse as his treacherous lieutenant Cao Man, Jackie Chan as the temple cook Wudao and Fan Bingbing as Hou's wife, Yan Xi. Wu Jing, Yu Shaoqun and Xing Yu play Shaolin monks. The film is a loose remake of the 1982 Jet Li film Shaolin Temple, moved to a different historical period, and it was released in both Mandarin and Cantonese.

The story is set in early 20th-century China during the Warlord Era. Hou Jie, a ruthless warlord, defeats his rival Huo Long and takes control of Dengfeng. When Huo seeks refuge at the Shaolin Temple, Hou follows him there, kills him and mocks the monks. Hou then plans to murder his sworn brother, Song Hu, but his ambitious second-in-command, Cao Man, turns the trap against him and sends assassins after them all. Song is killed, and Hou's young daughter is gravely injured in a fall from a cliff. In desperation, Hou carries her to Shaolin and begs the monks to save her, but she dies. His wife blames him and leaves him, and in a single night Hou has lost his power and his family.

Wandering the temple grounds, Hou is taken in by Wudao, the kind-hearted cook, who gives him food and shelter. Full of remorse, Hou becomes a monk, and through study and martial arts he absorbs Shaolin's principles and finds peace. Meanwhile, Cao has seized Hou's army and is brutalizing innocent people, and Hou must confront his past to stop him. While he distracts Cao, the monks raid Cao's camp to free the laborers, and Hou escapes with his wife. As Cao's forces close in, the monks decide to evacuate. Wudao leads the refugees to safety while Hou and a group of monks stay behind to hold off the attackers. The temple is pounded by artillery, killing many monks and soldiers. Hou defeats Cao in combat but then saves him from a falling beam, sacrificing his own life. He dies peacefully in the palm of the great Buddha statue, leaving Cao overcome with guilt.

Filming began in October 2009 with a ceremony at the Shaolin Temple. To avoid damaging the real temple, the production built its own replica in Zhejiang for 10 million yuan. Released in mainland China on January 19, 2011, and in Hong Kong a week later, it opened at number one in Hong Kong, Thailand and Singapore and set a box office record in Malaysia. It holds a 74% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Alvin and the Chipmunks: Chipwrecked
documents.tagline: Sun, Sea and Squeaks.
documents.overview: Playing around while aboard a cruise ship, the Chipmunks and Chipettes accidentally go overboard and end up marooned in a tropical paradise. They discover their new turf is not as deserted as it seems.
documents.plot:
Alvin and the Chipmunks: Chipwrecked is a 2011 American musical comedy film directed by Mike Mitchell. The movie is the third installment in the Alvin and the Chipmunks film series, following The Squeakquel (2009) and Alvin and the Chipmunks (2007).

The story begins with Alvin, Simon, and Theodore, the three main chipmunk characters, preparing for their Christmas concert tour. However, things take a turn when they are invited to perform at a luxurious cruise ship called the "Sea-Dog." The ship is owned by Dave Seville's (Jason Lee) friend, Ian Hawke (David Cross), who has recently become wealthy.

Upon arrival, the chipmunks meet their new friends, including Brittany and Jeanette, two human girls who are also on the cruise. However, things quickly take a turn for the worse when the ship is attacked by a group of pirates led by the infamous Captain Sykes (Jedward). The pirates steal the ship's treasure, which includes a valuable diamond necklace.

The chipmunks and their new friends must work together to outsmart the pirates and retrieve the stolen treasure. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous sea routes, wild animals, and even a rival group of singing chipmunks led by the villainous Alby (Zachary Gordon).

As the story unfolds, the characters learn valuable lessons about teamwork, friendship, and believing in themselves. The movie features a range of catchy musical numbers, including "The Chipmunk Song (Christmas Don't Be Late)," "I'm Right Here," and "We Can Make It Happen."

In the end, the chipmunks and their friends successfully defeat the pirates and recover the stolen treasure. The movie concludes with a heartwarming performance by the chipmunks at the Sea-Dog's Christmas concert, which is attended by a large audience of fans.

Overall, Alvin and the Chipmunks: Chipwrecked is a fun and entertaining film that combines music, adventure, and humor. While it may not be as memorable as some of its predecessors, it remains a enjoyable addition to the franchise.

documents.title: Jeepers Creepers 3
documents.tagline: Third Time's the Charm
documents.overview: Taking place on the last day of the Creeper’s twenty-three-day feeding frenzy, as the skeptical Sergeant Tubbs teams up with a task force hellbent on destroying the Creeper for good. The Creeper fights back in gory glory as its enemies grow closer than ever before to learning the secret of its dark origins.
documents.plot:
Written and directed by Victor Salva, Jeepers Creepers 3 is a 2017 American horror film and the third instalment in the Jeepers Creepers series. Set between the events of the first two films, it brings back Jonathan Breck as the Creeper, alongside Stan Shaw, Gabrielle Haugh, Brandon Smith and Meg Foster, while Gina Philips makes a cameo as Trish Jenner, her first appearance in the series since the original film.

The story begins a day after the first film. Police find the Creeper's truck full of corpses and rigged with deadly traps, and Sheriff Dan Tashtego tells Sergeant Davis Tubbs about the creature and what drives it. The Creeper soon reclaims the truck, abducting one of the officers transporting it. Tashtego assembles a team of hunters made up of relatives of the creature's past victims.

Elsewhere, Gaylen Brandon, whose son Kenny was killed by the Creeper, sees a vision of him warning that the monster will come for something he buried on her property and will kill her and her granddaughter Addison. When a group of teenagers discovers the truck in a field, the Creeper kills them all. Addison is later abducted after stumbling on the creature's attack at a plantation house.

Gaylen digs up a severed hand Kenny had found, and touching it reveals visions of how ancient the Creeper is. Tashtego's team catches up with the truck on the highway, but their bullets have little effect; Michael is killed and Tashtego dies at the Creeper's hands, leaving Tubbs to retreat.

Held captive in the truck, Addison triggers one of its traps and drives a metal pipe into the Creeper's head, costing it an eye. She escapes when the monster is struck by a passing truck, though it heals itself by consuming the driver. Gaylen and Buddy find Addison, and the Creeper returns to Gaylen's house to find a sign declaring that they know what it is. The next day Buddy leaves for a basketball game on the bus later attacked in the second film. Twenty-three years later, Trish writes an open letter vowing revenge for her brother Darry's death.

Originally billed as a one-night event, the film opened in 635 theaters on September 26, 2017, with a second showing in October, and grossed about $4 million worldwide during its brief run. It holds a 17% rating on Rotten Tomatoes from a small number of reviews.

documents.title: Another Earth
documents.overview: On the night of the discovery of a duplicate Earth in the Solar system, an ambitious young student and an accomplished composer cross paths in a tragic accident.
documents.plot: On the night a duplicate Earth is discovered in the solar system, the lives of a young woman and an accomplished composer become tragically connected after a fatal accident.

documents.title: A Very Harold & Kumar Christmas
documents.tagline: Christmas comes prematurely.
documents.overview: Six years have elapsed since Guantanamo Bay, leaving Harold and Kumar estranged from one another with very different families, friends and lives. But when Kumar arrives on Harold's doorstep during the holiday season with a mysterious package in hand, he inadvertently burns down Harold's father-in-law's beloved Christmas tree. To fix the problem, Harold and Kumar embark on a mission through New York City to find the perfect Christmas tree, once again stumbling into trouble at every single turn.
