documents.title: Tammy and the T-Rex
documents.tagline: He's the coolest pet in town!
documents.overview: An evil scientist implants the brain of Michael, a murdered high school student, into an animatronic Tyrannosaurus. Michael escapes, wreaks vengeance on the high school tormentors who killed him, and is reunited with his sweetheart Tammy. Together, the couple try to elude the mad scientist and the police and find a more appropriate vessel for Michael's brain.
documents.plot:
Tammy and the T-Rex is a 1994 American science fiction horror comedy directed by Stewart Raffill, who wrote it with Gary Brockette. Starring Terry Kiser, Ellen Dubin, Denise Richards, Paul Walker, George Pilgrim and John Franklin, it centers on Tammy, a high school student whose boyfriend, Michael Brock, has his brain transplanted into a robotic Tyrannosaurus rex by the mad scientist Dr. Gunther Wachenstein.

At cheerleading practice, Tammy is joined by her new boyfriend, Michael. Her violent, jealous former boyfriend, Billy, arrives with his gang to provoke Michael, and the fight that follows ends with the police taking Billy away while a distraught Tammy runs off in tears. In a dark warehouse, Dr. Wachenstein and his assistant, Helga, inspect a robotic Tyrannosaurus rex operated by remote control, and the doctor reveals his plan to implant a living human brain into the machine to give it consciousness, mobility and "immortality".

That night, Michael sneaks out to visit Tammy, but Billy and his thugs catch him and throw him into a wild animal park, where he is mauled by a lion and left in a coma. As his drunken uncle keeps watch at the hospital, Wachenstein and Helga declare Michael dead so they can take his brain for their robot. Once implanted, Michael escapes in the dinosaur's body, takes revenge on the high school bullies who tormented him and reunites with Tammy, who realizes who he is and begins searching for a more suitable body for him. Wachenstein pursues his creation in a chase that ends with Michael killing the doctor before police gun down the mechanical dinosaur. Tammy saves Michael's brain and takes it home, hooking it up to her computer and camera so that he can see and speak; when she performs a striptease for him, the connections spark.

According to Raffill, a theater owner from South America who had temporary use of an animatronic T-Rex destined for a park in Texas asked him to make a film with it, and Raffill wrote the story in a week so shooting could begin within a month. The opening scenes were filmed at Newbury Park High School in California. Made as an R-rated horror comedy, the film had its gore removed for its original American release, though versions in countries such as Italy kept it. In 2019, Vinegar Syndrome restored the uncut 90-minute version for select theaters and home video, and it was later licensed for the 2022 game High on Life. It holds 43% on Rotten Tomatoes, while the Gore Cut scores 100%.

documents.title: Bridesmaids
documents.tagline: Save the date.
documents.overview: Annie's life is a mess. But when she finds out her lifetime best friend is engaged, she simply must serve as Lillian's maid of honor. Though lovelorn and broke, Annie bluffs her way through the expensive and bizarre rituals. With one chance to get it perfect, she’ll show Lillian and her bridesmaids just how far you’ll go for someone you love.

documents.title: Final Destination 5
documents.tagline: We all share a common destination.
documents.overview: In this fifth installment, Death is just as omnipresent as ever, and is unleashed after one man’s premonition saves a group of coworkers from a terrifying suspension bridge collapse. But this group of unsuspecting souls was never supposed to survive, and, in a terrifying race against time, the ill-fated group frantically tries to discover a way to escape Death’s sinister agenda.
documents.plot:
Final Destination 5 is a supernatural horror film directed by Steven R. Monroe and written by Eric Heisserer. The movie takes place five years after the events of the fourth installment, with the main character Molly Walker (Shantel VanSanten) still trying to come to terms with her near-death experience.

The story begins with Molly, who has been experiencing recurring premonitions since her last encounter with death, which led to the demise of her friends. She is now working as a freelance photographer and is engaged to her boyfriend, Nick (Bjorn Johnson). The two are planning their wedding, but Molly's anxiety about her impending doom continues to haunt her.

As the story unfolds, Molly starts experiencing more premonitions, including one that foretells the collapse of a roller coaster at an amusement park. Despite her warnings, Nick and his friends decide to go on the ride, which ultimately leads to their deaths. Molly is left shaken and realizes that she must find a way to prevent others from meeting the same fate.

Molly's quest for answers takes her to a support group for people who have survived near-death experiences, where she meets a woman named Laura (Emmanuelle Vaugier) who has also experienced premonitions. Together, they embark on a journey to uncover the truth behind their abilities and find a way to prevent future deaths.

As Molly delves deeper into her research, she discovers that her premonitions are not just random events but are actually connected to an ancient curse that has been passed down through generations of people with similar abilities. The curse is linked to a mysterious figure known as "The Driver," who seems to be manipulating the course of events to bring about the deaths.

Molly and Laura soon realize that they must work together to break the curse and prevent further tragedies from occurring. Along the way, Molly's relationships with her loved ones are put to the test as she struggles to balance her desire to protect them with her own need for control.

The movie builds up to a thrilling climax as Molly and Laura face off against The Driver in an attempt to break the curse. In the end, they succeed in preventing further deaths, but not without some unexpected twists and turns.

Throughout the film, the themes of fate, free will, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control are explored. The movie also delves into the psychological effects of experiencing premonitions and the weight of responsibility that comes with knowing what's going to happen.

Overall, Final Destination 5 is a tense and suspenseful thriller that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats as they follow Molly's desperate quest to prevent further tragedies from occurring.

documents.title: Blitz
documents.tagline: It's cop-killer vs. killer-cop
documents.overview: A tough cop is dispatched to take down a serial killer who has been targeting police officers.
documents.plot:
Blitz is a 2011 British action thriller film directed by Elliott Lester and written by Nathan Parker, based on Ken Bruen's 2002 novel of the same name featuring his recurring character Detective Sergeant Tom Brant. Jason Statham stars as Brant, a violent police officer hunting a serial killer who is murdering police officers in South East London, with Paddy Considine as his partner Porter Nash, Aidan Gillen as the killer Barry Weiss, David Morrissey as journalist Harold Dunlop, Zawe Ashton as PC Elizabeth Falls, Luke Evans as DI Craig Stokes and Mark Rylance as Chief Inspector Bruce Roberts. Shot in London in August 2010, it was the first film produced by Lionsgate UK.

When two police constables are shot dead and Chief Inspector Roberts is bludgeoned to death, a hunt begins for a killer who is targeting the police in South East London. Porter Nash, an openly gay sergeant serving as acting inspector, is brought in to lead the investigation and faces ridicule from fellow officers, but finds an unlikely ally in the hot-tempered Tom Brant, a detective known for beating suspects. A tip from Brant's informant Radnor points them to Barry Weiss, a man who once boasted of setting a police dog on fire, and Brant recognizes him as someone he beat up in a billiard hall a year earlier. Weiss, craving notoriety, contacts the newspaper reporter Harold Dunlop and declares that he wants to be known as "the Blitz". When Radnor tries to sell information about Weiss's car full of trophies to Dunlop, Weiss kills him and removes the evidence. Brant realizes that all of the victims are officers who once arrested Weiss and that PC Falls is likely to be next; she survives an attack, but a young gang member she has been looking out for is killed. Releasing Weiss's picture to the media leads to his arrest, yet without solid evidence the police are forced to let him go. Knowing that Weiss wants revenge on Brant, the detectives set a trap at Roberts's funeral, which Weiss infiltrates in the dead officer's stolen uniform, forcing Brant to decide how far he will go to stop a killer the law cannot touch.

Lionsgate UK released Blitz in the United Kingdom on 20 May 2011. It grossed about $15.8 million worldwide and received mixed reviews, with a 48% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a consensus calling it a middling, familiar crime thriller that sidelines a game performance from Statham.

documents.title: Mezzo Forte
documents.tagline: Double the girls, double the guns!!
documents.overview: The target of hitgirl Mikura is a wealthy baseball team owner, but he turns out to be a powerful underworld boss. Mikura and her team are beset by countless heavily armed bodyguards and the boss' vicious daughter.
documents.plot:
Mezzo Forte (Japanese: メゾフォルテ) is a 2000 Japanese adult original video animation (OVA) directed by Yasuomi Umetsu. A spiritual sequel to Umetsu's Kite and set some time after it, it shares that work's highly trained female lead, darkly comic tone, slick and extremely violent action and, in its uncut form, explicit sexual content. It follows Mikura Suzuki and her small mercenary outfit, the Danger Service Agency (DSA).

Momokichi Momoi is a mob boss who owns a professional baseball team, the Peach Twisters, and disposes of underperforming players by having them killed; his daughter Momomi is even more vicious. A mysterious old man hires Mikura and her partners Kenichi and Tomohisa to kidnap Momokichi. Their attempt during a bowling match goes badly when the family's bodyguards intervene, and Mikura and Momomi seem to recognise one another before the team escapes, only to find that Momokichi has died in the struggle. As an enraged Momomi sets her men and the police on their trail, the DSA bury the body and press their client for the truth. He claims to be a former hitman of Momokichi's whom Momomi tried to kill when he retired, and says that with the father dead, the only way any of them will be safe is to eliminate the daughter. A fake ransom demand fails to draw her out, and Momomi captures Mikura, but Kenichi and Tomohisa have secretly swapped her for a robot double, which Momomi hands over to two criminals as punishment. The DSA then stage a hostage exchange using a robot copy of Momokichi; both sides attempt a double cross, a gunfight erupts, and the real Mikura ambushes and kills Momomi. The client now reveals himself as Hiroka, the family's head of security, who used the DSA to wipe out the Momois so he could take over their empire, and moves to dispose of the team. The DSA, however, had seen through him from the start and kill him by detonating the Momokichi robot. Afterwards they set about repairing their wrecked base, and Mikura senses that another job is coming.

As with Kite, Mezzo Forte was released in both Japan and the United States in two forms, one with the graphic sex scenes removed and one with them intact, while both keep the violence. In the US the OVA episodes were edited into a feature released on DVD in 2000 with about 20 minutes of footage not in the Japanese release, though none of the director's-cut sexual material. A Japanese international version with the extra footage followed on July 23, 2004.

documents.title: Termination Point
documents.tagline: Their only Hope is to Turn Back Time
documents.overview: Top secret government experiments with time travel have been shut down and declared as too dangerous to continue. The lead scientist has disappeared with the technology and a government manhunt is underway. When his name appears on an airline manifest after the flight has departed, the government orders the plane to turn back. But the plane drops from the radar, disappearing into thin air! As special agents try to locate the plane, scientists must deal with the repercussions from the time ripples that threaten to destroy the Earth.
documents.plot:
Termination Point is a 2007 Canadian science fiction action thriller made for television, directed by Jason Bourque from a screenplay by Peter Sullivan and produced by Insight Film Studios with CineTel Films. It stars Jason Priestley as federal agent Caleb Smith and Lou Diamond Phillips as Dr. Daniel Winter, a scientist who has vanished with a secret government device.

Top-secret government experiments in teleportation and time travel have been shut down as too dangerous, and their lead scientist, Winter, has disappeared with the technology, a portable teleporter that opens a wormhole through space and time and had previously been tested only on small animals such as mice. A passenger jet crashes in the American Midwest with no survivors, yet investigators discover that the aircraft, Flight 507 to Mexico, is not due to depart until the following day: it has apparently travelled into the past. When Winter's name turns up on the flight's manifest, the government orders the plane turned back and, to protect the project, the President authorises fighter jets to shoot it down, despite the pleas of Caleb, whose wife Claire and daughter Sarah are on board for a holiday.

At the last moment Winter activates the device by remote control and the plane vanishes into another dimension; only the passengers closest to the teleporter survive the jump. Aboard, the corrupt agent David Martin and his accomplice Liam take the survivors hostage and try to force Winter to send the aircraft back to coordinates of their choosing. On the ground, Caleb tracks down Winter's girlfriend and recovers a second remote hidden in her house, while the open wormhole spawns a swelling vortex in the sky whose lightning makes helicopters, buildings and people disappear, and which scientists warn will destroy the universe unless it is closed. Sarah restores the failing teleporter's power, and Caleb opens a wormhole of his own to reach the plane. In the ensuing struggle Claire is killed, Liam is struck by the lightning and Martin is thrown from the fuselage, before Caleb sends the plane back to the moment before Flight 507 took off. Forewarned by a photograph he sends to his own phone, he has Winter and the two conspirators arrested before departure.

The cast also includes Stefanie von Pfetten as Claire, Ashley Whillans as Sarah, Gary Hudson as Martin, Michael Eklund as Liam, Garwin Sanford and Erin Karpluk. The film premiered on German television on RTL II in March 2009.

documents.title: The Animatrix
documents.tagline: Free your mind.
documents.overview: Straight from the creators of the groundbreaking Matrix trilogy, this collection of short animated films from the world's leading anime directors fuses computer graphics and Japanese anime to provide the background of the Matrix universe and the conflict between man and machines. The shorts include Final Flight of the Osiris, The Second Renaissance, Kid's Story, Program, World Record, Beyond, A Detective Story and Matriculated.
documents.plot:
The Animatrix is a 2003 adult animated science fiction anthology produced by the Wachowskis, comprising nine short films that expand the world of The Matrix, some supplying backstory and others telling side stories. The Wachowskis wrote four of the shorts but left the animation to leading Japanese animators; Jack Fletcher directed the English-language voice work, and Keanu Reeves, Carrie-Anne Moss and Clayton Watson voice Neo, Trinity and the Kid.

In "Final Flight of the Osiris", the hovercraft Osiris discovers a vast Sentinel army drilling toward Zion; as the machines overrun the ship, Jue enters the Matrix to deliver a warning, and Captain Thadeus and the crew die in the explosion. The two-part "The Second Renaissance" recounts how humanity built a race of servant robots, how the trial and destruction of B1-66ER, an android that killed its owner in self-defense, led to persecution and an exodus to the machine nation of Zero One, whose economy came to dominate the world, and how war followed. After humans blot out the sun in "Operation Dark Storm", the machines win, harvest people as living batteries and create the Matrix to keep them pacified.

In "Kid's Story", a disaffected teenager contacted by Neo flees Agents and leaps from his school roof, awakening in the real world through "self-substantiation". "Program" pits Cis against her comrade Duo in a feudal-Japan simulation where he urges her to return with him to the Matrix; she kills him, then learns the encounter was a loyalty test. In "World Record", sprinter Dan Davis runs so fast that he briefly wakes in his pod; Agents leave him crippled, yet he still rises to whisper "Free". In "Beyond", a girl searching for her cat finds children playing in a haunted house full of glitches in the Matrix, which Agents posing as exterminators soon erase. "A Detective Story" follows Ash, a hard-boiled private eye hired to find the hacker Trinity, who ends up facing Agents alone after she escapes. In "Matriculated", rebels capture a machine and try to teach it empathy inside their own Matrix, but an attack leaves the converted robot as the sole survivor.

Four of the shorts debuted on the official Matrix website, and "Final Flight of the Osiris" played in theaters with Dreamcatcher. Warner Home Video released the collection on June 3, 2003, and it sold 2.7 million copies for $68 million. Reviews were positive, with 88% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Spy Kids: All the Time in the World
documents.original_title: Spy Kids: All the Time in the World
documents.overview: Eight years after the third film, the OSS has become the world's top spy agency, while the Spy Kids department has since become defunct. A retired spy Marissa is thrown back into the action along with her stepchildren when a maniacal Timekeeper attempts to take over the world. In order to save the world, Rebecca and Cecil must team up with their hated stepmother. Carmen and Juni have since also grown up and will provide gadgets to them.
documents.plot:
Spy Kids: All the Time in the World is a 2011 American spy action comedy written and directed by Robert Rodriguez, the fourth entry in the Spy Kids series. Released in "4D", it came with "Aroma-scope" scratch-and-sniff cards that let audiences smell scents from the screen. Jessica Alba, Joel McHale, Rowan Blanchard, Mason Cook, Ricky Gervais and Jeremy Piven join Alexa Vega and Daryl Sabara, who return from the first three films. It premiered at L.A. Live in Los Angeles on July 31, 2011, and Dimension Films released it in the United States on August 19.

Nine months pregnant and already in labor, OSS agent Marissa Wilson defies her boss, Danger D'Amo, to capture the criminal Tick Tock and recover data on a dangerous weapon called Project Armageddon. She then retires to family life with her husband, Wilbur, host of a spy-hunting television show, their new daughter and her stepchildren, twins Rebecca and Cecil, though Rebecca still resents her as a replacement for her late mother. When a villain called the Time Keeper begins speeding up time to punish a world that wastes it, Marissa is called back into service. His target is the Chronos Sapphire, the jewel in a necklace Marissa gave Rebecca. After henchmen raid the house, the twins learn the truth about their stepmother and discover that the family dog, Argonaut, is a talking robot. At OSS headquarters their step-cousin Carmen Cortez lets them pick gadgets from the defunct Spy Kids division, and their search leads them to Tick Tock's lair in a clock shop, where they learn of the Wells Experiment, a time-travel project that once froze a boy in time.

Wilbur, meanwhile, unknowingly films his family in battle and loses his job after destroying the footage. As Carmen's estranged brother, Juni, joins the case, the twins notice that Danger's name is an anagram of "Armageddon". He is the Time Keeper, the frozen boy grown up, desperate to go back and spend more time with his father, while Tick Tock and his henchmen are alternate versions of himself. Rebecca urges him to value the time he has, and after a trip through the vortex returns him an old man, he shuts the device down. The family reconciles, and Carmen and Juni relaunch the Spy Kids program.

Piven plays Danger and Gervais voices Argonaut. Reviews were largely negative, with 23% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a consensus that the franchise had run its course. It grossed about $85 million worldwide on a $27 million budget, the lowest total in the series.

documents.title: Mission: Impossible - Ghost Protocol
documents.tagline: No plan. No backup. No choice.
documents.overview: Ethan Hunt and his team are racing against time to track down a dangerous terrorist named Hendricks, who has gained access to Russian nuclear launch codes and is planning a strike on the United States. An attempt to stop him ends in an explosion causing severe destruction to the Kremlin and the IMF to be implicated in the bombing, forcing the President to disavow them. No longer being aided by the government, Ethan and his team chase Hendricks around the globe, although they might still be too late to stop a disaster.
documents.plot:
Mission: Impossible - Ghost Protocol is a 2011 action spy film directed by Brad Bird and produced by Christopher McQuarrie, J.J. Abrams, and Tom Cruise. The movie marks the fourth installment in the Mission: Impossible film series.

The story begins with Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise), a secret agent working for the Impossible Mission Force (IMF). Ethan is tasked with investigating a mole within the IMF who has been stealing sensitive information from the organization's computer systems. As he delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that the mole is actually William Brandt (Michael Nyqvist), a high-ranking official in the IMF.

Ethan soon realizes that the mole has stolen classified information about a top-secret operation codenamed "Ghost Protocol." The mission is to infiltrate the Kremlin and disable a nuclear launch system before it falls into the wrong hands. However, the mole has already alerted the Russian authorities, and Ethan must now work with his team to prevent a global catastrophe.

Ethan's team consists of Benji Dunn (Simon Pegg), a tech expert; Jane Carter (Paula Patton), an IMF agent; and William Brandt, who is initially working against them. As they embark on their mission, they face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, deadly traps, and ruthless adversaries.

The team's first stop is the Kremlin, where they must navigate through a series of obstacles to reach the launch system. Along the way, they encounter a group of skilled Russian agents led by Anatoly Sidorov (Michael Nyqvist), who are determined to stop them at all costs.

As the mission unfolds, Ethan and his team discover that the mole has been working with Sidorov, who is actually a former IMF agent turned rogue. The true mastermind behind Ghost Protocol is revealed to be Hendricks (Jeremy Renner), a former CIA operative who was thought to have died in a previous mission.

The final act of the movie takes place at the Kremlin's launch facility, where Ethan and his team must use all their skills and resources to disable the nuclear system. In a thrilling sequence of events, they face off against Sidorov and Hendricks, who will stop at nothing to achieve their goals.

In the end, Ethan and his team succeed in disabling the launch system, but not before Hendricks is killed by Benji Dunn. The movie concludes with Ethan and his team escaping from Russia, where they are greeted as heroes. As for William Brandt, he is revealed to be a double agent working for the IMF all along.

Overall, Mission: Impossible - Ghost Protocol is an action-packed thrill ride that showcases Tom Cruise's signature stunts and impressive physicality. The movie features stunning set pieces, clever plot twists, and memorable characters that add depth to the story.

documents.title: All Star Superman
documents.tagline: The measure of a man lies not in what he says, but what he does.
documents.overview: Lex Luthor enacts his plan to rid the world of Superman, once and for all. Succeeding with solar radiation poisoning, the Man of Steel is slowly dying. With what little times remains, the Last Son of Krypton must confront the revealing of his secret identity to Lois Lane and face Luthor in a final battle.
documents.plot:
Dr. Leo Quintum and his team are exploring the Sun when they are sabotaged by a booby-trapped genetically-enhanced time-bomb clone made by Lex Luthor. Superman stops the clone but in doing so receives an overdose of solar radiation; it has given him increased powers, but is slowly killing him. Luthor is arrested thanks to Clark Kent's article and sentenced to death. When Clark visits Luthor, Clark's energy frees Parasite who Luthor kills in self-defense. He then sneaks Clark out of Stryker's Island with help from his niece Nasthalthia.
Wanting to spend as much time as possible with Lois Lane, Superman reveals to her that he is Clark Kent, and takes her to the Fortress of Solitude. During this visit, Superman's secretive behavior and her indirect exposure to alien chemicals heightens Lois' paranoia. Superman is able to calm her, explaining his caginess was to hide her birthday present, a serum granting her superpowers for 24 hours.
After having Kandor grown on another planet, Superman encounters the Kryptonian astronauts Bar-El and Lilo who have improved Earth's technology. During Superman's scuffle with them, Bar-El and Lilo come down with a Kryptonite illness because the path they followed to Earth had residue of Kryptonite. At their suggestion, Superman projects Bar-El and Lilo into the Phantom Zone until a cure can be found.
Unbeknownst to anyone, Luthor reprogrammed one of the Fortress' robots to steal the serum Superman made for Lois' birthday. Luthor gains Superman's powers, enabling him to survive execution by electric chair. Superman learns that Luthor's secret ally Solaris has betrayed him by turning Earth's sun blue. With his robots, Superman engages Solaris in space. Superman's pet Sun-Eater sacrifices itself to weaken Solaris, which allows Superman to destroy it.
Clark returns to the Daily Planet, very ill, and collapses upon completing his article, "SUPERMAN DEAD". When the staff tries to save him, they realize that he has stopped breathing and his heart has stopped. Luthor arrives with Nasthalthia and attempts to kill Lois. Clark revives and fires a gravity gun at Luthor. As his powers fade, Luthor briefly sees the world as Superman does and weeps as he gains a measure of understanding. Luthor wishes the experience to continue, but when he reaches for his next vial of serum, he realizes that Superman has stolen his supply. Superman destroys the serum over Luthor's protests, pointing out that if Luthor truly cared about solving the world's problems, he would have done so long ago. Luthor somberly admits Superman is right.
With Superman's body starting to turn into pure energy, he proclaims his love for Lois and gives her his cape as a way to remember him before he leaves and flies into the sun, seemingly sacrificing himself to save the Earth.
Quintum visits Luthor in his cell.

documents.title: The Legend of Secret Pass
documents.tagline: As the forces of Darkness and Light collide, a child holds the key...to the Secret Pass.
documents.overview: A Native American teenager named Manu spends the summer with his grandfather high in the desert mountains. As a terrifying doom approaches, Manu must embrace his remarkable destiny and take on an incredible responsibility if he and his family are to thrive and survive.
documents.plot:
The Legend of Secret Pass is a 2010 American computer-animated fantasy adventure film directed by Steve Trenbirth from a screenplay by Karl Geurs and James Costello, drawing on Native American mythology about the shape-shifting Thunderbirds. Produced through companies including JC2 Animated Entertainment, Lords Productions, Strategic Dreamers 310 Studios and Jam Filled Entertainment, it features the voices of Frankie Muniz as the teenager Manu, Graham Greene as his grandfather, Cheryl Hines as his aunt Nitika and Christy Carlson Romano as his cousin Nica, with Michael Chiklis as the villain Calabar, Ron Perlman as Parker, Joe Pantoliano as Chucksta, David Cross as Loo, and Shelley Berman and Debi Derryberry in supporting roles.

The film opens with an extended account of the legend at its heart. Hidden in the mountains of the American Southwest is a secret pass leading to Natocchue, a spiritual paradise inhabited by benevolent spirits, where lost and abandoned animals can live in peace, away from the cruelty of the human world. The animals are led there by guardians, shamans chosen by the Spirit of the Wind and gifted with extraordinary powers; in every generation the spirit selects a new guardian and entrusts him with the key that opens the way through the pass. Manu lives in the desert mountains with his grandfather, Nitika and Nica, and spends his days racing, unaware of his family's heritage. He learns that the duty of guarding the animals has been handed down through his family and that the Spirit of the Wind has chosen him as the next guardian. Meanwhile a mismatched troop of animals, fleeing an ancient magic, crosses paths with Manu and Nica as the two children escape a strange whirlwind. Together with their family and these new animal companions, the young guardian must keep the key out of the hands of Calabar, Manu's uncle and a renegade former guardian who wants to seize the immense power of Natocchue for himself.

Rotten Tomatoes lists its streaming release as 15 January 2019, and its computer animation was widely criticized as dated. Ready Steady Cut found the opening exposition overlong and the animation reminiscent of a 2004 video game, though it judged the voice casting, the banter among the animals and the underlying story reasonable.

documents.title: Possessed
documents.tagline: The savior ... came!
documents.overview: When 13-year-old So-Jin disappears, her elder sister Hee-Jin returns to the apartment of their religious-maniac mother. Tae-Hwan, a cop, who reluctantly has to take the case seriously is confronted with more and more suicides that are difficult to explain rationally. And why does the skeptical Hee-Jin, who keeps having gruesome encounters with suicides, have to keep coughing?
documents.plot:
Possessed (Korean: 불신지옥, Bulsinjiok, literally "Hell of Unbelievers"), also released as Living Death, is a 2009 South Korean horror mystery film written and directed by Lee Yong-ju in his feature debut; he had previously been an assistant director on Bong Joon-ho's Memories of Murder. Nam Sang-mi stars as the college student Hee-jin, with Ryu Seung-ryong as the detective Tae-hwan, Kim Bo-yeon as Hee-jin's mother, Shim Eun-kyung as her younger sister So-jin, Moon Hee-kyung as the shaman Kyeong-ja, Jang Young-nam as Su-kyeong, Oh Ji-eun as So-jin's friend Jeong-mi and Lee Chang-jik as a security guard.

Hee-jin, worn down by a fever and a cough she cannot shake, is struggling through exams when her teenage sister So-jin calls her at three in the morning before the line goes dead. The next day their mother rings to say So-jin has disappeared. Returning to the family's apartment, covered with crosses, Hee-jin finds her mother, a fervent evangelical Christian convinced that hell awaits nonbelievers such as her elder daughter, barely coherent and relying on prayer rather than cooperating with the police. Tae-hwan, a gruff detective, wants to write So-jin off as a runaway until Hee-jin berates him into taking the case seriously.

As the two question the residents of the apartment block, a strange community of competing faiths emerges, including a shaman and an eccentric security guard, along with a chain of deaths beginning with Jeong-mi. A neighbour commits suicide, leaving a note addressed to So-jin, rumours spread that the girl was possessed, and Hee-jin learns that So-jin has not been the same since she nearly died in a car crash two years earlier, an accident that killed their father. The dead neighbour begins to haunt Hee-jin's dreams, and as she grows more frightened, the sceptical detective stands for reason, though even he is not free of superstition, while the mystery turns into a clash between evangelical Christianity, shamanism and disbelief.

Released by Showbox in August 2009, the film drew about 250,000 admissions. Variety praised its refreshing avoidance of K-horror clichés, its slow-burning mood and its treatment of faith, while finding the script diffuse; ScreenAnarchy, reviewing its North American premiere at the 2010 Tribeca Film Festival, found it formulaic. Lee won the screenplay prize at the Blue Dragon Film Awards, and Kim Bo-yeon won best supporting actress at the Buil Film Awards.

documents.title: The Sunset Limited
documents.tagline: Nothing is ever black or white.
documents.overview: A deeply religious black ex-con thwarts the suicide attempt of an asocial white college professor who tries to throw himself in front of an oncoming subway train, 'The Sunset Limited.' As the one attempts to connect on a rational, spiritual and emotional level, the other remains steadfast in his hard-earned despair. Locked in a philosophical debate, both passionately defend their personal credos and try to convert the other.
documents.plot:
The Sunset Limited is a 2011 American drama television film directed by Tommy Lee Jones and starring Jones opposite Samuel L. Jackson. Cormac McCarthy wrote the screenplay, adapting his own 2006 two-character play of the same name. The film marked the second collaboration between Jones and Jackson, following Rules of Engagement (2000), and it pits a devout Christian against a nihilist in a single, sustained debate over the worth of living.

The characters are identified only as Black and White. Black, played by Jackson, is an ex-convict who once committed murder and lived far from God but has since been redeemed by religious faith. White, played by Jones, is a college professor so overwhelmed by despair that he has just tried to throw himself in front of a subway train, the Sunset Limited. Black has stopped him and brought him back to his spare tenement apartment in New York, and the whole of the film unfolds in that one room as the two men argue about White's attempted suicide.

White insists that everything ends in death, that any life is minuscule against the span of time, and that whatever is made, however great, eventually fades away; he sees no reason to go on enduring misery and alienation. Black takes the opposite view, holding that God exists and that the troubles of life must be borne on the way to paradise, and he recounts his own violent past and conversion as proof that a person can change. Calling the Bible a guide for the ignorant and sick at heart, he works with mounting urgency to find words that might reach White. As the conversation moves from faith and suffering to what might make life worth living, White finally launches his own forceful assault on Black's beliefs. In the unresolved ending, White leaves to return to the subway, and Black, shaken but not abandoning his faith, is left alone, crying out to God over his failure to reach him.

The film was shot in Santa Fe, New Mexico, over twelve days, alternating two-shots and close-ups to keep the confined drama visually varied. It aired on HBO on February 12, 2011. Reviews were generally favorable, with a Metacritic score of 67 and a 68% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said arch dialogue and a claustrophobic setting undercut its ambition but that the dueling performances gave weight to the battle of wills. Newsday's Verne Gay called it a chance to see two magnificent actors at the peak of their powers, and Variety found it, though not entirely successful, almost hypnotic.

documents.title: Husk
documents.tagline: Join the harvest.
documents.overview: A group of friends stranded near a desolate cornfield find shelter in an old farmhouse, though they soon discover the dwelling is the center of a supernatural ritual.
documents.plot: A group of friends stranded near a desolate cornfield find shelter in an old farmhouse, though they soon discover the dwelling is the center of a supernatural ritual.

documents.title: Hoodwinked Too! Hood VS. Evil
documents.tagline: Not All Fairy Tales Go By the Book.
documents.overview: Red Riding Hood is training in the group of Sister Hoods, when she and the Wolf are called to examine the sudden mysterious disappearance of Hansel and Gretel.
documents.plot:
Hoodwinked Too! Hood vs. Evil is an American animated comedy of 2011 directed by Mike Disa, who wrote it with Cory Edwards, Todd Edwards and Tony Leech, as a sequel to Hoodwinked! (2005). Hayden Panettiere takes over from Anne Hathaway as Red Puckett, with Patrick Warburton as Wolf, Glenn Close as Granny, Joan Cusack as the witch Verushka, Bill Hader and Amy Poehler as Hansel and Gretel, Martin Short replacing Jim Belushi as Kirk the Woodsman and Cheech Marin and Tommy Chong among the supporting voices.

Some time after the first film, Red, Granny, Wolf and the squirrel Twitchy have joined the Happily Ever After Agency. While Red is away training with the Sisters of the Hood, Wolf, Granny and Twitchy try to rescue Hansel and Gretel from a wicked witch, but the mission goes wrong and Granny is captured. Red learns that a secret, all-powerful truffle recipe has been stolen, and Detective Nicky Flippers sends her, Wolf and Twitchy to recover it and free Granny. They learn that the jailed Boingo has been sending ingredients to the witch, but she slips away, and Red and Wolf blame each other, splitting up the team.

The witch tries to force Granny to recreate the lost recipe. Granny escapes and finds Hansel and Gretel, only to discover that the siblings are the real masterminds. Recaptured, she learns the witch is Verushka Van Vine, a jealous former classmate who always came second to her. Prompted by Twitchy, Wolf decides to apologise to Red, narrowly escaping the Three Pigs, now the siblings' hired muscle. On the way to Verushka's lair, he and Twitchy rescue Red, who had been caught trying to break in alone, and the three reconcile. With help from Kirk and his yodelling troupe, they infiltrate the siblings' hideout, but Red accidentally reveals the final ingredient, macadamia nuts. Eating the finished truffles, Hansel and Gretel become huge, powerful and nearly indestructible, rampage and betray Verushka, leaving her to be eaten by her giant spider, Bitsy. Instead, Granny and the others win over Verushka and Bitsy, then trick the siblings into eating so many truffles that they grow too big to move. The pair are jailed and put on a strict diet and exercise regime, while Red and Wolf head off on a new case involving a man with a flute pursued by ten thousand mice.

Released by the Weinstein Company in April 2011, the film was a box office disappointment, grossing $23.1 million worldwide against a $30 million budget. It scored 11% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Young Adult
documents.tagline: Everyone gets old. Not everyone grows up.
documents.overview: A divorced writer from the Midwest returns to her hometown to reconnect with an old flame, who's now married with a family.
documents.plot: A divorced writer from the Midwest returns to her hometown to reconnect with an old flame, who's now married with a family.

documents.title: The Hobbit: The Desolation of Smaug
documents.original_title: The Hobbit: The Desolation of Smaug
documents.tagline: Beyond darkness... beyond desolation... lies the greatest danger of all.
documents.overview: The Dwarves, Bilbo and Gandalf have successfully escaped the Misty Mountains, and Bilbo has gained the One Ring. They all continue their journey to get their gold back from the Dragon, Smaug.
documents.plot:
Following their battle with Azog and his Orc party, Thorin Oakenshield and his company are ushered by Gandalf to the nearby home of Beorn, a skin-changer who can take the form of a bear. That night, Azog is summoned to Dol Guldur by the Necromancer, who commands him to marshal his forces for war. Azog delegates the hunt for Thorin to his son Bolg.
After telling the company about the dangers of Mirkwood, including the Necromancer's rise and the Wood-elves being dangerous, Beorn escorts the company to the borders of Mirkwood, where Gandalf discovers Black Speech imprinted on an old ruin. This, and a prior request by Galadriel, prompts him to investigate the tombs of the Nazgûl. Before leaving the company, he warns them to remain on the path. They lose their way in the forest and are ensnared by giant spiders. Bilbo frees the dwarves with the help of the invisibility ring and begins to understand its dark influence when he drops the ring and brutally kills a giant centipede to retrieve it.
The remaining spiders are killed by the Wood-elves led by Tauriel and Legolas, who capture the Dwarves and bring Thorin before their king, Thranduil. Thorin confronts the king about neglecting the Dwarves of Erebor following Smaug's attack 60 years earlier and is consequently imprisoned with the other Dwarves. Having avoided capture, Bilbo helps them escape in empty wine barrels sent downstream. They are pursued by Wood-elves and ambushed by Bolg and his Orc party, resulting in a three-way battle as they rush down the river in the barrels. The Dwarves escape both groups of pursuers, but Kíli is wounded with a Morgul shaft. Thranduil seals off his kingdom when an Orc captive reveals that an evil army is amassing in the south, but Tauriel decides to leave and assist the Dwarves, and Legolas goes after her. Gandalf and Radagast investigate the tombs of the Nazgûl and find them empty. Gandalf discovers that the Nine have been called to Dol Guldur, deducing that Sauron has returned and is preparing for war.
The company is smuggled into Esgaroth by a bargeman called Bard. Thorin promises the Master of Laketown a share of the mountain's treasure, and they are given arms and sent off to the mountain. Due to his injury, Kíli is forced to remain behind at Bard's home, tended to by Fíli, Óin, and Bofur. Bilbo discovers the hidden entrance in the Lonely Mountain and is sent inside to retrieve the Arkenstone. However, he accidentally awakens Smaug, who reveals his knowledge of the dwarves' plot.
In Laketown, Bard, a descendant of Dale's last ruler, prepares his ancestor's last black arrow in fear of an attack by Smaug, but is arrested by the Master. Bolg and his Orcs infiltrate Laketown and attack the four Dwarves, but Tauriel and Legolas arrive to defeat them, while Bolg escapes.
Meanwhile, Gandalf enters Dol Guldur alone after sending Radagast to warn Galadriel of their discovery at the tombs. The Necromancer overpowers Gandalf and reveals himself as Sauron.

documents.title: Wrath of the Titans
documents.tagline: Feel the Wrath
documents.overview: Perseus tries to live a quieter life as a village fisherman while - dangerously weakened by humanity's lack of devotion - the gods are losing control of the long-imprisoned Titans and their ferocious leader, Kronos.
documents.plot:
Wrath of the Titans is a 2012 American fantasy adventure film directed by Jonathan Liebesman and written by Dan Abnett, Andy Bean, and Stephen Morgan. The movie is a sequel to the 2010 film Clash of the Titans.

The story begins with Perseus (Sam Worthington), the demigod son of Zeus, living in ancient Greece with his wife, Andromeda (Rosamund Pike), and their daughter, Helen (Talia Balsam). However, their peaceful life is disrupted when Hades (Danny Huston), the god of the underworld, kidnaps Perseus' wife and threatens to marry her unless Zeus sends one of his own children as a ransom.

Perseus sets out on a perilous journey to rescue Andromeda, accompanied by the wise man Cratus (Liam Neeson) and the warrior Athena (Gemma Arterton). Along the way, they encounter various mythological creatures, including the Minotaur, Medusa, and the Cyclops Polyphemus.

As Perseus navigates the underworld, he discovers that Hades has stolen Zeus' lightning bolt, which gives him immense power. The gods of Olympus are powerless without their most powerful weapon, and Hades plans to use it to conquer the world.

Perseus eventually reaches Hades' throne room, where he confronts his father-in-law and engages in a fierce battle with the god of the underworld. With the help of Athena and Cratus, Perseus manages to defeat Hades and shatter his helmet, rendering him powerless.

However, the journey is not without its costs. Perseus' mother, Queen Calliope (Polly Shannon), is killed by Hades, and he also suffers a mortal wound. As he lies dying, Athena uses her powers to heal him, but at great personal cost.

The movie concludes with Perseus returning to Greece as a hero, having saved the world from Hades' tyranny. However, the film ends on a somber note, suggesting that Perseus' journey has changed him forever and that he may not be the same demigod who set out at the beginning of the story.

Overall, Wrath of the Titans is an action-packed adventure film with plenty of mythological creatures and epic battles. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the original Clash of the Titans were pleased to see their favorite characters return in a new and exciting way.

keywords.name: based on myths, legends or folklore

documents.title: The Lone Ranger
documents.tagline: Never Take Off the Mask
documents.overview: The Texas Rangers chase down a gang of outlaws led by Butch Cavendish, but the gang ambushes the Rangers, seemingly killing them all. One survivor is found, however, by an American Indian named Tonto, who nurses him back to health. The Ranger, donning a mask and riding a white stallion named Silver, teams up with Tonto to bring the unscrupulous gang and others of that ilk to justice.
documents.plot:
The Lone Ranger is a 2013 American Western action-adventure film directed by Gore Verbinski and written by Ted Elliott and Terry Rossio. The movie is a remake of the classic 1938 serial of the same name, starring Johnny Depp as Tonto and Armie Hammer as the Lone Ranger.

The story begins in 1837, where we meet John Reid (Armie Hammer), a young Texas Ranger who is part of a group tasked with capturing the notorious outlaw Butch Cavendish (William Fichtner). During the mission, Reid's brother, Dan (James Badge Dale), is killed by Cavendish. Reid is left traumatized and vows to hunt down Cavendish.

Years later, in 1861, Reid is recruited by Chief Big Bear (Wes Studi) of the Comanche tribe to join him on a quest for revenge against Butch Cavendish, who has taken over the town of Red Rock and is terrorizing its residents. Reid meets Tonto (Johnny Depp), a mysterious and skilled warrior from the Comanche tribe.

Initially, Reid and Tonto have a rocky relationship due to their vastly different backgrounds and cultures. However, as they embark on their mission, they develop a strong bond and learn to trust each other. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, rival tribes, and Cavendish's henchmen.

As Reid and Tonto get closer to their goal, they realize that Cavendish is being manipulated by a wealthy industrialist named Marcus (Tommy Lee Jones). The industrialist has been using his wealth and influence to drive the Comanche out of their land and exploit its resources. Reid and Tonto must now confront not only Cavendish but also the corrupt industrialist.

The final confrontation takes place in Red Rock, where Reid and Tonto face off against Cavendish and Marcus. In a thrilling showdown, Reid and Tonto work together to defeat the villains and bring justice to the town.

Throughout the movie, there are several themes that emerge, including the importance of friendship, loyalty, and cultural understanding. The relationship between Reid and Tonto is particularly noteworthy, as they learn to put aside their differences and trust each other in order to achieve their goal.

The film features impressive action sequences, stunning cinematography, and memorable performances from its cast. While some critics felt that the movie deviated too far from the original serial, it remains a thrilling adventure that pays homage to the classic tale while also offering something new and exciting.

Overall, The Lone Ranger is an entertaining and visually stunning film that explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and cultural understanding in the context of the American West.

documents.title: War Horse
documents.tagline: Separated by war. Tested by battle. Bound by friendship.
documents.overview: Young Albert enlists to serve in World War I after his beloved horse is sold to the cavalry.
documents.plot:
War Horse is a 2011 epic war drama film directed by Steven Spielberg, based on the novel of the same name by Michael Morpurgo.

The story begins in 1914, on a farm in Devon, England, where a young boy named Albert Narracott (played by Jeremy Irvine) lives with his mother and father. The family owns a horse named Joey, a beautiful chestnut gelding who is Albert's best friend. However, their peaceful life is disrupted when the war breaks out, and the British army requisitions all horses for military use.

The Narracotts are forced to sell Joey to the cavalry, and he is sent off to France with the 13th Hussars. Meanwhile, Albert is left behind, feeling heartbroken and helpless. He writes a letter to Joey, which becomes his only connection to the horse.

As the war rages on, Joey faces numerous challenges and dangers, including being captured by the German army and sold to a French farmer named Pierre Bonnasse (played by Benedict Cumberbatch). Despite being mistreated and struggling to survive, Joey remains loyal and determined to return home.

Meanwhile, Albert grows up and joins the British army, hoping to find his beloved horse. He eventually becomes a lieutenant and is sent to France, where he searches for Joey. Along the way, he meets a young French girl named Emilie (played by Emily Mortimer), who helps him on his quest.

As the war intensifies, Albert and Joey are reunited in a dramatic and emotional scene. However, their reunion is short-lived, as they are separated again when Albert is injured and left behind. Joey continues to survive, facing many more challenges and dangers before finally being rescued by Albert's brother, Ted (played by Tom Hiddleston).

The film ends with Albert and his family reunited with Joey, who has been through unimaginable hardships but remains loyal and true to his owner. The story is a powerful tribute to the bond between humans and animals, as well as the devastating effects of war on individuals and communities.

Throughout the film, Spielberg uses stunning cinematography and heart-wrenching performances to bring the story to life. The film's themes of loyalty, sacrifice, and the human-animal connection are timeless and universal, making War Horse a moving and unforgettable cinematic experience.

documents.title: Project X
documents.tagline: Witness it
documents.overview: Three high school seniors throw a party to make a name for themselves. As the night progresses, things spiral out of control as word of the party spreads.
documents.plot:
Project X is a 2012 American found-footage teen comedy directed by Nima Nourizadeh in his feature debut, written by Michael Bacall and Matt Drake and produced by Todd Phillips. Thomas Mann, Oliver Cooper and Jonathan Daniel Brown star as three friends who throw a party that spirals out of control, with Kirby Bliss Blanton, Dax Flame, Alexis Knapp and Miles Teller. The film was loosely associated with a notorious 2008 party thrown by an Australian teenager whose online invitation drew hundreds of uninvited guests.

In Pasadena, California, high-school students Costa and J.B. plan a party for their friend Thomas Kub's seventeenth birthday, hoping to boost their popularity. Thomas's parents leave town for the weekend, warning him not to invite too many people and not to drive his father's Mercedes. Thomas is reluctant, but Costa pushes ahead and hires Dax, an audiovisual student, to film the night's events. While Costa and J.B. spread word of the party around school, Thomas invites his best friend Kirby, who secretly has feelings for him, and Alexis, a popular girl he has a crush on. Shopping for supplies, the boys bump into Miles Teller, who already knows about the party. They then buy marijuana from a drug dealer, T-Rick, and Costa steals his lawn gnome as a party mascot, provoking a chase.

At first nobody arrives, and Thomas fears the party will be a flop, but then guests start pouring in by the hundreds. Thomas tries to confine the party to the backyard and pool house, hiring two young security guards to protect the house, but the crowd swells as news spreads online and on the radio. Neighbors complain, police are deceived into leaving, and the chaos escalates: the house is overrun, a car ends up in the swimming pool, Thomas's romantic life becomes tangled between Kirby and Alexis, and T-Rick returns seeking revenge, armed with a flamethrower, as the party turns into a riot visible from news helicopters and fires spread across the neighborhood.

Project X received generally negative reviews, with critics condemning its depiction of reckless behavior, though some praised its energy. It was a box-office success, grossing over $100 million worldwide against a budget of about $12 million, and inspired a number of real-life party incidents.

documents.title: Megamind: The Button of Doom
documents.tagline: His Brain Is Off The Chain
documents.overview: For their first day on the job as the new protectors of Metro City, Megamind and Minion are selling off the gadgets from their evil lair. But when one seemingly harmless "button" unleashes the gigantic robot MEGA-MEGAmind, the duo will have to resort to their old tricks to restore order.
documents.plot: For their first day on the job as the new protectors of Metro City, Megamind and Minion are selling off the gadgets from their evil lair. But when one seemingly harmless "button" unleashes the gigantic robot MEGA-MEGAmind, the duo will have to resort to their old tricks to restore order.

documents.title: Barbie: A Fairy Secret
documents.tagline: Barbie lets you in on a secret...
documents.overview: Get ready for Barbie: A Fairy Secret, an amazing adventure with Barbie where she discovers there are fairies living secretly all around us! When Ken is suddenly whisked away by a group of fairies, Barbie's two fashion stylist friends reveal they are actually fairies and that Ken has been taken to a magical secret fairy world not far away! Barbie and her rival Raquelle take off with the fairy friends on an action-packed journey to bring him back. Along the way they must stick together and learn that the real magic lies not just in the fairy world itself, but in the power of friendship.
documents.plot:
Barbie: A Fairy Secret is a 2011 animated fantasy film directed by William Lau, written by Elise Allen and produced by Rainmaker Entertainment, the nineteenth entry in the Barbie film series. Diana Kaarina returns as the voice of Barbie, with Adrian Petriw as Ken, and the story shares its world with Barbie: A Fashion Fairytale (2010). It was released on DVD on March 15, 2011, and premiered on Nickelodeon the following month.

Barbie is attending the premiere of her latest film with her actor boyfriend Ken when her co-star and rival Raquelle steps on her gown and tears it. Her stylists Carrie and Taylor, who are secretly fairies, repair it with magic. A photographer named Crystal takes a picture of Ken and returns to Gloss Angeles, a hidden realm of fairies, where she shows it to Princess Graciella after slipping a love potion into her tea. The princess instantly falls for Ken, and the next day, during a quarrel between Barbie and Raquelle, Graciella and her attendants swoop in and carry him off through a portal.

Carrie and Taylor are forced to admit to the astonished Barbie and Raquelle that fairies exist, and explain that if a human marries a fairy, he must remain in the fairy world forever. In Gloss Angeles, Ken faces the fury of Graciella's boyfriend Zane, who challenges him to a series of duels. Barbie, Raquelle and the stylists travel by a magical Fairy Flyway to Paris, where the renowned fashion critic Lilianna Roxelle, the oldest and wisest fairy on Earth, reveals that the princess is under a love spell and gives Barbie an antidote. She also reveals that Carrie and Taylor were banished from the fairy realm.

In Gloss Angeles, the group buy fake wings and disguise themselves as cooks to reach the princess, but Crystal unmasks them and they are imprisoned. Trapped together, Barbie and Raquelle finally talk, and Raquelle admits she was hostile only because she never had the chance to be Barbie's friend. Their reconciliation breaks their prison and gives them real wings. They interrupt the wedding and Barbie sprinkles the antidote over Graciella.

Freed from the spell, the princess realises Crystal's deception and explains that she banished Carrie and Taylor because she felt abandoned by her old friends, and the three reconcile. Graciella marries Zane, punishes Crystal and sends the humans home, erasing their memories. Barbie wakes believing it was all a dream, but she and Raquelle are now friends, and Carrie and Taylor fly back to Gloss Angeles.

documents.title: Ice Age: Continental Drift
documents.tagline: The End of the World is Just the Tip of the Iceberg.
documents.overview: Manny, Diego, and Sid embark upon another adventure after their continent is set adrift. Using an iceberg as a ship, they encounter sea creatures and battle pirates as they explore a new world.
documents.plot:
Ice Age: Continental Drift is a 2012 animated adventure comedy film produced by 20th Century Fox. The movie serves as the fourth installment in the Ice Age franchise and follows the adventures of Manny, Sid, Diego, and Scrat as they embark on a perilous journey to save their home from destruction.

The story begins with Manny (voiced by Ray Romano), a woolly mammoth, who is struggling to come to terms with his impending doom. According to an ancient prophecy, the continents are destined to drift apart, causing the ice age to end and the world as they know it to cease to exist. The prophecy also states that the only way to prevent this catastrophe is for Manny to find the fabled "Frosty" – a magical crystal that can reverse the process.

Manny sets out on his journey with his friends Sid (voiced by John Leguizamo), a goofy and lovable sloth, and Diego (voiced by Denis Leary), a cunning saber-toothed tiger. Along the way, they encounter Scrat (voiced by Chris Wedge), Manny's obsessive acorn-loving companion, who is also on a quest to find his beloved snack.

As the group navigates through treacherous landscapes and encounters various obstacles, they begin to realize that their journey is not just about saving their home but also about learning to work together and trust each other. Along the way, they meet new characters, including Buck (voiced by Josh Peck), a young saber-toothed tiger who becomes Diego's protégé.

As the story unfolds, Manny and his friends face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, ferocious predators, and even their own personal demons. However, through it all, they remain determined to find Frosty and save their home.

In the end, Manny and his friends successfully locate Frosty, but not before realizing that the true power of friendship and teamwork is what truly matters. The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment of closure for the characters as they return home, forever changed by their journey together.

Throughout the film, the animation is stunning, with beautifully rendered landscapes and lovable character designs. The voice cast delivers memorable performances, bringing depth and humor to the story. Overall, Ice Age: Continental Drift is a fun and entertaining adventure that explores themes of friendship, perseverance, and the power of believing in oneself.

documents.title: Area 51
documents.tagline: They're Here.
documents.overview: Three young conspiracy theorists attempt to uncover the mysteries of Area 51, the government's secret location rumored to have hosted encounters with alien beings. What they find at this hidden facility exposes unimaginable secrets.
documents.plot: Three young conspiracy theorists attempt to uncover the mysteries of Area 51, the government's secret location rumored to have hosted encounters with alien beings. What they find at this hidden facility exposes unimaginable secrets.

documents.title: Fright Night
documents.tagline: You can't run from evil when it lives next door
documents.overview: A teenager suspects his new neighbour is a vampire. Unable to convince anyone, he tries to enlist the help of a self-proclaimed vampire hunter and magician.
documents.plot: A teenager suspects his new neighbour is a vampire. Unable to convince anyone, he tries to enlist the help of a self-proclaimed vampire hunter and magician.

documents.title: Chalet Girl
documents.tagline: How to marry a billionaire.
documents.overview: While working a job at an exclusive ski resort to support her Dad, Kim learns to snowboard and is so good at it that she enters a competition with a huge cash prize. She has to dig deep to overcome her fears, but her life gets more complicated through her spoken-for boss, Jonny.
documents.plot:
Chalet Girl is a 2011 British romantic comedy-drama film that explores the theme of self-discovery and empowerment through the lens of a young woman's journey to find her place in the world. The movie follows the story of Kim Matthews, a teenager from a troubled home who finds solace and confidence while working as a ski instructor at a chalet resort.

As Kim navigates her relationships with her colleagues and clients, she begins to shed her insecurities and assert herself, discovering a sense of purpose and belonging. Through her experiences, the film highlights the importance of female friendship, support, and camaraderie in helping women overcome their personal struggles and find their voice.

The movie also touches on themes of class and social status, as Kim's working-class background is contrasted with the more affluent clientele she encounters at the chalet resort. This dichotomy serves to underscore the film's exploration of identity, class, and privilege, raising questions about how these factors shape our experiences and relationships.

Ultimately, Chalet Girl is a heartwarming and uplifting film that celebrates the power of female friendship, self-discovery, and personal growth, offering a relatable and inspiring portrayal of a young woman's journey towards empowerment and independence.

documents.title: Johnny English Reborn
documents.tagline: A little intelligence goes a long way
documents.overview: The most prominent heads of state in the world begin gathering for a conference that could have a major impact on global politics. When MI-7 receives word that the Chinese premier has become the target of some high-powered killers, it falls on Johnny English to save the day. Armed with the latest high-tech weaponry and gadgets that would make even James Bond jealous, the once-disgraced agent uncovers evidence of a massive conspiracy involving some of the world's most powerful organisations, and vows to redeem his tarnished reputation by stopping the killers before they can strike.
documents.plot:
Johnny English Reborn is a 2011 spy comedy film directed by Oliver Parker and starring Rowan Atkinson as the titular character, Johnny English.

The movie begins with Johnny English, a bumbling but lovable British spy, who has been retired from active duty due to his ineptitude. However, when a former KGB agent named Dominic (played by Ross Kemp) is released from prison after serving time for treason, Johnny is forced back into action to stop him.

As Johnny delves deeper into the world of espionage once again, he discovers that Dominic has stolen a deadly virus known as "The Phoenix," which can be used to create an army of mindless drones. The virus is being sold on the black market, and it's up to Johnny to track down the buyer and prevent a global catastrophe.

Along the way, Johnny teams up with his new partner, Nancy (played by Natalie Imbruglia), a tough and capable agent who is initially skeptical of Johnny's abilities. As they work together, they develop a romantic connection, which adds an extra layer of complexity to their mission.

As the plot thickens, Johnny and Nancy find themselves in a series of hilarious misadventures, from infiltrating a high-stakes poker game to escaping from a group of henchmen. Despite his best efforts, Johnny consistently manages to botch his missions, leading to plenty of comedic moments.

However, as the stakes grow higher, Johnny begins to prove himself to be more than just a bumbling spy. He uses his unique skills and resourcefulness to outwit his enemies and stay one step ahead of Dominic's henchmen.

In the end, Johnny and Nancy successfully stop Dominic from selling the Phoenix virus, but not before he escapes with it. In a thrilling finale, Johnny and Nancy track down Dominic to an abandoned warehouse, where they engage in a high-speed car chase through the streets of London.

As the dust settles, Johnny emerges victorious, having saved the world from certain destruction. The movie ends on a romantic note, with Johnny and Nancy sharing a kiss as the credits roll.

Throughout the film, Rowan Atkinson's signature physical comedy and wit shine through, making Johnny English Reborn a hilarious and entertaining ride. Despite its lighthearted tone, the movie also explores themes of redemption and self-discovery, as Johnny learns to come to terms with his own limitations and find success in his own unique way.

Overall, Johnny English Reborn is a fun and action-packed spy comedy that will keep you laughing from start to finish. With its witty dialogue, physical humor, and charming performances, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

documents.title: Confessions of a Brazilian Call Girl
documents.tagline: The story of a family girl. Until take 2.
documents.overview: Rachel is a girl, adopted by an upper middle class family, who rebelled at 17 and left her family and studies at a traditional college in Sao Paulo to become a call girl. Shortly after starting work, she decided to write a blog about her experiences. Since some clients thought she looked like a surfer she adopted the name "Surfistinha" which means little surfer girl.
documents.plot: Seventeen-year-old Raquel Pacheco, who is adopted by an upper-middle-class family, decides to leave her adoptive family and studies at a traditional school in São Paulo behind to become a prostitute, and later a call girl. Shortly after starting work, she decides to write a blog about her experiences. Since some clients thought she looked like a surfer, she adopts the name "Surfistinha", which means "little surfer girl". Her blog becomes a sensation, and quickly becomes one of the most popular blogs in Brazil. Becoming famous, her life changes significantly. She goes on to be interviewed on Brazilian talk shows similar to Oprah and David Letterman, all the while continuing her blog about her racy exploits. However, soon afterwards the fame gets to her in the form of a drug addiction, which makes her do almost anything for a hit.

documents.title: Upside Down
documents.tagline: Two worlds. One future.
documents.overview: In an alternate universe where twinned worlds have opposite gravities, a young man battles interplanetary prejudice and the laws of physics in his quest to reunite with the long-lost girl of his dreams in this visually stunning romantic adventure that poses the question: what if love was stronger than gravity?
documents.plot: In an alternate universe where twinned worlds have opposite gravities, a young man battles interplanetary prejudice and the laws of physics in his quest to reunite with the long-lost girl of his dreams in this visually stunning romantic adventure that poses the question: what if love was stronger than gravity?

documents.title: Pride and Prejudice and Zombies
documents.tagline: Bloody lovely.
documents.overview: A zombie outbreak has fallen upon the land in this reimagining of Jane Austen's classic tale of the tangled relationships between lovers from different social classes in 19th century England. Feisty heroine Elizabeth Bennet is a master of martial arts and weaponry and the handsome Mr. Darcy is a fierce zombie killer, yet the epitome of upper class prejudice. As the zombie outbreak intensifies, they must swallow their pride and join forces on the blood-soaked battlefield in order to conquer the undead once and for all.
documents.plot:
Pride and Prejudice and Zombies, stylized as Pride + Prejudice + Zombies, is a 2016 action comedy horror film based on Seth Grahame-Smith's 2009 novel of the same name, itself a parody of Jane Austen's 1813 classic Pride and Prejudice. Written and directed by Burr Steers, it stars Lily James as Elizabeth Bennet and Sam Riley as Mr. Darcy, with Jack Huston, Bella Heathcote, Douglas Booth, Matt Smith, Charles Dance and Lena Headey in supporting roles. The film follows the general outline of Austen's novel while adding a plague of the undead.

In an early nineteenth-century England overrun by zombies, the five Bennet sisters, Elizabeth, Jane, Kitty, Lydia and Mary, have been trained by their father in weaponry and Chinese martial arts so they can defend themselves, while their mother is chiefly concerned with marrying them off to wealthy men. At a country ball the Bennets meet newcomers including the amiable and rich Charles Bingley, who is immediately taken with Jane, and Colonel Darcy, an aloof but formidable zombie hunter trained in Japanese martial arts. When the undead attack the ball, the sisters fight them off, and Darcy is quietly impressed by Elizabeth's skill, though his outward coldness and contempt for Mrs. Bennet's mercenary ambitions offend her.

Elizabeth is drawn to the charming officer George Wickham, who tells her that Darcy cheated him out of his inheritance and who claims that some zombies can be kept civilized by feeding them pig brains. When Darcy proposes, Elizabeth rejects him, angered by his role in separating Jane from Bingley, and the two literally come to blows. A letter from Darcy later reveals Wickham's true character. After Wickham runs off with Lydia and London falls to the undead, Darcy discovers that Wickham has been building a zombie army in a bid to rule the country. In the ensuing battle Wickham is exposed as undead himself, and Darcy is wounded as the army destroys a bridge to stop the horde. Elizabeth admits her love, accepts his second proposal, and the couple share a double wedding with Jane and Bingley, before a mid-credits scene shows Wickham's army arriving.

The film spent years in development, passing through directors including David O. Russell, Mike White and Craig Gillespie, with Natalie Portman originally set to star before remaining only as a producer. Burr Steers took over in 2013. Released in February 2016, it received mixed reviews and was a box office disappointment.

documents.title: Senna
documents.tagline: No Fear. No Limits. No Equal.
documents.overview: The remarkable story of Brazilian racing driver Ayrton Senna, charting his physical and spiritual achievements on the track and off, his quest for perfection, and the mythical status he has since attained, is the subject of Senna, a documentary feature that spans the racing legend's years as an F1 driver, from his opening season in 1984 to his untimely death a decade later.
documents.plot:
Senna is a 2010 documentary directed by Asif Kapadia about the life and death of the Brazilian Formula One champion Ayrton Senna. It follows his career from his debut at the 1984 Brazilian Grand Prix to his fatal crash at the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix, with particular emphasis on his rivalry with Alain Prost. It avoids narration and "talking head" interviews, using archival footage, voiceovers and Senna family home movies.

The film opens with footage of a young Senna racing go-karts, as he later recalls that in those days there was "no money, no politics – it was real racing." After brief early spells with Toleman and Lotus, Senna joins McLaren and becomes world champion. He clashes with his teammate Prost and with the sport's powerful regulator, Jean-Marie Balestre, and wins three titles in four years. The rivalry peaks in 1989 and 1990, when controversial collisions between the two decide the championship, and Senna blames Balestre's rulings for costing him the 1989 title. In 1991 he finally wins his home Grand Prix despite gearbox failure. A national icon, he champions driver safety and helps poor children in Brazil.

In 1992 and 1993, the computer-controlled cars of the rival Williams team dominate, and Senna watches Nigel Mansell and then Prost win the title. Prost, still resentful, blocks Senna from joining Williams. Senna takes Prost's seat for 1994 just as new rules ban the team's electronic aids. Williams struggles, and Senna suspects Benetton, whose Michael Schumacher wins the opening races, of cheating. The San Marino Grand Prix weekend brings crash after crash: Rubens Barrichello is badly hurt on Friday, Roland Ratzenberger is killed on Saturday, and two cars collide on race day. Shortly afterward, Senna crashes fatally after a mechanical failure. The film ends with his funeral and notes that no Formula One driver had died since, and that his family founded the Instituto Ayrton Senna to continue his charitable work.

After a screening at the 2010 Japanese Grand Prix, it premiered in São Paulo. It opened in Brazil in November 2010 and in the United Kingdom in June 2011. Rotten Tomatoes reported 93% approval, promising thrills and heartbreak even for non-fans. Empire called it deeply compelling, and The New York Times praised its editing while noting that viewers unfamiliar with the sport might find some episodes confusing. At the BAFTA Awards it won Best Documentary and Best Editing and was nominated for Outstanding British Film.

documents.title: 10 Years
documents.tagline: Who Got Fat? Who Didn't Change? Who Got Rich? Who Got Hot?
documents.overview: A group of friends reunite ten years after their high-school graduation.
documents.plot:
10 Years is a 2011 American independent romantic comedy film written and directed by Jamie Linden in his directorial debut. Set over a single night at a ten-year high school reunion, it features an ensemble cast including Channing Tatum, Jenna Dewan, Justin Long, Kate Mara, Rosario Dawson, Oscar Isaac, Chris Pratt, Aubrey Plaza and Anthony Mackie.

On the day of the reunion, Jake and his girlfriend, Jess, arrive at the home of his old friends Cully and Sam, now married. Others gather, including best friends Marty and AJ, the famous musician Reeves, and the adventurous Scott with his wife, Suki, and at the reunion they meet up with Garrity, his wife, Olivia, and his best friend, Andre. Elise, a reclusive classmate, arrives alone and is ignored by the organizer, former prom queen Anna. Jake shows his friends an engagement ring he has long meant to give Jess, but he is thrown when he meets his high school sweetheart, Mary, and her husband, Paul. Reeves reminisces with Elise after spotting an old photo of her in bright yellow shoes. Cully drunkenly attempts to apologize to classmates he bullied, and Marty and AJ compete for Anna. Jake and Mary recall the prom they never attended because her father had a heart attack that night.

The group moves on to a karaoke bar. Noticing Jake's behavior around Mary, Jess returns to the hotel, as does Paul. Pressured by his friends, Reeves sings his hit song "Never Had", and the line about yellow shoes tells Elise that it is about her; they kiss and spend the night together. Catching Marty and AJ toilet-papering her house, Anna reveals that she is an unhappy single mother of two, and the men admit their own failures: Marty is broke and AJ is divorcing. Cully's drunkenness upsets Sam, and Scott announces that he and Suki are returning to Japan. Mary asks Jake for the dance they missed at prom, giving them closure; she reveals that she is pregnant, and both agree they are happy with their lives. Back at the hotel, Jess tells Jake she left so that he could make his peace with Mary, and as they join their friends at a diner, Jake retrieves the ring from his car.

Shot around Albuquerque, the film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2011 but received only a limited theatrical release on September 14, 2012, grossing under $1 million. Reviews were mixed to positive, with 60% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 67; critics called it sweet and well cast but predictable.

documents.title: Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows
documents.original_title: Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows
documents.tagline: The game is afoot.
documents.overview: There is a new criminal mastermind at large (Professor Moriarty) and not only is he Holmes’ intellectual equal, but his capacity for evil and lack of conscience may give him an advantage over the  detective.
documents.plot:
Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows is a 2011 action mystery film directed by Guy Ritchie, starring Robert Downey Jr. as Sherlock Holmes and Jude Law as Dr. John Watson.

The movie begins with Sherlock Holmes (Robert Downey Jr.) and Dr. John Watson (Jude Law) living in London, England, in the year 1891. The story starts with a mysterious woman named Irene Adler (Rachel McAdams), who is revealed to be a former adversary of Holmes'. She has been presumed dead for years but returns, seeking revenge against Holmes.

Meanwhile, a series of murders takes place across Europe, all connected to a mysterious figure known as the "Severing Hand". The victims are all members of a secret society called the "Thaddeus Wadja" or "The Thaddeus Society", which is dedicated to the study and practice of alchemy.

As Holmes delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that the murders are linked to an ancient text known as the "Severing Hand's" manifesto. The text reveals a plan to unleash a deadly poison on London, which would kill millions of people.

Holmes and Watson team up with Irene Adler, who has her own reasons for wanting to stop the Severing Hand. Together, they embark on a thrilling adventure across Europe, following a trail of clues that lead them from Paris to Vienna.

As the story unfolds, Holmes' mental health is put to the test when he begins to experience hallucinations and paranoia. He becomes convinced that his arch-nemesis, Professor Moriarty (Jared Harris), has returned and is behind the murders.
