documents.title: Sundays at Tiffany's
documents.overview: Jane, a soon-to-be-married woman, is reunited with her imaginary friend Michael who returns in a human form. Soon, Jane begins doubting her feelings for her fiance as she gets attracted to Michael.
documents.plot:
Sundays at Tiffany's is a 2010 American romantic fantasy television film directed by Mark Piznarski for Lifetime, adapted from the 2008 novel of the same name by James Patterson and Gabrielle Charbonnet. Alyssa Milano, who also served as an executive producer, stars as Jane Claremont, with Eric Winter as her imaginary friend Michael, Ivan Sergei as her fiancé Hugh and Stockard Channing as her mother Vivian; Kristin Booth and Emily Alyn Lind, as the young Jane, also appear. The score is by Mateo Messina.

As a lonely girl in New York, Jane spends her Sundays at Tiffany's with her mother, a cold, controlling theatre producer embittered by her divorce, and brings along Michael, a boy of her own age whom only she can see. On Christmas Eve, which is also Jane's birthday, Michael explains that under the rules governing imaginary friends he must leave once she turns ten, and he vanishes from her life. Years later Jane is a successful businesswoman working alongside her mother at the theatre and is engaged to Hugh, a famous actor who seems more in love with his career than with her, with the wedding set for her birthday on Christmas Eve. Outwardly she insists that her life is perfect, but she has doubts, and her mother is more interested in controlling her than supporting her. Then Michael unexpectedly reappears, now a grown man and visible to everyone, having been summoned without her realizing it because she needs guidance. At first shocked and in denial, Jane gradually grows attached to him, rediscovering the value of simple things, while Michael adapts to the human world, finds work as a chef and begins to experience human feelings. Their friendship turns into love, and Hugh comes to see Michael as a threat. When Michael admits that the rules require him to leave her again on her birthday, the hurt Jane refuses to see him. On Christmas Eve, during the ceremony itself, she realizes her relationship with Hugh is loveless and calls off the wedding, only to find that Michael, against all expectations, has not disappeared and has become human, free to stay with her.

The film was shot in Toronto and on location between September 8 and October 1, 2010. Milano said she was drawn to the original concept and its flawed characters, and enjoyed reuniting with Winter and Sergei, with whom she had worked on Charmed. It premiered on Lifetime on December 6, 2010, drawing about 2.1 million viewers.

documents.title: Red Dawn
documents.tagline: Welcome to the Home of the Brave
documents.overview: A city in Washington state awakens to the surreal sight of foreign paratroopers dropping from the sky—shockingly, the U.S. has been invaded and their hometown is the initial target. Quickly and without warning, the citizens find themselves prisoners and their town under enemy occupation. Determined to fight back, a group of young patriots seek refuge in the surrounding woods, training and reorganizing themselves into a guerrilla group of fighters.
documents.plot:
Red Dawn is a 2012 American action film directed by Marc Webb and written by Chris Kerouac. The movie is a remake of the 1984 film of the same name, which was itself an adaptation of the Japanese novel "Battle Beyond the Stars" (, Sen no Rondo) by Yoshikazu Takeuchi.

The story begins with a group of teenagers living in the small town of Evergreen, Colorado, where they are preparing for their high school prom. The main characters include Jed Eckert (Chris Hemsworth), his brother Matt (Wiley Wiggins), and their friends Chris Hargensen (Alexandra Daddario) and Gage (Josh Peck).

As tensions rise between the United States and China, a group of Chinese soldiers invade Evergreen, killing many of the townspeople. The surviving teenagers take up arms to fight back against the invaders, with Jed becoming the leader of the resistance.

The group consists of Jed's brother Matt, Chris, Gage, and several other local teenagers who are determined to defend their home. They use guerrilla warfare tactics, including ambushes and sabotage, to harass and disrupt the Chinese forces.

As the battle between the Americans and the Chinese intensifies, Jed becomes increasingly obsessed with avenging his family's death and defeating the enemy. He also begins to develop feelings for Chris, who is initially hesitant to join the fight but eventually becomes a key member of the resistance.

The movie follows the group as they face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, limited resources, and internal conflicts. Along the way, Jed and his team encounter other groups of rebels, including a group of Russian soldiers who are fighting against the Chinese invasion.

As the final battle approaches, Jed's leadership is tested, and he must make difficult decisions to ensure the survival of his team. The movie culminates in an intense showdown between the Americans and the Chinese forces, with Jed facing off against the enemy commander.

In the end, Jed emerges victorious, but not without sacrifices. The movie ends on a bittersweet note, with Jed reflecting on the cost of war and the importance of protecting one's home.

Overall, Red Dawn is an action-packed thriller that explores themes of patriotism, loyalty, and sacrifice. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has its fans among action enthusiasts who appreciate its intense fight scenes and suspenseful plot.

documents.title: The Suite Life Movie
documents.overview: Cody and Zack are approached to join the Gemini Project, a high-tech research center studying the dynamics between twins. Shockingly, they find themselves interconnected in a whole new way! When one twin experiences something, the other twin feels it too. This newfound revelation helps them see eye to eye for the first time, and it puts them in more danger than they could have imagined.
documents.plot:
The Suite Life Movie is a 2011 American science fiction comedy-drama television film directed by Sean McNamara and written by Michael Saltzman. A Disney Channel Original Movie based on the sitcom The Suite Life on Deck, itself a spin-off of The Suite Life of Zack & Cody, it stars Dylan and Cole Sprouse, who also served as executive producers, alongside Brenda Song, Debby Ryan, Matthew Timmons, John Ducey, Matthew Glave and Phill Lewis. It premiered on Disney Channel on March 25, 2011.

Cody Martin cancels his spring break plans with his girlfriend Bailey Pickett and leaves the cruise ship SS Tipton, where he attends school, to take an internship with Dr. Donald Spaulding at a prestigious research institute, hoping to win a scholarship to Yale. Bailey is so upset that she stops speaking to him. Meanwhile, his twin brother Zack wants the car their parents promised Cody for college, and Cody refuses to give it up. When Zack crashes a billion-dollar research submarine into a seawall while showing off, and Cody wrecks another trying to stop him, Cody is fired and angrily declares that, though they are twins, they are not brothers. Elsewhere, heiress London Tipton eats a fruit meant for the institute's dolphins and gains the ability to understand them.

The estranged brothers are then recruited for the Gemini Project, run by Dr. Ronald Olsen, who studies the physical and emotional connections between twins. On a remote island filled with hundreds of other twin pairs, Olsen claims his goal is to create bonds of empathy that could end evil in the world. Using the same fruit, the experiment allows Zack and Cody to feel each other's sensations and then emotions, and each comes to understand the other: Cody wants the scholarship so he can be with Bailey, while Zack needs the car to find his own purpose. Soon after reconciling, they discover that Olsen has sinister plans. As the island's twins fall under mind control and hunt them down, Bailey, who has finally read Cody's letter explaining his choices, sets out with London, Woody and the ship's manager Mr. Moseby to rescue them, helped by information London receives from a dolphin. Working together, the brothers must use their new connection to defeat Olsen.

The film drew 5.2 million viewers on its premiere. It later aired around the world, and it has streamed on Disney+ since November 2019. BSC Kids rated it seven out of ten, calling it typical but surprisingly funny and a good choice for younger viewers.

documents.title: The Thing
documents.tagline: It's Not Human. Yet.
documents.overview: When paleontologist Kate Lloyd travels to an isolated outpost in Antarctica for the expedition of a lifetime, she joins an international team that unearths a remarkable discovery. Their elation quickly turns to fear as they realize that their experiment has freed a mysterious being from its frozen prison. Paranoia spreads like an epidemic as a creature that can mimic anything it touches will pit human against human as it tries to survive and flourish in this spine-tingling thriller.
documents.plot:
The Thing is a 2011 American science fiction horror film directed by Matthijs van Heijningen Jr. and written by Eric Heisserer. A direct prequel to John Carpenter's 1982 film of the same name, itself adapted from a 1938 John W. Campbell novella, it depicts the fate of the Norwegian Antarctic research team that uncovers a shape-shifting alien in the ice. The ensemble cast is led by Mary Elizabeth Winstead as paleontologist Kate Lloyd, Joel Edgerton as helicopter pilot Sam Carter, Ulrich Thomsen as scientist Sander Halvorson, Adewale Akinnuoye-Agbaje as co-pilot Derek Jameson and Eric Christian Olsen as research assistant Adam Finch.

In the winter of 1982, the Norwegian station Thule discovers an alien spacecraft buried in the Antarctic ice, along with the frozen body of a creature. Halvorson and Finch recruit Kate, who flies to the station with Carter, Jameson and crewman Griggs. The creature bursts out of its block of ice, kills a dog and absorbs a team member before being burned. An autopsy shows that its cells were copying those of its victim. When the helicopter leaves to take an injured man for treatment, Griggs transforms and attacks, and the aircraft crashes. Finding bloody dental fillings in a shower, Kate realizes that the alien can absorb and imitate its victims but cannot reproduce inorganic material. The geologist Juliette reveals herself as a Thing and is destroyed with a flamethrower, and the group quarantines itself.

Carter and Jameson stagger back from the crash and are isolated under suspicion. Kate's test of checking everyone for metal fillings clears all but four people, including Halvorson. In the chaos that follows, Carter and Jameson break in, station chief Edvard transforms and merges with Finch into a two-headed creature, and Kate and Carter burn it. The assimilated Halvorson flees to the spacecraft, which comes to life; Kate destroys him with a grenade, shutting it down. Realizing that Carter is wearing his earring in the wrong ear, she burns him too, then sets off for a Soviet base. The next morning, the surviving Lars confronts the returning pilot Matias as the station's dog, actually a Thing, runs off, and the two pursue it by helicopter.

The film opened in the United States on October 14, 2011. It was a box-office bomb, grossing $31.5 million worldwide against a $38 million budget. Reviews were mixed: Rotten Tomatoes gave it 34% approval, calling it a slave to Carpenter's superior version, and Metacritic gave it 49.

documents.title: Silent Hill: Revelation 3D
documents.tagline: This Halloween prepare for a 3D ride through hell.
documents.overview: Heather Mason and her father have been on the run, always one step ahead of dangerous forces that she doesn't fully understand, Now on the eve of her 18th birthday, plagued by horrific nightmares and the disappearance of her father, Heather discovers she's not who she thinks she is. The revelation leads her deeper into a demonic world that threatens to trap her forever.
documents.plot:
Silent Hill: Revelation 3D is a 2012 American supernatural horror film directed by Michael J. Bassett, written by Ron Schmidt and Frank Cappello, and starring Adelaide Clemens, Sean Bean, and Kit Harington.

The movie takes place four years after the events of Silent Hill: Revelation (2012). The story begins with Alex Shepherd (Adelaide Clemens), a young woman who has been searching for her adopted father, Harry Mason (Sean Bean), in the haunted town of Silent Hill. After receiving a mysterious letter from an unknown sender, Alex finally finds herself back in Silent Hill.

Upon arrival, she discovers that Harry is missing and sets out to find him. As she delves deeper into the town's mysteries, she encounters a group of cultists who are searching for their own god, known as "The God" or "The Otherworldly Being." The cultists believe that by sacrificing themselves, they can bring about the return of this being and gain ultimate power.

As Alex navigates through Silent Hill, she meets Sean (Kit Harington), a young man who claims to be Harry's son. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to uncover the truth behind Harry's disappearance and the cultists' sinister plans.

Throughout their adventure, Alex and Sean encounter various monsters from Silent Hill's eerie landscape, including Pyramid Head, Nurses, and other iconic creatures. Along the way, they also discover that the town is filled with alternate realities and dimensions, which are connected to the Otherworldly Being.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Harry has been searching for a way to save his daughter, Rose (Sienna Guillory), who was taken by the cultists. The group soon realizes that they must stop the cultists before it's too late and prevent the return of the Otherworldly Being.

The climax of the movie features an intense showdown between Alex, Sean, and the cultists in a desperate bid to save Harry and Rose. In the end, Alex manages to defeat the cult leader and shatter the portal that would have brought about the Otherworldly Being's return.

However, as the dust settles, it becomes clear that the movie has an ambiguous ending. The fate of Harry and Rose is left uncertain, leaving the audience wondering if they were truly saved or if there are still more challenges ahead for Alex and Sean.

Overall, Silent Hill: Revelation 3D offers a thrilling and suspenseful ride through the haunted world of Silent Hill. While it may not be as well-received as its predecessor, the movie provides an entertaining and terrifying experience for fans of the series.

documents.title: Diary of a Sex Addict
documents.overview: A restaurant owner leads a double life.
documents.plot:
Diary of a Sex Addict is a 2001 American erotic drama directed by Joseph Brutsman, who wrote the screenplay with Anthony Peck, the son of Gregory Peck. Produced by Nu Image and Millennium Films, it stars Michael Des Barres, Rosanna Arquette, Nastassja Kinski and Ed Begley Jr. The film premiered at the 58th Venice International Film Festival in August 2001 and was released on DVD in the United States on 13 November 2001.

Sammy Horn is a charming, middle-aged English chef who owns a luxurious restaurant and appears to be a devoted family man. He genuinely loves his wife, Grace, their young son and his work, but he is also a sex addict, driven to seek pleasure at any time and with almost any woman he meets. To feed his compulsion he builds an elaborate double life, juggling affairs and casual encounters while keeping them hidden from his family, and becomes increasingly trapped in a web of lies that threatens his marriage and everything he cares about.

Sincerely wanting to break the pattern, Sammy begins therapy with the psychiatrist Dr. Jane Bordeaux, and the story unfolds largely through his sessions with her, as he confesses the details of his secret life and tries to understand what drives it. The film follows his mounting anxiety as the gap between his public and private selves becomes harder to manage and the consequences of his behaviour close in on him.

Des Barres plays Sammy, with Arquette as Grace, Kinski as Dr. Bordeaux and Ed Begley Jr. as Dr. Aaron Spencer. The supporting cast includes Alexandra Paul as Katherine, Eva Jeníčková as Tatiana and A.J. Benza as a police detective, while the twins Cole and Dylan Sprouse share the role of Sammy's son, Sammy Jr. Brutsman shot the film on digital video, using jump cuts to convey the character's unravelling state of mind.

Critical response was mixed. Reviewing it for Radio Times, Jason Caro gave it three stars out of five, calling it less trashy than its title suggests and a frank, troubling attempt to take a genuine addiction seriously. He felt Des Barres struck the right balance of charm and sleaze, and that Arquette and Kinski lent the film credibility, though he found its plotless structure and barrage of rough sexual encounters wearing. Other reviewers were harsher, dismissing it as amateurish and exploitative.

documents.title: Wendy Wu: Homecoming Warrior
documents.tagline: Pretty. Tough.
documents.overview: It is the story of an average, popular American teenager named Wendy Wu who discovers that in order to win the coveted crown she must first learn the way of the warrior. Wendy Wu has a one track mind, and that track leads directly to the title of homecoming queen -- no unscheduled stops, and no unnecessary detours. When a mysterious Chinese monk named Shen arrives to mold Wendy into a fearless kung fu warrior, however, her royal aspirations suddenly jump the track as she desperately attempts to juggle her boyfriend, her homework, and of course, the fierce competition to become homecoming queen. Now, as Wendy begins to train her mind, body, and spirit in the ancient tradition of the martial arts and her inner warrior gradually begins to emerge, the girl who once obsessed over popularity finally begins to put that popularity into perspective as she gradually realizes what truly matters in life.

documents.title: Rise of the Planet of the Apes
documents.original_title: Rise of the Planet of the Apes
documents.tagline: Evolution Becomes Revolution.
documents.overview: A highly intelligent chimpanzee named Caeser has been living a peaceful suburban life ever since he was born. But when he gets taken to a cruel primate facility, Caeser decides to revolt against those who have harmed him.
documents.plot:
In San Francisco, pharmaceutical chemist Will Rodman tests the viral-based drug ALZ-112 on chimpanzees at the biotechnology company Gen-Sys to find a cure for Alzheimer's disease. ALZ-112 is given to a chimpanzee named Bright Eyes, greatly increasing her intelligence. However, during Will's presentation for the drug, Bright Eyes is forced from her cage, goes on a rampage, and is shot to death. Will's superior Steven Jacobs terminates the project and has the chimpanzees euthanized. However, Will's assistant Robert Franklin reveals that the reason for Bright Eyes' rampage was that she had recently given birth. Will reluctantly takes in the infant chimpanzee, eventually naming him Caesar. Discovering that Caesar has inherited his mother's intelligence through being exposed to ALZ-112, Will decides to raise him. Three years pass, Caesar becomes highly intelligent; he can communicate through sign language. Will begins a romantic relationship with primatologist Caroline Aranha. Will and Caroline introduce Caesar to the redwood forest at Muir Woods National Monument so he can roam. Meanwhile, Will treats his father, Charles, with ALZ-112, which seems to restore his cognitive ability.
Five years later, Caesar, now entering adulthood, questions his origins and place in the world. Charles's condition returns as his immune system becomes resistant to ALZ-112. Caesar injures an aggressive neighbor, Douglas Hunsiker, while defending a confused Charles. The local animal control subsequently takes him to an ape shelter. Caesar is tormented by the alpha chimpanzee, Rocket, and the chief guard, Dodge Landon. However, Caesar befriends Maurice, a former circus orangutan who also knows sign language. Caesar learns to unlock his cage, gaining free access to the common area. With the assistance of Buck, a gorilla, Caesar claims the position of alpha. Meanwhile, Jacobs clears the development of a more powerful gaseous version of the drug, the ALZ-113, when Will tells him it can improve intelligence. Will takes the drug home for his father, but Charles declines further treatment and dies overnight. After attempting to test the drug on a bonobo named Koba, Franklin accidentally becomes exposed to ALZ-113 and becomes ill. Despite the risks, Jacobs orders continued trials and Will consequently quits his position.
Attempting to warn Will at his home, Franklin sneezes blood onto Hunsiker and is later discovered dead. Will attempts to reclaim Caesar, but Caesar decides to stay. He escapes and steals the ALZ-113 canisters from Will's house and enhances the intelligence of the other apes in the shelter. When Dodge attempts to get him back into his cage, Caesar reveals he can talk; while freeing the apes, he fights with Dodge, whose cattle prod electrocutes him. The apes flee, releasing Koba and the remaining apes from Gen-Sys, and freeing additional apes from the San Francisco Zoo.

documents.title: A Good Lawyer's Wife
documents.tagline: A good wife, a cheating husband, a very sexy family drama...
documents.overview: A woman, married and with a child but becoming increasingly distant from her husband who is already cheating on her, reluctantly enters a secret relationship with her neighbor, a teenage boy.
documents.plot: A woman, married and with a child but becoming increasingly distant from her husband who is already cheating on her, reluctantly enters a secret relationship with her neighbor, a teenage boy.

documents.title: Three Steps Above Heaven
documents.tagline: Have you ever been about to touch the sky?
documents.overview: Story of two young people who belong to different worlds. It is the chronicle of a love improbable, almost impossible but inevitable dragging in a frantic journey they discover the first great love. Babi is a girl from upper-middle class that is educated in goodness and innocence . Hache is a rebellious boy, impulsive, unconscious, has a appetite for risk and danger embodied in endless fights and illegal motorbike races, the limit of common sense
documents.plot:
Three Steps Above Heaven is a Spanish drama film directed by Cora Zolfo, released in 2010. The movie is based on the novel of the same name by Tomás Aragón.

The story revolves around Álvaro (played by Eloy de la Iglesia), a young man who has been diagnosed with leukemia and is undergoing chemotherapy at a hospital in Madrid. During his treatment, Álvaro meets Elena (played by Aitor Lara), a fellow patient who becomes his closest friend and confidant.

As the story unfolds, we learn that Álvaro's life was not without its challenges before he fell ill. He had a troubled relationship with his family, particularly his father, who is portrayed as emotionally distant and critical. Álvaro also struggles with feelings of guilt and anger towards his mother, who abandoned him when he was young.

The title "Three Steps Above Heaven" refers to the three steps that Álvaro takes above the hospital's rooftop, where he finds a sense of freedom and escape from his troubles. These moments of solitude allow him to reflect on his life and confront his inner demons.

Throughout the film, we see Álvaro's relationship with Elena deepen, as they bond over their shared experiences as patients at the hospital. However, their friendship is put to the test when Álvaro begins to develop feelings for Elena, which complicates their already fragile emotional connection.

As the story progresses, Álvaro's health begins to decline, and he must come to terms with his mortality. The film takes a poignant turn as Álvaro confronts his father about his past and the reasons behind his mother's departure. This confrontation ultimately leads to a sense of closure and healing for Álvaro.

The movie concludes with Álvaro's passing, surrounded by Elena and his loved ones. However, in a surprising twist, we see that Elena has been given a second chance at life, thanks to a bone marrow transplant from an anonymous donor. The film ends on a hopeful note, as Elena begins her new journey towards recovery.

Overall, Three Steps Above Heaven is a powerful and emotional drama that explores themes of love, loss, and redemption. The film features outstanding performances from its cast, particularly Eloy de la Iglesia and Aitor Lara, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

documents.title: Flypaper
documents.tagline: Two sets of bank robbers.  One very sticky heist.
documents.overview: A man caught in the middle of two simultaneous robberies at a bank desperately tries to protect the teller with whom he's secretly in love.
documents.plot: A man caught in the middle of two simultaneous robberies at a bank desperately tries to protect the teller with whom he's secretly in love.

documents.title: Brave
documents.tagline: Change your fate.
documents.overview: Brave is set in the mystical Scottish Highlands, where Mérida is the princess of a kingdom ruled by King Fergus and Queen Elinor. An unruly daughter and an accomplished archer, Mérida one day defies a sacred custom of the land and inadvertently brings turmoil to the kingdom. In an attempt to set things right, Mérida seeks out an eccentric old Wise Woman and is granted an ill-fated wish. Also figuring into Mérida’s quest — and serving as comic relief — are the kingdom’s three lords: the enormous Lord MacGuffin, the surly Lord Macintosh, and the disagreeable Lord Dingwall.
documents.plot:
Brave is a 2012 animated fantasy adventure film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and released by Walt Disney Pictures. The film is set in Scotland in the 10th century and follows the story of Merida, a young princess with a fiery personality.

The movie begins with Merida, a skilled archer and horseback rider, celebrating her 18th birthday with her family at their castle. However, during the celebration, Merida's parents, King Fergus and Queen Elinor, announce that they have arranged for her to marry one of three suitors: two princes from neighboring kingdoms. Merida is not interested in marrying any of them and longs for independence and freedom.

Merida visits a witch who lives on the outskirts of the kingdom, where she learns about magic and makes a deal with the witch to change her fate. The witch gives Merida a magical cake that will alter her destiny, but warns her that the spell comes with unintended consequences.

As the story unfolds, Merida's wish is granted, and she finds herself transformed into a horse. She must navigate the challenges of being a horse while trying to reverse the spell and find a way to win back her parents' love and respect.

Meanwhile, Prince Harris and Prince Hamish, the two princes that Merida was supposed to marry, arrive at the kingdom, and tensions rise as they try to win Merida's hand in marriage. However, Merida is not interested and tries to escape from them.

As Merida struggles to reverse the spell, she learns valuable lessons about family, loyalty, and the importance of communication. She also discovers that her parents are not perfect but are loving and well-intentioned individuals who want what's best for her.

In the end, Merida finds a way to break the curse by using her own unique qualities and strengths to win back her parents' love and respect. The film ends with Merida and her family coming together in a heartwarming moment of reconciliation and understanding.

Throughout the movie, Brave features stunning animation, memorable characters, and a richly detailed Scottish setting. The film's themes of female empowerment, self-discovery, and the importance of family are timely and relevant, making it a beloved classic among audiences of all ages.

documents.title: 30 Minutes or Less
documents.tagline: A lot can happen in 30 minutes.
documents.overview: Two fledgling criminals kidnap a pizza delivery guy, strap a bomb to his chest, and advise him that he has mere hours to rob a bank or else...
documents.plot:
30 Minutes or Less is a 2011 American action comedy film directed by Ruben Fleischer and produced by Stuart Cornfeld, Ben Stiller and Jeremy Kramer. Jesse Eisenberg stars as Nick, a pizza delivery driver, with Aziz Ansari as his friend Chet, Danny McBride and Nick Swardson as a pair of inept criminals, Michael Peña and Fred Ward. Released by Sony Pictures on 12 August 2011, it was filmed in Grand Rapids, Michigan, where the story is set.

Nick is an aimless young man in Grand Rapids who rarely manages to deliver pizzas within his employer's thirty-minute guarantee. His friendship with Chet, a schoolteacher, falls apart when Chet learns that Nick slept with his twin sister, Kate, on the night of their high school graduation; Nick also learns that Kate is about to leave for a job in Atlanta. Meanwhile, Dwayne and his friend Travis live in the shadow of Dwayne's domineering father, known as the Major, who won a large lottery jackpot years earlier. Eager to get his inheritance, Dwayne learns from a stripper, Juicy, that a hitman named Chango could kill his father, but he needs $100,000 to pay him.

Dwayne and Travis decide to kidnap a stranger, strap a bomb to him and force him to steal the money. They order a pizza, knock Nick unconscious when he arrives and lock him into a vest rigged with explosives, which they threaten to detonate if he goes to the police or fails to bring them the money within ten hours. Nick turns to Chet, who reluctantly helps him rob a bank. The heist is chaotic, but the two escape with the cash. When Dwayne and Travis demand the money and take Kate hostage, the situation escalates into a showdown at a scrapyard with Chango, involving bluffs, a flamethrower and the bomb itself, which Nick eventually turns against his captors.

The film received mixed reviews, with critics finding the cast's comic energy engaging but the story slight and the humor uneven. It grossed about $40 million worldwide against a $28 million budget. It also attracted controversy for its resemblance to the real 2003 death of Brian Wells, a pizza delivery man in Erie, Pennsylvania, who was killed by a bomb locked around his neck during a bank robbery; the filmmakers said they had not been aware of the case.

documents.title: Monsters University
documents.tagline: School never looked this scary.
documents.overview: A look at the relationship between Mike and Sulley during their days at Monsters University — when they weren't necessarily the best of friends.
documents.plot:
Monsters University is a 2013 animated comedy-adventure film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and released by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie takes place about six years before the events of the original Monsters, Inc.

The story follows two young monsters, Mike Wazowski (voiced by Billy Crystal) and James P. Sullivan (Sulley, voiced by John Goodman), who are roommates at Monsters University (MU). Mike is a small, one-eyed green monster with a big personality, while Sulley is a large, furry blue monster with a gentle giant demeanor.

The two monsters meet on their first day of college and quickly become friends. However, they have different aspirations: Mike wants to attend the prestigious Scar School for Scaring, while Sulley dreams of becoming a Scarer at Monsters, Inc., the largest scream-processing factory in Monstropolis.

Despite their differences, Mike and Sulley decide to join the same fraternity, Oozma Kappa (ΩK), which is struggling to find its place on campus. The fraternity's president, Terry Perry (voiced by Peter Sohn), is a laid-back monster who wants to focus on partying rather than scaring.

As Mike and Sulley try to fit in with the ΩK fraternity, they face numerous challenges, including rival fraternities like the Roar Omega Roar (ROR) and the Scare Games. The ROR fraternity, led by Don Carlton (voiced by Steve Buscemi), is determined to win the Scare Games and prove their superiority.

Throughout the movie, Mike and Sulley learn valuable lessons about teamwork, friendship, and believing in themselves. They also discover that they have a unique bond that allows them to scare together more effectively than any other monster duo.

The climax of the movie takes place during the Scare Games, where Mike and Sulley face off against their rivals from ROR. In a thrilling finale, the two friends use their combined skills to outscare their opponents and win the Scare Games.

In the end, Mike and Sulley become an unstoppable team, and their friendship is cemented as they graduate from Monsters University with honors. The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment of Mike and Sulley's graduation ceremony, where they are celebrated as heroes by their fellow monsters.

Overall, Monsters University is a fun and entertaining film that explores the early days of two beloved characters. The movie's themes of friendship, teamwork, and believing in oneself make it a great addition to the Monsters, Inc. franchise.

documents.title: Dark Shadows
documents.tagline: Every Family Has Its Demons
documents.overview: Vampire Barnabas Collins is inadvertently freed from his tomb and emerges into the very changed world of 1972. He returns to Collinwood Manor to find that his once-grand estate and family have fallen into ruin.
documents.plot:
Dark Shadows is a 2012 American gothic romance film directed by Tim Burton and written by Seth Grahame-Smith. The film is based on the 1960s TV soap opera of the same name, created by Dan Curtis.

The story begins with Barnaby Collins (Johnny Depp), a wealthy and handsome young man who lives in the 18th century. He falls in love with Angelique Bouchard (Eva Green), a beautiful and mysterious woman from the Caribbean. However, their love is forbidden, as Angelique is a witch who seeks revenge against those who wronged her.

After being rejected by Barnaby, Angelique casts a spell that turns him into a vampire, and she disappears for over 200 years. The story then jumps to 1972, where we meet our protagonist, Victoria Winters (Bella Heathcote), a young governess who is hired to care for David Collins (Gulliver McGrath), the son of Barnaby's brother, Roger (Johnny Depp).

As Victoria settles into her new life in Collinwood Manor, she begins to experience strange and supernatural occurrences. She soon discovers that Barnaby has been living in the manor as a vampire, and that he is still under Angelique's spell.

Victoria becomes entangled in the web of supernatural events unfolding around her, including the ghostly apparitions of the past, including Josette du Pres (Michelle Pfeiffer), who was Angelique's lover and Barnaby's wife. As Victoria delves deeper into the mystery, she uncovers a dark family secret that has been hidden for centuries.

As the story unfolds, Victoria finds herself caught between her growing feelings for David and her desire to help Barnaby break free from Angelique's spell. Along the way, she must confront the evil forces of Angelique, who will stop at nothing to destroy those who threaten her power.

The film builds towards a climactic showdown between good and evil, with Victoria playing a key role in breaking the curse that has haunted the Collins family for centuries. In the end, Barnaby is freed from his vampiric state, and he and Victoria share a romantic moment, as the supernatural forces are vanquished.

Throughout the film, Tim Burton's signature style and visual flair bring the world of Dark Shadows to life, with stunning costumes, sets, and special effects. The cast delivers strong performances, particularly Johnny Depp, who brings his trademark eccentricity to the role of Barnaby Collins.

Overall, Dark Shadows is a visually stunning and entertaining film that pays homage to the original TV series while offering something new and unique for fans of Tim Burton's work.

documents.title: Frankenweenie
documents.tagline: The electrifying dog is back from beyond the grave
documents.overview: When a car hits young Victor's pet dog Sparky, Victor decides to bring him back to life the only way he knows how. But when the bolt-necked "monster" wreaks havoc and terror in the hearts of Victor's neighbors, he has to convince them that Sparky's still the good, loyal friend he was.
documents.plot:
Frankenweenie is a stop-motion animated film directed by Tim Burton, released in 2012. The movie is a remake of Burton's 1984 live-action short film of the same name.

The story revolves around Victor Frankenstein (voiced by Charlie Tahan), an 8-year-old boy who lives with his family in a suburban town. Victor is a shy and awkward child, often bullied by his peers at school. One day, while walking home from school, Victor's beloved dog, Sparky, gets hit by a car and dies.

Consumed by grief, Victor decides to bring Sparky back to life using science and electricity. He builds an electrocution machine in his garage, which he uses to shock Sparky's body, hoping to revive him. To his surprise, Sparky comes back to life, but with some unexpected consequences.

As the days pass, Sparky becomes increasingly monstrous, with glowing eyes and a grotesque appearance. Victor is torn between his love for his resurrected dog and his fear of what he has created. Meanwhile, Victor's family and friends are unaware of Sparky's transformation, adding to the isolation and loneliness that Victor feels.

As Sparky's behavior becomes more erratic and aggressive, Victor realizes that he must find a way to reverse the spell before it's too late. However, with each attempt to undo the magic, things only seem to get worse. The townspeople begin to suspect that something is amiss, and Victor's family starts to worry about his safety.

In the climactic final act, Victor discovers that Sparky's transformation is irreversible, and he must learn to accept his new reality. With the help of his father (voiced by Martin Short), Victor comes up with a plan to save Sparky from himself and restore balance to their lives.

The film ends on a bittersweet note, as Victor learns to let go of his attachment to Sparky's original form and finds a way to coexist with his resurrected dog. The movie concludes with Victor and Sparky sitting together in the park, surrounded by the beauty of nature, symbolizing the boy's acceptance of his new circumstances.

Throughout the film, Tim Burton's signature dark whimsy and visual style shine through, bringing the story to life in a way that is both hauntingly beautiful and endearingly quirky. The voice cast, including Martin Short, Catherine O'Hara, and Martin Landau, adds depth and humor to the narrative, making Frankenweenie a delightful and unforgettable viewing experience for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Melancholia
documents.tagline: Enjoy it while it lasts
documents.overview: Two sisters find their already strained relationship challenged as a mysterious new planet threatens to collide with Earth.
documents.plot: Two sisters find their already strained relationship challenged as a mysterious new planet threatens to collide with Earth.

documents.title: Home
documents.tagline: A stunning visual portrayal of Earth
documents.overview: In 200,000 years of existence, man has upset the balance on which the Earth had lived for 4 billion years. Global warming, resource depletion, species extinction: man has endangered his own home. But it is too late to be pessimistic: humanity has barely ten years left to reverse the trend, become aware of its excessive exploitation of the Earth's riches, and change its consumption pattern.
documents.plot:
Home is a 2009 French documentary directed by the photographer Yann Arthus-Bertrand and produced by Luc Besson, Denis Carot and François-Henri Pinault, with music by Armand Amar. Inspired by the director's photography book Earth from Above, the film is built almost entirely from aerial footage combined with a voice-over, and it is conceived as a travel journal about the bond between humanity and the planet. Its narrators varied by language: Glenn Close read the English version, Salma Hayek the Spanish, Isabella Rossellini the Italian and Zhou Xun the Chinese, while Jacques Gamblin voiced the French theatrical cut and Arthus-Bertrand himself the French television version.

The film begins with the formation of the Earth and the emergence of life, then traces how human societies spread across continents and, especially in the past few decades, began to reshape the planet at unprecedented speed. Sweeping images of deserts, forests, ice caps, farmland and megacities illustrate its central themes: water shortages, deforestation, melting ice, the depletion of natural resources and the impact of human activity on climate change. Rather than presenting a disaster film, Arthus-Bertrand frames it as a message of hope, arguing that humanity still has roughly ten years to change course.

The shoot took about eighteen months, with the director, a cameraman, a camera engineer and a pilot flying a small helicopter over more than fifty countries on every continent, including Antarctica. Stabilized high-definition Cineflex cameras mounted beneath the helicopter gave the footage its smooth, crane-like quality, and nearly 500 hours of raw material were recorded. With a budget of about 12 million euros, largely funded by the PPR group (later Kering), Home was released on World Environment Day, 5 June 2009, simultaneously in cinemas, on television, on DVD and free on YouTube in 181 countries, and it was screened outdoors on the Champ de Mars in Paris. It drew more than 8 million viewers on France 2 and tens of millions of views online. Critics praised its imagery but questioned its preachy narration and the contrast between its message and its luxury-goods sponsor. It was nominated for the César Award for Best Documentary.

documents.title: Turn Me On, Dammit!
documents.overview: In Skoddeheimen, Norway, 15-year-old Alma is consumed by her hormones and fantasies that range from sweetly romantic images of Artur, the boyfriend she yearns for, to daydreams about practically everybody she lays eyes on.
documents.plot: In Skoddeheimen, Norway, 15-year-old Alma is consumed by her hormones and fantasies that range from sweetly romantic images of Artur, the boyfriend she yearns for, to daydreams about practically everybody she lays eyes on.

documents.title: The Devil's Double
documents.tagline: The 80's were brilliant, if you were in charge.
documents.overview: A chilling vision of the House of Saddam Hussein comes to life through the eyes of the man who was forced to become the double of Hussein's sadistic son.
documents.plot:
In 1987, Latif Yahia, an Iraqi soldier fighting in the Iran–Iraq War, is called to become a "fedai" ("body double" or political decoy) for Uday Hussein, the son of president Saddam. Latif comes from an upper-class family and attended school with Uday, where students would remark on their likeness. He refuses the position. Furious, Uday has him imprisoned and tortured. Latif relents when his family is threatened. Latif undergoes cosmetic surgery to perfect his resemblance to Uday and practises emulating the latter's mannerisms and persona. Latif tries to resist Uday's exorbitant merrymaking and erratic behaviour, at one point fleeing a nightclub to attempt to see his family, who believe that he died in the war. However, he is apprehended by Uday's bodyguards and beaten by Uday. After an appearance at a conference with Kuwaiti leaders, an attempt is made on Uday's (Latif's) life, apparently by a member of a rebel opposition group, possibly a Kurd. The real Uday, though, is more concerned with the Kuwaitis, whom he believes were slant drilling into Iraq's Rumaila oil field. The First Gulf War is launched.
Uday eventually kidnaps a 14-year-old girl and forces her to escort him to a party. There, Uday becomes enraged with Saddam's personal bodyguard Kamel Hana Gegeo. Uday believes that Gegeo facilitated an affair Saddam had, which devastated his mother. Uday is also jealous at the trust Saddam places in Gegeo. When Gegeo passes sarcastic comments about Uday's advances towards the girl and drunkenly fires an AK-47 in the air, Uday butchers him with an electric knife in front of the guests. The next morning, Uday's bodyguards dump the girl's beaten, partially naked body. Furious, Saddam goes to the hospital, where Uday is overdosed on sleeping pills. Saddam beats Uday and nearly castrates him. Only the intervention of a doctor saves him. As the war is in full swing, Latif tries to distance himself from Uday and begins an affair with Sarrab, one of Uday's lovers.
Latif, acting as Uday, is later sent to Basra to rally support among Republican Guard soldiers as Coalition forces take control of the war. At Basra, another attempt is made on Latif's life. Latif nearly loses a finger in the assault, which would mean Uday would have to amputate his own finger to maintain their resemblance. Uday enters a hospital and threatens to slaughter everyone in it if they fail to save his finger. The doctors succeed.
Afterwards, Uday, accompanied by his usual party, crashes a wedding, eventually raping and beating the bride, who then commits suicide. Angry, Latif assaults Uday but is corralled by the latter's bodyguards, who threaten to kill him. Uday stops them. Later, Latif is confronted by the father of the girl Uday killed. Uday overhears them and is outraged by the man's pleas for "justice" and "compassion". Uday orders Latif to kill the man, but Latif refuses and instead slits his own wrists. He is dumped half-dead on his family's front door.

documents.title: Mirror Mirror
documents.tagline: The Snow White legend comes alive.
documents.overview: After she spends all her money, an evil enchantress queen schemes to marry a handsome, wealthy prince. There's just one problem - he's in love with a beautiful princess, Snow White. Now, joined by seven rebellious dwarves, Snow White launches an epic battle of good vs. evil...
documents.plot:
Mirror Mirror is a 2012 fantasy adventure film directed by Tarsem Singh and produced by Relativity Media. The movie is a retelling of the classic fairy tale Snow White, with a comedic twist.

The story begins with King Agnarr (Martin Klebba), the father of Queen Grimhilde (Julianne Moore) and her two daughters, Snow White (Lily Collins) and Ravenna (Milla Jovovich). The movie takes place in a fictional kingdom, where magic is real and mythical creatures roam free.

As the story unfolds, we learn that Queen Grimhilde was once a beautiful princess who fell in love with a prince. However, her stepmother, the Evil Queen, cast a spell on her, making her look old and ugly. The prince, unaware of the queen's true nature, married her instead of Snow White.

Years pass, and Queen Grimhilde becomes increasingly bitter and resentful towards Snow White, who is now the princess of the kingdom. She orders her huntsman to take Snow White into the forest and kill her, but the huntsman takes pity on Snow White and tells her to run away.

Snow White finds herself in a small cottage belonging to seven dwarfs: Doc (Nathan Lane), Grumpy (Billy Barty), Happy (Robert Carlyle), Sleepy (Martin Klebba), Bashful (Julian Sands), Sneezy (Stephen Mackintosh), and Dopey (Bo Peep's voice actor, not the same person as the other 6). The dwarfs welcome Snow White into their home, and she stays with them.

Meanwhile, Queen Grimhilde discovers that Snow White is still alive and orders her huntsman to bring back Snow White's heart. However, the huntsman tricks the queen by telling her that he has killed Snow White and brought back her heart in a box. The queen then disposes of the box, unaware that it contains a fake heart.

As time passes, Queen Grimhilde becomes increasingly vain and obsessed with staying young and beautiful. She orders her magic mirror to show her who is the fairest of them all, but the mirror reveals that Snow White is now the fairest of them all.

Enraged, Queen Grimhilde orders a huntsman to take Snow White into the forest and kill her again. However, this time, the huntsman tells Snow White about the queen's plan and advises her to escape. Snow White and the dwarfs come up with a plan to trick the queen and expose her true nature.

In the end, Queen Grimhilde is defeated by Snow White and her friends, who use magic and wit to outsmart her. The movie ends with Snow White and Prince Charming (Armie Hammer) falling in love and getting married, while Queen Grimhilde is banished from the kingdom.

Overall, Mirror Mirror is a fun and lighthearted retelling of the classic fairy tale Snow White. The movie features stunning visuals, witty dialogue, and memorable performances from its cast.

documents.title: Dolphin Tale
documents.tagline: Inspired by the amazing true story of Winter
documents.overview: A story centered on the friendship between a boy and a dolphin whose tail was lost in a crab trap.
documents.plot:
Sawyer Nelson is a lonely 11-year-old who has been falling behind academically in school since his father's abandonment five years earlier. Sawyer spends his time playing video games and building model airplanes and helicopters in his garage. His only friend is his college-aged cousin Kyle Connellan, a champion swimmer who hopes to compete in the Olympics. Kyle leaves to spend time in the army, to help pay for Olympic training. With his only friend gone, Sawyer becomes even more isolated and Sawyer's failing grades have required him to take summer school.
One day, while riding his bike to summer school, Sawyer finds a fisherman attempting to help an injured dolphin tangled in a crab trap. The dolphin is taken for treatment to Clearwater Marine Hospital (CMH), run by Dr. Clay Haskett. Clay's daughter Hazel names the dolphin Winter, after two prior dolphins, Summer and Autumn, had been treated successfully and returned to the ocean. Sawyer sneaks in to see Winter, and later starts to visit each day, being harassed by a crazy pelican named Rufus. Sawyer's mother, Lorraine, and Clay are hesitant, due to Sawyer's inexperience with marine animals, and repeatedly skipping summer school, but they realize that the friendship seems to benefit both Winter and Sawyer. Clay allows the visits to continue, and Lorraine withdraws Sawyer from summer school and lets him volunteer at CMA, and gives him a new wetsuit.
However, Winter's tail is wounded and must be amputated. Winter learns to swim without a tail by developing a side-to-side motion like a fish, but after an X-ray, Clay notices the unnatural motion is causing stress on her spine, which, if continued, will handicap and eventually kill her.
The news comes that Kyle has been injured severely in an explosion and is returning home for treatment. Sawyer is excited to see him, but devastated when Kyle skips his own welcoming party and stays at the local Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center, where Dr. Cameron McCarthy develops prosthetic limbs. Sawyer and his mother visit Kyle there, but Sawyer is insulted when Kyle asks them to leave. Not wanting to upset Sawyer, Kyle takes Sawyer for a walk and explains his situation and that he needs some time. At Sawyer's request, McCarthy agrees to make a prosthetic tail for Winter and convinces his prosthetic supplier Hanger Prosthetics and Orthotics to supply the parts at no cost. McCarthy manufactures a "homemade" model tail while waiting for the real one to arrive, but Winter rejects it by banging it against the pool wall. Meanwhile, Kyle gets more depressed when his friend and swimming partner, Donovan Peck, beats his old swimming records. McCarthy persuades Kyle to go home.
Faced with financial trouble, the CMA is heavily damaged by a hurricane. The board of directors agrees to close up and sell the land to a real estate developer. It finds homes for all the animals except Winter, who is not wanted due to her disability and may have to be euthanized.

documents.title: New Year's Eve
documents.tagline: The one night anything is possible.
documents.overview: The lives of several couples and singles in New York intertwine over the course of New Year's Eve.
documents.plot: The lives of several couples and singles in New York intertwine over the course of New Year's Eve.

documents.title: Megan Is Missing
documents.tagline: Megan and Amy are best friends. They share secrets. They chat with guys online. And in a few days, they will never be seen again.
documents.overview: Fourteen-year–old Megan and her best friend Amy spend a lot of time on the internet, posting videos of themselves and chatting with guys online. One night Megan chats with a guy named Josh who convinces her to meet him for a date. The next day, Megan is missing—forever. Based on actual cases of child abduction.
documents.plot:
Megan Stewart and Amy Herman are 14-year-old best friends from North Hollywood who went missing in January 2007. An unidentified, seemingly tech-savvy and omniscient narrator has assembled web-chat recordings, home movies, news reports and previously classified police material into a linear narrative of the weeks surrounding their disappearances. Whether this compiled documentary is meant to be a cautionary tale about online safety, or rather something more sinister, is left open to speculation.
Despite their friendship, the two girls share little in common. Megan is a popular high school honors student, but she also has a dysfunctional relationship with her mother who has a reckless and promiscuous sex life and a drug addiction. Amy, on the other hand, lives in Sherman Oaks, has a healthy relationship with her parents, is still a virgin and enjoys stuffed toys.
This friendship does not exempt Amy from bullying by Megan's friends. To help her fit in, Megan invites Amy to a rave party. Amy's experience in the party is unpleasant all round: she is slapped after refusing the advances of a male attendee, walks in on Megan performing fellatio on the party's host, and vomits on Megan's bisexual friend Lexie while she is making out with another girl.
Megan later assuages Amy's feelings of shame and inadequacy regarding the party, and explains that she first performed oral sex at age 10 with a 17-year-old camp counselor. On her birthday, Amy records a video diary with Megan on her new camera, during which Megan reveals that her stepfather had raped her at the age of nine, and continued to do so for two years, which led to his imprisonment and her self-destructive lifestyle. Her mother resents her for reporting him to authorities, which leads to their volatile relationship. Amy quickly hugs and comforts Megan.
Megan video chats with Lexie. It is strongly implied during this conversation that they share a brief sexual past and Lexie retains a crush on Megan. Lexie gives Megan's social media handle to Josh, who presents himself as a teenager from a nearby school. He only shares one picture and remains anonymous on video chat, claiming his webcam is broken. Despite several suspicions and contradictions, Megan is charmed by him. They agree to meet at a party, but he fails to reveal himself. She confronts him online but forgives him when he accurately describes what she was wearing and insists he is shy. Later, when Amy comes over to her house, Megan introduces her to him.
Josh convinces Megan to meet him behind a diner. She does not attend class the next day, and Amy's initial inquiries are brushed off by Lexie and her friend Kathy. News reports, however, later declare Megan officially missing. Grainy footage from the diner's security camera shows her being grabbed by the wrist by an indistinct older man. Amy investigates Megan's disappearance and talks online with Josh.

documents.title: The Skin I Live In
documents.tagline: The things the love of a madman can do...
documents.overview: A brilliant plastic surgeon creates a synthetic skin that withstands any kind of damage. His guinea pig: a mysterious and volatile woman who holds the key to his obsession.
documents.plot:
The Skin I Live In is a psychological thriller film directed by Pedro Almodóvar, released in 2011 under the production company El Deseo. The movie tells the story of Dr. Robert Ledgard, a brilliant and obsessive scientist who seeks revenge against those he believes wronged him.

The film begins with an elderly Robert (played by Antonio Banderas), a renowned plastic surgeon, living in a remote estate in Ireland. He is revealed to be a former prisoner, having spent 15 years behind bars for a crime he committed as a young man. The story then flashes back to Robert's past, where we see him as a young doctor (also played by Antonio Banderas) who becomes infatuated with a woman named Vera (played by Elena Anaya), the daughter of a wealthy and influential family.

Robert's obsession with Vera leads him to kidnap her and subject her to a series of gruesome experiments. He surgically alters her face, transforming her into a man, which he names Norman. Robert's goal is to create the perfect "son" for himself, someone who will be loyal and obedient only to him.

As the story unfolds, we see Robert's relationship with Norman (also played by Eduardo Noriega), his creation, evolve from one of paternal love to one of twisted obsession. Norman becomes a skilled and deadly assassin, carrying out Robert's orders without question. However, as time passes, Norman begins to develop his own identity and sense of self, which threatens Robert's control over him.

Meanwhile, Vera (Elena Anaya) is revealed to be alive and working as a nurse at the local hospital. She becomes embroiled in a complicated love triangle with her husband, Dr. General (played by Marisa Paredes), and her former lover, Norman.

The plot thickens as Robert's past catches up with him, and he is forced to confront the consequences of his actions. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Vera was actually the one who betrayed Robert to the authorities, leading to his imprisonment. This revelation sets off a chain reaction of events that ultimately leads to Norman's betrayal of Robert.

The film builds towards a tense and violent climax as Robert's world begins to unravel. In the end, Norman turns against Robert, killing him in a brutal and satisfying manner. The movie concludes with Vera, now free from her past, embracing her true identity and finding love with Dr. General.

Throughout the film, Almodóvar explores themes of obsession, identity, and the blurred lines between good and evil. The Skin I Live In is a masterclass in suspense and tension, with outstanding performances from its cast. The film's use of symbolism, particularly the skin that Robert uses to cover his face, adds depth and complexity to the narrative.

Overall, The Skin I Live In is a gripping and unsettling thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

documents.title: What's Your Number?
documents.tagline: Ally's looking for the best ex of her life.
documents.overview: Ally Darling is realizing she's a little lost in life. Her latest romance has just fizzled out, and she's just been fired from her marketing job. Then she reads an eye-opening magazine article that warns that 96 percent of women who've been with 20 or more lovers are unlikely to find a husband. Determined to turn her life around and prove the article wrong, Ally embarks on a mission to find the perfect mate from among her numerous ex-boyfriends.

documents.title: My Babysitter's a Vampire
documents.tagline: No parents. No rules. No pulse.
documents.overview: Geeky 14-year old Ethan is left to babysit his younger sister, Jane, with his best friend Benny but after Ethan inadvertently puts Jane in harm's way, his parents hire a professional babysitter, the beautiful yet mysterious 17-year-old Sarah who, unbeknownst to them, is actually a fledgling vampire.
documents.plot:
Ethan Morgan is a geeky high school freshman, not trusted by his parents to take care of his little sister Jane on his own. They hire Erica, a teenage girl from Ethan's school who is a huge fan of Dusk (a parody of Twilight), as a babysitter. Erica instead decides to attend a party thrown by Jesse, the vampire ex-boyfriend of her best friend Sarah. During a fight between Sarah and Jesse, Sarah ends up at Ethan's house and tells Ethan's parents that she was asked to babysit instead. Ethan becomes infatuated with Sarah. Ethan suddenly has a vision when touching Sarah, and notices she has no reflection in the mirror.
Sarah leaves to get Erica back from the party, knowing the party is full of bloodthirsty vampires. Curious, Ethan and his dorky best friend Benny follow Sarah. They see her feed on a rat and realize she is a vampire. Sarah explains that she is only a fledgling, a vampire who has not drunk human blood. The three of them are attacked by a vampire sent by Jesse, and head to the party to save Erica and their dimwitted friend, Rory. However, Erica has already been bitten and also bites Rory.
The next day, Ethan has a vision in which he sees a gravestone with the number 219 and a mysterious box, which is then uncovered by the vampires. The box is called the Cubile Animus or "Nest of Souls". Ethan and Sarah figure out Jesse's plan from an old book, learning that in the original settlement of the town, a man named Reverend Horace Black who led an evil cabal of vampires. During a lunar eclipse, the townspeople burned the members, leading to all '219' of their deaths. Ethan realizes that Jesse is, in fact, Horace Black, and plans to use the box to trap the souls of teens going to see the premiere of the new Dusk movie so he can resurrect the souls of his ancient group during the lunar eclipse.
Benny's grandmother, who reveals that she is an Earth Priestess, gives Ethan, Benny and Sarah enchanted daggers and a spell book to defeat the vampires. She explains that Ethan sees visions because he is a Seer, which enables him to see visions through touch, and Benny is a spellmaster, allowing him to cast spells. At the theater, the vampires begin to steal the souls of the teens, but are thwarted by the trio. In a vision, Ethan sees the tree he saw inside the old book, realizing it's the tree in his backyard, where they find Jesse. As the eclipse begins, Jesse attempts to hold Ethan and Benny down and resurrect the souls he already obtained from the Cubile Animus, but Sarah intervenes. When the box lands in Ethan's hands, he releases the vengeful souls that were captured, which destroy Jesse and return to their bodies.
The next day, Ethan, Benny and Sarah meet Erica and Rory, who have decided to live peacefully as vampires.

documents.title: Honey 2
documents.tagline: Go every step of the way.
documents.overview: After a brush with the law, Maria has returned to her gritty Bronx roots to rebuild her life with nothing but a talent for street dance and a burning ambition to prove herself.
documents.plot:
Honey 2 is a 2011 American dance film directed by Bille Woodruff and a sequel to his 2003 film Honey. Kat Graham stars as Maria Ramirez, a talented street dancer, with Randy Wayne, Seychelle Gabriel, Audrina Patridge, Melissa Molinaro and Lonette McKee, who reprises her role as Connie Daniels, the mother of the first film's heroine, Honey Daniels. The film was released in cinemas in the United Kingdom in June 2011 and went straight to DVD and Blu-ray in the United States in February 2012.

Seventeen-year-old Maria returns to the Bronx after a spell in juvenile detention, determined to rebuild her life with nothing but her talent for street dance and a burning desire to prove herself. She finds refuge at the neighborhood recreation center where, as a child, Honey's lively classes first sparked her passion for dancing. To stay out of trouble, she lives with Honey's mother, Connie, and holds down a job, while trying to avoid her old crew, the 718, and her controlling ex-boyfriend Luis, whose influence landed her in trouble in the first place.

At the center Maria meets Brandon, who runs the place and leads a group of dancers called the HD crew, a collection of talented misfits who lack direction. Maria joins them and pushes them to audition for "Dance Battlezone," a televised dance competition, even though it means going up against the 718, now led by Luis. The rival crew tries to intimidate HD in a street dance-off and temporarily lures away one of its members, Tina, involving her in crimes until she realizes what kind of people they are. As the competition progresses, Maria grows closer to Brandon, struggles to keep her past from catching up with her and must hold the HD crew together through setbacks, rivalries and doubts, as they work toward a final showdown with the 718 on national television.

Like the first film, Honey 2 received negative reviews from critics. It holds a 10 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it an unwanted sequel of banal missteps. Reviewers found the story formulaic, though some acknowledged the energy of the dance sequences and Graham's screen presence. The film was followed by two more straight-to-video sequels, Honey 3: Dare to Dance (2016) and Honey: Rise Up and Dance (2018), each with new characters.

documents.title: Colorful
documents.overview: Upon reaching the train station to death, a dejected soul is informed that he is lucky and will have another chance at life. He is placed in the body of a 14-year-old boy named Kobayashi Makoto, who has just committed suicide. Watched over by a neutral spirit named Purapura, the soul must figure out what his greatest sin and mistake in his former life was, before his time limit in Makoto's body runs out. He also has a number of other lesser duties he must complete, such as understanding what led Makoto to commit suicide in the first place and learning how to enjoy his second chance at life.

documents.title: The Muppets
documents.tagline: One girl has his dream.
documents.overview: When Kermit the Frog and the Muppets learn that their beloved theater is slated for demolition, a sympathetic human, Gary, and his puppet brother, Walter, swoop in to help the gang put on a show and raise the $10 million they need to save the day.
documents.plot:
The Muppets is a 2011 American musical comedy directed by James Bobin and written by Jason Segel and Nicholas Stoller, the seventh theatrical feature starring Jim Henson's Muppets. It stars Segel as Gary, Amy Adams as his girlfriend Mary, Chris Cooper as the oil magnate Tex Richman and Rashida Jones as television executive Veronica Martin, alongside Muppet performers including Steve Whitmire as Kermit the Frog, Eric Jacobson as Miss Piggy and Fozzie Bear, Dave Goelz as Gonzo and Peter Linz as Walter. Bret McKenzie served as music supervisor and wrote most of the original songs.

Walter, a Muppet growing up in Smalltown alongside his human brother Gary, is the Muppets' most devoted fan. When Gary takes his longtime girlfriend Mary on a trip to Los Angeles on vacation, Walter comes along. During a tour of the run-down Muppet Studios, Walter overhears Tex Richman plotting to buy the Muppet Theatre and drill for the oil beneath it. The Muppets can only save the theatre by raising ten million dollars before their contract expires.

Walter, Gary and Mary track down Kermit, who agrees to reunite the long-disbanded troupe to stage a telethon. Fozzie is performing in Reno with a crude tribute band called the Moopets, Gonzo has become a plumbing magnate, Animal is in anger management, and Miss Piggy is working as an editor at Vogue Paris. Once the gang is reassembled, they persuade a network to air the show, but must find a celebrity host, refurbish the theatre and fill the program, while Walter searches for his own talent. Meanwhile, Mary feels neglected by Gary's devotion to his brother, and Tex does everything he can to sabotage the telethon.

The film is a nostalgic celebration of the Muppets' history and a story about friendship and growing up, mixing classic songs such as "Rainbow Connection" with new numbers and guest appearances by celebrities such as Jack Black.

Released by Walt Disney Studios on 23 November 2011, The Muppets grossed over 171 million dollars worldwide on a 45 million dollar budget. It received widespread acclaim, with 95 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 75, and McKenzie's "Man or Muppet" won the Academy Award for Best Original Song. A sequel, Muppets Most Wanted, followed in 2014.

documents.title: Total Recall
documents.tagline: What Is Real?
documents.overview: Welcome to Rekall, the company that can turn your dreams into real memories. For a factory worker named Douglas Quaid, even though he's got a beautiful wife who he loves, the mind-trip sounds like the perfect vacation from his frustrating life - real memories of life as a super-spy might be just what he needs. But when the procedure goes horribly wrong, Quaid becomes a hunted man. Finding himself on the run from the police - controlled by Chancellor Cohaagen, the leader of the free world - Quaid teams up with a rebel fighter to find the head of the underground resistance and stop Cohaagen. The line between fantasy and reality gets blurred and the fate of his world hangs in the balance as Quaid discovers his true identity, his true love, and his true fate.
documents.plot:
Total Recall is a 2012 American science fiction action film directed by Len Wiseman from a screenplay by Kurt Wimmer and Mark Bomback, an adaptation of the 1990 film inspired by Philip K. Dick's 1966 short story "We Can Remember It for You Wholesale". It stars Colin Farrell, Kate Beckinsale and Jessica Biel, with Bryan Cranston, Bokeem Woodbine, John Cho and Bill Nighy, and unlike the original it is set entirely on Earth.

At the end of the 21st century, chemical warfare has left only two habitable regions: the wealthy United Federation of Britain and the Colony in Australia, whose workers commute daily through the planet's core on a gravity elevator called "The Fall". A Resistance branded as terrorists fights for better conditions in the Colony. Factory worker Douglas Quaid, troubled by dreams of being a spy with a mysterious woman, visits Rekall, a company that implants artificial memories, and chooses a secret-agent fantasy, but the technician finds he already holds real spy memories. Police storm the clinic and Quaid instinctively kills the entire squad. At home his wife, Lori, tries to kill him, revealing that she is a UFB agent and that their seven-year marriage is a six-week fiction.

Guided by a message from his former colleague Hammond and a recording he left himself, Quaid flees to the UFB, where he is rescued from Lori by Melina, the woman from his dreams. Another recording reveals that he is Carl Hauser, an agent of Chancellor Cohaagen who defected to the Resistance after learning of a kill code that could stop the robot army Cohaagen plans to use to seize the Colony. When his friend Harry claims Quaid is still dreaming and must kill Melina to wake, Quaid shoots Harry instead. Resistance leader Matthias begins searching Quaid's memories, but Cohaagen, who invented the kill code to locate him, storms the base, kills Matthias and captures Melina. Freed by Hammond, who dies in the attempt, Quaid sneaks aboard the Fall as it carries the robots, plants explosives and rescues Melina; the blast destroys the elevator, Cohaagen and his army. In an ambulance Quaid unmasks a disguised Lori and kills her, then reunites with Melina as the Colony declares independence.

Released by Columbia Pictures on August 3, 2012, it grossed $211.8 million worldwide on a $125 million budget. Reviews were negative, with 30% on Rotten Tomatoes and 43 on Metacritic.

documents.title: Straw Dogs
documents.tagline: Everyone Has A Breaking Point
documents.overview: L.A. screenwriter David Sumner relocates with his wife, Amy, to her hometown in the deep South. There, while tensions build between them, a brewing conflict with locals becomes a threat to them both.
documents.plot:
Straw Dogs is a 2011 American Southern Gothic psychological thriller written, produced and directed by Rod Lurie. A remake of Sam Peckinpah's 1971 film, itself adapted from Gordon Williams's novel The Siege of Trencher's Farm, it moves the story from Cornwall to rural Mississippi. James Marsden and Kate Bosworth star as David and Amy Sumner, with Alexander Skarsgård as Charlie, Amy's former boyfriend.

Screenwriter David and his actress wife, Amy, move to her hometown of Blackwater, Mississippi, to live in her late father's house while David finishes a script. In town David meets Charlie and his friends Norman, Chris and Bic, who have already been hired to repair the roof of the couple's barn, and Tom Heddon, an alcoholic former high school football coach who bullies Jeremy Niles, an intellectually disabled man he wrongly believes is stalking his teenage daughter, Janice. The workmen soon harass David, leer at Amy and drag out the job, and Amy grows resentful that David will not stand up to them. When the couple's cat is found strangled, the men deny involvement. Charlie invites David on a deer hunt, then returns to the house and rapes Amy, and Norman rapes her as well. Amy keeps silent but urges David to fire the crew, and he pays them off.

At a football game, Janice lures Jeremy into a locker room and forces herself on him; when Heddon comes looking for her, the panicked Jeremy holds her silent and accidentally smothers her. Haunted by memories of the assault, Amy asks to leave the game and, on the drive home, David accidentally hits Jeremy with the car and brings him home to await an ambulance. Learning of this over a police scanner, Heddon and Charlie's gang besiege the house demanding Jeremy, and Heddon kills the sheriff when he tries to intervene. David barricades the house and fights back killing Chris, Heddon and Bic, while Amy shoots Norman as he tries to rape her again. Charlie beats David and prepares to shoot him, but David snaps a bear trap shut on Charlie's neck, killing him, and as sirens approach and the barn burns, he declares that he got them all.

Filming began on August 16, 2009, in Shreveport and Vivian, Louisiana, and Sony Pictures Releasing released the film on September 16, 2011. It opened with $5.1 million and grossed about $11.2 million against a $25 million budget. Reviews were mixed to negative, with many critics comparing it unfavorably with the original; Rotten Tomatoes gave it 42%.

documents.title: The Art of Getting By
documents.tagline: The toughest lesson is love.
documents.overview: George, a lonely and fatalistic teen who's made it all the way to his senior year without ever having done a real day of work, is befriended by Sally, a popular but complicated girl who recognizes in him a kindred spirit.
documents.plot:
George Zinavoy is a lonely senior at a Manhattan preparatory school with a penchant for drawing and a nihilistic worldview. Obsessed with the inevitability of death, he never does homework and skips school frequently; as a result, he is placed on academic probation. One day while on the school roof, George encounters classmate Sally Howe smoking. When a teacher appears, he pulls out a cigarette and takes the fall for her. They become friends.
On Career Day at school, George meets young artist Dustin Heath, who becomes a mentor of sorts to George. He brings Sally with him to visit Dustin at his studio in Brooklyn and it becomes apparent that Dustin finds her attractive. She invites George to a New Year's Eve party, where she dances with an ex-boyfriend while George gets drunk, goes outside, throws up, and falls asleep on the street. Finding him there, Sally takes him to her place, putting him to bed on a pull-out next to her bed. They grow closer and George becomes more involved in school.
On Valentine's Day, George and Sally go out to dinner, and she starts asking questions about what he thinks of her. He is evasive, and she asks him if he will have sex with her. When George freezes, Sally backtracks and claims she was joking, as she considers him her only real friend. He becomes withdrawn and leaves early. As George continually avoids Sally and ignores her calls, she meets with Dustin at a bar one evening and flirts with him. Though Dustin initially resists Sally's advances out of respect for George, they soon begin a relationship.
After failing to write his English term paper, George is again sent to the principal's office. He is given two choices: be expelled, or make up all of the homework he has not done all year. Confronted by his mother and stepfather at home, he responds by telling his mother that his stepfather has been pretending to go to work for weeks. The stepfather attacks him and George knocks him down before taking off. He goes to Sally's and, in the hallway, kisses her. Sally kisses him back but pulls away, revealing Dustin in her apartment. Devastated, George leaves.
The next morning, George finds his mother in the park and she tells him she is divorcing his stepfather. Consoling her, he begins to rethink his life. He decides to make the effort to do his assignments. His art teacher gives him only one project, which must be honest and fearless. George completes the assignments and takes his final exams. Meanwhile, Sally continues seeing Dustin.
One day, George receives a text message from Sally. They meet and she tells him she is going backpacking with Dustin through Europe and skipping graduation. He tells her he is in love with her and they go back to her apartment, where they kiss. Sally tells him she loves him too and promises they will be together one day.
George turns in all his assignments and the principal tells him he will know he has passed if his name is called at graduation.

documents.title: The Great Gatsby
documents.tagline: Reserving judgments is a matter of infinite hope... I come to the admission that it has a limit.
documents.overview: An adaptation of F. Scott Fitzgerald's Long Island-set novel, where Midwesterner Nick Carraway is lured into the lavish world of his neighbor, Jay Gatsby. Soon enough, however, Carraway will see through the cracks of Gatsby's nouveau riche existence, where obsession, madness, and tragedy await.
documents.plot:
The Great Gatsby is a 2013 American drama film directed by Baz Luhrmann, based on F. Scott Fitzgerald's novel of the same name. The film stars Leonardo DiCaprio as Jay Gatsby, Tobey Maguire as Nick Carraway, Carey Mulligan as Daisy Buchanan, and Joel Edgerton as Tom Buchanan.

The story begins in 1922, with Nick Carraway (Tobey Maguire), a young man from the Midwest who moves to Long Island's West Egg to work in the bond business. Nick rents a small house next to a grand mansion owned by Jay Gatsby (Leonardo DiCaprio), who throws extravagant parties that attract wealthy and glamorous guests.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Gatsby's true intention is to win back his lost love, Daisy Buchanan (Carey Mulligan), who is now married to the wealthy and brutish Tom Buchanan (Joel Edgerton). Through Nick, Gatsby meets Daisy again, and they rekindle their romance. However, their love is complicated by the fact that Daisy is still married to Tom, and Gatsby's wealth and social status are not enough to overcome the obstacles in their way.
