As the summer progresses, Gatsby and Daisy's affair becomes more intense, but it also puts them at risk of being discovered by Tom, who will stop at nothing to keep his marriage intact. Meanwhile, Nick is drawn into Gatsby's world and becomes increasingly fascinated by the enigmatic millionaire.

The tension between Gatsby and Tom comes to a head when George Wilson (Jason Clarke), the owner of a gas station in the Valley of Ashes, seeks revenge against Gatsby for allegedly killing his wife, Myrtle. Unbeknownst to Gatsby, it was actually Daisy who was driving the car that killed Myrtle.

In the climax of the film, Tom's mistress, Myrtle, is killed in a car accident, and George Wilson mistakenly believes that Gatsby was responsible. In a fit of rage, George shoots Gatsby in his own pool, killing him. Daisy returns to Tom, and Nick moves away from Long Island, disillusioned with the excesses and superficiality of the wealthy elite.

The film ends with Nick reflecting on the tragic events that have unfolded, and the emptiness and decay of the wealthy communities he has observed. The final shot is of Gatsby's empty pool, a symbol of the lost love and the shattered dreams of the characters.

Overall, The Great Gatsby is a visually stunning and emotionally charged adaptation of Fitzgerald's classic novel, with outstanding performances from its cast. The film explores themes of love, greed, class, and the corrupting influence of wealth, set against the backdrop of the roaring twenties in New York City.

documents.title: Extremely Loud & Incredibly Close
documents.tagline: This is not a story about September 11th, it's a story about every day after.
documents.overview: A year after his father's death, Oskar, a troubled young boy, discovers a mysterious key he believes was left for him by his father and embarks on a scavenger hunt to find the matching lock.
documents.plot:
Nine-year-old Oskar Schell is autistic and lives in New York City with his parents Linda and Thomas Schell. He is close to his father, who stimulates him with missions to hunt for clues to New York City's "lost Sixth Borough". The tasks he is given force him to explore his surroundings and communicate with others, which is not easy for him.
On September 11, 2001, schools close early, so Oskar arrives home alone to find six answering machine messages left by his father from the World Trade Center. He hides under his bed, where his grandmother finds him and stays until Linda returns. Oskar is angry at his father's funeral, especially as the casket is empty, unable to make sense of his death.
A year later, Oskar has a secret hiding place with memories of his father, including the answering machine with its messages. In his father's room, he accidentally shatters a vase, and inside finds a key in an envelope with the word "Black" on it. He becomes obsessed with finding the lock the key fits, believing it a clue from his father.
Oskar finds 472 Blacks in the New York phone book, so plans to visit each one. He lies to his mother, with whom he is becoming increasingly distant, about his outings. He first meets Abby Black, who is in the starting process of a divorce, but she tells Oskar she did not know his father. Further encounters continue to be fruitless, but he meets a variety of people, photographing and recording notes on each one in a scrapbook.
One day, Oskar ventures into his grandmother's apartment, but instead of finding her there, encounters the reclusive elderly renter that has been living there, whom his grandmother had warned him to avoid. The renter does not speak, communicating instead with the words "yes" and "no" tattooed on his hands and a writing pad. Oskar confides in him, and the man offers to accompany Oskar on his outings.
As they explore the city together, Oskar learns to face his fears, such as those of public transport and bridges. Eventually, he concludes that the stranger is his grandfather. Oskar plays the increasingly desperate answering machine recordings for him, but the man becomes agitated. He refuses to listen to the final one, and tells Oskar to stop his search. Later, Oskar sees him arguing with his grandmother and packing to leave, so he angrily tries to confront him as his taxi pulls away, saying he knows he is his long-estranged grandfather.
Oskar then notices a phone number for an estate sale circled on the back of a newspaper clipping of his father's. When he dials the number, he reaches a surprised Abby, who takes Oskar to meet her ex-husband William. William realizes that Oskar's key is the one he has been looking for, which had been left to him in the vase by his own now deceased father. William had not known the key was in the vase when he had sold the vase to Oskar's father at the estate sale.

documents.title: 47 Ronin
documents.tagline: For courage. For loyalty. For honor.
documents.overview: Kai—an outcast—joins Oishi, the leader of 47 outcast samurai.  Together they seek vengeance upon the treacherous overlord who killed their master and banished their kind.  To restore honour to their homeland, the warriors embark upon a quest that challenges them with a series of trials that would destroy ordinary warriors.
documents.plot:
47 Ronin is a 2013 American fantasy action film directed by Carl Rinsch, his only theatrical feature, and written by Chris Morgan and Hossein Amini from a story by Morgan and Walter Hamada. It is a fantastical reimagining of Chūshingura, the story of the forty-seven ronin, real masterless samurai of 18th-century Japan who avenged the death of their lord, Asano Naganori, by killing his rival, Kira Yoshinaka. Keanu Reeves stars as Kai, a half-English, half-Japanese outcast, with Hiroyuki Sanada as Oishi, Tadanobu Asano as Lord Kira, Rinko Kikuchi as the witch Mizuki and Kou Shibasaki as Mika. Universal Pictures released it in December 2013.

Kai, found as a boy in a forest, is taken in by Lord Asano, the benevolent ruler of the Akō domain. He and Asano's daughter, Mika, fall in love, despite the contempt of Asano's samurai for Kai's mixed ancestry. Lord Kira, the shogun's master of ceremonies, plots to seize Akō with the help of Mizuki, a shape-shifting witch. During a hunt, a monstrous creature attacks Asano's party, and Kai kills it. When Shogun Tsunayoshi visits Akō, Kai recognizes one of Kira's concubines as the witch, but the chief counselor, Oishi, ignores his warning.

At a tournament for the shogun's entertainment, Kira's champion, a giant armored warrior, is pitted against Asano's chosen samurai, whom Mizuki incapacitates with magic. Kai fights in his place but is unmasked and beaten. That night, Mizuki bewitches Asano into attacking the unarmed Kira, and Asano is ordered to commit ritual suicide. His samurai are made ronin, forbidden to seek revenge, while Kai is sold into slavery and Mika is given a year to mourn before she must marry Kira. A year later, Oishi, released from imprisonment, gathers the scattered ronin and frees Kai, and together they seek weapons from mysterious forest demons who raised Kai, and plan to infiltrate Kira's castle during the wedding to avenge their lord, knowing that their act of loyalty will cost them their lives.

47 Ronin received negative reviews, with critics finding its fantasy elements at odds with the classic story and its characters underdeveloped, though the visuals and Sanada's performance were praised. It was a major box-office failure, grossing about $151 million worldwide against a budget estimated at over $175 million.

documents.title: 21 Jump Street
documents.tagline: They thought the streets were mean. Then they went back to high school.
documents.overview: In high school, Schmidt was a dork and Jenko was the popular jock. After graduation, both of them joined the police force and ended up as partners riding bicycles in the city park. Since they are young and look like high school students, they are assigned to an undercover unit to infiltrate a drug ring that is supplying high school students synthetic drugs.
documents.plot: When cops Schmidt and Jenko join the secret Jump Street unit, they use their youthful appearances to go undercover as high school students. They trade in their guns and badges for backpacks, and set out to shut down a dangerous drug ring. But, as time goes on, Schmidt and Jenko discover that high school is nothing like it was just a few years earlier -- and, what's more, they must again confront the teenage terror and anxiety they thought they had left behind.

documents.title: Killing Them Softly
documents.tagline: In America you're on your own.
documents.overview: Jackie Cogan is an enforcer hired to restore order after three dumb guys rob a Mob protected card game, causing the local criminal economy to collapse.
documents.plot: Jackie Cogan is an enforcer hired to restore order after three dumb guys rob a Mob protected card game, causing the local criminal economy to collapse.

documents.title: Drive
documents.tagline: There are no clean getaways.
documents.overview: Driver is a skilled Hollywood stuntman who moonlights as a getaway driver for criminals. Though he projects an icy exterior, lately he's been warming up to a pretty neighbor named Irene and her young son, Benicio. When Irene's husband gets out of jail, he enlists Driver's help in a million-dollar heist. The job goes horribly wrong, and Driver must risk his life to protect Irene and Benicio from the vengeful masterminds behind the robbery.
documents.plot:
Drive is a 2011 neo-noir crime thriller film directed by Nicolas Winding Refn, produced by Bold Films, and written by Hossein Amini.

The film takes place in Los Angeles, California, and follows the story of Driver (played by Ryan Gosling), a mysterious and introverted stunt driver who lives a solitary life. He is haunted by his past and struggles to form connections with others.

Driver's life changes when he meets Irene (played by Carey Mulligan), a single mother working as a waitress at a diner. She hires him to drive her and her son, Benicio (played by Kaden Leos), to a new home on the outskirts of town. Driver is drawn to Irene and begins to form a bond with her and her son.

However, their lives are disrupted when Irene's ex-boyfriend, Standard (played by Oscar Isaac), comes back into the picture. Standard is involved in a life of crime and has a history of violence. He becomes increasingly aggressive towards Irene and Benicio, putting them in danger.

As Driver tries to protect Irene and her son, he also becomes embroiled in Standard's world of crime. Driver agrees to drive Standard's partner, Bernie (played by Albert Brooks), on a series of heists, which puts him at odds with the law.

Throughout the film, Refn uses long takes and atmospheric soundscapes to create a sense of tension and unease. The cinematography is stunning, capturing the dark and gritty underbelly of Los Angeles.

As the story unfolds, Driver's past begins to surface. It is revealed that he was once involved in a violent incident with Standard, which left him with emotional scars. This backstory adds depth to Driver's character, making him more than just a stoic protagonist.

The film builds towards a climactic confrontation between Driver and Standard, which ends in tragedy. In the end, Driver must confront his own demons and make a choice that will determine the fate of Irene and Benicio.

Drive is a critically acclaimed film known for its atmospheric tension, stunning cinematography, and Ryan Gosling's nuanced performance as Driver. The film has been praised for its exploration of themes such as loneliness, violence, and redemption.

documents.title: It's Not You, It's Me
documents.overview: Javier se ha casado con María, el amor de su vida, y ahora lo único que desea es estar feliz con ella el resto de su vida, pero el destino se la quita poco después de la boda. Ahora Javier está enredado en sus emociones: ¿cómo aceptará la muerte de su mujer para encontrar nuevamente el amor?
documents.plot:
It's Not You, It's Me (Spanish: No eres tú, soy yo) is a 2010 Mexican romantic comedy directed by Alejandro Springall and starring Eugenio Derbez, Alejandra Barros and Martina García, with Juan Ramírez and Alberto Estrella in supporting roles. It is a remake of the 2004 Argentine film No sos vos, soy yo, written and directed by Juan Taratuto. Produced by Matthias Ehrenberg and shot in Mexico City, it was one of Derbez's first leading roles in a feature film, several years before his international success with Instructions Not Included.

Javier Herrera is a cardiovascular surgeon who has just married his longtime partner, María, and believes their future together is secure. Shortly after the wedding, however, María tells him that she has fallen in love with someone else and is leaving him. Javier suddenly finds himself with no wife, no work, no money and no home of his own, and he is forced to start his life over from scratch.

Unable to stop thinking about María, Javier slides into a comic depression. He sees therapists and even tries esoteric treatments in search of a cure for his broken heart. Following advice that a pet will help him meet women, he adopts a dog, but his attempts to date only remind him of his ex-wife. Things begin to change when he meets Julia, a free-spirited young single mother who works at a pet shop. Julia offers him friendship and affection without conditions, and the two begin a relationship. Yet Javier remains unable to let go of his past, and when María reappears, he must decide whether to cling to the life he lost or take a chance on the future Julia represents.

The film was released in Mexican cinemas in August 2010. It closely follows the structure and humor of the Argentine original while transferring the story to Mexico City, and it gave Derbez, then best known for his sketch comedy work on television, the chance to play a more grounded romantic lead, with Alejandra Barros as the departing wife and Colombian actress Martina García as Julia.

documents.title: Take Shelter
documents.tagline: Far away from the cruel world.
documents.overview: Plagued by a series of apocalyptic visions, a young husband and father questions whether to shelter his family from a coming storm, or from himself.
documents.plot:
Take Shelter is a 2011 American psychological thriller written and directed by Jeff Nichols, starring Michael Shannon as Curtis LaForche, a young husband and father, and Jessica Chastain as his wife Samantha. The film follows a man tormented by apocalyptic visions, who must decide whether to protect his family from a coming storm or from his own fear that he is losing his mind.

In the small town of LaGrange, Ohio, Curtis, a construction worker, begins to suffer vivid nightmares and hallucinations: rain falling like motor oil, menacing flocks of birds and people close to him turning violent. He hides his visions from Samantha and their deaf daughter Hannah, instead channeling his anxiety into an obsessive project to expand the storm shelter in his backyard.

His behavior becomes increasingly strange. He cuts off people who have hurt him only in his dreams, borrows heavy equipment from his employer without permission and takes out a risky loan for the shelter without telling his wife. Aware that his mother developed paranoid schizophrenia at about his age, Curtis seeks help at a free clinic, fearing that he has inherited the illness. When Samantha discovers what he has been doing, the strain on their marriage grows, even as the family prepares for Hannah's cochlear implant surgery. Losing his job and his health insurance, alienating friends and becoming the subject of gossip in the close-knit community, Curtis is torn between his conviction that a devastating storm is coming and the possibility that the threat lies within his own mind.

The film explores mental illness, family responsibility and fear in a small working-class community, building tension through ambiguity rather than spectacle.

Take Shelter premiered at the Sundance Film Festival and won the Critics' Week Grand Prix at Cannes in 2011 before its release by Sony Pictures Classics. It received critical acclaim, with 92 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 85, and won Saturn Awards for Nichols's writing and Shannon's performance.

documents.title: Grudge Match
documents.tagline: Stallone vs DeNiro
documents.overview: A pair of aging boxing rivals are coaxed out of retirement to fight one final bout -- 30 years after their last match.
documents.plot: A pair of aging boxing rivals are coaxed out of retirement to fight one final bout -- 30 years after their last match.

documents.title: Inception: The Cobol Job
documents.overview: The Cobol Job is a fourteen-minute animated prequel to Christopher Nolan’s award-winning movie: Inception, detailing the heist on Mr. Kaneda's mind by Nash, Cobb, Arthur, and several Cobol Engineering thugs.
documents.plot:
Inception: The Cobol Job is a 2010 animated motion comic that serves as a prequel to Christopher Nolan's science fiction thriller Inception, leading directly into the dream heist that opens the film. Written by Jordan Goldberg and directed by Ian Kirby, it runs roughly fourteen minutes and adapts a comic illustrated by Long Vo, Joe Ng and Crystal Reid of the studio Udon. The comic was first published online on Inception's official website and on Yahoo! Movies as part of Warner Bros.' viral marketing campaign for the film, and the animated version was later included among the bonus features on the second disc of the film's Blu-ray release in December 2010.

The story opens with Cobb recalling the lessons of his mentor Miles, who taught him the art of shared dreaming and insisted that creation should be for its own sake rather than for profit. Cobb, his point man Arthur and Nash, an unreliable architect chosen only because he was available, have been hired by Cobol Engineering to extract a secret from the mind of Mr. Kaneda, a paranoid executive. The dream takes the form of a downtown district of skyscrapers, a bank and an office tower, and Cobol insists on sending along several armed thugs as "tourists" to make sure the job gets done. Early on Cobb is distracted by a vision of his late wife Mal and is nearly killed by a bus, saved only by Arthur.

While Arthur and the tourists stage a jewellery-store robbery to draw off the police, Nash guides Cobb to Kaneda's office. Cobb threatens the executive and produces a bomb, but the dream begins to collapse after Nash is killed by Kaneda's receptionist. When Kaneda finally unlocks his computer, Cobb finds that the file he wants, the RDS-1 Energy Expansion Program, is protected by a password that only its originator, Saito, knows. The bomb goes off and Cobb wakes in a hostage room guarded by Cobol's men. The firm's chief, Woodruff, reveals that the information was meant to win Fischer Morrow's backing for an oil pipeline along Africa's eastern coast. Cobb agrees to go after Saito himself, on condition that there are no tourists and only he, Arthur and Nash take part, since Saito is trained in dream-sharing and will be on guard from the start. The prequel ends as Cobb prepares the plan that becomes the opening sequence of Inception.

documents.title: Too Big to Fail
documents.tagline: Main Street took the fall. Wall Street got the check.
documents.overview: An intimate look at the epochal financial crisis of 2008 and the powerful men and women who decided the fate of the world's economy in a matter of a few weeks.
documents.plot:
Too Big to Fail is a 2011 American biographical drama television film directed by Curtis Hanson and written by Peter Gould, based on Andrew Ross Sorkin's 2009 non-fiction book of the same name. Its ensemble cast includes William Hurt as Treasury Secretary Henry Paulson and Paul Giamatti as Federal Reserve Chair Ben Bernanke, along with Edward Asner, Billy Crudup, Topher Grace, Cynthia Nixon, Bill Pullman, Tony Shalhoub and James Woods. The film premiered on HBO on May 23, 2011, and chronicles the 2008 financial crisis, centering on the collapse of the investment bank Lehman Brothers and its effects on the global economy.

In 2008, in the middle of an election year, the subprime mortgage crisis is battering investment banks loaded with real estate assets. Having already guaranteed the sale of Bear Stearns to JPMorgan Chase at a fraction of its value, Paulson is wary of another bailout and refuses to intervene as shares of Lehman Brothers plunge. Lehman's chief executive, Richard Fuld, makes a series of poor decisions, and by Friday, September 12, the bank's stock has fallen to single digits. Timothy Geithner, head of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, urges Paulson to support a merger between Lehman and Bank of America, but Paulson insists that the other major banks guarantee any deal and summons their chief executives to an emergency weekend meeting at the Federal Reserve. While they negotiate, Bank of America unexpectedly agrees to buy Merrill Lynch instead, and a last-ditch sale to the British bank Barclays is blocked by regulators in London. Lehman files for bankruptcy on September 15, and the consequences are immediate: the stock market crashes, investors pull out their money, lending freezes and the insurance giant AIG faces a liquidity crisis that threatens the entire international financial system. With Bernanke warning of another Great Depression, Paulson and his team scramble to rescue AIG and to find a way to restore credit, debating plans to buy toxic assets or to inject capital directly into the banks while trying to persuade Congress and Wall Street to cooperate.

The film received generally favorable reviews, with a 74% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 67 out of 100. It earned 11 nominations at the 63rd Primetime Emmy Awards, and Giamatti won the Screen Actors Guild Award for his portrayal of Bernanke.

documents.title: Shark Night 3D
documents.tagline: Terror runs deep.
documents.overview: A weekend at a lake house in the Louisiana Gulf turns into a nightmare for seven vacationers as they are subjected to fresh-water shark attacks.
documents.plot:
Shark Night 3D is an action-thriller film that revolves around a group of college students who embark on a disastrous boat trip to a lake in search of thrills and adventure. The movie's narrative is driven by the theme of reckless abandon, as the characters' desire for excitement and freedom ultimately leads them into a perilous situation.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the true horror lies not with the sharks themselves, but with the characters' own flaws and weaknesses. The film expertly weaves together elements of suspense, terror, and social commentary, highlighting the dangers of peer pressure, impulsive behavior, and the consequences of underestimating the power of nature.

Throughout the movie, the characters are forced to confront their own mortality and the fragility of human life in the face of the natural world. The film's portrayal of the sharks as mindless killers serves as a metaphor for the unpredictable and often deadly forces that can be unleashed when humans overstep their boundaries.

Ultimately, Shark Night 3D is a cautionary tale about the importance of responsibility, respect, and self-awareness in the face of nature's fury. The movie's over-the-top action sequences and gruesome special effects serve as a reminder of the devastating consequences of playing with forces beyond human control.

documents.title: The Descendants
documents.tagline: The South Pacific ain't that terrific.
documents.overview: With his wife Elizabeth on life support after a boating accident, Hawaiian land baron Matt King takes his daughters on a trip from Oahu to Kauai to confront a young real estate broker, who was having an affair with Elizabeth before her misfortune.
documents.plot: With his wife Elizabeth on life support after a boating accident, Hawaiian land baron Matt King takes his daughters on a trip from Oahu to Kauai to confront a young real estate broker, who was having an affair with Elizabeth before her misfortune.

documents.title: The Woman in Black
documents.tagline: What did they see?
documents.overview: The story follows a young lawyer, Arthur Kipps, who is ordered to travel to a remote village and sort out a recently deceased client’s papers. As he works alone in the client’s isolated house, Kipps begins to uncover tragic secrets, his unease growing when he glimpses a mysterious woman dressed only in black. Receiving only silence from the locals, Kipps is forced to uncover the true identity of the Woman in Black on his own, leading to a desperate race against time when he discovers her true identity.
documents.plot: The story follows a young lawyer, Arthur Kipps, who is ordered to travel to a remote village and sort out a recently deceased client’s papers. As he works alone in the client’s isolated house, Kipps begins to uncover tragic secrets, his unease growing when he glimpses a mysterious woman dressed only in black. Receiving only silence from the locals, Kipps is forced to uncover the true identity of the Woman in Black on his own, leading to a desperate race against time when he discovers her true identity.

documents.title: Lemonade Mouth
documents.tagline: Poets, geniuses, revolutionaries.
documents.overview: After five disparate high school students meet in detention, they realize they have more in common than they think and form a band that becomes a champion for students sidelined by the high school elite.
documents.plot: When five ragtag freshman first meet in detention, it seems they have nothing in common. But, through music, they form an unbreakable bond and discover they have the makings of the greatest high school garage band in history! In the face of incredible odds, Olivia, Stella, Wen, Mohini and Charlie find they can make a real difference when they learn to lean on each other and let go of everything holding back their dreams.

documents.title: Tomboy
documents.tagline: There's a new kid in town.
documents.overview: A French family moves to a new neighborhood with during the summer holidays. The story follows a 10-year-old gender non-conforming child, Laure, who experiments with their gender presentation, adopting the name Mikäel.
documents.plot: Ten-year-old Laure isn't like most girls. She prefers football to dolls and sweaters to dresses. When Laure and her family move to a new neighbourhood, local girl Lisa mistakes Laure for a boy. Indulging in this exciting new identity, Laure becomes Mickaël, and so begins a summer of long sunny afternoons, playground games and first kisses. Yet with the school term fast approaching, and with suspicions arising amongst friends and family, Laure must face up to an uncertain future.

documents.title: Green Lantern: Emerald Knights
documents.tagline: Witness the Color of Will.
documents.overview: As the home planet of the Green Lantern Corps faces a battle with an ancient enemy, Hal Jordan prepares new recruit Arisia for the coming conflict by relating stories of the first Green Lantern and several of Hal's comrades.
documents.plot:
Green Lantern: Emerald Knights is a 2011 animated film that serves as a companion piece to the 2011 live-action film Green Lantern, directed by Martin Campbell. The movie takes place during the events of the original film and explores the history of the Green Lantern Corps through a series of vignettes.

The story begins with Hal Jordan (voiced by Jason O'Mara), who is struggling to come to terms with his failure as a test pilot and his subsequent recruitment into the Green Lantern Corps. He is visited by the Guardians of the Universe, who inform him that he has been chosen to be the new Green Lantern.

However, things take a turn when Hal discovers that the Guardians are planning to destroy the planet Oa, which serves as their homeworld, in order to prevent it from falling into the wrong hands. The Guardians believe that this is necessary to protect the universe from the evil Sinestro, who seeks to use the power of the yellow ring to conquer the cosmos.

As Hal tries to convince the Guardians to reconsider their decision, he is joined by other Green Lanterns, including John Stewart (voiced by Kevin Tanaka), Carol Ferris (voiced by Kyra Sedgwick), and Tom Kalmaku (voiced by Michael Dorn). Together, they embark on a series of adventures that take them across the galaxy.

One of these adventures takes Hal to the planet Poltarax, where he encounters the Green Lantern who was killed in action during the events of the original film. The Lantern's spirit is revealed to be that of Abin Sur (voiced by Nolan North), who had been a member of the Corps before his death.

Through a series of flashbacks, we learn about Abin's backstory and his struggles with the power of the ring. We also see how he came to be killed by Sinestro, who was seeking revenge against the Corps for their interference in his plans.

As Hal continues on his journey, he is joined by other Lanterns, including Laira (voiced by Mae Whitman) and Sojourner (voiced by Jennifer Hale). Together, they face off against Sinestro and his army of yellow-clad warriors.

The final battle takes place on the planet Oa, where Hal and the Guardians engage in a fierce struggle to prevent the destruction of their homeworld. In the end, it is revealed that the Guardians' plan was not entirely altruistic - they had been using the power of the ring to maintain control over the Corps for centuries.

The film ends with Hal coming to terms with his new role as a Green Lantern and his responsibilities to the Corps. He also begins to understand the true nature of the ring and its power, which he will continue to explore in future adventures.

Overall, Green Lantern: Emerald Knights is a visually stunning and action-packed film that explores the history and mythology of the Green Lantern Corps. While it may not be as well-known as some other DC Comics properties, it offers a unique perspective on the universe and its characters, and provides a compelling companion piece to the original live-action film.

documents.title: Sexual Predator
documents.tagline: The hunt for pleasure is the most basic instinct of all.
documents.overview: A female parole officer unwittingly gets involved with a handsome photographer who might be a serial killer.
documents.plot:
Sexual Predator, also known as Last Cry, is a 2001 American erotic thriller directed by Robert Angelo from a screenplay by Ed Silverstein. Produced by Marc Lawrence for Magic Hour Pictures and MRG Entertainment, with cinematography by David Trulli and music by Michael Vista, it stars Angie Everhart and Richard Grieco, with Kevin Fry, Elizabeth Barondes, Julian Christopher, Ray Valenti and Roy Abrahamson. Made for cable and home video, it belongs to the wave of softcore psychological thrillers popular in the late 1990s and early 2000s, and Angelo had already worked in the genre with films such as Mutual Needs and Forbidden Sins.

J.C. Gale (Grieco) is a photographer known for provocative erotic work. He is charged with the death of a woman who died during an act of erotic asphyxiation, and although he is found guilty, the conviction is reduced to manslaughter and he receives five years' probation. The victim was the best friend of Beth Spinella (Everhart), a probation officer who specializes in sex offenders, and she is assigned as his case officer. Beth sets out to build a sexual profile of Gale, but instead he gradually draws her into a world of erotic experiences, photographing her in his studio and taking her to a sex club, until he succeeds in seducing her. At the same time, someone begins stalking Beth, killing her cat and then murdering one of Gale's models. Her boyfriend Joe (Fry) is convinced that Gale is the killer, but Beth, fearing for her job, cannot reveal that she has been sleeping with the man she is supposed to supervise. The film ends with a twist revealing that the murderer is none of the characters the script has led the audience to suspect.

The film was released on DVD by Columbia TriStar. Critical reaction was sharply divided. Moria's Richard Scheib gave it three stars, calling it surprisingly slick and well photographed, praising the time it devotes to its plot, the unexpected complexity of its two leads and Grieco's darkly ambiguous performance, and describing the final twist as excellent, though he found it implausible that Beth would be allowed to supervise the man accused of killing her friend. Walter Chaw of Film Freak Central gave it zero stars, dismissing it as cheap and exploitative and criticizing its production values, acting, direction and screenplay.

documents.title: Student Services
documents.overview: Nineteen-year-old Laura is stressed by her first year at college when money worries distract her from her studies and so, desperate for cash, she answers an online advertisement for intimate companionship that leads her down a dangerous path.
documents.plot:
Student Services (French: Mes chères études) is a 2010 French television drama written and directed by Emmanuelle Bercot, adapted from Laura D.'s autobiographical book Mes chères études (2008). Déborah François stars as a cash-strapped first-year university student who drifts into selling sex to pay for her studies. The film was first broadcast by Canal+ on January 18, 2010, and later had a theatrical release in Poland and Italy.

Laura, 19, is determined to succeed at university, but the money from her job at a call centre is not enough to live on. She faints during a lecture because she has not been eating properly, and her working-class parents cannot afford to give her more. When her electricity is cut off over unpaid bills, she searches online for extra work and finds an advertisement from Joe, a 57-year-old man offering a hundred euros an hour to a student willing to keep him company. Telling herself it will happen only once, she meets him in a hotel room three days later. She is nervous and ashamed, but the practised Joe smooths things over, telling her that it is all about fantasy and that nowadays everything, fantasy included, is for sale. His money pays her bills and even a small party, and the episode becomes the start of a downward spiral. Exhilarated by money that seems so easily earned, she tries to forget the experiences themselves and remember only the envelopes of cash, and she keeps meeting men she finds online, with Joe becoming a regular. From the second client onward she wants to stop, but she never grows used to what is demanded of her. Clients push past her limits and cheat her out of payment, among them an abusive photographer and a man who meets her in a car park, and eventually even Joe betrays her. Strained further by her relationships with her callous first love Manu and the indolent Benjamin, Laura finally breaks down.

François plays Laura, with Alain Cauchi as Joe, Benjamin Siksou as Manu, Mathieu Demy as Benjamin, Anna Sigalevitch as Fanny and Marc Chapiteau as the photographer. Produced by Les Films du Kiosque, it was shot mainly in the centre of Besançon. François later said one sex scene, in which she lay trapped beneath a very heavy naked actor, was especially hard to film. Critics praised her performance, with MaryAnn Johanson calling the film well-acted and far more sad than scandalous, but several found the screenplay unconvincing for its thin character development.

documents.title: The Good Doctor
documents.tagline: Do no harm.
documents.overview: Dr. Martin Blake, who has spent his life looking for respect, meets an 18-year-old patient named Diane, suffering from a kidney infection, and gets a much-needed boost of self-esteem. However, when her health starts improving, Martin fears losing her, so he begins tampering with her treatment, keeping Diane sick and in the hospital right next to him.
documents.plot:
The Good Doctor is a 2011 American psychological thriller directed by Lance Daly and written by John Enbom. Orlando Bloom, who also produced the film, stars as Martin Blake, an ambitious young doctor, with Riley Keough, Taraji P. Henson, Rob Morrow, Michael Peña and J. K. Simmons in supporting roles. It premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival in April 2011.

Martin Blake, a British doctor, begins his residency at a hospital in Southern California. Outwardly charming and polite, he is in fact a deeply insecure narcissist who craves respect and control over others. His aloof manner alienates the nurses, especially the experienced Nurse Theresa, whom he believes do not show him the deference he deserves, and his first encounters with patients go poorly, leaving him on uncertain ground with his superiors.

Everything changes when Diane Nixon, an eighteen-year-old patient, is admitted with a kidney infection. Martin treats her successfully, and Diane and her family treat him as a hero, giving him the admiration he craves. As Diane recovers and is about to leave the hospital, Martin, unwilling to lose her attention and the validation she provides, begins secretly tampering with her medication to keep her ill, all while presenting himself as devoted to her care. Their relationship becomes increasingly inappropriate as he continues to visit her after she returns home. His manipulations eventually spiral out of control and lead to tragedy. An orderly named Jimmy discovers evidence of what Martin has done and blackmails him, and a police detective begins investigating, forcing Martin to go to ever greater lengths to protect himself and his career while maintaining the facade of the caring, dedicated doctor.

The film received mixed reviews, with a 66 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 52. Ronnie Scheib of Variety noted the black comedy lurking beneath its suspenseful surface, with more than a hint of Lolita-esque absurdity, and Sura Wood of The Hollywood Reporter called it a tense psychosexual film. Critics generally praised Bloom's unsettling performance against type.

documents.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
documents.original_title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
documents.tagline: Evil shall with evil be expelled.
documents.overview: This English-language adaptation of the Swedish novel by Stieg Larsson follows a disgraced journalist, Mikael Blomkvist, as he investigates the disappearance of a weary patriarch's niece from 40 years ago. He is aided by the pierced, tattooed, punk computer hacker named Lisbeth Salander. As they work together in the investigation, Blomkvist and Salander uncover immense corruption beyond anything they have ever imagined.
documents.plot:
The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo is a 2011 psychological thriller film directed by David Fincher, based on the bestselling novel of the same name by Stieg Larsson. The movie stars Daniel Craig as Mikael Blomkvist, a journalist, and Rooney Mara as Lisbeth Salander, a young hacker.

The story begins with Mikael Blomkvist, a successful but troubled journalist who has lost his job due to an article he wrote that was deemed too critical of the wealthy elite. He is approached by Henrik Vanger, the patriarch of a wealthy family in Sweden, who hires him to investigate the disappearance of his niece, Harriet, 40 years ago.

Henrik believes that Harriet's disappearance is connected to an ancient family curse and asks Blomkvist to uncover the truth. As Blomkvist delves deeper into the case, he meets Lisbeth Salander, a brilliant but troubled young hacker who has been institutionalized for her mental health issues. Despite their initial reluctance, they form an unlikely partnership to solve the mystery.

As they dig deeper, they uncover a web of dark secrets and corruption within the Vanger family, including a possible murder that may be connected to Harriet's disappearance. Lisbeth's hacking skills prove invaluable in uncovering evidence that Blomkvist would have otherwise missed.

Throughout their investigation, Blomkvist and Lisbeth develop a complex and intense relationship, with Lisbeth's troubled past slowly revealed. They face numerous obstacles, including the family's attempts to silence them and Lisbeth's own demons.

As they get closer to the truth, they discover that Harriet was not just any ordinary victim but had been involved in some shady dealings within the family. The investigation leads them to a shocking revelation: Harriet's disappearance is linked to an ancient ritual that has been passed down through generations of Vangers.

In the climactic final act, Blomkvist and Lisbeth confront the mastermind behind the ritual, who is revealed to be Henrik himself. In a stunning twist, it is revealed that Henrik had orchestrated Harriet's murder to cover up his own dark secrets and protect the family's reputation.

The film ends with Blomkvist and Lisbeth finally solving the mystery, but not without scars. Lisbeth has found a sense of purpose and belonging with Blomkvist, while he has gained a new appreciation for her unique skills and perspective. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, with Lisbeth finally finding some measure of peace and acceptance.

Overall, The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo is a gripping thriller that explores themes of corruption, power, and redemption. With its complex characters, intricate plot, and Fincher's masterful direction, it's no wonder this film has become a modern classic in the world of cinema.

documents.title: Happy Feet Two
documents.tagline: Every step counts.
documents.overview: Mumble the penguin has a problem: his son Erik, who is reluctant to dance, encounters The Mighty Sven, a penguin who can fly! Things get worse for Mumble when the world is shaken by powerful forces, causing him to brings together the penguin nations and their allies to set things right.
documents.plot:
Happy Feet Two is a 2011 animated musical comedy-drama film produced by Warner Bros. Animation and directed by George Miller, the director of the original Happy Feet.

The movie takes place two years after the events of the first film. Mumble (voiced by Elijah Wood), the tap-dancing Emperor Penguin, has become an international celebrity for his unique talent. However, with fame comes pressure to conform to traditional penguin norms, and Mumble struggles to balance his love for dance with the expectations of his colony.

The story begins with Mumble's father, Ramón (voiced by Hugo Weaving), who is struggling to find a suitable mate for his son due to Mumble's unusual appearance. Meanwhile, a new threat emerges in the form of a group of Adelie penguins from Antarctica, led by the ruthless and cunning Adelie (voiced by Brittany Murphy). The Adelies are determined to take over the Antarctic ice sheet and destroy the Emperor Penguins' home.

As Mumble navigates his relationships with his family and friends, he also discovers that he has a special connection to the Adelies. He learns that they possess a unique genetic trait that allows them to survive in the harsh Antarctic environment. However, this trait comes at a cost: it makes them aggressive and violent towards other penguins.

Mumble soon realizes that his tap-dancing abilities are not just a quirk, but a key to understanding the Adelies' behavior. He uses his dance moves to communicate with the Adelies and learn more about their motivations. Along the way, he befriends a young Adelie named Erik (voiced by Robyn Moore), who becomes his ally in the fight against the Adelies.

As tensions between the Emperors and Adelies escalate, Mumble must use his unique talents to bring peace to the two groups. He performs an epic dance battle with the Adelies, using his tap-dancing skills to outsmart and outmaneuver them. The dance battle is a thrilling display of penguin agility and creativity, showcasing the unique abilities of each species.

In the end, Mumble's efforts pay off, and the Emperors and Adelies are able to coexist peacefully. The movie concludes with Mumble returning home to his colony, where he is celebrated as a hero for his bravery and ingenuity. The film ends on a hopeful note, with Mumble's message of acceptance and understanding resonating throughout the penguin community.

Overall, Happy Feet Two is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of identity, community, and the power of dance to bring people together. With its stunning animation, catchy musical numbers, and lovable characters, it is a must-see for fans of animated films and music lovers alike.

documents.title: Jackass 3.5
documents.tagline: Warning: The stunts in this movie were performed by professionals, so neither you or your dumb little buddies should attempt anything from this movie.
documents.overview: Johnny Knoxville of 'Jackass' releases unused material of stunts, tricks, antics and shenanigans shot during the production of 'Jackass 3D' that didn't make it into the film, as well as the hilarious outtakes.
documents.plot: Johnny Knoxville of 'Jackass' releases unused material of stunts, tricks, antics and shenanigans shot during the production of 'Jackass 3D' that didn't make it into the film, as well as the hilarious outtakes.

documents.title: Arctic Predator
documents.overview: A team searching for a long-lost ship in the Arctic unwittingly unleash an alien creature that looks like it's made of ice.
documents.plot:
Arctic Predator, released in the United States as Frost Giant, is a 2010 science fiction horror thriller made for television, directed by Víctor García from a screenplay by Rafael Jordan and produced by UFO Films and Arctic Productions. It stars Dean Cain, the former television Superman, as J.C., the dedicated leader of an expedition searching the Arctic for a lost ship, with Steven Waddington, Lucy Brown and Louisa Clein in supporting roles.

J.C. and his small team of explorers and scientists are hunting for the wreck of a 19th-century sailing ship that vanished in the ice near an Arctic island nearly two hundred years earlier. J.C.'s interest is personal: the ship was captained by one of his distant ancestors, and his own life comes to mirror that of his forefather. When the team finally locates the frozen vessel and begins carefully thawing its centuries-old artefacts, they unwittingly release something that has been entombed in the ice alongside it: an alien creature that appears to be made of ice itself.

Once free, the creature begins stalking the members of the expedition one by one at their isolated base, killing them to absorb the heat and energy it needs to recover its strength and return to where it came from, and leaving its victims frozen solid. As a violent storm cuts the survivors off, a desperate attempt to escape by helicopter ends when the injured pilot crashes, and the team is forced to improvise crude solutions, at one point cauterising a wound with a household iron. J.C. must find a way to stop the monster before it kills everyone and reaches the mainland.

The cast also includes Mike Johnson, Laia Gonzàlez, Iliana Lazarova, Mike Straub, Erbi Ago and Velizar Binev. Reviews were largely negative. Critics described it as a low-budget stalk-and-slay picture borrowing heavily from The Thing, with a creature reminiscent of the Predator; Dread Central found it blandly assembled and frequently tedious, while others criticised its cheap computer-generated effects, repetitive deaths and stock characters. The Exploding Helicopter blog nonetheless singled out the subplot linking the hero to the ship's captain as one genuinely good idea, and several reviewers felt Cain did what he could with weak material.

documents.title: Think Like a Man
documents.tagline: Let the mind games begin.
documents.overview: The balance of power in four couples’ relationships is upset when the women start using the advice in Steve Harvey’s book, Act Like A Lady, Think Like A Man, to get more of what they want from their men. When the men realize that the women have gotten a hold of their relationship “playbook,” they decide that the best defense is a good offense and come up with a plan to use this information to their advantage.
documents.plot:
Think Like a Man is a 2012 American romantic comedy directed by Tim Story, written by Keith Merryman and David A. Newman and produced by Will Packer. It is based on comedian Steve Harvey's 2009 relationship advice book Act Like a Lady, Think Like a Man. The ensemble cast includes Kevin Hart, Meagan Good, Jerry Ferrara, Regina Hall, Michael Ealy, Terrence J, Taraji P. Henson, Romany Malco, Chris Brown and Gabrielle Union.

The film follows four couples in Los Angeles whose stories are presented through archetypes drawn from Harvey's book: "The Mama's Boy" and "The Single Mom", "The Non-Committer" and "The Girl Who Wants the Ring", "The Dreamer" and "The Woman Who Is Her Own Man", and "The Player" and "The 90 Day Rule Girl". The men are a group of friends who play basketball together, while each of the women turns to Harvey's book for guidance in dealing with the men in her life.

Following the book's advice, the women begin to gain the upper hand in their relationships, setting rules and pushing their partners to change. When the men discover the source of the women's sudden insight, they obtain copies of the book and try to use its advice to turn the tables on their partners, a strategy that soon backfires. As the romantic games escalate, each couple must confront what they really want, and the men and women learn that honesty and compromise matter more than any strategy.

Production took place in Los Angeles and Culver City, California, in 2011, and the film includes cameo appearances by several professional basketball players, including Lisa Leslie, Metta World Peace and Matt Barnes, who appear as themselves, while Harvey's book is central to the plot.

Think Like a Man was released by Screen Gems on April 20, 2012, and was a major box office success, grossing 96.1 million dollars worldwide on a budget of 12.5 million dollars and ending The Hunger Games' four-week run at the top of the North American box office. Reviews were mixed, with 55 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 51. A sequel, Think Like a Man Too, was released in 2014.

documents.title: Glee: The Concert Movie
documents.tagline: The embodiment of popular culture.
documents.overview: A concert documentary shot during the Glee Live! In Concert! summer 2011 tour, featuring song performances and Glee fans' life stories and how the show influenced them.
documents.plot:
Glee: The Concert Movie is a musical comedy-drama film that explores the themes of self-discovery, friendship, and the power of music to bring people together. The movie follows the glee club members as they prepare for their concert, navigating personal struggles, relationships, and conflicts along the way.

At its core, Glee: The Concert Movie is a story about finding one's identity and voice, both literally and figuratively. The characters are on a journey of self-discovery, trying to figure out who they are and where they fit in. Through their experiences with music, they learn valuable lessons about perseverance, teamwork, and the importance of embracing their individuality.

The movie also explores the theme of community and the impact that music can have on people's lives. The glee club is more than just a group of friends singing together; it's a support system, a safe space where they can be themselves and express themselves freely. As they prepare for their concert, they learn to come together as a team, supporting each other through the ups and downs of life.

Furthermore, Glee: The Concert Movie touches on the theme of social hierarchy and cliques. The characters are often divided into different groups, with some struggling to fit in or find their place within the group. However, through music, they learn to bridge these gaps and form connections with others who may seem different from them.

Overall, Glee: The Concert Movie is a heartwarming and entertaining film that celebrates the power of music and the importance of finding one's voice and community.

documents.title: The Guard
documents.tagline: The FBI are about to discover that things work a little differently around here.
documents.overview: When a small-town Irish cop with a crass personality is partnered with a straight-laced FBI agent to bust an international drug-trafficking ring, they must settle their differences in order to take down a dangerous gang.
documents.plot:
Sergeant Gerry Boyle is an officer of the Garda Síochána (police) in the Connemara district in the west of Ireland. He is crass and confrontational, regularly indulging in drugs and alcohol even while on duty. He is also shown to be well read and highly intelligent as well as having a softer side, showing concern for his ailing mother, Eileen.
Boyle and his new subordinate, Aidan McBride, investigate a murder, with evidence apparently pointing to an occult serial killer. Shortly after, Boyle attends a briefing by an American Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) agent Wendell Everett, sent to liaise with the Garda in hunting four Irish drug traffickers led by Francis Sheehy-Skeffington, who is believed to be awaiting a massive seaborne delivery of cocaine from Jamaica. Boyle recognises one of the men in Everett's presentation as the victim of the murder he and McBride had been investigating. McBride pulls over a car driven by Sheehy and his lieutenants Clive Cornell and Liam O'Leary and is shot dead. McBride's wife, Gabriela, reports McBride's disappearance to Boyle, who promises to look into it.
The strait-laced Everett suggests that he and the unorthodox Boyle team up to track down Sheehy and his men. Everett makes the rounds, encountering Irish-speaking residents who pretend not to understand English rather than deal with an outsider. Boyle has a sexual encounter with a pair of sex workers at a hotel in town. On his way back from the hotel, Boyle spots McBride's Garda car at a "suicide hotspot" along the coast but does not believe that McBride killed himself. Gabriela, an immigrant from Croatia, tells Boyle that McBride is gay and that she married him to obtain an Irish visa as well as to make McBride "look respectable".
Meeting Everett at a local pub, Boyle notices a closed-circuit television camera and remembers that the original suspect in the murder case claimed to be frequenting it at the time of the killing. Looking over the footage from the time of the murder, they see that the suspect's alibi is valid – and Everett also spots Sheehy and Cornell at the pub. Cornell delivers a payoff to the Garda inspectors to keep them off the case and is warned that Boyle "is too unpredictable". After Sheehy meets with Boyle to half-heartedly attempt blackmail and then to offer a bribe, both are refused. Tipped off by a young boy named Eugene, Boyle discovers a cache of weapons hidden in the bog by the Provisional Irish Republican Army (IRA) and says he will arrange its return. (It is later revealed that Boyle kept a few of the guns.) Shortly after having her last wish to hear a live pub band fulfilled, Boyle's mother kills herself by overdosing on pills.
Meeting at the bar again, Everett tells Boyle that Garda sources indicate Sheehy's shipment will be coming into County Cork and that he is leaving to investigate. Returning home, Boyle is confronted in his living room by O'Leary, who has been ordered by Sheehy to murder him.

documents.title: Escape from Planet Earth
documents.tagline: Earth's greatest secrets are about to break out!
documents.overview: Astronaut Scorch Supernova finds himself caught in a trap when he responds to an SOS from a notoriously dangerous alien planet.
documents.plot:
Escape from Planet Earth is a 3D animated science fiction comedy film directed by Cal Brunker and produced by The Weinstein Company, Blue Sky Studios, and eOne Films. Released on March 9, 2012, the movie follows the story of Scorch Supernova, an astronaut who embarks on a perilous journey to rescue his son, Gary, from the clutches of an evil alien overlord.

The film begins with Scorch (voiced by Brendan Fraser) and his wife, Bonnie (voiced by Sarah Jessica Parker), living on Earth with their young son, Gary. However, when Gary is kidnapped by the evil alien, Zorgon (voiced by John Cleese), who seeks to use him as a pawn in his plan for intergalactic domination, Scorch sets out on an epic journey to rescue his son.

Scorch's spaceship, the "Mother Ship," is destroyed, and he crash-lands on the planet Earth. With the help of a group of eccentric and lovable aliens, including Gary (voiced by Tom Cavanagh), B.O.B. (voiced by Ken Jeong), and Rastapopoulos (voiced by Seth MacFarlane), Scorch navigates through the dangers of Earth's surface to reach Zorgon's fortress.

As Scorch faces various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, wild animals, and human adversaries, he also learns valuable lessons about his son and himself. Along the way, Gary grows up and becomes more confident in his abilities, eventually helping his father on their quest.

The climax of the movie features an epic battle between Scorch's team and Zorgon's minions. In the end, Scorch and his allies successfully defeat Zorgon, rescue Gary, and return to Earth as heroes.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and colorful, with a mix of humor, action, and heartwarming moments. The voice cast delivers memorable performances, bringing depth and emotion to their characters.

Overall, Escape from Planet Earth is an entertaining and family-friendly adventure that explores themes of love, perseverance, and self-discovery. While it may not be as well-known as some other animated films, it has its own unique charm and is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Cold Fish
documents.tagline: He'll make you pick up the pieces.
documents.overview: Shamoto runs a small tropical fish shop. When his daughter Mitsuko is caught shoplifting at a grocery store a man named Murata steps in to settle things between the girl and the store manager. Murata also runs a tropical fish shop and he and Shamoto soon become friendly. However Murata hides many dark secrets behind his friendly face.
documents.plot: When fish shop owner Shamoto's teenage daughter Mitsuko is caught stealing, a generous middle-aged man named Murata helps resolve the situation. The man and his wife offer to have Mitsuko work at their opposing fish store. Shamoto soon discovers that something far more sinister lives behind Murata's friendly demeanor.

documents.title: Death Note Relight 2: L's Successors
documents.original_title: デスノート：リライト2 Lを継ぐ者
documents.overview: After the events of the first movie Yagami Light faces two new adversaries as he is trying to create a perfect world without crime or criminals. This movie continues the first tv special and is a summary of the last 12 episodes of the tv anime
documents.plot:
Death Note Relight 2: L's Successors (Japanese: Desu Nōto Riraito 2: L o Tsugu Mono) is a Japanese animated television film, the second of two compilation films condensing the anime series Death Note, which was directed by Tetsurō Araki at Madhouse and based on the manga by Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata. It follows Death Note Relight: Visions of a God, which aired in August 2007 and was advertised as the complete conclusion; the popularity of the series prompted this second special, which summarizes the second part of the anime, roughly its last dozen episodes. The voice cast includes Mamoru Miyano, Kappei Yamaguchi, Shidō Nakamura, Aya Hirano, Noriko Hidaka as Near and Masaya Matsukaze as Teru Mikami.

The story picks up after the death of the detective L. High school prodigy turned college student Light Yagami, who has been secretly killing criminals as "Kira" with a supernatural notebook that kills anyone whose name is written in it, now leads the Japanese Kira investigation as the new L, while the shinigami Ryuk watches in amusement. Years later, with cults worshipping Kira, two young potential successors to L emerge: Near, who works with the United States government, and Mello, who obtains a Death Note of his own and turns it against Near's team; the hunt for Mello costs Light's father, Soichiro, his life. As suspicion falls once more on Misa Amane, Light passes her notebook to the fervent Kira supporter Teru Mikami and makes the newscaster Kiyomi Takada Kira's public spokesperson. Mello kidnaps Takada, who kills him before Light silences her. Near then arranges a meeting between Light and the remaining task force members, where Mikami tries to kill them all, but his notebook has been replaced with a decoy. Exposed as Kira and badly wounded, Light begs Ryuk for help, but the shinigami writes Light's name in his own notebook, as he had promised when they first met.

The film was broadcast by Nippon Television on 22 August 2008, nearly a year after the first Relight special. Like its predecessor, it reworks the material rather than simply replaying it, adding and omitting scenes; it contains more new footage than the first special and drops the mafia subplot, concentrating on the confrontation between Kira and L's successors Near and Mello. The original series, broadcast from October 2006 to June 2007, is widely acclaimed.

documents.title: Iron Man 3
documents.tagline: Unleash the power behind the armor.
documents.overview: When Tony Stark's world is torn apart by a formidable terrorist called the Mandarin, he starts an odyssey of rebuilding and retribution.
documents.plot:
At a New Year's Eve party in 1999, Tony Stark meets scientist Maya Hansen, the inventor of Extremis, an experimental regenerative treatment that allows recovery from crippling injuries. Disabled scientist Aldrich Killian offers them a place in his company Advanced Idea Mechanics (A.I.M.), but Stark rejects him. Thirteen years later, Stark is suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder and has frequent panic attacks due to his experiences during the alien invasion of New York. He has built dozens of new Iron Man suits to cope with his insomnia, creating friction with his girlfriend Pepper Potts.
Meanwhile, a string of bombings is claimed by a terrorist known as the Mandarin. Stark's security chief Happy Hogan is badly injured in one such attack and is put into a coma, prompting Stark to issue a televised threat to the Mandarin, revealing his home address in the process. The Mandarin sends gunship helicopters to destroy Stark's home. Hansen, who came to warn Stark, survives the attack with Potts. Stark escapes in an experimental new Iron Man suit, which his artificial intelligence J.A.R.V.I.S. pilots to rural Tennessee, following a flight plan from Stark's investigation into the Mandarin. Stark's new armor is not fully functional and lacks sufficient power to return to Malibu, leading the world to believe that he died.
With the help of Harley Keener, a local boy, Stark investigates the remains of a local explosion bearing the hallmarks of a Mandarin attack. However, it occurred years before any known attack by a terrorist. He discovers the "bombings" were triggered by soldiers subjected to Extremis whose bodies explosively rejected the treatment, and were falsely attributed by A.I.M. as a terrorist plot to cover up Extremis' flaws. Stark witnesses Extremis firsthand when Mandarin agents Savin and Brandt attack him. Stark kills Brandt and incapacitates Savin. Meanwhile, Killian resurfaces and kidnaps Potts with assistance from Hansen. American intelligence agencies continue to search for the Mandarin, with James Rhodes—the former War Machine, now re-branded as the Iron Patriot—lured into a trap to steal his armor.
Tracing the Mandarin to Miami, Stark infiltrates his headquarters using improvised weapons. Inside, he discovers the Mandarin is English actor Trevor Slattery, who is oblivious to the actions carried out in his image. Killian, the mastermind behind Slattery's cover, captures Stark. Killian, who appropriated Hansen's Extremis research as a cure for his own disability and expanded the program to include injured war veterans, reveals he has subjected Potts to Extremis in the hope Stark will help fix Extremis' flaws while trying to save her. When Hansen betrays Killian by threatening to jeopardize his operations, Killian kills her.
Stark escapes and reunites with Rhodes, discovering that Killian intends to attack President Ellis aboard Air Force One, using the Iron Patriot armor, controlled by Savin.

documents.title: The Master
documents.tagline: Every man needs a guide.
documents.overview: Freddie, a volatile, heavy-drinking veteran who suffers from post-traumatic stress disorder, finds some semblance of a family when he stumbles onto the ship of Lancaster Dodd, the charismatic leader of a new "religion" he forms after World War II.
documents.plot:
The Master is a 2012 American period psychological drama film written and directed by Paul Thomas Anderson, starring Joaquin Phoenix as Freddie Quell, a troubled World War II Navy veteran, and Philip Seymour Hoffman as Lancaster Dodd, the charismatic leader of a movement called The Cause, with Amy Adams, Laura Dern and Jesse Plemons in supporting roles. Its inspirations included Scientology founder L. Ron Hubbard, Thomas Pynchon's novel V., John Huston's documentary about traumatized veterans Let There Be Light, and stories told to Anderson by Jason Robards. Produced by Annapurna Pictures and Ghoulardi Film Company and distributed by The Weinstein Company, it was shot almost entirely on 65 mm film, the first fiction feature shot and released in 70 mm since Hamlet in 1996.

In 1950, Freddie is a violent, sex-obsessed alcoholic who drifts from job to job, losing work as a department store photographer after a fight and fleeing a California farm when a colleague collapses after drinking his homemade liquor. In San Francisco he stows away on the yacht of one of Dodd's followers, and Dodd takes an interest in him, invites him to stay for his daughter's wedding and develops a taste for his potent moonshine. Dodd subjects Freddie to "processing", an intense series of psychological questions that brings him to tears over Doris, a girl he left behind at home. Freddie joins Dodd's family as they spread The Cause along the East Coast, but his loyalty takes the form of violence against anyone who challenges his mentor, troubling Dodd's wife Peggy, while Dodd's son Val confides that his father is making it up as he goes. After Dodd is arrested for practicing medicine without qualifications and Freddie attacks the police, the two clash furiously in their jail cells before reconciling, even as members of the movement come to fear Freddie. Dodd insists that rigorous conditioning can cure him, but Freddie struggles to submit, and he eventually rides off alone into the desert during a game on a salt flat, though the two men's story is not yet over.

The film premiered at the Venice Film Festival, winning the Silver Lion for Anderson's direction and a shared Volpi Cup for Phoenix and Hoffman, and opened in the United States on September 14, 2012, to wide acclaim. It received three Academy Award nominations, for Phoenix, Hoffman and Adams.

documents.title: Elysium
documents.tagline: He can save us all.
documents.overview: In the year 2159, two classes of people exist: the very wealthy who live on a pristine man-made space station called Elysium, and the rest, who live on an overpopulated, ruined Earth. Secretary Rhodes, a hard line government ofﬁcial, will stop at nothing to enforce anti-immigration laws and preserve the luxurious lifestyle of the citizens of Elysium. That doesn’t stop the people of Earth from trying to get in, by any means they can. When unlucky Max is backed into a corner, he agrees to take on a daunting mission that, if successful, will not only save his life, but could bring equality to these polarized worlds.
documents.plot:
Elysium is a 2013 science fiction action film directed by Neill Blomkamp and produced by TriStar Pictures and Sony Pictures. The movie takes place in a dystopian future where the world has been ravaged by poverty, crime, and corruption.

The story follows Max Da Costa (played by Matt Damon), a former soldier who works as a cleaner on the spaceship Elysium, a luxurious space station that serves as a refuge for the wealthy and powerful. The ship is home to the ruling class, who live in opulence and luxury, while the rest of humanity is left to struggle on Earth.

Max's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets Frey (played by Sharlto Copley), a fellow cleaner who has been injured during a botched assassination attempt. Max helps Frey escape from the ship's security forces, and in return, Frey gives Max a tour of Elysium and reveals its true nature.

As they explore the ship, Max learns that Elysium is actually a prison for the wealthy and powerful, who have escaped the chaos on Earth by fleeing to the ship. The ruling class has created a system where they can live in luxury while the rest of humanity is left to suffer on a desolate and polluted Earth.

Max becomes determined to take revenge against the people responsible for his sister's death, which was caused by the corrupt government that allowed the wealthy to escape to Elysium. He teams up with Frey and a group of rebels, including Tsele (played by Jodie Foster), a high-ranking official on Elysium who has grown disillusioned with the ship's ruling class.

As Max and his team plan their attack on Elysium, they realize that the only way to reach the ship is through a small airlock that can be opened for a limited time. The team must navigate the ship's security systems and fight off the ruling class's henchmen in order to reach the upper levels of the ship.

The final confrontation takes place on the upper deck of Elysium, where Max and his team face off against the ship's ruler, President Patrick Shaw (played by William Fichtner). In a tense showdown, Max manages to defeat Shaw and destroy the airlock, allowing him and Frey to escape from the ship.

However, as they make their way back to Earth, Max realizes that he has become a symbol of hope for the oppressed people on the planet. He decides to stay on Earth and fight for justice, using his newfound status to bring about change and equality.

The movie ends with Max standing on the surface of Earth, looking out at the desolate landscape, but also seeing a glimmer of hope for a better future. The final shot is of Elysium, now empty and abandoned, a symbol of the corrupt system that has been brought down by Max's actions.

Overall, Elysium is a thought-provoking sci-fi action film that explores themes of class struggle, corruption, and redemption. The movie features impressive visuals and a gripping storyline, making it a must-see for fans of science fiction and action movies.

documents.title: Pacific Rim
documents.tagline: To fight monsters, we created monsters.
documents.overview: As war between humankind and monstrous sea creatures wages on, a former pilot and a trainee are paired up to drive a seemingly obsolete special weapon in a desperate effort to save the world.
documents.plot:
Pacific Rim is a science fiction monster film directed by Guillermo del Toro and written by Travis Beacham. The movie takes place in a post-apocalyptic world where humanity is on the brink of extinction due to an invasion by giant monsters known as Kaijus from another dimension.

The story begins with a flashback of a catastrophic event that occurred 30 years ago, when a group of scientists discovered a way to harness the power of the Earth's core to create massive robots called Jaegers. The Jaegers are designed to fight against the Kaijus, which are enormous creatures that emerge from a portal in the ocean and wreak havoc on coastal cities.

The movie then jumps forward to the present day, where we meet our protagonist, Raleigh Becket (played by Charlie Hunnam), a former Jaeger pilot who lost his co-pilot and best friend, Yancy, during a mission. Raleigh is haunted by guilt and grief over Yancy's death and struggles to find purpose in his life.

Raleigh is recruited by the Jaeger program, led by Dr. Newton Geiszler (played by Idris Elba), who has developed a new technology that allows humans to control the Jaegers using brain-computer interfaces. Raleigh is paired with Mako Mori (played by Rinko Kikuchi), a young and talented pilot from Japan.

As they prepare for their first mission together, Raleigh and Mako are tasked with fighting against a Kaiju known as Gipsy Danger, which is terrorizing the city of San Francisco. The Jaegers are massive machines that require two pilots to operate, one on each side of the machine. The pilots must work in tandem to control the Jaeger's movements and attacks.

The battle against Gipsy Danger is intense and chaotic, with both Raleigh and Mako struggling to coordinate their efforts. Despite their differences, they begin to develop a bond as they fight for their lives.

As the movie progresses, we learn that the Kaijus are not just mindless monsters, but are actually creatures from another dimension that feed on human emotions. The Jaegers are designed to harness the power of the Earth's core to create energy blasts that can kill the Kaijus.

The final battle takes place in Hong Kong, where Raleigh and Mako face off against a massive Kaiju known as Knifehead. The fight is epic and intense, with both sides suffering heavy losses. In the end, Raleigh and Mako emerge victorious, but not without sacrifices.

The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Raleigh and Mako reflecting on their experiences and the bond they formed during their mission. Raleigh finally finds closure and purpose in his life, and we see him and Mako flying off into the sunset together.

Overall, Pacific Rim is an action-packed and visually stunning film that explores themes of grief, loss, and redemption. The movie features impressive practical effects and a talented cast, making it a must-see for fans of science fiction and monster movies.

documents.title: Trance
documents.tagline: Don't be a hero.
documents.overview: A violent gang enlists the help of a hypnotherapist in an attempt to locate a painting which somehow vanished in the middle of a heist.
documents.plot:
During a heist on an auction house, thieves take a package which presumably contains a valuable painting. Auctioneer Simon Newton attacks their leader Franck, who hits Simon on the head, knocking him unconscious. Later, Franck discovers that the package contains only an empty frame. Simon, the heist's "inside man", double-crossed him. Looking for the painting, the thieves kidnap and torture Simon. However, the blow to the head left him with a case of amnesia: he cannot recall where he hid the painting. They need a hypnotherapist to help him remember.
Simon chooses Elizabeth Lamb from a list. Using a fake name, Simon tells her that he is after some lost keys, hoping that she leads him to the painting instead. She quickly sees through Simon's façade, forcing the thieves to negotiate with her.
In exchange for a cut of the proceeds from the sale of the painting, Elizabeth keeps hypnotizing Simon. Between sessions, he reveals that his gambling addiction got him involved with Franck. Franck offered to settle Simon's debts in exchange for help stealing the painting.
In one session, Simon remembers that, during the heist, he cut the painting from the frame and hid it in his suit. When Franck was about to notice this, Simon attacked him. Shortly after the blow to his head, he awoke alone. While leaving the auction house, Simon was distracted by a text message and got hit by a red car. He erroneously remembers the driver as having been Elizabeth.
After Simon is put in another hypnotic state, the thieves discover that he is obsessed with her. She says that this is due to transference. If Elizabeth seduces Simon, she may get him to say where the painting is.

The two go on a date, where he abruptly cools toward her and goes home. She tells Franck that this happened because Simon is jealous of him. Franck and Elizabeth then have sex. One of the thieves sees this and tells Simon, who later decides to confront Elizabeth. Managing to trigger his lust and calm his jealousy, she hypnotizes him. By leading Simon through an imagined narrative in which Franck wants to kill him, Elizabeth learns the painting's location. However, she is caught by the thieves shortly after. Simon and Franck are sent to get the painting, while the other thieves stay to rape Elizabeth. When Franck is distracted by her screams, Simon overpowers him and kills the other thieves.
Elizabeth convinces Simon to spare Franck and bring him with them to get the painting. At a parking garage, the trio collect a red car and drive it to a warehouse. During the trip, Elizabeth reveals that Simon had previously come to her for help with his gambling addiction. They started an affair, but he became obsessive, jealous, and, eventually, abusive. Fearing for her life, she used hypnosis to make him forget her. When Franck hit Simon on the head, it brought back a vague sense of his memories of Elizabeth.

documents.title: Oz the Great and Powerful
documents.tagline: In Oz, nothing is what it seems.
documents.overview: Oscar Diggs, a small-time circus illusionist and con-artist, is whisked from Kansas to the Land of Oz where the inhabitants assume he's the great wizard of prophecy, there to save Oz from the clutches of evil.
documents.plot:
Oz the Great and Powerful is a 2013 American fantasy adventure film directed by Sam Raimi and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie is set in the late 19th century, about 20 years before the events of L. Frank Baum's classic novel "The Wonderful Wizard of Oz".

The story begins with Oscar Diggs (James Franco), a charming but unscrupulous magician who travels from town to town performing illusions and swindling people out of their money. One day, he arrives in Kansas, where he meets a young girl named Dorothy Gale (Mila Kunis) and her dog Toto. However, instead of being charmed by Oscar's tricks, Dorothy is skeptical of his abilities.

Despite his initial failure to impress Dorothy, Oscar soon finds himself drawn into the world of Oz, which is threatened by the evil witch Mombasa (Michelle Williams). The witches are a group of powerful sorceresses who rule over different regions of Oz, and they are at odds with each other. Mombasa seeks to overthrow the ruling council of witches and take control of the entire land.

As Oscar navigates this new world, he meets three witches - Glinda (Rachel Weisz), the Good Witch of the North; China Girl (Lindsay Duncan), a witch from the East; and the Wicked Witch of the West (Julianne Moore), Mombasa's sister. The witches are wary of Oscar's intentions, but they also see an opportunity to use him as a pawn in their struggle for power.

Oscar soon discovers that he has a special connection to Oz, which is revealed when he touches a magical crystal. This connection allows him to tap into the land's magic and perform incredible feats. However, it also makes him vulnerable to the witches' manipulation.

As the story unfolds, Oscar becomes embroiled in the conflict between the witches and must decide where his loyalties lie. Along the way, he forms a bond with Dorothy, who is struggling to find her place in Oz. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to stop Mombasa's plans and save the land from destruction.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between Oscar and Mombasa, with the fate of Oz hanging in the balance. In the end, Oscar emerges victorious, but not without scars. He realizes that his connection to Oz has changed him, and he must come to terms with his new role as a hero.
