Throughout the movie, Raimi explores themes of power, identity, and redemption. Oscar's journey is one of self-discovery, as he learns to harness his magic and find his place in the world. The film also features stunning visuals, impressive action sequences, and memorable performances from its cast.

Overall, Oz the Great and Powerful is a captivating tale that expands on the classic Wizard of Oz story while maintaining its essence. With its rich characters, engaging plot, and breathtaking visuals, it's a must-see for fans of fantasy adventure films.

documents.title: Silence
documents.tagline: Sometimes silence is the deadliest sound.
documents.overview: Two Jesuit priests travel to seventeenth century Japan which has, under the Tokugawa shogunate, banned Catholicism and almost all foreign contact.
documents.plot:
In 1633, in Japan, Jesuit priest Cristóvão Ferreira is forced to watch as several Catholic priests are tortured to death for refusing to renounce their faith.
In 1640, in Macau, the Jesuit Alessandro Valignano receives news that Ferreira has apostatized. In disbelief, Ferreira's Portuguese pupils, young Jesuit priests Sebastião Rodrigues and Francisco Garupe, set off to find him, guided by Kichijirō, a Japanese fisherman stranded in Macau who, although able to speak Portuguese, vehemently denies being Christian.
Arriving in a Japanese village called Tomogi, Rodrigues and Garupe find local Christians worshipping in secrecy in fear of "the Inquisitor." The villagers tell them that Kichijirō is actually a Christian who renounced his faith to save himself before the rest of his family were put to death by immolation; Rodrigues takes Kichijirō’s confession to grant him absolution.
When government officials arrive in the village to ferret out hidden Christians, they take four hostages, including Kichijirō, and force them to apostatize by stepping on a fumi-e, a carved image of Christ, which they all reluctantly do, and spitting on a cross, which only Kichijirō can force himself to do. The other three hostages are crucified on the shore and left to drown; their bodies are cremated so they cannot be given a Christian burial.
Garupe then leaves for Hirado Island and Rodrigues for Gotō Island, which is Kichijirō’s home. Kichijirō finds and hides Rodrigues, who again takes his confession, but then betrays Rodrigues to the authorities, who imprison him in Nagasaki with a number of Japanese Christians. After several of them refuse to step on a fumi-e, one of them is beheaded. When Kichijirō is imprisoned with them, Rodrigues reluctantly hears his confession again; Kichijirō is then released after he steps on the fumi-e.
Rodrigues is forced by the Inquisitor to watch as four Christians who have renounced their faith before the Inquisitor are drowned. He is shocked to see an emaciated Garupe with them; Garupe has been told he can save the condemned Christians by apostatizing, but he refuses to do so and instead swims out to try to save a drowning woman. The guards hold him underwater and he himself drowns. Rodrigues' faith in God is shaken.
Rodrigues is taken to meet Ferreira, who has assimilated into Japanese society. Ferreira, after being tortured, apostatized to save fellow Christians, and he now believes that Christianity has no place in Japan. He tells Rodrigues that he has been told to convince Rodrigues to abandon his faith. One night, Rodrigues is taken to watch five Christians being tortured. Ferreira tells him that they have already apostatized many times but that their torture will continue until Rodrigues also abandons his faith. Rodrigues hears what he believes is the voice of Jesus, giving him permission to step on the fumi-e, and he does.
Rodrigues works with Ferreira.

documents.title: Argo
documents.tagline: The movie was fake. The mission was real.
documents.overview: As the Iranian revolution reaches a boiling point, a CIA 'exfiltration' specialist concocts a risky plan to free six Americans who have found shelter at the home of the Canadian ambassador.
documents.plot:
Argo is a 2012 American thriller film directed by Ben Affleck, written by Chris Terrio, and produced by Warner Bros. Pictures.

The film is based on the true story of the CIA's rescue of six American diplomats from Iran during the 1979 hostage crisis. The story begins in November 1979, when a group of Iranian students storm the American embassy in Tehran, taking several American diplomats hostage. The situation escalates, and the United States government decides to send a team of CIA operatives to rescue the hostages.

The CIA identifies six Americans who are still in the country: Ambassador Bruce Laingen, his wife, and four other diplomats. However, due to the sensitive nature of their work, they cannot be extracted directly from Iran. Instead, the CIA comes up with a plan to use a Canadian filmmaker named John Chambers to pose as a Canadian film crew.

The CIA creates a fake movie production company called "Canada Films" and sends Chambers to Tehran to pretend to be filming a science fiction movie. The plan is for Chambers to gain the trust of the Iranian authorities, who are eager to cooperate with the Canadians in exchange for concessions on the hostage crisis.

Chambers meets with the Iranian officials and convinces them that he needs access to the American embassy to film a scene. He gains permission to enter the embassy, where he meets with the six American diplomats who are still being held captive. Chambers pretends to be filming a movie, but in reality, he is gathering information about the hostages' location and working with the CIA to come up with a plan for their rescue.

As the situation becomes more dire, Chambers realizes that his cover has been blown, and the Iranians have discovered that he is not who he claims to be. He must use all of his wits and charm to convince the Iranians that he is still a legitimate filmmaker, while also working with the CIA to come up with a plan for the rescue.

The film's climax features a tense and suspenseful sequence in which Chambers and the CIA operatives work together to extract the six American diplomats from Iran. The operation is fraught with danger, but ultimately, it is successful, and the hostages are safely evacuated.

Argo was widely praised by critics and audiences alike, and it won several awards, including three Academy Awards for Best Picture, Best Adapted Screenplay, and Best Film Editing. The film's success can be attributed to its gripping storyline, well-developed characters, and outstanding performances from the cast, particularly Ben Affleck as John Chambers.

Overall, Argo is a thrilling and suspenseful film that tells an incredible true story of bravery and ingenuity in the face of danger.

documents.title: Warcraft
documents.tagline: Two worlds. One home.
documents.overview: The peaceful realm of Azeroth stands on the brink of war as its civilization faces a fearsome race of invaders: orc warriors fleeing their dying home to colonize another. As a portal opens to connect the two worlds, one army faces destruction and the other faces extinction. From opposing sides, two heroes are set on a collision course that will decide the fate of their family, their people, and their home.
documents.plot:
Warcraft (also known as Warcraft: The Beginning) is a 2016 American action fantasy film based on Blizzard Entertainment's video game series, directed by Duncan Jones, who co-wrote it with Charles Leavitt. It stars Travis Fimmel as the human commander Anduin Lothar, Paula Patton as the half-orc Garona, Ben Foster as the guardian Medivh, Dominic Cooper as King Llane Wrynn and Toby Kebbell as the orc chieftain Durotan.

Draenor, the orcs' homeworld, is dying, consumed by fel magic. The warlock Gul'dan unites the orc clans into the Horde and opens a portal to the world of Azeroth by draining the life from captives. He leads an advance warband through, including Durotan of the Frostwolf Clan, his pregnant mate Draka and his friend Orgrim Doomhammer, to capture prisoners whose sacrifice will bring the rest of the Horde. On arrival, Gul'dan revives Durotan's dying newborn son, Go'el, with fel magic. As the orcs raid Azeroth, Lothar and the young mage Khadgar find traces of fel magic and are sent by King Llane to the guardian Medivh. A skirmish with the orcs yields a prisoner, Garona, who agrees to serve Stormwind and leads the humans to spy on Gul'dan's camp.

Despite Orgrim's objections, Durotan secretly meets Llane to propose an alliance, but the meeting is ambushed by the warchief Blackhand, who kills Lothar's son Callan. Khadgar discovers that Medivh, corrupted by fel magic, has been helping Gul'dan open the portal. Blackhand wipes out the Frostwolves; Draka sends Go'el down a river in a basket before she is killed. Durotan challenges Gul'dan to a ritual duel, but Gul'dan kills him by cheating with magic. As the humans attack the orc camp to free the prisoners, Lothar and Khadgar mortally wound Medivh, who uses his last strength to close the portal to Draenor and open one to Stormwind for the freed captives. Trapped, Llane orders Garona to kill him so she can win power among the orcs and someday make peace. Lothar kills Blackhand in a duel and is allowed to leave with the king's body. At Llane's funeral, the human nations, elves and dwarves form an alliance led by Lothar, while the infant Go'el is found by a human.

Warcraft premiered in Paris on May 24, 2016, and was released by Universal Pictures. It grossed $439.1 million worldwide, including $225.5 million in China, but was considered a financial disappointment given its $160 million budget. Critics found it visually impressive but derivative; Rotten Tomatoes reported 29% approval.

documents.title: Seventh Son
documents.tagline: When darkness falls, the son will rise. When the son falls, the dark knight will rise.
documents.overview: John Gregory, who is a seventh son of a seventh son and also the local spook, has protected the country from witches, boggarts, ghouls and all manner of things that go bump in the night. However John is not young anymore, and has been seeking an apprentice to carry on his trade. Most have failed to survive. The last hope is a young farmer's son named Thomas Ward. Will he survive the training to become the spook that so many others couldn't?
documents.plot:
In 1572, the witch Malkin is imprisoned underground by Gregory, the last of the Falcons, a knightly order which defended mankind against supernatural threats. Years later, Gregory works as a "spook" – a roving witch hunter.
Malkin escapes, killing Gregory's apprentice William, and flees to her mountain fortress. She restores the fortress and the beauty of her disfigured, loyal sister, Bony Lizzie. The coming centennial blood moon will make Malkin unstoppable.
Gregory seeks out Tom Ward – the seventh son of a seventh son – as his new apprentice. Tom's Mam gives him her necklace as a talisman, urging him to never take it off. In a town, Tom sees a girl, Alice, about to be burned as a witch. Recognizing her from his clairvoyant visions, Tom frees her. Alice requests that he not tell Gregory about her. She is revealed to be Lizzie's daughter, sent to spy on Gregory. Malkin begins gathering an army of minions.
Tom meets Gregory's assistant, Tusk. With only a week before the blood moon is full, reviving Malkin's full power, Tom must rush through his training while the trio head to Malkin's fortress. En route, Gregory is summoned to a walled city by an inquisitor whose forces have subdued one of Malkin's followers, a werebear named Urag. Tom hesitates when instructed to burn the werebear alive, causing Gregory to dismiss him and light the flame himself. Tom meets Alice again; the two share their feelings for each other and fall in love. They briefly consider running away, but Tom has a vision of Malkin killing Gregory and unleashing destruction upon the world. Tom returns to Gregory, who reveals that he once loved Malkin, leading him to imprison rather than kill her. Gregory feels responsible for every person killed by Malkin, and warns Tom never to show mercy to witches.
The trio are attacked on the road by an enormous boggart. Tom kills it and survives being swept down a waterfall. He is confronted by Bony Lizzie, whose attack is repelled by his Mam's necklace. Gregory recognizes it as the Umbran Stone, which increases the power of witches. It had once belonged to Malkin, until one of her witch followers – Tom's Mam – stole it, weakening Malkin enough for Gregory to trap her.
Malkin instructs Alice to steal the stone, promising to spare Tom's life. Malkin and her minions destroy the city where Urag was killed, to avenge his death. By chance, Tom's family is in the city; his Mam kills the warlock Strix and confronts Malkin with her own powers. Malkin kills her, mocking her for giving away the stone that might have saved her life.
Alice finds Tom and pleads with him to leave with her. Gregory tries to kill her, but Tom intervenes, allowing her to flee. Gregory points out she has taken the necklace, and Tom, Gregory and Tusk pursue her. Malkin's servant Radu attacks them; he captures Gregory and drives Tusk and Tom over a cliff, leaving them for dead.

documents.title: The Iceman
documents.tagline: Loving husband. Devoted father. Ruthless killer.
documents.overview: The true story of Richard Kuklinski, the notorious contract killer and family man.
documents.plot: The true story of Richard Kuklinski, the notorious contract killer and family man.

documents.title: Footloose
documents.tagline: There comes a time to cut loose
documents.overview: Ren MacCormack is transplanted from Boston to the small southern town of Bomont where loud music and dancing are prohibited. Not one to bow to the status quo, Ren challenges the ban, revitalizing the town and falling in love with the minister’s troubled daughter Ariel in the process.
documents.plot:
Footloose is an American musical drama of 2011 and a remake of the 1984 film, directed by Craig Brewer from a script he wrote with Dean Pitchford. Kenny Wormald stars as Ren McCormack, a Boston teenager who challenges a small Southern town's ban on dancing, with Julianne Hough as Ariel Moore, Dennis Quaid as her father, Reverend Shaw Moore, Andie MacDowell as her mother Vi, Miles Teller as Ren's friend Willard and Patrick John Flueger as Chuck.

After a night of partying, the reverend's son Bobby and his friends are killed in a head-on collision with a truck on a bridge outside Bomont, Georgia. In his grief, Shaw persuades the city council to pass a series of strict ordinances, including a ban on unsupervised dancing within the town limits. Three years later, Ren arrives in Bomont to live with his uncle Wes, aunt Lulu and their daughters after his mother's death from leukemia and his father's desertion. He befriends Willard and is drawn to Ariel, the reverend's rebellious daughter, who is secretly seeing the dirt-track racer Chuck. Provoked by Chuck, Ren wins a school bus race despite the bus catching fire. Shaw distrusts Ren and forbids his daughter to see him.

Ren and his classmates want to overturn the ban and hold a prom. As Ariel falls for Ren, her father complains to Wes, who tells him about Ren's mother and suggests that perhaps Ren is the one too good for Ariel. Ariel breaks up with Chuck, who hits her and leaves her with a black eye. At church, Shaw blames Ren and demands his arrest, but Ariel says he cannot blame everything on Ren as he did over Bobby and taunts him about her sex life; he slaps her, shocking Vi, who later tells him he has gone too far and that dancing and music are not the problem. Ren reads Bible passages to the city council showing that people danced even in ancient times, but Shaw has the votes to defeat him.

Ren's boss Andy Beamis offers his cotton mill, just across the line in neighboring Bayson, for the prom. Ren visits Shaw at the church, and the two find common ground in losing someone they loved; Ren insists the dance will happen anyway and politely asks permission to take Ariel, which Shaw grants. On prom night, Ren, Ariel, Willard, Ariel's friend Rusty and Andy run off Chuck's gang, and everyone dances to a country version of "Footloose".

Shot around Atlanta in late 2010 on a $24 million budget, the film was released by Paramount in October 2011 and grossed $63 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed to positive.

documents.title: Battlestar Galactica: Razor
documents.tagline: Fear gets you killed. Anger keeps you alive.
documents.overview: A two-hour Battlestar Galactica special that tells the story of the Battlestar Pegasus several months prior to it finding the Galactica.
documents.plot:
Razor takes place during the first thirty days of Lee Adama's Pegasus command during the period originally covered in the second half of season 2, after the episode "The Captain's Hand" but before "Lay Down Your Burdens", and uses flashbacks to show Rear Admiral Cain's orders during and shortly after the Cylon attack, as well as events occurring on the final day of the first Cylon War. Cain's actions in the wake of the holocaust are connected to the present by Kendra Shaw, self-described as Cain's legacy.
Events of the final day of the first Cylon war follow Lieutenant William Adama, a Viper pilot and Helena Cain, a child. Flashbacks of Adama discovering a lab housing the early Cylon experiments on humans as well as the first Cylon hybrid and Helena Cain abandoning her little sister during a Cylon invasion of Tauron finish as the first Cylon war ends. Each character is left hanging somewhat (Adama is unable to free the surviving prisoners and Cain cannot find her sister). These are shown to be driving forces for their actions as the show continues. Cain goes on to teach Shaw that you have to become a 'razor' to survive during war while referring to her pocket knife, which later becomes Kendra's and then is passed on to Kara Thrace at the end of the film. Admiral Adama teaches his son Lee a different lesson: that they cannot become butchers.
Lee Adama's priority as Pegasus commander is to restore trust and integrity to the troubled command, while preserving some continuity in the leadership that had evolved under Rear Admiral Cain. He picks Kendra Shaw as his executive officer, promoting her to major, despite the stark contrast between Cain's enthusiastic praise and subsequent Pegasus officers' complaints about Kendra's performance. First boarding Pegasus less than an hour before the Cylon attack on the colonies, Shaw follows Rear Admiral Cain's order to make a "blind jump" that saves the ship from destruction at Scorpion Fleet Shipyards.
Like Gaius Baltar on Galactica, Kendra discovers that the Cylons were about to infect the Pegasus with a computer software virus which would have disarmed Pegasus and left it helpless. After Pegasus receives reconnaissance information that all the colonies have been destroyed, Cain delivers a rallying speech inciting the crew to war for the purpose of revenge. The crew responds by chanting "So say we all!" throughout the ship; the Number Six Cylon agent Gina Inviere awkwardly joins in.
Lee Adama's first mission as commander of Pegasus is a mission to retrieve a lost science team. Antiquated Cylon Raiders from the first war appear and attack Pegasus. Simmering bitterness between Kara and Shaw is exacerbated when Shaw endangers Kara and her wingman to defend the battlestar. Both pilots land safely, though Kara has to destroy a Raider that follows her into Pegasus.

documents.title: Dream House
documents.tagline: Once upon a time, there were two little girls who lived in a house.
documents.overview: Publisher Will Atenton quits a lucrative job in New York to relocate his wife, Libby, and their daughters to a quaint town in New England. However, as they settle into their home the Atentons discover that a woman and her children were murdered there, and the surviving husband is the town's prime suspect. With help from a neighbor who was close to the murdered family, Will pieces together a horrifying chain of events.
documents.plot:
Dream House is a 2011 American psychological thriller directed by Jim Sheridan and produced by Morgan Creek Productions, starring Daniel Craig as Will Atenton, Rachel Weisz as his wife Libby, Naomi Watts as their neighbor Ann and Marton Csokas as Ann's estranged husband Jack. The film follows a man who discovers that the house he has moved into with his family was the scene of a terrible crime.

Will Atenton, a successful editor at a New York publishing house, quits his job to write a novel and spend more time with Libby and their two young daughters at their new home in a quiet Connecticut town. The family's happiness soon gives way to unease as a series of unsettling events occurs and their neighbors react to Will with suspicion. He learns that five years earlier a man named Peter Ward murdered his wife and two children in the house and was committed to a psychiatric hospital, from which he was recently released for lack of evidence.

Seeking answers, Will turns to his neighbor Ann, who is reluctant to help, while her estranged husband Jack is openly hostile. When Will visits the psychiatric facility, he discovers the truth: he himself is Peter Ward. Shot in the head during the attack, he has no memory of the killings and has constructed a new identity and the illusion that his family is still alive, living in a house that is in reality abandoned and condemned. Taken in by Ann, who believes in his innocence, Peter sets out to discover what really happened on the night of the murders and who was responsible, leading to a confrontation with the real killers.

The production was troubled: Sheridan reportedly clashed with Morgan Creek over the script and tried to remove his name from the film, and Sheridan, Craig and Weisz were said to dislike the final cut. The trailer was criticized for revealing the main plot twist.

Dream House was released by Universal Pictures on September 30, 2011, without advance screenings for critics. It was a critical and commercial failure, with 7 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 35.

documents.title: The Inbetweeners Movie
documents.tagline: Out of school. Out of their league.
documents.overview: High school graduation just wouldn’t be complete without an un-chaperoned, uninhibited and unforgettable final holiday. At least that’s what Will, Jay, Simon and Neil think when they book a two-week stay on an exotic Greek island. As their dreams of sun-drenched days and booze-filled nights are left hopelessly unfulfilled, the lads fight their way into the party scene with hilariously humiliating results in this smash hit UK raunchy comedy.
documents.plot:
The Inbetweeners Movie, known in North America simply as The Inbetweeners, is a 2011 British coming-of-age comedy based on the E4 sitcom The Inbetweeners. Written by series creators Damon Beesley and Iain Morris and directed by Ben Palmer, it was intended as the conclusion of the television series and stars Simon Bird, Joe Thomas, James Buckley and Blake Harrison, reprising their roles, with Emily Head, Laura Haddock, Tamla Kari and Lydia Rose Bewley. It was released in the United Kingdom and Ireland on 17 August 2011 by Entertainment Film Distributors.

Will McKenzie, Simon Cooper, Jay Cartwright and Neil Sutherland finish their A-levels and leave Rudge Park Comprehensive. Jay's grandfather has died and Simon has been dumped by his long-time crush and girlfriend, Carli. To celebrate the end of school and cheer up their friends, the four boys book a holiday in the party resort of Malia, on the Greek island of Crete. After a coach ride shared with chanting football supporters, they discover that their hotel is a rundown dump and head out into Malia's nightlife.

Tricked into visiting a deserted bar, the boys meet four girls on holiday: Alison, Lucy, Lisa and Jane. Will and Alison connect over their shared sense of humor, Simon frustrates Lucy by talking endlessly about Carli, Neil and Lisa sit in awkward silence, and Jay is annoyed when Jane takes an interest in him. Their first encounter goes badly, but the boys keep running into the girls over the course of the week. The holiday becomes a series of humiliating misadventures, as the friends fail to fit in at the resort's clubs, quarrel among themselves and wrestle with their own insecurities. Simon's obsession with Carli, who is also holidaying in Malia, threatens his chance with Lucy, while Jay must decide whether to stop boasting and admit his real feelings, and Will tries to win over Alison. By the end of the trip, the four friends come to appreciate each other and the girls they have met.

The film was a huge commercial success in the United Kingdom, becoming one of the highest-grossing comedies in British box-office history, and it received generally favorable reviews there, though its later release in the United States was greeted less warmly. It was followed by The Inbetweeners 2 in 2014.

documents.title: Never Back Down 2: The Beatdown
documents.overview: Four fighters from different backgrounds come together to train under an ex MMA rising star and then ultimately have to fight each other and the traitor in their midst.
documents.plot:
Never Back Down 2: The Beatdown, also released as The Fighters 2: The Beatdown in some markets, is a 2011 American martial arts film directed by Michael Jai White from a script by Chris Hauty. A sequel to Never Back Down (2008) and the second film in the series, it marked White's directorial debut. Michael Jai White stars as the mixed martial arts trainer Casey "Case" Walker Jr., alongside Dean Geyer as Mike Stokes, Alex Meraz as Zack Gomes, Todd Duffee as Tim Newhouse, Scott Epstein as Justin Epstein, Evan Peters as the promoter Max Cooperman and Jillian Murray as Eve, with Lyoto Machida and "Big" John McCarthy appearing as themselves.

Max is organizing another round of "The Beatdown", an underground fighting event, and four fighters are training in a vacant lot under the veteran martial artist Case. Zack has recently quit boxing after suffering a partially detached retina; Tim, a skilled MMA fighter, has a family sunk in debt since his father's death; Mike, a champion college wrestler, is struggling with his father having left his mother for another man; and Justin, a comic book store clerk, is a frequent target of bullies. A few weeks in, the trainees quarrel over who deserves to be there most, with Justin and Zack hurting each other. When police officers harass Case and threaten him with a probation violation, the team builds a new gym in which to train and hold the Beatdown. Snapping under constant bullying, Justin turns on his tormentors and then on the group itself, framing his mentor in an effort to send him to jail. The others unite to confront him in the tournament. Mike defeats Zack, while Justin attacks Tim in the restroom and knocks him out of the competition. In a gruelling final, Mike beats Justin by breaking his right shoulder with an omoplata submission hold, and when Justin tries to jump him from behind, he responds with a superman punch. Celebrating his win, Mike finally calls his father and invites him to dinner because they have much to discuss, and Case receives a call from McCarthy confirming his return to MMA.

The film premiered at the ActionFest festival in Asheville, North Carolina, on April 8, 2011, and was released on DVD by Sony Pictures Home Entertainment on September 13. Reviews were mixed, with critics praising the fight scenes, especially White's, while finding the story formulaic.

documents.title: Dragon
documents.tagline: Blood Always Leaves a Trail.
documents.overview: A sinful martial arts expert wants to start a new tranquil life, only to be hunted by a determined detective and his former master.
documents.plot:
Dragon (Chinese title Wu Xia) is a 2011 Hong Kong-Chinese martial arts film from director Peter Chan, starring Donnie Yen, who also served as action director, alongside Takeshi Kaneshiro and Tang Wei, with Jimmy Wang Yu and Kara Hui in support. Conceived as a remake of Chang Cheh's 1967 classic The One-Armed Swordsman, it soon became an original story, though it retains echoes of that film, including the casting of Wang, its original star.

In 1917, Liu Jinxi lives quietly in a village in Yunnan with his wife, Yu, her son Fangzheng and their younger son Xiaotian. When two bandits try to rob a shop while Liu is inside, a scuffle breaks out and both robbers end up dead, apparently through Liu's clumsy luck. The villagers hail him as a hero, but Xu Baijiu, a Sichuanese-speaking detective sent to look into the case, is suspicious, since one of the dead men was a feared fighter. By performing an autopsy he discovers that the robber died of a brain haemorrhage caused by a precise blow to the vagus nerve, and further evidence convinces him that Liu is a master martial artist hiding his skill behind misdirection and a former member of the 72 Demons, a savage gang of killers.

Confronted, Liu admits his past but insists he has changed. Xu nevertheless obtains a warrant for his arrest, and the corrupt magistrate sells Liu's location to the Master of the 72 Demons in hope of a reward. The Master, revealing that Liu is his son, kills the magistrate and sends his men to bring Liu back. Liu kills them and sends the villagers to shelter in a fortress, and Xu uses his knowledge of anatomy to help him fake his death, but the deception fails. To prove he has broken with the gang, Liu cuts off his own left arm. The Master, holding Liu's family hostage, agrees to release him only if Xiaotian takes his place. Liu attacks, but the Master's qigong makes him impervious to blades. Xu slips in beneath the floorboards and drives acupuncture needles into the Master's heel and neck, weakening him; the Master mortally wounds the detective but is then struck dead by lightning, drawn by the needles. Xu declares the case closed with his last breath, and Liu returns to peaceful family life.

The film premiered in the Midnight Screenings section at Cannes in May 2011 and topped the Chinese box office with more than 100 million yuan in its first week. Critics were positive; Variety likened it to A History of Violence set in 1917 China. It won the Hong Kong Film Award for Best Cinematography.

documents.title: Bullet to the Head
documents.tagline: Revenge Never Gets Old.
documents.overview: After watching their respective partners die, a cop and a hitman form an alliance in order to bring down their common enemy.
documents.plot: After watching their respective partners die, a cop and a hitman form an alliance in order to bring down their common enemy.

documents.title: The Hunger Games
documents.tagline: May The Odds Be Ever In Your Favor.
documents.overview: Every year in the ruins of what was once North America, the nation of Panem forces each of its twelve districts to send a teenage boy and girl to compete in the Hunger Games.  Part twisted entertainment, part government intimidation tactic, the Hunger Games are a nationally televised event in which “Tributes” must fight with one another until one survivor remains.  Pitted against highly-trained Tributes who have prepared for these Games their entire lives, Katniss is forced to rely upon her sharp instincts as well as the mentorship of drunken former victor Haymitch Abernathy.  If she’s ever to return home to District 12, Katniss must make impossible choices in the arena that weigh survival against humanity and life against love. The world will be watching.
documents.plot:
The Hunger Games is a dystopian science fiction film directed by Gary Ross, based on the novel of the same name by Suzanne Collins. The movie was released in 2012 and produced by Lionsgate.

In a post-apocalyptic future, the country of Panem is ruled by the tyrannical Capitol. As punishment for a past rebellion, the Capitol forces each of the 12 districts to participate in the Hunger Games, a brutal annual event where 24 tributes, 12 boys and 12 girls, are chosen to fight to the death in a televised event.

The story follows Katniss Everdeen (played by Jennifer Lawrence), a 16-year-old girl from District 12 who volunteers to participate in the Games in place of her younger sister Prim. Katniss is skilled with a bow and arrow and has experience hunting to feed her family after their father's death.

Katniss, along with fellow tribute Peeta Mellark (played by Josh Hutcherson), is transported to the Capitol to prepare for the Games. They are trained, interviewed, and paraded in front of the cameras to gain sympathy and sponsorships from the audience.

Once the Games begin, Katniss and Peeta must use their wits, skills, and alliances to survive against the other tributes. The Gamemakers, who control the arena, introduce various challenges and obstacles to make the game more exciting for the audience.

As the Games progress, Katniss forms alliances with Rue (played by Amandla Stenberg) from District 11 and Thresh (played by Dayo Okeniyi), a strong and skilled tribute from District 11. However, when Rue is killed by Career Tributes, Katniss becomes more determined to survive.

Meanwhile, Peeta's actions in the arena are carefully scripted to gain sympathy from the audience, making it difficult for Katniss to determine his true intentions. As the Games near their end, Katniss and Peeta are the last two survivors, and they threaten to eat poisonous berries rather than kill each other.

In a surprising twist, President Snow (played by Donald Sutherland) intervenes, and Katniss and Peeta declare their love for each other, forcing them to be declared co-winners of the Games. However, this act of defiance against the Capitol is seen as a threat, and Katniss becomes the face of the growing rebellion in District 12.

The movie ends with Katniss and Peeta's victory, but also sets the stage for the rest of the series, as Katniss becomes the Mockingjay, the symbol of the rebellion against the Capitol.

documents.title: A Fairly Odd Movie: Grow Up, Timmy Turner!
documents.original_title: A Fairly Odd Movie: Grow Up, Timmy Turner!
documents.overview: The television movie is set in the city of Dimmsdale and centers on the series' main protagonist Timmy Turner with his fairy godparents Cosmo and Wanda and his fairy godbrother Poof. In the movie, Timmy is now 23 years old but is still in fifth grade with his fairy-obsessed fifth grade teacher Mr. Crocker. Despite being grown up, Timmy finds a loophole in the fairy rulebook Da Rules: if he continues to act like a kid, he will still get to keep his fairies. However, the dilemma rises when Tootie, who was once a dorky girl when she was 10 years old, returns to Dimmsdale as an attractive woman. Timmy falls in love with her, a sign that he is growing up to an adult, which means he is closer to losing his fairies. Meanwhile, an oil business tycoon named Hugh J. Magnate, Jr., who teams up with Mr. Crocker, plans to use Timmy's fairies' magic in order to promote his oil business.
documents.plot:
13 years after the original series, Timmy Turner has grown into a 23-year-old man, but maintains a lifestyle of a 10-year-old to keep his fairy godparents, Cosmo and Wanda, and his godbrother, Poof. Timmy's refusal to mature greatly irritates his parents, who desperately encourage him to move out so that they can sell the family house and travel the world; and Jorgen von Strangle, the chief instructor of the Fairy Godparent Academy, who schemes to entice Timmy into giving up his fairies.
One day, Timmy reunites with Tootie, a childhood acquaintance who had an obsessive crush on him for years. Once a socially awkward child, she has grown into a beautiful activist, causing Timmy to fall for her instantly. After Timmy secretly uses wishes to help Tootie protest against the felling of a historic tree by oil tycoon Hugh J. Magnate, Jr., Cosmo and Wanda desperately try to repel Tootie, afraid that Timmy is outgrowing them. Timmy is torn between his love for Tootie and his desire to keep his fairies, which culminates in his hesitating to kiss Tootie. Annoyed, Tootie leaves him, telling him to be more mature.
Meanwhile, Timmy's fairy-obsessed schoolteacher Denzel Crocker teams up with Magnate to kidnap Timmy's fairies and use their magic for their own gain. Magnate deceives and kidnaps Tootie while Crocker captures Cosmo, Wanda and Poof, imprisoning them in a device programmed to use their magic to grant anybody's wishes. However, Magnate betrays Crocker, wishes he falls into a bottomless ballpit, and tortures the fairies by adjusting the wish-granting machine to electrocute them each time a wish is made. Timmy tracks down Magnate at his headquarters, which resembles a children's entertainment center, to rescue his fairies and Tootie. He battles both Magnate, who apparently had a troubled relationship with his father and suffers from his own maturity issues, and a toy robot brought to life with the fairies' magic. Timmy saves his fairies from being destroyed by Magnate as he tells Tootie he loves her and kisses her, but in doing so, he loses ownership of his fairies, who disappear out of containment. Magnate childishly laments losing his source of magic before his secretary Janice inadvertently incapacitates him.
Although Timmy is saddened by Cosmo, Wanda, and Poof's departure, he is happy to be free to finally pursue more mature endeavors, as he had longed to do. Jorgen returns to inform Timmy that, because of his courage, a new law was passed in Fairy World that will now permit him to keep his fairy godparents as long as he only makes unselfish wishes to help others. Tootie, Timmy, and his fairies form a charity organization to grant wishes that will mend all of the world's problems or travesties, flying away in a magical van, which turns around in midair and flies towards the camera.

documents.title: The Raven
documents.tagline: The only one who can stop a serial killer is the man who inspired him.
documents.overview: A fictionalized account of the last days of Edgar Allan Poe's life, in which the poet is in pursuit of a serial killer whose murders mirror those in the writer's stories.
documents.plot:
In 19th-century Baltimore, Maryland, several policemen discover a murdered woman sprawled on the floor of her apartment, which was locked from the inside. While police search for the killer's means of escape, they discover a second corpse in the chimney, later identified as the 12-year-old daughter of the first victim. A celebrated detective, Emmett Fields, is called to assist in the investigation and discovers that the crime resembles a fictional murder in a short story, "The Murders in the Rue Morgue", that he once read.
The writer Edgar Allan Poe is brought to Fields for questioning. After finding the body of Griswold, a rival of Poe, cut in half by a pendulum (as in Poe's story "The Pit and the Pendulum"), the pair deduce that someone is staging murders based on Poe's stories. Edgar's love, Emily Hamilton, is kidnapped at her father's masquerade ball, like the one described in Poe's "The Masque of the Red Death". The killer taunts Poe in a note, demanding that Edgar write and publish a new story. Poe's lodgings are burned down by people who believe he is exploiting the murders for his own journalistic ends, and he is forced to move in with Fields.
A clue from the killer referring to "The Cask of Amontillado" leads Poe and Fields to search the tunnels under the city with several policemen, discovering the walled-up corpse of a man dressed as Emily. They determine that the man is a sailor, and the clues on his body bring the pursuers to Holy Cross Church, where an empty grave with Emily's name on it has been prepared. As the police attempt to break down the church doors, the killer attacks and kills one of the policemen, then shoots and wounds Fields. Poe gives chase on horseback, but the killer escapes.
Poe writes one last newspaper column, offering his life for Emily's, suggesting that he could take poison. In the morning, the maid gives Poe a letter from the killer, accepting his terms, but the note was delivered long before the paper was distributed. Realizing that the killer must work at the paper, Poe races to confront his editor, Henry, but Henry is already dead, another note lying next to him that reads "getting warmer".
The real killer is the paper's typesetter, Ivan Reynolds, who congratulates Poe and offers him a drink. Ivan attempts to converse with Edgar, but Poe demands Emily's location. Ivan pours a vial of poison, promising to end the story as Poe had written it. Poe agrees and drinks the liquid. Ivan quotes "The Tell-Tale Heart", cluing Edgar that Emily is concealed beneath the printing floor. As the killer leaves, Poe uses the last of his strength to tear up a false section of floor and open a trapdoor leading to Emily's prison.
Poe rescues Emily, and they share a poignant moment before she is taken away by ambulance. Delirious from the poison, Edgar wanders off to a park bench to die. A man walking in the park recognizes him as the famous writer, and asks if he is all right.

documents.title: Trespass
documents.tagline: When terror is at your doorstep. You can run. Or you can fight.
documents.overview: Kyle and Sarah Miller have it all: a huge gated house on the water, fancy cars, and the potential for romance in their relationship. He's just back from a business trip and their teen daughter Avery is sneaking out to a party, when four thugs in security uniforms and ski masks stage a home invasion. They want what's in the safe: cash and diamonds. As Kyle stalls them, trying to negotiate for Sarah's freedom, the fault lines in Kyle and Sarah's marriage and the pasts of the four robbers come into play. Is there room here for heroism?
documents.plot:
Trespass is a 2011 American crime thriller film directed by Joel Schumacher, his final film, and written by Karl Gajdusek. Nicolas Cage and Nicole Kidman star as Kyle and Sarah Miller, a wealthy couple taken hostage in their home, with Ben Mendelsohn, Cam Gigandet, Liana Liberato, Jordana Spiro, Dash Mihok, Emily Meade and Nico Tortorella. It premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2011 and was released by Millennium Entertainment in a limited theatrical release and on video on demand in October 2011.

The Millers live in a luxurious, high-security mansion in Shreveport, Louisiana, where Kyle works as a diamond dealer. Their teenage daughter, Avery, sneaks out to a party against her parents' wishes but returns home upset after being harassed by the host. Meanwhile, a gang of robbers posing as police officers forces its way into the house: their leader, Elias, his girlfriend, Petal, his younger brother, Jonah, and an enforcer named Ty. They demand that Kyle open his safe, and when Avery returns, she too is taken captive.

The intruders soon discover that the family's wealth is an illusion: Kyle is effectively bankrupt, having bought everything on credit, and makes only a modest income appraising diamonds for former clients to keep up with the mortgage. Even Sarah's diamond necklace turns out to be a fake. As tempers rise, Elias breaks Kyle's hand, and an escape attempt by Kyle and Avery ends with Kyle shot in the leg. It emerges that Elias is a drug dealer working for a criminal syndicate who was robbed of $180,000 worth of drugs and committed the robbery under threat of retribution, and that Jonah, who once worked on the Millers' security system, had become obsessed with Sarah. As secrets about the family and the criminals are revealed, including suspicions that Sarah had an affair, the captors turn on one another, and the Millers must outwit them to survive the night.

Trespass was panned by critics, who found it overwrought, implausible and repetitive, filled with constant shouting and twists, and it was considered a waste of its talented stars. It was a box-office failure, earning only a small fraction of its reported $35 million budget, having been released in very few theaters at the same time as its on-demand debut.

documents.title: Hellraiser: Revelations
documents.tagline: The Return of Pinhead.
documents.overview: Two friends in Mexico discover the Lament Configuration and unleash Pinhead, but one decides to try to survive by swapping himself with someone else. Once they go missing, family members go in search of them, but find Pinhead instead.
documents.plot:
Hellraiser: Revelations is a 2011 American horror film written by Gary J. Tunnicliffe and directed by Víctor Garcia, the ninth installment in the Hellraiser series based on the work of Clive Barker. It stars Steven Brand, Nick Eversman and Tracey Fairaway, with Stephan Smith Collins as Pinhead, the leader of the sadomasochistic otherworldly beings known as the Cenobites.

Best friends Nico Bradley and Steven Craven run away from home and travel to Mexico, where they film themselves partying for days before vanishing without a trace. The Mexican authorities later return their belongings to their families, including a videotape recorded by Steven and an ornate puzzle box. A year later, the two families gather for an uneasy dinner. Steven's sister Emma, who was also Nico's girlfriend, is frustrated by the lack of answers and demands to know what is on the tape that her mother Sarah has been watching in secret.

When Emma views the footage, the story of the boys' final days begins to emerge in flashbacks. In Mexico, Nico killed a young woman they had picked up in a bar and used the crime to force Steven to keep traveling with him. Nico was then given the puzzle box by a vagrant who promised him unimaginable pleasures. At the house, Emma finds the box and tries to work it, and Steven suddenly reappears, bloodied and terrified. The families find themselves unable to leave as Steven warns that the Cenobites are coming, and the secrets and desires of everyone in the house come to the surface as the demons arrive to claim what they are owed.

The film was produced in a matter of weeks because Dimension Films needed to release a new Hellraiser film to retain the rights to the franchise. Because of the rushed schedule, longtime star Doug Bradley declined to take part, making it the first entry in which he did not play Pinhead.

Revelations received a single theatrical screening in March 2011, ostensibly open to the public, before being released on DVD on October 18, 2011. Reviews were overwhelmingly negative: none of the critics counted by Rotten Tomatoes gave it a positive review, and Dread Central wrote that it made all the earlier sequels look great by comparison.

documents.title: Setup
documents.overview: A group of friends plan out a detailed heist that turns deadly when one betrays the other by taking off with the goods. Taking matters into his own hands, Sonny seeks out his revenge teaming up with the most dangerous mob boss in town to get back what is rightfully his. When he finally comes face to face with his longtime friend he will be forced to make a life changing choice.
documents.plot:
Setup is a 2011 direct-to-video action thriller heist film directed by Mike Gunther, who wrote it with Mike Behrman. Curtis "50 Cent" Jackson stars as Sonny, with Bruce Willis as the mob boss Biggs and Ryan Phillippe as Vincent, and the cast also includes Jenna Dewan as Mia, Randy Couture as Petey, James Remar as William and Brett Granstaff as Dave. It was shot in Grand Rapids, Michigan, in late 2010.

In Detroit, three friends, Sonny, Dave and Vincent, carefully plan a heist of $5 million in diamonds, but Vincent betrays the others and shoots them both. Dave dies, while Sonny survives and seeks revenge by allying himself with Biggs, the most dangerous mob boss in town, in order to recover the money from the heist. Biggs sends Sonny with his henchman Petey to dig up $2 million buried in a cemetery, but Petey accidentally shoots himself. Sonny follows a woman named Mia to the home of the fence who handled the stolen goods and threatens him, and the frightened fence warns Vincent that he must deal with the loose end he left behind, only to be killed by Vincent. While Biggs's men brutally interrogate others to learn what happened to Petey, Vincent seeks help to eliminate Sonny, and Sonny visits Dave's grave and then Vincent's imprisoned father, asking whether there is anything he would like said to his son before Sonny kills him. Mia is murdered by the owner of the diamonds, who wants them back. In prison, an inmate named Saunders extorts $100,000 from Vincent to keep his father safe. Sonny hides part of Biggs's $2 million in a teddy bear packed in a box, then falsely tells Biggs that Vincent has his money, and a meeting between Biggs and Vincent ends in a deadly shootout. Vincent escapes, kills the owner of the diamonds when he breaks into his home, and is finally ambushed by Sonny at his car. Doused in oil and forced to dig his own grave, Vincent confesses that he betrayed his friends because Saunders had threatened his father and he needed the money. Sonny spares him, but Vincent's father is then killed in prison. Dave's girlfriend receives the teddy bear with the money, and Sonny drives away reflecting that while he could live with Vincent remaining alive, the question was whether Vincent could.

Lionsgate's Grindstone Entertainment Group released Setup on DVD and Blu-ray in the United States on September 20, 2011. In a handful of international markets it grossed about $2.1 million.

documents.title: Spooky Buddies
documents.overview: Disney's irresistible talking puppies are back in an all-new movie that takes them far across town to a mysterious mansion where something very spooky is going on.
documents.plot:
Spooky Buddies is a 2011 family comedy film that revolves around a group of canine friends who get caught up in a mystery surrounding a haunted mansion. The movie explores several key themes, primarily centered around friendship and loyalty.

At its core, Spooky Buddies celebrates the unbreakable bonds between dogs and their human companions. The film showcases how these relationships can transcend even the most extraordinary circumstances, as the canine characters work together to help their owners overcome challenges and fears. This theme is beautifully illustrated through the interactions between the dog characters, who demonstrate remarkable empathy, loyalty, and teamwork.

The movie also touches on the idea of facing one's fears and overcoming phobias. The human characters in the film are often held back by their own anxieties and doubts, but with the help of their canine companions, they learn to confront and overcome these obstacles. This theme is skillfully woven throughout the narrative, as the dogs encourage their owners to be brave and take risks.

Furthermore, Spooky Buddies highlights the importance of trust and communication in relationships. The dog characters are able to sense their owners' emotions and respond accordingly, demonstrating a deep understanding of human psychology. This theme is beautifully illustrated through the interactions between the dog characters and their owners, showcasing how open communication and empathy can lead to stronger, more meaningful relationships.

Overall, Spooky Buddies is a heartwarming film that celebrates the power of friendship, loyalty, and trust in overcoming even the most daunting challenges.

documents.title: Kon-Tiki
documents.overview: The true story about legendary explorer Thor Heyerdahl and his epic crossing of the Pacific on a balsa wood raft in 1947, in an effort to prove it was possible for South Americans to settle in Polynesia in pre-Columbian times.
documents.plot:
Kon-Tiki is an adventure drama film that tells the story of Thor Heyerdahl's historic 1947 expedition to sail a raft from South America to Polynesia. The movie explores several themes, primarily centered around human resilience, determination, and the power of nature.

At its core, Kon-Tiki is a testament to the human spirit's ability to overcome seemingly insurmountable challenges. The film follows Thor Heyerdahl, played by Pål Sverre Hagen, as he embarks on an incredible journey with his crew, facing treacherous seas, scorching sun, and personal conflicts along the way.

One of the primary themes is the relationship between humans and nature. As the crew navigates the vast Pacific Ocean, they are forced to confront their own vulnerabilities in the face of the unforgiving environment. The film highlights the delicate balance between human ingenuity and the natural world, showcasing both the beauty and brutality of the ocean.

The movie also delves into themes of exploration, discovery, and cultural exchange. Heyerdahl's expedition was not just a scientific endeavor but also a journey of self-discovery and cultural curiosity. As he encounters various island cultures, he is struck by their similarities to his own Norwegian heritage, sparking questions about identity, belonging, and the shared human experience.

Furthermore, Kon-Tiki touches on the idea of perseverance and the importance of teamwork. The crew faces numerous setbacks and disagreements, but ultimately, they come together to overcome their differences and achieve a common goal. This camaraderie is forged in the face of adversity, demonstrating that even in the most challenging situations, human connection can be a powerful force for survival.

Overall, Kon-Tiki is a film about the human condition, exploring our capacity for resilience, adaptability, and connection with the world around us.

documents.title: Headhunters
documents.tagline: The hunt is on.
documents.overview: An accomplished headhunter risks everything to obtain a valuable painting owned by a former mercenary.
documents.plot:
Roger Brown, Norway's most successful headhunter, supports his lavish lifestyle by stealing paintings with his partner, Ove. Roger has a mistress named Lotte, but eventually breaks up with her.
Roger's wife and art gallery owner, Diana, introduces him to Clas Greve, a former executive for GPS tech company HOTE. Roger, in the process of recruiting the CEO of HOTE's rival Pathfinder, considers Clas a suitable candidate.
Clas owns a lost Rubens painting believed to be worth millions. He is also a former member of TRACK, a special forces unit specialized in tracking people, and helped HOTE develop a nanotechnology GPS tracking gel. Roger swaps the Rubens painting with the counterfeit, but discovers Diana's cell phone beside Clas' bed, implying an affair. In retaliation, after a seemingly successful interview with Pathfinder executives, Roger informs Clas that the company is looking for someone else.
The next morning, Roger finds Ove in his car, apparently dead from a poison syringe. Just as Roger tries to dumps the body in a lake, Ove recovers, having not got a full dose of the poison. Roger drives Ove to his cabin and ignores his demands for medical attention, not wanting the police involved. Ove pulls out a gun, causing a shoot-out in which Roger accidentally kills him. Clas has followed him to Ove's cabin, but Roger escapes after a scuffle.
Surmising Clas may have installed a tracker on him, Roger steals Ove's car and spare uniform, then flees to an old farm. Clas arrives at the farm with his dog and murders the farmer. Roger evades them and kills Clas' dog when it attacks him. Driving away in a tractor, Roger sees a pursuing vehicle. In a panic, he falls from the tractor, only to find that his pursuer is a stranger wanting to help.
Waking in a hospital, Roger learns that the police is mistaking him for Ove, and arrest him for the farmer's murder. Driving to the station, the officers pull over to block a truck reported stolen. Clas is driving the truck, and Diana may have helped him by rubbing the GPS gel into Roger's hair. Clas rams the car off a cliff. Playing dead until Clas leaves, Roger shaves his head and hides his hair on an officer's corpse, then swaps clothes with a detective's disfigured body to fake his death.
Roger asks Lotte for help, but she is working for Clas. Clas, who is still secretly employed by HOTE, was planning to use Roger to get the Pathfinder job and steal their technologies. Lotte put the gel in Roger's hair and was to introduce him to Clas. However, Roger ended the affair before that could happen, so Clas used the Rubens painting to meet him through Diana. Lotte attacks him with a knife, causing Roger to fatally shoot her in self-defense. Roger returns home and admits everything to Diana, who apologizes for her affair with Clas. The next morning, Roger enters a morgue to retrieve the remaining evidence linking him to the murders (his cut hair), while Diana contacts Clas to ostensibly resume their affair.

documents.title: Very Good Girls
documents.tagline: When we lose our innocence, we have to find ourselves.
documents.overview: Two New York City girls make a pact to lose their virginity during their first summer out of high school. When they both fall for the same street artist, the friends find their connection tested for the first time.
documents.plot:
Best friends Lilly and Gerri spend their last summer in New York together. At Brighton Beach, they muse about swimming nude before Gerri suddenly takes off her shirt and runs into the water, followed by Lilly. On their way back home, they meet David, a guy selling ice cream. After an awkward conversation, David takes a picture of Lilly from the back.
Arriving home, Lilly sees her father with a woman in the office. She takes comfort in spending the evening with Gerri's family, who are loud and open in contrast to Lilly's stony mother and absent father. The girls talk and vow to lose their virginity before leaving for college.
As Lilly walks to work as a boat tour guide in Manhattan, David watches from a distance. He shows interest in her which she doesn't tell Gerri about, while Gerri exhibits an affection for him despite the lack of reciprocation, and despite neither girl knowing him well. David asks Lilly out, and she agrees.
Lilly's mother learns about her father's affair and asks him to leave, against Lilly's wishes. She begins to hang out with David and they kiss. Gerri invites David to an open mic night where she sings a song she wrote for him, while out of her sight, David takes Lilly's hand and holds it under the table.
Lilly's boss flirts with her, offering lucrative night shifts with an obvious implication. Walking home, she sees David waiting outside her house; they kiss and have sex in the garage. The next morning Lilly bumps into her father who apologizes, asking her to have dinner with him, which she declines. Afterward, David sneaks in through the bathroom window. They shower together before spending the day flocking around the city. They arrive at a basketball court where a stylishly dressed man strips to his underwear and dances ballet liberatingly. Kids join him while David videos.
Later in the evening, Lilly learns that Gerri's father died after collapsing in the subway. She leaves David to be with a despairing Gerri. Sharing her grief encourages Lilly to ask her mother to forgive her father. Gerri tells Lilly she can't stop thinking about David. Guiltily, Lilly rejects David's attempts to meet again. He confronts her and she rebuffs him, asking him to meet up with Gerri, but is dismayed when David complies. He comforts Gerri and they kiss in her backyard garden, which Lilly sees.
At her father's memorial service, Gerri tells Lilly she lost her virginity to David, prompting her to see her boss and agree to his advances. They kiss in the tour boat, but then she changes her mind. However, when she confronts David about having sex with Gerri and he does not respond, she lies and tells him she had sex with her boss. The next day, Lilly surprisingly finds her parents cooking in the kitchen as her mother has forgiven her father. David shows up, claiming he didn't sleep with Gerri, and Lilly storms off.
Gerri tells Lilly that David is leaving for Paris, so Lilly finds him, admitting she didn't sleep with her boss.

documents.title: Brownian Movement
documents.overview: A psychiatrist's adulterous past continues to haunt her and her husband after they move to India.
documents.plot:
Brownian Movement is a 2010 Dutch drama written and directed by Nanouk Leopold, a Dutch–German–Belgian co-production made by Serendipity Films, Circe Films and Coin Film with Bella Cohen Films and the broadcaster VPRO. It stars Sandra Hüller as Charlotte, a German doctor working in Brussels, and Dragan Bakema as her husband Max. The title alludes to Brownian motion, the seemingly random movement of particles suspended in a gas or liquid, though the film itself never explains it.

Charlotte appears to have a perfect life with Max, an attentive and handsome architect, and their young son Benjamin, to whom she reads the Brothers Grimm tale "The Girl Without Hands" at bedtime. Her marriage is affectionate and the couple's intimacy is warm and trusting. Yet she secretly rents a bare apartment where she meets men she picks from among her patients, most of them physically unprepossessing, for impulsive sexual encounters. When she unexpectedly runs into one of these men again and he tries to get close to her, she breaks down, attacks him and collapses.

Her affairs come to light, she is struck off the medical register and her marriage nearly falls apart. In couples therapy and a psychiatric assessment she struggles, or declines, to explain her behaviour, admitting she does not really know what she is supposed to feel. In the film's third section, two years later, the family has moved to India, where Max works as an architect; twins have been born and their happiness seems restored, but Max cannot shake his mistrust and begins following Charlotte on her solitary morning walks, which take her to a building under construction.

The cast also includes Sabine Timoteo, Ryan Brodie as Benjamin and Nicole Shirer. The film was shot by Frank van den Eeden and edited by Leopold's long-time collaborator Katharina Wartena, with music by Harry de Wit. It premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2010 and screened in the Forum section of the 2011 Berlin International Film Festival. Critics praised Hüller's subtle, empathetic performance and the luminous cinematography, but many found the film's long takes, sparse dialogue and elliptical storytelling slow and opaque; The Hollywood Reporter called it an inert endurance test, while Screen Daily detected powerful emotions beneath its cold surface.

documents.title: Superior Firepower: Making 'Aliens'
documents.overview: This feature-length documentary, made especially for the 2003 Aliens (1986) DVD release, is incredibly informative with all its interviews with both the cast and crew, as well as behind the scenes footage filmed during the making of the film. Every possible element towards what went into making the movie is included here and gives fans an overload of information to fill their brains with.
documents.plot:
Superior Firepower: Making 'Aliens' is a 2003 American documentary film directed and produced by Charles de Lauzirika about the production of James Cameron's 1986 science fiction film Aliens. Made by the Lauzirika Motion Picture Company for 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment, it was created for the Alien Quadrilogy DVD box set released in December 2003, following his documentary on the first film, The Beast Within: Making 'Alien', and preceding Wreckage and Rage: Making 'Alien 3'. It runs 185 minutes and has no narrator, telling its story instead through new interviews, archival interview clips and behind-the-scenes footage. Participants include producers Gale Anne Hurd and David Giler, Sigourney Weaver, Carrie Henn, Michael Biehn, Lance Henriksen, Bill Paxton, Jenette Goldstein and Mark Rolston, concept artists Syd Mead and Ron Cobb, production designer Peter Lamont, casting director Mary Selway, creature effects creator Stan Winston, effects supervisor John Richardson and composer James Horner, with Cameron appearing in archival interviews.

The documentary is divided into eleven chapters. It begins with the stalled early attempts at a sequel, Cameron's recruitment and the pay dispute that briefly threatened Weaver's return as Ripley, then moves to the design of the colony, the spaceships and the armored personnel carrier, and to the casting of the Colonial Marines and their military-style training. A chapter on the shoot at Pinewood Studios in 1985 details tensions between the American director and the British crew, including the replacement of the original cinematographer, and the late casting of Biehn. Further chapters examine the Marines' weapons and the action sequences, the redesigned facehuggers and warrior aliens, the bond between Weaver and the nine-year-old Henn, and the construction of the full-size Alien Queen puppet and the Power Loader for their climactic duel. The last chapters cover Horner's struggle to compose the score in very little time, which soured his relationship with Cameron for years, the miniature visual effects, and the film's reception, including Weaver's Academy Award nomination for Best Actress.

The documentary was later included in the Aliens collector's edition DVD and, in a reformatted widescreen version, in the Alien Anthology Blu-ray set, which added deleted segments known as enhancement pods.

documents.title: I Don't Know How She Does It
documents.original_title: I Don't Know How She Does It
documents.tagline: If it were easy, men would do it too.
documents.overview: A comedy centered on the life of Kate Reddy, a finance executive who is the breadwinner for her husband and two kids.
documents.plot:
When Kate Reddy receives a reminder from her daughter Emily about her kindergarten's bake sale, she buys a store-baked pie and puts it in a glass pie plate. Back home, Kate is greeted by her husband, Richard. They attempt to have sex, but she falls asleep due to exhaustion.
In the middle of the night, Kate goes to check on her children. The next morning, she is greeted with a hug by her two-year-old son, Ben. Kate pleads for Richard to stay home as the babysitter Paula is not yet there to take over.
Kate meets her friend, Allison, a single mother working as a lawyer. They later encounter "the Momsters" – Wendy Best and Janine LoPietro, who are both stay-at-home mothers. Kate's boss Clark Cooper assigns her a new project with Jack Abelhammer. In the morning as she leaves her house with her children calling out to her, she cries from guilt towards her children.
Later, Kate arrives in NYC and meets Jack with Momo, her junior research analyst. Momo is opposed to Kate's lifestyle and is highly career-driven. Kate apologizes to Jack before realizing that she has lice. She scratches her head profusely but manages to get through the meeting. Richard's mother Marla displays dismay with how much both Kate and Richard are working and hopes that Kate will spend more time with the children.
Kate travels between Boston and NYC, juggling her personal life and the major project with Jack. She is impressed by Jack's character. He begins to show admiration for Kate. Jack reveals that he was married once to someone he loved who became sick and passed away. He sends Kate home by getting her a cab.
Kate becomes more conscious of her contact with Jack. After a meeting in Boston, Momo reveals that she is pregnant. That night, Kate and Richard fight over the new babysitter.
After a meeting in Cleveland, Kate and Jack go to dinner. Afterwards, he takes her bowling. Kate reassures Allison that there is nothing romantic between them. She later informs Momo that she will be taking five days off from work to spend time with her family in Atlanta for Thanksgiving.
Momo reveals to Kate that she is planning to keep the baby. Later, Bunce teases Kate for taking time off from work. While in Atlanta, she silences her phone to be fully present during the week. All is going well as Kate prepares Thanksgiving dinner for the family. She is called back to work, but before she leaves, Ben finally speaks his first words, "Bye Bye, Mama".
Before the pitch, Momo experiences morning sickness. Despite her initial worries, Kate is reassured by Jack that the pitch went well. He informs her that he will be having lunch with the investor. The lunch goes well, but Jack later realizes he had many missed calls from Kate. The missed calls are from Richard, who could not get in touch with her.
The calls were to inform Kate that Ben has fallen down the stairs and hit his head. She rushes back to join them in the hospital, after which Kate and Richard have a fight.

documents.title: The Hunter
documents.tagline: Some mysteries should never be solved.
documents.overview: Martin, a mercenary, is sent from Europe by an anonymous biotech company to the Tasmanian wilderness on a hunt for the last Tasmanian tiger.
documents.plot:
Mercenary Martin David is hired by military biotech company, Red Leaf, to go to Tasmania and gather samples of a supposedly extinct marsupial, the thylacine (Tasmanian tiger), with further instructions to kill all remaining tigers to ensure no competing organisation will get their DNA.
Posing as a university biologist, Martin lodges in the home of the Armstrong family: Lucy and her two young children, Katie and Jamie. Lucy is perpetually benumbed from prescribed medication, taken after the disappearance of her environmentalist husband, Jarrah Armstrong. Speculation surrounds Jarrah's disappearance, particularly with regard to a longstanding conflict between the local loggers who are in desperate need of jobs, and the 'greenies', a group of environmentalists who have set up road blocks to the forest to prevent its deforestation. Martin goes into the bush for twelve days at a time, setting up various steel traps and makeshift snares, while waiting patiently to see if a tiger will surface. On each excursion, Martin leaves the family a map with his coordinates, to be used to search for him if he fails to return on schedule. During his short stays at the Armstrongs' to resupply, Martin slowly befriends the children, and discovers that Lucy's medication is delivered to her by Jack Mindy, who has been unofficially looking in on the family. Martin confiscates Lucy's medication, and bathes her while she is unconscious, after realising the detrimental effects of her dependency.
During one return from the bush, Martin finds Lucy has recovered from the symptoms of her addiction. Jamie provides Martin with a clue as to the tiger's whereabouts: a drawing of the tiger near trees and small bodies of water. From the drawing, Martin is able to deduce the tiger's location on his map. On his next trip out, Martin stumbles across Jarrah's skeletal remains and discovers that he had been shot through the head. Martin gives him a proper burial, but does not reveal his findings to the Armstrong family. On his return to the Armstrong house, Lucy informs him that Red Leaf had initially contracted Jarrah to locate the tiger, a pursuit he eventually abandoned in favour of taking up an environmental cause to protect wildlife and that Red Leaf wanted Jarrah to find the tiger because they believed that it had a paralysing venom in its bite.
While hiking to check his traps, Martin is ambushed by a rival Red Leaf operative sent to replace him. The man binds Martin's hands and instructs Martin to lead him to the tiger's cave, but Martin instead leads the operative past one of his steel traps. The operative steps on the trap, and its metal teeth bind his leg. The operative drops both rifles. Martin frees his hands, picks up one of the rifles, and kills the operative just as the operative frees himself from the trap and lunges for the other rifle. Searching the man's pockets, Martin finds the map he left with the Armstrong's, and realises the operative has been to their house.

documents.title: Prometheus
documents.tagline: The Search for Our Beginning Could Lead to Our End.
documents.overview: A team of explorers discover a clue to the origins of mankind on Earth, leading them on a journey to the darkest corners of the universe. There, they must fight a terrifying battle to save the future of the human race.
documents.plot:
As a spacecraft departs a planet, a tall humanoid alien drinks a black liquid, causing its body to dissolve. Its remains crumble into a waterfall, while its DNA breaks apart and recombines.
In 2089, archaeologists Elizabeth Shaw and Charlie Holloway discover a star map in Scotland that matches others found among unrelated ancient cultures. They interpret it as an invitation from humanity's forerunners, the "Engineers". Peter Weyland, the elderly CEO of Weyland Corporation, funds an expedition aboard the scientific vessel Prometheus to the distant moon LV-223. The crew travel in suspended animation, while the android David monitors the voyage.
The Prometheus lands on the barren, mountainous surface near a large artificial structure. Exploring it, the crew find stone cylinders, a monolithic statue of a humanoid head, and the decapitated corpse of a large alien. Shaw identifies the body as an Engineer and retrieves its head. Other corpses suggest the species is extinct. Crew members Millburn and Fifield become uneasy and try to return to the Prometheus, but become lost inside the structure. A storm forces the expedition to retreat. David secretly takes a cylinder, most of which ooze black liquid. The Engineer's DNA matches that of humans.
David investigates the liquid, deliberately contaminates a drink with a small sample, and offers it to Holloway, who drinks it after saying he would do anything for answers. Shortly afterwards, Shaw and Holloway have sex. Inside the structure, a snake-like creature kills Millburn and sprays corrosive fluid that melts Fifield's helmet, causing him to fall face first into a puddle. David discovers a control room containing an Engineer in stasis and a holographic star map highlighting Earth. Holloway rapidly becomes ill. He is taken back to the Prometheus, but mission director Meredith Vickers refuses him entry and, at his urging, burns him to death with a flamethrower. A medical scan then reveals that Shaw, previously infertile, is pregnant. She uses an automated surgery table to remove a squid-like creature from her abdomen. Shaw subsequently learns that Weyland, Vickers' father, has been in stasis aboard the ship. He intends to ask the Engineers how to overcome old age.
A mutated Fifield returns to the Prometheus and kills several crewmen before Captain Janek kills him. Janek theorises that the structure was an Engineer military base where a biological weapon escaped control. The base also contains a spacecraft. Weyland, David and the team return to the structure with Shaw. David awakens the surviving Engineer and speaks to him in Proto-Indo-European, explaining Weyland's request. The Engineer responds by decapitating David and killing Weyland and his companions, then reactivating the spacecraft. Shaw escapes and warns Janek that the Engineer intends to release the biological weapon on Earth and exterminate humanity.

documents.title: Arena
documents.tagline: There's no greater battle... Than the battle for your life.
documents.overview: David Lord finds himself forced into the savage world of a modern gladiatorial arena, where men fight to the death for the entertainment of the online masses.
documents.plot:
Arena is a 2011 American action film directed by Jonah Loop and released direct-to-video. Kellan Lutz stars as David Lord, a firefighter and paramedic forced to fight for his life, with Samuel L. Jackson as Logan, the organizer of a deadly underground tournament, Katia Winter, Johnny Messner, James Remar, Nina Dobrev and Derek Mears. It was released on home video in October 2011.

The Deathgames is an illegal internet broadcast in which kidnapped combatants fight to the death in a modern gladiatorial arena for a paying online audience. David Lord loses his pregnant girlfriend, Lori, in a car accident. Grief-stricken, he drinks at a bar, where a mysterious woman, Milla, watches him easily subdue a bouncer. She seduces him, then drugs him so that he can be abducted. Milla is a recruiter for the Deathgames, run by the smooth and confident Logan.

David wakes up as a prisoner in a hidden facility and is forced to fight. Logan promises him his freedom if he wins ten bouts in a row, and David agrees on one condition: that his tenth and final opponent must be Kaden, Logan's top fighter and enforcer. David wins fight after fight, becoming a hit with the online audience. For the penultimate match, Kaden arranges the release of a South African serial killer, Brutus Jackson, but David defeats him, which convinces Logan that Kaden fears him. Distressed by the risk to his business, Logan has a doctor inject David with a drug that will slow him down and make him easy prey for Kaden. As the final fight begins, flashbacks reveal that David's story is not what it seems: "David Lord" is the cover identity of an undercover government agent sent to infiltrate the Deathgames and bring down the organization, and the outcome of the battle will determine whether his mission succeeds.

Arena received mostly negative reviews, with critics focusing on its clichéd script and shallow plot, although Jackson's flamboyant performance and some of the fight choreography were noted as highlights. The film went straight to home video, where its star pairing of Lutz and Jackson was its main selling point.

documents.title: Kiss Me
documents.tagline: With Every Heartbeat
documents.overview: After they meet at their parent's engagement party, Mia and Frida are intrigued by and attracted to one another, despite Mia's own upcoming engagement to Tim. Mia must decide whether to continue her life with Tim or to follow her heart with Frida.
