documents.title: American Reunion
documents.tagline: Save the best piece for last.
documents.overview: The characters we met a little more than a decade ago return to East Great Falls for their high-school reunion. In one long-overdue weekend, they will discover what has changed, who hasn’t, and that time and distance can’t break the bonds of friendship.
documents.plot:
American Reunion is a 2012 American coming-of-age comedy film directed by Jon Hurwitz and Hayden Schlossberg, and written by Hurwitz and Schlossberg. The movie is the fourth installment in the American Pie franchise.

The film takes place nine years after the events of American Reunion (2009). Jim Levenstein (Jason Biggs), Michelle Flaherty (Alyson Hannigan), Stifler (Seann William Scott), Oz (Eddie Kaye Thomas), and Kevin (Thomas Ian Nicholas) are now in their mid-to-late 30s. They have all moved on with their lives, but the group is reunited when Jim's high school reunion invitation arrives.

The movie begins with Jim, who has just gone through a divorce, trying to reconnect with his friends and figure out what he wants from life. The group reunites at Jim's house for a weekend, where they reminisce about old times and try to recapture their youth. However, things quickly become complicated as the group faces various challenges, including marriage problems, career struggles, and midlife crises.

As the reunion progresses, the group discovers that some of them are still stuck in their high school ways, while others have grown up and moved on. Stifler, who has been struggling with his own identity crisis, tries to relive his glory days by hooking up with a younger woman (Anna Faris). Meanwhile, Oz is trying to balance his family life with his desire for freedom.

Throughout the movie, the group's dynamics are put to the test as they navigate their relationships and try to find their place in the world. The film features plenty of humor, including raunchy jokes and awkward moments, but also explores more serious themes like marriage, parenthood, and growing up.

As the reunion comes to a close, Jim realizes that he needs to take responsibility for his life and make some changes. He starts to reconnect with an old flame (Emma Stone), who has been a constant presence in his life throughout the series. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with the group having learned valuable lessons about friendship, love, and growing up.

Overall, American Reunion is a lighthearted, entertaining film that explores the ups and downs of adulthood. While it may not be as edgy or raunchy as some of its predecessors, it still delivers plenty of laughs and heartwarming moments.

documents.title: Piranha 3DD
documents.tagline: Twice the Teeth. Twice the Terror.
documents.overview: After the events at Lake Victoria, the prehistoric school of blood-thirsty piranhas make their way into swimming pools, plumbing, and a newly opened water park.
documents.plot:
Piranha 3DD is a 2012 American horror film directed by Marcus Nispel and written by Christopher Heston. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2010 film Piranha 3D, which was also produced by Dimension Films.

The story takes place in the same fictional town of Redemption, California, where a genetically engineered species of super-piranhas has been terrorizing the residents. The main character, Burt Gummer (played by Dave Franco), is the son of Matt Hooper (played by Eli Roth), who was killed by the piranhas in the previous film.

Burt, along with his friends Lina (played by Danielle Panabaker) and Jake (played by Chris Backus), embark on a road trip to visit their father's grave. However, they soon discover that the piranhas have evolved to become even more aggressive and deadly, and are now capable of surviving out of water.

As the group tries to survive the attacks, they also uncover a sinister plot by a wealthy businessman named Hunter Calloway (played by David Arquette), who is secretly behind the creation of the genetically engineered piranhas. Calloway's plan is to use the piranhas as a means to terrorize and control the town, thereby increasing property values and making him rich.

Throughout the film, Burt and his friends face numerous challenges as they try to outsmart the piranhas and stop Calloway's sinister plans. Along the way, they also encounter other characters who are trying to help them, including a local fisherman named Tom (played by Jake Abel) and a mysterious woman named Liz (played by Kelly Overton).

As the body count rises, Burt and his friends realize that they must find a way to stop the piranhas before it's too late. In the climactic final act, they discover that Calloway has been using a device to control the piranhas, and they must destroy the device in order to save the town.

In the end, Burt and his friends manage to defeat the piranhas and stop Calloway's plans, but not before many lives have been lost. The film ends with Burt reflecting on the events that transpired, and realizing that he has a newfound appreciation for his father's bravery and sacrifice.

Overall, Piranha 3DD is a campy and over-the-top horror film that delivers plenty of gore and suspense. While it may not be as well-received as its predecessor, it still provides an entertaining ride for fans of the genre.

documents.title: Hostel: Part III
documents.tagline: Do you feel lucky?
documents.overview: Set in Las Vegas, the film centers on a man who attends his best friend's bachelor party, unaware of an insidious agenda that plays into hunting humans.
documents.plot:
A young man named Travis goes into a room at a hostel in Las Vegas where a Ukrainian couple, Victor and Anka, are currently staying. Anka and Victor fall unconscious after being drugged by the beer Travis gave them and are swept up by a cleanup crew, and it is revealed that Travis is an enforcer of the Elite Hunting Club. Victor later wakes up in a cell in an abandoned building and watches as two guards drag Anka out of her cell.
A man named Scott leaves his fiancée Amy to go to Las Vegas to attend his own bachelor party with his friend Carter, Amy's former flame. There, they meet up with their other friends, Mike and Justin. The four go to a nightclub, where they meet Kendra and Nikki, two escorts Carter secretly paid to have sex with Scott. Kendra and Nikki tell the four men about a "freaky" party they could go to on the other end of town, and the four men take a cab to an abandoned building. At the party, Kendra makes a move on Scott, but he declines and tells her about how he previously cheated on Amy and almost lost her, and does not want it to happen again. Scott wakes up the next morning in his hotel room with Carter and Justin. The three wonder where Mike is, as he is not answering his phone.
Mike wakes in a cell next to Victor and starts panicking. Two guards take him to a glass room torture chamber in front of a live audience and strap him to a chair, and Mike is on display to be gambled upon by wealthy clients. A middle-aged client dressed as a doctor enters the room; Mike pleads with him, but the man cuts and peels Mike's face off before killing him. Worried about Mike's whereabouts, Scott, Carter, and Justin travel to Nikki's trailer, but cannot find her. Kendra arrives and reveals that Nikki is missing as well. Meanwhile at the Las Vegas Art Show, Nikki is brought into the same room as Mike and strapped to a table dressed as a cheerleader. Another man who speaks in Hungarian enters the room and releases a jar full of cockroaches onto Nikki, some of which crawl into her mouth and asphyxiate her to death.
Scott, Carter, Justin, and Kendra get a text from Mike's phone, sent by Travis, to meet him and Nikki in a hotel room. When they get there, everyone is kidnapped by Travis and wakes up in individual cells along with Victor. The two guards take Justin away, and Carter calls the guard and informs them that he is also a client. After he shows his Elite Hunting Club tattoo, the guards let him go. Scott, Justin, and Kendra are confused as to what happened and Carter revealed it was a members only franchise.
Justin is later strapped into a chair and Carter, Flemming, and Travis watch as a woman dressed as a Japanese cyberpunk ninja fatally shoots him with multiple crossbow bolts. The main event starts and Scott is strapped into a chair dressed in a tuxedo. He asks Carter why he is doing this, and Carter reveals he wanted Amy for himself, as they were in a relationship before she ended up with Scott.

documents.title: Wrong Turn 4: Bloody Beginnings
documents.tagline: Frost Is Not The Only Thing That Bites In the Snow!
documents.overview: A group of friends take refuge in a deserted sanatorium after they are left stranded in a snowstorm. Later, the place becomes a death trap when man-eating cannibals surround them.
documents.plot:
Wrong Turn 4: Bloody Beginnings is a 2011 slasher film written and directed by Declan O'Brien. It is the fourth installment of the Wrong Turn series and the first part of a prequel story to the original 2003 film, exploring the origins of the deformed cannibal brothers Saw Tooth, One Eye and Three Finger. The cast includes Jennifer Pudavick, Tenika Davis, Kaitlyn Wong and Terra Vnesa.

In 1974, at the Glenville Sanatorium in West Virginia, the head doctor shows a new colleague around the building, including the cell where the young Hillicker brothers, three cannibalistic patients, are held. After the doctors leave, the brothers escape, kill a guard and release the other inmates, starting a riot in which the staff are massacred.

In 2003, a group of college students set out on a winter break snowmobiling trip to a friend's cabin in the mountains. Caught in a snowstorm, they take shelter in the abandoned Glenville Sanatorium, unaware that the Hillicker brothers still live there. One of the students tells the others stories about the asylum and its cannibals, but her friends dismiss them. During the night, one of the group goes exploring and is killed, and the next day the students discover the cannibals butchering their missing friend's body. When they try to leave, they find that the brothers have sabotaged their snowmobiles. One student sets off on skis to find help while the others remain trapped in the building, and the brothers hunt them down one by one in a series of increasingly gruesome killings, as the survivors try to fight back and escape through the snow.

The film follows the series' formula of isolated victims and graphic violence, moving the setting to a snowbound asylum and offering a glimpse of the cannibals' early years.

Wrong Turn 4: Bloody Beginnings was released directly to DVD and Blu-ray by 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment on October 25, 2011. It received mixed reviews; Dread Central called it an objectively bad film that is still enjoyable to watch, while Little White Lies found the characters interchangeable and the plot derivative. It was followed by Wrong Turn 5: Bloodlines in 2012.

documents.title: Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance
documents.tagline: He rides again.
documents.overview: When the devil resurfaces with aims to take over the world in human form, Johnny Blaze reluctantly comes out of hiding to transform into the flame-spewing supernatural hero Ghost Rider -- and rescue a 10-year-old boy from an unsavory end.
documents.plot:
Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance is a 2012 American supernatural action film directed by Neveldine/Taylor, but released as 2011 due to a distribution deal. The movie stars Nicolas Cage as Johnny Blaze, also known as the Ghost Rider.

The story begins with Johnny Blaze (Nicolas Cage), who has been living in hiding for years after his last encounter with Mephisto (Peter Fonda). However, when a young boy named Robbie (Fergus Rees) is kidnapped by the devil's minions, Blaze is forced back into action to rescue him.

Blaze soon discovers that the boy is being held captive by the devil himself, and that he has been chosen as part of an ancient ritual to bring about the apocalypse. The only way to stop this from happening is for Blaze to ride the Ghost Rider again and put an end to Mephisto's plans.

As Blaze embarks on his quest, he teams up with a mysterious woman named Stakelbeck (Ciarán Hinds), who claims to be working against Mephisto. However, it becomes clear that Stakelbeck has ulterior motives, and is actually working for the devil himself.

The plot thickens as Blaze delves deeper into the world of demonic magic, encountering a range of supernatural creatures along the way. He also begins to question his own sanity, as he struggles to maintain control over his Ghost Rider persona.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Mephisto's plan is to use Robbie as a vessel for an ancient evil entity known as the "Devil's Son". This entity has the power to bring about the apocalypse, and only Blaze can stop it.

The climax of the film features an epic showdown between Blaze and Mephisto, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance. In the end, Blaze is able to defeat Mephisto and save Robbie from becoming a vessel for the Devil's Son.

However, the film ends on a bleak note, as Blaze is left feeling empty and unfulfilled after his victory. He realizes that he has lost himself to the Ghost Rider persona, and that he needs to find a way to reconcile his dual identity.

Overall, Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance is a dark and action-packed take on the Ghost Rider franchise. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the series will appreciate the film's over-the-top action sequences and supernatural thrills.

documents.title: Assassination Games
documents.tagline: Twice the fire... double the power!
documents.overview: Brazil is a contract killer, willing to take any job if the price is right. Flint left the assassin game when a ruthless drug dealer’s brutal attack left his wife in a coma. When a contract is put out on the same coldblooded drug dealer, both Brazil and Flint want him dead – one for the money, the other for revenge. With crooked Interpol agents and vicious members of the criminal underworld hot on their trail, these two assassins reluctantly join forces to quickly take out their target before they themselves are terminated.
documents.plot:
Assassination Games is a 2011 American action thriller directed by Ernie Barbarash from a screenplay by Aaron Rahsaan Thomas, starring Jean-Claude Van Damme and Scott Adkins as rival contract killers, with Ivan Kaye as their common enemy. Produced by the Motion Picture Corporation of America with Mediapro Studios and Rodin Entertainment on a budget of about $8 million, it was shot in Bucharest, Romania, and New Orleans in the autumn of 2010, with a score by Neal Acree.

Vincent Brazil is an assassin and master of bladed weapons who will take any job if the price is right. Roland Flint, a top marksman, has walked away from the profession since the drug kingpin Polo Yakur launched a brutal attack that left Flint's wife, Anna, in a coma from which she has never awoken. When a contract is put out on Yakur, both men want it: Brazil for the money, Flint for revenge. The two strangers start out as competitors working the same target, but with crooked Interpol agents protecting the dealer and vicious members of the criminal underworld closing in on them both, they reluctantly join forces to take Yakur down before they themselves are eliminated.

Van Damme plays Brazil and Adkins plays Flint, with Kevin Chapman as Culley, Valentin Teodosiu as Blanchard, Alin Panc as Kovacs, Michael Higgs as Godfrey and Marija Karan as October, Bianca Bree as Anna Flint and Kris Van Damme as Schell.

The project began life under the working title The Weapon, with Russell Mulcahy attached to direct and Steven Seagal set to co-star with Van Damme. After Seagal dropped out, Vinnie Jones was considered for the part before it went to Adkins. The film received a limited theatrical release in the United States on 29 July 2011, followed by a DVD release from Sony Pictures Home Entertainment that September, and opened in France and Russia later in 2011 and 2012.

Reviews were mixed. IGN rated it 6 out of 10 and called it a quick dose of action that should leave viewers moderately pleased, and Indiewire's Gabe Toro gave it a C, noting that it at least showed filmmakers who still understood how to shoot action. DVD Talk's Rohit Rao gave it two stars out of five, complaining of a convoluted script that mistakes meanness for grit, and DVD Verdict found it cheesy, pretentious and poorly paced.

documents.title: The Iron Lady
documents.tagline: Never Compromise.
documents.overview: A look at the life of Margaret Thatcher, the former Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, with a focus on the price she paid for power.
documents.plot:
The Iron Lady is a 2011 biographical drama about Margaret Thatcher, the longest-serving British prime minister of the 20th century and the first woman to hold the office. Phyllida Lloyd directed from a screenplay by Abi Morgan, loosely based on John Campbell's biography. Meryl Streep plays Thatcher, with Alexandra Roach as the young Margaret. Jim Broadbent and Harry Lloyd play her husband, Denis, and Anthony Head plays Geoffrey Howe.

In the present day, the elderly Thatcher, now suffering from dementia, keeps seeing and talking to Denis, who has died. Her memories take the story back through her life. As a girl, Margaret Roberts works in her family's grocery shop in Grantham and absorbs the political speeches of the father she idolizes, while her relationship with her mother is distant. She wins a place at Somerville College, Oxford, and later fights to break into a snobbish, male-dominated Conservative Party and win a seat in the House of Commons. She accepts Denis's proposal only after warning him that she will never be content as a housewife: "I don't want to die cleaning a teacup."

The flashbacks follow her through life as one of the few women in Parliament and as education secretary under Edward Heath. They show her friendship with Airey Neave, her run for party leader and her image makeover. As prime minister after the 1979 election, she pushes through monetarist policies and the austere 1981 budget over the doubts of the "wets" in her cabinet. She faces unemployment, riots, the miners' strike and the 1984 Brighton bombing. She sends a task force to recover the Falkland Islands from Argentina, forms an alliance with Ronald Reagan and presides over the late-1980s boom. By 1990, she has become imperious, berating her ministers, defending the poll tax amid riots and resisting European integration. Howe resigns after she humiliates him, Michael Heseltine challenges her and she is forced to resign after eleven years. In the present, Thatcher finally packs away Denis's belongings and tells him to go. As his ghost departs, he assures her that she will be fine on her own, and she washes a teacup alone in her kitchen.

Filming began on December 31, 2010. The film grossed $115 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, and Thatcher's children and biographer criticized its portrayal. Streep's performance was widely acclaimed and won her a third Academy Award, as well as a Golden Globe and a BAFTA. The film also won the Oscar for Best Makeup.

documents.title: Phineas and Ferb: The Movie: Across the 2nd Dimension
documents.original_title: Phineas and Ferb: The Movie: Across the 2nd Dimension
documents.tagline: An adventure so big, one dimension isn't enough.
documents.overview: Phineas and Ferb get trapped in an alternate dimension where the evil Doofenshmirtz rules the tri-state area. They must find a way back home with the help of their pet platypus named Perry, who they discover is a secret agent.
documents.plot: Phineas and Ferb get trapped in an alternate dimension where the evil Doofenshmirtz rules the tri-state area. They must find a way back home with the help of their pet platypus named Perry, who they discover is a secret agent.

documents.title: We Need to Talk About Kevin
documents.original_title: We Need to Talk About Kevin
documents.tagline: This conversation is long overdue.
documents.overview: After her son Kevin commits a horrific act, troubled mother Eva reflects on her complicated relationship with her disturbed son as he grew from a toddler into a teenager.
documents.plot: After her son Kevin commits a horrific act, troubled mother Eva reflects on her complicated relationship with her disturbed son as he grew from a toddler into a teenager.

documents.title: The Odd Life of Timothy Green
documents.original_title: The Odd Life of Timothy Green
documents.tagline: He's a force of nature.
documents.overview: A childless couple bury a box in their backyard, containing all of their wishes for an infant. Soon, a child is born, though Timothy Green is not all that he appears.
documents.plot:
The film is told from the perspective of Cindy (Jennifer Garner) and Jim Green (Joel Edgerton), as they explain their experience with a boy named Timothy (CJ Adams) in an effort to persuade an adoption agency to allow the couple to adopt a child.
Cindy, who works in the town's local museum, and Jim, who is employed at the town's historic pencil factory, reside in the fictitious town of Stanleyville, self-described as "the pencil capital of the world". The Greens are informed by doctors that they are unable to conceive. Distraught by the news, Jim convinces Cindy to dream up their ideal child and write the child's characteristics and life events on slips of notepad paper.
The couple place the notes inside a wooden box and bury it in their backyard garden. After an immediate thunderstorm, which seemingly affects only their property, a 10-year-old boy arrives at their home claiming the Greens as his parents. After finding the box they buried smashed to pieces around a large hole in the ground where they originally buried it, and finding the boy inside their house, covered in mud, they realize that the boy, named Timothy, is actually a culmination of all their wishes of what their child would be. The Greens also discover that Timothy has a startling feature; he has leaves growing on his legs, which he can only cover up by wearing long, green tube socks.
The next day, at a family picnic, Timothy is introduced to members of his family: Brenda Best (Rosemarie DeWitt), Cindy's pompous sister; James Green Sr. (David Morse), Jim's estranged father; and Mel (Lois Smith) and Bub (M. Emmet Walsh), Cindy's paternal aunt and uncle. The parents take Timothy to their friend and town botanist, Reggie (Lin-Manuel Miranda), where they learn that Timothy's leaves cannot be removed.
Timothy begins to attend school, where he meets Joni Jerome (Odeya Rush), a girl he encounters during a bullying incident. Jim takes Timothy to confront the bullies and Timothy is invited to a birthday pool party. There, Joni tries to take off his socks and is kicked in the head by Timothy, though they later become friends. Meanwhile, the town's pencil factory, the largest employer in Stanleyville, begins laying off its employees. Timothy convinces Cindy and Jim to design a prototype for a new pencil in an effort to keep the pencil-producing business viable.
Unbeknownst to the parents, one of Timothy's leaves falls off each time he fulfills one of the qualities listed on the original slips of paper. Timothy eventually reveals to Cindy and Jim that his time of existence is short and that he will eventually disappear. During another intense thunderstorm, he vanishes from their house and all they can find of him is the pile of paper slips.
The Greens' meeting with the adoption counselor concludes with Cindy presenting a letter that Timothy left them before leaving.

documents.title: Jack and Jill
documents.tagline: His twin sister is coming for the holidays... ...and it ain't pretty.
documents.overview: Jack Sadelstein, a successful advertising executive in Los Angeles with a beautiful wife and kids, dreads one event each year: the Thanksgiving visit of his twin sister Jill. Jill's neediness and passive-aggressiveness is maddening to Jack, turning his normally tranquil life upside down.
documents.plot:
Jack and Jill is a 2011 American comedy directed by Dennis Dugan and co-written by Adam Sandler, who stars in a dual role as twin siblings Jack and Jill Sadelstein. Katie Holmes plays Jack's wife Erin, and Al Pacino appears as a fictionalised version of himself. The film features numerous celebrity cameos, including Johnny Depp, Shaquille O'Neal, Drew Carey, John McEnroe and Regis Philbin, in his final film appearance. Its story follows a successful advertising executive whose holiday season is upended by a visit from his twin sister.

As children in the Bronx, Jill constantly sought the attention of her gifted twin brother, often in disastrous ways. As an adult, Jack is a successful advertising executive living in Los Angeles with Erin, their daughter Sofia and their adopted son Gary. Jill, unemployed and single, still lives alone in the family home in the Bronx, which she inherited after their mother's death the previous year.

Jill comes to stay for Thanksgiving and announces, to Jack's dismay, that she intends to remain until the end of Hanukkah, since her ticket is open-ended. Her loud, tactless behaviour embarrasses Jack in front of his guests, and after he snaps at her she runs off into the woods with her pet cockatoo, prompting Erin to insist that he apologise. Jill works her way through a list of activities she has planned, including an appearance on The Price Is Right. Meanwhile, Jack's biggest client demands that he persuade Al Pacino to appear in a Dunkin' Donuts commercial. When Pacino unexpectedly falls for Jill, Jack sees an opportunity to save his career by encouraging the romance, even though Jill has little interest in the actor, setting up a series of increasingly absurd situations that culminate in the making of the commercial.

The comedy relies heavily on Sandler's cross-dressing performance as Jill, product placement and Pacino's self-parody, and its underlying theme is the reconciliation between two very different siblings.

Jack and Jill was panned by critics, with about 3 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and it is often cited as one of the worst films ever made. At the 32nd Golden Raspberry Awards it became the first film to sweep every category, although it grossed about 149 million dollars worldwide.

documents.title: Redline
documents.tagline: The most violent race in the universe!
documents.overview: The most dangerous and exciting car race in the universe is held only once every five years. And that's tonight. The competitors are lined up at the starting block. In his vehicle, JP, the most daredevil driver on the circuit, is ready for the green light. Female driver Sonoshee, with whom he is secretly in love, is also on the starting line. She will stop at nothing to get on to that podium. In this race, not only is anything possible, but also anything is allowed. In fact, their adversaries have modified their vehicles to equip them with highly destructive weapons; with such participants, it is hardly surprising that Redline is forbidden by the authorities, who will try anything to halt the proceedings.
documents.plot:
Redline is a 2009 Japanese animated science fiction racing film produced by Madhouse and directed by Takeshi Koike in his directorial debut, written by Katsuhito Ishii, Yōji Enokido and Yoshiki Sakurai from Ishii's story. Its voice cast includes Takuya Kimura, Yū Aoi, Tatsuya Gashūin, Takeshi Aono and Tadanobu Asano.

On the planet Dorothy, "Sweet" JP competes in the Yellowline, the last qualifier for the Redline. His mechanic and friend Frisbee has fixed the race with a mafia boss, and when JP pushes for first instead of second, Frisbee remotely detonates a bomb hidden in JP's car, handing victory to the racer Sonoshee McLaren. Recovering in the hospital, JP learns he has been voted into the Redline after two qualifiers withdraw, because the race will be held on Roboworld, a planet ruled by militant cyborgs whose President has threatened to hang anyone involved. The racers gather on a demilitarized moon of Roboworld, where JP recruits the junk dealer Old Man Mole, who reluctantly accepts Frisbee and his dangerously powerful engine, and Roboworld's Colonel Volton warns the racers that the military will crush the event.

Saboteurs hired by the race commission disable an orbital cannon meant to destroy the Redline mothership as it exits hyperspace, while rebellious miners attack the military's power station. Furious, the President sends his army against the racers as they head into a mined zone hiding Funky Boy, a giant illegal bioweapon that awakens as they approach. The army shells it, wrecking much of the field; JP rights his overturned car and picks up Sonoshee, whose vehicle is destroyed, and Volton defeats Funky Boy by merging with another bioweapon. Frisbee, offered the same rigged deal, refuses to trigger the bomb this time and is rescued from the mobsters by Old Man Mole. In a neck-and-neck finish with the reigning champion, Machinehead, a drunken Mole accidentally sets off the explosive, hurling JP and Sonoshee over the line, and JP wins by the length of his pompadour before the two declare their love.

Redline took seven years to make and used more than 100,000 hand-drawn frames. It premiered at the Locarno International Film Festival on August 14, 2009, and opened in Japan on October 9, 2010. A box-office failure, it found success on home video and became a cult film; Anime News Network gave it an A+, calling it insanely exhilarating.

documents.title: Yu-Gi-Oh!: Bonds Beyond Time
documents.original_title: 劇場版 遊☆戯☆王 ～超融合！時空を越えた絆～
documents.tagline: Friendship protects the world. Dueling protects the future. This is the power set toward our futures!
documents.overview: After falling through a time-slip, Yusei Fudo (who has just had his powerful card stolen by a mysterious stranger) meets with Jaden Yuki and Yugi Muto, who agree to help Yusei defeat the evil Paradox, who is planning to destroy Pegasus before he can invent Duel Monsters.
documents.plot:
Yu-Gi-Oh!: Bonds Beyond Time is a 2010 Japanese 3D animated science fantasy action film produced to celebrate the tenth anniversary of the anime Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Monsters. It unites the heroes of three series, Yugi Muto of the original, Jaden Yuki of Yu-Gi-Oh! GX and Yusei Fudo of Yu-Gi-Oh! 5D's, against a time-travelling villain. Released in Japanese cinemas on January 23, 2010, it debuted at number six at the box office, and an English-language version was produced by 4Kids Entertainment.

In New Domino City, Yusei Fudo's friends Jack Atlas and Crow Hogan try to lift his spirits with a ride on their Duel Runners. A mysterious Turbo Duelist called Paradox appears and challenges Yusei, then seals his signature monster, Stardust Dragon, inside a card and vanishes. Soon afterwards they find a record of a strange battle in the past in Venice, Italy, which Yusei knows never happened, and New Domino City itself begins to disappear. The Crimson Dragon appears and grants Yusei's Duel Runner the power to travel through time.

In the past, Jaden Yuki is being attacked in Venice by corrupted versions of stolen monsters, among them Stardust Dragon. Yusei arrives with the Crimson Dragon just in time to protect him, and Paradox escapes further back in time. Jaden explains that he had been pursuing Paradox, who stole cards from his friends, and the two agree to join forces.

Years earlier, Maximillion Pegasus is hosting a Duel Monsters tournament in Domino City attended by Yugi Muto and his grandfather. Paradox unleashes his stolen monsters, killing Pegasus, Yugi's grandfather and many others, though Yugi survives. Because Pegasus's death would change the course of history, the Crimson Dragon sends Yusei, Jaden and Yugi thirty minutes back in time to prevent the attack. Yugi agrees to help, and his ancient alter ego takes over.

Confronted, Paradox explains that he comes from a ruined future far beyond Yusei's and believes the world can only be saved by erasing Duel Monsters, created by Pegasus, from history. The three heroes object that this would erase everyone connected with the game, and challenge him to a duel. Combining the powers of their monsters, they defeat him. The three say goodbye and promise to meet again, history is restored, and Yusei returns to his own time, hopeful for the future. Its DVD and Blu-ray releases reached number two on their respective Japanese sales charts.

documents.title: Ted
documents.tagline: Ted is coming.
documents.overview: John Bennett, a man whose childhood wish of bringing his teddy bear to life came true, now must decide between keeping the relationship with the bear or his girlfriend, Lori.
documents.plot:
In 1985, 8-year-old John Bennett is a friendless only child living in Norwood, Massachusetts. On Christmas Day, he wishes for his new gift, a jumbo teddy bear named Ted, to come to life and become his friend. The wish coincides with a shooting star and comes true; word spreads, and Ted briefly becomes a celebrity.
In 2012, the now 35-year-old John and Ted are still living together in an apartment in Boston with John's girlfriend Lori Collins, and are staunch companions enjoying a hedonistic life. As the couple's fourth anniversary approaches, Lori hopes to marry John, but feels he cannot move forward in life with Ted around. He is hesitant about making Ted leave, but is persuaded to act when they find Ted at home with a group of prostitutes, including one who defecated on the floor, while they were out for their anniversary dinner.
John finds Ted his own apartment and a job at a grocery store, where he begins dating his co-worker, Tami-Lynn. Lori learns that John has been skipping work, using her as an excuse, to spend most of his time with Ted. John and Lori are invited to a party put on by Lori's womanizing manager Rex, but Ted lures John away to a party at his apartment with the offer to meet Sam J. Jones, the star of their favorite film, Flash Gordon.
Intending to stay only for a few minutes, John gets caught up in the occasion. Lori finds John there and kicks him out of their apartment, breaking up with him. Devastated and furious, he blames Ted for ruining his life and ends their friendship.
Ted then goes to John's hotel room to inform him that Lori and Rex are attending a Norah Jones concert on a date together. Their conversation becomes an argument and then a violent brawl, but they reconcile. To repair John's relationship with Lori, Ted arranges for Norah Jones, an old lover of his, to help by having John express his love for Lori with a song during Norah's concert.
John does an off-key rendition of "All Time High", the theme song of Octopussy, which he and Lori watched on their first date. He is booed off stage, though the attempt touches Lori. She returns to her apartment, where Ted confesses to his role in John's relapse and offers to leave them alone forever if she talks to John, to which Lori agrees.
After Lori leaves, however, Ted is kidnapped by Donny, an obsessive stalker who has idolized him since he was a child. Donny plans to make Ted into his son Robert's new toy. Ted obtains a phone to contact John, but is recaptured.
Realizing Ted is in danger, John and Lori locate Donny's residence and track him. They chase them to Fenway Park, where Donny rips Ted in half. Two police cars arrive, forcing Donny to flee the scene. John and Lori gather Ted's stuffing, and Ted relays his wish for John to be happy with Lori before the magic in Ted fades away, making him a normal teddy bear again.
Unable to accept his death, John and Lori unsuccessfully attempt to repair Ted. Saddened by the incident, Lori makes a wish upon a shooting star.

documents.title: Carnage
documents.tagline: A new comedy of no manners
documents.overview: After 11-year-old Zachary Cowan strikes his classmate across the face with a stick after an argument, the victim's parents invite Zachary's parents to their Brooklyn apartment to deal with the incident in a civilized manner.
documents.plot:
When two grade-school boys get into a fight in the park that results in one boy, Zachary Cowan, hitting the other, Ethan Longstreet, in the face with a stick, their parents meet in a Brooklyn apartment to discuss the matter. Zachary's parents, Alan (Christoph Waltz) and Nancy Cowan (Kate Winslet), visit the home of Michael (John C. Reilly) and Penelope Longstreet (Jodie Foster), Ethan's parents. Their meeting is initially intended to be short, but due to various circumstances, the conversation continues to draw out.
In fact, Alan and Nancy begin to leave the apartment on two occasions, but are drawn back in to further discussion.
At first, the couples are friendly to each other, but their respective comments start to hurt feelings, making everyone argue with one another. Apart from fighting amongst themselves, the couples blame each other about who is responsible for the fight between their sons. Nancy calls the Longstreets "superficially fair-minded" and Penelope and Michael complain about Alan's arrogant and dull attitude. Everyone also gets irritated with Alan when he accepts endless business phone calls on his BlackBerry, interrupting the discussion, and showing he has more interest in his business problems than the matter at hand. Michael also receives many phone calls from his ailing mother, to his frustration.
Nancy accuses Michael of being a murderer because he, annoyed by the constant noise it made during the night, had earlier turned his daughter Courtney's pet hamster loose in the street. Penelope becomes emotional about the hamster and with everyone arguing with each other. Other issues include a risky drug Alan is working to defend and Michael's mother has been prescribed, and the question of idealism and responsibility that is part of Penelope's current work.
Michael offers everyone a glass of fine Scotch. Penelope claims she doesn't "get drunk" and Nancy drinks way too many and finally stops Alan's phone calls by dropping his cellphone in Penelope's flower vase full of tulips and water. Penelope and Nancy both laugh uproariously while Michael and Alan try to blow-dry the BlackBerry.
The conversation continues to decay into personal attacks and opinionated statements and, eventually, epithets are uttered. Penelope is ranting, calling Nancy's son a "snitch", and Nancy's true colors are revealed when she destroys the tulips and drunkenly and vulgarly states she is glad that her son beat up Penelope's and Michael's son. The couples realize the conversation is going nowhere. Alan's BlackBerry, lying on the coffee table, vibrates, and all four stare at it.
The film cuts to the hamster, alive and well in the park, where Ethan and Zachary are reconciling on their own.

documents.title: World War Z
documents.tagline: Remember Philly!
documents.overview: Life for former United Nations investigator Gerry Lane and his family seems content. Suddenly, the world is plagued by a mysterious infection turning whole human populations into rampaging mindless zombies. After barely escaping the chaos, Lane is persuaded to go on a mission to investigate this disease. What follows is a perilous trek around the world where Lane must brave horrific dangers and long odds to find answers before human civilization falls.
documents.plot:
World War Z is a 2013 apocalyptic horror film directed by Marc Forster, starring Brad Pitt as the main character, Gerry Lane.

The movie begins with Gerry Lane, a former United Nations employee, who is tasked with finding a way to stop the rapid spread of a zombie pandemic that has devastated the world. The zombies, known as "fast zombies," are highly aggressive and can move quickly, making them nearly impossible to kill.

Gerry's wife, Karin (Mireille Enos), is infected while trying to protect their children from the zombies, and he sets out on a perilous journey across the globe to find a way to stop the outbreak. He travels to Israel, South Korea, and Wales, where he meets various survivors who share their experiences with him.

As Gerry navigates through the treacherous landscape, he encounters numerous obstacles, including hordes of zombies, hostile human groups, and government conspiracies. Along the way, he also discovers that the zombies are not just mindless creatures but are actually reanimated corpses that have been infected by a virus.

Gerry's quest takes him to Jerusalem, where he meets a young girl named Segen (Fana Mokoena), who has managed to survive the outbreak by hiding in an underground bunker. Gerry and Segen form an unlikely alliance, and together they embark on a mission to find a way to stop the zombies.

The movie culminates with Gerry discovering that the key to stopping the zombies lies in a small town in Wales, where he finds a group of survivors who have developed a vaccine against the virus. However, just as Gerry is about to leave with the vaccine, he realizes that it may not be enough to save humanity.

Throughout the movie, Brad Pitt delivers a strong performance as Gerry Lane, conveying his determination and desperation as he navigates through the zombie-infested world. The film's action sequences are intense and suspenseful, making for an thrilling ride.

While World War Z received mixed reviews from critics, it has become a cult classic among fans of the zombie genre. Its unique take on the zombie apocalypse and its focus on human survival make it a compelling watch.

documents.title: The Pirates! In an Adventure with Scientists!
documents.original_title: The Pirates! In an Adventure with Scientists!
documents.tagline: It's a plunderful life
documents.overview: The luxuriantly bearded Pirate Captain is a boundlessly enthusiastic, if somewhat less-than-successful, terror of the High Seas. With a rag-tag crew at his side, and seemingly blind to the impossible odds stacked against him, the Captain has one dream: to beat his bitter rivals Black Bellamy and Cutlass Liz to the much coveted Pirate of the Year Award. It’s a quest that takes our heroes from the shores of exotic Blood Island to the foggy streets of Victorian London. Along the way they battle a diabolical queen and team up with a haplessly smitten young scientist, but never lose sight of what a pirate loves best: adventure!
documents.plot: The enthusiastic Pirate Captain, along with his rag-tag crew, sets out to beat his bitter rivals. The chaotic adventure takes them from exotic shores to Victorian London, and from a haplessly smitten scientist to a diabolical queen.

documents.title: The Five-Year Engagement
documents.tagline: A comedy about the journey between popping the question and tying the knot.
documents.overview: Exactly one year after Tom meets Violet, he surprises her with a wedding ring. By all accounts, Tom and Violet are destined for their happily ever after. However, this engaged couple just keep getting tripped up on the long walk down the aisle.
documents.plot:
In San Francisco, sous-chef Tom, and PhD graduate Violet, are happily engaged. Their wedding plans are interrupted when Tom's best friend Alex gets Violet's sister Suzie pregnant at Tom and Violet's engagement party, and Alex and Suzie quickly marry.
Violet is accepted into the University of Michigan's two-year post-doctorate psychology program, Tom agrees to move with her and delay their wedding. Later, he is disheartened to learn his boss planned to make him head chef.
Unable to find a suitable chef's position in Michigan, Tom is resigned to working at Zingerman's deli and takes up hunting with Bill, a fellow university faculty spouse. Violet settles into her new job under professor Winton Childs, working with Doug, Ming, and Vaneetha.
A prank results in Violet being chosen to lead the team's research project, studying people who choose to eat stale donuts rather than wait for fresh ones to arrive. Tom and Violet's nuptials are further delayed when Winton receives funding from the National Institutes of Health with Violet's help and extends her program. Tom is upset by the news, and he and Violet fight over his unhappiness with their new life.
As years pass, Tom becomes disillusioned and obsessed with hunting. Alex, Suzie, and their daughter Vanessa visit, and reveal Suzie is pregnant again. Tom responds that he no longer wants to have a child, surprising Violet, who offers to look after Vanessa with him, but the night turns into a disaster after Vanessa shoots Violet with Tom's crossbow.
Tom's downward spiral becomes evident when Violet sees him eat a stale donut. At a bar with colleagues, a drunken Violet and Winton kiss, which she instantly regrets. She tells Tom that she wants to plan their wedding immediately, and he happily agrees. When Violet confesses to kissing Winton, Tom loses faith in their relationship, which reaches a climax when Winton comes to their rehearsal dinner to apologize.
Tom chases Winton away, then leaves to get drunk alone. He runs into Margaret, an amorous co-worker, but opts not to have sex with her, and wakes up half-naked in the snow with a frostbitten toe, which must be amputated. Violet visits Tom at the hospital, and they call off their engagement once they arrive home.
Violet starts a relationship with Winton but often reminisces about Tom. He wishes her a happy birthday via email, including a video of Ming's ridiculous experiment on his friend Tarquin. Violet calls Tom, who has returned to San Francisco, working as a sous-chef under Alex and dating the hostess, Audrey. Their friendly-but-awkward conversation takes a turn as they argue over Violet's stale donuts experiment as a metaphor for their relationship, and both end the call upset.
Realizing Tom's unhappiness, Alex fires him out of love, telling him that he is the better chef and should open his own establishment. So, Tom launches a popular taco truck.

documents.title: A Thousand Words
documents.tagline: He only has 1000 words left to discover what matters the most.
documents.overview: Jack McCall is a fast-talking literary agent, who can close any deal, any time, any way. He has set his sights on New Age guru Dr. Sinja for his own selfish purposes. But Dr. Sinja is on to him, and Jack’s life comes unglued after a magical Bodhi tree mysteriously appears in his backyard. With every word Jack speaks, a leaf falls from the tree and he realizes that when the last leaf falls, both he and the tree are toast. Words have never failed Jack McCall, but now he’s got to stop talking and conjure up some outrageous ways to communicate or he’s a goner.

documents.title: Safe
documents.tagline: She has the code. He is the key.
documents.overview: After a former elite agent rescues a 12-year-old Chinese girl who's been abducted, they find themselves in the middle of a standoff between Triads, the Russian Mafia and high-level corrupt New York City politicians and police.
documents.plot:
Safe is a 2012 American action thriller written and directed by Boaz Yakin. Jason Statham stars as Luke Wright, an ex-cop and former cage fighter who ends up protecting a gifted child hunted by the Russian mafia, Chinese triads and corrupt New York police, with Chris Sarandon, Robert John Burke and James Hong in supporting roles.

After Luke accidentally wins a fixed fight, Russian mob boss Emile Docheski has his son Vassily and his men murder Luke's pregnant wife and vows to kill anyone Luke grows close to, leaving him homeless and adrift. In China, the young math prodigy Mei is abducted by triad boss Han Jiao, who uses her as a human calculator so his operation leaves no digital trail, and is sent to New York under the watch of the brutal Quan Chang. A year later Han has her memorize a long number, but the Russians ambush them and seize her, only to be attacked in turn by police working for the corrupt Captain Wolf, who is in Han's pay. Mei escapes into a subway station where Luke is contemplating suicide; recognizing one of his wife's killers among her pursuers, Luke kills the Russians, saves her from two crooked detectives and flees with her. In a hotel she explains the number, which Luke guesses is a safe combination, but Quan tracks her through her phone and recaptures her.

The mayor, Danny Tremello, warns Wolf that Luke was really a government assassin lent to the city after 9/11 alongside his former partner, Alex Rosen, to eliminate crime bosses, until Luke quit after exposing Wolf's corrupt squad. Luke kidnaps Vassily and forces Emile to reveal that the number opens a guarded Chinatown safe holding $30 million. He recruits Wolf's detectives with the promise of money, fights through the triads to the safe, then kills the detectives when Wolf betrays him. He bribes Alex, now the mayor's aide, to rescue Mei, and learns that a second safe holds the mayor's disc of evidence against every crime syndicate in the city. After Alex kills Quan to take Mei, Luke obtains a copy of the disc, and Mei wounds Alex during a standoff, letting Luke finish him. Luke returns Vassily through Wolf, pays Han for Mei's freedom, hides copies of the disc as insurance and heads to Seattle so Mei can attend a school for gifted children.

Shot in Philadelphia and New York on a $30 million budget, Safe was released by Lionsgate on April 27, 2012, and grossed $40.6 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, with 59% on Rotten Tomatoes and 55 on Metacritic.

documents.title: Marley & Me: The Puppy Years
documents.tagline: The World's Worst dog is Back
documents.overview: Fall into puppy love with “the world’s worst dog”, who now has a frisky voice and an attitude to match. Join Marley for his mischievous puppy years, as he and his summer pal, Bodie Grogan, wreak havoc on a neighborhood dog contest. Marley outwits Dobermans, Shepherds and Collies, while stealing hearts in his own unique and lovable way. Get your paws on MARLEY & ME: THE PUPPY YEARS and fetch big laughs for the whole family!
documents.plot:
Marley & Me: The Puppy Years, originally titled Marley & Me: The Terrible 2's, is a 2011 American direct-to-video family comedy that serves as an intermediate follow-up to the 2008 film Marley & Me. It was directed by Michael Damian, who wrote it with his wife, Janeen Damian. Unlike the original film, Marley has a speaking voice, provided by Grayson Russell. Travis Turner stars as Bodi Grogan, with Donnelly Rhodes as grandfather Fred, Alex Zahara as Hans Von Weiselberger, Sydney Imbeau as Kaycee and Chelah Horsdal as Bodi's mother, Carol.

Marley, a puppy some call the world's worst dog, is in the care of Bodi, a boy who has long begged his mother for a dog of his own. While Carol is away on a business trip, Bodi and Marley stay with Fred, a strict grandfather who insists on chores. On a walk, Bodi meets Kaycee, whose parents run a pug rescue center and who plans to enter three of her pugs in a puppy championship to raise money for it. Because each team needs three dogs, she introduces Bodi to Mrs. Crouch, whose two Labrador puppies, Fuchsia and Moose, join Marley, and the trio begin training for the course.

Meanwhile, Hans, whose three dogs, Turbo, Liesl and Axel, were the previous year's champions, trains them cruelly with shock collars. The day before the contest, Hans's assistant Henkle, posing as a spa worker, kidnaps Bodi's puppies along with Dundee, an Australian Shepherd also entered in the event, and locks them up with two German Shepherds, Trouble and Chipper. After pretending to menace the pups, the big dogs help them escape with a homemade seesaw that catapults them out, and the dirty puppies make it back to Bodi.

At the championship, Marley gets distracted mid-course and Bodi's team fails to place, while Hans takes first. Then Marley saves the day: a cat snips the collars off Hans's dogs, and Marley slips one into Hans's pocket, so that when the disobedient dogs prompt Hans to activate the collars, he shocks himself and drops the remote in view of the judge. Hans is disqualified, Dundee's team is declared the winner and Kaycee's pugs take second, while Bodi receives a sportsmanship prize. His mother turns up and sees how happy Marley makes him. Since Marley belongs to a relative, Bodi cannot keep him, but Hans loses his dogs: a family adopts Liesl and Axel, and Carol, now convinced her son is responsible, lets him adopt Turbo instead of sending him to a shelter. 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment released the film on DVD on June 1, 2011.

documents.title: Red Tails
documents.tagline: High-Octane Action and Daring Dogfights!
documents.overview: The story of the Tuskegee Airmen, the first African-American pilots to fly in a combat squadron during World War II.
documents.plot:
Red Tails is a 2012 American war drama film directed by Anthony Hemingway and produced by Lucasfilm Ltd., in association with 20th Century Fox, and Jerry Bruckheimer Films.

The film is set during World War II and tells the story of the Tuskegee Airmen, a group of African-American pilots who served in the United States Army Air Forces (USAAF) during the war. The movie begins with the introduction of the main characters: Captain Benjamin O. "B-24" O Malone Jr. (David Oyelowo), Lieutenant Colonel Peter "Pete" Skelly (Nate Parker), and Lieutenant Colonel John "Rip" Robertson (Tristan Wilds).

The story follows the Tuskegee Airmen as they undergo rigorous training at the Tuskegee Army Air Field in Alabama, where they face racism and skepticism from their white counterparts. Despite these challenges, the airmen prove themselves to be skilled pilots, earning the respect of their peers.

As the war intensifies, the Tuskegee Airmen are deployed to Italy, where they participate in several key battles against the German Luftwaffe. The film's climax features an intense dogfight between the Tuskegee Airmen and a group of enemy planes, which ends with the airmen emerging victorious.

Throughout the film, the characters grapple with issues of racism, prejudice, and identity. O Malone struggles to balance his duty as a pilot with his desire to prove himself in a society that doesn't trust him. Skelly faces personal demons, including a troubled relationship with his father. Robertson, meanwhile, finds solace in his faith and his relationships with his fellow pilots.

The film's title, "Red Tails," refers to the distinctive red paint applied to the tails of the Tuskegee Airmen's planes, which made them easily identifiable as friendly aircraft. The term also symbolizes the airmen's pride and identity, as they fly their planes into battle with courage and determination.

One of the most notable aspects of Red Tails is its attention to historical detail. The film features many authentic locations and props, including vintage aircraft and uniforms. The cast, which includes Cuba Gooding Jr., Tom Wilkinson, and Mahershala Ali, delivers strong performances that bring depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Red Tails is a powerful tribute to the Tuskegee Airmen, who played a crucial role in the Allied victory during World War II. The film's themes of perseverance, courage, and identity are timeless and universal, making it a compelling watch for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Texas Killing Fields
documents.tagline: No one is safe.
documents.overview: In the Texas bayous, a local homicide detective teams up with a cop from New York City to investigate a series of unsolved murders.
documents.plot: Souder, a homicide detective in a small Texan town, and his partner, transplanted New York City cop Detective Heigh, track a sadistic serial killer dumping his victims' mutilated bodies in a nearby marsh locals call 'The Killing Fields'. Though the swampland crime scenes are outside their jurisdiction, Detective Heigh is unable to turn his back on solving the gruesome murders. Despite his partner's warnings, he sets out to investigate the crimes. Before long, the killer changes the game and begins hunting the detectives, teasing them with possible clues at the crime scenes while always remaining one step ahead. When local girl Ann goes missing, the detectives find themselves racing against time to catch the killer and save the young girl's life.

documents.title: Journey 2: The Mysterious Island
documents.tagline: Believe the Impossible. Discover the Incredible.
documents.overview: Sean Anderson partners with his mom's boyfriend on a mission to find his grandfather, who is thought to be missing on a mythical island.
documents.plot:
Journey 2: The Mysterious Island is a 2012 American adventure film directed by Brad Peyton, starring Josh Hutcherson and Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson. The movie is a sequel to the 1995 film Jumanji.

The story begins with Sean Anderson (Josh Hutcherson), a teenager who has been searching for his missing father, Dr. Martin Anderson (Michael Caine), for years. His father was an explorer who disappeared on a mysterious island while searching for a legendary island called "Jumanji." Sean's life is turned upside down when he receives a cryptic message from his father, which leads him to the island.

Sean soon discovers that he has inherited his father's passion for adventure and exploration. He meets Hank Parsons (Dwayne Johnson), a former Marine who claims to be an expert on Jumanji. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to find Sean's father and uncover the secrets of the mysterious island.

As they navigate through the treacherous terrain, they encounter various obstacles, including deadly creatures, treacherous landscapes, and rival treasure hunters. Along the way, Sean learns valuable lessons about courage, perseverance, and the importance of family.

The duo soon discovers that Jumanji is not just a myth but a real place, filled with ancient ruins, hidden temples, and untold riches. However, they are not alone on the island, as they are pursued by a ruthless treasure hunter named Professor Shelly Oberon (Vanessa Hudgens) and her team.

As Sean and Hank delve deeper into the heart of Jumanji, they uncover a dark secret about the island's past and the true purpose of Dr. Anderson's expedition. They must use all their skills and ingenuity to outwit their enemies, overcome treacherous challenges, and find Sean's father before it's too late.

In the end, Sean and Hank successfully locate Dr. Anderson, who has been trapped in a mysterious curse that has been keeping him on the island for years. With the help of his son, Sean is able to break the curse and free his father from its grasp.

The movie concludes with Sean and Hank returning home, forever changed by their incredible adventure on Jumanji. The film ends on a hopeful note, as Sean reflects on the lessons he learned from his journey and the importance of following his dreams.

Overall, Journey 2: The Mysterious Island is an action-packed adventure that combines stunning visuals, heart-pumping action sequences, and a thrilling storyline. With its talented cast, including Josh Hutcherson and Dwayne Johnson, the movie is sure to delight fans of adventure films and leave them eager for more.

documents.title: G.I. Joe: Retaliation
documents.tagline: Heroes are made in America.
documents.overview: Framed for crimes against the country, the G.I. Joe team is terminated by Presidential order. This forces the G.I. Joes into not only fighting their mortal enemy Cobra; they are forced to contend with threats from within the government that jeopardize their very existence.
documents.plot:
G.I. Joe: Retaliation is a 2013 action film directed by Jon M. Chu and written by Rhett Reese, Paul Wernick, Zech Daley, and Art Marcum. The movie serves as the sequel to G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra (2009) and stars Dwayne Johnson, Channing Tatum, Bruce Willis, and Adrianne Palicki.

The film begins with a flashback sequence showing the events that led to the death of Duke (Channing Tatum), a member of the elite special forces team known as G.I. Joe. The story then jumps forward in time to the present day, where we see Duke's funeral being held. However, it becomes clear that something is amiss when the eulogy is interrupted by a group of masked assassins who kill several high-ranking officials.

The main character, Roadblock (Dwayne Johnson), is introduced as he tries to uncover the truth behind his friend Duke's death. He soon discovers that the event was orchestrated by a mysterious figure known as Cobra Commander (Luke Evans). Roadblock teams up with other G.I. Joe members, including Flint (Djimon Hounsou) and Lady Jaye (Adrianne Palicki), to take down Cobra.

As the story unfolds, we learn that Duke's death is connected to a conspiracy involving the U.S. government and a secret organization known as the "President's Guard." The President's Guard is led by Admiral William Shepherd (Bruce Willis) and is comprised of high-ranking officials who are secretly working with Cobra Commander.

The plot thickens when Roadblock discovers that he has been framed for Duke's murder, and that he is actually being hunted by the very people he is trying to take down. With the help of his G.I. Joe teammates, Roadblock sets out on a mission to clear his name and bring down the President's Guard.

Throughout the film, we see flashbacks of Duke's time with G.I. Joe, as well as his final moments before his death. These scenes provide insight into Duke's character and serve as a reminder of the camaraderie and sacrifice that defines the G.I. Joe team.

The movie culminates in an action-packed showdown between Roadblock and the President's Guard at the White House. In the end, Roadblock is able to clear his name and take down Cobra Commander, but not before realizing that Duke's death was just a small part of a larger conspiracy.

Overall, G.I. Joe: Retaliation is an action-packed film with plenty of twists and turns. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the franchise will likely enjoy the movie's over-the-top action sequences and nostalgic value.

documents.title: The Vow
documents.overview: Happy young married couple Paige and Leo are, well, happy. Then a car accident puts Paige into a life-threatening coma. Upon awakening she has lost the previous five years of memories, including those of her beloved Leo, her wedding, a confusing relationship with her parents, or the ending of her relationship with her ex-fiance. Despite these complications, Leo endeavors to win her heart again and rebuild their marriage.
documents.plot:
Paige Collins and her husband Leo come out of a movie theater on a snowy evening. On their way home, at a stop sign, Paige unbuckles her seatbelt to lean over and kiss Leo. At that very moment, a salt truck rams their car from behind and Paige flies through the windshield. Both of them are rushed to a hospital.
As Leo, in a voice-over, talks about how "moments of impact help in finding who we are," his relationship with Paige is explored – their courtship, engagement, and wedding at the Art Institute of Chicago, all interwoven with the present. Paige is put into an induced coma and later regains consciousness to discover she has lost all of her memories. Paige's parents, Bill and Rita Thornton, learn about this and visit her, meeting Leo for the first time.
Paige does not understand how Leo could be married to her yet not have met her own parents. She finds it even stranger that he does not know either. Nor does Paige understand why she left law school, broke off an engagement with her previous fiancé, Jeremy, and lost contact with her family and friends. Needing evidence of her relationship with Leo, he plays her a voice message as proof. Paige is against the idea of moving back in with her parents, so decides to return to Leo, hoping it will help her regain her lost memories. She is welcomed home with a surprise party thrown by her friends, none of whom she can recall, so she feels overwhelmed.
The next day, Paige ventures out to a café she regularly visited, but loses her way back. Paige calls her mother for help and returns to Leo. That evening, her parents, Bill and Rita, invite the couple to dinner; later, Paige's sister Gwen and her fiancé invite them out to a bar. Leo comes to feel that he doesn't fit in with Paige's family. Paige later meets Jeremy again at the bar. Realizing that she is becoming infatuated with Jeremy, Leo persists in trying to help her regain her memory. Paige secretly meets Jeremy at his office and asks him about their broken engagement. His answer is ambiguous; he is still clearly attracted to her. While Leo gives Paige a tour of her own studio, she suddenly lashes out at him. With Gwen's wedding approaching, Paige decides to stay with her parents. Leo asks Paige out on a date and spends the night with her, but the relationship is further strained when Bill attempts to persuade him to divorce her. When Jeremy begins taunting Leo, he eventually loses his temper and punches Jeremy. Paige rejoins law school and a heartbroken Leo reaches an epiphany that her memory may never return.
At a Trader Joe's, Paige meets Diane, an old friend who is unaware of Paige's amnesia. It's revealed that Diane had an affair with Bill, thus explaining why Paige has been estranged from her family. When Paige angrily confronts Rita about this, she tells Paige that she decided to stay with her father for everything he had done right instead of leaving him for one transgression.

documents.title: Paranormal Activity 3
documents.tagline: It Runs In The Family.
documents.overview: In 1988, young sisters Katie and Kristi befriend an invisible entity who resides in their home.
documents.plot:
Paranormal Activity 3 is a 2011 American supernatural horror film directed by Henry Joost and Ariel Schulman, and written by Christopher Landon. The movie serves as a prequel to the first two films in the series.

The story begins with Katie Featherston's character, Katie, who is now an adult, living in Chicago with her husband, Micah (Mark Fredrichs). They are expecting their first child, but their lives take a dark turn when they start experiencing strange occurrences. The camera work and editing style used in the film are similar to those of the previous two movies.

The main focus of the movie shifts to Katie's childhood, where we see her younger sister, Kristi (Katie Featherston), who is now 13 years old. Kristi has been experiencing terrifying supernatural events since she was a child, and their mother, Andrea (Lauren Bittner), tries to keep it a secret from her husband.

As the story unfolds, we learn that Kristi's experiences are connected to an ancient Native American ritual that took place in their home. The ritual was meant to summon a malevolent spirit, which has been awakened by Kristi's presence. The spirit begins to exert its influence over Kristi, causing her to become increasingly aggressive and violent.

The movie takes a darker turn as the events escalate, and Katie starts to experience similar supernatural occurrences. She becomes convinced that the same entity is responsible for both her sister's and her own experiences. As the tension builds up, Katie tries to uncover the truth behind the ritual and the entity's connection to their family.

In the climax of the movie, Katie discovers a dark secret about her family's past and the true nature of the entity. She realizes that the entity is not just a malevolent spirit but also a manifestation of her own fears and guilt. The movie ends with Katie trying to make amends for her family's past mistakes, while Kristi's fate remains uncertain.

Throughout the film, the camera work and editing style are used to create a sense of unease and tension, making the viewer feel like they are experiencing the events firsthand. The special effects are minimal, relying on suggestion and atmosphere to create the scares.

Overall, Paranormal Activity 3 is a well-crafted horror movie that explores themes of family secrets, guilt, and the supernatural. While it may not be as intense as some other horror movies, it provides a chilling experience for fans of the genre.

documents.title: The Host
documents.tagline: You will be one of us
documents.overview: A parasitic alien soul is injected into the body of Melanie Stryder. Instead of carrying out her race's mission of taking over the Earth, "Wanda" (as she comes to be called) forms a bond with her host and sets out to aid other free humans.
documents.plot: A parasitic alien soul is injected into the body of Melanie Stryder. Instead of carrying out her race's mission of taking over the Earth, "Wanda" (as she comes to be called) forms a bond with her host and sets out to aid other free humans.

documents.title: The Loft
documents.tagline: The right place to do wrong.
documents.overview: For five men, the opportunity to share a penthouse in the city -- in which to carry on extramarital affairs -- is a dream come true, until the dead body of an unknown woman turns up. Realizing that her killer must be one of their group, the men are gripped by paranoia as each one suspects another. Friendships are tested, loyalties are questioned, and marriages crumble while fear and suspicion run rampant.
documents.plot:
Five married men share ownership of an upmarket loft, which they use for discreetly meeting their respective mistresses. When the body of a murdered woman Sarah Deakins is found in that loft, the men begin to suspect each other of having committed the gruesome crime, as they are the only ones with keys to the premises. Through flashbacks, which are intertwined with scenes from the present, the story is unravelled.
The five men are:

Vincent Stevens: architect and designer of the building where the loft is situated. Married to Barbara and father of their children, he initially suggests the five friends use the loft as a private oasis. He is set up by the other men to be accused of the murder.
Dr. Chris Vanowen: a psychiatrist married to Allison and the elder maternal half-brother to siblings Philip and Zoe. He is the most reluctant of the men to the loft idea and the last to accept a key; Chris eventually does so because he is attracted to Anne, who eventually becomes his mistress. Anne warns Chris not to fall in love with her because she is a prostitute, and he gives her his key as proof he does not use the loft with other women.
Luke Seacord: married to Ellie, who is an insulin-dependent diabetic. He discovers the body in the loft and initially calls Vincent and the others over. The police later insinuate that Luke is attracted to Vincent, and it is Luke who records the men's activities in the loft without their knowledge.
Marty Landry: heavy drinker and a conspicuous lecher. He and his wife Mimi separate when a woman Marty slept with on a business trip shows up at their house.
Philip Trauner: half-brother to Chris and recently married to Vicky, the only daughter of a wealthy property developer who is also Philip’s boss. Philip is a drug user who grew up in a dysfunctional household with his abusive father and is very protective of his younger sister Zoe. He warns the other men off from having sex with her.

documents.title: Carjacked
documents.tagline: It's her car. Don't tell her what to do with it.
documents.overview: A single mom and her child are carjacked by a bank robber who has no intention of letting them go.
documents.plot:
Carjacked is a 2011 American thriller directed by John Bonito, whose previous feature was the action film The Marine, from a screenplay by Michael and Sherry Compton. Produced by Hollywood Media Bridge and released direct to video, it stars Maria Bello as Lorraine Burton and Stephen Dorff as Roy, with Connor Hill as Lorraine's young son Chad, Joanna Cassidy as an irascible member of a therapy group. The film runs 89 minutes.

Lorraine is a recently separated single mother with a low-paying job, struggling to make ends meet while raising her ten-year-old son. She buys gas a few dollars at a time, settles for frozen convenience-store snacks instead of pizza, attends group therapy sessions where she is encouraged to stand up for herself, and has to fend off her estranged husband, a soldier, who is seeking sole custody of Chad. One night, during a stop at a gas station, mother and son are carjacked by Roy, a charismatic bank robber on the run, who takes over the car and orders Lorraine to drive toward an uncertain destination, with no intention of letting them go. Much of the story unfolds inside the vehicle as the two adults trade barbs, alternate between moments of uneasy rapport and failed escape attempts, and engage in a power struggle over her and the boy's fate. Lorraine misses several chances to alert others, including at a police roadblock, and resorts to writing her license plate number and a plea for help in a diner restroom and to bouts of reckless driving. In the final stretch, the film turns into an action thriller, as Lorraine, who has finally had enough, takes up a shotgun and the chase ends in a massive pile-up.

Released on DVD in the United States in November 2011, Carjacked received largely negative reviews, with critics complaining that the promising premise and capable leads were wasted on a flat, implausible script. David Nusair of Reel Film Reviews gave it one star out of four, finding no menace or suspense, unconvincing dialogue and a heavy-handed self-empowerment subplot. Jason Rugaard of Movie Mavericks likened it to a lesser version of A Perfect World, praising Dorff's screen presence but faulting the static staging and a laughable script, with action arriving only after an hour. Jim McLennan of Film Blitz considered Bello and Dorff well cast and some of their conversations almost engaging, and enjoyed the outlandish climax, but wished the rest of the film had shared its energy.

documents.title: Tom and Jerry & The Wizard of Oz
documents.original_title: Tom and Jerry & The Wizard of Oz
documents.tagline: They're off to see the Wizard, the wonderful Wizard of Oz!
documents.overview: After a deadly storm, Tom and Jerry find themselves stranded on an unknown island ruled by the evil Wizard of Oz. As they try to find their way back home, they worry for their master Dorothy's safety.
documents.plot:
Tom and Jerry & The Wizard of Oz is a 2011 American animated musical fantasy comedy released direct to video, retelling Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer's 1939 film The Wizard of Oz, itself based on L. Frank Baum's 1900 novel, with the cat and mouse Tom and Jerry and other MGM cartoon characters written into the story and seen from their point of view. Directed by Spike Brandt and Tony Cervone, who also produced, from a script by Gene Grillo, it was made by Warner Bros. Animation and Turner Entertainment, with music by Michael Tavera and Sam Register as executive producer. Film scholar David McGowan has observed that the crossover was only possible because a series of mergers and acquisitions brought both properties under one media conglomerate.

On a Kansas farm, Aunt Em asks Tom and Jerry, here Dorothy Gale's pets alongside her dog Toto, to keep an eye on the girl. When a cyclone strikes, the pair are swept away to the Land of Oz and land on the yellow brick road. From Tuffy, a young Munchkin mouse, they learn that Dorothy and Toto have already set off for the Emerald City, and the three follow. Along the way they save Dorothy and her new companions, the Scarecrow, the Tin Man and the Cowardly Lion, from a rockslide engineered by the Wicked Witch of the West, and run into familiar faces such as Butch and Droopy.

The Wizard agrees to grant the travellers' wishes only if they bring him the Witch's broomstick. At her castle, the Witch's guards corner Dorothy and her friends and the Witch sets the Scarecrow on fire, but Tom, Jerry and Tuffy douse him with a bucket of water that also splashes the Witch, who melts away. When the Wizard then refuses to keep his promise, Jerry spots the man behind the curtain and, with Tom's help, exposes him. Back home in Kansas, no one believes Dorothy's story except Tom and Jerry, who confirm it.

Grey DeLisle voices Dorothy, with Nikki Yanofsky providing her singing voice; Joe Alaskey voices the Wizard, Butch and Droopy, Michael Gough the Scarecrow, Rob Paulsen the Tin Man, Todd Stashwick the Lion, Frances Conroy Aunt Em and Glinda, Laraine Newman the Wicked Witch, Stephen Root Uncle Henry and Kath Soucie Tuffy. Warner Home Video released it on DVD and Blu-ray on 23 August 2011. Common Sense Media gave it three stars out of five, and a sequel, Tom and Jerry: Back to Oz, followed in 2016.

documents.title: Lincoln
documents.tagline: The hours that changed history.
documents.overview: The revealing story of the 16th US President's tumultuous final months in office. In a nation divided by war and the strong winds of change, Lincoln pursues a course of action designed to end the war, unite the country and abolish slavery. With the moral courage and fierce determination to succeed, his choices during this critical moment will change the fate of generations to come.
documents.plot:
Lincoln is a 2012 American historical drama directed and produced by Steven Spielberg, starring Daniel Day-Lewis as President Abraham Lincoln. The screenplay by Tony Kushner was loosely based on Doris Kearns Goodwin's biography Team of Rivals: The Political Genius of Abraham Lincoln. The cast includes Sally Field as Mary Todd Lincoln, David Strathairn as Secretary of State William Seward, Joseph Gordon-Levitt as Robert Lincoln, James Spader, Hal Holbrook and Tommy Lee Jones as Thaddeus Stevens.

The film covers the final months of Lincoln's life, focusing on his campaign in January 1865 to have the House of Representatives pass the Thirteenth Amendment to the Constitution, which would abolish slavery. With the Civil War nearing its end, Lincoln fears that his Emancipation Proclamation, issued as a wartime measure, could be overturned by the courts once peace returns, and that the amendment will be impossible to pass after the Southern states rejoin the Union. He is determined to secure its approval before the war ends.

The amendment needs the support of conservative Republicans and of several Democrats, many of them lame ducks who lost their seats in the 1864 elections. Lincoln agrees to let Francis Preston Blair open peace negotiations with the Confederacy in return for his influence over conservative votes, a risky move because news of peace talks could doom the amendment. With Seward, Lincoln enlists political operatives who offer government jobs to wavering Democrats, while the radical abolitionist Thaddeus Stevens must be persuaded to moderate his views for the sake of victory. At the same time, Lincoln struggles with family tensions, including Mary's grief over the death of their son Willie and his eldest son Robert's desire to enlist.

Spielberg's film is a dialogue-driven portrait of political maneuvering, showing Lincoln as both a moral leader and a shrewd tactician.

Lincoln was released in November 2012 and grossed about 275.3 million dollars worldwide against a 65 million dollar budget. Critics acclaimed it, giving it 90 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes. At the 85th Academy Awards it received twelve nominations, including Best Picture and Best Director, and won Best Production Design and Best Actor for Day-Lewis, his third win in that category.
