documents.title: Barbie: Princess Charm School
documents.tagline: There's a Princess in every girl!
documents.overview: Barbie stars as Blair Willows, a kind-hearted girl who is chosen to attend Princess Charm School: a magical, modern place that teaches dancing, how to have tea parties, and proper princess manners. Blair loves her classes -- as well as the helpful magical sprites and her new friends, Princesses Hadley and Isla. But when royal teacher Dame Devin discovers that Blair looks a lot like the kingdom’s missing princess, she turns Blair’s world upside down to stop her from claiming the throne. Now Blair, Hadley and Delancy must find an enchanted crown to prove Blair’s true identity in this charming and magical princess story!
documents.plot:
Barbie: Princess Charm School is a 2011 computer-animated fantasy film directed by Zeke Norton and written by Elise Allen, produced by Mattel Entertainment under the Barbie Entertainment name together with Rainmaker Entertainment. The twentieth installment in the Barbie film series, it was released on DVD on September 13, 2011, and made its television debut on Nickelodeon two months later. Barbie stars as Blair Willows, an ordinary girl who discovers a hidden royal destiny.

In the kingdom of Gardania, teenage Blair works as a waitress in a small café to help support her adoptive mother and her younger sister, Emily. One day she learns from a television broadcast that she has won the lottery for a scholarship to Princess Charm School, a magical academy where princesses from many kingdoms are educated and where commoners can train as Lady Royals, the advisors to princesses. Emily confesses that she entered Blair's name many times, and their mother encourages her to seize the opportunity.

At the school, Blair is welcomed by a golden retriever named Prince and Headmistress Privet, and is assigned a fairy assistant called Grace. She befriends her roommates, Princess Isla, who mixes electronic music, and the sporty Princess Hadley. She also meets the haughty Dame Devin, sister-in-law of the late queen, and her daughter Delancy, who is due to be crowned ruler of Gardania at graduation. Clumsy and struggling in her classes, Blair improves with the headmistress's help despite repeated sabotage by Devin and Delancy. Exploring the palace, the girls notice Blair's striking resemblance to the late Queen Isabella and come to suspect that she may be the long-lost Princess Sophia, believed to have died with the royal family. Determined to find the legendary crown that glows only for the true heir, Blair and her friends must outwit Dame Devin before the coronation.

The film is a lighthearted fairy tale about friendship, kindness and self-confidence, emphasizing that true royalty comes from character.

Like other entries in the long-running series, Princess Charm School was made for a young audience and distributed primarily on home video, following its DVD debut in September 2011 with a Nickelodeon broadcast that November.

documents.title: You May Not Kiss the Bride
documents.original_title: You May Not Kiss the Bride
documents.tagline: Till honeymoon do us part
documents.overview: An unassuming pet photographer is thrown into serious action, adventure and romance when he's forced to marry a Croatian bride and spend his honeymoon at a remote tropical resort where she is kidnapped.
documents.plot:
Unassuming pet photographer Bryan Lighthouse (Dave Annable) is thrown into a serious action and romance adventure when he is forced to marry Masha Nikitin (Katharine McPhee) to pay a debt to her criminal parents against his will. Masha's father Vlatko (Ken Davitian) marries her to Bryan to get her a green card, under the condition that Bryan cannot touch her. Off to spend their honeymoon at a remote tropical resort somewhere in Tahiti, Masha's former boyfriend Brick (Vinnie Jones), who is in love with her (although she does not return the feeling), follows them.
After Masha catches Bryan dancing with a hotel waitress, she storms off, as it is hinted she hates womanizers. Feeling bad, the waitress Lani (Tia Carrere) suggests Bryan take Masha on a romantic outing, to a secret beach encased by a tropical rainforest to make it up to her. While teasing Bryan at the secret cove, Masha flees into the rainforest and is kidnapped.
Bryan searches for Masha back at the hotel, unaware she has been kidnapped. He then finds that his psychotic assistant, Tonya (Mena Suvari), who is in love with him, has tracked him down to the resort. Tonya has brought condoms and tries to have sex with him. After Bryan informs her that he does not want to have sex with her, Tonya agrees to help find Masha, but tells him that she will one day force him to have sex with her, after trying to have sex with him one more time.
After receiving a call from Masha's kidnappers demanding a ransom, Bryan asks Lani for help. While Bryan, Lani, and Tonya are making plans, Brick storms in and Lani and Tonya escape off the balcony, leaving Bryan to face Brick's wrath. When Brick finds a condom Tonya had brought on the unmade, wrecked bed, he assumes that Bryan had attempted to take Masha's virginity and hits him. Bryan barely escapes, while Brick calls Masha's father back in the USA and informs him of Masha's kidnapping, making it sound as if Bryan had been the kidnapper. Meanwhile, the kidnappers turn out to be two American INS agents Agent Meyers (Howard Bishop) and Agent Ross (Kevin Dunn).
Afterwards Brick tells Masha's father Vlatko about the condom and Bryan's supposed attempt to have sex with Masha, Vlatko becomes enraged and prepares to fly to the island. Lani calls her cousin, Ernesto (Rob Schneider) to help find Masha with his helicopter. A chase scene occurs between Brick and the four heroes (Bryan, Lani, Tonya, and Ernesto) and ends with the group making a hasty escape in Ernesto's helicopter, only to later crash-land by a fishing village. Deciding to rest on a beach at the edge of the village, Ernesto and Tonya kiss passionately, unconcerned of Masha's dire condition, and Lani and Bryan storm off in anger. Alone, Ernesto and Tonya almost have sex in a boat in the grass, but Brick soon shows up and knocks them out, revealing that Brick is in on the kidnapping. Separated, Lani and Bryan obliviously go in separate directions.

documents.overview: Second film of the Mardock Scramble series. Balot and a severely injured Oeufcoque seem to be at the mercy of an obsessed Boiled. Dr. Easter comes to the rescue and the group escapes to "Paradise" where many secrets of Mardock lie and where Balot will need to come to a decision herself about what she will and can do.

documents.title: The Lorax
documents.tagline: Meet the original force of nature.
documents.overview: A 12-year-old boy searches for the one thing that will enable him to win the affection of the girl of his dreams. To find it he must discover the story of the Lorax, the grumpy yet charming creature who fights to protect his world.
documents.plot:
The Lorax is a 2012 American animated musical fantasy comedy film directed by Chris Renaud and Kyle Balda, and produced by Illumination Entertainment. The movie is based on the children's book of the same name by Dr. Seuss.

In the beginning, we are introduced to the beautiful and vibrant forest of Thneedville, where a young boy named Ted (voiced by Zac Efron) lives with his mother. Ted loves to play outside and explore nature, but his mother is more concerned about making money and buying things for him. She buys him a Truffula tree seed, which she hopes will grow into a beautiful Truffula tree.

However, the seed is actually a Truffula tuft, which is a small, colorful tuft that grows on the Truffula trees. Ted plants the tuft in his backyard and takes care of it, but he soon realizes that it's not growing into a real tree. He decides to buy more tufts from the Once-ler (voiced by Ed Helms), who claims they will grow into beautiful Truffula trees.

The Once-ler tells Ted that the only way to make the tufts grow is to chop down all the Truffula trees in the forest and use their tufts to make a product called Thneed. The Once-ler explains that he needs the tufts to make the Thneeds, which are a type of plastic-like material used for various products.

As the story progresses, we see the devastating effects of the Once-ler's actions on the environment and the Truffula trees. The forest becomes barren and polluted, and the creatures that live there begin to disappear. The Lorax (voiced by Danny DeVito), a small, furry creature who speaks up for the environment, tries to stop the Once-ler from chopping down the trees.

The Once-ler ignores the Lorax's warnings and continues to chop down the Truffula trees, using their tufts to make Thneeds. The forest becomes increasingly polluted, and the creatures begin to disappear. Ted realizes that his mother's actions have contributed to the destruction of the forest and decides to take action.

In the end, Ted convinces his mother to stop buying Thneeds and instead focus on taking care of nature. The Once-ler is left alone, surrounded by the remnants of his destructive actions. The Lorax appears one last time, and the Once-ler finally understands the importance of preserving the environment.

The movie ends with a message about the importance of taking care of our planet and respecting the natural world. The Truffula trees begin to grow again, and the forest is restored to its former beauty. Ted and his mother are seen playing in the forest, surrounded by the beautiful Truffula trees, and the Lorax is seen watching over them.

Overall, The Lorax is a heartwarming story about the importance of environmental conservation and the power of individual actions to make a difference.

documents.title: Vamps
documents.tagline: Dating Sucks
documents.overview: The modern-day story focuses on two beautiful young vampires who are living the good nightlife in New York until love enters the picture and each has to make a choice that will jeopardize their immortality.
documents.plot:
Vamps is a 2012 American comedy horror film written and directed by Amy Heckerling. Alicia Silverstone and Krysten Ritter lead a cast that includes Dan Stevens, Richard Lewis, Wallace Shawn, Justin Kirk, Kristen Johnston, Malcolm McDowell and Sigourney Weaver. The story follows two vampires who try to keep up with trends and stay youthful while living without human blood and dealing with the malevolent vampire who created them.

Goody and Stacy are vampires enjoying life in New York City. Goody was turned in 1841 by the vampire Cisserus, and after leaving the man she loved in the 1960s she struggled with her existence until Cisserus turned Stacy in 1992. Goody taught Stacy to live on rat blood and use her new powers, while Stacy helps Goody stay young and fashionable. Goody hides her true age, fearing that Stacy will see her as old. At a vampire support meeting she learns that if their maker, or "stem", Cisserus is killed, they will revert to their human ages. Working as an exterminator at a hospital, Goody meets her former boyfriend Danny for the first time since the 1960s. They reconnect while she pretends to be her own daughter, but Danny discovers the truth when he sees her bite a man to stop a stroke, and she explains that she left so that he could build a life with someone who could grow old with him.

When the government uses the Patriot Act to hunt vampires, Goody devises a plan to alter the records of every vampire in the New York area during a solar eclipse, and the vampires celebrate its success with a party, though Cisserus massacres a restaurant full of people. Stacy begins dating Joey, a college student who turns out to be the son of the vampire hunter Dr. Van Helsing. After seeing Stacy climb down his building before dawn, Joey accepts what she is. Stacy then becomes pregnant and learns that the baby can survive only if she becomes human again, which requires killing Cisserus. With Joey and Van Helsing, the two women kill him. Stacy, now forty, looks much the same, but Goody ages rapidly. Revealing her true age, she visits Times Square with Stacy and Joey to reminisce and crumbles to dust as the sun rises. Years later, Van Helsing plays with Stacy and Joey's daughter, named after Goody, and is amused to see that she has fangs.

The film received a limited theatrical release on November 2, 2012, followed by Blu-ray and DVD editions. Reviews were mixed, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting a 56% approval rating from 18 critics.

documents.title: The Big Year
documents.tagline: Everyone is searching for something.
documents.overview: Three fanatical bird-watchers spend an entire year competing to spot the highest number of species as El Nino sends an extraordinary variety of rare breeds flying up into the U.S., but they quickly discover that there are more important things than coming out on top of the competition.
documents.plot:
The Big Year is a 2011 American comedy directed by David Frankel from a screenplay by Howard Franklin, starring Steve Martin, Jack Black and Owen Wilson, with Rashida Jones and Jim Parsons in supporting roles. It is loosely based on Mark Obmascik's 2004 non-fiction book The Big Year: A Tale of Man, Nature and Fowl Obsession, which chronicled three real birders competing to spot the most bird species in North America in a single calendar year. The film keeps that premise but replaces the real participants with fictional characters.

Three men set out to complete a Big Year. Kenny Bostick, a roofing contractor played by Wilson, holds the existing record of 732 birds and guards it obsessively, even though his wife Jessica had hoped this would be the year they focused on having a child, and his fixation on birding has already cost him two marriages. Brad Harris, played by Black, is a 36-year-old Baltimore computer programmer who can identify almost any bird by its call alone; divorced, living with his parents and stuck in a job he dislikes, he hopes the challenge will give him purpose and earn his father's respect. Stu Preissler, played by Martin, is the founder of a successful Manhattan chemical company who wants to retire, but a pending merger means his two successors keep summoning him back to New York.

Over the course of the year the three criss-cross the continent chasing sightings, while competing with each other and many other birders. Brad and Stu become friends and help one another, and Brad falls for a fellow birder named Ellie. Bostick, meanwhile, uses underhanded tricks to inflate his own count and sabotage his rivals, at the expense of his marriage.

By December, Stu has happily retired and is enjoying his new grandson, Brad has begun a relationship with Ellie, and Bostick finds himself alone after his wife leaves him. When the results are published, Bostick has set a new record of 755 species, with Brad second and Stu fourth. Brad reflects that although Bostick got more birds, he and Stu got more of everything else. The film closes with Brad and Ellie birding together on a rocky coast and Stu hiking in the Rockies with his grandson, while Bostick birds alone in China.

Shot in and around Vancouver in 2010, the film drew mixed reviews, though the three leads were praised, and it was a box-office bomb, grossing about $7.4 million against a $41 million budget.

documents.title: A Cinderella Story: Once Upon a Song
documents.original_title: A Cinderella Story: Once Upon a Song
documents.tagline: Can the girl with a dream voice sing happily ever after?
documents.overview: In this modern telling of the classic tale, aspiring singer Katie Gibbs falls for the new boy at her performing arts high school. But Katie's wicked stepmother and stepsister are scheming to crush her dream before she can sing her way into his heart.
documents.plot:
A Cinderella Story: Once Upon a Song is a 2011 American musical teen comedy film directed by Damon Santostefano, a standalone sequel to Another Cinderella Story (2008) and the third installment in the A Cinderella Story series. Lucy Hale stars as Katie Gibbs, an aspiring singer, with Freddie Stroma as Luke Morgan, Missi Pyle as her stepmother, Gail, Megan Park as her stepsister, Bev, and Matthew Lintz as her stepbrother, Victor. It was released on DVD and digital platforms in September 2011 and premiered on ABC Family in January 2012.

Katie, an orphaned teenager with a beautiful voice, lives with her adoptive family, the Van Ravensways, who treat her as a servant: the shallow Gail, the spoiled Bev and the mischievous Victor. She accepts their mistreatment without complaint, fearing that Gail will send her back to foster care. Gail is the headmistress of the Wellesley Academy of the Arts, where Guy Morgan, the English head of Kensington Records, enrolls his son, Luke. Hoping to change her life, Katie slips her demo CD into Guy's briefcase. Guy asks Luke to produce an upcoming showcase at the academy, though Luke is reluctant to follow in his father's footsteps.

Bev, a terrible singer, is determined to win a recording contract with Guy. When Guy calls to say that he loves the demo, Gail claims that it belongs to Bev and that Katie stole it. Gail, Bev and Victor then scheme to use Katie's voice while Bev lip-syncs, with Victor using his technical skills to manipulate the audio. Meanwhile, Katie and Luke bond over their shared love of music, though Luke does not know that she is the voice he has been searching for. In a nod to the classic fairy tale, Katie attends a costume party in disguise and catches Luke's attention before slipping away, and with the help of her friends, including Victor, who eventually turns against his family's deceit, Katie must find the courage to reveal the truth and claim her voice at the showcase.

The film received negative reviews from the few critics who covered it. Mike McGranaghan of The Aisle Seat gave it one and a half stars out of four, likening it to a feature-length version of tween television shows such as iCarly and Victorious, while The DVD Sleuth rated it one out of two. It was followed by A Cinderella Story: If the Shoe Fits in 2016.

documents.title: God Bless America
documents.tagline: Taking out the trash, one jerk at a time.
documents.overview: Fed up with the cruelty and stupidity of American culture, an unlikely duo goes on a killing spree, killing reality TV stars, bigots and others they find repugnant.
documents.plot:
God Bless America is a 2011 American black comedy film written and directed by Bobcat Goldthwait. Blending political satire with dark humor, it stars Joel Murray as Frank Murdoch, a middle-aged man, and Tara Lynne Barr as Roxy, a teenage girl, who embark on a killing spree after bonding over their shared disgust with what American culture has become in the years after 9/11. The cast also includes Alexie Gilmore, Mackenzie Brooke Smith and Travis Wester.

Frank is an insurance salesman who is sickened by the cruelty and vapidity he sees in television, talk radio and the internet. Divorced, he is kept awake by his neighbors' screaming baby, while his spoiled young daughter Ava lives with his ex-wife. In a single stretch he is fired from his job and told by an indifferent doctor that he has a terminal brain tumor. Watching television that night, he sees a talent show mocking a disabled contestant named Steven Clark and then a reality program about Chloe, a monstrously spoiled teenager. On the verge of suicide, Frank instead steals his neighbor's car, drives to Chloe's school and shoots her. Her classmate Roxanne "Roxy" Harmon witnesses the killing, applauds it and follows Frank to his motel, where she talks him out of killing himself. Insisting that only genuinely awful people should die, the pair go on to murder Chloe's parents and then roam the country targeting rude moviegoers, a man who double-parks, extremist protesters and a right-wing political commentator, while Roxy dreams of escaping with Frank to France. Frank's world shifts when his doctor calls to say the tumor diagnosis was a mix-up with another patient, and again when he learns that Roxy has lied about her troubled home life; her parents are in fact respectable and worried about her. After the two part ways, Frank arms himself with an assault rifle and storms the studio of the talent show, where he takes the audience hostage and delivers a speech about the state of American society as police surround the building.

God Bless America premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 9, 2011, and also screened at South by Southwest, before a video-on-demand release in April 2012 and a theatrical release in May. It holds a 65% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it uneven and somewhat thin but with ideas of primal appeal, and a Metacritic score of 56.

documents.title: Detachment
documents.overview: A chronicle of three weeks in the lives of several high school teachers, administrators and students through the eyes of substitute teacher, Henry Barthes. Henry roams from school to school, imparting modes of knowledge, but never staying long enough to form any semblance of sentient attachment.

documents.title: Goon
documents.tagline: Meet Doug, the nicest guy you'll ever fight.
documents.overview: Doug Glatt, a slacker who discovers he has a talent for brawling is approached by a minor league hockey coach and invited to join the team as the "muscle." Despite the fact that Glatt can't skate his best friend, Pat, convinces him to give it a shot, and Glatt becomes a hero to the team and their fans, until the league's reigning goon becomes threatened by Glatt's success and decides to even the score.
documents.plot:
Doug Glatt is a polite, kind-hearted, but dim-witted bouncer at a local dive bar in the fictional hockey crazed town of Orangetown, Massachusetts. He feels ostracized from society, especially since his father and brother are both highly educated wealthy and successful physicians.
Doug attends a local minor league hockey game with his best friend, Pat, who hosts a public broadcast show recapping weekly hockey highlights called Hot Ice. Pat taunts the visiting team during a fight and one of their players climbs into the stands while shouting out a homophobic slur. Doug, whose brother is gay, steps in and easily beats up the opposing player. The next day, he gets a phone call from the coach of his hometown team Orangetown Assassins, who offers him a tryout to be an enforcer. He gets the position despite being a hilariously bad skater, and trains relentlessly to bring his skills up to par.
Meanwhile, legendary veteran enforcer, Ross "The Boss" Rhea is demoted to the minors after serving a 20-game suspension for slashing an opponent in the head from behind. Three years prior, he hit and concussed the highly skilled prospect Xavier Laflamme, who has had trouble recovering from the incident due to his fear of being hit again.
As a result, Laflamme is still stuck in the minors, playing for the Halifax Highlanders. As Doug's reputation grows, he earns the nickname "Doug the Thug". The head coach of the Assassins tells Doug that his brother, Highlanders' coach Ronnie, wants to hire him to protect Laflamme and be his roommate.
The Highlanders experience success with Doug as their enforcer, and he quickly becomes popular among fans and teammates, much to the disapproval of his parents and Laflamme, who loses ice time and the alternate-captaincy to him. Doug meets Eva, a hockey fan with a penchant for sleeping with players at a bar in Halifax and the two become romantically involved.
With four games left on their schedule, the Highlanders need two wins to secure a playoff spot. On a road game in Quebec, after an opposing player concusses Laflamme with a heavy hit, Doug savagely beats the player unconscious and is suspended for the next game against Rhea and the St. John's Shamrocks.
Doug encounters Rhea at a diner, where Rhea dismisses his belief that he is a hockey player, insisting that they are both "goons", and asserts that fans just want to see them bleed. Though Rhea acknowledges Doug's physical prowess and gives Doug his respect, he warns him that if they ever meet on the ice, he will not hold back. The Highlanders, with Doug suspended and Laflamme hospitalized, lose to the Shamrocks. The aging captain of the Highlanders, an inexperienced fighter, challenges Ross to a fight. Ross offers him a chance to back out but the player declines and quickly loses.
Doug reaches out to Laflamme and promises to always protect him on the ice; the incident touches Laflamme, who reconsiders his animosity towards him.

documents.title: We Bought a Zoo
documents.tagline: A True Zoo Story
documents.overview: Benjamin has lost his wife and, in a bid to start his life over, purchases a large house that has a zoo – welcome news for his daughter, but his son is not happy about it. The zoo is in need of renovation and Benjamin sets about the work with the head keeper and the rest of the staff, but, the zoo soon runs into financial trouble.

documents.title: Special Forces
documents.tagline: Survival. Honor. Sacrifice.
documents.overview: Afghanistan. War correspondent Elsa Casanova is taken hostage by the Taliban. Faced with her imminent execution, a Special Forces unit is dispatched to free her. In some of the world’s most breathtaking yet hostile landscapes, a relentless pursuit begins between her kidnappers who have no intention of letting their prey escape them and a group of soldiers who risk their lives in pursuit of their single aim – to bring her home alive. This strong, independent woman and these men of duty are thrown together and forced to confront situations of great danger that inextricably bind them – emotionally, violently and intimately.
documents.plot:
Special Forces (French: Forces spéciales) is a 2011 French war action film directed by Stéphane Rybojad, starring Diane Kruger, Djimon Hounsou, Benoît Magimel, Denis Ménochet, Mehdi Nebbou, Raphaël Personnaz and Tchéky Karyo. Shot on location in France, Djibouti and Tajikistan, it follows a team of elite French commandos on a desperate hostage-rescue mission on the border between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

Elsa Casanova, a French journalist based in Kabul, publishes an article branding the warlord Zaief "the butcher of Kabul". Her informant Maina warns her that Zaief will seek revenge, and returns to him expecting to be killed in an honour killing. Elsa, refusing to abandon her, tries to save her with the help of her friend and colleague Amen, who has urged her to leave the country. Zaief's men ambush and capture them both. Amen tells Elsa to show no fear, but she breaks down when their friend Salemani is brutally murdered in front of her, and Zaief releases a video of the killing that reaches the French government.

A small team of French special forces operators, drawn mainly from the naval commandos, is sent in to rescue the hostages. They locate Zaief's hideout in Pakistan and witness Maina's execution before freeing Elsa and Amen. But a bullet destroys their radio during the escape, leaving them unable to contact their base or call for extraction. With no other choice, the commandos set out on foot across the mountains toward the Khyber Pass and the Afghan border, pursued relentlessly by Zaief and his gunmen.

The journey becomes a brutal ordeal. In a village where Elsa asks for shelter, one commando is killed by a sniper, and when Zaief's fighters arrive the warlord himself kills Amen. One by one the soldiers fall: the team's marksman dies drawing the enemy away, another succumbs to his wounds in a snowstorm, and a fourth is killed in a further attack, in which the commando Kovax finally kills Zaief after the warlord seizes Elsa as a hostage. An avalanche then strikes the survivors; Kovax saves Elsa and his wounded comrade Tic-Tac but breaks his leg, and the two men persuade Elsa to go on alone. Exhausted, she reaches a road and is rescued, then refuses to be sent home, and Admiral Guezennec carries her to a helicopter to lead the search that finds both men alive.

The film was poorly received by English-language critics, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 15% approval; the Los Angeles Times called it a leaden, video-game-style war film.

documents.title: Born to Race
documents.tagline: Only one can win it all.
documents.overview: Born To Race is the story of Danny Krueger, a rebellious young street racer on a collision course with trouble. After an accident at an illegal street race, he is sent to a small town to live with his estranged father, a washed up NASCAR racer. When Danny decides to enter the NHRA High School Drags, he's forced to seek his father's help in taking down the local hot shot.

documents.title: The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel
documents.tagline: Share the journey. Share the laughter.
documents.overview: British retirees travel to India to take up residence in what they believe is a newly restored hotel. Less luxurious than its advertisements, the Marigold Hotel nevertheless slowly begins to charm in unexpected ways as the residents find new purpose in their old age.
documents.plot:
Several British retirees decide to move to Jaipur, India, to stay in the Best Exotic Marigold Hotel, advertised as an exotic retirement home. Evelyn Greenslade, a widowed housewife, must sell her house to pay off her husband's debts; Graham Dashwood, a High Court judge who lived in Jaipur as a child, abruptly retires to return there; Jean and Douglas Ainslie hope to have an affordable retirement, after investing in their daughter's internet business; Muriel Donnelly, a former housekeeper, decides to have a hip operation in India to avoid waiting times; Madge Hardcastle, after several unsuccessful marriages, searches for new romance overseas; and Norman Cousins, an aging lothario, attempts to relive his youth.
After an eventful journey to Jaipur, the retirees discover the hotel is a dilapidated site, run by the energetic but inept manager, Sonny Kapoor. Sonny's mother moves into the hotel in the hope of convincing her son to invest in a more secure job. Evelyn gets a job at a local call centre, where Sonny's girlfriend Sunaina and her older brother Jay work. Graham takes long walks in search of familiar ground. While Jean hides in the hotel, overwhelmed by the cultural changes, Douglas explores the city. Muriel, at first xenophobic to Indians, comes to appreciate her doctor and her maid Anokhi. Madge joins the Viceroy Club and, surprised to find Norman there, helps him get into a relationship with a woman named Carol.
Graham confides to Evelyn that he is gay, returning to Jaipur to find his long lost Indian lover Manoj, whom he had to leave due to a scandal involving the pair. He, Evelyn, and Douglas eventually find Manoj, who has been happily married for years, but is overjoyed to see Graham again. Some time later, Graham passes away peacefully from an existing heart condition. After Graham's funeral, Evelyn breaks down in Douglas' arms, over her husband's death. Jean, increasingly pessimistic and envious, accuses Douglas of having an affair, only for Douglas to denounce their marriage. Jean then reveals their daughter's business has paid off, and they can return home.
Sonny and Sunaina have a falling out over a misunderstanding when Madge sleeps in Sonny's bedroom, further worsened when Mrs. Kapoor rejects Sunaina. Sonny becomes disheartened and decides to close the hotel. Evelyn encourages Sonny to express his love to Sunaina. Together, they race to the hotel, announcing to Mrs. Kapoor their intention to marry, regardless of her approval. Young Wasim, a hotel employee, reminds Mrs. Kapoor she and her late husband were in a similar situation when they wished to marry against their families' wishes. Moved, Mrs. Kapoor blesses Sonny's marriage.
Muriel, investigating the hotel's accounts, convinces an investor to keep the hotel open and agrees to act as a deputy manager to help Sonny. The residents agree to remain in the hotel, Carol moving in with Norman.

documents.title: The Artist
documents.tagline: A breath of fresh vintage air
documents.overview: Hollywood, 1927: As silent movie star George Valentin wonders if the arrival of talking pictures will cause him to fade into oblivion, he sparks with Peppy Miller, a young dancer set for a big break.
documents.plot:
In 1927, silent film star George Valentin is posing for pictures outside the premiere of his latest hit film when a young woman, Peppy Miller, accidentally bumps into him. Valentin reacts with humor and shows off with Peppy for the cameras. The next day, Peppy is on the front page of Variety with the headline "Who's That Girl?" She capitalizes by auditioning as a dancer and is spotted by Valentin, who insists that she have a part in Kinograph Studios' next production, despite objections from studio boss Al Zimmer. While performing a scene in which they dance together, Valentin and Peppy show great chemistry. With a little guidance from Valentin, who draws a beauty spot on her cheek, Peppy rises through the industry, earning more prominent starring roles.
Two years later, Zimmer announces plans to cease production of silent films at Kinograph Studios, but Valentin is dismissive, insisting that sound is just a fad. In a dream, he begins hearing sounds from his environment (as does the audience) but cannot speak himself. He decides to leave the studio for the chance to produce, finance, and direct his own silent film, Tears of Love. The film opens on the same day as Peppy's new sound film Beauty Spot and the 1929 stock market crash. Valentin's only chance of avoiding bankruptcy is for his film to be a hit. Unfortunately, audiences flock to Peppy's film instead, while only a few people attend Valentin's. With Valentin ruined, his wife, Doris, kicks him out, and he moves into an apartment with his valet/chauffeur, Clifton, and his dog. Peppy quickly becomes the first of several major new Hollywood sound film stars.
Later, the bankrupt Valentin is forced to auction his personal effects, and after realizing he has not paid the loyal Clifton in over a year, gives him his car before firing him. Depressed and drunk, Valentin sets fire to a stack of his old films. As the nitrate film blazes out of control, he is overwhelmed by the smoke and passes out inside the burning house, clutching a single film canister. However, Valentin's dog attracts the help of a nearby policeman, and after being rescued, Valentin is hospitalized for injuries suffered in the fire. Peppy visits the hospital and discovers that the film he rescued is the one with them dancing together. She asks for him to be moved to her house to recuperate. Valentin awakens in a bed at her house to find that Clifton is now working for Peppy. His ego hurt, Valentin shows ingratitude for Peppy having taken him in, prompting Clifton to remind him of his changing luck.
Peppy insists to Zimmer that Valentin co-star in her next film, threatening to quit Kinograph if he does not agree. After Valentin learns that Peppy bought his possessions at auction, he returns in despair to his burnt-out apartment. Peppy arrives and finds that Valentin is about to attempt suicide. She tells him she only wanted to help him. They embrace, and Valentin tells her it is no use; no one wants to hear him speak.

documents.title: Kill List
documents.tagline: Who’s next?
documents.overview: Nearly a year after a botched job, a hitman takes a new assignment with the promise of a big payoff for three killings. What starts off as an easy task soon unravels, sending the killer into the heart of darkness.
documents.plot:
Jay and Gal are two former British soldiers turned hitmen. While Gal is laid-back, Jay is still reeling from a disastrous mission in Kyiv. Despite his wife Shel's urgings, Jay has not obtained full employment, to the point where they are financially broke.
Shel organizes a dinner party, which was joined by Gal and his girlfriend Fiona, a human resources manager. During the party, Gal reveals he has a new job for them, which Jay eventually accepts. Meanwhile, Fiona goes to the toilet, carves a symbol on the back of the bathroom mirror, and collects a tissue with Jay's blood. Jay and Gal meet the client, who has a list of three people he wants killed. The employer unexpectedly cuts Jay's hand and his own, so that the contract is effectively signed in blood.
Their first target, captioned as "The Priest", recognizes Jay and thanks him just before being killed. The second name on the list, "The Librarian", is an archivist who keeps a collection of horrific, sickening videos of an undisclosed nature. Jay is deeply disturbed by the videos and breaks down in tears. As the duo enter the archivist's home, an enraged Jay beats him senseless and tortures him into identifying the videos' creators. As Gal goes to raid the safe, the archivist thanks Jay, who proceeds to savagely beat him to death with a hammer. In the archivist's files, Gal finds a folder on himself and Jay, including details of their Kyiv mission. Although they do not recognize it, the files include the symbol that Fiona carved in Jay's mirror.
Jay insists they kill the archivist's associates. Gal drives them to the location of the creators of the videos, where Jay brutally murders all of them. Gal informs Jay that, from the archivist's safe, he took enough money to cover the contract money. The pair decide to abandon the contract and return home. When his cut hand becomes infected, Jay visits his regular doctor, only to find he has been replaced by another man who will only give him cryptic advice.
Jay and Gal return to their client and offer to find replacements for the last hit. The client refuses and says that both hitmen and their families will be killed if they do not complete the contract. Shel takes their son Sam to the family's cottage for safekeeping while Jay and Gal go back to work.
Their final mark, "The MP", is a Member of Parliament who lives in a mansion. While observing the house, the pair witness a strange ceremony in the woods that culminates in human sacrifice. Jay opens fire with an assault rifle, and the leader of the ceremony presents himself for Jay to execute. He kills the leader and several cultists before the remaining masked members chase the hitmen into an underground complex. They capture and disembowel Gal, forcing Jay to perform a mercy killing on him. Emerging from the tunnels, Jay flees to the family cottage and meets with Shel. When he goes outside, he finds their car tires have been slashed and lit torches have been placed around the nearby field.

documents.title: The Human Centipede 2 (Full Sequence)
documents.tagline: 100% medically INaccurate.
documents.overview: Inspired by the fictional Dr. Heiter, disturbed loner Martin dreams of creating a 12-person centipede and sets out to realize his sick fantasy.
documents.plot:
The Human Centipede 2 (Full Sequence) is a 2011 psychological body horror film written, directed and co-produced by Tom Six, a Dutch and British co-production and the sequel to The Human Centipede (First Sequence) (2009). Shot mostly in black and white, it stars Laurence R. Harvey as a disturbed Londoner obsessed with the first film, with Ashlynn Yennie, who appeared in the original, playing a fictionalised version of herself. The British Board of Film Classification initially refused it a certificate, and it was only released in the UK after extensive cuts.

Martin Lomax is a short, asthmatic and mentally impaired man who works the night shift as a security attendant in an East London car park, where he watches The Human Centipede over and over on his laptop. He lives in a squalid council flat with his cruel mother, who blames him for his father's imprisonment for abusing him as a child. His psychiatrist, Dr. Sebring, behaves inappropriately towards him and keeps him heavily medicated, dismissing his fixation on the film and on his pet centipede as a passing phase linked to his childhood trauma.

Martin's obsession turns into a plan to build his own twelve-person centipede. He rents a run-down warehouse and begins abducting people from the car park and elsewhere, including a young couple, a pregnant woman and her partner, and two drunk young women. When his mother discovers and destroys his scrapbook and tries to get rid of his centipede, he kills her, then lures his hostile neighbour into a trap. He murders Dr. Sebring after spotting him on a security camera and abducts the people with him. His final victim is Ashlynn Yennie herself, whom he lures to London with a fake audition for a Quentin Tarantino film.

With no medical training, Martin assembles his centipede from his crude sketches using hammers, staple guns and duct tape, and several victims die or are left for dead. The film depicts the ensuing torture in graphic, deliberately repellent detail. The pregnant woman revives, flees and escapes by car after giving birth. When the chain breaks apart, Martin kills most of the captives, but Ashlynn turns on him before he fatally wounds her. In a final scene he is back in his tollbooth watching the first film, leaving it unclear how much was real.

The film was widely condemned by critics for its extreme content, holding a 28% Rotten Tomatoes approval rating, and was followed by The Human Centipede 3 (Final Sequence) in 2015.

documents.title: Seeking Justice
documents.tagline: Vengeance always has a price
documents.overview: After his wife is assaulted, a husband enlists the services of a vigilante group to help him settle the score.
documents.plot:
Seeking Justice is a 2011 American thriller film directed by David Michôd and written by Michael Koryta. The movie stars Nicolas Cage, January Jones, and Guy Pearce.

The story begins with Gary Fencik (Nicolas Cage), a former Marine who has just been released from prison after serving time for a crime he did not commit. Gary is struggling to find work and support his family, including his wife Maureen (January Jones) and their young daughter. The situation becomes even more dire when the police inform them that they have lost custody of their child due to Gary's past conviction.

One day, while out on a walk with his daughter, Gary witnesses a brutal rape in progress. He intervenes and saves the victim, but not before she is severely injured. The police are called, and Gary is once again drawn into the justice system. As he tries to navigate this new situation, he becomes fixated on finding the perpetrator.

Gary's investigation leads him to suspect that the rapist may be connected to a wealthy businessman named Robert Segal (Guy Pearce). As Gary delves deeper into the case, he discovers that Segal is involved in some shady dealings and has connections to the police department. Gary becomes convinced that Segal is responsible for the rape and sets out to confront him.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Gary's obsession with finding the perpetrator is not just about justice, but also about redemption and proving himself as a father. The film builds towards a tense confrontation between Gary and Segal, which ultimately leads to a dramatic showdown.

Throughout the movie, Cage delivers a powerful performance as Gary Fencik, bringing depth and nuance to the character's complex emotions. January Jones provides solid support as his wife Maureen, who is struggling to cope with their situation. Guy Pearce brings a sense of smarmy entitlement to his portrayal of Segal, making him a compelling adversary for Gary.

The film's climax is intense and suspenseful, with Gary facing off against Segal in a desperate bid for justice. The ending is both satisfying and haunting, leaving the audience with a lasting impression of Gary's journey and the consequences of his actions.

Overall, Seeking Justice is a gripping thriller that explores themes of redemption, justice, and the complexities of human nature. With strong performances from its cast and a tense, suspenseful plot, it is a compelling watch for fans of the genre.

documents.title: The Grey
documents.tagline: Live or Die on This Day
documents.overview: Following a grueling five-week shift at an Alaskan oil refinery, workers led by sharpshooter John Ottway, are flying home for a much-needed vacation. But a brutal storm causes their plane to crash in the frozen wilderness, and only eight men, including Ottway, survive. As they trek southward toward civilization and safety, Ottway and his companions must battle mortal injuries, the icy elements, and a pack of hungry wolves.
documents.plot:
The Grey is a 2011 American survival drama film directed by Joe Carnahan, not 2012, and produced by Scott Free Productions. Here's a detailed plot summary:

The film follows Ottway (Liam Neeson), a former U.S. Army Ranger who has lost his wife to cancer. He is struggling to cope with the loss and feels disconnected from the world around him.

Ottway is hired as a wolf hunter in Alaska, where he is tasked with killing a pack of gray wolves that have been terrorizing a local rancher's livestock. The rancher, Hugh (Holmes Osborne), is more interested in getting rid of the wolves than in understanding their behavior or habitat.

As Ottway sets out on his mission, he meets Hugh's son, Danny (Ed Harris), who has also lost his wife to cancer and is struggling with his own grief. The two men form an unlikely bond as they embark on a journey through the Alaskan wilderness.

However, things take a turn for the worse when Ottway discovers that the wolves are not just ordinary animals, but are actually being driven out of their natural habitat by human activities such as logging and mining. He also learns that the pack is led by a massive gray wolf named Bear (voiced by Frank Welker).

As Ottway and Danny journey deeper into the wilderness, they face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, harsh weather conditions, and encounters with the wolves. Along the way, Ottway begins to see parallels between his own grief and the struggles of the wolves.

In a dramatic turn of events, Ottway and Danny are forced to flee from the pack after they stumble upon one of their dens. As they try to outrun the wolves, Ottway is gravely injured by Bear's attack.

As Ottway lies dying, he comes to terms with his own mortality and finds a sense of peace in the natural world around him. He also begins to see that the wolves are not just mindless killers, but are actually an integral part of the ecosystem.

In the end, Ottway dies from his injuries, but not before passing on his knowledge and understanding of the wolves to Danny. The film ends with Danny standing alone in the wilderness, surrounded by the very creatures that had brought him closer to healing and finding peace.

Overall, The Grey is a powerful exploration of grief, loss, and the human relationship with nature. Through Ottway's journey, the film shows how even in the darkest moments, there can be a sense of redemption and connection with the world around us.

documents.title: Oslo, August 31st
documents.tagline: Live today. One minute at a time.
documents.overview: One day in the life of Anders, a young recovering drug addict, who takes a brief leave from his treatment center to interview for a job and catch up with old friends in Oslo.
documents.plot:
Anders is a recovering drug addict in an Oslo rehab clinic. On his first opportunity to take an overnight trip from the rehab centre, he meets an old girlfriend and then attempts suicide by filling his pockets with rocks and walking into a lake. Unable to go through with it, he returns to the rehab centre, where he does not mention his suicide attempt in group therapy.
On 30 August, he is given a day's leave to attend a job interview in the city centre. He goes to visit his friend Thomas and his wife Rebecca and their two children. While there, he admits that after meeting his old girlfriend Malin, he felt nothing, and never loved another former girlfriend, Iselin, which Thomas tries to play off. Anders slowly reveals to him that he is having suicidal thoughts. At 34 years of age, he feels he is too old to start over and is unenthused about the interview as an editorial assistant that he is applying for. He sees Thomas as being happy, but Thomas talks about his own difficulties in life including being too tired to maintain passion with his wife, having limited time to focus on his career, and the lack of true friendships as he gets older. As the two part on good terms, Thomas begs Anders not to do anything stupid, while also inviting him to a party later that evening, which is being held by their mutual friend Mirjam.
Anders goes to his job interview, but beforehand calls the girlfriend he was dating while he was on drugs, Iselin, and getting her voicemail, begs her to call him back.
At the job interview, when he is asked about the gaps in his resume, Anders admits to being a former drug addict, causing the interviewer to grow uncomfortable. Anders abruptly ends the interview, taking his application with him and throwing it in the bin.
Following his interview, Anders has plans to meet with his sister, Nina, but is surprised and angry when Nina's girlfriend, Tove, shows up instead, eventually admitting that Nina does not want to see him and finds it difficult he is being let out of rehab. Tove is supposed to go with Anders to the family home, which is being sold to pay for his rehab, but Anders refuses to let her accompany him and takes the keys and leaves alone instead.
Anders goes to Mirjam's party hoping to meet Thomas. Instead, he runs into old friends unaware of his recent sobriety, and quickly breaks it by drinking at the party. The party is Mirjam's birthday and they eventually have a conversation about how difficult Mirjam finds ageing as all her female friends have children and her male friends are dating increasingly younger women. To comfort her, Anders gives her a lingering kiss, which makes things awkward between them. Anders retreats to a room alone and again calls Iselin, leaving a message on her voicemail wondering if she still loves him and hinting that he would like to get back together with her. He then rifles through the coats and purses of the party-goers, stealing money and abruptly leaving when he is caught by Mirjam.

documents.title: Secret of the Wings
documents.tagline: Two Worlds. One Magical Secret.
documents.overview: Tinkerbell wanders into the forbidden Winter woods and meets Periwinkle. Together they learn the secret of their wings and try to unite the warm fairies and the winter fairies to help Pixie Hollow.
documents.plot:
Secret of the Wings is a 2012 animated fantasy film produced by DisneyToon Studios. The movie follows the story of Periwinkle, a young fairy who lives in the kingdom of Pixie Hollow with her friends and family.

Periwinkle is a bit of an outcast among her peers because she has wings that are too small to fly. She longs to soar through the skies like the other fairies but feels inadequate due to her limited abilities. Periwinkle's best friend, Iridessa, tries to reassure her that being different doesn't make her any less special.

One day, a new fairy named Zarina arrives in Pixie Hollow. Zarina is a skilled and powerful fairy from the kingdom of Nyx, where fairies are born with wings that can control the elements. Zarina's arrival sparks tension among the fairies, as some begin to fear her abilities and others are drawn to her power.

Periwinkle becomes fascinated with Zarina and decides to follow her on a journey to learn more about her new friend. Along the way, Periwinkle discovers that Zarina is being forced by her mother, Queen Clarion, to use her powers for evil purposes. Zarina's wings are slowly losing their magic due to her mother's manipulation, and she fears that she will lose herself forever.

As Periwinkle and Zarina spend more time together, they form a strong bond, and Periwinkle helps Zarina to see the error of her ways. Together, they come up with a plan to stop Queen Clarion and break the curse that has been cast over Nyx.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Periwinkle and Zarina face off against Queen Clarion in an epic battle. With the help of their friends, including Iridessa, Fawn, and Rosetta, they manage to defeat the queen and shatter the curse that had been cast over Nyx.

In the end, Zarina's wings are restored to their former glory, and she is able to use her powers for good once again. Periwinkle learns a valuable lesson about embracing her unique qualities and finding strength in her differences. The movie concludes with a heartwarming moment of friendship between Periwinkle and Zarina as they look out at the sunset together.

Overall, Secret of the Wings is a beautifully animated film that explores themes of self-acceptance, friendship, and the power of believing in oneself. With its engaging storyline and lovable characters, it's no wonder this movie has become a beloved favorite among Disney fans.

documents.title: Digimon Adventure: Our War Game
documents.original_title: デジモンアドベンチャー / ぼくらのウォーゲーム
documents.overview: A year after the events of the first season, a virus Digimon called Diaboromon appears and starts attacking the Internet. The children and their Digimon unite once more in order to prevent him from destroying every communications network on the planet.
documents.plot:
Following the return of the DigiDestined from the Digital World, Izzy discovers a corrupted Digimon on the Internet that grows by consuming data. He rushes over to Tai's apartment, where they observe its consumption disrupt computer systems across Japan. Tai and Izzy are contacted by their Digimon partners Agumon and Tentomon from the Digital World; they battle the corrupted Digimon, but are defeated.
With the local PSTN crashed, Tai and Izzy attempt to contact the other DigiDestined by an emergency voicemail system, but most of the DigiDestined are unavailable. Fortunately, they are able to contact Matt and T.K., who are visiting their grandmother in rural Shimane. Matt and T.K.'s Digimon partners Gabumon and Patamon join the fight, but are quickly defeated by the enemy.
The enemy Digimon, having evolved into Diaboromon, creates thousands of duplicates of itself and hacks The Pentagon to launch an LGM-118 Peacekeeper missile aimed at an unknown target. Izzy deduces that Diaboromon is playing a guessing game, where by defeating the original Diaboromon, the missile won't activate its fuse. Upon entering the area with thousands of Diaboromon, WarGreymon and MetalGarurumon are overwhelmed by their attacks, not helped by them being slowed down as a result of thousands of e-mails being sent to Tai and Izzy by other children observing the battle on their computers around the world.
Desperate, Tai and Matt magically enter their computers, and rally their Digimon to jointly evolve into Omnimon and defeat the duplicates. With only mere seconds left until the missile hits, Izzy forwards the thousands of emails to the original Diaboromon, slowing him enough to be defeated by Omnimon. With Diaboromon vanquished, the disarmed missile crashes harmlessly into Tokyo Bay.

documents.title: Oblivion
documents.tagline: Earth is a memory worth fighting for
documents.overview: Jack Harper is one of the last few drone repairmen stationed on Earth. Part of a massive operation to extract vital resources after decades of war with a terrifying threat known as the Scavs, Jack’s mission is nearly complete. His existence is brought crashing down when he rescues a beautiful  stranger from a downed spacecraft. Her arrival triggers a chain of events that  forces him to question everything he knows and puts the fate of humanity in his hands.
documents.plot:
Oblivion is a 2013 science fiction film directed by Joseph Kosinski and written by Josie McClelland, Karl Gajdusek, and Michael DeLuise. The movie stars Tom Cruise as Jack Harper, a repairman who lives on a post-apocalyptic Earth.

The story begins in the year 2177, where humanity has retreated to a generation ship called the Ark, fleeing a catastrophic event known as "The Great War" that devastated the planet. The war was caused by an alien invasion, which wiped out most of human civilization and left behind only a few scattered settlements.

Jack Harper is one of these survivors, living on a floating city called New York, where he works as a repairman for the company that maintains the city's defenses against the alien threat. Jack's life is mundane and lonely, with his only companion being his AI assistant, Sara (Andrea Riseborough).

However, Jack's life takes a dramatic turn when he encounters a mysterious woman named Julia (Olga Kurylenko), who claims to be from the Ark. She reveals that she has been sent to Earth to investigate the alien threat and that she needs Jack's help to complete his mission.

As they journey across the planet, Jack and Julia discover that the aliens have created a massive machine known as "The Oblivion," which is destroying entire cities on Earth in order to harvest their resources. The machine is also creating a rift in space-time, causing time dilation effects that are accelerating the aging process of those who live on Earth.

Jack and Julia soon realize that they are not alone in their quest. A group of rogue soldiers, led by Colonel Spear (Morgan Freeman), are also searching for the Oblivion, but with sinister intentions. The soldiers plan to use the machine's power to gain control over the Ark and rule humanity.

As Jack and Julia navigate through the treacherous landscape, they encounter various obstacles and challenges, including hostile alien creatures and treacherous terrain. Along the way, Jack begins to question his own identity and purpose, as he grapples with the consequences of his actions in the past.

The climax of the movie takes place at the Oblivion's core, where Jack and Julia must confront Colonel Spear and his team. In a thrilling showdown, Jack uses his knowledge of the machine's mechanics to disable it, saving humanity from destruction.

In the end, Jack and Julia succeed in their mission, but not without sacrifices. The movie concludes with Jack returning to New York, where he is welcomed as a hero. However, as he looks out at the city, he realizes that he has been given a new purpose: to protect humanity from the alien threat and ensure its survival.

Overall, Oblivion is a visually stunning film with impressive special effects, but it also explores themes of identity, sacrifice, and redemption in a thought-provoking way.

documents.title: Naruto Shippuden the Movie: Blood Prison
documents.original_title: 劇場版 NARUTO -ナルト- ブラッド・プリズン
documents.overview: After his capture for attempted assassination of the Raikage, leader of Kumogakure, as well as killing Jōnin from Kirigakure and Iwagakure, Naruto is imprisoned in Hōzukijou: A criminal containment facility known as the Blood Prison. Mui, the castle master, uses the ultimate imprisonment technique to steal power from the prisoners, which is when Naruto notices his life has been targeted. Thus begins the battle to uncover the truth behind the mysterious murders and prove Naruto's innocence.
documents.plot:
Naruto Shippuden the Movie: Blood Prison (also titled Naruto the Movie: Blood Prison) is a 2011 Japanese animated action fantasy film based on Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto manga and anime. Directed by Masahiko Murata for Studio Pierrot from a script by Akira Higashiyama, it is the eighth Naruto film and the fifth in the Shippuden era, and it sends its hero into a notorious prison after he is accused of an attempted assassination.

A hooded figure attacks the Fourth Raikage of the Hidden Cloud Village and, when unmasked, appears to be Naruto Uzumaki. Back in the Hidden Leaf, Tsunade announces that Naruto is wanted for the assassination attempt and for killing ninja of other villages, and despite his protests he is sent to Hōzuki Castle, the "Blood Prison" in the Hidden Grass Village. Its warden, Mui, places a seal on him that cripples his chakra, so every escape attempt and every challenge to Mui ends in agony and solitary confinement. Admired by the other inmates, Naruto tries again to flee by sea and is rescued from a whirlpool by Ryūzetsu, a Hidden Grass agent working undercover, who reveals that Mui framed him and sacrificed his own son Muku to the mysterious Box of Ultimate Bliss years earlier. Aided by the scheming inmate Maroi, the pair stage a riot, but Mui captures Naruto and uses his chakra to open the box, wishing for his son's return. A grown Muku emerges, stabs his father and transforms into the demon Satori, which can anticipate its enemies' attacks. Naruto, in Sage Mode, and the toad Gamabunta are overwhelmed until Killer B and Naruto's friends arrive, and Tsunade reveals that the arrest was a ruse to get Naruto inside to destroy the box. Realising Satori reads fears rather than thoughts, Naruto fights it on even terms and, with the dying Mui's help, defeats it with his Rasenshuriken. Muku ends both his father's life and his own, and Ryūzetsu gives her life to revive the mortally wounded Naruto. At her grave he ties on her headband and vows to cherish the life she gave him.

Junko Takeuchi voices Naruto, with Masaki Terasoma as Mui, Mie Sonozaki as Ryūzetsu and Yūichi Nakamura as Muku; the English dub stars Maile Flanagan, Matthew Mercer and Carrie Keranen. Distributed by Toho, it opened in Japan in July 2011 and grossed about ¥800 million. Yusuke Kamiji performed the theme song "Otakebi", and Viz Media released the film in North America on February 18, 2014.

documents.title: Evangelion: 3.0 You Can (Not) Redo
documents.original_title: ヱヴァンゲリヲン新劇場版:Q
documents.tagline: What was destroyed can (not) be rebuilt.
documents.overview: Fourteen years after Third Impact, Shinji Ikari awakens to a world he does not remember. He hasn't aged. Much of Earth is laid in ruins, NERV has been dismantled, and people who he once protected have turned against him. Befriending the enigmatic Kaworu Nagisa, Shinji continues the fight against the angels and realizes the fighting is far from over, even when it could be against his former allies. The characters' struggles continue amidst the battles against the angels and each other, spiraling down to what could inevitably be the end of the world.
documents.plot:
Fourteen years after the worldwide cataclysm called the Third Impact, Asuka Langley Shikinami and Mari Illustrious Makinami, pilots of the Evangelion mecha, retrieve a container from Earth's orbit carrying Evangelion Unit 01 and its pilot Shinji Ikari. When Asuka grabs the container with her Evangelion unit, it releases attack drones. Unit 01 awakens and destroys the drones, then deactivates and descends back to Earth. Kaworu Nagisa watches and says he has been waiting for Shinji.
Salvaged from Unit 01, Shinji is fitted with an explosive choker and sent to Captain Misato Katsuragi, who now leads WILLE, an organization intent on destroying her previous employer NERV, the paramilitary organization that deploys the Evangelion units. As more drones attack, Misato launches the flying battleship Wunder, powered by Unit 01, to destroy them. She warns that Shinji will be killed if he pilots any Evangelion units because of the Third Impact, which has also kept the pilots from aging. The other occupant of Unit 01, Rei Ayanami, was never found.
An Evangelion unit, Mark.09, intercepts the Wunder. Hearing Rei's voice, Shinji escapes with the unit. Rei takes him to the ruined NERV headquarters. Gendo Ikari, Shinji's father and NERV's leader, informs him that he is to pilot a new Evangelion, Unit 13, with Kaworu. Shinji befriends Kaworu as they practice piano duets together, but discovers that Rei is unable to remember anything and only follows orders. Kaworu shows Shinji the ruins of Tokyo 3, explaining that Shinji's awakening of Unit 01 caused the Third Impact. He also reveals that Gendo plans to force humanity's evolution by triggering a mass extinction, removing humanity's individuality and reuniting with his deceased wife Yui Ayanami.
Gendo's assistant Kozo Fuyutsuki invites Shinji to play shogi and reveals that Yui is within Unit 01 as the control system. Rei is one of several clones of Shinji's mother; the Rei who rescued him is only the latest. Shinji is distraught by this. Kaworu removes Shinji's choker and wears it to gain his trust.
Shinji and Kaworu pilot Unit 13 on their mission to use the Spears of Cassius and Longinus, two ancient weapons, to undo the Third Impact; Rei follows in Mark.09. When Unit 13 reaches the body of the alien lifeform Lilith, Kaworu realizes that the spears are not what he expected. Kaworu, Asuka and Mari try stopping Shinji, but Shinji removes the spears. On Gendo's orders, Mark.09 decapitates Mark.06 to release the Twelfth Angel, which is absorbed by Unit 13.
The awakened Unit 13 rises into the sky, starting another cataclysm, the Fourth Impact. Kaworu reveals that as the First Angel, he is now "cast down" to the Thirteenth. Rei loses control of Mark.09, which boards Wunder on its own in an attempt to take control of the ship. Rei ejects from her unit and Asuka blows up her own unit to destroy Mark.09.

documents.title: Red Lights
documents.tagline: How much do you want to believe?
documents.overview: Two investigators of paranormal hoaxes, the veteran Dr. Margaret Matheson and her young assistant, Tom Buckley, study the most varied metaphysical phenomena with the aim of proving their fraudulent origins. Simon Silver, a legendary blind psychic, reappears after an enigmatic absence of 30 years to become the greatest international challenge to both orthodox science and professional sceptics. Tom starts to develop an intense obsession with Silver, whose magnetism becomes stronger with each new manifestation of inexplicable events. As Tom gets closer to Silver, tension mounts, and his worldview is threatened to its core.
