documents.title: Now You See Me
documents.tagline: 4 amazing magicians. 3 impossible heists. 1 billion dollars. This is no illusion.
documents.overview: An FBI agent and an Interpol detective track a team of illusionists who pull off bank heists during their performances and reward their audiences with the money.
documents.plot:
Now You See Me is a 2013 heist thriller film directed by Louis Leterrier and written by Ed Solomon, Boaz Yakin, Edward Ricourt, and Ted Griffin. The movie stars Jesse Eisenberg, Woody Harrelson, Mark Ruffalo, Isla Fisher, Dave Franco, Michael Caine, and Morgan Freeman.

The story begins with a series of high-profile magic shows performed by four street magicians: J. Daniel Atlas (Jesse Eisenberg), Henley Reeves (Isla Fisher), Merritt McKinney (Woody Harrelson), and Jack Wilder (Dave Franco). The group is led by Atlas, who has a mysterious past and a talent for escaping from seemingly impossible situations.

The four magicians are approached by an FBI agent, Dylan Rhodes (Mark Ruffalo), who is tasked with investigating a series of high-stakes heists that have been committed using magic as a distraction. The thief, known only as "FBI Agent Thompson's" nemesis, has stolen millions of dollars from various financial institutions around the world.

As the investigation unfolds, it becomes clear that the magicians are not just ordinary performers but are actually skilled thieves who use their magic skills to commit the heists. They call themselves "The Four Horsemen," and they seem to be always one step ahead of the law.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when the Four Horsemen reveal that they have been working with a mysterious figure known as "Thaddeus Bradley" (Michael Caine), a former magician who has turned to a life of crime. Bradley is revealed to be the mastermind behind the heists, and he uses his knowledge of magic and illusions to manipulate the magicians and keep them in line.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Atlas has a personal connection to Bradley, who was once his mentor. Atlas's past is slowly revealed, showing how he became disillusioned with the world of magic and turned to a life of crime.

The movie builds towards a thrilling climax as the Four Horsemen plan one final heist, which they hope will expose their true identities and bring them to justice. However, things don't go according to plan, and the magicians are forced to use all their skills to escape from the authorities and clear their names.

In the end, Atlas and his team succeed in pulling off a daring escape, but not before revealing that they have been playing a cat-and-mouse game with Bradley all along. The movie ends on a cliffhanger, leaving the audience wondering what will happen next.

Overall, Now You See Me is a thrilling and entertaining movie that combines magic, mystery, and action to create a unique and captivating story.

documents.title: Act of Valor
documents.tagline: The only easy day was yesterday.
documents.overview: When a covert mission to rescue a kidnapped CIA operative uncovers a chilling plot, an elite, highly trained U.S. SEAL team speeds to hotspots around the globe, racing against the clock to stop a deadly terrorist attack.
documents.plot:
Act of Valor is a 2012 American action thriller film directed by Mike McCoy and Scott Waugh, written by Aaron Guzikowski, and produced by Tom Cruise, Doug Liman, and Don Grubbs.

The movie follows the story of two Navy SEALs, Lieutenant Alex Shaw (played by Taylor Kitsch) and Petty Officer Michael "Bible" Stone (played by Alexander Skarsgård), who are part of an elite counter-terrorism unit. The film's narrative is presented in a unique way, as it is framed as a documentary-style film, with the characters' voicesover explaining their actions.

The story begins with Lieutenant Shaw and Petty Officer Stone on a mission to rescue a group of hostages being held by a Mexican cartel leader, Carlos Rueda (played by Efrain Funes). The two SEALs are sent to infiltrate the cartel's hideout in Mexico, where they encounter various obstacles and dangers.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Lieutenant Shaw is on a personal mission to rescue his father, who was kidnapped by the cartel. Petty Officer Stone, on the other hand, is initially hesitant to join the mission, but eventually agrees to help his fellow SEAL.

Throughout the film, the two characters face numerous challenges, including intense firefights with the cartel members and navigating treacherous terrain. Along the way, they also encounter a local Mexican woman, Elena (played by Teresa Perez), who becomes an ally in their mission.

As the story reaches its climax, Lieutenant Shaw and Petty Officer Stone launch a final assault on the cartel's hideout, resulting in a intense and action-packed confrontation with Carlos Rueda. In the end, the two SEALs successfully complete their mission, rescuing the hostages and killing the cartel leader.

Throughout the film, the action sequences are fast-paced and intense, showcasing the skills and training of the Navy SEALs. The movie also explores themes of loyalty, duty, and sacrifice, as Lieutenant Shaw and Petty Officer Stone put themselves in harm's way to complete their mission.

Overall, Act of Valor is an action-packed thrill ride that showcases the bravery and skill of the Navy SEALs. While some critics have argued that the film's narrative is predictable and lacks depth, it remains a thrilling and entertaining watch for fans of action movies.

documents.title: Zombie Apocalypse
documents.tagline: Mankind Survived... But Not Alive.
documents.overview: Months after a zombie plague has wiped out 90 percent of the American population, a small group of survivors fight their way cross-country to a rumored refuge on the island of Catalina.
documents.plot:
Zombie Apocalypse, also released as 2012: Zombie Apocalypse, is a 2011 American zombie horror film produced by The Asylum for the Syfy channel. Directed by Nick Lyon, it stars Ving Rhames, Taryn Manning, Johnny Pacar, Lesley-Ann Brandt and Gary Weeks. It premiered on Syfy on October 29, 2011, and was released on DVD and Blu-ray that December.

Flashbacks explain that in June 2012 a virus known as VM2 was discovered in a woman in France. Within a month most of Europe was infected, and the disease spread around the world, turning its victims into flesh-eating zombies. Six months later, the plague has killed about ninety percent of the population of the United States.

Near Los Angeles, three survivors, Ramona, Billie and Kevin, are searching an auto repair shop for supplies when the noise draws a horde of zombies. Kevin is bitten before another group of survivors, Henry, Julian, Cassie and Mack, arrives to fight off the attackers; Cassie kills Kevin as he begins to turn. The two groups join forces, and Mack reveals that they are heading for Catalina Island, where a survivor camp is said to await anyone who can reach the ferry. On the way, they scavenge a surf shop, are attacked by a fast-moving "runner" zombie, and are forced to kill a stray dog that becomes infected. A supposed safe zone at a high school turns out to be abandoned, and when the gym is suddenly flooded with zombies, Billie is bitten.

The group is split apart in a burning neighborhood. Mack, Julian and Ramona are rescued by a band of archers, Brockton, Myrah and Sarah, while Henry and Cassie continue on alone. Julian is bitten when a zombie bursts out of a portable toilet, and before he can sacrifice himself as a distraction he begins to turn, forcing Mack to kill him. Henry and Cassie collect grenades from an abandoned army post, and an explosion they set off helps the others escape. The groups reunite on the rooftops and fight their way to the docks, where they find supplies and quarantine instructions, but also a pair of infected tigers. Brockton is killed and Henry is bitten, and Cassie grants his request to end his life. In the final scene, the remaining survivors watch as the ferry approaches.

Reviews were mixed to negative. The A.V. Club dismissed it as a dull riff on The Walking Dead, and Dread Central and DVD Talk found it routine, while Starburst considered it a cheap and cheerful genre film with enough good ideas and performances to entertain.

documents.title: Jack Reacher
documents.tagline: The Law Has Limits. He Does Not.
documents.overview: When a gunman takes five lives with six shots, all evidence points to the suspect in custody. On interrogation, the suspect offers up a single note: "Get Jack Reacher!" So begins an extraordinary chase for the truth, pitting Jack Reacher against an unexpected enemy, with a skill for violence and a secret to keep.
documents.plot:
Jack Reacher is a 2012 American action thriller film directed by Christopher McQuarrie and based on the novel of the same name by Lee Child.

The movie begins with Jack Reacher (Tom Cruise), a former Major in the United States Army Military Police Corps, who has been traveling across the country for months. He arrives in Margrave, Georgia, where he meets a local police chief, Captain Will Sword (David Morse). Reacher is initially mistaken for a fugitive and arrested by the police, but he soon proves himself to be an innocent man.

Reacher's attention is drawn to a mysterious case involving a former Army officer, Major General James Greer (Robert Duvall), who has been accused of murdering his wife. The general claims that he was framed and wants Reacher's help in clearing his name. Reacher agrees to assist the general, but soon discovers that there are more complex forces at play.

As Reacher delves deeper into the case, he uncovers a conspiracy involving a corrupt government agent, Captain Susan Turner (Rosamund Pike), who is working with a private military company called Enoch Edwards Inc. The company is involved in a plot to sell advanced military technology to the highest bidder, and they will stop at nothing to achieve their goals.

Reacher's investigation puts him directly in the crosshairs of the conspirators, and he must use his unique skills and experience to stay one step ahead of them. Along the way, he meets a local woman, Joan (Alicia Lively), who becomes his ally and potential love interest.

As the story unfolds, Reacher discovers that Captain Turner is being framed by her own colleagues, including Enoch Edwards Inc.'s CEO, Bob Brown (Richard Jenkins). The conspirators will do anything to silence Reacher and maintain their cover, but he refuses to back down.

The plot thickens as Reacher confronts the masterminds behind the conspiracy. In a thrilling climax, Reacher faces off against Captain Turner's colleagues and takes them down one by one. He also discovers that Major General Greer is alive and well, and that he has been working undercover to gather evidence against the conspirators.

In the end, Reacher exposes the truth about the conspiracy and brings the perpetrators to justice. The movie concludes with Reacher leaving Margrave, ready for his next adventure, as Captain Turner finally gets her due recognition for her bravery and loyalty.

Throughout the film, Tom Cruise delivers a strong performance as Jack Reacher, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The supporting cast, including Robert Duvall and Rosamund Pike, also deliver memorable performances that add to the tension and suspense of the story.

documents.title: Hysteria
documents.tagline: A comedy about the birth of the vibrator in Victorian England.
documents.overview: Two doctors in Victorian England use manual stimulation of female genitalia to cure their patients' ills, leading to the invention of the vibrator.
documents.plot:
Set at the end of 1880, the film depicts the invention of the vibrator. Dr. Mortimer Granville is a young physician who has difficulty with his occupation due to constant arguments over modern medicine. He gets a job assisting Dr. Dalrymple, whose practice specializes in the treatment of "hysteria", a popular diagnosis for women of that time. Medical practitioners like Dr. Dalrymple tried to manage hysteria by massaging the genital area, decently covered under a curtain, to elicit "paroxysmal convulsions", without recognizing that they were inducing orgasms. Granville meets Dr. Dalrymple's daughters, Emily, and her older sister Charlotte – a premodern feminist who runs a settlement house in a poor section of East London.
Granville seems to be good at massaging and getting a sizeable following, while at the same time, Dr. Dalrymple suggests he might eventually take over the business and marry Emily. One night after work, Charlotte comes in with her friend Fannie, who has broken her ankle. After he helps treat her, Dalrymple forbids Granville from offering any future assistance to Charlotte, hoping to dissuade her from her work in the slums. Meanwhile, the increased clientele at the practice is hard on Granville, and his hand musculature is unable to keep up with the task; an attack of cramp results in his dismissal. Fortunately, his friend, Lord Edmund St. John-Smythe, has developed an electrical feather duster, and its vibrations give Dr. Granville the idea of modifying the gadget for use as an electric massager. After successfully using it on the Dalrymple's maid Molly, he persuades Dr. Dalrymple to try the device on his patients, resulting in massive success. Mortimer and Emily then become engaged, while Charlotte struggles with supporting the welfare house.
At the engagement party, Charlotte is arrested while protecting Fannie from a police officer. Emily and Dr. Dalrymple urge Granville to testify at her trial that she is hysterical in order to prevent her from being sent to prison. During the trial, the prosecutor recommends that Charlotte be sent to a sanatorium and be forced to undergo a hysterectomy. As Mortimer speaks, he explains that the symptoms of hysteria are too common to be regarded as a mental illness and that he himself believes that Charlotte is the most generous and caring person he knows. The judge agrees with Mortimer's argument, and Charlotte is sentenced to just thirty days in prison for her assault on the policeman.
Emily decides to end her engagement with Granville after realising her only motive was to please her father. The vibrator now enters the stage as a medical device for to treat the condition, reducing treatment time while greatly increasing customer satisfaction. The royalties from its sale result in independent wealth for Granville, who has fallen in love with Charlotte. Pledging to use some of his wealth to establish a clinic at her settlement house, he proposes marriage to Charlotte and she accepts.

documents.title: The Sorcerer and the White Snake
documents.overview: The Sorcerer and the White Snake is an ancient Chinese fable about a woman demon who falls in love with a mortal is brought to life through the latest advances in CGI and action techniques.
documents.plot:
The Sorcerer and the White Snake, previously known as It's Love and Madame White Snake, is a 2011 Chinese-Hong Kong action fantasy film directed by Ching Siu-tung and starring Jet Li as the Buddhist abbot Fahai. Based on the Chinese folk tale Legend of the White Snake, it co-stars Raymond Lam as the herbalist Xu Xian, Eva Huang as the White Snake Susu, Charlene Choi as the Green Snake Qingqing and Wen Zhang as Fahai's apprentice Neng Ren, with Vivian Hsu, Miriam Yeung and Chapman To in supporting roles.

Abbot Fahai and his young apprentice Neng Ren travel the land subduing demons and imprisoning them in the Lei Feng Pagoda, as they do after capturing an ice harpy on a mountaintop. On another mountain, two snake spirits, Susu and her sister Qingqing, watch a young herbalist, Xu Xian, gathering herbs. When Qingqing frightens him into a lake, Susu takes human form and saves him by breathing her own life essence into him with a kiss. Enchanted by the encounter, Susu follows Xu Xian to the city, where the two fall in love and marry, while he remains unaware that his bride is a snake demon.

Meanwhile, during a fight with bat demons, Neng Ren is bitten and begins turning into a bat demon himself. Fleeing his master, he is befriended by the playful Qingqing and discovers that he has kept his human feelings despite his transformation. Fahai, who believes that humans and demons cannot coexist, becomes suspicious of Susu and gives Xu Xian a dagger capable of killing demons. When Fahai sets out to expose Susu's true nature, she risks everything to protect Xu Xian and their love, defying the abbot in a spectacular confrontation between demon magic and Buddhist power.

The film reinterprets the classic legend as a romantic fantasy about love between humans and spirits, using extensive computer-generated effects and wire-work martial arts.

The film was shot in 3-D and was screened out of competition at the 68th Venice International Film Festival on 3 September 2011. It was released in mainland China on 28 September 2011 and in Hong Kong the following day.

documents.title: The Phantom of the Opera at the Royal Albert Hall
documents.original_title: The Phantom of the Opera at the Royal Albert Hall
documents.tagline: The 25th anniversary of the first public performance of Phantom of the Opera.
documents.overview: A disfigured musical genius, hidden away in the Paris Opera House, terrorises the opera company for the unwitting benefit of a young protégée whom he trains and loves. The 25th anniversary of the first public performance of Phantom of the Opera was celebrated with a grand performance at the Royal Albert Hall in London.
documents.plot:
The Phantom of the Opera at the Royal Albert Hall is a 2011 British concert film of Andrew Lloyd Webber's 1986 stage musical, itself based on Gaston Leroux's 1910 novel. Staged in full to mark the show's 25th anniversary, it stars Ramin Karimloo as the Phantom, Sierra Boggess as Christine Daaé and Hadley Fraser as Raoul, Vicomte de Chagny, with Wendy Ferguson as Carlotta, Liz Robertson as Madame Giry and Daisy Maywood as Meg Giry.

At an auction in Paris in 1905, Raoul buys a music box as a restored chandelier recalls "the strange affair of the Phantom of the Opera". In 1881, as new managers take over the Opéra Populaire, a falling backdrop sends the prima donna Carlotta storming out, and young Christine, secretly tutored by an unseen "Angel of Music", triumphs in her place, catching the eye of her childhood friend Raoul, the company's new patron. The masked Phantom reveals himself as her teacher and leads her through her mirror to his lair across an underground lake, where she unmasks him in curiosity before he returns her to the theater. When the managers defy his demand that Christine take the lead in Il Muto, he reduces Carlotta's voice to a croak and hangs the stagehand Joseph Buquet. On the roof, Raoul and Christine pledge their love, and the eavesdropping Phantom brings down the chandelier in revenge.

Six months later, at a masked ball, the Phantom orders the company to stage his opera Don Juan Triumphant with Christine, now secretly engaged to Raoul, in the lead, and Madame Giry reveals that he is a disfigured prodigy who escaped from a traveling fair. Raoul plans to trap him at the premiere; Christine, torn, visits her father's grave, where the Phantom nearly bewitches her before Raoul intervenes. During the performance the Phantom takes the place of Piangi, who is found strangled, and Christine unmasks him before the audience. He carries her to his lair and threatens to kill the captive Raoul unless she stays, but her compassionate kiss moves him to free them both, and when the mob arrives, Meg finds only his mask.

Three performances were filmed on October 1 and 2, 2011, the last broadcast live to cinemas worldwide, and footage from all three was edited for release. In a grand finale, Lloyd Webber brought out the original creative team and London cast, including Michael Crawford and Sarah Brightman, who sang the title song with four former Phantoms. Home video releases followed in Britain in November 2011 and North America in February 2012.

documents.title: The Expendables 2
documents.tagline: Back for War.
documents.overview: Mr. Church reunites the Expendables for what should be an easy paycheck, but when one of their men is murdered on the job, their quest for revenge puts them deep in enemy territory and up against an unexpected threat.
documents.plot:
The Expendables 2 is a 2012 action film directed by Simon West and written by Richard Wenk. The movie stars Sylvester Stallone, Jason Statham, Jet Li, Dolph Lundgren, Randy Couture, Bruce Willis, and Arnold Schwarzenegger.

The story begins with Barney Ross (Sylvester Stallone), the leader of a group of elite mercenaries known as The Expendables, who are hired by a wealthy businessman named Mr. Smith (Samuel L. Jackson) to take down a ruthless dictator named Medivac (Jean-Claude Van Damme). However, things take a turn when Ross discovers that Medivac is actually working for a powerful arms dealer named Mr. Church (Arnold Schwarzenegger), who has been secretly manipulating the situation to further his own interests.

As The Expendables embark on their mission, they are joined by new recruits including Billy Ray Lynch (Randy Couture) and Lee Christmas (Jason Statham). However, things quickly go awry when the team discovers that Medivac is not just a simple dictator, but a complex character with his own motivations and backstory.

Throughout the movie, The Expendables face off against a series of formidable opponents, including Medivac's henchmen and Church's deadly mercenaries. Along the way, Ross must also confront his own demons and make difficult choices that will impact the fate of his team.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Mr. Church is not just a simple arms dealer, but a mastermind who has been manipulating events from behind the scenes. He reveals that he has been using Medivac to further his own agenda, which involves selling advanced military technology to the highest bidder.

In the end, The Expendables must use all their skills and resources to take down Mr. Church and his minions. The movie culminates in an epic showdown between Ross and Church, with the fate of the world hanging in the balance.

The Expendables 2 received mixed reviews from critics, but was a commercial success, grossing over $285 million worldwide. Despite its flaws, the movie delivered on its promise of high-octane action and explosive set pieces, making it a must-see for fans of the genre.

documents.title: 12 Years a Slave
documents.tagline: The extraordinary true story of Solomon Northup
documents.overview: In the pre-Civil War United States, Solomon Northup, a free black man from upstate New York, is abducted and sold into slavery. Facing cruelty as well as unexpected kindnesses Solomon struggles not only to stay alive, but to retain his dignity. In the twelfth year of his unforgettable odyssey, Solomon’s chance meeting with a Canadian abolitionist will forever alter his life.

documents.title: Percy Jackson: Sea of Monsters
documents.tagline: Where There Are Gods, There Are Monsters.
documents.overview: In their quest to confront the ultimate evil, Percy and his friends battle swarms of mythical creatures to find the mythical Golden Fleece and to stop an ancient evil from rising.
documents.plot:
Percy Jackson: Sea of Monsters is a 2013 fantasy adventure directed by Thor Freudenthal and written by Marc Guggenheim, adapted from Rick Riordan's 2006 novel The Sea of Monsters. A sequel to Percy Jackson & the Olympians: The Lightning Thief (2010), it stars Logan Lerman as the demigod son of Poseidon, with Alexandra Daddario as Annabeth Chase, Brandon T. Jackson as the satyr Grover Underwood, Douglas Smith as Tyson, Leven Rambin as Clarisse La Rue, Jake Abel as Luke Castellan, and Stanley Tucci and Nathan Fillion as the gods Dionysus and Hermes.

Years earlier, Zeus's daughter Thalia gave her life to save her friends from monsters and was transformed into a tree whose magic shields Camp Half-Blood. Now Percy, mocked as a one-quest wonder by the camp bully Clarisse, meets Tyson, a young Cyclops who turns out to be his half-brother. When the tree is found to have been poisoned by the treacherous Luke and the barrier begins to fail, Annabeth proposes retrieving the Golden Fleece, which can heal it and which Grover senses lies across the Sea of Monsters, the place humans call the Bermuda Triangle. The camp director, Mr. D, gives the quest to Clarisse instead, while an oracle warns of a prophecy that a child of one of the three eldest gods will either save or destroy Olympus, possibly meaning Percy.

Percy, Annabeth, Grover and Tyson set off anyway. After a ride in a taxi driven by the Graeae, Luke's followers seize Grover, and the friends end up captive on Luke's yacht, where he reveals his plan to use the Fleece to revive the Titan Kronos. They escape, are swallowed with Clarisse's ship by Charybdis, blast their way free and land on the Florida coast at the lair of the Cyclops Polyphemus, where they rescue Grover and seize the Fleece. Luke ambushes them and starts raising Kronos, but Percy defeats the Titan with his sword; Annabeth, killed by the Manticore, is revived by the Fleece. Back at camp, the Fleece heals the tree and restores Thalia to life, so the prophecy may refer to her.

Filming began in April 2012 in British Columbia and New Orleans. Released on August 7, 2013, the film grossed about $202 million worldwide, but critics were lukewarm: Rotten Tomatoes gave it 42% approval, Metacritic 39, and CinemaScore audiences a "B+".

documents.title: Thor: The Dark World
documents.tagline: Delve into the darkness
documents.overview: Thor fights to restore order across the cosmos… but an ancient race led by the vengeful Malekith returns to plunge the universe back into darkness. Faced with an enemy that even Odin and Asgard cannot withstand, Thor must embark on his most perilous and personal journey yet, one that will reunite him with Jane Foster and force him to sacrifice everything to save us all.
documents.plot:
Thor: The Dark World is a 2013 superhero film directed by Alan Taylor and produced by Kevin Feige. The movie is the sequel to Thor (2011) and the eighth film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU).

The story begins with Thor (Chris Hemsworth), the crown prince of Asgard, who has been imprisoned on Earth for 12 months as punishment for his actions during the events of Thor. Meanwhile, Jane Foster (Natalie Portman), a scientist and Thor's love interest, is struggling to cope with her newfound powers as the wielder of Mjolnir, Thor's hammer.

The Dark Elves, led by Malekith (Christopher Eccleston), have returned to Asgard seeking to harness the power of the Aether, a powerful energy source that can be used to destroy entire galaxies. The Dark Elves plan to use the Aether to break free from their prison and conquer the universe.

Thor is freed from his imprisonment and returns to Asgard, where he reunites with his brother Loki (Tom Hiddleston), who has been working with the Dark Elves. However, it becomes clear that Loki's intentions are not entirely pure, and he is struggling with his own morality.

As the story unfolds, Thor and Jane team up with Erik Selvig (Stellan Skarsgård) and Darcy Lewis (Kat Dennings) to stop Malekith and his minions from unleashing the Aether on Asgard. Along the way, they encounter the Warriors Three, a group of Asgardian warriors who are tasked with protecting the realm.

The plot thickens as Thor discovers that Loki is working to prevent the Dark Elves from obtaining the Aether, which would allow them to destroy Asgard and rule over the universe. However, it becomes clear that Loki's actions are motivated by a desire to protect his adopted brother and the people of Asgard.

In the climactic final battle, Thor and his allies face off against Malekith and the Dark Elves. The Aether is unleashed, causing chaos and destruction throughout Asgard. In the end, Thor manages to defeat Malekith and banish the Dark Elves from the realm.

The movie concludes with Loki's redemption arc coming full circle as he sacrifices himself to save his brother and the people of Asgard. Thor and Jane share a moment of intimacy, and the movie ends on a hopeful note, setting the stage for the events of Avengers: Age of Ultron.

Overall, Thor: The Dark World is an action-packed adventure that explores themes of family, loyalty, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has its fans and provides an exciting addition to the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

documents.title: Mad Max: Fury Road
documents.tagline: What a Lovely Day.
documents.overview: An apocalyptic story set in the furthest reaches of our planet, in a stark desert landscape where humanity is broken, and most everyone is crazed fighting for the necessities of life. Within this world exist two rebels on the run who just might be able to restore order.
documents.plot:
Mad Max: Fury Road is an action-adventure film directed by George Miller, released in 2015 by Village Roadshow Pictures. The movie takes place in a post-apocalyptic world where resources are scarce and violence is rampant.

The story begins with Imperator Furiosa (Charlize Theron), a tough and skilled warrior who works for the tyrannical leader Immortan Joe (Hugh Keays-Byrne). Furiosa is tasked with escorting five wives, including the young and innocent Capable (Nicholas Hoult), to a distant location where they will be sacrificed to appease Immortan Joe's followers.

However, Furiosa has other plans. She secretly loads the wives into her vehicle, a heavily modified 1973 Ford Falcon XB GT, and sets out on a journey to escape from Immortan Joe's stronghold. Unbeknownst to Furiosa, she is being pursued by Max Rockatansky (Tom Hardy), a former cop who was captured by Immortan Joe's followers and forced to participate in the tyrant's brutal games.

As Furiosa and her wives flee across the desert, they are ambushed by Immortan Joe's gang. In the ensuing battle, Furiosa kills several of the gang members and escapes with the wives. Max, who has been watching from a distance, decides to join forces with Furiosa, and together they embark on a perilous journey to take down Immortan Joe.

The duo faces numerous challenges as they navigate through the treacherous landscape, including treacherous terrain, deadly creatures, and rival factions vying for power. Along the way, Max and Furiosa develop a complex and intense relationship, with Max struggling to reconcile his past traumas with his growing feelings for Furiosa.

As they near Immortan Joe's stronghold, Max and Furiosa hatch a plan to infiltrate the fortress and take down the tyrant. The final confrontation is intense and brutal, with Max and Furiosa facing off against Immortan Joe and his followers in a desperate bid for survival.

In the end, Max and Furiosa succeed in defeating Immortan Joe, but not without great cost. The movie ends with Max and Furiosa driving away from the stronghold, ready to face an uncertain future together. The film's climax is both exhilarating and emotionally resonant, leaving the audience on the edge of their seats as they wonder what will become of these two complex and fascinating characters.

Throughout the movie, George Miller's direction is masterful, using a combination of stunning stunts, breathtaking cinematography, and a pulsating score to create an immersive and thrilling experience. The cast delivers outstanding performances, with Charlize Theron and Tom Hardy delivering standout roles as Furiosa and Max.

Overall, Mad Max: Fury Road is a gripping and visually stunning film that explores themes of survival, redemption, and the power of human connection in the face of overwhelming adversity.

documents.title: The Devil Inside
documents.tagline: No soul is safe.
documents.overview: In Italy, a woman becomes involved in a series of unauthorized exorcisms during her mission to discover what happened to her mother, who allegedly murdered three people during her own exorcism.
documents.plot:
The Devil Inside is a 2012 American supernatural horror film directed by William Brent Bell, who co-wrote it with Matthew Peterman. Presented as found footage, it stars Fernanda Andrade as Isabella Rossi, a woman drawn into a series of exorcisms while trying to understand why her mother killed three people, with Simon Quarterman and Evan Helmuth as the priests Ben Rawlings and David Keane.

On October 30, 1989, Maria Rossi killed three people during an exorcism performed on her, and has since been held in a church psychiatric hospital in Rome. Her daughter, Isabella, learned of the killings from her father, who died three days after telling her. Twenty years later, Isabella is making a documentary about exorcism with filmmaker Michael Schaefer and travels to Rome to visit her mother, meeting priests Ben and David, who perform unauthorized exorcisms. Maria speaks in shifting accents and bears inverted crosses carved into her skin. She tells Isabella that killing a child is against God's will, seemingly alluding to an abortion her mother could not have known about.

The priests take her to the exorcism of a young woman, Rosalita, who calls Isabella by name and attacks the crew. During an exorcism of Maria, she taunts Ben about his past, and the ritual fails, but she appears to pass demons on to David and Isabella. Ben finds that four demons speak through Maria at once. While performing a baptism, David begins forcing the infant under the holy water before collapsing, and Ben later finds him at home with his forearms covered in blood, as Maria's had been. When police arrive, David seizes an officer's gun and, unable to finish reciting the Lord's Prayer, shoots himself. Isabella has a seizure and in the hospital slashes a nurse's throat. As Ben and Michael drive her to seek help, she breathes into Michael's mouth, possessing him, and he steers into oncoming traffic, killing himself and Ben, while Isabella vanishes from the wreck. A closing title says the case remains unresolved.

Peterman conceived the idea in 2005 after reading about the Catholic Church's exorcism school. Shot in 2010 in Bucharest and Rome, it was acquired by Paramount's low-budget label Insurge Pictures and released on January 6, 2012. It was not screened for critics, who panned it, giving it 6% on Rotten Tomatoes and 18 on Metacritic, with an F CinemaScore and a widely mocked ending. Even so, it grossed $101.8 million on a $1 million budget.

documents.title: Hotel Transylvania
documents.tagline: Even monsters need a vacation
documents.overview: Welcome to Hotel Transylvania, Dracula's lavish five-stake resort, where monsters and their families can live it up and no humans are allowed. One special weekend, Dracula has invited all his best friends to celebrate his beloved daughter Mavis's 118th birthday. For Dracula catering to all of these legendary monsters is no problem but the party really starts when one ordinary guy stumbles into the hotel and changes everything!
documents.plot:
Hotel Transylvania is a 3D computer-animated comedy-horror film directed by Genndy Tartakovsky and produced by Sony Pictures Animation. The movie was released on September 21, 2012.

In the beginning of the story, Count Dracula (voiced by Adam Sandler) has grown tired of his solitary life as a vampire. He longs for companionship and decides to open a hotel specifically designed for monsters from all over the world. The hotel is called Hotel Transylvania, and it's a place where creatures of the night can live in peace without humans knowing about them.

The story revolves around Jonathan (voiced by Andy Samberg), a human who accidentally stumbles upon the hotel while on a road trip with his friend Mavis (voiced by Selena Gomez). Unbeknownst to Jonathan, he is the son of Van Helsing (voiced by Jon Lovitz), a famous vampire hunter.

As Jonathan and Mavis spend more time together, they develop feelings for each other. However, their love is threatened when Dracula discovers that Jonathan is not just any ordinary human but the son of his arch-nemesis. The Count tries to keep Jonathan away from Mavis, fearing that he will be killed by Van Helsing.

Meanwhile, a group of humans, led by Frankenstein's monster (voiced by Kevin James), werewolves (voiced by David Spade and Steve Buscemi), and other creatures, arrive at the hotel for a monster convention. However, things take a turn when an army of human hunters, led by Van Helsing, arrives at the hotel to destroy all the monsters.

As the humans and monsters clash, Jonathan and Mavis must work together to stop the villains and save their love. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about acceptance, understanding, and the importance of being true to oneself.

In the end, Jonathan and Mavis confess their love for each other, and Dracula finally accepts that his daughter has found someone who truly loves her for who she is. The movie ends with a grand monster party, where all the creatures come together in peace and harmony.

Hotel Transylvania was well-received by critics and audiences alike, praised for its witty humor, lovable characters, and positive message about acceptance and inclusivity. The movie spawned two sequels, Hotel Transylvania 2 (2015) and Hotel Transylvania 3: Summer Vacation (2018), as well as an animated series and a live-action film in development.

documents.title: The Dictator
documents.tagline: Make way for Aladeen.
documents.overview: The heroic story of a dictator who risks his life to ensure that democracy would never come to the country he so lovingly oppressed.
documents.plot:
The Republic of Wadiya, located in the Horn of Africa, has for two decades been ruled by dictator Omar Aladeen. Upon his death, he is succeeded by his immature son, Admiral-General Haffaz Aladeen. Aladeen surrounds himself with female bodyguards, sponsors terrorism, changes many words in the Wadiyan dictionary to "Aladeen", and develops nuclear weapons to be used against Israel. He also refuses to sell Wadiya's oil fields, a promise he made to Omar before his death. After the United Nations Security Council resolves to intervene militarily, Aladeen travels to the Headquarters of the United Nations in New York City to address the council.
Shortly after arriving, Aladeen is kidnapped by Clayton, a bodyguard hired by Aladeen's uncle Tamir Mafraad, whom Omar passed over as successor in favor of Aladeen. Tamir then replaces Aladeen with a decoy; a very dim-witted shepherd named Efawadh whom he intends to manipulate into signing a document democratizing Wadiya while opening up the oil fields to foreign interests. Aladeen escapes after Clayton accidentally burns himself to death in a failed torture attempt. When Clayton's burnt corpse is discovered, Tamir thinks that Aladeen has been killed. Meanwhile, Aladeen is practically unrecognizable, as Clayton has shaved off his beard.
Wandering through New York City in civilian clothes, Aladeen assumes the false identity of "Allison Burgers" and encounters Zoey, a human rights activist who offers him a job at her progressive, alternative-lifestyle cooperative. Aladeen refuses the offer and encounters Nadal, the former chief of Wadiya's nuclear weapons programme, whom Aladeen thought he had previously executed over an argument about the missile design. Aladeen follows him to New York's "Little Wadiya" district, which is populated by refugees from his own country, and enters a restaurant called Death to Aladeen. Aladeen recognizes some of the patrons as people he had ordered to be executed. Aladeen's true identity is almost uncovered but Nadal saves him. Nadal reveals that Aladeen has never executed anybody, as all the people who Aladeen had been ordered to be executed are simply sent into exile to the United States. Nadal agrees to help Aladeen regain his power, on the condition that Aladeen makes him head of Wadiya's nuclear programme again. Aladeen later accepts Zoey's job offer, as she is catering at the hotel where the signing will occur. Aladeen grows closer to Zoey and eventually falls in love with her. While turning around Zoey's struggling business, Aladeen begins imposing strict schedules on everyone, forming a personality cult around Zoey and intimidating an inspector into giving the store a good review.
However, Aladeen's relationship with Zoey becomes strained after he decides to reveal his true self to her; she cannot love a man who was so brutal to his people.

documents.title: What to Expect When You're Expecting
documents.original_title: What to Expect When You're Expecting
documents.tagline: It's too late to pull out now
documents.overview: Challenges of impending parenthood turn the lives of five couples upside down. Two celebrities are unprepared for the surprise demands of pregnancy; hormones wreak havoc on a baby-crazy author, while her husband tries not to be outdone by his father, who's expecting twins with his young trophy wife; a photographer's husband isn't sure about his wife's adoption plans; a one-time hook-up results in a surprise pregnancy for rival food-truck owners.

documents.title: Justice League: Doom
documents.tagline: The end of justice.
documents.overview: An adaptation of Mark Waid's "Tower of Babel" story from the JLA comic. Vandal Savage steals confidential files Batman has compiled on the members of the Justice League, and learns all their weaknesses.
documents.plot:
Justice League: Doom is an American animated superhero film of 2012 directed by Lauren Montgomery and written by Dwayne McDuffie, his last script before his death. Loosely based on the 2000 JLA storyline "Tower of Babel" and a standalone sequel to Justice League: Crisis on Two Earths, it was the 13th DC Universe Animated Original Movie. Kevin Conroy voices Batman, Tim Daly Superman, Susan Eisenberg Wonder Woman, Nathan Fillion Green Lantern, Carl Lumbly Martian Manhunter, Michael Rosenbaum the Flash and Phil Morris Vandal Savage, many reprising roles from the earlier animated series.

The immortal Vandal Savage plans to wipe out two thirds of humanity and found a new civilisation. He has Mirror Master steal from the Batcomputer the contingency plans Batman devised to neutralise his teammates should they go rogue, alters them to be lethal, and recruits Cheetah, Star Sapphire, Metallo, Bane, Mirror Master and Ma'alefa'ak as the Legion of Doom. Bane lures Batman to his parents' empty graves and buries him alive in his father's coffin. Martian Manhunter is poisoned at his own birthday party and set ablaze with magnesium; Cheetah infects Wonder Woman with nanomachines that make everyone look like Cheetah; Mirror Master straps a bomb to the Flash that will explode if he slows; Star Sapphire breaks Green Lantern's will until he renounces his ring; and Metallo, disguised as a suicidal man on the Daily Planet roof, shoots Superman with a Kryptonite bullet.

Spurred by Bane's taunting recording, Batman escapes, while Cyborg disables Wonder Woman's nanites. Together they save Martian Manhunter, Batman guides the Flash to leave the bomb inside an Arctic iceberg and shows Green Lantern that the hostages he failed were androids, and the heroes cut the bullet from Superman. Using a tracer Batman hid in his files, the League defeats the Legion, but Savage launches a rocket to trigger a devastating solar flare; the heroes use the Hall of Doom's technology to phase the whole planet so that the flare passes harmlessly. Savage is jailed for life, Cyborg joins the team and Batman resigns, telling Superman that the League itself is his plan should Superman ever turn.

Released on home video on 28 February 2012, it earned over $7.5 million in domestic sales, and IGN rated it 7 out of 10, calling it a highly enjoyable ride but a short adaptation.

documents.title: Avatar: The Way of Water
documents.tagline: Return to Pandora.
documents.overview: Set more than a decade after the events of the first film, learn the story of the Sully family (Jake, Neytiri, and their kids), the trouble that follows them, the lengths they go to keep each other safe, the battles they fight to stay alive, and the tragedies they endure.
documents.plot:
Avatar: The Way of Water is a 2022 science fiction epic film directed by James Cameron, produced by Lightstorm Entertainment, and distributed by 20th Century Studios. The film is the sequel to Avatar (2009) and continues the story of Jake Sully (Sam Worthington), a human who infiltrates the Na'vi tribe on Pandora.

The story takes place four years after the events of the first film. Jake has married Neytiri (Zoe Saldana), a Na'vi warrior, and they have three children together. The family lives in an underwater city called Hometree, which is home to the Ikran riders, a group of Na'vi who ride on the backs of giant flying creatures known as ikran.

The human corporation RDA (Resources Development Administration) has returned to Pandora, seeking to mine the planet's valuable minerals. The humans are led by Colonel Miles Quaritch (Stephen Lang), who is determined to capture Jake and his family. However, Jake and Neytiri have formed a strong bond with the Na'vi people, and they refuse to betray them.

As tensions between humans and Na'vi escalate, Jake and his family must navigate the dangers of Pandora's oceanic world. They encounter fierce sea creatures, including giant predators known as the "sea dragons," which are used by the humans to hunt down the Na'vi.

Meanwhile, Jake's children begin to exhibit signs of being "Ikran riders," a rare genetic trait that allows them to bond with the ikran. As they grow older, they must learn to control their abilities and protect themselves from the dangers of Pandora.

The film features stunning visual effects, showcasing the beauty and diversity of Pandora's oceanic world. The action sequences are intense and thrilling, as Jake and his family fight to defend their home against the human threat.

Overall, Avatar: The Way of Water is a visually stunning and emotionally resonant film that expands on the world and characters introduced in the first film. It explores themes of identity, community, and the clash between technology and nature, raising questions about our relationship with the natural world and our place within it.

documents.title: Texas Chainsaw 3D
documents.tagline: Evil wears many faces.
documents.overview: A young woman learns that she has inherited a Texas estate from her deceased grandmother. After embarking on a road trip with friends to uncover her roots, she finds she is the sole owner of a lavish, isolated Victorian mansion. But her newfound wealth comes at a price as she stumbles upon a horror that awaits her in the mansion’s dank cellars.
documents.plot:
Texas Chainsaw 3D is a 2013 American slasher film directed by Marcus Nispel and written by Seth Grahame-Smith. The film serves as a sequel to the original 1974 film, Texas Chain Saw Massacre, and ignores all other films in the franchise.

The story begins with Erin Harson (Juno Temple), a young woman who is on her way to visit her sister, Sarah (Alexandra Daddario), at a family reunion. However, upon arrival, Erin discovers that Sarah has been missing for several days, and she sets out to find her. Along the way, she meets a group of friends, including Morgan (Finn Jones), Matt (Samuel Hunt), and Penny (Jessica McNamee).

As they journey through rural Texas, the group encounters various obstacles, including a run-in with a chainsaw-wielding killer who is revealed to be Leatherface (Toby Sebastian). The group soon discovers that Sarah has been kidnapped by Leatherface and his family, who are cannibals.

The group decides to split up in search of Sarah, but they are eventually picked off one by one by Leatherface and his family. Erin manages to evade the family's clutches for a while, but she is eventually captured and subjected to a series of gruesome tortures.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Erin has a personal connection to Leatherface, who is revealed to be her long-lost brother. The film's plot takes a dark turn as Erin is forced to confront her family's twisted past and the reason behind her brother's descent into madness.

In the end, Erin manages to outsmart Leatherface and his family, but not before she is severely injured. With the help of a mysterious stranger (Michael Biehn), Erin is able to escape and exact revenge on Leatherface, killing him in a bloody confrontation.

Throughout the film, there are several nods to the original Texas Chain Saw Massacre, including a memorable scene where Erin discovers a series of old photographs depicting her family's dark past. The film also features a number of gruesome kills, many of which are reminiscent of the original film.

Overall, Texas Chainsaw 3D is a bloody and intense horror film that pays homage to the original while still managing to stand on its own as a unique entry in the franchise.

documents.title: The Last Stand
documents.tagline: Not in his town. Not on his watch.
documents.overview: Ray Owens is sheriff of the quiet US border town of Sommerton Junction after leaving the LAPD following a bungled operation. Following his escape from the FBI, a notorious drug baron, his gang, and a hostage are heading toward Sommerton Junction where the police are preparing to make a last stand to intercept them before they cross the border. Owens is reluctant to become involved but ultimately joins in with the law enforcement efforts
documents.plot:
After leading an operation gone terribly wrong, former LAPD narcotics detective Ray Owens moves to the small town of Sommerton Junction, Arizona, where he settles down as sheriff of Sommerton County. Commanding his small force of deputies Jerry Bailey, Sarah Torrance, and Mike Figuerola, the invariably minor crimes Owens handles range from the mayor illegally parking his Chevrolet Camaro to eccentric weapons collector Lewis Dinkum firing off guns at slabs of meat with the deputies.
One night, Gabriel Cortez, an international drug lord and race car driver, is broken out of an FBI prisoner transport in Las Vegas and flees in a modified Chevrolet Corvette C6 ZR1, taking Agent Ellen Richards as his hostage as he attempts to reach Mexico at high speeds. His henchmen and mercenaries cover his escape by destroying a large roadblock in Bullhead City, Arizona, and the FBI loses track of him after he tricks an FBI helicopter, frustrating Agent John Bannister, who suspects a mole helped Cortez.
In the early morning, Owens and his deputies conduct a welfare check on local farmer Parsons, who has missed a regular delivery, and learn he has been murdered. Bailey and Torrance search the farm and discover Cortez's henchman Thomas Burrell and his mercenaries, who are assembling a bridge for Cortez to cross the nearby canyon that marks the U.S.–Mexico border. Owens, alerted to Cortez's approach by Bannister warning law enforcement agencies along the border, tries to order Bailey and Torrance to fall back, but the mercenaries open fire; Owens and Figuerola rescue them, but Bailey is mortally wounded and dies in their retreat.
As Owens and his deputies regroup at the sheriff's station, Bannister dispatches a SWAT team to secure Sommerton Junction, but Cortez outmaneuvers them and forces their vehicles to crash. With no help that could arrive in time before Cortez's arrival, and Burrell and his men preparing to clear out the town by force, Owens rallies Torrance and Figuerola and deputizes Frank Martinez, an Iraq War veteran and Torrance's ex who was in jail that night, to help them in Bailey's place.
At daybreak, Owens and his deputies arm themselves with Dinkum's firearm collection and barricade the town's main road to prepare an ambush. When Burrell and his men arrive to clear the way for Cortez, Figuerola opens fire early to save a civilian and is wounded by a sniper. Covered by Torrance and Martinez, Owens and Dinkum use a Vickers machine gun mounted on the back of a school bus to defeat the mercenaries, and Owens kills Burrell after he injures Dinkum. Cortez arrives and throws Agent Richards from his Corvette before fleeing into a corn field, pursued by Owens in the mayor's Camaro, before both collide with a swather. A dazed Cortez reaches the bridge and is met by Owens, who rejects Cortez's bribe offers and engages him in a brutal fight, eventually managing to incapacitate and handcuff Cortez.

documents.title: Chronicle
documents.tagline: What are you capable of?
documents.overview: Three high school students make an incredible discovery, leading to their developing uncanny powers beyond their understanding. As they learn to control their abilities and use them to their advantage, their lives start to spin out of control, and their darker sides begin to take over.
documents.plot:
In Seattle, teenager Andrew Detmer is bullied in school, abused by his alcoholic father Richard, and his mother Karen has cancer. The family struggles with medical debt after Richard loses his firefighter job. Andrew’s only friend is his cousin Matt Garetty. Andrew buys a video camera and begins a video diary of his life.
Matt invites Andrew to a party to help him mingle, but he leaves after his filming causes an altercation with another attendee. Popular student Steve Montgomery asks Andrew to record a large hole he and Matt found in the woods. They go down the hole and find a glowing crystalline object. The object reacts violently, and the camera shorts out.
A few days later, Andrew, Matt, and Steve develop telekinetic abilities. Unable to revisit the hole after authorities close it, they use their powers for pranks, but after Andrew pushes a rude motorist into a lake, the trio agree to Matt's suggestion to exercise restraint when using their powers.
After Steve discovers that the trio can fly, they agree to travel around the world together after graduation, with Andrew especially eager to visit Tibet. Steve persuades Andrew to use his powers for a magic act at the school talent show, impressing their classmates. Andrew enjoys his new popularity at a house party, but the night ends badly when he drunkenly vomits on a classmate he intended to have sex with, and Steve accidentally offends him while trying to lighten the mood.
After discovering Andrew’s hidden camera, Richard confronts him, believing he has squandered money meant for school and for Karen's medical treatments. The confrontation escalates until Andrew loses control and uses his powers against Richard, resulting in a violent altercation that forces him to flee his home. Overwhelmed with emotion, he flies into a thunderstorm, where Steve finds him, having telepathically sensed Andrew's distress. Despite Andrew's desire for solitude, Steve refuses to leave but is struck and killed by lightning.
In the aftermath of the party, Andrew faces social ostracism again. He retaliates against a bully using his telekinetic abilities and begins to see himself as an apex predator—stronger and justified in his aggression. Matt attempts to warn Andrew of the consequences, but their argument escalates into a fight. Andrew overpowers Matt, demanding that he stay out of his life.
Desperate to save his ailing mother, Andrew disguises himself in his father's firefighting gear, using his powers to rob a gang and a gas station. During the latter robbery, an explosion occurs, resulting in Andrew being hospitalized under police custody. Richard visits his hospital room and reveals that Karen died while he was searching for Andrew. Consumed by grief and anger, Richard holds Andrew responsible for her death. Andrew then unleashes his powers, demolishing the hospital room.
Matt, sensing Andrew's turmoil, rushes to the hospital with his girlfriend Casey after learning about the explosion.

documents.title: Jupiter Ascending
documents.tagline: Expand your universe.
documents.overview: In a universe where human genetic material is the most precious commodity, an impoverished young Earth woman becomes the key to strategic maneuvers and internal strife within a powerful dynasty…
documents.plot:
Jupiter Ascending is a 2015 science fiction film written and directed by the Wachowskis and Tom Tykwer, produced by Grant Hill and Lana Wachowski. The movie stars Mila Kunis, Channing Tatum, Eddie Redmayne, Tilda Swinton, and Cate Blanchett.

The story begins in a dystopian future where humans are oppressed by an alien species known as the "Mortals." These Mortals have enslaved humanity, forcing them to live in poverty and servitude. The protagonist, Jupiter Jones (played by Mila Kunis), is a young woman who discovers that she is actually an immortal being from the planet Cukelar, which was destroyed by the Mortals.

Jupiter's life takes a dramatic turn when she meets Balem Abrasax (played by Eddie Redmayne), the son of the powerful and ruthless leader of the Mortals, Stinger Abrasax. Balem reveals to Jupiter that she is the reincarnation of Queen Lyta, an immortal being who was once the queen of Cukelar.

As Jupiter learns more about her past and her true identity, she becomes embroiled in a rebellion against the Mortals. She meets Caine Wise (played by Channing Tatum), a skilled warrior from the planet Cukelar, who is tasked with protecting Jupiter on her journey to reclaim her rightful place as queen.

The plot thickens as Jupiter and Caine embark on a perilous quest to gather allies and resources for their rebellion. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous landscapes, deadly creatures, and rival factions vying for power.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Balem's intentions are not entirely pure. He seeks to use Jupiter's powers to overthrow his father and take control of the Mortals' empire. Meanwhile, Stinger Abrasax is determined to crush the rebellion and maintain his family's grip on power.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the rebels and the Mortals, with Jupiter at its center. In a surprising twist, it is revealed that Balem has been manipulating events from behind the scenes, using Jupiter's powers to further his own ambitions.

In the end, Jupiter must make a choice between her loyalty to Caine and her destiny as queen. With the help of her new allies, she manages to defeat Balem and shatter the Mortals' hold on humanity. However, the film concludes with a sense of uncertainty, leaving the audience wondering about the future of this new world order.

Throughout the movie, the Wachowskis explore themes of identity, power, and rebellion, weaving together elements of science fiction, fantasy, and adventure. While Jupiter Ascending received mixed reviews from critics, it has developed a loyal fan base over the years, particularly among those who appreciate its unique blend of action, drama, and visual spectacle.

documents.title: Black Butterfly
documents.overview: Paul is a down-on-his-luck screenwriter who picks up a drifter and offers him a place to stay. However, when the deranged stranger takes Paul hostage and forces him to write, their unhinged relationship brings buried secrets to light.
documents.plot:
Black Butterfly is a 2017 American thriller directed by Brian Goodman from a screenplay by Marc Frydman and Justin Stanley, based on Papillon Noir, a 2008 French television film directed by Christian Faure. It stars Antonio Banderas, Jonathan Rhys Meyers and Piper Perabo, with Abel Ferrara, Vincent Riotta and Nathalie Rapti Gomez, and was released by Lionsgate Premiere on May 26, 2017.

Paul, a reclusive writer, sits in his remote cabin typing "I'm stuck" over and over. His real-estate agent, Laura, is trying to sell the property, and Paul, whose wife has left him, wants to move away. In town he clashes with an aggressive truck driver, and when the trucker confronts him at a diner, a stranger throws the man out. Paul later picks up the stranger, a drifter named Jack, and offers him a place to stay for a few days finding on the way that the power and communication lines are down. Jack cooks and does odd jobs around the house, but keeps needling Paul about his lack of ideas.

One morning Jack wakes Paul with a knife at his throat and, at gunpoint, makes him a prisoner in his own home, and when Paul writes a few pages of a screenplay, Jack throws them into the fire. Jack makes Paul accept a grocery delivery without raising suspicion, forces him and Laura to sink her car in the pond and shoots the local sheriff, before dragging Laura into another room. Freeing himself and seizing his rifle, Paul thanks Jack for arriving just in time to take the blame for the murders Paul himself has committed, and plants his souvenirs of the killings in Jack's bag. But the rifle is loaded with blanks. Paul wakes handcuffed as FBI agents search the house: Laura and the sheriff are alive and are agents too, and the FBI has been tracking Paul for years for four murders, beginning with his wife. When Paul refuses to reveal where the bodies are, Jack notices that an old photograph shows the farm before the pond existed and realizes where Paul's wife is buried. Paul then wakes on his couch, realizes the whole story was a dream, and types the title "Black Butterfly" on a fresh page.

Banderas plays Paul, Rhys Meyers plays Jack and Perabo plays Laura, with Ferrara as Pat and Riotta as Lieutenant Carcano. Critics were divided, with 40% of the 20 reviews collected by Rotten Tomatoes positive and a Metacritic score of 43, indicating mixed or average reviews.

documents.title: End of Watch
documents.tagline: Every moment of your life they stand watch
documents.overview: Two young officers are marked for death after confiscating a small cache of money and firearms from the members of a notorious cartel during a routine traffic stop.
documents.plot: Two young officers are marked for death after confiscating a small cache of money and firearms from the members of a notorious cartel during a routine traffic stop.

documents.title: Black Gold
documents.overview: On the Arabian Peninsula in the 1930s, two warring leaders come face to face. The victorious Nesib, Emir of Hobeika, lays down his peace terms to rival Amar, Sultan of Salmaah. The two men agree that neither can lay claim to the area of no man’s land between them called The Yellow Belt. In return, Nesib adopts Amar’s two boys Saleeh and Auda as a guarantee against invasion. Twelve years later, Saleeh and Auda have grown into young men. Saleeh, the warrior, itches to escape his gilded cage and return to his father’s land. Auda cares only for books and the pursuit of knowledge. One day, their adopted father Nesib is visited by an American from Texas. He tells the Emir that his land is blessed with oil and promises him riches beyond his wildest imagination. Nesib imagines a realm of infinite possibility, a kingdom with roads, schools and hospitals all paid for by the black gold beneath the barren sand. There is only one problem. The precious oil is located in the Yellow Belt.
documents.plot:
In the early 20th century, Emir Nesib (Antonio Banderas) and Sultan Amar (Mark Strong) end their border war over "The Yellow Belt." Nesib wins, taking Amar's sons as hostages. Ten years later, Thurkettle, an American geologist, discovers oil in the Yellow Belt, violating the peace pact. Nesib modernizes his kingdom but faces opposition from tribes. Saleh, Amar's son, tries to convince Amar to allow oil extraction but is killed.
Desperate to maintain oil revenues, Nesib marries Auda to his daughter Leyla (Freida Pinto), dissolving the pact with Amar. Auda, sent to persuade Amar, discovers Amar's resistance to exploiting the Yellow Belt. Amar plans to attack Nesib's city, Hobeika, using prisoners as decoys. Auda leads the decoy army, but Nesib's forces overpower them. Auda's plan to lead prisoners to the sea fails, leading them to face a slaver tribe. Auda defeats the tribe, earning the loyalty of other tribes.
Auda is mistakenly shot but revives during funeral rites. Tribals believe he is a prophesied leader. Auda, vowing to "overturn the chessboard," unites tribes against Nesib. Amar agrees to Auda's terms but is killed by the Beni Sirri sheikh. Auda's army, angered, attacks Hobeika, overwhelming Nesib's forces. Auda becomes ruler of both kingdoms through his marriage to Leyla.
In the aftermath Nesib abdicates in favor of Leyla. Auda confronts Nesib, sparing him and sending him to Houston to protect their interests. The film concludes with Auda, now ruler, choosing his people over foreign interests and spending time with his pregnant wife.

documents.title: The Numbers Station
documents.tagline: The code has never been compromised. Until now.
documents.overview: When the moral values of a longtime wetwork black ops agent is tested during his last operation, he receives an unfavorable psych evaluation. Now he is given a break and a seemingly uncomplicated assignment of simply protecting the security of a young female code announcer, code resources and remote station they are assigned to. After an ambush and one phone call later, it becomes a complicated fight for their survival.
