documents.title: The Intouchables
documents.tagline: Sometimes you have to reach into someone else's world to find out what's missing in your own.
documents.overview: A true story of two men who should never have met – a quadriplegic aristocrat who was injured in a paragliding accident and a young man from the projects.
documents.plot:
At night in Paris, Driss is driving Philippe's Maserati Quattroporte at high speed. Chased through the streets by the police, they are eventually cornered. Driss claims the quadriplegic Philippe must get to a hospital urgently; Philippe pretends to have a seizure and the fooled police officers escort them. After arriving at the hospital, Driss drives away.
The story of friendship between the two men is then told as a flashback: Philippe, a wealthy quadriplegic owner of a luxurious hôtel particulier, and his assistant Magalie are interviewing potential live-in caregivers. Driss has no ambitions to get hired; he is only waiting to get a signature on a document proving his interview was rejected, to continue receiving his benefits. He is told to return the next morning to collect his signed document.
The next day when Driss returns, Philippe's aide Yvonne greets him, telling him he has the job on a trial basis. Despite being uninterested and inexperienced, he does well caring for Philippe, albeit using unconventional methods. Driss learns the extent of his employer's disability, aiding Philippe in every aspect of his life. A friend of Philippe's reveals that Driss was imprisoned for six months for robbery, but Philippe disregards the warnings, stating he does not care about Driss' past. As Driss is the only one who does not treat Philippe with pity, he will not fire Driss as long as he does his job properly.
Philippe explains his disability resulted from a paragliding incident and that his wife died without bearing children. Gradually, Driss helps him to organise his private life, despite having problems with his adopted daughter Elisa. Driss discovers modern art, opera and starts painting. For Philippe's birthday, a private classical music concert is performed in his living room. Driss later finds Elisa in her room and discovers she had taken pills because her boyfriend dumped on her, she asks Driss to talk to him in exchange for money. Philippe educates Driss on famous classical pieces, but Driss only recognises them as advert music or cartoon themes. Feeling the concert is too boring, Driss plays Earth, Wind & Fire's "Boogie Wonderland", livening up the party, with the guests also enjoying the music.
Discovering Philippe has a purely epistolary relationship with a woman called Eléonore who lives in Dunkirk, Driss encourages his employer to meet her, but Philippe fears her reaction when she discovers his disability. Driss persuades him to talk to her by phone. Philippe agrees to send a photo of himself in a wheelchair to her, but he hesitates and asks his aide, Yvonne, to send a picture as he was before his accident. A date between them is agreed to, but Philippe is too scared to meet Eléonore at the last minute and leaves with Yvonne before she arrives. Philippe then calls Driss, inviting him to fly with him in his Dassault Falcon 900 private jet for a paragliding weekend in the Alps.

documents.title: A Monster in Paris
documents.tagline: You can find love anywhere… even in insects
documents.overview: Paris, 1910. Emile, a shy movie projectionist, and Raoul, a colourful inventor, find themselves embarked on the hunt for a monster terrorizing citizens. They join forces with Lucille, the big-hearted star of the Bird of Paradise cabaret, an eccentric scientist and his irascible monkey to save the monster, who turns out to be an oversized but harmless flea, from the city's ruthlessly ambitious police chief.
documents.plot:
A Monster in Paris is a 2011 French animated musical fantasy film directed by Rémi Bezançon, Jean-Benjamin Machuel, and Christophe Lautrette. The movie is set in the late 19th century and follows the story of a young girl named Coco, who lives with her mother in a small apartment in Paris.

Coco's life takes a dramatic turn when she meets a mysterious and handsome stranger, Raoul, who claims to be a famous musician. However, their meeting is interrupted by a monster that attacks Coco's apartment building, causing chaos and destruction throughout the city.

As Coco tries to make sense of the monster's appearance and its connection to her life, she discovers that it is actually a manifestation of her own fears and desires. The monster is revealed to be a symbol of Coco's inner world, which she has been trying to suppress due to the difficulties of her mother's illness.

Throughout the movie, Coco embarks on a journey through Paris, meeting various characters who help her understand herself and her place in the world. She meets a group of street performers, including a charming and talented musician named Raoul, who becomes her love interest.

As Coco navigates the city, she also encounters a mysterious figure known as the "Monster," which is revealed to be a manifestation of her own fears and desires. The Monster is a powerful symbol of Coco's inner world, and it serves as a reminder that she must confront her own emotions in order to move forward.

In the end, Coco comes to terms with her feelings and learns to accept herself for who she is. She also finds love and happiness with Raoul, and the two share a romantic dance at the Moulin Rouge, a famous Parisian nightclub.

The movie features stunning animation, beautiful music, and a captivating storyline that explores themes of identity, self-acceptance, and the power of imagination. The film's use of fantasy elements adds to its sense of wonder and magic, making it a delightful and enchanting experience for audiences of all ages.

Overall, A Monster in Paris is a charming and imaginative movie that celebrates the beauty and creativity of Parisian culture. With its stunning animation, catchy music, and captivating storyline, it is a must-see film for anyone who loves animation, music, or simply great storytelling.

documents.title: Sleep Tight
documents.tagline: Someone is watching over you
documents.overview: César, an unhappy concierge, maintains a peculiar relationship with the very diverse inhabitants of the upper-class apartment building where he works in Barcelona.
documents.plot: César, an unhappy concierge, maintains a peculiar relationship with the very diverse inhabitants of the upper-class apartment building where he works in Barcelona.

documents.title: Barbie: A Perfect Christmas
documents.tagline: Being together is what makes a perfect Christmas.
documents.overview: Join Barbie and her sisters Skipper, Stacie and Chelsea as their holiday vacation plans turn into a most unexpected adventure and heartwarming lesson. After a snowstorm diverts their plane, the girls find themselves far from their New York destination and their holiday dreams. Now stranded at a remote inn in the tiny town of Tannenbaum, the sisters are welcomed by new friends and magical experiences. In appreciation for the wonderful hospitality they receive, they use their musical talents to put on a performance for the whole town. Barbie and her sisters realize the joy of being together is what really makes A Perfect Christmas!
documents.plot: The vacation plans of Barbie and her sisters take a turn due to a snowstorm. Stranded in Tannenbaum town, they find themselves amidst a holiday venture where they learn a heartwarming lesson.

documents.title: Detective Conan: Quarter of Silence
documents.original_title: 名探偵コナン 沈黙の15分（クォーター）
documents.overview: The Governor of Tokyo, Yuichiro Asakura, receives a threatening letter the day before the opening of Touto Line, a new train line for the Tokyo Metro. During the opening ceremony of the line, Conan Edogawa and the Detective Boys are driven by Professor Agasa and pass under the Touto Line. Conan, having heard about the threatening letter, notices explosives connected to the Touto railway; Using his original voice to inform the police as Shinichi Kudo, he is able to stop the train and divert traffic away from the explosives preventing any deaths.
documents.plot:
The Governor of Tokyo, Yuuichiro Asakura, receives a threatening letter the day before the opening of Tohto Line, a new train line for the Tokyo Metro. During the opening ceremony of the line, Conan Edogawa and the Detective Boys are driven by Dr. Agasa and pass under the Tohto Line. Conan, having heard about the threatening letter, notices explosives connected to the Tohto railway; Using his original voice to inform Juzo Megure as Shinichi Kudo, he, Miwako Sato and Wataru Takagi are able to stop the train and divert traffic away from the explosives preventing any deaths.
Conan researches Asakura's political history for a clue on the culprit and learns the governor was in charge of the construction of dam in Kitanosawa, a fictional town in the Niigata Prefecture. Due to the dam's construction, the citizens of Kitanosawa were forced into a new town and their old homes were drowned by the dam. Since Asakura's trip to celebrate the anniversary of the dam is canceled by the bombing, Conan speculates information on the bomber could be found in Kitanosawa and plans a trip there.
Conan, the Detective Boys, Ran, Kogoro Mouri, and Sonoko Suzuki travel to Kitanosawa and enjoy the day playing. They are introduced to a group of locals; Keisuke Yamao, Mizuki Toono, Fuyumi Tachihara, Takehiki Mutou, and Shougo Hikawa. The group reveals they were all childhood friends and were part of the group which relocated to the new village. They also reveal it is their first gathering in eight years since Yamao was in prison for killing Toono's sister, Natsuki Toono, in a hit and run. The next day, Tachihara's son, Touma, awakens from his eight-year coma with no memory of his accident. Later that day, Hikawa is found dead in a field. Originally, it was assumed to be suicide since only Hikawa's footprints were found in the snow. Conan reveals Hikawa was killed by an electroshock weapon. The culprit then waited for it to snow and walked away backwards to suggest Hikawa was alone. During a diamond dust caused by the sunrise, Touma experiences a flashback on the day of the accident.
Conan investigates Hikawa's belongings and finds a newspaper clipping detailing a jewelry store was robbed the day before the hit and run. A cell site is destroyed by bombs leading Conan to hypothesize who the possible culprit is. Meanwhile, the Detective Boys and Touma are hunted down by a sniper. Conan intervenes and leads them to safety. Taking a route towards the dam, Conan explains Yamao is the culprit. Yamao robbed the jewelry store in a distant town and drives back to Kitanosawa. On the way, he runs over Natsuki, a scene which Touma notices. Touma is then chased by Yamao and sees the diamonds, explaining why the diamond dust startled his memories. Touma escapes but falls down a cliff leading to his coma. Yamao then buries the jewels in a property in Kitanosawa and turns himself over to the authorities for Natsuki's death.

documents.title: Killing Season
documents.tagline: The purest form of war is one on one.
documents.overview: Two veterans of the Bosnian War, one American, one Serbian, clash in the remote Smoky Mountain wilderness.
documents.plot:
During the Bosnian War, American troops witness atrocities and shoot Serb soldiers whom they hold accountable.
In present-day Belgrade, Serbia, former Scorpions soldier Emil Kovač, who survived the shootings, meets his informant to retrieve a file on American military veteran and former NATO operative Colonel Benjamin Ford.
Meanwhile, Ford has retreated to a cabin in Sevier County, Tennessee, to try to forget the war. Now a recluse, Ford meets Kovač, posing as a European tourist, during a hunting trip. The two men become friendly until Kovač reveals his true identity.
Intent on revenge, Kovač initiates a gory game of cat-and-mouse with Ford. The latter is badly injured but is quick to rebound. It is revealed that Ford shot Kovač in the back, crippling him for years.
After a showdown, Kovač is overpowered by Ford. They reach a peaceful compromise, however, after understanding each other's predicament. Kovač quietly returns to Serbia, happily stating, "I am healing", when the injuries to his face are shown while Ford visits his son, who is making up for missing his grandson's baptism.

documents.title: Contraband
documents.tagline: What would you hide to protect your family?
documents.overview: When his brother-in-law runs afoul of a drug lord, family man Chris Farraday turns to a skill he abandoned long ago—smuggling—to repay the debt. But the job goes wrong, and Farraday finds himself wanted by cops, crooks and killers alike.
documents.plot: When his brother-in-law runs afoul of a drug lord, family man Chris Farraday turns to a skill he abandoned long ago—smuggling—to repay the debt. But the job goes wrong, and Farraday finds himself wanted by cops, crooks and killers alike.

documents.title: Playing for Keeps
documents.tagline: This holiday season, what do you really want?
documents.overview: A former sports star who's fallen on hard times starts coaching his son's soccer team in an attempt to get his life together.
documents.plot: A former sports star who's fallen on hard times starts coaching his son's soccer team in an attempt to get his life together.

documents.title: The Lucky One
documents.overview: A Marine travels to Louisiana after serving three tours in Iraq and searches for the unknown woman he believes was his good luck charm during the war.
documents.plot:
Logan Thibault, a US Marine serving in Iraq, witnesses a Marine called "Aces" die attempting to aid one of his men during an ambush. The following morning, he finds a picture of a young woman on the ground just before a mortar attack destroys where he had been sitting, killing many around him. Unsuccessful at finding the photo's owner, he keeps it. Logan's squad-mate declares the woman in the picture his "guardian angel," just before an explosion destroys their Humvee.
Logan returns to Colorado to live with his sister's family, who have been looking after his dog Zeus. Suffering from PTSD and survivor guilt, he decides it is best to leave and departs to search for the woman in the photo. Logan and Zeus walk to Louisiana, where a lighthouse in the photo has provided a clue. He shows the photo around town and a local resident tells him that the woman used to be married to his friend, a local deputy sheriff.
Logan finds the woman, Beth Green, but has difficulty explaining why he is there. She assumes he wants a job, and her grandmother, Ellie, ends up hiring him. At first, Beth is irritated by Logan's presence, but she begins to warm to him due to his calm demeanor, willingness to work, and competence in repairing machinery. Logan develops a supportive relationship with Beth's son Ben, who is without a positive male influence since the death of Beth's brother Drake.
Beth's former husband, Sheriff's Deputy Keith Clayton—the son of the town's judge—is immediately suspicious of Logan. He is brusque and overbearing with the former Marine. He discourages his son Ben from playing the violin around him, which leads the boy to practice in his tree house.
On the anniversary of Drake's death, Beth becomes distraught and Logan calms her down. Keith tries to stop the budding relationship between Beth and Logan, but she stands up to him, showing that she is no longer intimidated by him.
Discovering that Logan was asking about Beth when he first arrived in town, Keith steals the photo, making her believe that Logan has been stalking her. Her trust destroyed, she is distraught and sends Logan away. Ellie tries to soften Beth, explaining it isn't Logan's fault he survived and Drake did not.
An intoxicated Keith sees Logan walking with his dog and angrily confronts him, drawing his gun while people on the street begin to panic and run. Logan disarms him, turning the weapon over to another officer. He then heads home to pack, finding a photo of Beth's brother Drake inside a book Ben had given him. The tattoo on Drake's forearm says "Aces" and he realizes that Drake was the sergeant from the night raid. Logan returns to Beth's to tell her what he knows of how Drake died.
At Judge Clayton's, Keith is shocked and embarrassed over what he did, although his father assures him it will all blow over before the election. Keith walks out into a gathering storm, leaving his badge behind, pleading to Beth to reconcile.

documents.title: The Possession
documents.tagline: Fear The Demon That Doesn't Fear God
documents.overview: A young girl buys an antique box at a yard sale, unaware that inside the collectible lives a malicious ancient spirit. The girl's father teams with his ex-wife to find a way to end the curse upon their child.

documents.title: Magic Mike
documents.tagline: Work all day. Work it all night.
documents.overview: Mike, an experienced stripper, takes a younger performer called The Kid under his wing and schools him in the arts of partying, picking up women, and making easy money.
documents.plot:
Mike Lane has big plans for a business of his own but pays his bills through a series of odd jobs, most notably performing as the star performer at the Xquisite Strip Club in Tampa. It is owned by Dallas, who has dreams of creating an "empire" of male strip clubs.
Mike soon meets 19-year-old Adam, a recent college dropout looking for a construction job. He takes him under his wing and encourages him to begin stripping at Xquisite. Mike is introduced to Adam's sister Brooke. Despite his on-and-off relationship with Joanna, Mike finds himself attracted to Brooke and promises to look after Adam.
Adam falls further into the excessive lifestyle of the Xquisite dancers, using drugs and having sexual encounters with many clients. When Dallas announces he has a plan to move their act to Miami, Mike confides in Brooke that he is tired of the lifestyle and wants to get a small business loan to pursue his dream of opening a custom furniture business.
The bank declines his loan application and Mike realizes that he has to stay in the business to continue to pay his bills. He later attends a hurricane party at Dallas' house, where Adam becomes part of a scheme created by Tobias, Xquisite's DJ, to sell drugs to Xquisite's clients, and is eventually given a package of ecstasy. Adam begins using drugs regularly, and Mike notices more of Adam's reckless behavior, to the chagrin of Brooke, who is relying on Mike to protect him.
A few days later, Mike and Adam perform for a private party at a sorority house where Adam brings the package of drugs with him. There, Adam gives a young woman an ecstasy pill, causing a brawl between him and the woman's boyfriend. The performers are forced to flee without the drugs, which Adam says were worth $1,000. They also do not collect their payment, which infuriates Dallas.
After the next night's show, Mike and Adam take drugs and go to a club. Adam vomits and passes out; Brooke finds him on Mike's floor the next morning. Brooke angrily confronts Mike about his lifestyle, and ends her friendship with him. Tobias and his suppliers break into Mike's house looking for Adam, revealing that the drugs were actually worth $10,000. Mike gives up most of his life savings to pay Adam's debt in full, but Adam acts ignorant of the close encounter afterwards, quietly angering Mike.
Later, before the dancers' final performance at Xquisite, Mike decides he has had enough. Knowing that Dallas has no loyalty to any of them and is driven by greed, Mike leaves the club through the back. After realizing Mike is not coming back, Dallas promotes Adam to replace him as lead dancer.
Mike drives to Brooke's apartment and tells her he has quit stripping. Brooke has learned what he did for Adam, and she invites him to join her for breakfast. She playfully asks what they can do until morning, and then kisses him.

documents.title: The Smurfs 2
documents.tagline: Get ready to get naughty!
documents.overview: The evil wizard Gargamel creates a couple of mischievous Smurf-like creatures called the Naughties that he hopes will let him harness the all-powerful, magical Smurf-essence. But when he discovers that only a real Smurf can give him what he wants, and only a secret spell that Smurfette knows can turn the Naughties into real Smurfs, Gargamel kidnaps Smurfette and brings her to Paris, where he has been winning the adoration of millions as the world¹s greatest sorcerer. It's up to Papa, Clumsy, Grouchy, and Vanity to return to our world, reunite with their human friends Patrick and Grace Winslow, and rescue her! Will Smurfette, who has always felt different from the other Smurfs, find a new connection with the Naughties Vexy and Hackus or will the Smurfs convince her that their love for her is True Blue?

documents.title: The Cold Light of Day
documents.tagline: Instinct is his greatest weapon.
documents.overview: After his family is kidnapped during their sailing trip in Spain, a young Wall Street trader is confronted by the people responsible: intelligence agents looking to recover a mysterious briefcase.
documents.plot:
Will Shaw, who owns a consultancy business in San Francisco that is about to go into insolvency, reluctantly visits his family in Spain for a holiday. He is met there by his father, Martin, an adviser for the U.S. government, with whom he has a tense relationship.
Will's preoccupation with his phone results in a sailing accident where Will leaps to save his brother's girlfriend Dara from being hit by the yacht's boom but she hits her head on a winch. Martin grabs the phone and throws it into the ocean. Will swims to town to fetch medical supplies and to cool down.
When Will returns, the yacht has moved and his family is gone. He goes to the police and they lead him to Zahir, who knows where his family is. He senses something is amiss, and attempts to escape in a police car. Martin appears, and helps Will by beating the officers.
Martin reveals he is a CIA agent, and that the people who kidnapped their family are after a briefcase he had taken on an assignment. Martin meets his CIA team leader Jean Carrack in Madrid, who claims she no longer has the briefcase, but he knows she is lying.
As Martin returns to his car, Gorman, a sniper, kills him. Will retrieves Martin's phone as Gorman starts shooting at him and gives chase. As Will escapes, he takes a call from the kidnappers, who want to speak to "Tom", providing a 21 hour deadline and a meeting point to exchange the briefcase for his family.
Receiving no help from the US embassy, Will is picked up by Carrack in a car outside, but he realizes she is untrustworthy. He feigns illness and she, disgusted by the thought of him vomiting in her car, has the car pulled over and Will gets away.
Will arranges a meeting with his father's friend Diego at his office and meets receptionist Lucia Caldera, Diego's niece, where he fights off one of Carrack's men. The pair go to Diego's apartment, but they find that he has been killed by Carrack and Gorman.
Will and Lucia escape across the rooftops, but he is shot. She takes him to a nightclub, to a friend who has medical experience who cauterizes the wound. Lucia explains that "Tom" is Martin's alias in Spain, and she is Will's half-sister, Martin's daughter by another woman.
As Will arrives at the meeting point, he is grabbed and tortured for his father's whereabouts by the kidnappers, actually Israeli Mossad agents led by Zahir, who was using the briefcase to lure a traitor when Martin stole it from them. They realize Carrack framed Martin and she has the briefcase, so they want Will to lure her out. He briefly sees his family before Zahir releases him.
Will meets Lucia at the nightclub, where she starts a tab on Carrack's credit card. Gorman appears and is subdued by bouncers at the club and tortured for information but he refuses to budge. Will lets Gorman escape so that he leads them to Carrack, who tries to sell the briefcase in an underground car park.

documents.title: The Awakening
documents.tagline: Sometimes dead does not mean gone.
documents.overview: In 1921, England is overwhelmed by the loss and grief of World War I. Hoax exposer Florence Cathcart visits a boarding school to explain sightings of a child ghost. Everything she believes unravels as the 'missing' begin to show themselves.
documents.plot: In post–War England, a writer and sometime-ghost hunter investigates a reported haunting at a boys boarding school.

documents.title: Turbo
documents.tagline: SLO NO MO
documents.overview: The tale of an ordinary garden snail who dreams of winning the Indy 500.
documents.plot:
Turbo is a 2013 computer-animated comedy-adventure film produced by DreamWorks Animation. The movie follows the story of Theo, a garden snail who dreams of becoming a racing champion.

The film begins with Theo, a humble and unassuming garden snail, living in a small pond with his family. Despite his slow pace, Theo has a big dream: to become the fastest snail in the world. However, his family and friends think he's crazy, as snails are not built for speed.

One day, while swimming in the pond, Theo is exposed to a strange substance that gives him superhuman speed. He becomes the fastest snail in the world, but also develops a turbo-powered engine that allows him to move at incredible velocities.

Excited by his newfound abilities, Theo sets out on an adventure to become a racing champion. He meets a group of street-smart racers who teach him how to navigate the high-speed world of racing. There's Guy Gagne, a cocky and arrogant car driver; Tito, a wise-cracking and fast-talking street rat; and Burn, a tough and intimidating motorcycle rider.

As Theo navigates this new world, he faces numerous challenges and obstacles. He must learn to control his turbo-powered engine, avoid danger, and outsmart his rivals. Along the way, he befriends a young girl named Tito's sister, Tola, who becomes his love interest.

However, not everyone is happy about Theo's newfound success. Guy Gagne, in particular, sees Theo as a threat to his own racing career and tries to sabotage him at every turn. The two engage in an epic rivalry that takes them on a wild ride through the streets of New York City.

As the big racing championship approaches, Theo must confront his own doubts and fears. Can he overcome his slow start and become the champion? Will he be able to balance his love for racing with his newfound fame?

The film's climax features an action-packed racing sequence that takes Theo and his friends on a thrilling ride through the streets of New York City. In the end, Theo emerges victorious, but not without learning valuable lessons about perseverance, friendship, and believing in himself.

Turbo is a heartwarming and hilarious animated film that celebrates the power of dreams and determination. With its colorful characters, witty humor, and high-speed action sequences, it's a movie that will leave audiences cheering for more.

documents.title: Walking with Dinosaurs
documents.tagline: The Greatest Adventure in 70 Million Years
documents.overview: Walking with Dinosaurs 3D is a film depicting life-like 3D dinosaur characters set in photo-real landscapes that transports audiences to the prehistoric world as it existed 70 million years ago. The film is based on the 1999 documentary television miniseries Walking with Dinosaurs, produced by the BBC. Walking with Dinosaurs 3D is being produced by Evergreen Studios, the company that produced Happy Feet, and it is was released on October 11, 2013.
documents.plot:
Walking with Dinosaurs is a 2013 documentary film that follows the life story of a young Pachyrhinosaurus named Patchi, from his birth to adulthood. The film is narrated by Fionn Whitehead and features stunning computer-generated imagery (CGI) animation.

The movie begins with the birth of Patchi, who emerges from his egg in the Late Jurassic period, around 75 million years ago. The scene is set in a lush, prehistoric forest filled with towering trees and teeming with life. Patchi's mother, a Pachyrhinosaurus matriarch, takes care of him, teaching him essential survival skills such as hunting and social behavior.

As Patchi grows, he faces numerous challenges, including fierce rivalries with other young dinosaurs, treacherous terrain, and the threat of predators like Tyrannosaurs. Despite these obstacles, Patchi perseveres, learning valuable lessons from his mother and other experienced dinosaurs.

One of the most significant plot points in the film is Patchi's encounter with a group of intelligent and social Troodons. The Troodons are depicted as being highly intelligent and resourceful, using tools to hunt and gather food. Patchi forms a close bond with one of the Troodons, who becomes his ally and friend.

As Patchi approaches adulthood, he faces a critical decision: whether to stay in his family group or venture out on his own. After much contemplation, Patchi decides to leave his family and explore the world beyond his forest home. This marks a significant turning point in his life, as he must rely solely on himself to survive.

The film's climax features an epic battle between Patchi and a Tyrannosaurus Rex. The two dinosaurs engage in a fierce fight, with Patchi using all his skills and cunning to outwit the predator. In the end, Patchi emerges victorious, having proven himself as a formidable hunter.

The movie concludes with Patchi, now a mature adult, standing proudly on a hill overlooking his forest home. He has come full circle, from a vulnerable hatchling to a confident and powerful dinosaur. The film ends with a sense of closure and new beginnings, as Patchi looks out towards the horizon, ready to face whatever challenges the future may hold.

Overall, Walking with Dinosaurs is an engaging and visually stunning documentary that explores the life cycle of a Pachyrhinosaurus. Through Patchi's journey, we gain insight into the social behavior, intelligence, and adaptability of these fascinating creatures.

documents.title: The Campaign
documents.tagline: May the best loser win.
documents.overview: Two rival politicians compete to win an election to represent their small North Carolina congressional district in the United States House of Representatives.
documents.plot:
Democratic Congressman Cam Brady, who has run unopposed for the 14th district of North Carolina for four elections, is exposed when he has an affair with a supporter that is heard on a phone call, damaging his upcoming campaign for a fifth term. With eight weeks to go before the election, corrupt businessmen Glenn and Wade Motch persuade tour guide Marty Huggins to run against Cam as a Republican nominee. The Motch brothers ultimately intend to use Marty to forward a profitable scheme with a Chinese company.
After Cam humiliates Marty at a brunch event, campaign manager Tim Wattley (also on the payroll of the Motch brothers) transforms Marty's image into that of a successful entrepreneur and family man. This pays off during his first debate with Cam as he takes the viewers by storm with his resolve to bring back jobs to North Carolina. Marty is able to undermine Cam's campaign by challenging him to recite the Lord's Prayer (the correct wording of which eludes Cam) and by using Rainbowland, a story written by Cam as a child, to accuse him of being a Communist; the latter results in a fight breaking out at a town hall debate between Cam, Marty and their respective supporters.
Cam further damages his campaign when he accidentally punches a baby and Uggie the canine actor, on both occasions having intended to hit Marty. In response, Cam runs two campaign ads, one portraying Marty as an Al Qaeda terrorist (based on Marty's facial hair) and the other leaning into Cam's affair (despite it being received extremely negatively by women). However, Cam's popularity recovers after a mishap at a snake handling ceremony, which results in his hospitalization.
Cam later realizes his son intends to use his campaign methods against his opponent for class president, and realizes he is setting a bad example. Cam travels to Marty's home to make peace but ends up getting drunk and is arrested for drunk driving when Marty, encouraged by Tim, reports him. Marty then airs another television advertisement, with Cam's son addressing him as "dad".
Furious, Cam seduces Marty's wife, Mitzi, and records them having sex before releasing it as a campaign ad. This leads his campaign manager Mitch Wilson to resign on principle and prompts his wife to leave him and take their children with her, leaving Cam despondent about the coming election. Marty leaves Mitzi as a result of the ad but gets revenge on Cam by shooting him during a hunting trip, causing his popularity to increase further.
Marty meets with the Motch brothers soon afterwards, but learns of their "insourcing" plans with China; they intend to establish a factory complex within the 14th district and import Chinese workers to reduce shipping costs. Marty, realizing he has been used, rejects their support. The Motch brothers in turn defect to Cam's side, revitalizing his campaign and paying his wife to appear alongside him at campaign events to give the impression of reconciliation.

documents.title: The Scorpion King 3: Battle for Redemption
documents.original_title: The Scorpion King 3: Battle for Redemption
documents.tagline: From the Producers of The Mummy
documents.overview: Since his triumphant rise to power in the original blockbuster "The Scorpion King", Mathayus' kingdom has fallen and he's lost his queen to plague. Now an assassin for hire, he must defend a kingdom from an evil tyrant and his ghost warriors for the chance to regain the power and glory he once knew. Starring Ron Perlman ("Hellboy") and Billy Zane ("Titanic"), and featuring 6-time WWE champion Dave Bautista and UFC star Kimbo Slice, "The Scorpion King 3: Battle for Redemption" takes "The Mummy" phenomenon to an all-new level of epic action and non-stop adventure.
documents.plot:
The Scorpion King 3: Battle for Redemption is a 2012 American direct-to-video sword-and-sorcery action film directed by Roel Reiné and the third entry in The Scorpion King series. Victor Webster takes over the role of Mathayus from Dwayne Johnson, with Bostin Christopher, Temuera Morrison, Krystal Vee, Selina Lo, Kimbo Slice, Dave Bautista, Billy Zane as Talus and Ron Perlman as Horus. Universal Studios Home Entertainment released it on home video in January 2012.

Years after becoming the Scorpion King, Mathayus loses his wife, Queen Cassandra, to a plague, just as she had once foreseen that his peaceful reign could not last. Grief-stricken, he lets his kingdom crumble and returns to life as a sword for hire. In Egypt, Talus resents his elder brother Horus, who was made king instead of him, and plans to take his throne. To do so he marches into the Far East to seize the Book of the Dead from Ramusan, a king allied to Horus. Horus hires Mathayus to stop him, pairing him with the boisterous Teutonic warrior Olaf.

Talus abducts Ramusan's daughter, Princess Silda, and Ramusan promises that whoever saves her may marry her and with her claim a kingdom. Before Mathayus can reach her, she is carried off by ninja warriors under a mysterious leader known as Cobra. Talus hires Mathayus and Olaf to bring back the princess and Cobra's head, and the pair find their way to an outlaw camp, where they discover that Cobra is Silda herself. Talus, meanwhile, overruns Ramusan's palace, wounds the king and takes the book, using it to raise three dead champions, Zulu Kondo, Agromael and Tsukai, who prove their power by slaughtering his own best men.

Talus sends Tsukai and Zulu Kondo against the exiles' camp; Mathayus, Olaf and Silda's ninjas defeat Zulu Kondo, but Tsukai escapes. Posing as Silda's rescuers and offering a fake head of Cobra, Mathayus and Olaf enter the palace. In the battle that follows, Silda duels Tsukai and Olaf battles Agromael, while Mathayus reaches the dying Ramusan; using the Book of the Dead, they turn the undead warriors against Talus. Ramusan dies, the ninjas overwhelm Talus, and the champions kneel to Mathayus as ruler of both kingdoms. When Horus reaches the gates, he finds Mathayus restored as the Scorpion King.

Reviews were poor; IGN rated it 4 out of 10, faulting its dialogue, acting and stagey action.

documents.title: Beethoven's Christmas Adventure
documents.overview: A Christmas elf accidentally takes off in Santa's sleigh, crash lands in a small town, and loses the magic toy bag. Beethoven must rescue the elf, recover the bag from greedy crooks, and return the sleigh to Santa in time to save Christmas.

documents.title: Michael Jackson: The Life of an Icon
documents.original_title: Michael Jackson: The Life of an Icon
documents.overview: See Michael Jackson, one of the most recognizable and popular entertainers of all time, like never before in the feature-length tribute Michael Jackson: The Life of an Icon. Known to millions of fans worldwide for his record-breaking albums, groundbreaking music videos, mesmerizing dance moves and humanitarian efforts, his true story has never really been told...until now. This unprecedented look into the King of Pop's fascinating life includes all-new interviews with his mother Katherine Jackson as well as siblings Tito and Rebbie Jackson, family, friends and music legends such as Smokey Robinson, Dionne Warwick and many more.

documents.title: Into the White
documents.tagline: Inspired by the true world war II story.
documents.overview: Based on a true story. On 27 April 1940, Luftwaffe pilot Horst Schopis' Heinkel 111 bomber is shot down near Grotli by an RAF Blackburn Skua L2940 fighter, which then crash-lands. The surviving German and English crew members begin to at shoot each other, but later find themselves huddled up in the same cabin. In order to survive the harsh winter in the Norwegian wilderness, they have to stand together. An unlikely, lifelong friendship blossoms.
documents.plot:
Into the White is a 2012 Norwegian war drama film directed by Espen Sandberg and Joachim Trier, produced by Trollhättan Film. The movie is set during World War II and tells the story of three young Norwegian airmen who are shot down behind enemy lines.

The film begins with Lieutenant Stig Engstrom (played by Mikkel Abels), Lieutenant Sverre Okken (played by Anders Baasmo Christiansen), and Lieutenant Magnus Isaksen (played by Jonas Holm) on a mission to bomb German airfields. However, their plane is hit by anti-aircraft fire, and they are forced to make an emergency landing in the Norwegian wilderness.

The three pilots soon discover that they are not alone in the forest. They encounter a group of German soldiers who have also been stranded behind enemy lines. Initially, tensions run high between the two groups, but as they spend more time together, they begin to form an uneasy alliance.

As the days pass, the Norwegian and German pilots learn about each other's lives and motivations. Stig, Sverre, and Magnus are all young men who have been forced to confront the harsh realities of war, while their German counterparts, Hauptmann Müller (played by Lasse Hallström), Oberleutnant von Roeder (played by Mads Sjøgård Pettersen), and Oberleutnant von Roeder's brother, are all struggling with their own demons.

As the situation becomes more desperate, the two groups must work together to survive. They share what little food they have, and the Germans teach the Norwegians how to navigate using a compass. The Norwegians, in turn, show the Germans the beauty of the Norwegian wilderness.

Despite their differences, the pilots begin to form bonds with each other. Stig, Sverre, and Magnus learn about the human cost of war from their German counterparts, while Hauptmann Müller and his men are forced to confront the harsh realities of their own actions.

As the days turn into weeks, the pilots realize that they must find a way to escape the forest before it's too late. They hatch a plan to make a break for it, but things don't go according to plan. The Germans are discovered by their superiors, and the Norwegians are forced to flee.

In the end, only one of the Norwegian pilots is able to escape, while the others are captured or killed. The film ends with Stig, Sverre, and Magnus reflecting on the experience they shared in the forest. They realize that despite being on opposite sides of the war, they formed a bond that will stay with them for the rest of their lives.

Into the White is a powerful and emotional film that explores the human cost of war. The movie features stunning cinematography and outstanding performances from its cast. The film's themes of survival, sacrifice, and redemption are timeless and universal, making it a must-see for anyone interested in World War II history or drama.

documents.title: Nurse 3-D
documents.tagline: Your pain is her pleasure.
documents.overview: Abby Russell, a beautiful, dedicated nurse with a sinister side, has a secret life in which she targets and punishes dishonest men.
documents.plot:
Abby Russell works as a nurse in Manhattan but is secretly a serial killer who targets unfaithful men. She murders a man by severing his femoral artery and then throws him off of the roof of a nightclub. The following day, she attends the graduation ceremony of nurse Danni Rodgers, a student she mentored, and meets Danni's mother and stepfather, Larry Cook. However, Danni is ill-prepared for her first day of duty, and her superior, Dr. Morris, berates her for not responding quickly to an emergency. Abby views the situation with disgust, as she knows that Dr. Morris is a sadist who takes pleasure in tormenting new nurses.
Abby is irritated when Danni chooses to call her paramedic boyfriend, Steve, for support. She is pleased when Danni's call to Steve ends badly due to a fight over Danni's refusal to move in with him. She explains to Abby that she is distrustful of her stepfather Larry, which is justified when Abby and Danni witness him having an affair while en route to a nightclub. Unknown to Danni, Abby spikes her drink with a date rape drug, enabling Abby to get Danni to have sex with both her and random strangers. The next day, Danni wakes to find herself in Abby's apartment and leaves. Afterwards, Abby downloads several photos that she had taken from the previous night before leaving to see a psychiatrist, revealed to be Larry.
Abby seduces Larry, alluding to her past history with her father. Confirming that he is unfaithful to Danni's mother, Abby shows up at his place of work and convinces him to give her a ride, during which she paralyzes him with vecuronium bromide, resulting in a car accident. After hearing of her stepfather's death, Danni seeks solace from Abby, only for Abby to grow angry when Danni says she will move in with Steve. Abby comments that she hopes that Larry's genitals were severed in the car crash. Danni is skeptical of Abby as she had not informed her of the crash. Abby slowly convinces Detective John Rogan that Danni is mentally unstable and obsessed with her.
The next day, Abby runs into Rachel Adams, a new human resources employee who remarks that Abby resembles a girl she knew that was sent to a mental institution. Abby invites Rachel out for drinks and takes the opportunity to harass Danni by calling her via Skype and showing Danni a video of Abby injecting chemicals into Rachel. Danni tries to go to the police, only for Detective Rogan to dismiss her claims as evidence of her trying to hurt Abby in retaliation. He uses the photographs Abby took as proof to this effect, which Steve sees as a result of Danni summoning him to the police station for support. This prompts an argument between the two, and Steve leaves. Danni tries to approach Dr. Morris for help, only for him to use this as an opportunity to blackmail Abby into having sex with him. Abby pretends to agree to this arrangement but uses the opportunity to dismember and murder him. That same night Abby also murders Rachel.

documents.title: Big Miracle
documents.tagline: A family of whales trapped beneath the ice. One unforgettable rescue.
documents.overview: Based on an inspiring true story, a small-town news reporter (Krasinski) and a Greenpeace volunteer (Barrymore) enlist the help of rival superpowers to save three majestic gray whales trapped under the ice of the Arctic Circle. ‘Big Miracle’ is adapted from the nonfiction book ‘Freeing the Whales: How the Media Created the World’s Greatest Non-Event’ by Tom Rose.
documents.plot: A small-town news reporter and a Greenpeace volunteer enlist the help of rival superpowers to save three majestic gray whales trapped under the ice of the Arctic Circle.

documents.title: One Piece 3D: Straw Hat Chase
documents.original_title: ONE PIECE 3D 麦わらチェイス
documents.overview: One Piece 3D: Straw Hat Chase is the 11th One Piece film of the series, and is set before the time-skip. This is One Piece's first movie release to be in 3D CGI. The movie is also the first One Piece film since Movie 3 to be a double-feature. This time, the film was featured with "Toriko 3D: Gourmet Adventure", both being billed as the "Jump Heroes Film". The double-feature was released on March 19, 2011.granmaster
documents.plot:
One Piece 3D: Straw Hat Chase is a 2011 Japanese computer-animated short film produced by Toei Animation and the eleventh theatrical release based on Eiichiro Oda's manga One Piece. Directed by Hiroyuki Satō from a screenplay by Yasuyuki Tsutsumi, it was the first film in the series made entirely in CGI and in stereoscopic 3D, as well as its first short, running about 30 minutes. It was released on 19 March 2011 as part of the "Jump Heroes Film" double bill with Toriko 3D: Gourmet Adventure. Oda supervised the original characters' designs, and the music, including the instrumental theme "Break into the Light", was provided by the Tokyo Ska Paradise Orchestra. The regular voice cast returns, led by Mayumi Tanaka as Luffy, with Kazuya Nakai, Akemi Okamura, Kappei Yamaguchi, Hiroaki Hirata, Ikue Otani, Yuriko Yamaguchi, Kazuki Yao and Chō, while comedian Tomomitsu Yamaguchi voices all three original characters.

Schneider, an aging pirate who senses that he does not have long to live, decides to disband his tiny crew, which consists only of himself and his old dog Buzz, in order to spare his companion. Buzz refuses to leave, so Schneider sets him an impossible challenge: if he can steal the straw hat of the famous pirate Monkey D. Luffy, the crew will stay together. Buzz, who ate a Devil Fruit that allows him to transform into a giant eagle, succeeds, snatching the treasured hat that Luffy received from Shanks. The Straw Hat Pirates, who had rescued Schneider from a drifting ship, set off in a long, frantic pursuit of the eagle, while Chopper tends to the ailing old man. The chase eventually leads Luffy and Buzz into a Navy base, where the crew fights its way through the Marines and wins. In the end Luffy recovers his hat, Schneider and Buzz befriend the Straw Hats, and the old pirate promises not to break up his crew. A closing flashback shows Shanks entrusting the hat to the young Luffy.

The film was the last of the series set before the story's two-year time skip. Its release came days after the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake, which forced the postponement of stage greetings in the Kanto region and closures of some theaters; it opened seventh at the box office and ultimately earned about ¥790 million, the lowest total in the film series. It received an animation award at the 65th Motion Picture and Television Engineering Society of Japan awards.

documents.title: Assassin's Creed: Embers
documents.overview: Taking place after the events of Assassin's Creed: Revelations in the year 1524 in Tuscany, follow the retired Assassin Ezio Auditore as he teams up with Shao Jun during his final battles.
documents.plot:
Assassin's Creed: Embers is a Canadian animated short film of 2011 produced by UbiWorkshop and written by Darby McDevitt, based on the Assassin's Creed games. It concludes the story of Ezio Auditore da Firenze, the hero of Assassin's Creed II, Brotherhood and Revelations, who is voiced again by Roger Craig Smith. Angela Galuppo voices both the Chinese Assassin Shao Jun and Ezio's daughter Flavia, Anna Tuveri voices his wife Sofia Sartor and Peter Arpesella plays a young Italian man. The film was included as a bonus with the Signature and Collector's Editions of Assassin's Creed: Revelations.

The story is set in 1524, twelve years after Ezio discovered the secret library of Altaïr. Having retired from the Assassin Order, he lives quietly in the Tuscan countryside with Sofia and their children Flavia and Marcello, and writes his memoirs. Then a stranger arrives: Shao Jun, a Chinese Assassin who has come to learn from him about his life in the Brotherhood. Ezio wants her gone, but Sofia lets her stay the night. When he catches her reading his memoirs he orders her out, but relents when she asks what being an Assassin means.

On a visit to Florence, his birthplace, he tells her how the execution of his father and brothers in the town square drove him to become an Assassin, and that such a life brings only suffering. Leaving the city, they are attacked by a man who also seems to be Asian. After killing him, Shao Jun explains that she was once a concubine of the Jiajing Emperor and is being hunted by his agents, and that her former master freed her from the emperor's grip. Back at the villa, Ezio sends his family away, knowing more killers will follow, and teaches Shao Jun the key to freeing her people. That night more of her pursuers attack, and the two Assassins defeat them all, though Ezio is left exhausted. In the morning he gives her a small box to use only if she loses her way and sends her off as two riders approach.

Some time later, Ezio, now suffering from heart trouble, travels to Florence with Sofia and Flavia. Resting on a bench, he is approached by a young man with a scarred face who complains about the women of Florence, reminding Ezio of his own youth. The young man leaves, and Ezio dies of a heart attack in front of his family. The film closes with a final letter to Sofia, in which Ezio writes that of everything that sustained him through life, his love for the world and for the people around him was the strongest.

documents.title: A Princess for Christmas
documents.tagline: Sometimes dreams come true
documents.overview: After her sister and brother-in-law's tragic deaths, an American woman who is the guardian for her young niece and nephew is invited to a royal European castle for Christmas by her late brother-in-law's father, the Duke of Castlebury. Feeling out of place as a commoner, she is determined to give her family a merry Christmas and surprises herself when she falls for a handsome prince.
documents.plot:
A Princess for Christmas, billed in the United Kingdom as A Christmas Princess and previously known as Christmas at Castlebury Hall, is an American television comedy drama of 2011 directed by Michael Damian. Katie McGrath stars as Jules Daly, Sam Heughan as Prince Ashton, and Roger Moore as Edward, Duke of Castlebury, with Travis Turner and Leilah de Meza as Jules's nephew Milo and niece Maddie, Miles Richardson as the butler Paisley and Charlotte Salt as Ashton's girlfriend, Lady Arabella.

Jules works in an antique shop in Buffalo, New York, and has become guardian to Milo and Maddie since the death of her sister and brother-in-law. Maddie is mischievous and Milo a rebellious teenager who hates Christmas because it reminds him of his parents. Laid off just before the holidays, and with the babysitter quitting over Maddie's pranks, Jules is visited by Paisley, butler to the children's wealthy paternal grandfather, Duke Edward, who invites them to spend Christmas at his castle in Castlebury. Told that the Duke is ill, Jules reluctantly accepts, only to find him in perfect health. She is immediately smitten with Ashton, brother of the children's late father, Charles, whom the Duke disowned for marrying Jules's sister.

Finding no Christmas trees in the palace because the Duke dislikes them, Jules and Maddie bring one in anyway. Edward is furious until Maddie hands him an ornament identical to one his brother gave him as a boy, and, his heart thawing, he orders a Christmas Eve ball. Ashton teaches Milo archery and tells him about Charles. Overhearing the Duke and Ashton disparaging an unrefined guest they would rather not invite, Jules assumes they mean her, and after her gown is accidentally burned she quietly heads home. The housekeeper, Mrs. Birch, and Paisley fetch her back from the train station with a dress from Vienna. At the ball Ashton realises that Arabella cares only for his title, and he explains to Jules that their remarks were about Bunny McCracken, a woman who hates children. The two dance, Arabella's family fails to turn the Duke against Jules and storms out, and Jules agrees to stay longer. The family catch Santa leaving gifts, and later Jules and Ashton marry and ride away in a carriage.

Shot in early 2011 at Peleș Castle and other locations around Bucharest, Romania, the film premiered on the Hallmark Channel on 3 December 2011.

documents.title: Ice Age: A Mammoth Christmas
documents.tagline: Get ready for a chilling fun holiday adventure with the Ice Age herd!
documents.overview: When Sid accidentally destroys Manny's heirloom Christmas rock and ends up on Santa's naughty list, he leads a hilarious quest to the North Pole to make things right and ends up making things much worse. Now it's up to Manny and his prehistoric posse to band together and save Christmas for the entire world!
documents.plot:
Ice Age: A Mammoth Christmas is a 2011 American animated Christmas television special produced by Blue Sky Studios and directed by Karen Disher, part of the Ice Age franchise. Ray Romano, John Leguizamo, Denis Leary and Queen Latifah reprise their roles as Manny, Sid, Diego and Ellie, with Billy Gardell as Santa Claus. Much of the animation was produced by Reel FX Creative Studios. It premiered on Fox in the United States on 24 November 2011, aired on Channel 4 and E4 in the United Kingdom at Christmas, and was released on DVD and Blu-ray two days after its American broadcast.

Set between the events of Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs and Ice Age: Continental Drift, the special follows the herd as Christmas approaches. Manny brings out the Christmas Rock, a family heirloom from his childhood that is said to help Santa find them, as a surprise for his daughter, Peaches. He warns the clumsy sloth Sid to stay away from it. Sid, doubting that Santa could find the rock, decides to make his own decoration and chooses a tree, which Crash and Eddie help him decorate. But when he tops it with an ice star, the star flies off and shatters the Christmas Rock.

Furious, Manny declares that Sid is on Santa's "Naughty List," while dismissing the idea of Santa to Ellie. Peaches overhears and is upset that her father does not believe, and angry at how he treated Sid. Determined to make amends and get off the Naughty List, Sid sets out for the North Pole to apologize to Santa in person, accompanied by Peaches, Crash and Eddie, with Manny, Ellie and Diego following to bring them home. Along the way the group meets a tiny reindeer named Prancer, who guides them to Santa's workshop, where Sid's well-meaning blunders cause chaos that threatens to ruin Christmas. To save the holiday, the herd must help Santa deliver presents, inventing several Christmas traditions along the way, and Manny learns to believe again. Meanwhile, Scrat pursues his acorn in a holiday-themed subplot.

In keeping with the franchise's playful approach to prehistory, the special offered prehistoric origins for familiar Christmas customs such as the Christmas tree, the naughty-and-nice list and Santa's flying reindeer.

documents.title: Devil's Due
documents.tagline: The Devil Always Gets His Due
documents.overview: An unexpected pregnancy takes a terrifying turn for newlyweds Zach and Samantha McCall.
documents.plot:
Devil's Due is a 2014 American found-footage supernatural horror film directed by Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett in their feature directorial debut and written by Lindsay Devlin. It stars Allison Miller as Samantha McCall and Zach Gilford as her husband Zach, with Sam Anderson as Father Thomas. Produced for 20th Century Fox, the film was developed after the directors' segment 10/31/98 in the 2012 horror anthology V/H/S attracted studio attention.

Zach McCall begins recording a video diary on the eve of his wedding to Sam, so that their future children will have a record of the family's history. The newlyweds spend their honeymoon in the Dominican Republic, where a fortune teller unsettles Sam by telling her that she was born from death and that they have been waiting for her. Later that night, lost in an unfamiliar part of the city, the couple accepts a ride from a taxi driver who takes them to an underground nightclub. After drinking heavily, they black out, and Sam is taken to a hidden chamber where she is subjected to a satanic ritual. The next morning they wake up in their hotel remembering nothing.

A few weeks after returning home, Sam discovers that she is pregnant despite having taken birth control pills. The couple is delighted at first, but Zach continues filming everything, and the footage gradually reveals that something is wrong. During the first ultrasound the monitor briefly turns to static, and as the pregnancy progresses, Sam develops nosebleeds, bruising, a craving for raw meat despite being a vegetarian, sudden bursts of violent rage and frightening displays of strength and telekinesis. Strangers seem to be watching the house, and hidden cameras are secretly installed to monitor her. As Zach investigates, he uncovers evidence that a cult has chosen Sam to carry a child for a sinister purpose and that their lives are in grave danger.

The film combines the found-footage format with the themes of Rosemary's Baby, using home video, security cameras and other recording devices to tell its story.

Devil's Due was released on January 17, 2014. It received negative reviews, with 21 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it derivative and mostly uninspired, and a Metacritic score of 34.

documents.title: Book of Dragons
documents.tagline: All New Dragons
documents.overview: So you want to be a dragon trainer do you? Prepare yourself for adventure, excitement and training as Hiccup, Astrid, Toothless and Gobber tell the legend behind the Book of Dragons and reveal insider training secrets about new, never-before-seen dragons.
documents.plot: So you want to be a dragon trainer do you? Prepare yourself for adventure, excitement and training as Hiccup, Astrid, Toothless and Gobber tell the legend behind the Book of Dragons and reveal insider training secrets about new, never-before-seen dragons.

documents.title: The Smurfs: A Christmas Carol
documents.overview: When Grouchy Smurf behaves badly to everyone and refuses to celebrate Christmas, the Smurfs of Christmas Past, Present and Future teach him to appreciate Christmas.
documents.plot:
The Smurfs: A Christmas Carol is a 2011 American animated short film based on the Smurfs comics created by the Belgian artist Peyo and adapted from Charles Dickens's 1843 novella A Christmas Carol. Directed by Troy Quane from a script by Todd Berger, it was produced by Sony Pictures Animation, with animation by Sony Pictures Imageworks and Duck Studios. The voice cast includes George Lopez as Grouchy Smurf, Jack Angel as Papa Smurf, Melissa Sturm as Smurfette, and Fred Armisen, Gary Basaraba, Anton Yelchin and Hank Azaria.

On Christmas Eve, the Smurfs prepare for their holiday celebration. Grouchy refuses to take part and declares that he hates Christmas, to everyone's dismay. Papa Smurf brews a potion intended to restore Grouchy's festive spirit, and it ends up in Grouchy's mug of smurfberry nog. After drinking it he passes out, and when he wakes, the world around him, and he himself, has turned into hand-drawn animation.

Smurfette appears as the Smurf of Christmas Past and shows him earlier holidays, when Grouchy, longing for a hang glider, was disappointed year after year to receive yet another new hat from Papa Smurf, until a prank by Jokey made him lose his temper and turn against Christmas. Brainy, as the Smurf of Christmas Present, reveals how Grouchy's refusal to help has forced the others to take on extra work, leading Clumsy to set the tree on fire, and shows Papa lovingly crafting each Smurf's hat. Hefty, as the Smurf of Christmas Future, warns that if Grouchy does not change, the Smurfs will wander into the forest trying to cheer him up and fall into the clutches of Gargamel and his cat Azrael.

Grouchy wakes on Christmas morning transformed, admits he was wrong and realizes that the holiday is about a family that loves him. Papa gives him his gift first, a hat made especially for him, and after placing the star on the tree Grouchy uses it as a makeshift hang glider before crash-landing in the snow, joking that he hates that Christmas comes only once a year.

The short's hand-drawn sequence was based on Peyo's original designs. Melissa Sturm voiced Smurfette in place of Katy Perry, who was unavailable because of her concert tour. The short was released on DVD on December 2, 2011, as part of a holiday gift set with The Smurfs, and as a stand-alone DVD in 2013.

documents.title: TEKKEN: Blood Vengeance
documents.original_title: 鉄拳 ブラッド・ベンジェンス
documents.tagline: The power to change everything. A fate they were not prepared for.
documents.overview: Set in the rich Tekken universe, Tekken: Blood Vengeance 3D follows Xiaoyu Ling, seasoned martial artist and high school student, tasked by the G Corporation to infiltrate an international school in Kyoto to gather information on the mysterious student Shin Kamiya. Before she can make any progress in the investigation, Shin is kidnapped by an unknown assailant. Digging deeper into Shin’s background in an attempt to rescue him, Xiaoyu learns about the frightening underbelly of the Mishima Zaibatsu. Jin Kazama, Kazuya Mishima… and the late Heihachi Mishima’s conspiracy that’s stained with blood.

documents.title: Gone
documents.tagline: No one believes her. Nothing will stop her.
documents.overview: Jill Conway is trying to rebuild her life after surviving a terrifying kidnapping attempt. Though she is having a difficult time, she takes small steps toward normalcy by starting a new job and inviting her sister, Molly, to move in with her. Returning home from work one morning, Jill discovers that Molly has vanished, and she is certain that the same man who previously abducted her has returned for revenge.
documents.plot:
Gone is a 2012 American thriller directed by Heitor Dhalia from a screenplay by Allison Burnett, starring Amanda Seyfried. Her casting in the lead was announced in February 2011. Set in Portland, Oregon, the story follows a young woman whose claims about a serial killer have never been believed and who must find him herself when her sister disappears.

A year earlier, Jill Conway was abducted by a brutal killer and held in a pit among the remains of his previous victims. She escaped, but because she had once been institutionalized, the police concluded that the attack never happened. Now she shares a house with her sister, Molly, and works as a waitress at the Lucky Star Diner. Returning home after work, Jill finds that Molly has vanished. The police again dismiss her, with the exception of Detective Hood, who has just joined the homicide unit, so Jill sets out to investigate on her own.

Following a trail of clues, Jill learns that a locksmith's van was parked outside her home overnight, rented by the owner's son, Nick, to a man calling himself Digger. A receipt leads her to a hardware store and then to the Royal Hotel, where she discovers that his real name is Jim LaPointe and finds duct tape, pet food and matches from her own diner in his abandoned room. Getting his phone number from her coworker Sharon, she calls him, and he directs her to a remote spot in Forest Park, insisting he does not have Molly. Meanwhile Molly, who had been held under Jill's own house, breaks free and tells the police what happened, proving that Jill was right all along. In the woods Jill photographs the remains of earlier victims and finds the hole where she was once kept. LaPointe attacks her; she shoots him and, after he admits he took Molly as bait to lure her back, pours kerosene into the pit and sets him on fire despite his pleas. At home she tells the police that the man existed only in her head, but an anonymous package containing photographs of the victims and a map to the grave later arrives at the police department.

The film was poorly received. Rotten Tomatoes reported 12% approval, Metacritic scored it 36 and CinemaScore audiences gave it a C+; critics found it formulaic and forgettable, although one reviewer found Seyfried as reliable as anyone could hope. It was a box office disappointment, grossing about $18.1 million worldwide.

documents.title: Aliens vs Avatars
documents.overview: Six college friends blowing off steam on a camping trip, find themselves caught up in a cat and mouse hunt with an Alien monster. Not knowing what to do or who to trust, they struggle to protect themselves. Reluctantly, they join forces with another, seemingly friendly, alien, Ava, who orbits the Earth and appears to them in the form of an avatar. Having only one chance at stopping the monster, they must race to locate and repair the Ava’s earth sent robot, before it slaughters them one by one.
documents.plot:
Aliens vs Avatars is a 2011 American low-budget science fiction horror film directed by Lewis Schoenbrun from a script credited to Ted Chalmers and David S. Sterling, produced by Sterling Entertainment and Tom Cat Films. A mockbuster riffing on the titles of Alien vs. Predator and James Cameron's Avatar, it follows a conflict between a vicious alien species and shape-shifting extraterrestrials, with six college friends caught in the middle. Its distributor, Summer Hill Entertainment, later retitled it Alien vs. Alien.

Six college friends head into the wilderness on a camping trip to blow off steam, only to find themselves the quarry of a monstrous alien that begins hunting them in a deadly game of cat and mouse. Unsure what they are facing or whom to trust, the group struggles to defend itself as the creature closes in. Help appears in the form of Ava, another, seemingly friendly alien who orbits the Earth and can reach them only by appearing in the form of an avatar. Reluctantly joining forces with her, the survivors learn that they have just one chance to stop the monster: they must find and repair the robot Ava has sent down to Earth before the creature slaughters them one by one.

The cast is led by Jason Lockhart as Tyler, Kim Argetsinger as Jesse and Cassie Fliegel as Ava, with Dylan Vox as Jake, Marlene Mc'Cohen as Tiffany, Ginny You as Dana and Georgina Tolentino as Crystal. The film was shot in Los Angeles in the summer of 2010, while Schoenbrun was finishing post-production on The Amazing Bulk; he considered it the harder production of the two because of its many shooting locations.

The film received no theatrical release and was issued directly to video, DVD and television on 20 September 2011, becoming Schoenbrun's most widely released film that year. Reviews were overwhelmingly negative. The horror blogger Baron Craze dismissed its dialogue as half-baked drivel and found it boring, and Richard Scheib called it only marginally better made than the kind of film teenagers shoot on a camcorder over successive weekends, though it found some fans on home video in Japan. In 2012 Tom Cat Films sued hundreds of anonymous "John Doe" defendants in U.S. federal court for allegedly downloading the film illegally, a suit that commentators described as copyright trolling.

documents.title: The Apparition
documents.tagline: Once you believe, you die.
documents.overview: Plagued by frightening occurrences in their home, Kelly and Ben learn that a university's parapsychology experiment produced an entity that is now haunting them. The malevolent spirit feeds on fear and torments the couple no matter where they run. Desperate, Kelly and Ben turn to a paranormal researcher, but even with his aid, it may already be too late to save themselves from the terrifying presence.
documents.plot:
On May 21, 1973, six people conduct The Charles Experiment, a parapsychological experiment, in which they stare at a drawing of a deceased man, Charles Reamer, hoping to summon his spirit. Years later, four college students, Patrick (Tom Felton), Lydia (Julianna Guill), Ben (Sebastian Stan) and Greg (Luke Pasqualino) attempt to recreate the Charles Experiment on a larger scale by using modern technology. During the experiment, something attacks the students and pulls Lydia into the wall vanishing.
Some time later, Ben and his girlfriend Kelly (Ashley Greene) are living together. One evening, they discover strange burn marks on their counters. Kelly finds both doors wide open, even though they had locked them. They decide to change the locks and install surveillance cameras. Later, Kelly finds a large amount of mold and spores on the laundry room floor while Ben finds even more in a crawlspace. Ben gets 36 "urgent" emails from Patrick that first inform him of a new attempt at the Charles Experiment, followed by a warning that "containment failed" and finally "you are in danger".
After witnessing an apparition, the couple go to a hotel, but they are attacked there as well. As they flee, they receive a call from Patrick and meet him. Patrick explains that the initial experiment enabled a malevolent entity to enter their world, but that he has built a room surrounded by a negative current that he believes protects him from it. They return to Kelly and Ben's house to try a new experiment to contain the entity. During the experiment, the house begins to shake and break apart, then abruptly stops. While Kelly and Ben are outside, Patrick is pulled into the darkness and vanishes. Unable to find Patrick, they flee to the safety chamber in his house.
Inside the house, they hear Patrick's personal log being played back, including information about the members of the original experiment. Of the original six, two died, one committed suicide and the other three disappeared. After entering the safety chamber, Ben disappears. Kelly exits the chamber and finds Ben's contorted corpse. Patrick's narration explains that the entity gets stronger with each person it claims, and that it will wear its victims down until they are too weak to resist.
With no escape, Kelly wanders around, and enters an empty Costco. She walks to the camping section, enters a tent and waits to be killed by the entity, having fully given up resisting. A number of hands appear from behind and the entity slowly grabs hold of her as the movie cuts to black.

documents.title: Children Who Chase Lost Voices
documents.tagline: A journey to say goodbye.
documents.overview: The film centers on Asuna, a young girl who spends her solitary days listening to the mysterious music emanating from the crystal radio she received from her late father as a memento. One day while walking home she is attacked by a fearsome monster and saved mysterious boy named Shun. However, Shun disappears and Asuna embarks on a journey of adventure to the land of Agartha with her teacher Mr. Morisaki to meet a Shun again. Through her journey she comes to know the cruelty and beauty of the world, as well as loss.
