documents.title: In the Land of Blood and Honey
documents.original_title: In the Land of Blood and Honey
documents.tagline: Love can change what we want… war can change who we are
documents.overview: During the Bosnian War, Danijel, a soldier fighting for the Serbs, re-encounters Ajla, a Bosnian who's now a captive in his camp he oversees. Their once promising connection has become ambiguous as their motives have changed.
documents.plot:
In Sarajevo, 1992, Ajla Ekmečić is an ethnic Bosniak artist and lives with her sister, Lejla, who is a single mother of a baby boy. One evening, she meets her boyfriend, ethnic Serb police officer Danijel Vukojević, at a club. They enjoy the evening together, but many of the patrons are killed and Danijel is badly injured when the club is destroyed by artillery fire, signifying the opening salvo of the Bosnian War.
Some months later, Ajla and Lejla prepare to flee the now besieged city, but their neighborhood is occupied by the Army of Republika Srpska before they can escape. The men are separated from the women to be executed while Ajla and several other younger, more attractive women are taken away on buses to a Serb rape camp.
In the camp, the soldiers instruct the women on what life will be like and then ask the women what sort of duties they can perform. A doctor named Esma volunteers to perform medical services. Another woman says she can sew; rather than use her skills, an officer rapes her in front of the other women to demoralize them. Before another soldier can do the same to Ajla, the camp's commander takes her away, where it is revealed he is none other than Danijel.
The former couple struggle to grasp the magnitude of their predicament, especially given that inter-ethnic relationships are forbidden, and any evidence of such a relationship could compromise both Danijel and his father Nebojša, a General of the VRS Main Staff. Danijel tells Ajla that to shelter her from sexual abuse at the hands of the other soldiers, he has said that she is his "personal property." Danijel quickly learns he is to be transferred to another military base in Sarajevo, and tells Ajla how to escape in his absence. She succeeds the second time.
Ajla shelters herself in the forest outside the city, where she is found by Bosniak guerrilla forces, who take her back to their camp. In the camp, she happily reunites with Lejla, though this happiness is short-lived when Lejla informs her that her baby was murdered by Bosnian Serb forces some months earlier, sending her into inconsolable grief. Over a campfire, the guerrillas lament the paradoxical insanity of the war, one in particular pointing out that despite the events of the war, he cannot hate all Serbs as his mother is a Serb. Lejla then agrees, and says she only hates the nationalistic Serbs. At this moment, it's found out that Ajla was Danijel's prisoner and lover, and the guerrillas concoct a plan for her to get captured by Danijel's men in order to gain proximity to him, and therefore act as a mole.
Falling for the bait, Danijel orders his men to capture Ajla under the guise of her being Danijel's painter. They end up rekindling their relationship, but Danijel's orders to his men to leave her alone are deemed suspicious. Thus, Nebojša learns of Ajla's existence and the special treatment she receives. While Danijel is at the front line, Nebojša visits Ajla and orders her to paint a portrait of him.

documents.title: Pastorela
documents.overview: Agent Jesus Juarez (aka Chucho) has always played the Devil in his town's Nativity Play. This Christmas, when the new pastor of the church recasts the role, the two men engage in a battle between good and evil.
documents.plot:
Pastorela is a 2011 Mexican Christmas black comedy written and directed by Emilio Portes, his second feature after the award-winning black comedy Conozca la cabeza de Juan Pérez. A Las Producciones del Patrón production made with support from IMCINE and FIDECINE, it stars Joaquín Cosío as Jesús "Chucho" Juárez, Carlos Cobos as Father Edmundo Posadas and Eduardo España as Vulmaro, with Ana Serradilla as a nun, Dagoberto Gama as a police commander, Melissa Bahnsen as Magdalena, Héctor Jiménez as a possessed man, José Sefami as "El Tuerto", Silverio Palacios as Doctor Godínez and Eduardo Manzano as a cardinal.

Chucho Juárez is a judicial agent of the federal police who lives with his daughter Magdalena in the Mexico City neighborhood of San Miguel de Nenepilco. For as long as he can remember, he has played the Devil every year in the parish pastorela, the traditional Nativity play organized by Father Benito. This Christmas, however, things change. While Chucho is busy investigating the murder of a deputy prosecutor, he fails to notice that Father Benito has suffered a fatal heart attack in the middle of an affair with a nun, and he misses the casting session held by the new parish priest, the exorcist Edmundo Posadas. The newcomer leaves him out of the play and gives the coveted role of the Devil to Vulmaro, Chucho's compadre. Unwilling to give up a part he regards as his by tradition, the policeman launches a fierce struggle against the priest, a classic battle between good and evil in which both men go to any lengths, tearing apart the venerable tradition along the way.

Portes, a graduate of the Centro de Capacitación Cinematográfica, reworked the script in a 2007 screenwriting workshop supervised by the writer Vicente Leñero, and the film was shot between December 2008 and February 2009. He described it as an acid, unbridled comedy with touches of police action and fantasy, and as a portrait of a society that loves to live by its traditions and their absurdity, adding that he hoped the main characters would move beyond the archetypes of cop and priest to become more complex and endearing. Pastorela opened in Mexico on 11 November 2011 and was released in the United States by Pantelion. At the 54th Ariel Awards in 2012 it received fourteen nominations and was the big winner, taking best picture, best director and best original screenplay along with costume design, makeup and visual effects awards.
production_companies: Fondo de Inversión y Estímulos al Cine (FIDECINE)

documents.title: The Watch
documents.tagline: Got protection?
documents.overview: Four everyday suburban guys come together as an excuse to escape their humdrum lives one night a week. But when they accidentally discover that their town has become overrun with aliens posing as ordinary suburbanites, they have no choice but to save their neighborhood - and the world - from total extermination.
documents.plot:
The Watch is a 2012 American science fiction comedy film directed by Akiva Schaffer and written by Rafe Young. The movie stars Ben Stiller, Vince Vaughn, Jonah Hill, and Richard Ayoade.

The story begins with Evan Treborn (Ben Stiller), a suburban father who has just moved to the suburbs with his wife, Trish (Vicky Krieps). Evan is excited to start a new life but soon discovers that he's not alone in the neighborhood. He meets his neighbors, Jay (Jonah Hill) and Steve (Richard Ayoade), who are both eccentric and paranoid.

The three men form an unlikely friendship as they try to protect their homes from an alien invasion. They soon discover that aliens have landed on Earth and are planning to destroy humanity. The aliens, known as the "Slugs," are small, slimy creatures that can blend into human society and are nearly invisible.

As the Slugs begin to infiltrate the neighborhood, Evan, Jay, and Steve must band together to stop them. Along the way, they encounter a series of wacky misadventures, including a run-in with a group of bumbling Slugs who are trying to take over a local convenience store.

Throughout the movie, the three main characters struggle with their own personal demons. Evan is a suburban dad trying to balance his family life with his desire for adventure and excitement. Jay is a slacker who has lost touch with reality, while Steve is a socially awkward scientist who is obsessed with aliens.

As the Slugs become more aggressive in their attacks, the three men must put aside their differences and work together to save humanity. Along the way, they discover that the Slugs are not just mindless monsters but rather a complex species with their own culture and motivations.

In the end, Evan, Jay, and Steve come up with a plan to defeat the Slugs by using a combination of science and humor. The movie ends with a comedic twist as the three men successfully defeat the aliens, but not before they realize that they've become more like each other than they ever thought possible.

Overall, The Watch is a hilarious and action-packed comedy that explores themes of friendship, paranoia, and the absurdity of modern life. With its talented cast and witty script, the movie is sure to delight fans of science fiction and comedy alike.

documents.title: Friends with Kids
documents.tagline: Love. Happiness. Kids. Pick two.
documents.overview: In the wake of their friends' marriages and eventual offspring, longtime pals Julie and Jason decide to have a child together without becoming a couple. By becoming "time-share" parents, they reason, they can experience the joys of parenthood without significantly curbing their personal freedom. However, when Julie and Jason both become involved with others, they discover that they secretly harbor romantic feelings for each other.
documents.plot:
Jason (an advertising executive) and Julie (a charitable investment advisor) are longtime best friends now in their mid-30s that live in the same building in Manhattan. Not romantically involved, they are close friends with two childless married couples, the placid Alex and Leslie and the sex-obsessed Ben and Missy.
During the next four years, after both couples have children, their marriages suffer. Following a chaotic birthday party for Jason at Alex and Leslie's place in Brooklyn, Jason and Julie discuss how it would be better to have children first, to 'get it out of the way' since 'time is running out', and only then meet the person that you wanted to marry.
After more discussion, Jason and Julie decide to have a child together, despite never having had romantic feelings for each other, and then to continue to date other people, to find 'their one'. Although their friends predict disaster, they adjust to their new relationship with baby Joe far better than their friends had imagined.
Jason and Julie begin dating again and enter into budding relationships with young actress Mary Jane and divorced father Kurt, respectively. During a couples winter getaway in Vermont, Ben calls Jason and Julie's thought process and parenting skills into question. In the ensuing argument, Ben decries their arrangement as untenable in the long term and humiliates Missy. Jason defends his decision to have a child with Julie, saying that he loves her deeply and that she was the soundest choice of person for him to start a family with.
After returning from Vermont, Ben and Missy separate and later divorce. Shortly thereafter, at Julie's birthday dinner out (about 18 months after Joe's birth), Jason is surprised to find that she invited only him. Julie tells him that Kurt wants her to meet his children that weekend but that this new degree of commitment has made her realize that she is in love with Jason, who, along with Joe, have become her closest family.
A stunned Jason tells Julie that his love for her has never been romantic and has asked Mary Jane to move in with him. Heartbroken, Julie leaves the restaurant, and soon moves out of her Manhattan apartment to Brooklyn, putting some space between herself and Jason. A few months thereafter, Jason and Mary Jane break up over their differing feelings about children, and both Julie and Jason return to dating others.
Several months later, at a bar with Ben, Jason confides that he does have feelings for Julie, but that their messy split makes acting on such feelings impossible. Ben disagrees, noting the differences between his and Missy's sex-based relationship and Jason and Julie's long-lasting friendship.

documents.title: Ender's Game
documents.tagline: This is not a game.
documents.overview: Based on the classic novel by Orson Scott Card, Ender's Game is the story of the Earth's most gifted children training to defend their homeplanet in the space wars of the future.
documents.plot:
Ender's Game is a science fiction film directed by Gavin Hood, based on the novel of the same name by Orson Scott Card. The movie was released in 2013 and produced by Gavin Hood, Gail Katz, and Ted Field.

The story takes place in a future where humanity is under attack by an alien species known as the Formics. To counter this threat, the International Fleet (IF) has been searching for a commander who can lead the war effort against the Formics. The IF discovers a young boy named Andrew "Ender" Wiggin, who is six years old and has exceptional intelligence.

Ender's mother, Mazer Rackham, was a renowned military commander who led the IF to victory in the first contact with the Formics. However, she died shortly after the war, leaving behind her three children: Peter, Valentine, and Ender. The International Fleet takes Ender away from his family and enrolls him in Battle School, a rigorous training program designed to prepare young students for command.

At Battle School, Ender is forced to fight against other students in simulated battles, known as "games." He quickly rises through the ranks due to his exceptional strategic thinking and leadership skills. However, Ender struggles with the moral implications of war and the pressure to conform to the IF's expectations.

As Ender progresses through the games, he forms close relationships with his fellow students, including Bean, a talented but awkward student who becomes one of Ender's closest friends. Meanwhile, Valentine, Ender's older sister, begins to question the morality of the war effort and the IF's motives.

The final game pits Ender against the most skilled opponents in the school, including a ruthless commander named Graff. In the end, Ender emerges victorious but at great emotional cost. He is forced to confront the harsh realities of war and the true nature of his training.

After graduating from Battle School, Ender is promoted to command a fleet of ships against the Formics. However, he soon realizes that the IF has been manipulating him throughout his training, using him as a pawn in their own game. The film ends with Ender's realization that he was used to lead a suicidal mission against the Formics, and that he may have become the very thing he was trained to destroy.

The movie received mixed reviews from critics but was praised for its visual effects and performances by Asa Butterfield as Ender Wiggin. However, some fans of the book criticized the film's adaptation, feeling that it did not accurately capture the complexity and nuance of Orson Scott Card's novel.

documents.title: The Impossible
documents.tagline: Nothing is more powerful than the human spirit.
documents.overview: In December 2004, close-knit family Maria, Henry and their three sons begin their winter vacation in Thailand. But the day after Christmas, the idyllic holiday turns into an incomprehensible nightmare when a terrifying roar rises from the depths of the sea, followed by a wall of black water that devours everything in its path. Though Maria and her family face their darkest hour, unexpected displays of kindness and courage ameliorate their terror.
documents.plot:
In December 2004, Dr. Maria Bennett, her husband Henry, and their three sons — Lucas, Thomas, and Simon — go on holiday to Khao Lak, Thailand. Arriving on Christmas Eve, they settle in and begin to enjoy the new Orchid Beach Resort. Two days later, the Indian Ocean tsunami inundates the area. Maria and Lucas manage to survive the deluge by clinging to debris, though Maria sustains serious injuries to her leg and chest. They help a toddler, Daniel, and are soon found by locals who transfer them to a hospital in the city of Takua Pa. Daniel is separated from them during the journey. At the hospital, Maria encourages Lucas to help others find their family members while she goes into surgery.
Meanwhile, Henry and the two younger boys have also survived and are together. Henry leaves Simon and Thomas with another family who are then taken to the mountains for safety by local relief crews. Henry stays behind to search for Maria and Lucas in the rubble. While out looking, injured and alone, he is picked up by a passer-by and driven to a nearby bus station with other survivors.
Communication facilities are scarce but a German tourist named Karl, who has also been separated from his family, lends Henry his cell phone. Henry calls Maria's father and promises him that he will look everywhere for Maria and Lucas. Karl volunteers to accompany Henry in his search and to look for his own family, who were at the beach when the tsunami hit.
While Maria is in surgery, her medical chart is mixed up with that of a woman named Muriel Barnes, who has died. Lucas returns to find his mother's bed empty and is then taken to a tent where children without families are kept safe. He assumes his mother is dead and is devastated by that. The mistake is discovered when Lucas cannot identify any of the dead woman's jewelry and he is subsequently reunited with his mother, who had been moved to a private room in the ICU. While he waits in the hospital, Lucas sees Daniel, who has been reunited with his father. Henry and Karl search for their families in various places before they arrive at the hospital, where Henry is given five minutes to look. Karl gives him a piece of paper with the names of his family members.
A vehicle carrying Simon and Thomas also stops outside the hospital and the boys get off so Simon can urinate. From a distance, Lucas recognizes his father and while searching for him in the chaotic crowd outside, Lucas's brothers spot him and they reunite. Henry finds the three of them together. He learns that Maria remains in the hospital, ready to undergo more surgery for her leg. As the anesthesia puts her to sleep, Maria experiences flashbacks of how she came to be injured and how she surfaced the water. While she is in surgery, Lucas tells Henry he has something really important to tell Maria.
The following day, the family boards an ambulance airplane to Singapore so Maria may receive further medical treatment.

documents.title: [REC]³ Genesis
documents.tagline: You may kiss the bride.
documents.overview: A pair of newlyweds must fight to survive when their wedding reception descends into chaos and carnage when their guests become infected by a virus that turns them into hungry zombies.
documents.plot:
[REC]³ Genesis is a 2012 Spanish action horror film directed and co-written by Paco Plaza. The third installment in the [REC] series, it largely abandons the found-footage format of the earlier films and runs concurrently with the first. Diego Martín and Leticia Dolera star as Koldo and Clara, newlyweds whose reception is overrun by the series' infection.

At their reception at a country estate, a veterinarian recently bitten by a dog turns violent, and the infection spreads through the party. The couple are separated in the chaos. Koldo hides in the kitchen with his cousin Adrián, Clara's sister Tita, the wedding photographer Atun and a copyright inspector nicknamed "Royalties", and all but the heavyset Atun escape through the air ducts. Outside, Royalties is killed by an infected policeman. The survivors take refuge in a chapel the infected cannot enter. Over the public address system, Koldo hears Clara say that she is alive and pregnant, and he sets out to find her.

Clara, hiding in the security room with the priest, flees with friends Rafa and Natalie while the priest holds off the infected with prayer. Koldo reaches the security room just in time to watch Adrián, Tita, his grandmother and others being killed. Natalie is bitten, and the entertainer "Sponge John" shoots Clara's infected mother before being bitten himself. Hearing a song Koldo is playing in the ballroom, Clara turns back, takes up a chainsaw and fights her way through the crowd, and is forced to kill Rafa after he is bitten. The reunited couple are surrounded until the priest's voice reading scripture over the speakers paralyzes the infected. In the garden, however, Clara is bitten by Koldo's grandfather, who is immune to the prayer because he is deaf. Koldo amputates her arm to stop the infection, but it fails. At the estate gates, surrounded by police and a GEO special operations unit, the couple share a last kiss before Clara turns and bites him, and both are shot dead holding hands.

Filmax greenlit the third and fourth films in 2010. Unlike the earlier installments, they were directed separately, with Plaza making Genesis and Jaume Balagueró the fourth. It was shot in Barcelona in 2011. The film premiered at the Grand Rex in Paris, screened at South by Southwest and opened in Spain on 30 March 2012. Reviews were mixed. Rotten Tomatoes reported 40% approval, faulting the loss of the handheld style. [REC] 4: Apocalypse followed in 2014.

documents.title: Madagascar 3: Europe's Most Wanted
documents.tagline: They Have One Shot to Get Back Home.
documents.overview: Animal pals Alex, Marty, Melman, and Gloria are still trying to make it back to New York's Central Park Zoo. They are forced to take a detour to Europe to find the penguins and chimps who broke the bank at a Monte Carlo casino. When French animal-control officer Capitaine Chantel DuBois picks up their scent, Alex and company are forced to hide out in a traveling circus.
documents.plot:
Madagascar 3: Europe's Most Wanted is a 2012 animated musical comedy film produced by DreamWorks Animation. The movie serves as the third installment in the Madagascar film series.

The story begins with Alex the lion (voiced by Ben Stiller), Marty the zebra (voiced by Chris Rock), Gloria the hippopotamus (voiced by Jada Pinkett Smith), and Melman the giraffe (voiced by David Schwimmer) living on a traveling circus, led by Stefano the lion tamer. However, their lives are turned upside down when they discover that the circus is in danger of being shut down due to financial difficulties.

The group decides to embark on a journey to Europe, where they hope to find a new home for the circus and save it from extinction. Along the way, they meet a new character, Vitaly (voiced by Sacha Baron Cohen), a Russian circus performer who becomes an ally to the group.

Upon arriving in Europe, the group discovers that Vitaly is being pursued by Interpol agents, led by Captain Chantel DuBois (voiced by Frances McDormand). The agents believe that Vitaly is wanted for his involvement in a jewel heist. However, it is revealed that Vitaly is actually innocent and has been framed.

As the group navigates through Europe, they face various challenges and obstacles, including being pursued by the Interpol agents and dealing with their own personal struggles. Meanwhile, Alex begins to question his identity as a lion and his role in the circus.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when the group discovers that Vitaly's real target is a valuable diamond necklace worth millions of dollars. The group decides to help Vitaly clear his name and find the real thief.

In the end, the group successfully outsmarts the Interpol agents and retrieves the stolen necklace. However, in the process, they also discover that the true mastermind behind the heist is none other than Stefano, who had been seeking revenge against the circus for abandoning him.

The movie concludes with the group returning to New York City, where they are welcomed back as heroes. Alex finally finds his place in the circus and comes to terms with his identity as a lion. The movie ends on a high note, with the group performing a musical number together, celebrating their newfound freedom and happiness.

Overall, Madagascar 3: Europe's Most Wanted is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of identity, friendship, and redemption. With its catchy musical numbers and lovable characters, it is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Get the Gringo
documents.tagline: The odds are against him. So is everyone else.
documents.overview: A career criminal nabbed by Mexican authorities is placed in a tough prison where he learns to survive with the help of a 9-year-old boy.
documents.plot: A career criminal nabbed by Mexican authorities is placed in a tough prison where he learns to survive with the help of a 9-year-old boy.

documents.title: In the Name of the King 2: Two Worlds
documents.original_title: In the Name of the King 2: Two Worlds
documents.tagline: Fight to the End
documents.overview: Granger, an ex-Special Forces soldier gets thrown back to medieval times to fulfill an ancient prophecy. Venturing through the now war torn Kingdom of Ehb, he teams up with an unlikely band of allies with the goal of slaying the leader of the "Dark Ones". Fighting against all odds, they must free the land from the grasp of the evil tyrant Raven and save the world.
documents.plot:
In the Name of the King 2: Two Worlds is a 2011 fantasy adventure film directed by Uwe Boll and the sequel to In the Name of the King: A Dungeon Siege Tale (2007), which starred Jason Statham. Dolph Lundgren stars as Granger, a former special forces soldier, with Natassia Malthe, Lochlyn Munro, Aleks Paunovic and Natalie Burn. Shot in British Columbia, it was released on DVD and Blu-ray in the United States and Canada on 27 December 2011, with a 3D version included in the German Blu-ray edition.

Granger, a veteran of the special forces, lives a quiet life in modern-day Vancouver until a group of hooded assassins attack him in his home. After fighting them off, he is pulled through a time portal and finds himself hundreds of years in the past, in the forested medieval Kingdom of Ehb, a land torn apart by war. He learns that he is the subject of an ancient prophecy that foretells the arrival of a warrior from another world who will save the kingdom.

Reluctantly accepting his role, Granger joins an unlikely band of allies, including a female healer known as Manhattan, who accompanies him on his quest. His task is to destroy the leader of the sinister Dark Ones, a witch known only as the Holy Mother, whose power threatens the realm. As he travels through the war-ravaged countryside, Granger fights monsters, assassins and enemy soldiers, using both his modern military training and the medieval weapons of his new surroundings. Along the way he must earn the trust of his companions, who are suspicious of the strange warrior and his modern ways. Fighting against overwhelming odds, Granger must free the land from the evil tyrant Raven, save the kingdom from destruction and find a way to return to his own time.

The film received negative reviews, as was typical of Boll's films, with critics deriding its low budget, script and effects, although some reviewers noted that Lundgren brought a degree of conviction to the role. It was followed by a third installment, In the Name of the King 3: The Last Mission (2014), also directed by Boll.

documents.title: Fullmetal Alchemist the Movie: The Sacred Star of Milos
documents.original_title: 鋼の錬金術師 嘆きの丘（ミロス）の聖なる星
documents.tagline: Finally tell the story of forbidden bonds
documents.overview: After a mysterious prisoner with only a few weeks left on his sentence breaks out of prison in Central City, the Elric brothers attempt to track him down. The search leads them to Table City in the southwestern country of Creta, where Alphonse rescues a young alchemist named Julia from the very man they are trying to capture. In the thick of the fight, they literally tumble into Julia's home turf, the slums of Milos Valley, and are embroiled in the grassroots rebellion of her people.
documents.plot:
Fullmetal Alchemist: The Sacred Star of Milos (Japanese: 鋼の錬金術師 嘆きの丘の聖なる星) is a 2011 Japanese animated fantasy action film based on Hiromu Arakawa's manga Fullmetal Alchemist. Produced by Bones following the success of the television series Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood and directed by Kazuya Murata, it features Romi Park as Edward Elric and Rie Kugimiya as his brother Alphonse, with Maaya Sakamoto, Toshiyuki Morikawa and Sakiko Tamagawa. It premiered in Japan on 2 July 2011, with audiences receiving an exclusive manga booklet, and was licensed by Funimation for release in North America in 2012.

The Elric brothers, Edward and Alphonse, pursue an escaped convict, Melvin Voyager, who uses an unusual form of alchemy, but he gets away. They learn that he escaped with only two months of his sentence remaining, and among his belongings they find a newspaper page from which a photograph has been cut. The missing image shows Julia Crichton, a young woman arrested for illegally entering Table City, a remote town on the border between Amestris and the neighboring country of Creta.

Intrigued, the brothers travel to Table City aboard a prison train, which is attacked by a wolf-chimera and by the Black Bats, flying fighters seeking to free what they believe are Milosian prisoners. Pursuing Melvin, the Elrics reach a prison, where he breaks through the walls to find Julia, and Miranda, the leader of the Black Bats, also tries to rescue her. Julia and Al fall into the Valley, a slum in the vast chasm surrounding Table City where the oppressed Milos people live, and Melvin reveals his true identity. The brothers learn that the Milosians, whose land was taken by Creta and Amestris, dream of reclaiming their homeland, and that their hopes rest on a legendary object known as the Sacred Star of Milos. As the Elrics become involved in the Milosians' struggle, they discover a terrible secret about the source of the star's power and a plot involving a dangerous form of alchemy.

The film received mixed reviews. Critics praised its animation, action sequences and the voice cast's return, but many felt it was a standard side story that added little to the franchise and that its new characters lacked depth compared with those of Brotherhood.

documents.title: Winx Club: The Secret of the Lost Kingdom
documents.original_title: Winx Club - Il segreto del regno perduto
documents.overview: Sixteen years ago the most powerful warrior wizards of the Magic Dimension sacrificed themselves to fight against absolute evil. Now the fate of a kingdom is in the hands of a young girl - Bloom, the fairy of the Dragon's flame. Accompanied by her Winx Club girlfriends, Bloom must overcome the greatest challenge of all: enter the depths of the obscure dimension, fight against evil to bring her parents back to life and reveal the mystery linked to her origins. The destiny of the entire Magic Dimension depends on the outcome of this conflict.

documents.title: Kung Fu Panda: Secrets of the Masters
documents.original_title: Kung Fu Panda: Secrets of the Masters
documents.overview: Po and the Furious Five uncover the legend of three of kung fu's greatest heroes: Master Thundering Rhino, Master Storming Ox, and Master Croc.
documents.plot:
Some time after saving China from being conquered by Lord Shen, during the night, under the pretense of an emergency, Po leads Tigress and Mantis in breaking into the new Masters' Council exhibit, in tribute of Masters Thundering Rhino, Storming Ox and Croc. Although Tigress and Mantis are annoyed at the deception, Po engages their interest in the story of how the trio of masters first met.
Long ago, in the city of Jinzhou, where kung fu was practiced for the sport of street fighting, Rhino, Ox and Croc were small-time pit fighters who attracted the attention of Master Oogway, who, seeing their talent and focus, wished them to find something worthy for which to fight. As the trio fought to a standstill, two of the villainous Wu Sisters were freeing their leader and eldest sister, Su Wu. To recapture them, Oogway persuades Rhino, Ox and Croc to help him find the sisters at Hubei Volcano. However, to his disappointment, Oogway has to appeal to them with vague prospects of being put on a path to riches to get that cooperation.
While the Wu Sisters plot to unite the various criminal gangs to seize control of China, Oogway has to brush off each of his compatriot's petty proposals during the journey to abandon the others for their benefit. At camp, Oogway discovers that, although Croc and Ox are motivated by narcissism and greed, respectively, Rhino has a deep-seated need to win the respect of his father, Master Flying Rhino. To that, Oogway suggests to all that their current goals will keep them only wanting more, and "changing course" can lead to better lives for all. Before the trio can comprehend Oogway's point, a messenger bird from the Sisters arrives to reveal their plan, and Oogway has the company set off immediately.
To encourage them to change their ways, Oogway secretly leads the trio on an extremely dangerous path across the Bridge of Mists, and forces them to cooperate so they all can safely pass, to illustrate his point of selflessness. However, when the trio finally learns that Oogway's metaphorical promise of riches actually meant "emotional riches", their protests accidentally get them trapped on a river of lava. Oogway manages to get them to safe ground, but he falls over a lava fall, leaving them with only the advice, "Remember the path", to guide them.
Dispirited by their loss, the trio try to find their way home. However, they encounter a rabbit village devastated by the Wu Sisters, and its citizens desperately try to hire them for protection. Moved by the villagers' plight, the trio decline the fee and resolve to stop the Wu Sisters, for the sake of a higher ideal.
The trio interrupt the Wu Sister's summit, and reveal that they are doing this purely for honor, which intimidates the various visiting gangs to retreat, while the Wu Sisters fight alone. Although the Wu Sisters prove too much to fight individually, Rhino, Ox and Croc manage to combine their talents to defeat them in a coordinated attack.

documents.title: Jack the Giant Slayer
documents.tagline: Prepare for a giant adventure
documents.overview: The story of an ancient war that is reignited when a young farmhand unwittingly opens a gateway between our world and a fearsome race of giants. Unleashed on the Earth for the first time in centuries, the giants strive to reclaim the land they once lost, forcing the young man, Jack into the battle of his life to stop them. Fighting for a kingdom, its people, and the love of a brave princess, he comes face to face with the unstoppable warriors he thought only existed in legend–and gets the chance to become a legend himself.
documents.plot:
Jack the Giant Slayer is a 2013 American fantasy adventure film directed by Bryan Singer and written by Darren Lemke, David Koepp, and Christopher McQuarrie. The movie is based on the classic fairy tale "Jack and the Beanstalk" but offers a unique twist on the original story.

The film begins in medieval England, where King Braemar (Ian McShane) is preparing for war against the giant Riddoch (Craig Parkinson). However, before the battle can begin, the king's son Jack (Nicholas Hoult) is kidnapped by the giant. The only way to rescue Jack is to climb up a magical beanstalk that grows in the castle gardens.

Jack sets out on his journey, accompanied by a young woman named Isabelle (Ewan McGregor), who claims to be a skilled warrior. As they ascend the beanstalk, they encounter various obstacles and creatures, including giant spiders and treacherous terrain.

Upon reaching the top of the beanstalk, Jack and Isabelle discover that Riddoch is not just a mindless beast but a complex character with his own motivations and backstory. The giant's true intention is to steal the magical golden harp, which has the power to heal any wound.

As Jack navigates the giant's lair, he also discovers that Riddoch was once a human king who was cursed by an evil sorcerer. The curse transformed him into a giant, and he has been searching for a way to break it ever since.

Meanwhile, back in England, King Braemar is facing his own struggles as he prepares for war against the giants. He must also contend with his own son's disappearance and the pressure from his advisors to launch an attack on the giants before they can be defeated.

As Jack and Isabelle continue their journey, they face numerous challenges and obstacles, including a treacherous path that leads them deeper into the giant's lair. Along the way, Jack also discovers that he has a special connection to the magical harp and that it holds the key to breaking Riddoch's curse.

In the end, Jack and Isabelle successfully defeat Riddoch and shatter the curse that has been cast upon him. The golden harp is recovered, and King Braemar is able to launch a successful attack on the giants. However, the movie ends with a twist: Jack returns home as a hero, but he also carries with him the knowledge of his own destiny and the secrets of the magical world.

Overall, Jack the Giant Slayer offers a unique take on the classic fairy tale, exploring themes of identity, redemption, and the power of music. The film features stunning visuals, impressive action sequences, and a talented cast, making it a must-see for fans of fantasy adventure movies.

documents.title: Rise of the Guardians
documents.tagline: You better believe.
documents.overview: When an evil spirit known as Pitch lays down the gauntlet to take over the world, the immortal Guardians must join forces for the first time to protect the hopes, beliefs and imagination of children all over the world.
documents.plot:
Rise of the Guardians is a 2012 animated fantasy adventure film produced by DreamWorks Animation. The movie takes place in a world where mythical creatures like Santa Claus, the Easter Bunny, the Tooth Fairy, and Jack Frost are real, but they live separate lives, each with their own domain.

The story begins with a young boy named Jack Frost (voiced by Chris Pine), who is struggling to find his place in the world. He's an outcast among humans and mythical creatures alike, as he doesn't quite fit into either category. Meanwhile, the other Guardians are busy preparing for the annual holiday season.

However, a dark force known as Pitch (voiced by Jude Law) threatens to ruin Christmas and the other holidays. Pitch is a malevolent spirit who feeds on children's fears and nightmares, and he seeks to destroy the world of humans and mythical creatures alike.

As Jack Frost navigates his way through this treacherous landscape, he meets Santa Claus (voiced by Alec Baldwin), the Easter Bunny (voiced by Hugh Laurie), the Tooth Fairy (voiced by Isla Fisher), and other Guardians. Together, they form an unlikely alliance to stop Pitch and save Christmas.

Throughout the movie, Jack Frost learns valuable lessons about friendship, belonging, and finding his true purpose in life. Along the way, he also discovers that he has a special connection to the world of humans and mythical creatures, which makes him a unique and powerful ally in the fight against Pitch.

As the story unfolds, the Guardians face numerous challenges and obstacles as they work together to defeat Pitch and save Christmas. The movie features stunning animation, witty humor, and heartwarming moments that make it a delightful treat for audiences of all ages.

Ultimately, the Guardians succeed in defeating Pitch and restoring balance to the world. Jack Frost finds his place among the other Guardians, and he becomes an integral part of their team. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with the Guardians looking forward to a bright future filled with joy, laughter, and adventure.

Overall, Rise of the Guardians is a charming and entertaining film that celebrates the magic of imagination and the power of friendship. With its lovable characters, engaging storyline, and stunning animation, it's a must-see for fans of animated movies and fantasy adventures.

documents.title: Geek Charming
documents.overview: Film geek Josh is looking for the subject of his new documentary when a chance meeting puts the perfect star in his sights—Dylan, his school's most popular junior. But Dylan's hopes of using the film to become Blossom Queen don't quite match with Josh's goal to make a hard-hitting exposé about popularity. Will Josh shoot the film as planned, or show Dylan as the truly interesting person she is?
documents.plot:
In Washington, Dylan Schoenfield is the most popular girl at Woodlands Academy. After accidentally dropping her expensive handbag into a mall fountain, she is surprised when classmate and film enthusiast Josh Rosen retrieves it. In exchange, Dylan agrees to be the subject of Josh's documentary about high school popularity. Hoping the film will boost her campaign to become Blossom Queen, Dylan initially cooperates, but her diva behavior leads to an argument, and Josh removes her from the project.
Determined to make amends, Dylan spends time with Josh and his friends watching a film, after which Josh reinstates her in the documentary. During a visit to Dylan's house, Josh learns that her late mother was crowned Blossom Queen in 1985, revealing Dylan's emotional connection to the title. As the two grow closer, Josh's film club friends resent his increasing time with Dylan, suspecting a crush he denies. When Josh forgets about a math competition to go on a date with another girl, Amy, he seeks Dylan's advice on how to impress her. Dylan invites them to a party hosted by her boyfriend, Asher, but Amy feels out of place. Asher grows jealous, assuming Dylan and Josh are secretly involved. Amy later rejects Josh's invitation to the spring formal, suggesting that his real interest lies with Dylan.
Dylan's social life soon unravels: Asher breaks up with her for "acting like a nerd", and her best friends abandon her when she loses her social status. Meanwhile, Josh's friends replace him as film club president. At the documentary's premiere, Dylan expects the film to improve her popularity, but is humiliated when the audience laughs at her shallow behavior. Believing Josh betrayed her, she storms out before seeing the film's ending, which includes his heartfelt praise of her personal growth.
The next morning, Amy visits Dylan and convinces her to watch the entire film, explaining that it actually portrays her positively. That night at the Spring Formal, Dylan arrives wearing her mother's dress. To her surprise, she is crowned Blossom Queen, just as her mother had been. On stage, Dylan delivers an emotional speech, apologizing for her past behavior and expressing gratitude to Josh and Amy. Afterward, Dylan and Josh reconcile and share a kiss, now fully appreciating each other for who they are.

documents.title: A Lonely Place to Die
documents.tagline: Out here, there's nowhere to hide.
documents.overview: A group of five mountaineers are hiking and climbing in the Scottish Highlands when they discover a young Serbian girl buried in a small chamber in the wilderness. They become caught up in a terrifying game of cat and mouse with the kidnappers as they try to get the girl to safety.

documents.title: 12 Dates of Christmas
documents.tagline: Twelve chances to get it right.
documents.overview: In an attempt to win back her ex-boyfriend on Christmas Eve, Kate ends up ruining her blind date with Miles, a handsome guy she's been set up with. In a strange twist of fate, Kate is given the chance to re-live Christmas Eve twelve times.
documents.plot: In an attempt to win back her ex-boyfriend Jack on Christmas Eve, Kate ends up ruining her blind date with Miles, a handsome guy she's been set up with. In a strange twist of fate, Kate is magically given the chance to re-live Christmas Eve twelve times!

documents.title: Good Luck Charlie, It's Christmas!
documents.tagline: For the Duncan family, Christmas is about to take a major detour.
documents.overview: Teddy Duncan's middle-class family embarks on a road trip from their home in Denver to visit Mrs. Duncans Parents, the Blankenhoopers, in Palm Springs. When they find themselves stranded between Denver and Utah, they try to hitch a ride to Las Vegas with a seemingly normal older couple in a station wagon from Roswell, New Mexico. It turns out that the couple believes they are the victims of alien abduction. The Duncan's must resort to purchasing a clunker Yugo to get to Utah, have their luggage stolen in Las Vegas, and survive a zany Christmas with Grandpa and Grandma Blankenhooper.
documents.plot:
Good Luck Charlie, It's Christmas! is a 2011 American Christmas road comedy television film based on the Disney Channel sitcom Good Luck Charlie, created by Phil Baker and Drew Vaupen. Directed by Arlene Sanford and written by Geoff Rodkey, it stars Bridgit Mendler as Teddy Duncan, Leigh-Allyn Baker as Amy Duncan, Bradley Steven Perry as Gabe, Mia Talerico as Charlie, Eric Allan Kramer as Bob and Jason Dolley as PJ, with Debra Monk and Michael Kagan as Amy's parents. In the United Kingdom and Ireland it was known as Good Luck Charlie: The Road Trip Movie.

The story takes place between the series' second and third seasons. The Duncan family is preparing to spend Christmas with Amy's parents, Petunia and Hank, in Palm Springs, California. Teddy wants to go to Florida for spring break with her best friend Ivy, but Amy refuses to let her travel alone. At the airport, Bob tells Teddy that she can go if she pays for the plane ticket herself. When the flight turns out to be overbooked and the airline offers a free ticket to anyone who gives up a seat, Teddy volunteers, and Amy leaves the plane to follow her.

Mother and daughter soon discover that the next available flight will not arrive until after Christmas. After Amy's argument with an airline employee gets them thrown out of the airport, the two set off on a chaotic cross-country journey by bus, by a battered rental car that does not survive the trip, and by hitchhiking, meeting a series of eccentric strangers along the way. Meanwhile, the rest of the family has its own troubles in Palm Springs: Bob suffers constant criticism from his disapproving mother-in-law, Charlie breaks things around the house, PJ gets a painful sunburn, and Gabe accidentally turns his grandfather into a video-game addict. As the holiday approaches, Teddy and Amy learn to appreciate each other while racing to reunite with the family in time for Christmas.

The film mixes road-movie misadventures with the family humor of the series, focusing on the relationship between a teenage daughter and her mother.

Good Luck Charlie, It's Christmas! premiered on Disney Channel on December 2, 2011, and drew about 6.9 million viewers on its original broadcast.

documents.title: The Baytown Outlaws
documents.tagline: A Southern Whip-Ass Extravaganza!
documents.overview: When three redneck brothers agree to help a woman save her son from an abusive father, they become targets on the run from an odd cast of characters.
documents.plot:
The Baytown Outlaws is a 2012 American action comedy film directed by Barry Battles and written by Battles and David W. Egan. 

The movie revolves around three brothers, Jake, Wyatt, and Chet, who are former outlaws trying to leave their outlaw past behind them. However, when they discover that the corrupt sheriff of Baytown is embezzling funds meant for the town's children, they decide to take matters into their own hands.

As the story unfolds, themes of redemption, family, and loyalty become apparent. The film explores how the brothers' complicated relationships with each other and their desire to make amends for past mistakes drive them to confront the corrupt sheriff and fight for justice in Baytown.

Throughout the movie, there is also a strong emphasis on the consequences of violence and the cyclical nature of crime. The characters are forced to confront the harsh realities of their own actions and the impact they have had on those around them.

Ultimately, The Baytown Outlaws is a story about finding redemption and making amends through selfless acts of bravery and loyalty, as the brothers put aside their differences and work together to protect the people and town they care about.

documents.title: Lockout
documents.tagline: Take no prisoners.
documents.overview: Set in the near future, Lockout follows a falsely convicted ex-government agent , whose one chance at obtaining freedom lies in the dangerous mission of rescuing the President's daughter from rioting convicts at an outer space maximum security prison.
documents.plot:
Lockout is a 2012 French science fiction action film directed by James Mather and Brian Smith, produced by EuropaCorp and Canal+, and written by James Mather and Brian Smith.

The movie takes place in the future where the United States has created a maximum-security prison called the "Taurus-I" to house the world's most notorious terrorists. The story follows Vincent Moses (played by Guy Pearce), an ex-Special Forces operative who is recruited for a high-stakes mission to rescue his daughter, Sophia (played by Maggie Grace), from the prison.

However, things take a turn when it becomes clear that the real purpose of the mission is not to rescue Sophia but to prevent a catastrophic event. The Taurus-I has been taken over by a group of terrorists led by Admiral William Lynch (played by Peter Stormare) and his second-in-command, General Hugo Gernick (played by Tim Roth). They plan to use the prison's advanced technology to hold the world hostage.

Vincent is paired with Lenina Huxley (played by Carla Gugino), a tough-as-nails prison administrator who becomes his unlikely ally. As they navigate the treacherous landscape of the Taurus-I, Vincent and Lenina must work together to prevent the terrorists from carrying out their plan.

Throughout the movie, Vincent's character undergoes significant development as he confronts his troubled past and grapples with the moral implications of his mission. Meanwhile, Lenina's tough exterior hides a complex and vulnerable individual who is driven by her own motivations for helping Vincent.

As the story unfolds, the tension builds towards a thrilling climax where Vincent and Lenina must face off against Lynch and Gernick in a desperate bid to save the world from destruction. The movie features plenty of action-packed sequences, including intense hand-to-hand combat and high-stakes chases through the prison's corridors.

Ultimately, Vincent and Lenina succeed in stopping the terrorists' plan, but not without sacrifices. The movie ends on a bittersweet note, with Vincent reflecting on the true cost of his mission and the consequences of playing with fire when it comes to global security.

Overall, Lockout is a gripping sci-fi thriller that explores themes of redemption, loyalty, and the blurred lines between right and wrong in a world where the stakes are high. With its breakneck pace, memorable characters, and pulse-pounding action sequences, Lockout is a must-see for fans of the genre.

documents.title: To Rome with Love
documents.tagline: Romance! Adventure! Hilarity! Italy!
documents.overview: Four tales unfold in the Eternal City: While vacationing in Rome, architect John encounters a young man whose romantic woes remind him of a painful incident from his own youth; retired opera director Jerry discovers a mortician with an amazing voice, and he seizes the opportunity to rejuvenate his own flagging career; a young couple have separate romantic interludes; a spotlight shines on an ordinary man.
documents.plot:
Hayley's Story
American tourist Hayley becomes engaged to lawyer Michelangelo while spending a summer in Rome. Hayley's parents, Jerry and Phyllis, fly to Italy to meet her fiancé. During the visit, Michelangelo's mortician father Giancarlo sings in the shower and Jerry, a retired—and critically reviled—opera director, is inspired to bring his gift to the public. He convinces Giancarlo to audition in front of a room of opera bigwigs but Giancarlo performs poorly in this setting.
Jerry realizes Giancarlo's talent is tied to the comfort and freedom of the shower. He stages a concert in which Giancarlo performs at the Teatro dell'Opera while actually washing himself onstage in a shower. This is a great success, so Jerry and Giancarlo stage Pagliacci with an incongruous shower present in all scenes. Giancarlo receives rave reviews but retires from opera singing, preferring to work as a mortician and spend time with his family.
Antonio's Story
Newlyweds Antonio and Milly plan to move to Rome after his uncles offer him a job in their family business. Before meeting Antonio's relatives, Milly gets lost in Rome and loses her cell phone. Ending up at a film shoot, Milly meets Luca Salta, an actor she idolizes. Back at her hotel, Anna, a prostitute, is mistakenly sent to Antonio's room.
Before Antonio can clarify the misunderstanding, his relatives arrive. To save face, Antonio convinces Anna to pose as Milly. The group goes to lunch and then to a party. Antonio talks to Anna about how pure Milly is. Upon discovering Antonio was a virgin before meeting Milly, she seduces him in the bushes.
Luca takes Milly to his hotel room. She decides to have sex with him, but then an armed thief breaks in. Luca's wife and a private investigator show up. Milly and the thief climb into bed and fool Mrs. Salta into believing the room is theirs while Luca hides in the bathroom. Once his wife has left, Luca runs off. Milly has sex with the thief instead. After returning to the hotel room, she and Antonio decide to return to their rustic hometown—but first begin to make love.
Leopoldo's Story
Leopoldo lives a mundane life with his wife and two children until he wakes up one morning to discover he has become a national celebrity. Paparazzi document his every move, wanting to know everything about him. Leopoldo even becomes a manager at his company and begins dating models and attending prestigious events. The constant attention wears on him. One day, in the middle of an interview, the paparazzi spot a man "who looks more interesting" and abandon Leopoldo. At first, Leopoldo welcomes the return to his old life, but one afternoon he breaks down, missing the attention.
John's Story
John, a well-known architect, visits Rome with his wife and their friends. He had lived there some 30 years before, and would rather revisit his old haunts than go sightseeing with the others. Looking for his old apartment building, John meets American architecture student Jack, who recognizes him.

documents.title: Small Fry
documents.overview: A fast food restaurant mini variant of Buzz forcibly switches places with the real Buzz and his friends have to deal with the obnoxious impostor.
documents.plot:
Small Fry, released as Toy Story Toons: Small Fry, is a 2011 American animated short film written and directed by Angus MacLane. The second short in the Toy Story Toons series built around characters from the Toy Story features, it premiered in theaters alongside the feature film The Muppets on November 23, 2011.

At the Poultry Palace, a fast-food chicken restaurant, Bonnie is disappointed with the Zurg belt buckle that comes with her kids' meal and asks for a Mini Buzz Lightyear instead, but the remaining ones are only for display. Inside the display case, one Mini Buzz complains that they will never be played with, while a Mini Zurg is happy to stay put. When Bonnie plays in the ball pit with Rex and the real Buzz, whom she has brought along, Mini Buzz slips out of the case, drags Buzz under the balls and takes his place. Bonnie's mother packs up the toys without noticing the switch. Mini Buzz convinces Rex that the ball pit plastic shrank him, but the other toys at Bonnie's house see through the impostor at once.

Buzz climbs out of the pit to find the restaurant closed for the night. Looking for a way out, he stumbles into a storeroom where discarded fast-food toys hold a support group for abandoned toys led by a mermaid named Neptuna. Taking Buzz for another castaway, the group makes him join the meeting, but during a role-playing therapy exercise he befriends Gary Grappling Hook and uses him to escape. At home, the other toys interrogate Mini Buzz and plot a rescue mission, only for Buzz to walk in on his own and confront the little impostor. Mini Buzz later opens up at the support group with Buzz beside him as his sponsor, and in a post-credits scene Mini Zurg is delighted with the electronic belt buckle as his new companion.

Tim Allen voices Buzz and Teddy Newton voices Mini Buzz, with Tom Hanks, Joan Cusack, Don Rickles, Estelle Harris, Wallace Shawn, John Ratzenberger and Timothy Dalton voicing Bonnie's other toys and Emily Hahn as Bonnie. Jane Lynch voices Neptuna and MacLane voices several characters, including Gary Grappling Hook. The toys in the short include a Condorman figure, a nod to the 1981 Disney adventure comedy Condorman, which MacLane joked might stir up interest in a gritty reboot.

documents.title: Hamilton: In the Interest of the Nation
documents.overview: Carl Hamilton manages to infiltrate an international gang that has stolen advanced Swedish GPS-guided missiles. But the league is subjected to a sudden deadly attack by a well drilled group of mercenaries of unknown clients. Hamilton escapes the massacre, but the rockets have disappeared without a trace.
documents.plot:
Hamilton: In the Interest of the Nation (Swedish: Hamilton – I nationens intresse) is a 2012 Swedish spy thriller directed by the Danish filmmaker Kathrine Windfeld and supported by the Swedish Film Institute. Mikael Persbrandt stars as Carl Hamilton, the intelligence officer created by the novelist Jan Guillou, with Saba Mubarak, Jason Flemyng, Pernilla August and Gustaf Hammarsten in supporting roles. Conceived as the first part of a planned trilogy, it was followed by Agent Hamilton: But Not If It Concerns Your Daughter.

Carl Hamilton is a commander in Sweden's foreign intelligence service. After a rare moment of peace with his girlfriend, a Polish doctor living in Stockholm, he is sent on an undercover assignment in Central Asia to infiltrate an international gang of smugglers and arms dealers who are about to sell Swedish-made GPS-guided artillery shells to terrorists. His survival depends on convincing the criminals that he is Russian. When the dealers meet the buyers, the transaction collapses into violence, and Hamilton is forced to kill and flee, leaving the weapons behind.

Back in Sweden, he is reprimanded by a new superior and returns, after a four-month unexplained absence, to his girlfriend, telling her he wants to leave the service. But the trauma of his mission follows him into his sleep, and a nightmare ends in a tragedy that shatters his attempt at a normal life. His mentor, known as DG, persuades him not to turn himself in and sends him abroad to rescue a Swedish technician linked to the smuggled munitions. Hamilton uncovers a plot by Sectragon, an American private military company that hopes to ignite a new war for profit and even plans to assassinate a foreign head of state on Swedish soil, and he works with the PLO operative Mouna al Fathar to stop it.

The film was a box-office hit in Sweden, topping the charts on its release in January 2012 and becoming the most successful Swedish film of the year domestically, with more than 500,000 admissions. By the end of that month it had been sold to more than ten foreign markets. On its release Hamilton was frequently compared with James Bond, and reviews were mostly positive. Much of the film was shot in Jordan, standing in for several foreign locations.

documents.title: House at the End of the Street
documents.original_title: House at the End of the Street
documents.tagline: Fear reaches out... for the girl next door.
documents.overview: A mother and daughter move to a new town and find themselves living next door to a house where a young girl murdered her parents. When the daughter befriends the surviving son, she learns the story is far from over.
documents.plot:
Newly-divorced doctor Sarah and her daughter Elissa move to a small, upscale suburb. They discover the house they are moving into is on the same street as the house in which a girl named Carrie Anne killed her parents four years prior. She fled and left her brother Ryan as the sole survivor. Ryan now lives alone in the house and is hated by his neighbors; Bill, a local police officer, is his only supporter.
Elissa starts seeing Ryan against Sarah's wishes. Ryan confides in Elissa that Carrie Anne fell from a swing when they were little; he was supposed to be watching her while their parents were getting high on drugs. The brain damage made her extremely aggressive, leading to their parents' murder. Ryan is revealed to be secretly taking care of a now grown Carrie Anne in the basement in the house. Carrie Anne escapes and approaches a couple in a car while brandishing a kitchen knife. Ryan accidentally kills her. Grieving, he goes to a diner and he meets a waitress named Peggy.
One night, a group of high school boys pick a fight with him; he breaks one of their legs in self-defense and flees. Elissa drives to his house and discovers the basement and Peggy, who Ryan has kidnapped and dressed as Carrie Anne. Ryan knocks Elissa unconscious.
Elissa wakes tied to a chair. Ryan tells her Carrie Anne didn't kill their parents because she died during the swing set accident and he killed their parents after they blamed him for his sister's death and began abusing him. Ryan had entered a cycle of kidnapping and killing women as Carrie Anne surrogates.
He kills Peggy and decides Elissa will become his new Carrie Anne. Bill arrives but Ryan stabs him to death. Elissa tries to escape in Ryan's car, but he traps her in the car trunk with Peggy's body. Sarah arrives and is stabbed by Ryan and Elissa escapes and shoots Ryan with Bill's gun and knocks him out with a hammer.
Elissa and Sarah move away and Ryan is placed in a psychiatric ward. He begins to hear the voices of his deceased parents calling him Carrie-Anne. A flashback reveals a young Ryan about to blow out birthday candles while dressed in girl's clothing. His mother refers to him as Carrie Anne; he protests that he is Ryan. She violently slaps him across the face in response, insisting he is Carrie Anne.

documents.title: Lawless
documents.tagline: When the law became corrupt, outlaws became heroes.
documents.overview: Set in the Depression-era Franklin County, Virginia, a bootlegging gang is threatened by authorities who want a cut of their profits.
documents.plot:
In 1931, the Bondurant brothers — middle brother, Forrest, eldest brother, Howard, and youngest brother, Jack — are running a successful moonshine business in Franklin County, Virginia. The brothers use their gas station and restaurant as a front for dealing, with the assistance of Cricket, Jack's mechanically gifted friend, who builds and maintains their stills. Jack witnesses rum-runner, Floyd Banner, fatally shoot two federal agents in broad daylight for trying to arrest him.
Forrest hires Maggie, a financially struggling dancer, as a waitress. Shortly afterward, the gas station is visited by newly appointed U.S. Marshal Charley Rakes, accompanied by the sheriff and corrupt state's attorney, Mason Wardell. Rakes demands that he and Wardell receive a cut of profits from all bootleggers in the county, including Forrest, in exchange for ignoring their operations. Forrest stands his ground, and implores his fellow bootleggers to unite against Rakes, but they refuse.
Meanwhile, Jack lusts after Bertha, daughter of the local Brethren preacher. He attends their church service drunk, embarrassing himself but piquing her interest. Jack walks in on a visit from Rakes to Cricket's house, and is beaten by him, as a message to his brothers. Later that night, Forrest throws out two drunk customers who had been harassing and threatening Maggie. After Maggie leaves, Forrest is ambushed by the two men, who slit his throat. Maggie returns looking for Forrest but is beaten and raped by the men. She hides the assault from Forrest, not wanting him to take revenge.
While Forrest recovers at a hospital, Jack, deciding to retire from bootlegging rather than cross Rakes any further, crosses the county line with Cricket to sell their remaining liquor. They are ambushed by Banner and his crew, but are spared when Jack reveals he is a Bondurant, whom Banner admires for their stance against Rakes. Banner confesses to Jack the address of his brother's assailants, revealing that both men are former bootleggers who escaped punishment for their crimes by working as deputy marshals for Rakes.
Forrest and Howard find, torture, and kill the men, and send one of their testicles to Rakes. Banner becomes a regular client of the brothers, who invest their profits into setting up larger stills deep in the woods. Jack continues to court Bertha. Maggie decides to return to Chicago, but Forrest convinces her to stay and provides her with a spare room; they soon develop a romantic relationship. On a day trip, Jack decides to show Bertha the brothers' secret operation, but they are followed and ambushed by Rakes and his officers. Howard and Jack flee but Cricket and Bertha are caught. The police take Bertha home, while Cricket has his neck snapped by Rakes.
After Cricket's funeral, the sheriff warns the Bondurants that Rakes has set up a blockade at the bridge to trap them while Wardell arranges for Prohibition agents to round up every bootlegger in the county.

documents.title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Dog Days
documents.original_title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Dog Days
documents.tagline: School's out for summer.
documents.overview: It's summertime, and Greg Heffley is looking forward to playing video games and spending time with his friends. However, Greg's dad has other plans: He's decided that some father-son bonding time is in order. Desperate to prevent his dad from ruining summer vacation, Greg pretends he has a job at a ritzy country club. But Greg's plan backfires, leaving him in the middle of embarrassing mishaps and a camping trip gone wrong.
documents.plot:
Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Dog Days is a 2012 American comedy film directed by David Bowers and written by Jeff Kinney, based on the novel of the same name. The movie stars Zachary Gordon as Greg Heffley, Devon Bostick as Rodrick Heffley, and Rachael Harris as Susan Heffley.

The story begins with Greg Heffley (Zachary Gordon) trying to navigate his summer vacation. His parents have given him a lot of freedom, but he's not sure how to handle it. Greg is worried that he'll get into trouble or lose his friends. Meanwhile, Rodrick (Devon Bostick), his older brother, is trying to make the most of his own summer by getting a job and impressing girls.

As the story progresses, Greg tries to fit in with his friends Rowley (Robert Capron) and Fregley (Grayson Russell). However, things don't go as planned. Greg gets into various misadventures, including trying to start a pet-sitting business and getting into a rivalry with a new kid at school.

One of the main plot points is Greg's attempt to impress a girl named Angie (Laine MacNeil) by pretending to be more mature than he actually is. However, things quickly spiral out of control as Greg tries to keep up the act and avoid getting caught.

Throughout the movie, there are also several flashbacks that show Greg's summer vacation from the previous year, which provides some comedic relief and insight into his character development.

As the story reaches its climax, Greg learns a valuable lesson about being true to himself and not trying to be someone he's not. He also comes to terms with his relationships with his family members, particularly his brother Rodrick.

The movie ends on a positive note, with Greg reflecting on what he's learned from his summer vacation. Despite the ups and downs, Greg is grateful for the experiences he had and the friends who stood by him throughout it all.

Overall, Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Dog Days is a lighthearted and entertaining movie that explores themes of identity, friendship, and growing up. With its relatable protagonist and humorous plot twists, it's sure to appeal to fans of the book series and anyone looking for a fun summer watch.

documents.overview: After a zombie becomes involved with the girlfriend of one of his victims, their romance sets in motion a sequence of events that might transform the entire lifeless world.

documents.overview: Flight 7500 departs Los Angeles International Airport bound for Tokyo. As the overnight flight makes its way over the Pacific Ocean during its ten-hour course, the passengers encounter what appears to be a supernatural force in the cabin.

documents.title: Taken 2
documents.tagline: First they took his daughter. Now they're coming for him.
documents.overview: In Istanbul, retired CIA operative Bryan Mills and his wife are taken hostage by the father of a kidnapper Mills killed while rescuing his daughter.
documents.plot:
Taken 2 is a 2012 action-thriller film directed by Olivier Megaton and written by Luc Besson and Robert Mark Kamen. The movie stars Liam Neeson, Maggie Grace, Famke Janssen, and Jon Voight.

The story begins with Bryan Mills (Liam Neeson), a former CIA operative who has retired to Istanbul, Turkey, where he lives with his wife Kim (Famke Janssen) and their young daughter Molly (Maggie Grace). However, their peaceful life is disrupted when Kim's family is kidnapped by the Abductions Club, a Turkish crime syndicate that demands $10 million in exchange for her safe return.

The kidnappers reveal that they have been tracking Bryan since his last adventure, and they are determined to make him pay for killing their leader, Murad (Arben Bajraktaraj), during his previous encounter with the Abductions Club. The group's leader, Rana (Ariane Labed), is a ruthless and cunning woman who will stop at nothing to get what she wants.

As Bryan tries to navigate this new threat, he must also contend with the Turkish authorities, who are skeptical of his claims that Kim was kidnapped by the Abductions Club. With the help of his daughter Molly, who has been trained in hand-to-hand combat and surveillance skills, Bryan sets out on a mission to rescue Kim and take down the Abductions Club.

As the story unfolds, Bryan's past comes back to haunt him, and he is forced to confront his own demons in order to save his family. The movie features plenty of intense action sequences, including a memorable fight scene between Bryan and Rana's henchmen at a nightclub.

Throughout the film, Liam Neeson delivers his signature performance as Bryan Mills, bringing his trademark blend of grit, humor, and vulnerability to the role. Maggie Grace shines as Molly, who proves herself to be a capable and resourceful young woman in her own right.

The movie's climax features an intense showdown between Bryan and Rana, which culminates in a thrilling finale that will keep viewers on the edge of their seats. In the end, Bryan emerges victorious, but not without scars - both physical and emotional.

Overall, Taken 2 is a gripping and entertaining action-thriller that delivers plenty of excitement and suspense. While it may not be as tightly wound as its predecessor, the movie still has all the ingredients that made the first film so successful: high-octane action, memorable characters, and a healthy dose of humor.

Rating: 4/5 stars

documents.title: Gangster Squad
documents.tagline: No Names. No Badges. No Mercy.
documents.overview: Los Angeles, 1949. Ruthless, Brooklyn-born mob king Mickey Cohen runs the show in this town, reaping the ill-gotten gains from the drugs, the guns, the prostitutes and — if he has his way — every wire bet placed west of Chicago. And he does it all with the protection of not only his own paid goons, but also the police and the politicians who are under his control. It’s enough to intimidate even the bravest, street-hardened cop… except, perhaps, for the small, secret crew of LAPD outsiders led by Sgt. John O’Mara and Jerry Wooters who come together to try to tear Cohen’s world apart.
