documents.title: Wreck-It Ralph
documents.tagline: The story of a regular guy just looking for a little wreck-ognition.
documents.overview: Wreck-It Ralph is the 9-foot-tall, 643-pound villain of an arcade video game named Fix-It Felix Jr., in which the game's titular hero fixes buildings that Ralph destroys. Wanting to prove he can be a good guy and not just a villain, Ralph escapes his game and lands in Hero's Duty, a first-person shooter where he helps the game's hero battle against alien invaders. He later enters Sugar Rush, a kart racing game set on tracks made of candies, cookies and other sweets. There, Ralph meets Vanellope von Schweetz who has learned that her game is faced with a dire threat that could affect the entire arcade, and one that Ralph may have inadvertently started.
documents.plot:
Wreck-It Ralph is a 2012 animated science fiction comedy film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. The movie takes place in a world where arcade games are alive, and follows the story of Ralph, an antagonist character from the classic arcade game Fix-It Felix.

The film begins with Ralph (voiced by John C. Reilly), a large, green, hulking monster who lives in the Nicelanders' arcade game "Fix-It Felix." In this game, Ralph's job is to wreck the apartment building so that Felix (voiced by Jack McBrayer) can fix it and earn points for the game. However, Ralph feels unappreciated and lonely, as he is only allowed to play with the Nicelanders' arcade games when no one else is around.

One day, Ralph decides to explore other arcade games to find a new purpose in life. He visits Sugar Rush, a fast-paced racing game where he meets Vanellope von Schweetz (voiced by Sarah Silverman), a glitchy and energetic character who becomes his friend. However, their fun is short-lived as Ralph discovers that the game's main character, Vanellope, has been banned from competing in the Sugar Rush Grand Prix due to her glitch.

Ralph decides to help Vanellope enter the tournament, but things become complicated when he realizes that the only way for her to compete is by exploiting a bug in the game. Ralph and Vanellope's friendship deepens as they work together to fix the bug and save the Sugar Rush Grand Prix.

Meanwhile, Felix becomes jealous of Ralph's newfound friendships and tries to sabotage his efforts. However, Ralph eventually finds a new purpose in life when he realizes that being an antagonist is not all bad - it allows him to have fun and be himself.

In the end, Ralph and Vanellope successfully fix the bug, and Vanellope wins the Sugar Rush Grand Prix. The movie ends with Ralph returning to Nicelanders' arcade game, but this time as a hero, having found a new sense of belonging and purpose in life.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and colorful, with a mix of 8-bit and 16-bit graphics that pay homage to classic video games. The voice acting is also excellent, with John C. Reilly bringing Ralph's lovable but gruff personality to life, while Sarah Silverman adds a fun and quirky touch to Vanellope.

Overall, Wreck-It Ralph is a heartwarming and hilarious film that explores themes of identity, friendship, and finding one's purpose in life. The movie features a talented voice cast, stunning animation, and a story that will leave audiences laughing and cheering for more.

documents.title: Silver Linings Playbook
documents.tagline: Watch For The Signs
documents.overview: After spending eight months in a mental institution, a former teacher moves back in with his parents and tries to reconcile with his ex-wife.
documents.plot:
After 8 months' treatment in a psychiatric hospital in Baltimore for bipolar disorder, Patrizio "Pat" Solitano Jr. is released into the care of his parents, Patrizio Sr. and Dolores, at his childhood home in Upper Darby Township, Pennsylvania. His primary focus is to reconcile with his ex-wife, Nikki. She has moved away and obtained a restraining order against him after he found her in the shower with another man and badly beat him.
Pat's therapist, Cliff Patel, tries to convince him to keep taking his medication because a repeat of his violent outbursts might send him back to the hospital in Baltimore. Pat tells him that he has a new outlook on life: He attempts to see the good, or silver lining, in all that he experiences. Meanwhile, Pat experiences a series of anxiety attacks, sometimes triggered by hearing "My Cherie Amour" by Stevie Wonder, other times he imagines hearing the song during an anxiety attack.
Pat attends dinner at his best friend Ronnie's house, where Ronnie's sister-in-law, Tiffany Maxwell, a widow with an unnamed disorder, is also a guest. They connect, talking about different psychiatric medications they have taken to manage their mental illnesses. She tries to offer him casual sex, but Pat is focused on getting Nikki back. Trying to get closer to him, Tiffany offers to deliver a letter to Nikki if, in return, he partners with her in an upcoming dance competition. Convinced that helping Tiffany will show Nikki he has changed and has developed sensitivity to others, Pat agrees. Pat and Tiffany start practicing over the following weeks.
Hoping to open a restaurant, Patrizio Sr. has resorted to illegal bookmaking. Having bet most of his money on a Philadelphia Eagles game, Patrizio asks Pat to attend for good luck, irrationally believing Pat's attention to the game affects its outcome. Pat points out this is OCD ideation but appeases his father. Pat asks Tiffany for time off from practice to attend the game. She gives him a typed reply from Nikki, which cautiously hints they may be able to reconcile. Before entering the stadium, Pat and his brother Jake get into a fight with racist fans and are arrested. The Eagles lose the game, and Patrizio Sr. is furious.
When Patrizio Sr. claims that the Eagles lost because of Tiffany's newfound involvement in Pat's life, Tiffany refutes his allegations by pointing out that Philadelphia sports teams had done better whenever she and Pat were together. Convinced, Patrizio makes a parlay with his friend Randy: If the Eagles win their week 16 game against the Dallas Cowboys and Tiffany and Pat score five out of ten in their dance competition, he will win back double the money he lost on the first bet.
Pat is reluctant, but Tiffany, Dolores, and Patrizio conspire to persuade him to dance in the competition, telling him Nikki will be there. Noticing that the letter from Nikki includes the phrase "If it's me reading the signs..."

documents.title: Les Misérables
documents.tagline: Fight. Dream. Hope. Love.
documents.overview: An adaptation of the successful stage musical based on Victor Hugo's classic novel set in 19th-century France, in which a paroled prisoner named Jean Valjean seeks redemption.
documents.plot:
Les Misérables is a musical drama film directed by Tom Hooper, released in 2012 by Universal Pictures. The film is based on the novel of the same name by Victor Hugo and features an all-star cast, including Hugh Jackman, Anne Hathaway, Eddie Redmayne, Amanda Seyfried, and Samantha Barks.

The story begins in 1815, six months after the June Rebellion in Paris. Jean Valjean (Hugh Jackman), a former prisoner who was released from prison after serving nineteen years for stealing a loaf of bread to feed his sister's seven children, is pursued by the ruthless police inspector Javert (Russell Crowe). Valjean seeks redemption and a new life, but Javert is determined to capture him.

Valjean meets Bishop Myriel (Mark Addy), who shows him kindness and compassion, teaching him the value of humanity. Valjean vows to use his newfound wealth and influence for good, and he becomes a successful businessman and mayor of Montreuil-sur-Mer.

However, Javert's obsession with capturing Valjean continues, and he eventually tracks him down in Paris. Valjean is forced to flee, but not before he rescues a young girl named Fantine (Anne Hathaway), who is forced into prostitution to support her daughter Cosette.

Valjean promises to care for Cosette after Fantine's death, and he raises her as his own. As Cosette grows up, she falls in love with Marius Pontmercy (Eddie Redmayne), a young revolutionary who joins the student-led uprising against the French government.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Javert is killed by Valjean during a confrontation at the barricades during the June Rebellion. Meanwhile, Cosette and Marius are separated from each other, and Cosette becomes ill with tuberculosis.

In the end, Marius finds Cosette again, and they reunite. The film ends with the characters coming together to mourn the loss of Javert and to celebrate their newfound freedom and love for one another.

Throughout the film, the music plays a crucial role in conveying the emotions and themes of the story. The iconic songs, such as "I Dreamed a Dream," "Do You Hear the People Sing?," and "One Day More," bring depth and complexity to the characters and their struggles.

The film received widespread critical acclaim for its performances, direction, and music. Anne Hathaway's powerful performance in "I Dreamed a Dream" earned her an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress.

documents.title: Hope Springs
documents.tagline: Sometimes to keep the magic, you need to learn a few tricks.
documents.overview: After thirty years of marriage, a middle-aged couple attends an intense, week-long counseling session to work on their relationship.

documents.title: How to Train Your Dragon 2
documents.tagline: The training is over.
documents.overview: Five years have passed since Hiccup and Toothless united the dragons and Vikings of Berk. Now, they spend their time charting unmapped territories. During one of their adventures, the pair discover a secret cave that houses hundreds of wild dragons -- and a mysterious dragon rider who turns out to be Hiccup's mother, Valka. Hiccup and Toothless then find themselves at the center of a battle to protect Berk from a power-hungry warrior named Drago.
documents.plot:
How to Train Your Dragon 2 is a 2014 American computer-animated adventure comedy film directed by Dean DeBlois and Chris Sanders. The movie takes place five years after the events of the first film.

The story begins with Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III (voiced by Jay Baruchel), now a young adult, who has become the chief of Berk's Viking village. He is struggling to find his place in the world and prove himself as a leader. Meanwhile, a new threat emerges in the form of a dragon hunter named Drago Bludvist (voiced by Djimon Hounsou), who seeks to destroy all dragons and rule the world.

Drago is revealed to be the son of Stoick the Vast's (voiced by Gerard Butler) long-lost brother, who was thought to have been killed in a dragon attack. Drago's true intention is to find his father's lost treasure, which he believes is hidden on Berk. He also seeks to destroy the dragons and rule the world.

Hiccup teams up with his friends Astrid (voiced by America Ferrera), Snotlout (voiced by Jonah Hill), Ruffnut (voiced by Kristen Wiig), and Tuffnut (voiced by T.J. Miller) to stop Drago and save their village. Along the way, they discover that Drago's true intention is not just to destroy dragons but also to find his father's treasure.

As Hiccup and his friends journey to stop Drago, they encounter new dragons, including a massive dragon known as the "Boneknapper". They also learn more about their own pasts and the history of Berk. Hiccup discovers that he has a special connection to the dragons and can communicate with them in ways that no one else can.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Drago reveals his true intentions: to use the dragons' tears, which are collected from their eyes, to heal his own dying body. The dragons' tears have the power to cure any wound, making Drago nearly invincible.

In the end, Hiccup and his friends come up with a plan to stop Drago and save Berk. They use the dragons' tears to create a powerful blast that destroys Drago's ship and sends him crashing into the sea. The movie ends with Hiccup and Astrid sharing a romantic moment, and the Vikings celebrating their victory over Drago.

Throughout the movie, there are many humorous moments, including Snotlout's attempts to prove himself as a Viking warrior and Ruffnut and Tuffnut's comedic antics. The movie also explores themes of identity, community, and the importance of understanding and respecting other cultures.

Overall, How to Train Your Dragon 2 is an exciting and action-packed adventure that expands on the world and characters introduced in the first film. It features stunning animation, engaging characters, and a thrilling plot that will keep audiences entertained from start to finish.

documents.title: Mr. Peabody & Sherman
documents.tagline: He's Leaving His Mark On History
documents.overview: A young boy and his dog, who happens to have a genius-level IQ, spring into action when their time-machine is stolen and moments in history begin to be changed.
documents.plot:
Mr. Peabody & Sherman is a 2014 American computer-animated science fiction comedy produced by DreamWorks Animation, based on the "Peabody's Improbable History" segments of the animated series Rocky & Friends. Directed by Rob Minkoff and written by Craig Wright, it features the voices of Ty Burrell, Max Charles, Ariel Winter, Stephen Colbert, Leslie Mann and Allison Janney. The project was first conceived as a hybrid live-action film before being redeveloped as a fully animated feature in 2006, when Minkoff joined DreamWorks Animation to direct.

Mr. Peabody is a genius beagle, a Nobel laureate, inventor and gourmet, who has legally adopted a human boy, Sherman. Using his time machine, the WABAC, he teaches his son history first-hand. On Sherman's first day of school, he contradicts his classmate Penny Peterson about the legend of George Washington and the cherry tree, and a scuffle ensues in which Penny taunts him as a dog and Sherman bites her. The incident brings in Ms. Grunion, a child protective services agent who threatens to take Sherman away if she judges Peabody an unfit parent.

To smooth things over, Peabody invites Penny's family to dinner, but Sherman secretly takes Penny on a trip in the WABAC. She stays behind in ancient Egypt intending to marry King Tut, and Peabody and Sherman must rescue her. A power failure strands them in Renaissance Florence with Leonardo da Vinci, where the children crash his flying machine, and further adventures take them to the Trojan War. Strains emerge between father and son as Sherman learns of Grunion's plans, and when Sherman breaks the rules of time travel, a rip in the space-time continuum sends historical figures pouring into present-day New York. Peabody and Sherman must repair history together, with Sherman standing up for his father and those around them affirming that a dog can indeed be a loving parent.

Released by 20th Century Fox in March 2014, the film opened against 300: Rise of an Empire and earned about $275.7 million worldwide. Against a budget of $145 million, it was considered an underperformer, and DreamWorks Animation took a $57 million write-down. Critics generally responded favorably to its humor and visual inventiveness. It was followed by the Netflix series The Mr. Peabody & Sherman Show, with Chris Parnell voicing Peabody.

documents.title: Tangled Ever After
documents.overview: The kingdom is in a festive mood as everyone gathers for the royal wedding of Rapunzel and Flynn. However, when Pascal and Maximus, as flower chameleon and ring bearer, respectively, lose the gold bands, a frenzied search and recovery mission gets underway. As the desperate duo tries to find the rings before anyone discovers that they’re missing, they leave behind a trail of comical chaos that includes flying lanterns, a flock of doves, a wine barrel barricade and a very sticky finale. Will Maximus and Pascal save the day and make it to the church in time? And will they ever get Flynn’s nose right?
documents.plot:
Tangled Ever After is a 3D animated short film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios and released in 2012 as part of the Disney Princess franchise. The story takes place after the events of the feature film Tangled.

The short begins with Rapunzel, now living in the kingdom with Eugene Fitzherbert (Flynn Rider), who has become a royal guard. However, on the day of their coronation ceremony, disaster strikes when Mother Gothel's magical flower is stolen by a group of thieves. The thief, who is revealed to be Pascal's long-lost brother, is after the flower's magic and plans to use it to gain ultimate power.

Rapunzel and Eugene team up with the thief's accomplices, including a charming and cunning thief named Jack (voiced by Zachary Levi), to retrieve the stolen flower. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including a wild chase through the kingdom and a showdown with Mother Gothel's minions.

As Rapunzel and Jack work together to outsmart their enemies, they develop a strong bond and learn more about each other's pasts. Meanwhile, Eugene struggles with his own feelings of inadequacy as he watches Rapunzel grow into her royal role.

In the end, Rapunzel and Jack successfully retrieve the flower, but not before it is revealed that the thief was actually working to protect the kingdom from Mother Gothel's evil plans. The group returns to the palace, where they are greeted as heroes. Eugene finally finds his place in the kingdom, and Rapunzel realizes that she doesn't need her magical powers to be happy.

The short ends with a heartwarming moment between Rapunzel and Eugene, as they share a tender kiss under the stars. The film concludes on a hopeful note, emphasizing the importance of friendship, teamwork, and finding one's true purpose in life.

Overall, Tangled Ever After is a delightful and action-packed addition to the Tangled franchise, offering a fresh take on the beloved characters while maintaining their signature charm and humor.

documents.title: Paranormal Activity 4
documents.tagline: All the activity has led to this...
documents.overview: It has been five years since the disappearance of Katie and Hunter, and a suburban family witness strange events in their neighborhood when a woman and a mysterious child move in.
documents.plot:
Paranormal Activity 4 is a supernatural horror film directed by Oren Peli and written by Oren Peli and Christopher Landon. The movie takes place four years after the events of the third installment, Paranormal Activity 3.

The story begins with Katie Featherston's character, Katie, now married to Micah Sloat (Mark Fredricks) and living in a new house on the outskirts of town. They have two children, but their lives are disrupted by strange occurrences that start happening around them. The family soon discovers that they are being haunted by a malevolent spirit.

As the events escalate, Katie becomes increasingly convinced that the spirit is connected to her own past and the reason for its presence in their home. She starts experiencing terrifying visions and nightmares, which she believes are attempts by the spirit to communicate with her.

The movie's plot thickens as Katie discovers an old video camera in the attic of their new house, which seems to be capturing evidence of the paranormal activity. The footage shows a young girl, who is believed to be Katie's sister, Elizabeth (played by Katie Featherston), being terrorized by the malevolent spirit.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the spirit is connected to an ancient evil that has been awakened in the house. The family soon realizes that they are not alone and that the spirit is determined to claim their souls.

The climax of the movie takes place when Katie discovers a dark secret about her own past and the reason for the spirit's presence in their home. She learns that she was possessed by the same malevolent entity as a child, which explains why it has been drawn to her family.

In the end, Katie is able to confront the spirit and break its hold on her family. However, not before it unleashes a terrifying attack on them, leaving them shaken and traumatized.

Throughout the movie, the filmmakers use clever camera work and editing techniques to create a sense of tension and unease. The use of found footage adds to the realism of the film, making the audience feel like they are experiencing the events firsthand.

Overall, Paranormal Activity 4 is a chilling horror film that builds on the success of its predecessors. It's a gripping story that explores themes of family, trauma, and the supernatural, leaving viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

documents.title: From Up on Poppy Hill
documents.tagline: Let’s walk facing upwards.
documents.overview: Two high schoolers find hope as they fight to save an old wartime era clubhouse from destruction during the preparations for the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.
documents.plot:
From Up on Poppy Hill is a 2011 Japanese animated drama film written and directed by Gorō Miyazaki, the eldest son of Studio Ghibli's co-founder Hayao Miyazaki. The film is set in 1964, during the height of Japan's post-war economic boom.

The story takes place in the seaside town of Shirokane, where a group of high school students are struggling to find their place in the world. The main character, Umi Kitano, is a shy and introverted girl who has just transferred to Shirokane High School from a rural area. She becomes fast friends with Shun Kazama, a charismatic and confident student who is also an avid photographer.

As they explore the town together, Umi and Shun stumble upon a mysterious clubhouse hidden in the attic of a former school building. The clubhouse was once the hangout spot for the school's baseball team, but it has been abandoned since the team disbanded years ago. The two friends decide to restore the clubhouse to its former glory and make it their own secret hideout.

As they work on the clubhouse, Umi and Shun begin to uncover the town's history and secrets. They learn about the town's past glories as a major industrial center and the struggles of its people during World War II. They also discover that the clubhouse was once the site of a tragic accident that resulted in the death of several students.

Through their research, Umi and Shun develop feelings for each other, but they are hesitant to express them due to their different personalities and social status. Meanwhile, the town is facing a crisis as the local factory, which has been the backbone of the economy, announces its closure due to declining profits.

As the school year comes to a close, Umi and Shun must confront their own feelings for each other and find a way to save the clubhouse from being demolished. In the process, they learn valuable lessons about friendship, love, and the importance of preserving the past.

The film's title, "From Up on Poppy Hill," refers to the iconic poppy hill that dominates the town's landscape. The hill is a symbol of the town's history and resilience, and it serves as a backdrop for Umi and Shun's journey of self-discovery.

Throughout the film, Miyazaki explores themes of identity, community, and the power of human connection. He also pays tribute to the post-war generation in Japan, who were shaped by the country's tumultuous history and struggled to find their place in the world.

Overall, From Up on Poppy Hill is a poignant and beautifully animated film that celebrates the beauty of small-town life and the importance of preserving our collective past.

documents.title: Cloud Atlas
documents.tagline: Everything is Connected
documents.overview: A set of six nested stories spanning time between the 19th century and a distant post-apocalyptic future. Cloud Atlas explores how the actions and consequences of individual lives impact one another throughout the past, the present and the future. Action, mystery and romance weave through the story as one soul is shaped from a killer into a hero and a single act of kindness ripples across centuries to inspire a revolution in the distant future.  Based on the award winning novel by David Mitchell. Directed by Tom Tykwer and the Wachowskis.
documents.plot:
The story jumps between eras, spanning hundreds of years, until each storyline eventually resolves. Communications from characters in prior storylines are found in some of the future storylines, connecting a few of them. Characters appear to recur in each era, but change relationships to each other, suggesting reincarnation or other connection between souls through the ages.
In the Chatham Islands, 1849, American lawyer Adam Ewing is waiting for his transport ship to be repaired. He witnesses the whipping of Autua, an enslaved Moriori man. Autua stows away on Ewing's ship, having noticed Ewing's sympathy, and persuades him to advocate for Autua to join the crew as a free man. Autua saves Ewing's life before the ship's doctor, Henry Goose, can poison Ewing and steal his gold under the guise of treating him for a parasitic worm. In San Francisco, Ewing and his wife Tilda denounce her father's complicity in slavery and leave for New York to join the abolition movement.
In 1936, British composer Robert Frobisher finds work as an amanuensis to aging composer Vyvyan Ayrs, allowing Frobisher to compose his own masterpiece, "The Cloud Atlas Sextet". As the sextet nears completion, Ayrs demands credit for it and threatens to expose Frobisher's bisexuality if he refuses. Frobisher shoots and wounds Ayrs and goes into hiding. Frobisher finishes the sextet and shoots himself before his lover Rufus Sixsmith arrives.
In San Francisco, 1973, journalist Luisa Rey meets Sixsmith, now a nuclear physicist. Sixsmith tips off Rey to a conspiracy to create a catastrophe at a nuclear reactor run by Lloyd Hooks, who secretly promotes oil-energy interests. He is killed by Hooks' hitman, Bill Smoke, before he can give her a report as proof. Scientist Isaac Sachs passes her a copy of Sixsmith's report, but Smoke kills Sachs and then runs Rey's car off a bridge, destroying the report. With help from the plant's head of security, Joe Napier, Rey evades another murder attempt, and Smoke is bludegoned to death. With another copy of the report from Sixsmith's niece, Rey plans to expose the plot.
In London, 2012, Dermot Hoggins, a belligerent Irish gangster-turned-author, murders a critic after a harsh review of his memoir, generating huge sales. Hoggins's brothers threaten the publisher, the aging Timothy Cavendish, for Hoggins's profits. Timothy's brother, Denholme, tells him to hide at Aurora House, which he heads to while reading a manuscript about Rey. Believing Aurora House is a hotel, Timothy signs in, only to discover he has unwittingly committed himself to a nursing home where all outside contact is prohibited; Denholme reveals that he sent Timothy there as revenge for an affair with his wife. Timothy escapes with three other residents, resumes his relationship with an old flame, and writes a screenplay about his experience.
In Korea in 2144, Sonmi-451 is a "fabricant", a humanoid clone indentured as a fast food server in a dystopian Neo Seoul.

documents.title: Moonrise Kingdom
documents.tagline: A tormenting and surprising story of children and adults during the stormy days of the summer of 1965.
documents.overview: Set on an island off the coast of New England in the summer of 1965, Moonrise Kingdom tells the story of two twelve-year-olds who fall in love, make a secret pact, and run away together into the wilderness. As various authorities try to hunt them down, a violent storm is brewing off-shore – and the peaceful island community is turned upside down in more ways than anyone can handle.

documents.title: On the Road
documents.tagline: The best teacher is experience.
documents.overview: Dean and Sal are the portrait of the Beat Generation. Their search for "It" results in a fast paced, energetic roller coaster ride with highs and lows throughout the U.S.
documents.plot:
In 1947 New York, on the day his father is buried, Sal Paradise is out with his friend Carlo Marx who is, like him, an aspiring writer. They're invited by mutual friend Chad to meet Dean Moriarty, a young car thief from Denver, and Dean's 16-year-old wife Marylou. Sal and Carlo befriend Dean, smoking marijuana with him and visiting a jazz nightclub where they meet saxophonist Walter, who also befriends them. Sal teaches Dean how to write before Dean leaves for Denver with Carlo.
After much contemplation, writer's block, and a solemn visit to his father's grave, Sal decides to join his friends in Denver and embarks on the road for the first time. There, Sal meets Camille, an art college student for whom Dean is divorcing Marylou. Carlo starts to question his sexuality, and Carlo and Dean start an affair. Carlo, Sal, Camille, and Dean visit a bar where Dean plays "I've Got the World on a String" on the jukebox, and Camille bonds with Sal. Carlo tells Sal he thinks he might be gay, and he plans to travel to Africa.
Sal leaves aboard a bus and meets Terry. The two travel to California, where Terry works on cotton fields with her family while Sal helps. Sal and Terry have a brief affair before Sal, realizing he isn't made to work in the fields, heads back home.
In December 1948, Dean, Marylou, and Ed Dunkel arrive at Sal's sister's home in North Carolina, having left Ed's wife Galatea with Old Bull Lee in Louisiana. Sal's family feeds the trio, who haven't eaten for 30 hours, and the next day the trio, Sal, and Sal's mother drive back to New York. The guys and Marylou celebrate New Year's Eve at Carlo's place. Later, Dean convinces Sal to partake in a threesome with him and Marylou. Sal starts kissing Marylou, but Dean's presence makes him nervous, so he tells Dean to go to the kitchen. Following this, Dean and Marylou have sex, while Sal listens in the other room.
The next day, they ride off to California and leave Ed at Bull's. When they arrive in San Francisco, Dean drives to Camille's place, leaving Sal and Marylou to rent a room, where the two have sex. The next morning, Marylou leaves to return to her sailor fiancé in Denver, and Sal goes over to visit Dean and Camille, who by now have a child together and are expecting a second. Sal and Dean visit a nightclub, leaving Camille alone to deal with the baby. When they return home, she kicks Dean out.
Sal and Dean travel to Denver in search of Dean's father, but have no luck finding him. They then travel back to New York with a tall, thin salesman from whom Dean tries to get money in exchange for sex. Dean succeeds, which gives him and Sal enough money to get where they need to go.
Eight months later, Dean asks Sal if he would like to drive to Mexico. When they arrive a kid gets high with them and leads them to a whorehouse, where Dean and Sal dance and have sex with some of the prostitutes. They later roam the streets getting stoned and drunk.

documents.title: Sand Sharks
documents.tagline: Just When You Thought You Were Safe Out of the Water
documents.overview: Just when you thought it was safe to go back to the beach, it appears that our large fishy friends have found a way to chomp on you when you're chilling out on the sand too!
documents.plot:
Two people on dirt bikes are riding on the beach, but are then attacked by a predator in the sand. Meanwhile, Jimmy Green (Corin Nemec) the son of the Mayor (Edgar Allan Poe IV) of the small island town of White Sands returns home to throw a party. At the same time the local sheriff John Stone (Eric Scott Woods) is investigating the deaths of the men from earlier believing it to be a murder. Years prior to the events John's wife and child along with 13 other people were murdered in a shark fling at a party Jimmy threw and doesn't believe they are dealing with it again. John's sister, Deputy Brenda Stone (Vanessa Evigan), contacts a shark expert against her brother's wishes.
A couple is devoured by a sand shark and on the other side of the beach as Jimmy is preparing for a layout with Willie (Delpaneaux Wills), Erin (Hilary Cruz) and Amanda Gore (Gina Holden) is confronted by John and Brenda (the latter had a previous fling with Jimmy and is not happy to see him). Just then, a couple having fun on the beach are both attacked by a sand shark causing panic.
At a town meeting, the locals can't afford to have the beaches closed as the town is already in a financial crisis. A man named Angus McSorely (Robert Pike Daniel) tells them they are dealing with actual sand sharks that can swim through sand and offers to take care of them for the town, but is written off as crazy. Sandy Powers (Brooke Hogan), the shark expert Brenda called, was watching the meeting and has a talk with John while examining a shark tooth.
At night two men are being stalked by a sand shark while on their raft in the water. They try to escape but the shark moves on land and devours them. Fearing his party may be cancelled, Jimmy calls someone to bring an already dead shark but because the tooth found does not match the dead shark, the beach must stay closed.
After a power outage caused by the shark, Brenda arrests Jimmy and we learn of their relationship from before the film's events. They spot John on the beach with three guys at gun point as one of them brought a fake shark to fool him into keeping the beaches open. After seeing a dorsal fin moving in the sand they all realize the old man was right. Sparky (Jack Kennedy) who brought the fake shark does not hear the others telling him to get off the sand as he was trying to get the power back on and is killed by the shark who ultimately dies after chomping on the electrical cable causing it to explode and turn to glass.
With the threat gone the beaches are reopen and the party is back on. However the tooth found earlier is only a baby tooth and Sandy believes the dead shark's mother is out there looking for its baby. With the party underway it is revealed there are more sand sharks as both Amanda and Willie are killed by one. More sand sharks appear and start killing the party goers and Brenda is also killed trying to get people off the beach.

documents.title: You're Next
documents.tagline: Did You Remember To Lock Your Door?
documents.overview: When the Davison family comes under attack during their wedding anniversary getaway, the gang of mysterious killers soon learns that one of their victims harbors a secret talent for fighting back.

documents.title: Frenemies
documents.tagline: Geek vs Chic. Beauty vs Beast. Downtown vs Uptown. What happens when three sets of BFF's become enemies?
documents.overview: Zendaya and Bella Thorne, who play Rocky and CeCe in hit Disney Channel series Shake It Up, star in this Disney Channel Original Movie. Three pairs of friends relationships go from good to bad and back again. Several couple fall out over girls, boys and work. Can all these couples settle their differences and be friends again?
documents.plot:
Frenemies is a 2012 Disney Channel Original Movie, a teen comedy-drama anthology based on Alexa Young's novel of the same name. Daisy Mayer directed from a script by Dava Savel, Wendy Weiner and Jim Krieg, and the cast is led by Bella Thorne and Zendaya, then the leads of Shake It Up, alongside Nick Robinson, Stefanie Scott, Mary Mouser in a dual role, Connor Price, Dylan Everett and Jascha Washington, in his final film role. Set in the fictional town of Waterbury, New Jersey, it weaves together three stories of friends who turn into rivals and back again.

In the first, science prodigy Jake Logan is inseparable from his dog Murray. Popular classmate Julianne wants Jake as her science-project partner to secure another A, and the dog seems to see through her. To get Murray out of the way, she soaks Jake's prized NASA certificate in her perfume and slips it through his door; Murray, mistaking it for one of her love notes, tries to flush it, and the furious Jake tells him to leave. The runaway dog is taken in by Savannah, a skateboarder with a crush on Jake. When Jake uncovers the plot, Savannah exposes Julianne's habit of using people for grades, and Murray returns home.

In the second, best friends Avalon and Halley run a fashion web magazine called GeeklyChic. Cherie St. Claire of the New York publisher Burns Publications offers to buy it, but says only one of them can be senior editor and asks each to write a cover story to decide. Their rivalry escalates over an interview with a French pop singer, until he admits he is really an American named Johnny Frankewski. The girls choose to share the byline, which costs them the deal, but a television show picks up their story and GeeklyChic goes global.

In the third, tomboy Savannah and wealthy private-school girl Emma, who look exactly alike, swap lives, each believing the other has it better. Complications follow when Emma, posing as Savannah, flirts with Jake, and Savannah goes out with Emma's boyfriend Lance, but at Emma's birthday ball the girls make up and switch back, and the film closes with a dance.

The film was shot in Richmond Hill, Ontario, in the spring of 2011, and premiered on Disney Channel in the United States and Canada on 13 January 2012, drawing about 4.2 million viewers on its debut.

documents.title: Bachelorette
documents.tagline: Old habits party hard.
documents.overview: Three friends are asked to be bridesmaids at a wedding of a woman they used to ridicule back in high school.
documents.plot:
Regan Crawford is having lunch with her longtime friend, Becky Archer, who reveals that she will marry her boyfriend, Dale. Although secretly jealous of the fact that her friend is now engaged, Regan notifies their two other friends Gena Myers and Katie Lawrence.
Six months later, the women are preparing for Becky's bachelorette party that evening; Gena flies from Los Angeles to New York City, and the four meet at the hotel, where Katie announces that Gena has brought cocaine for them all. At the dinner party that night, Gena runs into her ex Clyde, whom she sees flirting with Dale's younger sister, and Katie runs into Joe, a former classmate and pot dealer. Trevor, the best man, gives a speech at the party, and Gena says in her toast that she once caught Becky forcing herself to throw up in the high school bathrooms.
After the dinner, the women go to their suite, where Katie's co-worker arrives and does a striptease for them, but Becky stops it after he jokingly calls her "Pigface", a cruel high school nickname. She leaves the bachelorette party, and Regan, Gena and Katie stay in the room where they keep drinking and doing cocaine. Drunk and high, the three accidentally rip Becky's bridal gown, and Katie stains it with a nosebleed.
Regan contacts a friend who owns a bridal store, who reluctantly agrees to open it for them in the middle of the night. After unsuccessfully searching the store for a dress for Becky, Katie reveals that she can sew, which leads them on a hunt for thread and a sewing machine. Trevor text messages Regan, inviting them to stop by the strip club where the men are, which they agree to. Gena takes the dress into the strip club's bathroom where she attempts to clean it; there, she has a conversation with a stripper who uses the dress as a towel and toilet paper.
Regan, furious over the situation, gets into an argument with Gena who insists they confess everything to Becky, and it is revealed in the argument that Gena had an abortion. Gena leaves the club with Clyde and the dress.
Meanwhile, Joe attempts to woo Katie, who is heavily intoxicated and high on cocaine, and Regan ends up having sex with Trevor in the strip club bathroom. Clyde and Gena spend the evening together reminiscing and have sex. Meanwhile, Joe and Katie spend the night in the hotel swimming pool, where Katie reveals that she attempted suicide the year before. Becky calls and asks Regan to come to her room so they can talk; in their conversation, it is revealed that Regan is bulimic, and that Becky covered it for her in high school. Just as Regan begins to tell Becky about her dress, Becky's mother arrives, and they begin to prepare for the wedding.
Gena and Clyde head to the wedding in the morning while the party planners can't find the dress. Gena asks a maid at the hotel to help her to touch-up the dress before bringing it to Becky; meanwhile, Katie locks herself in the bathroom and overdoses on Xanax.

documents.title: Compliance
documents.tagline: How far would you go?
documents.overview: On a particularly busy day at a suburban Ohio fast food restaurant, manager Sandra receives a phone call from a police officer saying that an employee has stolen money from a customer.
documents.plot:
Compliance is a 2012 American thriller written and directed by Craig Zobel, starring Ann Dowd, Dreama Walker, Pat Healy and Bill Camp. It is closely based on the strip search phone call scams that culminated in an incident at a fast-food restaurant in Mount Washington, Kentucky, in 2004, in which a caller posing as a police officer persuaded a restaurant manager and others to subject an innocent employee to unlawful and humiliating treatment. The names of the real people were changed.

On a busy day at a ChickWich fast-food restaurant in Ohio, the manager, Sandra, is already under pressure when she receives a phone call from a man who identifies himself as Officer Daniels. He claims that a customer has accused one of her employees of stealing money from her purse and that he is in contact with Sandra's regional manager. Based on his description, Sandra identifies Becky, a young cashier, as the suspect and brings her into the back office. Becky denies the accusation, but the caller insists that Sandra detain her until police officers arrive.

Speaking with calm authority and invoking legal consequences, the caller persuades Sandra to search Becky's belongings and then to strip-search her, claiming that the alternative is jail. Over the course of several hours, as Sandra returns to running the busy restaurant, the caller enlists other employees and finally Sandra's fiancé, Van, to watch over Becky, escalating his demands into increasingly degrading and abusive acts. Only when an older maintenance worker refuses to cooperate and Sandra calls her regional manager does the deception unravel. The police eventually trace the calls to a family man working as a telemarketer, and in the aftermath Sandra insists that she too was a victim.

The film examines obedience to authority and the ease with which ordinary people can be manipulated into participating in abuse.

Compliance premiered at the 2012 Sundance Film Festival, where it provoked strong reactions, and received a limited release in the United States in August 2012. It received generally positive reviews, with 89 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised its sensitive direction and strong performances. Dowd's performance as Sandra won the National Board of Review Award for Best Supporting Actress.

documents.title: The First Time
documents.tagline: Nervous is normal.
documents.overview: Dave, a high school senior, spends most of his time pining away over a girl he can’t have. Aubrey, a junior with artistic aspirations, has a hot boyfriend who doesn’t quite understand her or seem to care. Although they go to different schools, Dave and Aubrey find themselves at the same party. When both head outside to get some air, they meet. A casual conversation sparks an instant connection, and, over the course of a weekend, things turn magical, romantic, complicated, and funny as Aubrey and Dave discover what it's like to fall in love for the first time.
documents.plot:
High school senior, Dave, meets junior, Aubrey, outside a house party, while rehearsing a confession of love for his best friend, Jane. The police bust the party, and Aubrey asks Dave to walk her home despite having a boyfriend. She invites him to her room, and they have wine and talk. Aubrey asks him if he is still a virgin, and he admits he is. However, she refuses to answer the same question. Then they accidentally fall asleep. The next morning, Aubrey's mother's knock wakes them, so Dave sneaks out the window. Dave meets with his friends, Simon and Big Corporation, for breakfast, and they believe Aubrey may have lied about having a boyfriend. That night Dave, Jane, and their friends go to the movies. Aubrey also unexpectedly shows up with her boyfriend, Ronny. During the movie, Aubrey gets jealous at how close Dave and Jane are getting and leaves the theater, and Dave follows her. Dave gets her cell number and invites her and Ronny to a gathering afterwards.
Later, Aubrey and Jane talk about Dave. She sees Jane has high praise for him, but does not appreciate him. Meanwhile, a drunk Ronny brags that he and Aubrey are planning to have sex that night. Dave finds Aubrey and tells her not to do it as her first time should be with someone special. She opposes the romantic notion of the first time being so important and says it is none of his business. Ronny finds them and tells Aubrey they need to go. Dave intercedes, nearly fighting before his buddies intervene. Aubrey leaves with Ronny. At the end of the party, Dave is in a bedroom with Jane, and he realizes he would rather be with Aubrey and leaves. He gets a text from Aubrey asking him to pick her up, he obliges. As Dave and Aubrey cruise, she tells him she broke up with Ronny, and they hold hands. They then pass the aftermath of a car accident, teens who had offered them a ride right the previous night. Upsetting Aubrey, Dave pulls over. They realize their mutual feelings and kiss.
They meet at a park with Dave's little sister Stella the next day. Aubrey's parents are out for the night, so she invites Dave over. He contemplates bringing a condom, but decides against it. As they make out, they hesitate before deciding to have sex. Dave awkwardly puts on a condom Aubrey has. Afterwards, both are upset as it felt unsatisfying, and feel awkward talking about it. Everything they say makes it worse, so they agree it was a mistake and should not see each other. However, they both regret it; Aubrey keeps hoping Dave will call, while he repeatedly starts to, but hangs up.
Meeting with Simon and Big Corporation, he tells them the idea of sex was better than the reality. Big Corporation tells him he and Aubrey just hit a speed bump because it was their first time, but they should try again. The following morning, Aubrey tells her parents she regrets pushing Dave away, and they try to soothe her. When she walks outside, Dave is waiting for her in the driveway.

documents.title: The Day
documents.tagline: Fight. Or die.
documents.overview: Open war against humanity rages. For five survivors – lost and on the run – the pursuit is relentless, the bullets are dwindling and the battle is everywhere. This is a 24-hour look into their lives.
documents.plot:
The Day is a 2011 Canadian post-apocalyptic thriller film directed by Douglas Aarniokoski from a screenplay by Luke Passmore. It stars Shawn Ashmore as Adam, Dominic Monaghan as Rick, Shannyn Sossamon as Shannon, Cory Hardrict as Henson and Ashley Bell as Mary, with Michael Eklund as the leader of a cannibal tribe.

In a ravaged countryside, five survivors, the last of a group that once numbered twelve, wander in search of food and shelter while avoiding the savage cannibal tribes that roam the land, carrying two jars of seeds they hope to plant. Adam is haunted by flashbacks of the day he left his wife and daughter in the car while he searched a house for supplies, only for them to be taken. With Henson ill, the group shelters in an abandoned farmhouse. While cleaning up at a stream, Mary is chased by a tribal scout and shoots him. In the basement, the men find boxes of tins that turn out to hold rocks, setting off a trap that sounds an alarm, seals them in and kills Rick. Shannon and Mary kill the cannibals who come for the men, but one of them recognizes a tribal mark on Mary's thigh before she kills him. After freeing the men, Shannon knocks Mary out, and the survivors tie her to a chair. Adam, enraged by Rick's death, tortures her, cutting the mark from her skin until Henson stops him. Mary finally explains that she had nothing to do with the loss of Adam's family; she had slaughtered her own tribe in their sleep after they killed and ate her younger sister, who had broken her leg. She warns that the tribe that laid the trap is coming. The four burn Rick's body and fortify the house, and at night waves of attackers storm it. Henson dies saving Shannon, and when Shannon accidentally kills the tribal leader's young son, the leader sends his daughter to take revenge. At dawn the cannibals set the house ablaze with Molotov cocktails. Mary stays behind so the others can escape, only to find that Shannon has taken her shotgun shells, and Adam returns to save her, dying of his wounds. In the woods, the leader's daughter cuts Shannon's throat. After cremating Adam, Mary meets the girl, who feigns innocence before reaching for a blade, but Mary kills her first and walks away.

Shot in Ottawa in the fall of 2010, the film premiered at the 2011 Toronto International Film Festival and opened in 12 US theaters in August 2012, grossing $20,984. Reviews were mixed, with 31% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 41.

documents.title: Julia X
documents.overview: Meeting a man on the Internet, Julia decides to see him in person, only to get abducted and branded with the letter "x" by that guy. A game of cat and mouse follows, but the story has an unexpected twist.
documents.plot:
Julia X (released in 3D as Julia X 3D) is a 2011 American horror thriller with darkly comic touches, directed by P.J. Pettiette, who devised the story, from a screenplay by Matt Cunningham, and produced by Dixie Theatrical Corporation on a budget of about $4 million. It stars Valerie Azlynn as Julia, Kevin Sorbo as a serial killer known only as the Stranger, and Alicia Leigh Willis as her sister Jessica, with Joel David Moore and Ving Rhames. It premiered on 24 September 2011.

Julia meets a man she has been chatting with online for a date at a restaurant but, uneasy, cuts the evening short. As she heads home he overpowers her in her car and forces her to drive to his lair, where he strings her up from a hook in his garage. She briefly frees herself and hides, but he catches her and brands her with the letter X, the mark he leaves on his victims. Bound in the back of his van, she discovers the body of a previous victim, branded W; while he is burying it she gets hold of the keys to her handcuffs and escapes, fleeing through fields and swamp to a derelict house and then an abandoned school building. There she ambushes him and knocks him out, and her sister Jessica drives up to collect her.

The tables turn. The sisters, it emerges, are predators themselves who lure men like him, and they take the unconscious Stranger home, tie him to a chair with barbed wire and torment him. Flashbacks reveal their abusive childhood, and tension grows between protective Julia and Jessica, who resents always playing second fiddle and wants to be the bait for once. When Jessica kidnaps Sam, a young mechanic from across the street, the situation spirals: the Stranger breaks free and a frantic chase through the house follows. In the end Jessica betrays her sister, stabbing Julia, killing the Stranger and setting the house on fire, then resumes the game under the name Julia Y, while a final shot suggests Julia may have survived.

Joel David Moore plays Sam and Ving Rhames appears in a role credited simply as The Man. In Germany the film ran into trouble with the ratings board, which refused it a theatrical certificate, and the uncut version was later placed on the country's index of media harmful to minors. Critic Christian Ihle of the taz praised its socio-political subtext and its entertaining middle section but found the opening chase dreadful.

documents.title: The Imposter
documents.tagline: There are two sides to every lie.
documents.overview: In 1994 a 13-year-old boy disappeared without a trace from his home in San Antonio, Texas. Three-and-a-half years later he is found alive thousands of miles away in a village in southern Spain with a horrifying story of kidnap and torture. His family is overjoyed to bring him home. But all is not quite as it seems.
documents.plot:
The story begins in a phone box in Spain where Bourdin phones the police saying he is a tourist who has found a young boy in a phone box and the police should collect him. He is taken to a children's home and says he is American. He asks to be left in an office overnight to call his family. There he uses records in the office to contact various sheriff's offices in the USA asking about missing children. Through one lead he gets the name Nicholas Barclay. He then calls to another US agency claiming to be a Spanish official and asking to fax info on Nicholas. This is done and begins a task of Bourdin trying to look like Nicholas, including getting matching tattoos and dying his hair blond.
Nicholas's family is told of the discovery and the sister flies to Spain to collect him. A court decides it is Nicholas and he is declared a US citizen. She takes him back to San Antonio in Texas where most of the family accept him. The mother is especially keen to welcome him and recognize him as her son.
Bourdin, who turned out to have a long record of impersonating various children, real or imaginary, embellished his claim to be Nicholas Barclay by alleging that he had been kidnapped for purposes of sexual abuse by Mexican, European and U.S. military personnel and transported from the US to Spain. His impersonation fooled several officials in Spain and the U.S., and he was apparently accepted by many of Barclay's family members, even though he was seven years older than Barclay, spoke with a French accent, and had brown eyes and dark hair rather than Barclay's blue eyes and blonde hair. The impersonation was eventually discovered as a result of the suspicions of a private investigator, Charles (Charlie) Parker, and an FBI agent, Nancy Fisher. Bourdin was arrested and Interpol confirmed he was Bourdin, was 23 years old and had a long criminal record. In custody Bourdin tells the police that the family killed the real Nicholas and that is why they accepted him, as it hid the crime. The main suspect is his brother Jason, who is already dead and is therefore a ready scapegoat.
Layton said of Bourdin: "He invites sympathy. He has this childlike quality about him, and he can be very charming. And at other times he can be quite repellent, because he can be remorseless and you're reminded about what he did. So as a filmmaker, I was asking: how can I find a way of getting the audience to experience a bit of that?"

documents.title: Liberal Arts
documents.tagline: Sometimes students make the best teachers.
documents.overview: Newly single, 35, and uninspired by his job, Jesse Fisher worries that his best days are behind him. But no matter how much he buries his head in a book, life keeps pulling Jesse back. When his favorite college professor invites him to campus to speak at his retirement dinner, Jesse jumps at the chance. He is prepared for the nostalgia of the dining halls and dorm rooms, the parties and poetry seminars; what he doesn’t see coming is Zibby – a beautiful, precocious, classical-music-loving sophomore. Zibby awakens scary, exciting, long-dormant feelings of possibility and connection that Jesse thought he had buried forever.
documents.plot:
Liberal Arts is a 2012 American romantic comedy-drama written and directed by Josh Radnor, who also stars as Jesse Fisher, a thirty-five-year-old college admissions officer. Elizabeth Olsen plays Zibby, a nineteen-year-old student, with Richard Jenkins, Allison Janney, Elizabeth Reaser, John Magaro and Zac Efron. The film was shot largely at Kenyon College in Ohio, Radnor's alma mater, and premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2012 before its release that September.

Jesse, a New York college admissions officer who loves literature, is newly single and dissatisfied with his life and career. He believes that the happiest time of his life was his years at a small liberal arts college in Ohio, where he could read and study surrounded by like-minded people. When his favorite former professor, Peter Hoberg, invites him back to campus for his retirement dinner, Jesse eagerly returns.

There he meets Zibby, a sophomore drama student and the daughter of Peter's friends. They run into each other at a campus party and spend the next day together walking around the campus, talking about life, books and music. Jesse also reconnects with Judith Fairfield, his former professor of Romantic literature, whom he has long admired, and meets Nat, an eccentric free spirit, and Dean, a brilliant but depressed student who, like Jesse, always carries a book. After Jesse returns to New York, he and Zibby begin a correspondence through handwritten letters, sharing music and growing closer. Meanwhile, Peter, lost at the prospect of retirement, asks to stay on but learns that his replacement has already been hired. When Zibby invites Jesse back to campus, hinting that she is ready to take their relationship further, he must confront the sixteen-year age difference between them, his own nostalgia for a past that may not have been as perfect as he remembers, and what it means to grow up.

Liberal Arts received generally positive reviews, with a 71 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said that, while it could have used more bite, it succeeded as a good-natured and surprisingly clever look at the addictive pull of nostalgia for youth. It scored 55 on Metacritic, and critics praised Olsen's and Jenkins's performances.

documents.title: Robot & Frank
documents.tagline: Friendship doesn't have an off switch
documents.overview: Curmudgeonly old Frank lives by himself. His routine involves daily visits to his local library, where he has a twinkle in his eye for the librarian. His grown children are concerned about their father’s well-being and buy him a caretaker robot. Initially resistant to the idea, Frank soon appreciates the benefits of robotic support – like nutritious meals and a clean house – and eventually begins to treat his robot like a true companion. With his robot’s assistance, Frank’s passion for his old, unlawful profession is reignited, for better or worse.
documents.plot:
Set in the near future, aging ex-convict and thief Frank Weld lives alone and suffers from increasingly severe mental deterioration and dementia. Frank's son Hunter, an attorney with a family of his own, grows tired of making weekly visits to his father's home without his kids, but is reluctant to put his father into full-time care, so he purchases a robot companion, which is programmed to provide Frank with therapeutic care, including a fixed daily routine and cognition-enhancing activities like gardening.
Initially wary of the robot's presence in his life, Frank warms up to his new companion when he realizes the robot is not programmed to distinguish between legal recreational activities and criminal ones, and can assist him in lock-picking. Together, the two commit a heist in order to win the affection of the local librarian, Jennifer: they steal an antique copy of Don Quixote from the library, which is being renovated and turned into a community center in the wake of declining interest in print media.
In the meantime, Frank's daughter Madison, who is away on a philanthropic trip in Turkmenistan, learns of the robot and returns to convince her father to get rid of the machine, which she finds ethically objectionable. Frank insists on keeping the robot, and they commit one last heist, stealing jewels from Jake, the rich young developer at the head of the library renovation project. The police become involved and begin to question and monitor Frank, who maintains his innocence, feigning deathly illness so that Hunter will return to see him. In order to cover his tracks, Frank is faced with the decision of whether to wipe the memory of his robot, even as his own memory rapidly deteriorates.
Frank goes to the library where he discovers that Jennifer is his ex-wife, which he had forgotten. He then returns home where the robot convinces him to wipe its holographic memory; it argues that it is not a real person and its sole reason for existence is to help Frank, which it can best do by helping him avoid jail. Frank then moves into a full-time care facility to help him cope with his dementia. During a visit from his family, he slips Hunter a note, implying that the jewels are hidden under the tomato plants in the garden that the robot made.

documents.title: Tooth Fairy 2
documents.tagline: He didn’t ask for it. He wasn’t expecting it. He’s not prepared for it.
documents.overview: Larry Guthrie, who loses his first love to the town hot shot, decides to win her back by volunteering with the children at her after-school program. When Larry accidentally tells the kids the Tooth Fairy is make-believe, he soon is transformed into a tutu-clad fairy with the "sentence" of collecting teeth.
documents.plot:
Larry Guthrie (Larry the Cable Guy), a dreamer from a small town, is awarded the title of "Metro County Miracle." While on his way to a child's birthday party, Larry and his girlfriend Brooke (Erin Beute) stop at a raffle for a Camaro convertible. Larry puts his name in the raffle, against Brooke’s will, and wins the chance to get the car. In order to win, Larry has three chances to knock down two bowling pins on either side of the lane. On his third try, with both bowling pins left, he slips on nacho cheese sauce and successfully knocks down the pins with the bowling ball. Some time later, after Larry and Brooke end their relationship, Larry finds out that Brooke is engaged to the hotshot of the town, Beauregard "Bo" Billings (David Mackey). Bo Billings is a candidate for mayor of the town, which motivates Larry to attempt to win her back.
In order to win back Brooke's affection, Larry volunteers at the local after-school program that Brooke runs. On his first day volunteering, he tells one of the children that the Tooth Fairy isn't real, deeply upsetting the little boy Gabe, and making him doubt the realness of the Tooth Fairy.
That night, Larry is approached by a Tooth Fairy named Nyx and gets a head-to-toe pink fairy outfit, who tells him he is a substitute Tooth Fairy and must collect ten teeth in ten days. Larry is given fairy dust to help him and is told that if he fails to collect ten teeth, his greatest memory will be taken away.
Larry awakens from what he thought was a dream, but soon finds out he was wrong. The following night, he turns into the Tooth Fairy and goes to collect his first tooth. He manages to collect it, with some difficulty, but is very proud of his abilities. The next night, he turns into the Tooth Fairy again.
During this time, he is beginning to make improvements at the after-school program, helping them raise money for new supplies. Brooke is starting to warm up to him and tells him she is happy with what he has done. The couple goes wedding cake testing, where Larry, unlike Bo, who shows up to get her away from Larry, remembers Brooke is allergic to strawberries and likes orange buttercream, which impresses her. He then offers to go out and buy the supplies with the money they made, in hopes of impressing Brooke further.
Shortly after Larry collects the supplies for the program, he turns into the Tooth Fairy and is forced to serve his duties. While he is collecting a tooth, Bo steals the supplies, in order to make Larry look bad. When Larry returns from collecting the tooth, he is shocked to find his car empty, and has to break the news to Brooke and the kids the next day.
Feeling discouraged, Larry decides to quit his job as the Tooth Fairy and lose what he thought was his greatest memory. When he finds out that winning the Metro County Miracle wasn't his greatest memory, he is confused. He decides to reclaim his role as the Tooth Fairy, with little time to spare.

documents.title: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
documents.original_title: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
documents.tagline: We are infinite.
documents.overview: Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, 1991. High school freshman Charlie is a wallflower, always watching life from the sidelines, until two senior students, Sam and her stepbrother Patrick, become his mentors, helping him discover the joys of friendship, music and love.
documents.plot:
The Perks of Being a Wallflower is a 2012 American coming-of-age drama written and directed by Stephen Chbosky, based on his 1999 novel. Logan Lerman stars as Charlie, a withdrawn freshman, with Emma Watson as Sam and Ezra Miller as Patrick. Mae Whitman, Nina Dobrev, Kate Walsh and Paul Rudd, as his English teacher, co-star.

In 1991, Charlie, depressed since childhood and recently out of a psychiatric hospital, starts high school with no friends but his English teacher. He meets two seniors, the stepsiblings Patrick and Sam, who invite him to a party after the homecoming dance. There he discovers that Patrick is secretly seeing Brad, the closeted star quarterback. When Charlie reveals that his best friend killed himself the year before, Sam and Patrick take him into their group. Driving home, Sam stands in the back of the pickup in the Fort Pitt Tunnel as an unknown song plays. Charlie tutors Sam for the SAT so she can get into Penn State, and they grow close. Learning he has never been kissed, she gives him his first kiss, despite her crush on Craig. At a New Year's party, Charlie takes LSD and is overwhelmed by memories of his beloved Aunt Helen, who died in a car crash while buying his seventh birthday present.

Dating Mary Elizabeth, Charlie kisses Sam on a dare in front of her, and the group shuts him out. After Brad's father catches him with Patrick, Brad publicly turns on Patrick. When Brad's friends beat Patrick in the cafeteria, Charlie blacks out and fights them off, regaining his friends. The night before she leaves, she and Charlie kiss, but her touch triggers a disturbing flashback. Once she is gone, his mental state collapses, and he calls Candace, blaming himself for Helen's death. Candace sends the police. In the hospital, a psychiatrist helps him recover the repressed memory that Helen sexually abused him. When he is released, Sam and Patrick return, and the three drive through the tunnel to the now-identified song, David Bowie's "Heroes". Charlie stands in the truck bed, feeling alive and infinite.

Chbosky insisted on writing and directing. Filming took place in Pittsburgh in 2011. The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival to a standing ovation and was released by Summit Entertainment on September 21, 2012, grossing about $33.4 million worldwide. Critics praised Chbosky's script and direction and the three lead performances. Rotten Tomatoes reported 85% approval, and Roger Ebert gave it three and a half stars.

documents.title: Boyhood
documents.tagline: 12 years in the making.
documents.overview: The film tells a story of a divorced couple trying to raise their young son. The story follows the boy for twelve years, from first grade at age 6 through 12th grade at age 17-18, and examines his relationship with his parents as he grows.
documents.plot:
Boyhood is a coming-of-age drama film written and directed by Richard Linklater, released in 2014. The film follows the life of Mason Jr., played by Ellar Coltrane, from age 6 to 18 over the course of 12 years.

The film begins with Mason Jr. (played as a child) living with his parents, Mason Sr. (played by Ethan Hawke) and Olivia (played by Patricia Arquette), in Austin, Texas. The family is shown to be struggling financially, but they are loving and supportive. As the story progresses, we see Mason Jr. grow up alongside his siblings, including his older sister Samantha (played by Lorelei Linklater).

The early years of Mason Jr.'s life are marked by a sense of stability and normalcy, with his parents trying to provide for him and his siblings despite their financial struggles. However, as the years pass, we see Mason Jr. face various challenges, including bullying at school, romantic relationships, and family conflicts.

One of the most significant plot points in the film is the divorce of Mason Sr. and Olivia, which occurs when Mason Jr. is 14. This event has a profound impact on Mason Jr., who struggles to come to terms with his parents' separation. The film also explores Mason Jr.'s relationships with his friends, including his best friend, Joe (played by Kyle Chandler), and his romantic interests, including his first love, Jessica (played by Emma Wright).

Throughout the film, Linklater uses a unique narrative structure, where each year of Mason Jr.'s life is represented by a different actor playing him. This allows for a sense of continuity and growth, as we see Mason Jr. evolve from a young boy to a teenager and eventually an adult.

The film's climax occurs when Mason Jr. graduates from high school and sets off on his own path in life. The final scenes show Mason Jr. as a young man, struggling to find his place in the world and navigate the challenges of adulthood.

Overall, Boyhood is a powerful and poignant coming-of-age story that explores themes of family, love, and identity. Through its unique narrative structure and strong performances, the film provides a nuanced and realistic portrayal of growing up and finding one's place in the world.

documents.title: A Few Best Men
documents.tagline: You are cordially invited to absolute mayhem
documents.overview: A groom and his three best men travel to the Australian outback for a wedding.
documents.plot:
A Few Best Men is a 2011 Australian comedy film directed by Stephan Elliott from a screenplay by Dean Craig. Xavier Samuel stars as David Locking, a young British man who travels to the Blue Mountains of Australia for his wedding, accompanied by his three best men. The cast also includes Kris Marshall as Tom, Kevin Bishop as Graham, Tim Draxl as Luke, Laura Brent as the bride, Mia Ramme, Olivia Newton-John as her mother, Barbara, Jonathan Biggins as her father, Jim, Rebel Wilson as Daphne Ramme, Steve Le Marquand as Ray and Elizabeth Debicki as Maureen.

David meets Mia while on holiday in Tuvalu, and only a week later he proposes. The couple plan to marry at her family's home in the Blue Mountains, and David rounds up his three best friends from Britain to fly out and serve as his best men. Mia's father, Jim, is a politician, and the arrival of the rowdy groomsmen at a family wedding with so much at stake for appearances is a recipe for disaster.

Once the friends arrive, the wedding weekend quickly spirals out of control. The three accidentally make off with a stash of drugs belonging to Ray, a local drug dealer, who comes after them to get his property back. Further trouble follows when the father-in-law's prized ram ends up stoned, and the guests' antics escalate through a series of increasingly outrageous mishaps that threaten to derail the ceremony, embarrass the bride's family and test David's relationship with Mia before the couple can finally make it down the aisle.

A Few Best Men premiered at the Mill Valley Film Festival in California on 14 October 2011 and was released in Australia on 26 January 2012 and in the United Kingdom on 31 August 2012. Newton-John sang most of the soundtrack, which Universal Music Australia released in January 2012. The film opened on 235 Australian screens with $1.9 million, third for the week, and went on to earn about $5.3 million locally, the fourth most successful Australian film of the year. Reviews were mostly negative, with 18% approval on Rotten Tomatoes; SBS's Fiona Williams gave it one star and called it overlong and flimsy. However, David Stratton and Margaret Pomeranz each gave it four stars on At the Movies, Stratton singling out Newton-John as hilarious. The film was nominated for the AACTA Award for Best Original Music Score, and a sequel, A Few Less Men, followed in 2017.
