documents.title: Le Chef
documents.tagline: Competition Can Be Delicious
documents.overview: A veteran chef faces off against his restaurant group's new CEO, who wants to the establishment to lose a star from its rating in order to bring in a younger chef who specializes in molecular gastronomy.
documents.plot:
Le Chef (French: Comme un chef) is a 2012 French comedy film directed by Daniel Cohen, starring Jean Reno as the celebrated chef Alexandre Lagarde and Michaël Youn as Jacky Bonnot, a talented but stubborn self-taught cook. The cast also includes Raphaëlle Agogué as Jacky's pregnant girlfriend Beatrice, Julien Boisselier as the restaurant's ambitious shareholder Stanislas Matter, Santiago Segura as a self-proclaimed expert in molecular gastronomy, Salomé Stévenin as Alexandre's daughter, Pierre Vernier as the restaurant's main shareholder Paul Matter and Kentaro as Alexandre's right-hand man.

Jacky Bonnot dreams of becoming a great chef, but his perfectionism and refusal to compromise keep getting him fired from restaurant jobs. With his girlfriend expecting a baby, he promises to take any work he can find and is hired as a painter at a retirement home, where he secretly helps the cooks transform the menu. News of his talent reaches Alexandre Lagarde, the star chef of the Cargo Lagarde restaurant and host of a television cooking show, who is facing a crisis of his own.

Lagarde's restaurant is at risk of losing one of its stars, and Stanislas Matter, the son of its main shareholder, wants to replace him with a younger chef specializing in fashionable molecular cuisine. Lagarde hires Jacky as an unpaid intern to help him reinvent his menu, but their clashing temperaments lead to constant conflict. As Jacky hides his new job from his girlfriend and their relationship suffers, the two chefs, aided by the retirement home's cooks, set out to understand molecular gastronomy and win over the critics who will decide the restaurant's fate.

The film satirizes trends in haute cuisine and the rivalry between traditional French cooking and molecular gastronomy, while telling a story of mentorship and second chances.

Le Chef had its international premiere at the 62nd Berlin International Film Festival in 2012 before its release in France in March 2012. Cohen Media Group distributed it in the United States.

documents.title: Pixie Hollow Games
documents.overview: Rosetta and new arrival Chloe band together to try to break the garden fairies' legendary losing streak in the Pixie Hollow Games, a sports spectacle filled with pixie pageantry, fantastic fairy events and hilarious surprises.
documents.plot:
Pixie Hollow Games is a 23-minute animated television special based on Disney's Disney Fairies franchise, first broadcast on Disney Channel on 19 November 2011. Produced by Disneytoon Studios and animated by Prana Studios, it features the voices of Megan Hilty as Rosetta, Brenda Song as the newcomer Chloe, Jason Dolley, Tiffany Thornton and Zendaya, along with returning cast members Mae Whitman as Tinker Bell, Lucy Liu, Raven-Symoné, Pamela Adlon and Angela Bartys. Inspired loosely by J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan by way of Disney's adaptation, the story follows the fairies of Pixie Hollow as they compete in an Olympic-style tournament.

Rosetta, an elegant garden fairy who prefers beauty and comfort to hard work, meets Chloe, an enthusiastic new garden fairy who has been training for the Pixie Hollow Games, a contest between the different fairy talents. The garden fairies have never won and are expected to lose again, but Chloe is convinced they can change their luck. When the teams are chosen, Chloe has already volunteered, and to her dismay Rosetta is selected as her partner. Certain that they will be eliminated in the first round, Rosetta shows up for the opening night in a fancy gown.

The heavy favorites are the storm fairies Rumble and Glimmer, whose long winning streak has earned them championship rings for almost every finger. The first event is a frog-riding race, in which Rosetta's reluctance to get onto her frog causes chaos on the track, but the pair advance when another team's equipment fails. Over the following days, Rosetta and Chloe compete in dragonfly water-skiing, a game played with twig spheres and mouse polo, gradually climbing the rankings. As the competition becomes more intense, Rosetta begins to take the games, and her partner, seriously, but tensions arise between the two as they reach the final event, where they must face Rumble and Glimmer and discover what being a team really means.

The special was released on DVD in 2012, along with other short films from the franchise. It was originally planned as part of a series of specials and features in the Tinker Bell series and was followed by the theatrical feature Secret of the Wings (2012). Like the other entries in the franchise, it centers on friendship and on the different talents of the fairies, here celebrated through teamwork and sportsmanship.

documents.title: Desire
documents.tagline: Love, desire and complications...
documents.overview: In a social context deteriorated by a countrywide economic crisis, the life of several people will be turned upside down after they meet Cécile, a character who symbolizes desire.
documents.plot:
Q, released in the United States as Desire, is a 2011 French erotic drama written and directed by Laurent Bouhnik. Set in Cherbourg, the film follows a loose group of young people whose lives are disrupted by a woman who embodies desire. The cast includes Déborah Révy, Hélène Zimmer, Gowan Didi, Johnny Amaro and Johan Libéreau. The film attracted attention for its unsimulated sex scenes, which members of its cast later discussed publicly.

Cécile is a 20-year-old woman whose father has recently died. Unable to confront her grief, she throws herself into sexual encounters with a succession of partners, friends and strangers alike. At the same time she appoints herself a guide to the people around her, sometimes seducing them and sometimes counseling patience, offering frank advice on how to give and receive pleasure. Her sometime boyfriend is Chance, a small-time criminal who loves her but cannot satisfy her. His friend Matt, who works as a mechanic, keeps pressuring his girlfriend Alice to sleep with him, but Alice does not feel ready. Meanwhile Chance and his friends scramble to earn money while trying to stay out of reach of rival criminals they have crossed.

On a ferry, Cécile eavesdrops on a married couple, flirts with the husband and slips him her number. It emerges that the wife has suffered a traumatic experience that makes intimacy difficult for her, and the couple's discussions about Cécile become a way of approaching their own problems. Alice, too, becomes involved in helping them, arranging a meeting in which the husband and wife come together blindfolded in an attempt to repair their relationship.

At a party organized by a group of women, Chance arrives carrying the urn holding the ashes of Cécile's father, which she has never been able to deal with. He tells her that he loves her and challenges her to take care of herself as she tries to care for everyone else. They leave together, and as they drive along the coast Cécile finally scatters her father's ashes. Having failed to find peace through her many encounters, including ones with Chance, Matt and Alice, she discovers another path toward healing and tells Chance that she loves him, though she knows it will not be easy.

The film's explicit content made it a subject of controversy. Hélène Zimmer, one of the lead actresses, said in 2015 that she had taken the role because of the challenge it represented, but admitted that she would happily remove the unsimulated sex scenes if she could.

documents.title: 2-Headed Shark Attack
documents.tagline: 1 Body, 2 Heads and 6,000 Teeth
documents.overview: A Semester at Sea ship is attacked and sunk by a mutated two-headed shark, and the survivors seek refuge on a deserted atoll. The coeds, however, are no longer safe when the atoll starts flooding.
documents.plot:
A group of wakeboarders is attacked and devoured by a two-headed great white shark. Meanwhile, Sea King, a Semester at Sea-like ship led by Professor Franklin Babish and his wife Anne, hits a dead shark, which becomes lodged in the boat's propeller, damaging the hull and causing the boat to take on water. The two-headed shark then attacks the boat and breaks the radio antenna, preventing the ship co-captain Laura from summoning help. Babish and the students use a dinghy to take shelter on a nearby deserted atoll, while Anne remains on the Sea King with Laura and the ship's crew, Han and Dikilla. Laura is ripped in half by the two-headed shark.
Meanwhile, Babish and the students explore the atoll. Assembling in an abandoned fishing village, they search for scrap metal to repair the boat. Haley and Alison go swimming topless with Kirk, and are eaten by the two-headed shark. The rest of the group meet up and find two speedboats before an earthquake hits, causing Babish to injure his leg. Dana bandages Babish's leg, while Jeff and Mike accompany him back to the Sea King on the dinghy. En route, Jeff and Mike are eaten by the shark while attempting to swim to the Sea King.
The students find two boats on the island, which Kate and Paul fix. Cole finds a gasoline tank to fuel them, but steals one of the boats together with Ryan, Jamie and Alex. Kate, Paul and Dana follow in the other boat. They are all unaware of the shark, which attacks Cole's boat. Ryan falls into the water and is eaten, alerting the others to the shark's presence. Paul concludes that it is drawn to Cole's boat as it has a bigger engine. Cole bails, and the shark eats Jamie and Alex. When the survivors reach shore, Kate confronts Cole for abandoning Jamie and Alex. Minutes later, the Sea King is abandoned and the survivors meet on the island.
Another earthquake then hits. The group realizes that the earthquakes are actually the atoll collapsing in on itself. They hook up a generator to metal poles and place them in the water to distract the shark while Kate and Cole travel to the Sea King and repair the hull. The plan works until the shark attacks the poles, knocking Han and Dikilla into the water to their deaths. Kate fixes the ship, only for Cole to drive away without her, forcing her to swim back to the atoll. The two-headed shark attacks the Sea King, causing it to sink and send out a distress signal; Cole escapes on a lifeboat but his cellphone rings alerting the shark. The shark attacks and eats Cole. The atoll is sinking too, prompting everyone to flee for their lives.
Kristen and Dana get separated from the group and are devoured. Franklin and Anne also get separated from the group, and after running into a dead-end due to a tsunami approaching the atoll, they share one final kiss as the shark eats them. The rest of the group end up in the water as the tsunami strikes the island. The remaining students swim into the half-sunk village chapel to hide, but the shark breaks in.

documents.title: Stoker
documents.tagline: Innocence Ends.
documents.overview: After India's father dies, her Uncle Charlie, who she never knew existed, comes to live with her and her unstable mother. She comes to suspect this mysterious, charming man has ulterior motives and becomes increasingly infatuated with him.
documents.plot: Following her father Richard's death in an unexplained road accident, reclusive teenager India Stoker withdraws further into the quiet rural life she shares with her emotionally disturbed mother Evie. But her curiosity is stirred when her mysterious uncle Charlie, who she has never met, suddenly arrives unannounced. Told that the darkly charismatic Charlie will now be staying at the house, India's initial well-founded distrust of her uncle's motivations begins to waver as she finds herself becoming ever more deeply entranced by his sinister charms.

documents.title: Absolutely Anything
documents.tagline: Great power. Total irresponsibility.
documents.overview: Eccentric aliens give a man the power to do anything he wants to determine if Earth is worth saving.
documents.plot:
Absolutely Anything is a 2015 British science fiction comedy film directed by Terry Jones, written by Terry Jones and Graham Linehan, and produced by Phoenix Pictures.

The movie follows the story of Neil Clarke (played by Simon Pegg), an ordinary man who lives in London. On his 65th birthday, he receives a letter from God (voiced by Alan Rickman) informing him that he has been chosen to receive five gifts: anything he wants, and they will be granted instantly.

Neil is initially skeptical but decides to use the gifts for personal gain. He chooses a private island, a spaceship, a million pounds, an infinite supply of his favorite food (pizza), and the ability to make anyone do what he wants. However, things quickly take a turn when Neil's new life becomes too much to handle.

Neil soon realizes that having unlimited power and wealth comes with its own set of problems. He starts to use his gifts to manipulate those around him, including his friends and family. His newfound abilities also attract the attention of various celebrities, who are all vying for a chance to receive one of Neil's gifts.

As Neil navigates his new life, he begins to question the morality of his actions and the true nature of his gifts. He starts to realize that having absolute power can be both liberating and suffocating. Meanwhile, God (Alan Rickman) is watching from above, occasionally intervening in Neil's life to guide him towards a more positive path.

Throughout the movie, Neil encounters various characters who are all trying to get their hands on one of his gifts. These include a group of eccentric billionaires, a pop star, and even a group of aliens who are interested in studying human behavior.

As the story unfolds, Neil begins to understand that true happiness comes from within and that having absolute power is not as fulfilling as he thought it would be. In the end, Neil decides to give up his gifts and return to his ordinary life, realizing that being human is what truly makes him special.

The movie ends with Neil reflecting on the lessons he has learned and the importance of humility and gratitude. The film features a talented ensemble cast, including Kate Ashfield, Joanna Lumley, and Bill Nighy, among others.

Overall, Absolutely Anything is a witty and entertaining comedy that explores themes of power, morality, and the human condition. With its unique blend of humor and heart, it's a must-see for fans of science fiction and comedy alike.

documents.title: Inside Llewyn Davis
documents.tagline: At a crossroads in the music world, where success remains elusive.
documents.overview: In Greenwich Village in the early 1960s, gifted but volatile folk musician Llewyn Davis struggles with money, relationships, and his uncertain future.
documents.plot:
Inside Llewyn Davis is a 2013 black comedy-drama written, directed, produced and edited by Joel and Ethan Coen. Oscar Isaac, in his breakthrough role, plays a struggling folk singer in Greenwich Village in 1961, with Carey Mulligan, Justin Timberlake, John Goodman, Garrett Hedlund, F. Murray Abraham and Adam Driver. Loosely inspired by Dave Van Ronk's memoir, it features folk songs performed live in full, with music produced by T Bone Burnett. It premiered at Cannes in May 2013, winning the Grand Prix.

In February 1961, Llewyn Davis's solo album is not selling, he has no money and sleeps on friends' couches. After a set at the Gaslight Café he is beaten in an alley by a stranger in a suit. Waking in the apartment of the Gorfeins, an academic couple, he accidentally lets their ginger cat out, and ends up carrying it around the city. Staying with the singers Jim and Jean Berkey, he learns that Jean is pregnant and may be carrying his child; she furiously demands that he pay for an abortion. His sister urges him to go back to the merchant marine.

To raise money he joins Jim and Al Cody in recording a silly novelty song about space travel, taking a $200 fee instead of royalties. At the clinic he discovers that a former girlfriend he had paid to have an abortion two years earlier had in fact kept the child. At dinner with the Gorfeins he lashes out when Mrs. Gorfein sings the harmony of his late partner Mike, who killed himself, and the cat he returned turns out to be the wrong one.

Llewyn rides to Chicago with the gruff jazz musician Roland Turner and the silent beat poet Johnny Five. When Johnny is arrested and Roland lies unconscious after an overdose, Llewyn abandons the car and the cat. In Chicago he plays for the impresario Bud Grossman, who is unmoved and suggests he join a trio, which he refuses. Hitchhiking home, he hits a cat on the road. Back in New York he cannot ship out because his sister threw away his seaman's licence, and he drunkenly heckles a performer at the Gaslight. The Gorfeins' real cat, Ulysses, has found its own way home. The story loops back to the opening night: as a young Bob Dylan takes the stage, Llewyn is beaten in the alley by the heckled singer's husband.

Widely acclaimed, the film holds 92% on Rotten Tomatoes and earned two Academy Award nominations.

documents.title: Noah
documents.tagline: The end of the world is just the beginning.
documents.overview: A man who suffers visions of an apocalyptic deluge takes measures to protect his family from the coming flood.
documents.plot:
Noah is a 2014 American epic drama directed by Darren Aronofsky, who co-wrote the screenplay with Ari Handel. Inspired by the biblical story of Noah's Ark in the Book of Genesis and drawing on the Book of Enoch, it stars Russell Crowe as Noah, with Jennifer Connelly, Ray Winstone, Emma Watson, Logan Lerman and Anthony Hopkins. Paramount Pictures released it in North America on 28 March 2014, in 2D and IMAX, with a 3D conversion in other countries.

As a boy, Noah witnesses the murder of his father, Lamech, by Tubal-cain, a descendant of Cain who covets their land. Years later, Noah lives quietly with his wife Naameh and their sons Shem, Ham and Japheth. After a vision of a great flood, he takes his family to seek the counsel of his grandfather, Methuselah. On the way they find a massacred village and adopt its sole survivor, a young girl named Ila, whose wound leaves her unable to bear children. Pursued by the killers, they flee into the land of the Watchers, fallen angels who were turned into giant stone creatures as punishment for helping Adam and Eve after their banishment from Eden.

Methuselah helps Noah interpret his visions and gives him a seed from the Garden of Eden. When Noah plants it, water springs up and a forest grows instantly, convincing the Watchers that he is doing the Creator's work, and they help him build an enormous ark. Years later, as birds, snakes and other animals stream toward the nearly completed vessel, Tubal-cain and his army arrive to claim it. Noah defies him, declaring that there is no escape for the descendants of Cain, and the Watchers defend the ark. As the rains begin and Tubal-cain launches a desperate assault, Noah comes to believe that the Creator intends humanity, including his own family, to perish after the animals have been saved. His grim conviction tears his family apart, particularly when Ila, now married to Shem, unexpectedly becomes pregnant, and Noah must choose between obedience to what he believes is divine will and mercy.

Noah received generally positive reviews, with praise for its ambition, visuals and performances, although it drew criticism and controversy from some religious groups over its departures from scripture and was banned in several countries. It grossed over $359 million worldwide, making it Aronofsky's highest-grossing film.

documents.title: Knight of Cups
documents.tagline: A quest.
documents.overview: Rick is a screenwriter living in Los Angeles. While successful in his career, his life feels empty. Haunted and confused, he finds temporary solace in the decadent Hollywood excess that defines his existence. Women provide a distraction to his daily pain, and every encounter brings him closer to finding his place in the world.

documents.title: Seven Psychopaths
documents.tagline: They Won't Take Any Shih Tzu.
documents.overview: A struggling screenwriter inadvertently becomes entangled in the Los Angeles criminal underworld after his oddball friends kidnap a gangster's beloved Shih Tzu.
documents.plot: A struggling screenwriter inadvertently becomes entangled in the Los Angeles criminal underworld after his oddball friends kidnap a gangster's beloved Shih Tzu.

documents.title: Black Panther
documents.overview: Black Panther is the ruler and protector of the African nation of Wakanda. Using technology, wits, and extraordinary fighting ability he must protect his nation from an invasion led by Ulysses Klaw, the man who killed his father.
documents.plot:
Black Panther is an American motion comic series from Marvel Knights Animation, released here as a single two-hour feature compiling its six 20-minute episodes. Based on the Marvel Comics hero, it closely adapts "Who Is the Black Panther?", the story arc written by Reginald Hudlin and drawn by John Romita Jr., both of whom supervised the production, with Hudlin then serving as BET's president of entertainment; the main change from the comic is that Juggernaut replaces the Rhino. Mark Brooks and Jon Schnepp directed. Djimon Hounsou voices T'Challa, with Kerry Washington as Princess Shuri, Alfre Woodard as the Queen Mother and others, Jill Scott as Storm, Carl Lumbly as Uncle S'Yan, Stephen Stanton as Ulysses Klaw and Stan Lee as General Wallace.

In a secret briefing in Washington, the intelligence agent Everett K. Ross recounts the history of Wakanda, a technologically advanced African nation ruled by a warrior king who bears the title Black Panther, including King T'Chaka's defeat of a young Captain America. In the present, a masked challenger wins Wakanda's annual tournament for the throne, defeating the reigning Black Panther, T'Chaka's brother, and is revealed as Prince T'Challa, to the chagrin of his sister Shuri, who had hoped to compete. Now king, T'Challa must manage jealousy within the royal court while hunting the man who murdered his father.

That man, the assassin Klaw, has been rebuilt with cybernetic enhancements and is assembling a team of villains, among them Juggernaut, Batroc the Leaper, Cannibal, the Black Knight and the Radioactive Man, to invade Wakanda for its vibranium. The Queen Mother recalls T'Challa's youthful travels in Egypt, where he befriended the young mutant Storm, and Klaw remembers how he killed T'Chaka. When the assault comes, Juggernaut and the Black Knight lead the attack, Shuri is trapped in a vibranium mine with the Radioactive Man, and Storm comes to help on her own. T'Challa defeats the Black Knight in aerial combat, Shuri uses his fallen Ebony Blade against the Radioactive Man, and after a final battle in which Klaw is killed, T'Challa orders a force of American Deathlok soldiers out of his country.

The series aired on Australia's ABC3 in January 2010 and on BET in November 2011, was released on DVD in January 2011, and was posted free on Marvel's YouTube channel in 2018. Reviewers praised its cast and political themes while noting the limits of the motion-comic format.

documents.title: Big Eyes
documents.tagline: She created it. He sold it. And everyone bought it.
documents.overview: In the late 1950s and early '60s, artist Walter Keane achieves unbelievable fame and success with portraits of saucer-eyed waifs. However, no one realizes that his wife, Margaret, is the real painter behind the brush. Although Margaret is horrified to learn that Walter is passing off her work as his own, she is too meek to protest too loudly. It isn't until the Keanes' marriage comes to an end and a lawsuit follows that the truth finally comes to light.

documents.title: Terminator Genisys
documents.tagline: Reset the future
documents.overview: The year is 2029. John Connor, leader of the resistance continues the war against the machines. At the Los Angeles offensive, John's fears of the unknown future begin to emerge when TECOM spies reveal a new plot by SkyNet that will attack him from both fronts; past and future, and will ultimately change warfare forever.
documents.plot:
In 2029, Human Resistance leader John Connor launches a final offensive against Skynet, an artificial general intelligence system seeking to eliminate the human race. Before the Resistance can triumph, Skynet activates time displacement equipment and sends a T-800/Model 101 Terminator back to 1984, to kill John's mother Sarah. John's right-hand man, Kyle Reese, volunteers to travel back in time to protect her. While floating in the equipment's magnetic field, Kyle sees John being attacked by another Resistance soldier. This creates a temporal paradox that alters the timeline and causes Kyle to experience childhood memories from a parallel version of himself.
However, when it arrives in 1984 Los Angeles, Skynet's T-800 is attacked by "Pops", a reprogrammed T-800. The two fight until Sarah arrives and shoots the Skynet controlled T-800, which crashes its system. An unknown party had sent Pops to 1973 to protect Sarah when she was nine years old after her parents were killed by a T-1000 sent by Skynet. After arriving in 1984, Kyle steals a homeless man's pants, but is soon intercepted by the T-1000. Eventually, the T-1000 corners him, but Sarah and Pops rescue him. The three run to the sewers, pursued by the T-1000, but Sarah and Pops melt it with an acid trap.
Sarah and Pops have constructed makeshift time displacement equipment like Skynet's and Sarah plans to stop Skynet by traveling to 1997, the year it becomes self-aware. However, realizing that the past has been altered, Kyle is convinced that the future has also changed. He recalls a warning he received in his childhood vision, convincing Sarah that they instead must travel to 2017 to stop Skynet. After fighting the T-1000, Pops has sustained exterior damage that prevents him from time traveling. He stays in 1984 and plans to meet up with Kyle and Sarah in the future, preparing for their arrival in the meantime.
In 2017, Kyle and Sarah materialize in the middle of a busy San Francisco highway and are apprehended by city police. While being treated for injuries, Sarah and Kyle learn that Skynet is called "Genisys"—a soon-to-be-unveiled global operating system which is embraced by the public. John then appears and rescues Sarah and Kyle. Pops arrives and shoots John, revealing that John is now an advanced Terminator. The resistance soldier who attacked John is revealed to have been Skynet in physical disguise as a T-5000 Terminator named Alex. While Kyle was traveling back in time, Alex attacked John and infected him with nanomachines that converted him into a cyborg on a cellular level. John, brainwashed to ensure Skynet's creation, traveled back in time to assist Cyberdyne Systems with the development of Genisys, hence securing Skynet and its machines' rise. Pops fights John before trapping him long enough for them to escape.
A day before Skynet's worldwide attack, Sarah, Kyle, and Pops retreat to a safe house and make final preparations to destroy Cyberdyne's Genisys mainframe.

documents.title: That's My Boy
documents.tagline: The story of a child… and his son.
documents.overview: While in his teens, Donny fathered a son, Todd, and raised him as a single parent up until Todd's 18th birthday. Now, after not seeing each other for years, Todd's world comes crashing down when Donny resurfaces just before Todd's wedding.
documents.plot:
That's My Boy is a 2012 American comedy film directed by Dennis Dugan and starring Adam Sandler, Andy Samberg, and Lea Michele. The movie follows the story of Donny Berger (Adam Sandler), a 39-year-old slacker who has never grown up.

The film begins with Donny's high school reunion, where he is still living in his parents' basement. His father, Sid (Dennis Dugan), is a successful businessman, and his mother, Mary (Joyce Van Patten), is a kind-hearted woman who always tries to help her son. However, Donny's laziness and lack of ambition have made him a disappointment to his family.

Donny's life takes an unexpected turn when he meets a young woman named Molly (Lea Michele), who is the daughter of Sid's business partner, Kurt (Kevin James). Molly is a beautiful and charming woman who has just graduated from college and is looking for a job. Donny, being the ladies' man that he thinks he is, tries to impress her with his fake stories about his accomplishments.

As Donny spends more time with Molly, he begins to develop real feelings for her. However, their relationship is put to the test when Donny's past comes back to haunt him. His high school sweetheart, Charlotte (Vanessa Bayer), returns and reveals that she has been in love with Donny all along. Donny must choose between his old life and a new one with Molly.

Meanwhile, Sid is dealing with his own problems. He is struggling to find a suitable partner for Kurt's daughter, and he becomes increasingly frustrated with Donny's lack of motivation. The two men engage in a series of comedic battles, with Donny trying to prove himself as a capable adult.

As the story unfolds, Donny must confront his past mistakes and learn to take responsibility for his life. With the help of Molly and his family, he begins to grow up and become a better person. In the end, Donny realizes that he has found true love with Molly and decides to leave his old life behind.

The movie ends on a positive note, with Donny and Molly starting a new life together. Sid finally finds a suitable partner for Kurt's daughter, and Donny's family is happy to see him grow up. The film concludes with a heartwarming moment of Donny and Molly sharing a kiss, symbolizing their love and commitment to each other.

Overall, That's My Boy is a lighthearted comedy that explores themes of growing up, love, and redemption. With its talented cast and witty dialogue, the movie provides an entertaining ride for audiences.

documents.title: The ABCs of Death
documents.tagline: 26 Directors, 26 Ways to Die.
documents.overview: An ambitious anthology film featuring segments directed by over two dozen of the world's leading talents in contemporary genre film. Inspired by children's educational ABC books, the film comprises 26 individual chapters, each helmed by a different director assigned a letter of the alphabet. The directors were then given free reign in choosing a word to create a story involving death.
documents.plot: The film begins showing a close up of a funnel with blood pouring ominously from it. The blood proceeds to fill up various rooms inside of a house before filling up the interior of a small room containing letter blocks. The room floods as the blocks float to the top spelling out the title. Throughout the film, the blocks spell out the titles to all the segments with each of the segments ending and beginning with a focus on, or a fade into, the color red.

documents.title: Foxcatcher
documents.tagline: Ambition. Power. Control.
documents.overview: The greatest Olympic Wrestling Champion brother team joins Team Foxcatcher led by multimillionaire sponsor John E. du Pont as they train for the 1988 games in Seoul - a union that leads to unlikely circumstances.
documents.plot: The greatest Olympic Wrestling Champion brother team joins Team Foxcatcher led by multimillionaire sponsor John E. du Pont as they train for the 1988 games in Seoul - a union that leads to unlikely circumstances.

documents.title: The East
documents.tagline: Spy on us, we'll spy on you.
documents.overview: An operative for an elite private intelligence firm finds her priorities irrevocably changed after she is tasked with infiltrating an anarchist group known for executing covert attacks upon major corporations.
documents.plot:
Jane, an operative for private intelligence firm Hiller Brood, is assigned by her boss, Sharon, to infiltrate The East, an underground activist, anarchist and environmentalist organization that has launched a vandalistic attack against a corporate leader and threatens two more as retribution for ecological crimes. Calling herself Sarah, she joins drifters in hitching train rides. When one drifter, Luca, helps her escape from the police, she identifies the symbol of The East hanging from Luca's car mirror. Sarah self-inflicts an arm injury that she tells Luca was caused in the escape so he can get her medical attention. He takes her to a seemingly abandoned house in the woods where members of The East live and one of them, Doc, treats her.
Sarah is given two nights to recover before she must leave. At an elaborate dinner involving straitjackets, Sarah is tested and fails, exposing how selfishly she and many others live their lives. Sarah is caught spying one night by Eve (a group member who is deaf) and signs to her she is an undercover agent, threatening Eve with jail if she stays; Eve leaves the next morning. Sarah is recruited to fill the missing member's role on a "jam", a term for protest by subversive means. Sarah reluctantly participates in The East's next jam and learns that the group's members have all been damaged by corporate activities. For example, Doc was poisoned by a fluoroquinolone antibiotic and his neurosystem is degenerating. The East infiltrates a party for the antibiotic company's senior executives and adds the antibiotic to the champagne. The East announce this via YouTube: one executive's health begins to fail, revealing the drug's side effects. After seeing the jam's effectiveness, compounded by her attraction to charismatic Benji, Sarah questions the morality of her job.
Another member, Izzy, is the daughter of a petrochemical CEO. The group uses this connection to gain access to him and forces him to bathe in the waterway he has been using as a toxic dumping ground. This goes wrong when security arrives and shoots the fleeing Izzy. At the squat, Doc's hands tremble too much for him to perform surgery. Working under his guidance, Sarah manages to remove the bullet but Izzy dies. This is the catalyst for Sarah and Benji's romance and they have sex.
Sarah implores Benji to leave, but he insists they participate in a fourth and final jam. Sarah initially refuses but gives in. When she awakens after sleeping in the car, she realizes that Benji is driving her to Hiller Brood's headquarters. He reveals that he has always suspected her of being a spy, as did Luca, who brought her in as a test. Benji wants Sarah to obtain a non-official cover (NOC: unofficial espionage agents) global list of Hiller Brood agents, to "watch" them. Having copied the list onto her cell phone's memory card, Sarah runs into Sharon and confronts her about the firm's activities, revealing her new allegiances.

documents.title: Flight
documents.tagline: Some miracles are not what they seem.
documents.overview: Commercial airline pilot Whip Whitaker has a problem with drugs and alcohol, though so far he's managed to complete his flights safely. His luck runs out when a disastrous mechanical malfunction sends his plane hurtling toward the ground. Whip pulls off a miraculous crash-landing that results in only six lives lost. Shaken to the core, Whip vows to get sober -- but when the crash investigation exposes his addiction, he finds himself in an even worse situation.
documents.plot:
Flight is a 2012 American drama film directed by Robert Zemeckis, starring Denzel Washington as Whip Whitaker, a commercial airline pilot.

The movie begins with Whip Whitaker (Denzel Washington) flying for Southern Air, a regional airline. Whip is a skilled and experienced pilot, but he has a troubled past. He was involved in a plane crash that killed everyone on board, except himself, when he was just 19 years old. The incident left him with severe anxiety and PTSD.

The story then jumps to the present day, where Whip is now flying for Southern Air again. He's still struggling with his demons, but has managed to keep them under control. However, during a flight from Atlanta to Charlotte, Whip becomes disoriented due to a combination of factors, including his medication, fatigue, and stress.

As the plane hits turbulence, Whip becomes increasingly agitated, and eventually loses consciousness. The plane crashes in a field, killing everyone on board except for one passenger, a young girl named Hyde (Nico Parker). The incident is ruled as an accident, but Whip's colleagues are suspicious of his involvement.

Whip is forced to take a leave of absence from flying due to the incident, and he becomes a recluse. He starts attending AA meetings and begins to rebuild his life. However, he struggles with feelings of guilt and shame over the crash, which affects his relationships with those around him, including his girlfriend, Nicole (Donna Freeman).

As Whip tries to come to terms with what happened, he meets a young girl named Hyde who was on board the plane. Despite the trauma she experienced, Hyde is determined to help others and make a difference in the world. Whip becomes a mentor to her, and through their interactions, he begins to confront his past and find redemption.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Whip's colleagues start investigating him for possible involvement in the crash. Whip's reputation is tarnished, and he faces pressure from the airline and the authorities. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Whip had been taking sedatives before the flight, which contributed to his loss of control.

In the end, Whip comes clean about what happened and takes responsibility for his actions. He also finds a way to make amends with those around him, including Hyde and Nicole. The movie ends on a hopeful note, as Whip begins to rebuild his life and find redemption through his relationship with Hyde.

Throughout the movie, Denzel Washington delivers a powerful performance as Whip Whitaker, bringing depth and nuance to the character. His portrayal of a complex and flawed individual is both heartbreaking and inspiring, making Flight a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film.

documents.title: Oldboy
documents.tagline: Ask not why you were imprisoned. Ask why you were set free.
documents.overview: An everyday man has only three and a half days and limited resources to discover why he was imprisoned in a nondescript room for 20 years without any explanation.
documents.plot:
Oldboy is a 2013 American neo-noir action thriller directed by Spike Lee and written by Mark Protosevich, a remake of the 2003 South Korean film by Park Chan-wook, which was itself loosely based on a Japanese manga. It stars Josh Brolin as Joe Doucett, Elizabeth Olsen as Marie Sebastian and Sharlto Copley as the mysterious Adrian Pryce, with Samuel L. Jackson in a supporting role.

In 1993, Joe Doucett is a hard-drinking, abrasive advertising executive whose life is falling apart. After a night of heavy drinking following the loss of a major client, he blacks out and wakes up locked in a windowless room resembling a cheap hotel. His unseen captors feed him and supply him with alcohol, but never explain why he is being held. Through the television he learns that his ex-wife has been raped and murdered, that he is the prime suspect and that their young daughter Mia has been adopted.

Over the next twenty years, Joe stops drinking, trains his body and plans for revenge, compiling a list of everyone who might have wanted to imprison him and writing letters to the daughter he hopes to meet one day. Then, without warning, he is drugged and released, waking up outside with money and a cell phone. With the help of his old friend Chucky, a bar owner, and Marie, a young nurse moved by his story, Joe sets out to find the people responsible. A taunting voice on the phone, calling himself the Stranger, challenges him to discover who imprisoned him and why, promising proof of his innocence in his ex-wife's murder if he succeeds. Joe's brutal search leads him back through his own past and toward a revelation more devastating than his imprisonment.

Lee's version retains the original's famous corridor fight with a hammer while altering many story details, while the version released was a producers' re-edit that left Lee and Brolin unhappy.

Oldboy was released in the United States by FilmDistrict on November 27, 2013, and was a commercial failure, earning about 885,000 dollars in its first five days, one of the weakest Thanksgiving openings on record. Reviews were negative, with 39 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 49, and many critics felt it did not measure up to the original.

documents.title: The Big Wedding
documents.tagline: It's never too late to start acting like a family.
documents.overview: To the amusement of their adult children and friends, long divorced couple Don and Ellie Griffin are once again forced to play the happy couple for the sake of their adopted son's wedding after his ultra conservative biological mother unexpectedly decides to fly halfway across the world to attend. With all of the wedding guests looking on, the Griffins are hilariously forced to confront their past, present and future - and hopefully avoid killing each other in the process.
documents.plot:
Don and Ellie Griffin were a New England couple married for 20 years before they divorced. They have three children from their marriage: Lyla, Jared and adopted son Alejandro, who originates from Colombia.
In preparation for Alejandro's wedding, Ellie arrives at Don's (and her old) home and lets herself in. She interrupts Don just as he is about to perform oral sex on Bebe, his girlfriend of eight years (and Ellie's former best friend). All are embarrassed, but they make small talk and he shows Ellie to her room.
Meanwhile, Alejandro and his fiancée Missy are meeting with Father Moinighan, the priest who will be marrying them. It is revealed that his biological mother Madonna is going to be coming from Colombia to the wedding, which upsets him because he does not have a "traditional" family, and it is believed that his Catholic mother will not approve of that nor the fact that Don and Ellie are divorced.
Lyla, who reveals that she is separated, goes to the hospital and, after passing out briefly, sees Jared, an obstetrician. They talk and it is revealed that he is a virgin and is waiting for the "right one".
Back home, Alejandro tells Ellie that his mother is coming to the wedding. Explaining that, as she is a devout Catholic and does not believe in divorce, Alejandro asks Ellie and Don to pretend to be married for the next three days. Hearing this, Bebe becomes upset with Don and leaves the house. Madonna arrives with Alejandro's biological 20-year-old sister Nuria. Nuria flirts with Jared after she brazenly strips naked to skinnydip in the family's lake.
That evening, the family goes out to dinner with Missy and her bigoted parents Muffin and Barry, and Bebe shows up as their waitress, which surprises everyone. Meanwhile, Nuria starts fondling Jared under the table, and Ellie sees Nuria giving Jared a handjob. She takes Nuria to the restroom for a chat, telling her that American women are not as forward and desire romance before having sex.
When they arrive home, Jared tells Nuria that he wants to have sex, as she had suggested earlier, but she tells him no, asking him instead to do romantic things for her, such as read her poetry. Don and Ellie, meanwhile, end up having sex when Ellie, still pretending to be Don's wife, sleeps in his room.
Ellie and Madonna go for a walk in the woods and talk. Neither understands the other's language, although they think they are communicating on some level. At the same time, Don and Lyla talk privately, and she reveals that she is pregnant.
On the wedding day, before the ceremony, Don tells Bebe that he had sex with Ellie. Although Bebe says that she forgives them, she still punches him in the face. She also reveals that Ellie cheated on Don with Missy's father before Don cheated on her. Muffin says that she knows about Ellie and Barry, and tells them that she is bisexual, implying that she is interested in a sexual affair with both Bebe and Ellie.

documents.title: Movie 43
documents.tagline: The biggest cast ever assembled for the most outrageous comedy ever made.
documents.overview: Fifteen directors and an all-star cast created this twisted comedy that follows three teens on the hunt for the world's most banned film.
documents.plot:
Movie 43 is a 2013 American anthology comedy film directed by Peter Segal, written by Jake Kasdan, Jason Segel, and Nicholas Stoller, and starring an ensemble cast including Emma Stone, Hugh Jackman, Kate Winslet, and Stephen Merchant.

The film consists of six separate stories, each with its own unique tone and style. The first story, "The Catch," stars Halle Berry as a woman who is trying to get revenge on her cheating ex-boyfriend (played by Chris Parnell). However, things take a dark turn when she discovers that he has been replaced by a lookalike.

The second story, "The Getaway," stars Kate Winslet and Hugh Jackman as a couple who are on the run from the law after a botched heist. As they try to escape, they realize that their relationship is not as strong as they thought it was.

The third story, "The Catch: Part Two," serves as a sequel to the first story and follows the same characters as they try to take revenge on the lookalike who replaced Berry's character.

The fourth story, "Milk," stars Seth MacFarlane as a man who is trying to get his girlfriend (played by Emma Stone) to lose weight. However, things take a dark turn when he discovers that she has been hiding a shocking secret.

The fifth story, "Pedestal," stars Stephen Merchant and Johnny Knoxville as two men who are trying to make it big in the world of adult entertainment. However, their plans are foiled when they discover that their rival is not what he seems.

The sixth and final story, "The Catch: Part Three," serves as a conclusion to the first story and follows Berry's character as she tries to take revenge on her ex-boyfriend once again.

Throughout the film, the tone shifts from dark comedy to slapstick humor, making it a challenging watch for some viewers. However, fans of the genre will likely find it entertaining and hilarious.

Overall, Movie 43 is a unique and unpredictable film that explores themes of love, relationships, and revenge. While it may not be to everyone's taste, it is certainly an interesting and thought-provoking watch.

documents.title: Trouble with the Curve
documents.tagline: Whatever Life Throws at You.
documents.overview: Slowed by age and failing eyesight, crack baseball scout Gus Lobel takes his grown daughter along as he checks out the final prospect of his career. Along the way, the two renew their bond, and she catches the eye of a young player-turned-scout.

documents.title: Life of Pi
documents.tagline: Believe The Unbelievable
documents.overview: The story of an Indian boy named Pi, a zookeeper's son who finds himself in the company of a hyena, zebra, orangutan, and a Bengal tiger after a shipwreck sets them adrift in the Pacific Ocean.
documents.plot:
In the early 2010s Montreal, a writer meets Pi Patel, whom he has been told would be a good subject for a book. Pi tells the writer the following story:
Pi is born in 1960, named Piscine Molitor Patel after Piscine Molitor, a famous French swimming pool. In secondary school in Pondicherry, he adopts the Greek letter "Pi" as his nickname to avoid bullying, because his first name Piscine sounds like 'pissing'. He is raised in a Hindu family, but in 1973, he is introduced to Christianity and then Islam and decides to follow all three religions as he "just wants to love God".
Pi's mother supports his desire to grow, but his rationalist father tries to secularize him. Their family owns a zoo, and Pi takes interest in a Bengal tiger named Richard Parker. After he gets dangerously close to Richard Parker, his father forces him to witness it killing a goat.
In 1977, Pi's father announces that due to "The Emergency" they must move to Canada, where he intends to settle and sell the animals. The family books passage with the animals on a Japanese freighter. During a storm, the ship founders while Pi is on deck. He struggles to find his family but a crewman throws him into a lifeboat. A freed plains zebra jumps onto the boat with him, breaking its leg. The ship sinks into the Mariana Trench, drowning his family.
After the storm, Pi awakens in the lifeboat with the zebra and is joined by a Bornean orangutan. A spotted hyena emerges from under a tarpaulin, forcing Pi to retreat to the end of the boat. The hyena kills the zebra and later the orangutan. After some time, Richard Parker emerges from under the tarpaulin and kills the hyena before retreating to cover.
Pi fashions a small raft, which he tethers to the lifeboat to be safe from Richard Parker. His moral code is against killing, but he begins fishing, enabling him to sustain the tiger. When the tiger jumps into the sea to hunt for fish and swims toward Pi, he considers letting him drown but ultimately helps him into the boat. One night, a humpback whale destroys the raft and its supplies. Pi trains Richard Parker to accept him in the boat and realizes that caring for the tiger is helping to keep himself alive.
Weeks later, they encounter a floating island. It is a lush jungle of edible plants, freshwater pools and a large population of meerkats, enabling Pi and Richard Parker to eat, drink and regain strength. At night the island transforms into a hostile environment. Richard Parker retreats to the lifeboat while Pi and the meerkats sleep in the trees; the water pools turn acidic. Pi deduces that the island is carnivorous after finding a human tooth embedded in a flower.
Pi and Richard Parker leave the island, reaching Mexico after more than 200 days at sea. Pi is heartbroken that Richard Parker does not acknowledge him before disappearing into the jungle.

documents.title: Journey to the Center of the Earth
documents.original_title: Journey to the Center of the Earth
documents.tagline: Same Planet. Different World.
documents.overview: On a quest to find out what happened to his missing brother, a scientist, his nephew and their mountain guide discover a fantastic and dangerous lost world in the center of the earth.
documents.plot:
Journey to the Center of the Earth is a 2008 American 3D science fantasy action-adventure film directed by Eric Brevig. An adaptation of Jules Verne's 1864 novel in which the book itself exists within the story, it stars Brendan Fraser as volcanologist Trevor Anderson, Josh Hutcherson as his nephew Sean, and Aníta Briem as Icelandic guide Hannah Ásgeirsdóttir.

In 2007, Boston volcanologist Trevor learns that the lab of his brother, Max, who vanished ten years earlier, is closing for lack of funding, and he has forgotten that his 13-year-old nephew, Sean, Max's son, is coming to stay for ten days. Sean's mother leaves a box of Max's belongings, including a copy of Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth filled with Max's notes. Studying them, Trevor decides to investigate in Iceland, and Sean, now curious about the father he barely knew, insists on coming. Seeking another scientist who shared Max's theories, they meet his daughter, Hannah, who says he has died and that both men believed Verne's novels were true accounts. She agrees to guide them up a mountain to an instrument that has suddenly begun transmitting again.

A lightning storm drives them into a cave whose entrance collapses, trapping them in an old mine, where they find a tunnel studded with gems, including diamonds that Sean pockets, before the floor gives way and they plunge to the center of the Earth. There they find Max's old shelter, his journal and his body, which they bury. Trevor realizes from Max's notes that the temperature is rising and that they have about 48 hours to reach a geyser that can carry them back to the surface. Crossing an underground sea on a raft, they are attacked by piranhas, and Sean is separated from the others; guided by a small glowing bird, he is rescued by Trevor from an albino Giganotosaurus. Finding the geyser dry, Trevor ignites magnesium in the rock with a flare, and the blast of water and steam shoots them out of Mount Vesuvius in Italy. Sean's diamonds pay for damage to a vineyard, fund Max's lab and buy Trevor and Hannah, who have fallen for each other, a new home. As Sean's visit ends, Trevor hands him a book about Atlantis.

Warner Bros. Pictures released the film on July 11, 2008, and it introduced the 4DX motion-seat format in Seoul. It grossed $245 million worldwide against a $60 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with 60% on Rotten Tomatoes, and 57 on Metacritic, while audiences gave it an A− CinemaScore.

documents.title: J. Edgar
documents.tagline: The most powerful man in the world.
documents.overview: As the face of law enforcement in the United States for almost 50 years, J. Edgar Hoover was feared and admired, reviled and revered. But behind closed doors, he held secrets that would have destroyed his image, his career, and his life.
documents.plot:
The film uses a nonlinear narrative, alternating between J. Edgar Hoover's role in establishing the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and his later years trying to safeguard it against perceived threats. As a frame story, the aging Hoover narrates the events of the Bureau's early years to a series of agents he has assigned to ghostwrite a book about it.
In 1919, Attorney General A. Mitchell Palmer survives an assassination attempt by anarchists and assigns Justice Department employee Hoover to a division dedicated to purging radicals. Helen Gandy rejects Hoover's awkward advances, but becomes his personal secretary and confidant. By arranging to make the anarchist Emma Goldman eligible for deportation, Hoover creates legal precedent to deport numerous other radicals. Following the Palmer Raids, Palmer loses his job and his successor, Harlan F. Stone, appoints Hoover as director of the department's Bureau of Investigation. Hoover has Gandy create a confidential file in which he collects incriminating information on people in power.
With the First Red Scare over, Hoover focuses the Bureau on fighting gangsters. When the Lindbergh kidnapping captures national attention in 1932, he urges passage of the Federal Kidnapping Act, increasing the Bureau's power. He establishes the FBI Laboratory, applying forensic science techniques to the investigation, and has the registration numbers on the ransom bills monitored. Though Charles Lindbergh Jr. is found dead, these techniques lead to the arrest and conviction of Bruno Richard Hauptmann for the crime.
Well into adulthood, Hoover continues to live with his mother, who is his moral guide. He hires Clyde Tolson to the Bureau in 1930; the two develop a rapport and Hoover promotes Tolson to associate director. When Hoover confesses to his mother that he is uncomfortable in romantic situations with women, she says she would rather have him dead than gay. When Tolson tells Hoover that he loves him, Hoover panics and claims that he wants to marry actress Dorothy Lamour. Tolson becomes infuriated and the two fight, culminating in Tolson kissing Hoover and threatening to end their association if Hoover ever talks about another woman again. Hoover's mother dies, and he is grief-stricken.
Following an embarrassing line of questioning by Senate Appropriations Committee chair Kenneth McKellar in 1933, Hoover becomes increasingly vengeful against those who challenge his reputation and the Bureau's. He uses covert listening devices to collect compromising information which he uses to blackmail political figures over the years, including President Franklin D. Roosevelt and Attorney General Robert F. Kennedy, protecting his position and increasing the Bureau's power. He starts COINTELPRO, an illegal counterintelligence program, to fight what he perceives as a new wave of radicals, culminating in his failed attempt to blackmail Martin Luther King Jr. into declining the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964 via the FBI–King letter.

documents.title: Radio Rebel
documents.tagline: Can the girl who never speaks... Become the voice of a generation?
documents.overview: High school senior Tara is so painfully shy that she dreads speaking to anyone in the hallways or getting called on in class. But in the privacy of her bedroom with her iPod in hand, she rocks out -- doing mock broadcasts for Miami's hottest FM radio station, which happens to be owned by her stepfather. When a slot opens up at The SLAM, Tara surprises herself by blossoming behind the mike into confident, "Radio Rebel" -- and to everyone's shock, she's a hit!

documents.tagline: Everything comes full circle
documents.overview: Inspired by Arthur Schnitzler's classic La Ronde, screenwriter Peter Morgan and director Fernando Meirelles' 360 combines a modern and dynamic roundelay of stories into one, linking characters from different cities and countries in a vivid, suspenseful and deeply moving tale of love in the 21st century. Starting in Vienna, the film beautifully weaves through Paris, London, Bratislava, Rio, Denver and Phoenix into a single, mesmerizing narrative.
documents.plot:
360 is a 2011 ensemble drama directed by Fernando Meirelles and written by Peter Morgan, a loose adaptation of Arthur Schnitzler's 1897 play Reigen. Its international cast includes Anthony Hopkins, Jude Law, Rachel Weisz, Ben Foster, Moritz Bleibtreu and Dinara Drukarova, in interlocking stories of couples, desire and chance that circle from Vienna through Paris, London and Denver to Berlin.

In Vienna, Slovak sisters Mirka and Anna meet Rocco, who runs an escort agency, and Mirka begins working under the name Blanca. Her first client, businessman Michael Daly, walks out after an associate loudly questions whether she is a prostitute, and the associate later blackmails Michael into a deal. In Paris, an Algerian man secretly pines for a married woman and seeks advice from his imam and a therapist. In London, Michael's wife, Rose, ends her affair with Rui, only for Rui to find that his girlfriend, Laura, has photographed them together and left him.

Flying home to Brazil, Laura is stranded by bad weather in Denver alongside John, a father searching for his long-missing daughter, and Tyler, a sex offender just released after six years in prison who fears his own impulses. She invites Tyler to her hotel room, but he rejects her drunken advances and locks himself in the bathroom. John, moved by Laura's farewell hug, travels to Phoenix to examine remains that prove not to be his daughter, and at an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting he resolves to accept her unknown fate. There Valentina reveals that she is the woman the Algerian man watched; she wants to leave her husband, Sergei, driver for a crooked Russian businessman, because she loves her boss. Back in Paris, the dentist she works for, the Algerian man, asks her to find another job, and both are heartbroken.

In Vienna, Sergei's boss hires Mirka, while Sergei and Anna bond over books and learning English as he drives her around the city. Mirka's plan to rob the businessman with Rocco unravels when he reads her phone, but Rocco attacks him, and Mirka escapes with the cash as Anna writes her sister a goodbye letter. In Berlin, Michael and Rose reunite, and Michael's associate glimpses a new young woman arriving for a photo shoot with Rocco.

The film opened the 2011 London Film Festival, and Magnolia Pictures released it on demand in June 2012 and in U.S. theaters that August. Reviews were negative, with 19% on Rotten Tomatoes and 43 on Metacritic.

documents.title: Conquest 1453
documents.tagline: The fall of an empire will be the rise of another.
documents.overview: After the death of his father Murat II, Mehmet II ascends to the Ottoman throne. After braving internal and external enemies, he decides to complete what he was destined to do: Conquer Constantinople.
documents.plot:
The film opens in Medina during the time of the Islamic prophet Muhammad, 627 AD. Abu Ayyub tells other sahabas that Constantinople will be conquered by a blessed commander and army.
The story shifts abruptly to the 15th century. Sultan Muhammad al-Fatih was given the throne by his father Murad II when he was 12; he learns of his father's death while governing the Sanjak of Saruhan. This causes him much grief and paves the way for his ascension to the throne again, after the death of his brother Fathıl IV. When Sultan Mehmet had first ascended the throne, he was also 12 years old. Murad II, suffocated by the political hostility of his margraves and viziers, relinquished the throne due to the impact of his deep grief caused by his beloved son Mohamed's death and enthroned Mehmet. Grand Vizier Halil Pasha, who had a great influence on the Janissaries and the state, was dissatisfied because of this situation. He was especially troubled with Sultan Mehmet indicating that Constantinople's conquest is vitally essential. He made Sultan Murat inherit the throne again in anticipation of the possibility of crusaders occupying Ottoman territories by taking advantage of Mehmet. Mehmet was suspended from the throne and sent to the Sanjak of Saruhan.
Now, Mehmet succeeds to the throne again and is even more powerful. His priority target is still the conquest of Constantinople. He gains inspiration from the words of Muhammad: “Constantinople will surely be conquered. What a blessed commander is its and what a blessed army is its army.”
He works out everything that will take him to the target. At the outset, Mehmet decides that he should live in peace with contiguous countries until he makes the preparations for his campaign. He sends messengers to the Papal States, to the Kingdom of Hungary, to the Serbian Despotate, to the Kingdom of Poland, to the Republic of Genoa and to the Republic of Venice and notifies them of his intention to live in peace. He restores the dockyard of Gallipoli and because of this action, 100 galleys can be produced there in a year. Meanwhile, the Byzantine Emperor Constantine XI Palaiologos thinks that Sultan Mehmet is inexperienced and lacking in foresight. Constantine demands heavy appropriations, trying to use to his advantage his possession of the captive Prince Orhan. Constantine's main intention is to make Sultan Mehmet lose his reputation by capitulating to his demands. Sultan Mehmet appears to accept his demands, but this is just a strategy of deceit.
As soon as the news of Karaman's rebellion is received, Ottoman armies set out for Akşehir. Karamanoğlu İbrahim was not expecting such a mighty army. He demands peace. Sultan Mehmet accepts the peace, because he does not want his armies to be harmed unnecessarily. After the military expedition, on the return journey, a group of janissaries confront the state tent and ask for payment. They had not actually engaged in battle. In response, Sultan Mehmet sends out enthronements.

documents.title: Leafie, a Hen Into the Wild
documents.tagline: A story of love, sacrifice and courage
documents.overview: Based on a bestselling preteen novel of the same title that has sold more than 1 million copies in Korea, “Leafie, A Hen into the Wild” is about a laying hen named Leafie who is destined to live the “same old” repetitive life confined on the chicken farm.  Her fate changes when she escapes from the chicken farm and hatches a duck egg. With the duckling (who believes Leafie to be his mother), sets off on a journey into the wild with her new son to find her freedom.
documents.plot:
Leafie lives on a chicken farm with other egg-laying hens in battery cages. She dreams of being a mother, despite her inability to incubate her own eggs. Dreaming of having children, she escapes the farm, feigning death and tricking the farmer into dumping her outside but is threatened by a one-eyed weasel. She is saved by mallard duck Wanderer who traps One-Eye in the farmer's wheelbarrow. Leafie tries to join a troupe of animals residing outside the farm, but their rooster refuses to allow her into his flock, insisting that she would only spend her life laying eggs. Leafie leaves the farm and into the wilderness, meeting Mr. Otter, who helps her find a home on Wanderer's behalf. Leafie meets Wanderer again, and discovers he has a mate, whom One-Eye kills later that night.
At Wanderer's nest, Leafie finds a single egg. Wanderer decides to let Leafie take care of the egg as he leaves to confront One-Eye. He pleads Leafie to take his unborn child to the Everglades, believing she will understand its purpose there. That night, One-Eye returns, and Wanderer engages her in a fight to the death in which One-Eye prevails. The egg then hatches into a duckling that imprints on Leafie. She adopts the duckling, naming him Greenie, before setting off for the Everglades. As Leafie raises Greenie, Mr. Otter teaches him to swim, with help from a bat and owl to teach him to fly. Meanwhile, Mr. Otter accidentally confesses that the local waterfowl are unaccepting of Leafie in their community. She then meets up with Greenie, who had been bullied by a group of mandarin ducks and blames Leafie for him being an outcast before running away.
Subsequently, Mr. Otter comforts Leafie by telling her about Wanderer's backstory: he was a flock guard that broke his wing fighting One-Eye and also permanently blinded one of her eyes, before being captured by the farmer and escaping. Meanwhile, Greenie is lured to the farm by four white ducks before being caught by the farmer, who intends on clipping his wings. To rescue Greenie, Leafie and Mr. Otter release all the hens from their cages as a distraction, then Mr. Otter scares off the farmer and frees Greenie. However, the rooster stops them, calling Leafie a disgrace to the chickens. Leafie knocks away his comb, making the animals discover it is fake; one of the white ducks decides to replace him as the troupe leader, helping Leafie, Greenie and Mr. Otter escape. After Mr. Otter departs, One-Eye pins Greenie onto a tree; the two plummet over a cliff as the tree snaps away. Leafie laments Greenie's apparent sacrifice, but Greenie escapes by successfully flying as One-Eye climbs back up.
A flock of mallards soon arrive in autumn, from whom Greenie learns of an upcoming contest to nominate the new flock guard upon realizing Wanderer's words. The ducks flee from Greenie, seeing the string around his leg from his previous encounter with the farmer, but Leafie reassures Greenie's entry, removing the string in time.

documents.title: Dragon Ball Z: Plan to Eradicate the Super Saiyans
documents.original_title: ドラゴンボール 超サイヤ人絶滅計画
documents.overview: Dr. Raichi is one of the only survivors of the Tuffles, a race that once lived on Planet Plant before the coming of the Saiyans. The Saiyans not only massacred the entire Tuffle race, but also stole their technology and conquered the planet, renaming it Planet Vegeta in honor of their king. Raichi managed to escape with a capsule and found refuge on the Dark Planet, a world at the end of the universe. His only wish is to eradicate the last remaining Saiyans.
documents.plot:
Dragon Ball Z: Plan to Eradicate the Super Saiyans (Japanese: Doragon Bōru: Sūpā Saiya-jin Zetsumetsu Keikaku) is a 2010 Japanese original video animation, a complete remake of a two-part 1993 OVA that had been produced as a companion to the Famicom card-battle role-playing game Dragon Ball Z Side Story: Plan to Eradicate the Saiyans, developed by Tose and published by Bandai. The voice cast is led by Masako Nozawa as Goku, Gohan and Turles, with Ryō Horikawa as Vegeta, Toshio Furukawa as Piccolo, Takeshi Kusao as Trunks, Ryūsei Nakao as Frieza and Cooler, Yusaku Yara as Lord Slug and Shinji Ogawa as the villain Dr. Raichi.

The story centres on Dr. Raichi, the last survivor of the Tuffles, a technologically advanced race that once lived on Planet Plant before it was invaded by the Saiyans. The Saiyans massacred the Tuffles, seized their technology and renamed the planet Planet Vegeta in honour of their king. Raichi escaped and took refuge on a distant dark world, where he has spent years preparing his revenge on the last remaining Saiyans.

On Earth, Raichi's devices begin releasing a substance called Destron Gas, which threatens to wipe out all life on the planet. When Mr. Popo discovers that only a few hours remain before the planet is destroyed, Goku, Gohan, Vegeta, Trunks and Piccolo race around the world to destroy the gas machines. They succeed in destroying all but one, which is protected by an impenetrable energy barrier. At that moment, some of their most dangerous past enemies, Frieza, Cooler, Turles and Lord Slug, reappear and attack them. King Kai explains that these villains are ghost warriors who will keep returning to life unless they are defeated in the same way they originally died. Tracking the source to Raichi's hideout, the heroes discover that the ghosts are generated by Hatchiyack, a machine powered by the hatred of the Tuffles, and they must face both Raichi and the monstrous power of the machine itself to save the Earth.

The story functions as a crossover that reunites the heroes with villains from several Dragon Ball Z films and story arcs, offering fans a series of rematches in a compact format.

The 1993 game on which the story is based sold around 300,000 copies in Japan and received a score of 22 out of 40 from Famitsu. Its original OVA had been released in two parts as video strategy guides, and its footage was later reused in a 1994 Playdia video game before the story was fully reanimated in 2010.

documents.title: Samsara
documents.overview: Filmed over nearly five years in twenty-five countries on five continents, and shot on seventy-millimetre film, Samsara transports us to the varied worlds of sacred grounds, disaster zones, industrial complexes, and natural wonders.
documents.plot: The official website describes, "Expanding on the themes they developed in Baraka (1992) and Chronos (1985), Samsara explores the wonders of our world from the mundane to the miraculous, looking into the unfathomable reaches of humanity's spirituality and the human experience. Neither a traditional documentary nor a travelogue, Samsara takes the form of a nonverbal, guided meditation."

documents.title: Now Is Good
documents.tagline: Live every moment, love every minute
documents.overview: A girl dying of leukemia compiles a list of things she'd like to do before passing away. Topping the list is her desire to lose her virginity.
documents.plot:
Tessa is 17 years old with terminal acute lymphoblastic leukaemia. Aided by her best friend, Zoey, she fulfils an undisclosed bucket list before her impending death. One night, both attempt to engage in sex with two boys they pick up in a club.
Tessa goes on a radio talk show with her overbearing father in which she pokes fun at her terminal diagnosis and approaches it with humour. Tessa is loving and caring towards her brother Cal towards whom she feels guilty for stealing her parents' attention and gives him days that are all about him while dealing with her father trying to treasure every moment with his daughter. Her mother is supportive but rarely there for her. Tessa gets the last of her chemotherapy equipment removed from her body so that she can live the rest of her days normally. She meets her new neighbour Adam, who is taking care of his handicapped widowed mother and putting his own life on hold such as going to university, and Tessa instantly befriends him. Adam joins Tessa and Zoey on their adventures, and he takes care of both of them while they take hallucinogenic mushrooms before going into the forest and finding great cliffs, followed by going to a party at which Tessa and Adam start developing feelings for each other. Tessa and Zoey continue to fulfil Tessa's bucket list by stealing from a store, but after being caught, Tessa discovers that Zoey stole a pregnancy test, which suggests that she may be pregnant.
Tessa and Adam go to the beach together and begin a romantic relationship. Tessa introduces Adam to her father, who disapproves of the relationship because Tessa's health is currently in steep decline after she stopped chemotherapy. He tells Adam that Tessa's condition will get worse and that Adam will not be up to it. Tessa takes Zoey to a clinic. Zoey's pregnancy is confirmed, with Zoey not sure if she will keep the baby.
Tessa and Adam attempt to go on a regular date, but Tessa breaks out in a huge nose bleed that leads to her hospitalisation. Adam freezes, which leaves Tessa's mother to take her to hospital. While she is hospitalised, Adam begins painting her name all over the city so that when Tessa leaves the hospital, she can see her name is all over the city. That will fulfil one of her bucket list items that everyone will know she existed and leave Tessa satisfied and smiling. Zoey reveals to Tessa she is keeping the baby, which will be due in April. Tessa and Adam begin spending every night together so that Tessa will not be alone at night anymore; however, Tessa's father refuses the request because of their age and what Tessa is going through although he relents after Tessa reveals she is willing to take the risk despite the burden coming from her impending death.
Tessa visits her doctor, who tells her that her cancer is causing her immune system to collapse and her life will soon end. She will not make it to April to see Zoey's baby being born.
