documents.plot: After suffering a stroke, an altruistic maid announces that she wants to quit her job and move into an old people's home.

documents.title: Transformers: Age of Extinction
documents.tagline: This is not war, it's extinction.
documents.overview: As humanity picks up the pieces, following the conclusion of "Transformers: Dark of the Moon," Autobots and Decepticons have all but vanished from the face of the planet. However, a group of powerful, ingenious businessman and scientists attempt to learn from past Transformer incursions and push the boundaries of technology beyond what they can control - all while an ancient, powerful Transformer menace sets Earth in his cross-hairs.
documents.plot:
Transformers: Age of Extinction is a 2014 science fiction action film directed by Michael Bay, produced by Don Murphy and Tom DeSanto, and distributed by Paramount Pictures.

The movie takes place five years after the events of Transformers (2009). The story follows Cade Yeager (Mark Wahlberg), an inventor who discovers Optimus Prime's (Peter Cullen) hidden location in his backyard. Unbeknownst to Cade, he has inadvertently triggered a global alert that attracts the attention of the Decepticons.

The Autobots, led by Optimus Prime, are hunted down and nearly destroyed by the Decepticons, who seek revenge for their defeat in the previous film. The Autobots' leader, Optimus Prime, is severely damaged and left for dead.

Cade teams up with Drift (Kurosh Kharlamov), a former Decepticon who has defected to the Autobot side, and Harold Attinger (Kelsey Grammer), an FBI agent tasked with capturing Cade. However, Attinger's true intentions are revealed as he is secretly working for the Decepticons.

As the story unfolds, Cade discovers that the Decepticons plan to use a powerful energy source known as the "AllSpark" to destroy humanity. The Autobots, led by Optimus Prime, must find a way to stop the Decepticons and save humanity from extinction.

The movie features a mix of action, adventure, and humor, with a focus on Cade's character development and his relationships with Drift and Harold. The film also explores themes of redemption, sacrifice, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control.

Overall, Transformers: Age of Extinction received mixed reviews from critics but performed well at the box office, grossing over $1 billion worldwide. While it was not as well-received as its predecessor, the movie still delivered on its promise of high-octane action and exciting robot battles.

documents.title: Recoil
documents.tagline: They each have a score to settle.
documents.overview: A cop turns vigilante after his family is murdered, exacting vengeance on the killers - and then on all criminals who have slipped through the system.
documents.plot:
Recoil is a 2011 Canadian-American action film directed by Terry Miles, starring Steve Austin as a vigilante hunting the men who murdered his family. Danny Trejo, Serinda Swan, Keith Jardine, Lochlyn Munro and Noel Gugliemi co-star. It premiered in the United States on March 6, 2012.

In 2009 Ryan Varrett, a police officer in Dallas, survived an attack by a gang that killed his wife and nine-year-old son, killing three of the attackers himself. He has since left the force and taken to the road, tracking down and executing everyone involved, while FBI Special Agent Frank Sutton of the Seattle office investigates the string of dead criminals.

After killing a rapist, Ryan arrives in the small town of Hope, Washington, where a gas station owner, Kirby, points him to a little hotel run by a woman named Darcy. There he finds Rex Santiago, one of the gang members who attacked his family. Hope is controlled by the Circle, a drug- and gun-running biker gang led by Rex's brother Drayke, a fugitive wanted by the ATF, and the local sheriff, Cole, is in his pocket. When Ryan kills Rex, Drayke declares war on him and the town becomes a battlefield.

Ryan learns that Drayke planned the attack on his family as part of a campaign of revenge against the police officers who had sent him to a prison where he was brutalised. After Drayke's right-hand man Crab murders Kirby, Ryan burns Crab to death. Sutton arrives in Hope, and while Cole tries to pass off Rex's death as an accident, the sheriff's son, Deputy Hedge, who is not on the gang's payroll, explains how the Circle went from protecting the town to dealing guns and methamphetamine.

The bikers seize Darcy and beat Ryan, taking them both to an abandoned ferry that serves as Drayke's headquarters. Ryan breaks free, defeats Drayke's men and rescues Darcy. Cole, meanwhile, takes his own life, and Hedge and Sutton set out after Drayke. Ryan confronts the gang leader, whom he remembers from the night of the attack, and their fight ends when Sutton shoots Drayke dead.

Sutton chooses not to arrest Ryan, Hedge becomes sheriff, and Darcy decides to stay in Hope as Ryan leaves town, promising to send her a postcard. The film drew moderately positive reviews, with some critics appreciating its return to a plainer style of action filmmaking.

documents.title: Barbie in A Mermaid Tale 2
documents.tagline: Splash Into the Sea-quel with Barbie!
documents.overview: Surf's up for Barbie as she returns as Merliah, the fun and fashionable surfing champion who's also a magical mermaid princess! In this exciting sea-quel, Merliah makes a splash when she heads to Australia for the ultimate surfing competition. When the evil mermaid Eris escapes from her whirlpool with plans to take over the throne of Oceana, Merliah and her sea friends dive in to stop her. It's a fresh new adventure where Merliah learns that anything is possible and she really can have the best of both worlds!
documents.plot:
Barbie in a Mermaid Tale 2 is a 2012 computer-animated fantasy film directed by William Lau and produced by Mattel's Barbie Entertainment with Rainmaker Entertainment. The twenty-second entry in the Barbie film series and a sequel to Barbie in a Mermaid Tale (2010), it marked the return of Kelly Sheridan as the voice of Barbie, who plays the surfer Merliah Summers. Ashleigh Ball, Kathleen Barr, Nicole Oliver and Nakia Burrise are among the supporting voice cast. It was released on DVD in February 2012 and premiered on television on Nickelodeon in March.

A year after discovering that she is half-mermaid and a princess of the ocean kingdom of Oceana, Merliah wins a qualifying round of an invitational surfing competition, narrowly beating her rival Kylie Morgan, and both advance to the finals in Australia. Using her magical necklace to become a mermaid, Merliah shares the news with her mother, Queen Calissa. Calissa, however, is preparing for the Changing of Tides ceremony in the ancient undersea city of Aquellia near New Zealand, held every twenty years to bless a member of the royal family with the power to spin Merillia, the magical substance that keeps merfolk alive. The ceremony falls on the same day as the surfing final, and mother and daughter argue before parting.

In Australia, Kylie cheats to beat Merliah in the next round, although Merliah's daring handstand wins over the crowd. That night Kylie is approached by Alistair, a rainbowfish working for the wicked mermaid Eris, Calissa's sister, who has escaped imprisonment. Eris plans to steal Merliah's power and take over the ocean kingdom, and she lures Kylie into her scheme with the promise of a mermaid tail and victory in the contest. With the help of her dolphin friend Zuma, her friends and the merfolk, Merliah must stop Eris before the ceremony, balancing her dream of winning the competition with her responsibilities to her mother and her people.

Like other entries in the Barbie series, the film was aimed at young children and released primarily on home video, where it was promoted alongside a line of mermaid dolls and accessories. Its story continues the themes of friendship, family and believing in oneself that run through the series.

documents.title: Dragons: Gift of the Night Fury
documents.original_title: Dragons: Gift of the Night Fury
documents.overview: Hiccup and Toothless go on an exciting adventure and discover an island of new dragons.
documents.plot:
Dragons: Gift of the Night Fury is a 2011 American computer-animated Christmas short film from DreamWorks Animation, directed by Tom Owens and set in the world of How to Train Your Dragon (2010). It was released directly on DVD and Blu-ray on November 15, 2011, paired with another short, Book of Dragons. Jay Baruchel, Gerard Butler, Craig Ferguson, America Ferrera and Jonah Hill reprise their voice roles from the feature film as the Vikings of the island of Berk.

As Berk prepares for Snoggletog, its traditional winter holiday, the village's dragons suddenly and mysteriously fly away together, leaving the Vikings who have only recently befriended them heartbroken. The one dragon left behind is Toothless, the Night Fury, who cannot fly without Hiccup because of his damaged tail. Feeling sorry for his friend, Hiccup builds him an automatic prosthetic tailfin that allows him to fly unaided, a gift of independence, and Toothless soon takes off as well.

Three days later Hiccup discovers that Fishlegs has secretly kept his dragon Meatlug chained up to stop her leaving. When the dragon breaks free, she accidentally carries Hiccup away with her to a distant island of hot springs where the dragons of Berk have gathered to lay and hatch their eggs. Toothless, however, is nowhere to be found. Back on Berk, Astrid and the other teenagers find the eggs Meatlug left in her nest and hide them around the village as presents to cheer everyone up. The plan goes badly wrong, as dragon eggs hatch with an explosion, and the village is left heavily damaged, much to the alarm of Hiccup's father Stoick.

On the island, Hiccup finds Astrid's dragon Stormfly and Snotlout's dragon Hookfang with their new hatchlings. His request for a lift home sets off the dragons' return flight, and because the babies are too young to fly that far he loads them onto an old shipwreck so the adults can tow them. The returning dragons and their young bring joy to Berk, but Hiccup remains saddened by Toothless's absence.

During the Snoggletog celebrations Toothless finally returns, bringing back the helmet Hiccup lost at sea earlier, and the two are joyfully reunited. The next morning Toothless throws away the automatic tail and asks Hiccup to refit the old one, so that they can fly together again with Hiccup steering, showing that the dragon values their partnership more than his independence.

documents.title: Insidious: Chapter 2
documents.tagline: It will take what you love most.
documents.overview: The haunted Lambert family seeks to uncover the mysterious childhood secret that has left them dangerously connected to the spirit world.
documents.plot:
Insidious: Chapter 2 is a 2013 American supernatural horror film directed by James Wan and written by Leigh Whannell. The movie serves as a prequel to the first film, exploring the backstory of Josh Lambert's (Patrick Wilson) possession and his wife Renai's (Rose Byrne) subsequent journey.

The story begins with Josh, a paranormal investigator, who is struggling to cope with the aftermath of his previous encounter with the spirit world. He is haunted by nightmares and visions of his son Dalton (Ty Simpkins), who was possessed by an evil entity in the first film. Josh's wife Renai tries to be supportive, but their relationship is strained due to Josh's inability to shake off the traumatic events.

As Josh delves deeper into his past, he discovers that his father, John (Lew Temple), a fellow paranormal investigator, had been investigating a series of mysterious child abductions. The investigation leads them to a house in New York City, where they encounter a malevolent entity known as "The Red-Faced Demon." This demon is responsible for the abductions and is connected to an ancient ritual that has been passed down through generations.

Josh's father becomes increasingly obsessed with uncovering the truth behind the ritual, which ultimately leads to his downfall. The story takes a dark turn when Josh discovers that his father had made a pact with the entity, trading his own soul for the chance to save his son from the spirit world.

As Josh tries to make sense of his family's past and the events that led to his possession, he begins to experience more terrifying visions and nightmares. He becomes convinced that the only way to save himself and his family is to confront the entity head-on.

The climax of the film features a heart-pumping sequence where Josh faces off against the Red-Faced Demon in an abandoned asylum. With the help of his father's research, Josh manages to uncover the secrets behind the ritual and ultimately defeats the demon, saving his own soul.

However, the victory comes at a great cost, as Josh is left with severe emotional trauma and a newfound understanding of the horrors that lie beyond the veil of reality. The film concludes with Josh returning home to Renai and Dalton, but the audience is left wondering if he has truly overcome his demons or if they will continue to haunt him.

Overall, Insidious: Chapter 2 is a gripping horror film that explores themes of trauma, possession, and the supernatural. With its tense atmosphere and well-crafted plot twists, it sets the stage for the events of the first film and provides a chilling glimpse into the world of the Insidious franchise.

documents.title: Starlet
documents.overview: An unlikely friendship forms between 21 year-old Jane and the elderly Sadie after Jane discovers a hidden stash of money inside an object at Sadie's yard sale.
documents.plot:
Starlet is a 2012 American independent drama directed, edited and co-produced by Sean Baker, who co-wrote it with Chris Bergoch. It follows an unlikely friendship that develops in the San Fernando Valley between a 21-year-old woman, played by Dree Hemingway, and an 85-year-old widow, played by Besedka Johnson in her only screen role.

Jane, who also goes by Tess, lives in an apartment rented by Melissa and her boyfriend, Mikey, with her Xolo dog, Starlet. Told she cannot repaint her room because Mikey uses it for "shoots", she looks for change at neighborhood yard sales and buys a thermos from a crotchety old woman named Sadie. At home, Jane discovers a stash of cash hidden inside. After splurging on a few luxuries, she decides to return the money, but Sadie shuts the door on her before she can explain. Jane persists, and despite Sadie's prickliness a friendship forms. Jane learns that Sadie has always loved Paris but never gone there, and that she was married to a successful gambler, was widowed long ago and never had children.

It emerges that Jane, Melissa and Mikey all work in adult films. When Melissa is fired after clashing with their boss, Jane persuades him to suspend her for a month instead, and Jane herself is promoted. While Jane works a porn convention, Starlet slips away from Sadie, who eventually finds the dog. A drunken Melissa urges Jane to spend her windfall on someone she cares about, expecting to benefit herself, but Jane buys two first-class tickets to Paris and persuades Sadie to come. Enraged, Melissa throws Jane out, and their boss gives her a room in a house shared by other performers. Out of spite, Melissa tells Sadie about the money Jane found. Sadie briefly begins unpacking, then resumes preparing for the trip. When Jane, unaware that Sadie knows, picks her up for the airport, Sadie asks to stop at the cemetery to leave flowers on her husband's grave. Nearby, Jane notices the grave of Sadie's daughter, who died at about 18, and returns to the car before the two drive off together.

The film was shot entirely in Los Angeles in August and September 2011. Starlet premiered at South by Southwest on March 11, 2012, where Johnson received Special Jury Recognition and was released by Music Box Films on November 9, 2012. It grossed $146,222. Critics praised it, with 87% on Rotten Tomatoes and 74 on Metacritic, and it won the Independent Spirit Robert Altman Award. Johnson died a year after its release.

documents.title: Much Ado About Nothing
documents.tagline: Shakespeare Knew How to Throw a Party
documents.overview: A modern retelling of Shakespeare's classic comedy about two pairs of lovers with different takes on romance and a way with words.
documents.plot: The plot of the film is largely unchanged from that of Shakespeare's original play. Differences include the modern-day setting, switching Conrade's gender, eliminating several minor roles and consolidating others into Leonato's aide, and expanding Ursula's role by giving her a number of Margaret's scenes. In addition, the film adds background to the relationship between Beatrice and Benedick by showing, in an opening scene, a morning after they apparently slept together, and later, flashbacks that confirm this. Benedick is beardless in both, so this is presumably some time before the plot of the movie takes place.

documents.title: Romeo & Juliet
documents.tagline: The most dangerous love story ever told.
documents.overview: In Verona, bad blood between the Montague and Capulet families leads to much bitterness. Despite the hostility, Romeo Montague manages an invitation to a masked ball at the estate of the Capulets and meets Juliet, their daughter. The two are instantly smitten but dismayed to learn that their families are enemies. Romeo and Juliet figure out a way to pursue their romance, but Romeo is banished for his part in the slaying of Juliet's cousin, Tybalt.
documents.plot:
Romeo & Juliet is a 2013 film adaptation of William Shakespeare's tragedy, directed by Carlo Carlei from a screenplay by Julian Fellowes. Douglas Booth and Hailee Steinfeld play the young lovers, with Damian Lewis as Lord Capulet, Kodi Smit-McPhee as Benvolio, Ed Westwick as Tybalt, Stellan Skarsgård as the Prince and Paul Giamatti as Friar Laurence. It keeps the original story but only part of Shakespeare's dialogue, a choice many critics objected to. It opened in Britain and the United States on 11 October 2013.

In late medieval Verona, the rich Montague and Capulet families have been enemies for generations. After a brawl in the market, the Prince warns that anyone who breaks the peace again will pay with their life. Young Romeo Montague pines for Rosaline, a Capulet, and despite his cousin Benvolio's advice he slips into a Capulet feast with Benvolio and Mercutio hoping to see her. Instead he meets Juliet; they fall instantly in love, dance and kiss, and only afterwards learn from her Nurse that they belong to opposing houses.

That night Romeo enters the Capulet garden, hears Juliet declare her love from her balcony and climbs up to her, and they resolve to marry. Friar Laurence agrees to wed them in secret, hoping the match will heal the feud. Soon after the ceremony, Tybalt confronts Romeo and his friends and kills Mercutio, and Romeo kills Tybalt in revenge. The Prince banishes him. Romeo spends one night with Juliet before fleeing, and Lord Capulet orders his daughter to marry Count Paris, threatening to disown her if she refuses.

Desperate, Juliet turns to the Friar, who gives her a potion that will make her appear dead until Romeo can take her away to Mantua, and sends a letter explaining the plan. The letter never arrives, and Romeo hears from Benvolio that Juliet is dead. He buys poison, kills Paris at the tomb and drinks it beside Juliet, who wakes just as he dies in her arms. Refusing to leave with the Friar, she stabs herself with Romeo's dagger. At their funeral the families finally reconcile.

Critics found it unremarkable, with a 25% Rotten Tomatoes approval rating, and it grossed about $3 million, though its score was honoured by the International Film Music Critics Association.

documents.title: Despicable Me 2
documents.tagline: Back 2 Work
documents.overview: Gru is recruited by the Anti-Villain League to help deal with a powerful new super criminal.
documents.plot:
Despicable Me 2 is a 2013 American computer-animated comedy film produced by Illumination Entertainment and distributed by Universal Pictures.

The movie begins with Gru (voiced by Steve Carell), a supervillain who has retired from his life of crime after being caught by the Anti-Villain League (AVL). However, he is forced back into action when AVL agent Lucy Wilde (voiced by Kristen Wiig) asks for his help in stopping a new villain, Vector (voiced by Ken Jeong).

Vector is a former supervillain who has stolen the Moon and plans to sell it on the black market. Gru agrees to work with Lucy to stop Vector, but things get complicated when he starts to develop feelings for her.

As Gru and Lucy work together, they start to uncover Vector's true intentions. They also discover that Vector is actually a former AVL agent who was thought to be dead. Vector's plan is to use the Moon as collateral to fund his own evil schemes.

Meanwhile, Gru's adopted daughters Margo (voiced by Miranda Cosgrove), Edith (voiced by Dana Gaier), and Agnes (voiced by Elsie Fisher) are dealing with their own issues. Margo is struggling in school, Edith is trying to fit in with the cool kids, and Agnes is obsessed with a villainous character from her favorite movie.

As Gru and Lucy get closer to stopping Vector, they also have to deal with the girls' antics. The girls start to develop their own supervillain skills, which causes chaos and destruction in the city.

In the end, Gru and Lucy are able to stop Vector and recover the Moon. However, Gru realizes that he doesn't need to be a supervillain to be happy. He decides to retire from his life of crime for good and focus on being a normal family man.

The movie ends with Gru and Lucy sharing a romantic kiss, and the girls getting into their own brand of mischief. The final scene shows Gru's new life as a suburban dad, complete with a backyard pool and a minivan.

Overall, Despicable Me 2 is a heartwarming and hilarious film that explores themes of family, love, and redemption. It features stunning animation, witty humor, and lovable characters that make it a must-see for both kids and adults.

documents.title: So Undercover
documents.tagline: Meet the FBI's new secret weapon
documents.overview: When the FBI hires her to go undercover at a college sorority, Molly Morris (Miley Cyrus) must transform herself from a tough, streetwise private investigator to a refined, sophisticated university girl to help protect the daughter of a one-time Mobster. With several suspects on her list, Molly unexpectedly discovers that not everyone is who they appear to be, including herself.

documents.tagline: Experience the Fallout
documents.overview: A group of six tourists looking to go off the beaten path, hire an 'extreme tour guide' who, ignoring warnings, takes them into the city of Pripyat, the former home to the workers of the Chernobyl nuclear reactor, but now a deserted town since the disaster more than 25 years earlier. After a brief exploration of the abandoned city, the group members find themselves stranded, only to discover that they are not alone.

documents.tagline: They met as enemies, but fate brought them together.
documents.overview: During the invasion of Normandy the photograph of a slim Korean man in German uniform was found. It transpired that the man had served as a soldier in the Japanese, Russian and German armies. His incredible story inspired director Kang Je-Gyu to create this epic war drama.

documents.title: The Raid
documents.tagline: 1 Ruthless Crime Lord, 20 Elite Cops, 30 Floors of Hell
documents.overview: Deep in the heart of Jakarta's slums lies an impenetrable safe house for the world's most dangerous killers and gangsters. Until now, the run-down apartment block has been considered untouchable to even the bravest of police. Cloaked under the cover of pre-dawn darkness and silence, an elite swat team is tasked with raiding the safe house in order to take down the notorious drug lord that runs it.  But when a chance encounter with a spotter blows their cover and news of their assault reaches the drug lord, the building's lights are cut and all the exits blocked. Stranded on the sixth floor with no way out, the unit must fight their way through the city's worst to survive their mission. Starring Indonesian martial arts sensation Iko Uwais.
documents.plot:
The Raid, released in the United States as The Raid: Redemption, is a 2011 Indonesian action thriller written, edited and directed by the Welsh filmmaker Gareth Evans. Iko Uwais stars as Rama, a rookie member of the police Mobile Brigade, with Joe Taslim as Sergeant Jaka, Donny Alamsyah as Andi, Yayan Ruhian as Mad Dog, Pierre Gruno as Lieutenant Wahyu and Ray Sahetapy as the drug lord Tama Riyadi. Its fights showcase the Indonesian martial art pencak silat, choreographed by Uwais and Ruhian.

Rama joins a 20-man squad led by Jaka and Wahyu on a raid to arrest Tama, who rules a rundown apartment block in Jakarta that shelters criminals and addicts, aided by his lieutenants Andi and Mad Dog. The officers clear the lower floors undetected but are spotted on the sixth. Tama's reinforcements wipe out the men outside, he cuts the power and announces over the loudspeakers that the police are trapped. Wahyu admits that the raid was his own unauthorised scheme to remove Tama, who has corrupt friends in the police, and that no backup is coming. Most of the squad is massacred. Rama hacks through a floor with an axe so the survivors can escape to the apartment below, then blows up the attackers with a propane tank rigged in a refrigerator.

The survivors split up. Rama hides the wounded officer Bowo with a reluctant law-abiding tenant before fighting his way past a machete gang. He then meets Andi, who turns out to be his estranged elder brother, the man their father urged him to find; Andi refuses to leave his criminal life. Mad Dog fights Jaka hand to hand and kills him, while Tama discovers Andi's betrayal on his surveillance cameras and has him captured. Rama, rejoining Wahyu and officer Dagu, battles through a drug laboratory, then splits off to rescue Andi, and the brothers kill Mad Dog after a brutal fight. Wahyu murders Dagu and seizes Tama, who reveals he was warned of the raid and that Wahyu's corrupt superior has set him up. Wahyu shoots Tama and tries to kill himself, but his gun is empty. Andi arranges the survivors' escape and gives Rama Tama's recordings of corrupt officials, choosing to remain in the underworld where he can protect his brother.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival and earned strong reviews, with 87% on Rotten Tomatoes; The Guardian's Peter Bradshaw gave it five stars. It was followed by The Raid 2 in 2014.

documents.title: Alex Cross
documents.tagline: Don't Ever Cross Alex Cross
documents.overview: After Washington DC detective Alex Cross is told that a family member has been murdered, he vows to track down the killer. He soon discovers that she was not his first victim and that things are not what they seem.
documents.plot:
Alex Cross is a 2012 American action thriller directed by Rob Cohen, starring Tyler Perry as the title character, a psychologist and police detective, and Matthew Fox as a professional killer nicknamed Picasso. The screenplay by Marc Moss and Kerry Williamson is based on James Patterson's 2006 novel Cross. The third film in the Alex Cross series, it was conceived as a reboot, and unlike its predecessors it was released by Summit Entertainment rather than Paramount.

Dr. Alex Cross works as a detective for the Detroit Police Department alongside his childhood friend Thomas Kane and their colleague Monica Ashe, who are secretly romantically involved. At home, Cross lives a happy family life with his mother, his pregnant wife Maria and their two children. When a businesswoman is tortured and murdered, Cross deduces that the killer is a lone professional, possibly a former special forces operative, who leaves behind a charcoal drawing of his victim, earning him the nickname Picasso.

Linking the victim to two other businessmen, the team predicts Picasso's next target and manages to prevent the assassination in a gunfight, though the killer escapes after being wounded. Cross believes Picasso is too focused on his targets to come after the detectives, but he is wrong. Picasso strikes back at the team personally, murdering people close to them in revenge, and Cross is left devastated. Driven by grief and rage, Cross and Kane set out to hunt down the assassin by any means necessary, a pursuit that pushes Cross to the limits of his principles and forces him to think like the man he is chasing to discover who is ultimately behind the killings.

The film recasts the character as a younger, more physical action hero, torn between his family life, a possible move to an FBI job in Washington and his obsession with the case.

Released on October 19, 2012, Alex Cross opened in fifth place and grossed about 34.6 million dollars worldwide on a 35 million dollar budget. Critics panned it, giving it 11 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus blamed Cohen's direction and a tasteless, lazily written script, and a Metacritic score of 30.

documents.title: Cirque du Soleil: Worlds Away
documents.tagline: Experience a Journey Like Never Before
documents.overview: An original story featuring performances by Cirque du Soleil. A young woman is entranced by an Aerialist. When they fall into the dreamlike world of Cirque du Soleil and are separated, they travel through the different tent worlds trying to find each other.

documents.title: The Human Centipede 3 (Final Sequence)
documents.tagline: 100% politically incorrect.
documents.overview: Taking inspiration from The Human Centipede films, the warden of a notorious and troubled prison looks to create a 500-person human centipede as a solution to his problems.
documents.plot:
The Human Centipede 3 (Final Sequence) is a 2015 body horror black comedy from writer-director Tom Six, the concluding chapter of his Human Centipede trilogy. Dieter Laser and Laurence R. Harvey, the leads of the first two films, return in new roles as the sadistic prison warden Bill Boss and his accountant Dwight Butler, with Eric Roberts as Governor Hughes, Bree Olson as Bill's secretary Daisy, and Clayton Rohner, Robert LaSardo and Tommy "Tiny" Lister. Six appears as himself.

At George H. W. Bush State Prison, somewhere in the American Southwest, Bill, a cannibalistic and deranged warden, rules through brutality, breaking one inmate's arms and scalding another. When Governor Hughes visits and threatens to fire both men unless the violence stops, Bill retaliates with a wave of savage punishments. Dwight then proposes surgically joining all the inmates together mouth to anus to form a giant "human centipede", the ultimate deterrent to crime. Bill is at first opposed.

After a nightmare about being attacked by prisoners, Bill summons Tom Six, the director of the Human Centipede films, who assures him that the procedure shown in them is "100% medically accurate" and gives his blessing on condition that he can watch the operation. Screening the films for the inmates sparks a riot in which Daisy is beaten into a coma before a special forces team restores order. Bill sedates the prisoners one by one with a tranquilliser gun, shooting dead those deemed unsuitable and one inmate who wants to join. When the operation is complete, Hughes is horrified to find not only the centipede, which now includes Daisy, but also a "human caterpillar" made from limbless death-row inmates and lifers, and he tells the pair they deserve execution. Bill shoots Dr. Jones in a rage, but Hughes soon returns, having changed his mind, to declare the centipede exactly what America needs. After he leaves, Bill kills Dwight for trying to take credit for the idea, and the film ends with the naked warden whooping with joy in a watchtower above the centipede as "The Star-Spangled Banner" plays. A Blu-ray alternate ending presents the events as a dream of Dr. Josef Heiter, leading into the first film.

Released in theatres and on video on demand on 22 May 2015, the film was almost universally panned for its relentless gore and repetitive story, scoring 20% on Rotten Tomatoes. It earned Golden Raspberry nominations for Worst Prequel, Remake, Rip-off or Sequel and Worst Director.

documents.title: Bad Ass
documents.tagline: They messed with the wrong senior citizen.
documents.overview: Decorated Vietnam hero, Frank Vega returns home only to get shunned by society leaving him without a job or his high school sweetheart. It's not until forty years later when an incident on a commuter bus makes him a local hero where he's suddenly celebrated once again. But his good fortune suddenly turns for the worse when his best friend is murdered and the police aren't doing anything about it.
documents.plot:
Bad Ass is a 2012 American action film written and directed by Craig Moss and loosely inspired by the 2010 viral video of a fight on an AC Transit bus, which a bystander recorded and posted to YouTube. Danny Trejo stars as Frank Vega, alongside Charles S. Dutton and Ron Perlman. Production wrapped by May 2011, after which SC Films took the sales rights to the Cannes Film Festival market. The film was sold to Wild Bunch for Germany and Pinnacle Films for Australia, and Samuel Goldwyn Films gave it a US theatrical release in April 2012, with 20th Century Fox handling ancillary and international rights.

Frank, an unemployed Vietnam War veteran, becomes an overnight celebrity after he beats up two abusive skinheads on a city bus. Dubbed "Bad Ass", he finds his face on T-shirts and graffiti, is invited onto talk shows and is offered ride-alongs by the police. His best friend and fellow veteran, Klondike Washington, moves in with him and leaves a USB flash drive in his care, but soon afterward Klondike is killed in an alley by two thugs. Grief-stricken and frustrated by the slow police investigation, Frank begins digging on his own. At the scene he finds a spent cartridge casing and a pendant bearing a woman's picture, which leads him to a pawn shop where he learns it belongs to a man named Terence.

Tracking Terence through his girlfriend, whom he finds at a massage parlor and follows home, Frank breaks in and forces Terence to talk about the boss who ordered the killing. He learns that Klondike died because of the flash drive, which holds information about an oil well project tied to Mayor Williams. Frank turns the drive over to Officer Malark and goes after Panther, the drug lord behind the murder, but is captured and tortured for the drive's whereabouts. When Panther finds Frank's address in his wallet and heads there, Frank follows and defeats him in a fight. Panther is arrested, the news reveals the mayor's involvement, and Frank gets on with his life.

Dutton plays Panther and Perlman plays Mayor Williams. Reviews were mostly negative, and some reports even wondered whether the project was a hoax. Vulture's Sarah Benned joked that the trailer might be a parody, and Cinema Blend likened it to Trejo's mock trailer for Machete. Mark Olsen of the Los Angeles Times found it hard to tell what was bad deliberately and what was simply mishandled, while Rotten Tomatoes counted 20% approval from five critics.

documents.title: Turkish for Beginners
documents.overview: During an emergency landing on a deserted island suddenly traumatized by antiauthoritarian education Lena Schneider (Josefine Preuss) together with the Turkish Super Macho Cem Öztürk (Elyas M'Barek) must fight for survival. After initially Cem macho repulsive acts on Lena, a jellyfish in the water and sand in a bikini, she recognizes the time the romantic core behind his cool facade. Meanwhile, meet also their parents, who obdurate psychologist Doris (Anna Stieblich) and Metin Öztürk (Adnan Maral) to work together to find their missing children. So both generations take an involuntary Turkish Basic Course for beginners.
documents.plot:
Turkish for Beginners (Türkisch für Anfänger) is a 2012 German comedy written and directed by Bora Dagtekin, who created the ARD television series of the same name and made his feature directing debut with this film. Rather than continuing the show, it retells from scratch how the Schneider and Öztürk families meet. Almost the entire television cast returned, led by Josefine Preuß as Lena Schneider, Elyas M'Barek as Cem Öztürk, Anna Stieblich as Doris, Adnan Maral as Metin, Pegah Ferydoni as Yağmur and Arnel Tači as Costa, with Katja Riemann, Günther Kaufmann and Frederick Lau in supporting roles. It was produced by Rat Pack Filmproduktion with Constantin Film, ARD Degeto and several regional broadcasters.

Raised by Doris, a free-spirited therapist of the 1968 generation, Lena has become her opposite: controlled, rule-bound and wary of emotion. For her graduation, mother and daughter fly to Thailand, sitting next to the Öztürks, a widowed police detective, Metin, and his children, the macho would-be rapper Cem and his sister Yağmur. When an ash cloud forces the plane to ditch in the Indian Ocean, most passengers are rescued, but Lena drifts ashore on a deserted island in a life raft with Cem, Yağmur and Costa, a stuttering Greek. Their radio contact with their parents reveals that the raft's beacon is too weak to be located.

As the castaways struggle to get by, Lena and Cem constantly clash. After Lena steps on a sea urchin and suffers an allergic reaction, Cem carries her to a village of supposed cannibals, who turn out to speak fluent German and are hosting a researcher who treats her. At a celebration, Lena believes she slept with Cem while intoxicated and later overhears that he had made a bet about it. Meanwhile, Doris and Metin fall in love at the resort. Once reunited with her mother, the hurt Lena drives the Öztürks away by making Metin believe that the mafia clan that put the family in witness protection has found them. When she later watches her camcorder footage and sees that Cem only watched over her while she slept, she confesses everything. She and Doris catch up with the Öztürks on the plane as they leave with new identities, and both couples are reunited.

Shot over 37 days in 2011 in Munich, Berlin and Thailand, whose islands Ko Kut and Ko Chang stood in for the Andaman Islands, the film premiered in Munich on 6 March 2012 and opened in German cinemas on 15 March 2012.

documents.title: The Only Living Boy in New York
documents.original_title: The Only Living Boy in New York
documents.overview: When a young man learns that his overbearing father is having an affair, he tries to stop it, only to be seduced by the older woman as well.
documents.plot:
The Only Living Boy in New York is a 2017 American drama directed by Marc Webb and written by Allan Loeb, its title shared with a manuscript that figures in the story. It stars Callum Turner as Thomas Webb, a young man adrift in Manhattan, Kate Beckinsale as Johanna, Pierce Brosnan as his father Ethan, Cynthia Nixon as his mother Judith, Kiersey Clemons as his friend Mimi and Jeff Bridges as his mysterious neighbor W.F. Gerald.

Thomas Webb, a recent college graduate living in Manhattan, is unsure of what to do with his life and harbors an unrequited crush on his friend Mimi. He strikes up a friendship with W.F. Gerald, an eccentric, hard-drinking neighbor who begins offering him advice about life. One night, Thomas sees his father, Ethan, a successful publisher, kissing a woman named Johanna. Fearing the effect the affair would have on his fragile mother, Judith, Thomas starts following Johanna and confronts her, demanding that she leave his father alone.

Johanna, an editor who works with Ethan, dismisses Thomas as a naive child, but the two soon begin an affair of their own. Thomas, who has always wanted to be a writer but was told by his father that his work was merely serviceable, confides in W.F., who turns out to be a reclusive, successful writer whom Thomas has inspired to write again; Thomas later discovers a manuscript titled The Only Living Boy in New York in his apartment. As Thomas's relationships with Johanna, Mimi and his parents grow more tangled, he must confront both his father's secrets and a revelation about his own family history that changes his understanding of who he is.

The film was compared by critics to coming-of-age stories such as The Graduate, examining family secrets, infidelity and a young man's search for identity in New York.

The Only Living Boy in New York was released by Roadside Attractions and Amazon Studios on August 11, 2017. It received generally negative reviews, with 33 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it narratively messy and cloying, and a Metacritic score of 33.

documents.title: Bridget Jones's Baby
documents.tagline: Relationship status: beyond complicated
documents.overview: After breaking up with Mark Darcy, Bridget Jones's 'happily ever after' hasn't quite gone according to plan. Fortysomething and single again, she decides to focus on her job as top news producer and surround herself with old friends and new. For once, Bridget has everything completely under control. What could possibly go wrong? Then her love life takes a turn and Bridget meets a dashing American named Jack, the suitor who is everything Mr. Darcy is not. In an unlikely twist she finds herself pregnant, but with one hitch she can only be fifty percent sure of the identity of her baby's father.
documents.plot: After breaking up, Bridget Jones' happily-ever-after hasn't quite gone according to plan. Fortysomething and single again, she decides to focus on her job and surround herself with old friends and new. For once, Bridget has everything completely under control. Then her love life takes a turn when she meets Jack. A week later, she runs into Mark before she finds herself pregnant, but with one hitch - she's not sure of the identity of her baby's father - Mark or Jack.

documents.title: Rush
documents.tagline: Everyone's driven by something.
documents.overview: A biographical drama centered on the rivalry between Formula 1 drivers James Hunt and Niki Lauda during the 1976 Formula One motor-racing season.
documents.plot:
Rush is a 2013 biographical sports drama directed by Ron Howard and written by Peter Morgan, centred on the rivalry between the Formula One drivers James Hunt and Niki Lauda during the 1976 season. Chris Hemsworth plays Hunt and Daniel Brühl plays Lauda, with Olivia Wilde, Alexandra Maria Lara and Natalie Dormer in supporting roles. It premiered in London on 2 September 2013 and screened at the Toronto International Film Festival before its British release.

The two men first clash in a Formula Three race in 1970, and their contrasting temperaments define the story: Hunt is a charismatic, hard-living British playboy who races on instinct, while Lauda is a blunt, methodical Austrian who treats driving as engineering. Lauda buys his way into Formula One with a bank loan, joins Ferrari and wins the 1975 world championship. Hunt, after his Hesketh team folds for lack of sponsorship, joins McLaren and marries the model Suzy Miller, while Lauda begins a relationship with Marlene Knaus.

Lauda dominates the start of 1976, while Hunt endures disqualification, mechanical setbacks and the collapse of his marriage when Suzy leaves him for Richard Burton. Restored points and renewed focus bring him back into contention. Lauda, newly married, worries that happiness has made him vulnerable. Before the German Grand Prix he urges drivers to cancel the race on the rain-soaked Nürburgring, but Hunt argues him down. On the second lap Lauda's Ferrari suffers a suspension failure, crashes and bursts into flames, leaving him with severe burns to his head and lungs.

Hunt, guilt-stricken, wins race after race while Lauda endures agonising treatment, and just six weeks later Lauda returns at Monza to finish fourth, earning Hunt's deep respect. The championship comes down to the torrential Japanese Grand Prix, with Hunt three points behind. Lauda withdraws after two laps, judging the conditions too dangerous, and Hunt battles through to finish third, winning the title by a single point. Afterwards Hunt revels in fame while Lauda tells him to defend his title, and in a closing voiceover Lauda reflects on Hunt's early death at 45 and on how their rivalry drove them both.

Rush was well received, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 89% approval and particular praise for the two leads, Howard's direction, the racing sequences and Hans Zimmer's score. It grossed about $98 million worldwide against a $38 million budget.

documents.title: Anna Karenina
documents.tagline: An epic story of love.
documents.overview: In Imperial Russia, Anna, the wife of the officer Karenin, goes to Moscow to visit her brother. On the way, she meets the charming cavalry officer Vronsky to whom she is immediately attracted. But in St. Petersburg’s high society, a relationship like this could destroy a woman’s reputation.
documents.plot:
Anna Karenina is a 2012 historical romantic drama directed by Joe Wright, with a screenplay by Tom Stoppard adapted from Leo Tolstoy's 1878 novel. Keira Knightley, in her third film with Wright, plays Anna, the wife of senior statesman Alexei Karenin, played by Jude Law. Aaron Taylor-Johnson plays the cavalry officer Count Vronsky, Domhnall Gleeson plays Konstantin Levin and Alicia Vikander plays Kitty.

In the Russian Empire in 1874, Dolly has thrown out her unfaithful husband, Stiva Oblonsky. His sister Anna, who lives in Saint Petersburg with Karenin and their son Seryozha, travels to Moscow to reconcile them. Kitty, Dolly's sister, rejects the landowner Levin, hoping to marry Vronsky. Anna meets Vronsky, and they are instantly attracted. At a ball he favors Anna over Kitty, then follows her to Saint Petersburg. He turns down a posting in Tashkent, and they become lovers. Anna becomes pregnant, and her reaction to Vronsky's fall at a horse race betrays her. She admits the affair to Karenin, who demands that she give him up.

Karenin decides to divorce her, while Levin and Kitty reunite and marry. Anna nearly dies giving birth to a daughter, and Karenin forgives her. She first resolves to stay with him, but Vronsky persuades her to leave for Italy with the baby. At Levin's estate, Kitty defies convention by helping Masha, a prostitute, nurse Levin's sickly brother Nikolai. Returning to Saint Petersburg, Anna is turned away by Karenin when she tries to see Seryozha on his birthday, and she is publicly shunned at the opera. Taking morphine and consumed by jealousy, she suspects that Vronsky's mother wants him to marry the young Princess Sorokina. On a train journey, tormented by imagined betrayal, Anna asks God for forgiveness and throws herself under a train. The film ends with Levin and Kitty raising their child and the retired Karenin at his estate, watching Seryozha and Anna's daughter play.

Wright staged most of the story on a single soundstage at Shepperton Studios dressed as a dilapidated theatre. The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival and grossed about $69 million worldwide. Reviews were generally positive: critics praised the cast but were divided by the theatrical concept, and Rotten Tomatoes called it bold and stylized "for both better and worse." It received four Academy Award nominations, and Durran won both the Oscar and the BAFTA for Best Costume Design.

documents.title: Ben 10: Destroy All Aliens
documents.overview: Based on the original animated series Ben 10.  Ben becomes targeted by an evil Mechamorph Warrior, named "Retaliator," who mistakenly blames Ben for something he did not do and attempts to destroy all aliens.

documents.title: The Bling Ring
documents.tagline: Living the Dream, One Heist at a Time
documents.overview: Inspired by actual events, a group of fame-obsessed teenagers use the Internet to track the whereabouts of famous celebrities, then rob their homes of riches.
documents.plot:
Quiet teenager Marc Hall transfers to Indian Hills High School in Agoura Hills, California. He befriends fame-obsessed Rebecca Ahn. While at a party at her house, Rebecca persuades Marc to sneak away with her and steal valuables from unlocked vehicles on the streets. As they begin hanging out regularly, Marc starts to view Rebecca as a sister figure.
One day, when Marc mentions that a wealthy acquaintance of his is vacationing in Jamaica, Rebecca convinces Marc to join her in breaking into the empty house, where she steals money, a handbag similar to one that her idol Lindsay Lohan has, cash and the keys to a Porsche, that they use to flee the scene. They go on a shopping spree with the money, buying luxury items. Marc visits a nightclub with Rebecca and meets her friend Chloe Tainer, along with sisters Nicki and Sam Moore. The group notices celebrities Kirsten Dunst and Paris Hilton. Later, while researching Paris on the internet, Marc and Rebecca learn she is out of town. They find her address, go to her house and on finding a key under the doormat, break in. They go through Paris's belongings and take some of her jewelry, including a bracelet that Rebecca later flaunts to Nicki, Sam, and Chloe at a party.
At Nicki's request, Rebecca and Marc take her, Sam, and Chloe back to Paris's house. They marvel at Paris's lavish lifestyle and steal shoes, bags, dresses, cash, and jewelry. A drunk Chloe gets into an accident while driving away; she is arrested and sentenced to community service. Marc and Rebecca return to rob Paris's house a third time and are nearly discovered by security. They then rob the home of Audrina Patridge, using the internet to determine when she will not be home, and later sell unwanted items at an outdoor market.
The group burgles the home of Megan Fox, Nicki's younger sister Emily squeezing through a pet door to get in. Nicki discovers a handgun inside, and Sam playfully threatens Marc with it before taking it to her boyfriend Rob's home. When he grabs her, the gun goes off, though no one is injured. The group later robs the home of Orlando Bloom and his girlfriend, Miranda Kerr. Marc finds a case filled with seven of Orlando's Rolex watches and a roll of cash. Chloe helps Marc sell the watches to her friend Ricky, a nightclub manager. The teens later return to Paris's house with Rob, who finds and steals large amounts of jewelry.
A news report containing security footage from the robbery at Patridge's home concerns Marc, but Rebecca is undeterred. She instigates a burglary at the home of Rachel Bilson, and the group ultimately breaks into Lindsay Lohan's house and robs it. Shortly thereafter, Rebecca moves to Las Vegas with her father, ostensibly due to troubles at home, leaving some of her stolen items with Marc. Media coverage of the Hollywood Hills burglaries intensifies, the public labeling the criminals "The Bling Ring".

documents.title: Temptation: Confessions of a Marriage Counselor
documents.original_title: Temptation: Confessions of a Marriage Counselor
documents.tagline: Betrayal Burns Forever
documents.overview: A marriage counselor's personal and professional life becomes complicated after she enters into a relationship with one of her clients.
documents.plot: Judith has known her husband Brice since they were children, but now their marriage is growing stale. Having just completed her graduate work in psychotherapy, she's eager to begin a career as a marriage counselor. She takes an internship at a matchmaking firm for millionaires and meets Harley, a charismatic billionaire investor who makes no effort to hide his attraction to Judith. Although quite resistant at first, eventually Judith succumbs to his charms, placing her marriage in jeopardy and forever altering the course of her life.

documents.title: RoboCop
documents.tagline: We've got the future under control.
documents.overview: In RoboCop, the year is 2028 and multinational conglomerate OmniCorp is at the center of robot technology.  Overseas, their drones have been used by the military for years, but have been forbidden for law enforcement in America.  Now OmniCorp wants to bring their controversial technology to the home front, and they see a golden opportunity to do it.  When Alex Murphy – a loving husband, father and good cop doing his best to stem the tide of crime and corruption in Detroit – is critically injured, OmniCorp sees their chance to build a part-man, part-robot police officer.  OmniCorp envisions a RoboCop in every city and even more billions for their shareholders, but they never counted on one thing: there is still a man inside the machine.
documents.plot:
In 2028, OmniCorp revolutionizes warfare by introducing robotic peacekeeping drones. CEO Raymond Sellars wants to market this technology to U.S. law enforcement, but the Dreyfus Act bans the use of domestic militarized drones. Knowing that a majority of Americans oppose military systems in communities, Sellars consults roboticist Dr. Dennett Norton on the viability of developing cyborgs with OmniCorp technology. Norton warns him that the process would be incredibly traumatic, and that they must find the right candidate.
A Detroit police detective, Alex Murphy, is selected after a car-bomb planted by crime boss Antoine Vallon leaves him critically injured. Norton persuades Alex's wife, Clara, to approve the procedure. Upon waking, Alex escapes after realizing his transformation, but Norton shuts him down and returns him to the lab. Norton reveals that most of his body is gone, leaving only parts of his head with a repaired cybernetic brain, respiratory organs, heart, and right hand. Horrified, Alex asks for euthanasia, but Norton urges him to live for the possibility of being reunited with his family. During training with Rick Mattox, Alex struggles to match the drones; Norton creates a new subroutine that allows Alex' programming to take control of his actions, making him incredibly efficient but also reducing his empathy.
Before his public unveiling, Alex experiences an emotional breakdown and Norton has no choice but to completely suppress his emotions. During the ceremony, RoboCop identifies and apprehends a wanted fugitive in the crowd. As he reduces crime in Detroit, the public becomes more supportive of repealing the Dreyfus Act. Realizing Clara is inquiring about her husband, Sellars instructs Norton to distance her from him.
Clara tells RoboCop about David's nightmares and social withdrawal. Driven by this, Alex overrides his programming to access sealed files on his attempted murder. Learning of Vallon's culpability, he guns down the boss and all of his men in a fierce shootout. With help from his former partner Jack Lewis, Alex then tracks down the two dirty cops who betrayed him to Vallon. Upon realizing that the Chief of Police covered up their actions, he attempts to arrest her only to be remotely deactivated by Mattox.
Through Pat Novak's news show, Sellars uses the incident to get the Dreyfus Act repealed. When Clara threatens public exposure unless she's allowed to see her husband, Sellars lies to her that Alex died from surgical complications while secretly ordering his men to euthanize him. Norton helps Alex escape just as OmniCorp goes into full lockdown.
Alex forces his way inside and overcomes the building's automated security as the police arrive. Mattox is able to subdue him but is swiftly killed by Lewis. Reaching the rooftop helipad, Alex finds Sellars holding his wife and son at gunpoint while revealing that Robocop's programming prevents him from harming any top executive of OmniCorp.

documents.title: Would You Rather
documents.tagline: Tell yourself it's just a game.
documents.overview: Desperate to help her ailing brother, a young woman agrees to compete in a deadly game of "Would You Rather" hosted by a sadistic aristocrat.
documents.plot:
Would You Rather is a 2012 American psychological horror thriller film directed by David Guy Levy and starring Brittany Snow as Iris and Jeffrey Combs as Shepard Lambrick, with Jonny Coyne, Lawrence Gilliard Jr. and Enver Gjokaj. Based on the party game of the same name, it follows a young woman who enters a deadly game to pay for her brother's leukemia treatment. Crispin Glover was originally cast as Lambrick but left before filming, which took place in the Los Angeles area in July 2011.

Iris is struggling to pay for the treatment of her younger brother, Raleigh, who has leukemia. Their oncologist, Dr. Barden, introduces her to Shepard Lambrick, a wealthy philanthropist who promises to pay for the treatment and find a bone marrow donor if she wins a game at his dinner party. The other guests include Shepard's arrogant son Julian, a war veteran named Travis, a paralyzed elderly woman named Linda, a gambling addict named Peter, a recovering alcoholic named Conway, and Lucas, Amy and Cal. Over dinner Shepard tempts them with money: Iris, a vegetarian, eats meat for $10,000, and Conway drinks Scotch for $50,000. Shepard then reveals the game, a deadly version of "would you rather", in which the last player standing wins. When Conway tries to leave, he is shot dead by the butler, Bevans.

The rounds grow more brutal. After a round of electric shocks, the players must either stab their neighbor with an ice pick or whip Travis with a sjambok; Linda bleeds to death and Travis is fatally injured. An escape attempt leaves Cal dead, and Dr. Barden, who tries to help Iris, is killed. In the third round, the players choose between two minutes submerged in a barrel of water and an unknown task on a card: Peter dies when a firecracker explodes in his hand, Lucas slices his own eye, Iris survives the water, and Amy drowns after her card doubles the time. In the final round, Iris must kill Lucas to win or spare him and forfeit the prize. She shoots him. Shepard gives her the money and reveals that a donor has already been found, but when Iris returns home she discovers that Raleigh has killed himself with an overdose of his medication, rendering her terrible choices meaningless.

The film premiered at Screamfest on October 14, 2012, and was released in select theaters and on video on demand by IFC Midnight on February 8, 2013. Reviews were mixed: Rotten Tomatoes reported 61% approval, praising the premise but faulting its gore, while Metacritic gave it 20.

documents.title: Rust and Bone
documents.overview: Put in charge of his young son, Ali leaves Belgium for Antibes to live with his sister and her husband as a family. Ali's bond with Stephanie, a killer whale trainer, grows deeper after Stephanie suffers a horrible accident.
documents.plot:
Alain "Ali" van Versch, an unemployed single father in his twenties, arrives in Antibes to look for work to support his young son, Sam. Having no money, he crashes with his sister Anna, a cashier who already has her own share of problems with financial instability and temporary employment.
Ali gets a job as a bouncer in a nightclub, which allows him to continue his passion for kickboxing by training during the day. One evening, Ali meets Stéphanie after she is injured in a club brawl. He escorts her back to her home, where he learns she is an orca trainer at Marineland. Ali offers his phone number to Stéphanie before leaving. He later gets a new job as a security guard, where his co-worker Martial informs him of an illegal fighting racket where he can earn money in bouts.
At Marineland, Stéphanie suffers an accident during a show. She wakes up in the hospital to realize that her legs have been amputated. Now in a wheelchair and trying to adjust to life without her legs, Stéphanie is deeply depressed. She gives Ali a call. Ali visits her and takes her to a beach, where he persuades her to go swimming; though hesitant at first, Stéphanie eventually forgets her self-consciousness and is liberated by the experience.
Ali and Stéphanie begin to spend more time together, and her self-image improves. After she is outfitted with artificial limbs, she persists in learning to walk again. Stéphanie learns about Ali's involvement in mixed martial arts and has him bring her to watch his fights. After a frank discussion with Stéphanie, Ali offers to have sex with her to help her adjust to her new body. Their friendship evolves to include casual sex, though Stéphanie prevents deeper intimacy by forbidding kissing during their encounters.
On a night out with Ali and friends at the club where Ali formerly worked, Stéphanie feels rejected when Ali dances with another woman and goes home with her. A man at the bar tries to make a pass at Stéphanie, but stops short when he sees her prosthetic legs under her skirt. The man apologizes to her, prompting Stéphanie to fly into a rage and attack him. She is escorted from the club.
The next day, Stéphanie questions Ali about their relationship. She says that if they continue to have casual sex, they have to respect each other's feelings and be more discreet about their other involvements. Their intimacy increases and, one night Stéphanie lets down her guard and kisses Ali. Stéphanie also begins managing Ali's bets for his fighting when Martial leaves town.
Anna is fired from her job when the managers catch her taking home expired food products. Her co-workers tell her that Ali was found installing surveillance cameras at their work, as management wanted surveillance of employees' activities. Anna has a tense fight with her brother Ali, culminating in a standoff between him and her partner Richard, who demands that Ali leave Anna's flat and not come back.

documents.title: The Place Beyond the Pines
documents.tagline: One moment can change your life.
documents.overview: A motorcycle stunt rider considers committing a crime in order to provide for his wife and child, an act that puts him on a collision course with a cop-turned-politician.
documents.plot:
In 1994, Luke Glanton is a motorcycle stuntman with a traveling carnival. In Schenectady, he meets his ex-lover Romina Gutierrez, who is now with a man named Kofi Kancam and has a son, Jason. When Romina tells Luke that he is Jason's real father, he quits the carnival to stay nearby. Romina is doubtful Luke can provide for them.
During a spirited ride through the woods, Luke impresses auto-mechanic Robin Van Derk Hook and begins working part-time for him. When Luke asks for more work to support his family, Robin reveals his past as a bank robber and suggests they commit robberies together. Luke robs the banks at gunpoint and drives his motorcycle into a box truck driven by Robin. Luke uses his share of the money to get close to Romina and Jason.
One day, Luke lets himself into Romina and Kofi's house to assemble a crib for Jason. When Kofi demands he leave, Luke strikes him with a wrench and is arrested. Robin bails him out of jail but refuses to do any more heists, fearing Luke is too reckless, and dismantles Luke's bike. Luke gives his share of the robberies to Romina who wants nothing to do with him anymore, then steals money from Robin to pay for a new bike.
Luke botches his first attempt robbing a bank alone, resulting in an auto chase and his pursuit by rookie cop Avery Cross. After crashing, Luke breaks into a house and calls Romina, asking her not to tell Jason about him. Avery confronts Luke and panics when he sees his gun, shooting first and wounding Luke in the stomach. Luke fires back, hitting Avery in the leg, before falling out a window to his death.
Avery, a married man with a baby son named A.J., is hailed as a hero for killing the "Moto Bandit". Though troubled by Luke's death, he lies to the District Attorney that Luke fired first. A group of corrupt officers pressure Avery to help them find the money from Luke's bank robberies from Romina's home, resulting in Avery holding baby Jason as he sleeps while another officer retrieves the cash. Avery tries to return his cut to Romina, who rejects it. When his chief refuses to go after the corrupt officers, Avery secretly records one of them asking him to steal evidence and leverages the recordings into an assistant district attorney position.
Fifteen years later, Avery is running for Attorney General of New York. A.J., now a rebellious teenager, moves in with his father and transfers to Schenectady High School, befriending the now-teenage Jason, with neither boy knowing the history between their fathers. When the teens are arrested for drug possession, Avery recognizes Jason's name and gets his charge dropped to a misdemeanor. He orders A.J. to stay away from him.
Kofi, now Jason's legal stepfather, tells Jason his birth father's name, which allows him to discover Luke's past. Jason visits Robin, who tells him about Luke and their friendship. A.J. pressures Jason to steal OxyContin for a party. At the party, Jason discovers that A.J.'s father is the man who killed Luke.

documents.title: Under the Skin
documents.tagline: An otherworldly perspective on the human condition.
documents.overview: A seductive alien prowls the streets of Glasgow in search of prey: unsuspecting men who fall under her spell.
documents.plot:
In Glasgow, a motorcyclist retrieves an inert young woman from the roadside and places her in the back of a van, where a naked woman dons her clothes. After buying clothes and make-up at a shopping centre, the woman drives the van from town to town, picking up single men with few friends. She lures a man into a dilapidated house. As he undresses, following the woman into a void, he is submerged in a liquid abyss.
At a beach, the woman attempts to pick up a swimmer, but is interrupted by the cries of a drowning couple attempting to rescue their dog, as it is pulled out to sea. The swimmer rescues the husband, but the husband rushes back into the water to save his wife and both drown. As the swimmer lies exhausted on the beach, the woman strikes his head with a rock, drags him to the van, and drives away, ignoring the couple's distraught baby. The motorcyclist retrieves the swimmer's belongings, ignoring the baby crying on the beach.
The woman visits a nightclub and picks up another man. At the house, he follows her into the void and is submerged in the liquid. Suspended beneath the surface, he sees the swimmer floating naked beside him, alive but bloated and immobile. When he reaches to touch him, the swimmer's body collapses, leaving only his empty skin floating in the liquid as a red mass empties through a trough.
The next day, the woman receives a rose from a street vendor, purchased by another man in traffic. She listens to a radio report about the missing family from the beach. The woman enters a dark room and is examined by the motorcyclist. She seduces a lonely man with facial tumours but lets him leave after examining herself in a mirror. The motorcyclist intercepts the man and bundles him into a car, then sets out in pursuit of the woman.
In the Scottish Highlands, the woman abandons the van in the fog. She walks to a restaurant and attempts to eat cake, but retches and spits it out. On a bus, she meets a man who offers to help her. At his house, he prepares a meal for her and they watch television. Alone in her room, she examines her body in a mirror. They visit a ruined castle, where the man carries her over a puddle and helps her down some steps. At his house, they kiss and begin to have sex, but the woman stops and examines her genitals.
Wandering in a forest, the woman meets a commercial logger and shelters in a bothy. She wakes up to find the logger molesting her. She runs into the wilderness but he catches and attempts to rape her. He tears her skin, revealing a featureless body. As the woman extricates herself from her skin, the man douses her in fuel and burns her alive. The motorcyclist looks out across a snowy field.

documents.title: Detective Conan: The Lost Ship in the Sky
documents.original_title: 名探偵コナン 天空の難破船（ロスト・シップ）
documents.overview: A terrorist group invades a laboratory containing a deadly bacteria and destroys the lab with an explosion. They later announce via the internet they have gained possession of the bacteria and declare themselves to be the Red Siamese Cats, a terrorist group that was eradicated a decade ago.
documents.plot:
A terrorist group invades a laboratory containing a deadly bacteria and destroys the lab with an explosion. They later announce via the internet that they have gained possession of the bacteria and declare themselves to be the Red Siamese Cats (赤いシャムネコ, Akai Shamu Neko), a terrorist group that was eradicated a decade ago.
Conan Edogawa, Kogoro, Ran Mouri and the Detective Boys are invited by Sonoko Suzuki's uncle, Jirokichi, to fly in his airship to witness his attempt at capturing Kaito Kid by baiting him with the jewel called Lady Sky (レディー スカイ, Redī Sukai). Kid replies to Jirokichi's challenge with a letter announcing that he will steal Lady Sky when the airship approaches Osaka. Aboard the airship, besides its employees and the police, there are four others who are working for the media: Takamichi Fujioka, a journalist; Masaki Mizukawa, a TV director; Kasumi Nishitani, a reporter; and Junpei Ishimoto, a cameraman. Meanwhile, a waitress enters the smoking room where an ampoule with the logo of the Red Siamese Cats is seen under the sofa. Conan reminisces to Dr. Hiroshi Agasa about the time Ran thought an airship was an unidentified flying object and asks him to keep it a secret. A waiter overhears Conan in the shadows.
Conan's group is given a tour of the airship; Ran diverges from the group to get a better look at Lady Sky. She meets a waiter wearing a bandage similar to the one she gave to a maintenance personnel and grabs his arm deducing he is actually Kid in disguise. She then subdues Kid and threatens to hand him over to Ginzo Nakamori. Kid removes the mask in an attempt to pretending to be Shinichi Kudo and convincing Ran by telling her she thought the airship was a UFO once, but she still doesn't trust him and let him go anyway. Meanwhile, the waitress begins to develop a rash on the back of her arms. Jirokichi receives a phone call who tells him the bacteria in the smoking room before hanging up. Nakamori confirms through the ampoule that it is the work of the Red Siamese Cats. Fujioka begins to develop a rash over his whole body and approaches the group whilst in pain before being knocked out by Ran. The waitress with the rash is found unconscious by a short-haired waitress; Fujioka and the unconscious waitress are quarantined in a separate room. Conan leaves to search for The Junior Detective League who are exploring the ship.
Conan finds them in the attic of the airship. There, they witness an unknown culprit unlock the roof allowing the Red Siamese Cats to enter and hijack the ship. Their leader announces they plan to get revenge on Jirokichi who assisted in eradicating the terrorist group and that they will detonate the bombs on the ships or release a second ampoule containing the bacteria if they resist. Conan finds the four bombs in the attic of the ship and disarms them; He notes it was strange they used bombs and bacteria to hijack the ship and attempts to figure out their ulterior motive.

documents.title: The Man with the Iron Fists
documents.original_title: The Man with the Iron Fists
documents.tagline: You can't spell Kung Fu without F and U!
documents.overview: In feudal China, a blacksmith who makes weapons for a small village is put in the position where he must defend himself and his fellow villagers.
documents.plot:
The Man with the Iron Fists is a 2012 martial arts film written and directed by RZA, starring Russell Crowe, Lucy Liu, and Jamie Chung. The movie is set in 19th-century China during the Qing dynasty.

The story begins with a young blacksmith named Lin Po (Jamie Chung), who lives in a small village in southern China. Lin is an orphan who was raised by his adoptive father, a kind-hearted blacksmith. However, their peaceful life is disrupted when a group of bandits, led by the ruthless and cunning Miao San (Lu Han), attack the village. The bandits are seeking to steal the legendary Golden Lotus, a powerful artifact that can grant immense power.

Lin's adoptive father is killed in the battle, and Lin sets out on a journey to avenge his death and protect the Golden Lotus. Along the way, he meets a mysterious woman named Yu Shu Lien (Lucy Liu), who claims to be a skilled warrior and offers to help Lin on his quest.

As they journey through treacherous landscapes and battle against Miao San's men, Lin and Yu Shu Lien discover that the Golden Lotus is hidden in a temple guarded by a powerful sorcerer. The sorcerer, named Tu (Jamie McDevitt), has been using the Golden Lotus to gain control over the region.

Lin and Yu Shu Lien eventually reach the temple, where they face off against Tu and his minions. In a thrilling battle, Lin uses his martial arts skills and the power of the Golden Lotus to defeat Tu and shatter the sorcerer's staff.

However, Miao San is not defeated so easily. He reveals that he has been working with a powerful warlord named Lord Shen (Russell Crowe), who seeks to conquer all of China using the Golden Lotus's power. Lin and Yu Shu Lien must now join forces with Lord Shen's men to defeat Miao San and stop Lord Shen's plans.

The final battle is intense, with Lin facing off against both Miao San and Lord Shen. In the end, Lin emerges victorious, having defeated both villains and saved China from their evil plans.

Throughout the movie, RZA pays homage to classic martial arts films, incorporating elements of kung fu and Chinese mythology into the story. The film's action sequences are fast-paced and thrilling, with a mix of sword fights, hand-to-hand combat, and magical battles.

Overall, The Man with the Iron Fists is an entertaining and action-packed adventure that combines elements of martial arts, fantasy, and historical drama.
